# One block per comment, opened by '=== <address> [<type>]'. Blocks are address-ordered,
# then ordered by type within an address. Loader fixup comments are excluded.
=== 00010000 [PLATE]
Trap at the first byte of the loaded image: INT3 to break into a debugger, then JMP back to itself, so control that lands on offset 0 halts there instead of running on into the code that follows.
Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(cstrt386), BEGTEXT segment head - byte-exact library match]
Evidence: cc eb fd followed by thirteen 90 bytes occurs exactly once in Watcom 10.0a LIB386/DOS/CLIB3S.LIB, at file offset 0x452c, directly after the PUBDEF block naming ___begtext, __nullarea, _cstart_, __exit, __do_exit_with_msg__ and __GETDS - the startup module cstrt386, as its BEGTEXT LEDATA content. The image holds those same 16 bytes here. Not binary_artifact: shipped inside a library object, not synthesised by this link, so it comes back by linking CLIB3S. Not fdps: no game data, strings or callers; game code starts at 00010010 where _TEXT begins. Not ail: nothing AIL-side reaches it. The five DATA xrefs are the constant 0x10000 mis-read as an address; the only true reference is its own backward jump.
Name: no library symbol identified - cstrt386 places ___begtext at offset 3, immediately after these bytes, so the trap carries no symbol of its own, and 3 bytes are too few for Function ID.
Boundary: 00010000-00010002, the INT3 plus the unconditional self-JMP are the whole body; the 13 trailing 90 bytes are BEGTEXT alignment padding, already defined as data and labelled ___begtext at 00010003.
Signature: no convention is exercised - no argument is read, no frame built, and the self-JMP means it never returns. Ghidra's __watcall void(void) is its guess, unconfirmed, and left as is because it is vacuously true here.

=== 00010001 [EOL]
JMP self (eb fd) inside the Watcom CRT trap stub at 00010000: bytes 2-3 of the BEGTEXT segment of cstrt386.obj (CLIB3S), not a function entry and not linker fill

=== 00010003 [EOL]
13 x 0x90 single-byte NOP alignment padding up to the 0x10 boundary at the next function entry 00010010

=== 00010010 [PLATE]
Advance a single battle-map actor one behavior step, dispatching on the low nibble of unit record byte 0x34.
Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record / fdps_battle_move_unit_toward / fdps_play_sfx and touches game globals; no Function ID hit in either library set]
Evidence: References game-defined symbols and data (unit record array DAT_00069cd8 with 0x50-byte stride, DAT_0006013c, DAT_000640d8, DAT_00063f78/88/8c, DAT_00069cd0, strings "Chess.wav" and "Posion.saf"), which a separately compiled vendor object could not do. Called from fdps_title_demo and three other game dispatchers. Function ID matched nothing in the Watcom 10.0x libraries or in ailv3.lib, and at 1861 bytes with a 12-way state switch it is not linker-emitted glue, so crt, ail and binary_artifact are all excluded.
Name: Game code, so fdps_ + snake_case; no vendor symbol involved.
Boundary: 00010010-00010754, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 / SUB ESP,0x4c at the entry and the matching MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET at the end; the 11 bytes after it are Watcom alignment padding (LEA EAX,[EAX+0] / LEA EDX,[EDX+0] / MOV EBX,EBX) up to the separate function fdps_chapter_30_revive_wave_4_undead, which this body itself calls at 0001067e.
Signature: __cdecl, void (int actor_index, int side_select); both arguments read from [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], plain RET with caller cleanup, no value returned. Confirmed by the assembly, not a guess.

Algorithm:
Resolves the actor record for the given index through fdps_get_unit_record (0002d210); the same record is reachable as DAT_00069cd8 + index * 0x50, confirming the 0x50-byte stride. If bit 0 of record[5] is set the actor is inactive and the function returns immediately.

Otherwise it reads the behavior mode from the low nibble of record[0x34] plus record[0x35] / record[0x36] (a destination pair) and an event slot index in record[0x3d], and dispatches:
  mode 0, 1, 2  -- try the movement handlers 00012c10 / 000126b0 / 000127c0 / 00012230 in a fixed per-mode order and fall back to 000120d0 when every attempt fails.
  mode 3, 9     -- when 00012c10 does not claim the actor, query 0002dc20 for a target; if one exists move toward its x/y with fdps_battle_move_unit_toward, otherwise take the handler-chain fallback. BOTH arms call 0002da50 (000101af in mode 3, 00010505 in mode 9). Mode 3 clears DAT_00069cd0 AFTER the walk at 000101ee; mode 9 never touches DAT_00069cd0 at all. The two fallback ladders also differ in length: mode 9's runs 00012c10 first (0001058a), mode 3's does not, because mode 3 has already spent 00012c10 as its entry gate at 00010173.
  mode 4, 7     -- clear DAT_00069cd0, call 0002da50 and walk toward the record[0x35]/record[0x36] destination. Mode 7, on arrival, plays the "Posion.saf" effect through 00026e00 when record[7] lies in 0x24..0x27, then retires the actor with MOV byte ptr [EAX+0x5],0x1 at 000104b8 -- a WHOLE-BYTE store of 1 over record[5], not a bit set, so bit 7 (the redraw/acted mark) and every other flag in that byte are cleared at the same time.
  mode 5         -- event step: if the per-slot flag (&DAT_000640d8)[record[0x3d]] is still clear and 00013e10 yields a destination, walk there; on arrival read the entry at DAT_0006013c + slot * 3, whose byte at +0x53 (0001033e) is a script opcode and whose SIGNED 16-bit word at +0x54 (MOVSX at 00010352) is its operand -- one signed word, not two bytes taken separately. The copy into record[0x31]/record[0x32] is GATED by CMP dword ptr [EBP-0x18],0x2 / JGE 0x00010388 at 00010359: an opcode of 2 or more writes NEITHER field. 00025d20 is called inside that gate when the opcode is zero. Outside it, at the JGE target 00010388, the slot flag is set unconditionally, then fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes, the switch of the actor to mode 7 (0001039a) and "Chess.wav" through fdps_play_sfx.
  mode 8         -- no action, returns immediately.
  mode 10, 11   -- the driven modes: 00013040 or 00013420, gated extra handlers 00027180 / 00013c90 when DAT_00063f8c / DAT_00063f88 reach 6, then 00012230, and finally 00012e50 or the 000126b0 / 000120d0 fallback depending on DAT_00063f78. Mode 11 additionally invokes fdps_chapter_30_revive_wave_4_undead when record[7] is in 0x3c..0x3e.

After dispatch it re-reads the record, calls 0002e030 with the actor's current x/y and 1, sets bit 0x80 of record[5] to mark the actor for redraw, and calls fdps_render_view_frame.

Parameters:
  actor_index -- index into the actor record array at DAT_00069cd8 (0x50 bytes per record).
  side_select -- the acting side; 0 from fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase (00012a08), 1 from fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase (00012bab), the actor's own side byte record[6] from fdps_title_demo (0002adb8). Passed unchanged to every movement handler and scorer.

Returns:
  Nothing.

=== 00010755 [EOL]
Alignment padding: multi-byte NOP forms filling 11 bytes up to the 0x10 boundary at 00010760.

=== 00010760 [PLATE]
Chapter 30's undead top-up: every 死靈 and 白骨戰士 of the map's wave 4 that has been killed is put back on the battlefield at full health, which is why that chapter's reinforcements can never be cleared out.

Algorithm:
Sweeps unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1, resolving each 0x50-byte record through fdps_get_unit_record. A record is passed over unless its character id at +7 is 0x55 (死靈) or 0x6a (白骨戰士) and fdps_unit_is_retired reports it retired, so only the wave-4 undead that are already dead are touched.

For each one it rebuilds the occupancy grid at DAT_00060144 -- fdps_map_grid_reset, then fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control(0) and (1), which between them mark every unit still in play -- and reads the grid header, tile width at +0 and tile height at +2. The anchor tile is the type's scripted spawn point in map29.cod: (5, 12) for character id 0x55, (15, 13) for 0x6a. It then scans the whole grid row by row, cell (x, y) at DAT_00060144 + 4 + (y * width + x) * 2, skipping every cell whose byte 0 has bit 0x40 set (a unit stands there). For each remaining cell whose Manhattan distance to the anchor is no greater than the best so far it calls fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) and keeps the cell when the terrain movement cost that publishes at DAT_00069d09 is below 5. The best-so-far distance starts at 0xff, and the test is "no greater than", so among the cells that tie at the shortest distance the last one in scan order wins.

The chosen cell's x and y go into record bytes +0 and +1, fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(unit_index) scrolls the view onto the unit, and the screen flashes: 0x41 calls to fdps_set_palette_range over the palette at DAT_000643bc with an equal r/g/b bias stepping from 0x40 down to 0, each followed by delay(4). A bias of 0x40 clamps every DAC channel to 0x3f, so the picture snaps to white and fades back to the normal palette over about a quarter of a second. FUN_00026e00(1, &unit_index_byte, "Posion.saf") then plays that MISC.VFS effect animation over the one unit.

Last it stores 0 into the record's status byte at +5, which drops both the retired bit 0 and the redraw bit 0x80 and so puts the unit back in play, copies max HP (+0x42) over current HP (+0x40), and calls fdps_map_grid_reset again to leave the grid blank for the movement code.

Everything from the grid rebuild onwards runs once per killed unit, so the white flash and the effect animation play once for each undead that is brought back on this pass.

The only caller is fdps_map_actor_behavior_step, from its behavior-mode 11 branch and only when the acting unit's character id at +7 is 0x3c..0x3e -- the three forms of 平衡之神 -- so in the shipped data this runs on every behavior step the chapter 30 boss takes.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; game globals and game callees throughout]

Rebuild note:
The nearest-tile search accepts a cell whose distance merely ties the best so far, so the last tie in row-major scan order is the tile used, not the first. Writing the obvious "<" there puts the revived unit somewhere else whenever the anchor tile itself is taken, which on this map it usually is.

=== 000109af [EOL]
Single-byte 0x90 alignment NOP between FUN_00010760 and FUN_000109b0

=== 000109b0 [PLATE]
Is this unit retired -- has it left the battle for good?

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit record for unit_index through fdps_get_unit_record, reads the flag byte at record offset 5, and returns bit 0 of it, narrowed to 0 or 1.

Bit 0 is the retired flag. fdps_map_actor_behavior_step returns immediately for any actor whose bit 0 is set, and sets that bit itself when a mode 7 actor reaches the end of its scripted walk; bit 7 of the same byte is the shorter-lived per-turn redraw flag, not this one. Callers use the predicate both ways round: 00018350 counts the units of a type for which it returns zero, and 00010760 gathers the units for which it returns non-zero to a type-specific anchor tile and fades them out.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit record array (0x50 bytes per record), the same index fdps_get_unit_record takes.

Returns:
  1 when the unit is retired, 0 when it is still in play.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record; no library byte match in either the Watcom or the AIL Function ID set]

=== 000109e5 [EOL]
Alignment padding: multi-byte NOP forms between FUN_000109b0 and FUN_000109f0.

=== 000109f0 [PLATE]
Collects the battle units standing in the area of effect centred on one map tile that a targeting mode accepts, and returns how many there are.

Algorithm:
Walks the unit records based at DAT_00069cd8 with stride 0x50 over the DAT_00060150 records the battle holds. For each record it reads the unit's tile position from bytes +0 (x) and +1 (y) and forms the Manhattan distance abs(x - tile_x) + abs(y - tile_y) through the CRT abs. A record is dropped when bit 0 of the status byte at +5 is set (the retired flag fdps_unit_is_retired returns) or when that distance is not below max_dist; the limit is exclusive, so max_dist 1 selects the centre tile alone. What is left is filtered on select_mode against the side byte at +6 and the acted bit 0x80 of byte +5, the bit fdps_battle_mark_unit_done sets and fdps_units_clear_status_bit7 clears at the turn boundary: mode 0 keeps side 0 (enemy units), mode 1 keeps every non-zero side (guest NPCs and the player's party), mode 2 keeps side 2 units that have already acted this turn, mode 3 keeps side 2 (the player's party), and any other value keeps nothing -- so the item select_mode values 4 and 5 come back with a count of 0. Each surviving unit's index is appended to out_indices as one byte when that pointer is non-NULL, and the running match count is returned. Neither the record coordinates nor the length of out_indices is checked.

The mode 2 arm is unreachable with the shipped data. The one caller forwards its own mode argument unchanged, and every producer of that argument is accounted for: the literals 0, 3, 4, 5 and 6 at the hard-coded call sites of fdps_map_cursor_select_loop (00015574, 00015f4b, 00025624, 00025784, 00027fa6, 00027ff9), the ITEM.DAT select_mode byte +0x15 at 000254ed (only 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 occur across the table), and the MAGICDAT.DAT target byte +0x06 at 00027e2d (only 0, 1 and a single 3 occur). Nothing produces a 2.

The same select_mode numbering means something different in fdps_collect_targets_in_range, which is called with the same ITEM.DAT and MAGICDAT.DAT bytes in the same statement pairs: there mode 2 keeps side 1 with no state test (00012077), here it keeps side 2 that has already acted (00010abb, 00010ac8).

Parameters:
  tile_x -- column of the centre tile, 0-based; fdps_map_cursor_select_loop passes the cursor pixel position DAT_00069cd4 divided by the 0x18 tile size
  tile_y -- row of the centre tile, 0-based, from DAT_00069ccc / 0x18
  max_dist -- exclusive Manhattan-distance limit in tiles; the caller derives it from the area-of-effect global DAT_00069cd0, which the item and spell code sets to the record's radius + 2 and otherwise holds at 1, decremented by one when it is above 1
  out_indices -- caller-supplied byte array that receives the index of every matching unit, or NULL to count only; fdps_map_cursor_select_loop passes NULL
  select_mode -- 0 to 3, selecting the filter above; it reaches here as the mode argument of fdps_map_cursor_select_loop, which carries either a literal or the item record's select_mode field at offset 0x15 or the spell record's target field at offset 0x06

Returns:
  The number of units that matched, 0 when none did. fdps_map_cursor_select_loop treats any non-zero result as "the cursor tile holds a legal target" and confirms the selection.

Pool: fdps  [game map data: 0x50-byte unit stride over the globals DAT_00060150 and DAT_00069cd8; no Function ID hit in either library set and the only callee is the CRT abs]

Rebuild note:
The select_mode table here is not the one fdps_collect_targets_in_range uses, although both are called with the same ITEM.DAT byte 0x15 or MAGICDAT.DAT byte 0x06 in the same statement pair: mode 2 means side 2 with the acted bit 0x80 set here (00010abb, 00010ac8) but side 1 with no state test there (00012077). Factoring the two into one shared 'does this unit match the target filter' helper -- the obvious cleanup -- silently changes which units the confirm key accepts. The distance test is also strictly less-than against a limit the caller has already decremented, so writing dist <= max_dist widens every area of effect by a tile. And the match counter advances even when out_indices is NULL (00010af3 skips only the store, not the increment at 00010b03), so folding the increment into the append -- the natural way to write 'push this index' -- makes the count-only call, which is the only call there is, always return 0.

=== 00010b1b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning next function to 0x00010b20

=== 00010b20 [PLATE]
Blanks the battle map's working grid so a new movement range or target mask can be computed over it.

Algorithm:
Returns at once when the grid pointer DAT_00060144 is null. Otherwise it reads the grid header -- signed 16-bit tile width at +0, tile height at +2 -- and walks the width*height cells that begin at +4, two bytes per cell, in row-major order. In each cell byte 0, the zone-of-control flag byte, is ANDed with 0x3f: that clears bit 0x40 (a unit stands on this tile, so it may not be entered) and bit 0x80 (this tile adjoins a unit, so movement entering it must stop), the two bits that 00010c30 and 00010da0 set and that the movement flood fill at 00010de0 tests. Cell byte 1, the step cost, is stored 0xff, the unreachable/empty sentinel that the flood fill relaxes downwards and that fdps_move_path_trace and 00011da0 read back. The low six bits of byte 0 are deliberately preserved, but no code in the program writes or reads them. fdps_field_load_chapter_resources allocates this grid as 4 + width*height*2 bytes, stores the two header words, and calls this function to bring the cells up; the battle routines call it again before each range or targeting pass.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; its only data reference is the game-owned map grid global and all 14 static callers are game code]

=== 00010b8e [EOL]
Alignment padding: mov eax,eax (8b c0), 2-byte no-op before 16-byte-aligned entry FUN_00010b90.

=== 00010b90 [PLATE]
Marks the zone of control of every unit on the side opposite the caller's, so the movement range flood-filled onto the battle grid afterwards cannot be walked through them.

Algorithm:
Caches the unit record array base from the global at 00069cd8 and walks the DAT_00060150 records it holds, stepping a record pointer by the 0x50-byte stride once per index. A record is passed over when bit 0 of its status byte at +5 is set -- the retired flag fdps_unit_is_retired reads -- and when the truth value of its side byte at +6 agrees with side_select: side_select 0 keeps only the records whose side byte is non-zero, any non-zero side_select keeps only the records whose side byte is zero. Only the truth value of each is used, never the number. For every record that survives it calls fdps_move_grid_mark_zone_of_control with the record's tile column and row, the bytes at +0 and +1, which makes that tile impassable and turns the four tiles beside it into movement stoppers on the grid at DAT_00060144.

Side byte +6 is 0 for the enemy side, 1 for the neutral side and 2 for the player side, so a caller that passes the truth value of its own moving unit's side gets the zones of control of the units that oppose it and no others: fdps_battle_unit_turn passes 1 for the player unit whose turn it is and so marks the side-0 enemies. Callers run fdps_map_grid_reset first and the range flood fill fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range after, then fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles with the same side value, which removes the tiles of the units on the caller's own side from the range; between the two, tiles held by the opposing side cannot be entered at all while tiles held by the caller's own side can be crossed but not stopped on. fdps_chapter_30_revive_wave_4_undead and fdps_deploy_unit instead call this twice in a row, with 0 and then 1, which between them covers every unit, so the grid carries the whole map's zones of control before those two look for a placement tile.

Parameters:
  side_select -- the side whose units are NOT to be marked, as a truth value: 0 marks the units whose side byte at +6 is non-zero, any non-zero value marks the units whose side byte is zero. Callers pass their moving unit's own side, or sweep 0 and 1 to mark everyone.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set and the body hash is unique in the image; it walks the game's own 0x50-byte unit record array and its only callee and all five callers are battle-layer game code]

Rebuild note:
The side test uses only the truth value of the record's side byte, never its value: side_select 1 marks exactly the units whose byte +6 is 0. Writing the obvious C -- if (rec[6] != side_select) -- is wrong, because side bytes run 0 (enemy), 1 (neutral) and 2 (player), so with side_select 1 a naive inequality would also stamp a zone of control on every player unit and shrink the moving player unit's own movement range.

=== 00010c26 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6) + lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0] (4), aligning FUN_00010c30 to 16 bytes.

=== 00010c30 [PLATE]
Marks one unit's zone of control on the battle movement grid: the tile it stands on becomes impassable and the four tiles beside it become movement stoppers.

Algorithm:
Returns at once when the grid pointer DAT_00060144 is null. Otherwise it reads the grid header -- signed 16-bit tile width at +0, tile height at +2 -- and addresses cells as DAT_00060144 + 4 + 2 * (width * y + x), the two-bytes-per-cell layout fdps_map_grid_reset builds and blanks. Byte 0 of a cell is the zone-of-control flag byte, byte 1 the accumulated step cost. It ORs 0x80, "movement entering this tile must stop", into each orthogonal neighbour that exists: (tile_x-1, tile_y) only when tile_x is non-zero, (tile_x, tile_y-1) only when tile_y is non-zero, (tile_x+1, tile_y) only when tile_x < width-1, (tile_x, tile_y+1) only when tile_y < height-1. It then ORs 0x40, "a unit stands on this tile, so it may not be entered", into the cell at (tile_x, tile_y) itself, with no bounds check on the centre. Both bits are sticky and stay set until fdps_map_grid_reset ANDs the byte with 0x3f, so repeated calls accumulate the zones of every unit into one grid. fdps_move_grid_set_stop_flag @ 00010da0 has no neighbour logic at all -- it ORs 0x80 into the single tile it is handed -- and its body (MOV EAX,[DAT_00060144] / MOVSX word ptr [EAX] / IMUL EAX,[EBP+0x18] / ADD EAX,[EBP+0x14] / ADD EAX,EAX / ADD base / ADD EAX,0x4 / OR byte ptr [EAX],0x80) is exactly what each of the four neighbour marks here consists of; it has no callers anywhere in the image, and this function is where its code went, expanded at all four sites. The movement flood fill at 00010de0 is what reads the bits back: 0x40 refuses the tile outright, 0x80 lets it be entered but records the full movement allowance as its cost so expansion stops there; 00010760 tests 0x40 alone when it hunts for an unoccupied tile near an anchor.

Parameters:
  tile_x -- column of the unit's tile, 0 .. grid width-1; the caller 00010b90 passes unit record byte +0
  tile_y -- row of the unit's tile, 0 .. grid height-1; the caller 00010b90 passes unit record byte +1

Returns:
  nothing

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in the Watcom libraries or in ailv3.lib, body hash unique in the image; twelve reads of the game map global DAT_00060144 and no runtime, AIL or DOS idiom]

=== 00010d9d [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_00010da0 to 4 bytes.

=== 00010da0 [PLATE]
Sets the movement-stops-here flag on one cell of the battle movement grid at DAT_00060144.

Algorithm:
Loads the grid base pointer from DAT_00060144 and the signed int16 width from its first word, forms the cell address base + 4 + 2 * (tile_y * width + tile_x), and ORs 0x80 into the cell's first byte. The grid is laid out as {int16 width; int16 height; cell cells[]} with two bytes per cell: byte 0 holds the movement flags -- 0x40 a unit stands here so the tile may not be entered, 0x80 the tile may be entered but movement ends there -- and byte 1 holds the flood-filled step cost, 0xff meaning unreachable. fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range is what reads the bit back: expanding onto a neighbour whose flag byte has 0x80 set, it replaces the accumulated cost with the whole movement allowance, so the tile can be stepped onto but not moved through. fdps_map_grid_reset clears both flag bits (byte 0 &= 0x3f) when it blanks the grid, and fdps_move_grid_mark_zone_of_control sets this same bit on the four tiles beside a unit with the same addressing written out inline -- this entry is the one-cell primitive of that pair. tile_x and tile_y are not bounds-checked against the header. There is also no null check on DAT_00060144: 00010dac MOV EAX,[0x00060144] is immediately followed by 00010db1 MOVSX EAX,word ptr [EAX], so the pointer is dereferenced unguarded, unlike fdps_map_grid_reset (00010b20) and fdps_move_grid_mark_zone_of_control (00010c30), which both open with CMP dword ptr [0x00060144],0 / JZ to the epilogue.

Nothing in the image calls this entry or takes its address, so it is unreferenced code the linker kept from an object whose other functions are used.

Parameters:
  tile_x -- column in the movement grid, 0 .. width-1 where width is the first word of the block at DAT_00060144
  tile_y -- row in the movement grid, 0 .. height-1 from the second word of that block

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [shared game data: reads and writes the game global DAT_00060144, the map grid every neighbour in this run of functions works on; no Function ID hit in either library set]

=== 00010dd8 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea eax,[eax+0x0] plus 2-byte mov edx,edx, aligning next function to 16 bytes.

=== 00010de0 [PLATE]
Flood-fills one unit's movement range into the battle movement grid: starting from the tile the unit stands on it relaxes the accumulated movement cost of every tile the unit can still afford to enter.

Algorithm:
Takes the movement grid from DAT_00060144 -- word width at +0, word height at +2, then width*height cells of 2 bytes each from +4, cell byte 0 flags and cell byte 1 accumulated cost. fdps_map_grid_reset leaves every cost at 0xff and clears flag bits 0x40/0x80 before the fill, and fdps_move_grid_mark_zone_of_control / fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control set those bits over it. Writes cost 0 into the start tile and seeds frontier buffer 0 with (start_x, start_y). The frontier is a pair of double-buffered queues: tile columns in the 2 x 0x190-byte array at DAT_00063c50, tile rows in the one at DAT_00063930, the two 16-bit entry counts on the stack, and a 0/1 buffer selector flipped by XOR 1 at the end of every wave.
Each wave zeroes the other buffer's count and walks the current frontier entry by entry. For an entry it reads that tile's own accumulated cost out of cell byte 1, then tries the four neighbours in the order up, right, down, left, each guarded against the map edge (y != 0, x < width-1, y < height-1, x != 0). For each neighbour it calls fdps_map_load_tile_info with the neighbour's tile coordinates, which publishes that tile's terrain type in DAT_00069d09, and forms the candidate cost as the current tile's cost plus class_move_cost[DAT_00069d09]. The neighbour is accepted when the candidate cost is <= move_points, its flag bit 0x40 (impassable) is clear, and the candidate cost is below the cost already stored in it. Flag bit 0x80 (movement stops on this tile) then replaces the candidate cost with move_points before it is stored, so no expansion can leave that tile again. The accepted neighbour's column and row are appended to the other buffer and its count bumped. When a wave ends with the other buffer empty the fill is finished and the routine returns.
Every direction block also reads the neighbour's terrain tile id out of the layer at [DAT_00069cb0]+0xb, masks it with 0x3ff and uses it to look a byte up in the 4-byte-stride table at [DAT_00069c98]+0x13; the tile id feeds only that lookup and the byte it fetches is never read at all. Note the layer is indexed with the MOVEMENT GRID's row stride, not with the width in the terrain layer's own header at +7 that fdps_map_load_tile_info uses.

Parameters:
  class_move_cost -- the acting unit's class record, which both named callers obtain from fdps_get_class_record; its first eight bytes are the movement cost of each terrain type, 0xff meaning impassable
  start_x -- column of the tile the fill starts from, in tiles, 0..width-1
  start_y -- row of the tile the fill starts from, in tiles, 0..height-1
  move_points -- the movement allowance to spend; a tile stays reachable while its accumulated cost is <= this. fdps_battle_move_unit_toward passes 0x64 for the calls where it wants the whole map covered rather than one unit's real allowance.

Returns:
  Nothing. The result is the accumulated cost byte of every reached cell of the movement grid at DAT_00060144, which fdps_move_path_trace then walks to build a path.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; owns the game's battle map and frontier globals and is called only by battle code]

Rebuild note:
Flag bit 0x80 on a destination cell does not stop the fill at that cell: it replaces the candidate cost with move_points, stores that, and still queues the cell, which is what starves any further expansion out of it while leaving it relaxable again by a cheaper route. Writing the obvious 'movement stops here' (store the real cost and skip the enqueue, or treat the cell as impassable) puts different cost bytes into the grid, and fdps_move_path_trace reads those same bytes to build the path, so the unit walks a different route.

=== 0001145b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning next function entry to 0x11460

=== 00011460 [PLATE]
Walks the battle movement-cost grid at DAT_00060144 (header: word width, word height, then width*height 2-byte cells, byte 1 holding the flood-filled step cost with 0xff = unreachable; cell stride 2, row stride 2*width): modes 0 and 1 step from (start_x,start_y) to the cheapest of the four neighbours until the tile equals (goal_x,goal_y), recording one direction code per step (0 = y-1, 1 = x+1, 2 = y+1, 3 = x-1, 4 = no move) and finally copying them into out_path in reverse order, returning the step count; mode 0 moves only on a strictly lower cost so equal-cost runs keep the current heading, while mode 1 also accepts an equal cost provided the previously recorded step used a different direction code, making ties turn instead of running straight; mode 2 ignores the goal and instead scans the unit table (count in DAT_00060150, records via fdps_get_unit_record), keeps only units whose record byte +0x06 has the opposite truth value to start_x -- start_x == 0 keeps the units whose side byte is non-zero, and any non-zero start_x keeps the units whose side byte is 0 -- and whose record byte +0x05 bit 0 is clear, tracks the lowest cost cell at (unit.x,unit.y), then writes that unit's x and y into out_path[0] and out_path[1] and returns the minimum cost; the function returns -1 when the start tile is already 0xff or when no unit matched.
Pool: fdps  [game map and unit-table globals, only game callers, no library match]
Evidence: Reads the game's own map-header global DAT_00060144 and unit-count global DAT_00060150, calls only fdps_get_unit_record and decodes unit-record bytes +0x00/+0x01/+0x05/+0x06; all five call sites are game code (fdps_battle_move_unit_toward, FUN_000126b0, fdps_battle_unit_turn). Signature: __cdecl, int fdps_move_path_trace(int goal_x, int goal_y, uchar *out_path, int start_x, int start_y, int mode) - six dword arguments read from [EBP+0x14] upward, bare RET with the caller doing the cleanup, result in EAX. mode is only read as a byte; start_x carries the side filter rather than a coordinate when mode is 2.
Rebuild note: in modes 0 and 1 the cost a neighbour has to beat is reseeded from the START tile's cost at the top of every step, not from the cost of the tile the walk is standing on -- MOV EAX,[EBP-0x28] / MOV [EBP-0x20],EAX at 00011631 opens the loop and [EBP-0x28] is written exactly once, at 00011600, before the loop is entered. Reseeding from the current cell is the obvious reading and is a different function: where no neighbour undercuts the tile it is standing on, the original still steps to any neighbour cheaper than the start tile, while the tightened form leaves the direction code at 4, moves nothing, records nothing, and never reaches the goal the loop's only exit tests for.

=== 000118f0 [PLATE]
Removes the tiles that units of one side stand on from the movement range just flood-filled into the battle movement grid, so the moving unit cannot end its move on top of one of them.

Algorithm:
Reads the grid base pointer DAT_00060144 and its first word, the signed 16-bit tile width, then walks the unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8 with stride 0x50 over the DAT_00060150 records the battle holds, advancing a record pointer in step with the loop index. A record is passed over when its index equals exclude_unit_index, so the moving unit keeps its own tile; when bit 0 of the status byte at +5 is set, the retired flag fdps_unit_is_retired reads; and when the truth value of the side byte at +6 disagrees with side_select -- side_select 0 keeps only records whose side byte is 0, any non-zero side_select keeps only records whose side byte is non-zero. For each record that survives it forms the address DAT_00060144 + 2 * (record[1] * width + record[0]) + 5, which is byte 1 of the cell at column record[0], row record[1] in the {int16 width; int16 height; uint16 cells[]} grid fdps_map_grid_reset documents, and stores 0xff there. Byte 1 is the flood-filled step cost and 0xff is its unreachable sentinel, so the tile leaves the range: fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles stops collecting it and fdps_move_path_trace will not step onto it. Neither the record's coordinates nor exclude_unit_index are range-checked against the grid header.

All three call sites run the same three-step sequence -- fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control(side), fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range, then this -- and hand the same side value to the first and the last (0001550e/00015566, 00011bcf/00011bf7, 0001233e/00012369). fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control stamps the zone-of-control bits (0x40 on the tile, 0x80 around it) on the units of the opposite truth value. Between the two, the tiles of the units on the other side cannot be entered at all, while the tiles of the units on this side can be crossed but not stopped on.

The side byte at record +6 runs 0 for the enemy side, 1 for the NPC side and 2 for the player side -- fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase sweeps for 0, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase for 1, fdps_battle_end_phase_if_all_units_done for 2. Because this function reduces that byte to a truth value, the partition it applies is {enemy} against {NPC, player}: a player unit moving with side_select 1 has both the player units' and the NPC units' tiles removed from its range, while an enemy actor moving with side_select 0 has only the other enemies' tiles removed. NPC units therefore obstruct the player exactly as comrades do, and never obstruct the enemy AI.

Parameters:
  exclude_unit_index -- index of the unit whose movement range this is, 0 .. DAT_00060150 - 1; its tile is left reachable, so standing still stays a legal choice. fdps_battle_unit_turn passes the unit whose turn it is; fdps_battle_move_unit_toward and fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack pass theirs straight through.
  side_select -- picks which units block, as a truth value: 0 for the units whose record byte +6 is zero (the enemy side), non-zero for the units whose record byte +6 is non-zero (the NPC and player sides). Only the truth value is used, never the number itself, and the sense is the complement of the identically named argument of fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control. Callers pass the moving unit's own side -- fdps_battle_unit_turn passes the constant 1 for a player unit, and fdps_title_demo passes an actor's record byte +6 down through fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; it walks the game's own unit record array and movement grid, and all three callers are battle-layer game code]

Rebuild note:
side_select is a truth-value selector, not a side code. Side bytes run 0 = enemy, 1 = NPC, 2 = player, while fdps_battle_unit_turn passes the literal 1 for a player unit, so the obvious rewrite `if (record[6] == side_select)` would block only the NPC units during a player unit's move and let that unit end its turn standing on a comrade. It has to be written as `(record[6] != 0) == (side_select != 0)`. The consequence is a real rule and not an accident to be tidied away: because the byte is reduced to a truth value, NPC-side units block the player exactly as player units do, and never block the enemy AI. The mirrored trap sits in fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control, which takes the same argument with the opposite polarity.

Alignment padding: 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_000119b0 to 16 bytes.

=== 000119b0 [PLATE]

In that byte bit 0 is the retired flag read by fdps_unit_is_retired and bit 7 is the acted-this-turn flag: fdps_battle_end_phase_if_all_units_done tests record[5] & 0x81 and skips any unit for which it is non-zero, so raising 0x80 stops this unit from holding the player phase open, and fdps_units_clear_status_bit7 clears the bit on every unit when fdps_battle_advance_turn opens the next turn. === 000119e0 [PLATE]
Moves a unit toward a requested destination tile: traces a path, retargets to the furthest walkable tile when the direct route is blocked, then picks the reachable tile nearest the target and animates the move.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; body is entirely game-domain]
Evidence: Calls only game routines - fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_get_class_record, fdps_move_path_trace, fdps_map_load_tile_info, fdps_animate_move_path - and reads the map probe result at DAT_00069d0c. malloc/free/abs are consumed, not joined. All callers are battle and map code. Not crt or ail (no library byte match, no vendor state area), not binary_artifact (945-byte body with a real frame).
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code; no library symbol identified, and none exists to identify.
Boundary: 000119e0-00011d90, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 to matching epilogue 89 ec 5d 5f 5e 5b c3; the 15 bytes after are lea-form alignment padding before FUN_00011da0.
Signature: __cdecl, int (int dest_x, int dest_y, int unit_index, int side_select) at [ebp+0x14/0x18/0x1c/0x20], caller-cleaned (add esp,0x10 at every call site), result in EAX. The fourth argument is a side truth value, not a mode: it reaches only fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control (00010be9..00010c07, marks the units whose side byte at +6 is non-zero when the argument is 0) and fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles (0001197a..0001199d, which reads it with the opposite polarity).

Algorithm:
1. fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) supplies tile x at +0x00, tile y at +0x01, a class index at +0x20 and a movement/terrain cost selector at +0x3b.
2. fdps_get_class_record(class_index + 1) yields the movement context; malloc(100) is the step buffer (one direction code per step) and malloc(0x800) is the reachable-tile list (x,y byte pairs).
3. Mark the opposing units' zones of control with fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control(side_select), then build the movement cost map with fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range(ctx, x, y, cost_selector) - only the flood builds the cost map, the mark does not - and path from the unit to (dest_x, dest_y) with fdps_move_path_trace(x, y, step_buf, dest_x, dest_y, 0), which returns the step count or -1 for no path.
4. On failure, retry with the relaxed flag 1. If a relaxed path exists, replay it step by step (direction 0 = y+1, 1 = x-1, 2 = y-1, else x+1), probing each tile with fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) and reading DAT_00069d0c. The last tile whose probe is not 0xff becomes the new destination - the request is retargeted to the furthest usable tile along the blocked route.
5. Rebuild the movement map, then narrow it with fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles(unit_index, side_select), which does the OPPOSITE of flooding the unit's reach: it stores the 0xff unreachable sentinel into the occupied units' cells, so the mover may cross them but may not stop on them. Collect the tiles that survive with fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles(tile_buf), which returns their count.
6. Scan those tiles and keep the one minimising |tx - dest_x| + |ty - dest_y|, breaking ties on the smaller ||dx| - |dy||.
7. Path to the chosen tile with the strict flag 0. If the step count is non-zero, fdps_animate_move_path(unit_index, step_buf, step_count) performs the move and the result is 1; otherwise 0.
8. Free both buffers and return.

Grid setup rounds: the grid is set up four separate times and the rounds are NOT interchangeable. Round 1 at 00011a5a does not reset first, so it inherits whatever the caller staged. Round 2 at 00011aaa resets and floods with NO mark and a literal allowance of 100. Rounds 3 (00011bc6) and 4 (00011cef) reset + mark + flood, and only round 3 calls fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles. Collapsing them into one shared setup would change which tiles the walk may cross and which it may finish on.

Alignment padding: three multi-byte LEA NOP forms aligning 00011da0 to 16 bytes.

=== 00011da0 [PLATE]
Collects every marked cell of the battle map's working grid into a caller-supplied array of (x, y) byte pairs and returns how many there are.

Algorithm:
Reads the grid pointer DAT_00060144 for the header -- signed 16-bit tile width at +0, tile height at +2 -- and sets the scan cursor to grid+5, which is byte 1 of the first cell; there is no null check on the pointer. Walks the width*height cells in row-major order two bytes at a time, so the cursor runs straight through the grid and is never recomputed per row. A cell counts as marked when its byte 1 is not 0xff, the grid's exclusion sentinel: fdps_map_grid_reset stores 0xff into byte 1 of every cell, 00010de0 relaxes it downwards to the flood-filled movement cost, and 00011e50 writes 0 into the cells its targeting mask selects -- so the same test yields the movement range for fdps_battle_move_unit_toward and the targetable tiles for 00013040. For each marked cell it writes the x index to out_coords[0] and the y index to out_coords[1], advances out_coords by two and bumps the counter. The grid is only read, never modified; callers wipe it afterwards with fdps_map_grid_reset. Nothing bounds the number of pairs written -- it is however many cells are marked.

Parameters:
  out_coords -- caller-supplied byte array receiving one (x, y) pair per marked cell, x first. Coordinates are tile indices, x in 0..width-1 and y in 0..height-1 of the grid header. Callers pass a malloc block: 0x800 bytes from fdps_battle_move_unit_toward, 0x1900 from 00012230, 0x190 from 00013040 and 00013420.

Returns:
  The number of (x, y) pairs written, that is the number of marked cells; 0 when nothing is marked.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; reads the game map global DAT_00060144 and is called only by battle-block game code]

Rebuild note:
This routine writes one (x, y) pair per marked cell with no upper bound, yet two of its four callers (00013040 and 00013420) hand it a 0x190-byte block that holds only 200 pairs, so a wide movement range or targeting mask overruns their heap allocation. Writing the obvious defensive version -- adding a capacity or max_count parameter, or sizing the callers' mallocs to width*height*2 -- deviates from the original; reproduce the signature and the allocation sizes as they are.

=== 00011e4b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning next function entry to 0x11e50.

=== 00011e50 [PLATE]
Collects the battle units that an attack, item or spell used from one map tile can reach, and returns how many there are.

Algorithm:
Works over the movement grid at DAT_00060144 -- word width at +0, word height at +2, then width*height cells of two bytes each from +4, cell byte 0 flags and cell byte 1 accumulated cost -- painting the reachable set into the cost bytes. It does not reset the grid itself: it expects to find it as fdps_map_grid_reset leaves it, every cost 0xff, and every calling function calls fdps_map_grid_reset again before the grid is next used, usually on the instruction after the cleanup (000123fe, 00015dd0, 00025335) but sometimes further on (00015f2c's reset is at 00015f56, after CALL 0x0002b4f0; 00027e14's at 00027e41).

A range_code below 0x10 gives the flood-filled shape. fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range spreads out of (tile_x, tile_y) with range_code movement points over the cost table of fdps_get_class_record(0), the PROMAP.DAT default row whose eight terrain costs are all 1, so one point buys one tile -- but the fill still refuses cells whose flag bit 0x40 marks them impassable, so walls cut the range short. When min_dist is non-zero the routine then sweeps every cell in row-major order from grid+5 in steps of 2 and writes 0xff back into each one whose Manhattan distance abs(x - tile_x) + abs(y - tile_y) is below min_dist, cutting the near tiles out again.

A range_code of 0x10 or more gives the straight-line shape: range_code - 0x10 is the reach, no flood fill runs, and the routine writes cost 0 into every cell of row tile_y and of column tile_x within that many tiles of the centre. That branch reads no terrain and skips the min_dist step entirely.

It then walks unit indices 0 through DAT_00060150 - 1, taking each record through fdps_get_unit_record and reading the unit's tile out of bytes +0 (x) and +1 (y). A unit is dropped when bit 0 of the status byte at +5 is set -- the retired flag fdps_unit_is_retired reads -- or when the cost byte of the cell it stands on is still 0xff. What is left is filtered on the side byte at +6: select_mode 0 keeps side 0 (enemy units), 1 keeps every non-zero side (guest NPCs and the player's party), 2 keeps side 1 (guest NPCs), 3 keeps side 2 (the player's party). Any other value keeps nothing, so the ITEM.DAT select_mode values 4 and 5 come back with a count of 0. Each surviving index is appended to out_indices as a single byte when that pointer is non-NULL, and the running count is returned. Neither the coordinates held in the records nor the length of out_indices is checked.

Parameters:
  tile_x -- column of the centre tile, 0-based; fdps_battle_action_menu, FUN_000252b0 and FUN_00027c20 pass the map cursor pixel position DAT_00069cd4 divided by the 0x18 tile size, the map-AI callers the candidate tile they are scoring
  tile_y -- row of the centre tile, 0-based, from DAT_00069ccc / 0x18 on those same callers
  out_indices -- caller-supplied byte array that receives the index of every matching unit, or NULL to count only; fdps_battle_action_menu passes NULL when it is only probing whether a command has a legal target
  range_code -- reach and shape in one value: 0..0xf is that many tiles of flood-filled reach, 0x10 and above is a straight-line cross with arms of (range_code - 0x10) tiles. fdps_battle_action_menu passes the equipped item's range_max (ITEM.DAT +0x0c), FUN_000252b0 the item's use_distance (+0x10, the field that carries the straight-line bit) and its use_radius (+0x12), FUN_00013c90 and FUN_00013420 the ability descriptor's byte +4
  min_dist -- exclusive minimum Manhattan distance in tiles: 0 keeps everything, 1 drops the centre tile alone, and a bow's range_min of 2 drops the centre and its four neighbours. Ignored on the straight-line branch
  select_mode -- 0 to 3, choosing the side filter above; it arrives as ITEM.DAT +0x15 from the item callers and as the acting unit's own side byte from the map AI

Returns:
  The number of units that matched, 0 when none did. fdps_battle_action_menu tests it for zero to decide whether a battle command has anything to act on.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_class_record and fdps_get_unit_record; owns battle-map and unit-table globals]

Rebuild note:
The maximum reach is a flood fill over the movement grid, not a Manhattan disc: writing abs(dx) + abs(dy) <= range_code selects a different set of tiles wherever an impassable cell (flag bit 0x40) blocks the spread, even though the min_dist cut on the very same call really is Manhattan. The straight-line branch also skips min_dist altogether, so an item with the 0x10 bit set in use_distance can still take its own user as a target however large min_dist is.

=== 000120d0 [PLATE]
Rests one battle-map unit: recovers a fifth of its maximum HP with the white rest flash and REST.WAV, and reports whether the unit was in a state to rest at all.

Algorithm:
Resolves the record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and refuses the rest, returning 0 without touching anything, when current HP (signed word +0x40) already equals maximum HP (signed word +0x42), or when the poison timer at +0x25 or the paralysis timer at +0x26 is running -- the same three-part guard fdps_battle_advance_turn applies to the units it rests at the turn boundary.
Otherwise it plays the rest and then applies it:
  - Sets the map-cursor overlay mode data_fdps_map_cursor_draw_mode to 0, the value at which fdps_draw_map_cursor draws no cursor, and brings the view onto the unit with fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit.
  - Allocates a 0x15180-byte (360x240) scene buffer with malloc, composites the map into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers, then overpaints the resting unit with fdps_blit_unit_sprite(buf, unit_index, 0xff00, 3): blit mode 3 is fdps_blit_rle_recolor and the parameter 0xff00 forces every pixel to palette index 0xff, so the unit shows as a flat white silhouette.
  - Waits out a whole VGA vertical retrace on port 0x3da bit 3 through inp -- spinning first until the bit is set, then until it clears -- and presents the frame with fdps_blit_rect(buf + 0x21d8, 0x168, 0xa0504, 0x140, 0x138, 0xc0): the 312x192 map viewport, from (24,24) of the 360-byte-wide buffer to (4,4) of the mode 13h screen at 0xa0000.
  - Plays REST.WAV through fdps_play_sfx, waits delay(0x28), and frees the buffer.
Then the heal: current HP += maximum HP / 5, a signed IDIV so the fifth is rounded toward zero, clamped down to maximum HP and written back to +0x40 as a word. The 20% figure is the one the game's own instructions quote for resting. Finally data_fdps_map_cursor_draw_mode is set to 1, putting the plain map cursor back, and the result is 1.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr; handed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit and fdps_blit_unit_sprite, and range-checked by none of them. fdps_battle_action_menu passes the unit whose turn it is, from the menu's last command and only when its own fourth argument is 0; fdps_map_actor_behavior_step passes the actor it is stepping, as the last-resort branch of every behaviour mode in which the actor found nothing else to do.

Returns:
  1 -- the unit rested: the flash and sound played and its HP has been raised.
  0 -- the unit was already at full HP, poisoned or paralysed; nothing was drawn, played or changed.
  Neither caller reads the value.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the AIL set and the body hash is unique in the image; both callers and every non-CRT callee are named game code, and the body works on the game's unit-record fields and the REST.WAV asset name]

Rebuild note:
The sequence ends at free() with nothing repainting the view, so the white silhouette is left standing on screen for the caller to clear; it is not a delay(0x28)-long flash. fdps_battle_advance_turn runs the same flash and does call fdps_render_view_frame afterwards, so copying that shape here, or adding the repaint that looks missing, cuts the flash short.

=== 0001222c [EOL]

=== 00012230 [PLATE]
Picks the best physical attack one map-AI actor could make this turn -- the tile to move to and the unit to hit -- and publishes that choice in the AI decision globals.

Algorithm:
Zeroes the attack score global DAT_00063f78 on entry, so a caller reads a fresh score even down the early-return path. Resolves the actor with fdps_get_unit_record and keeps its attack stat (signed word at record +0x48) and its defence stat (signed word at +0x4a). fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot(unit_index, 0) looks for the equipped weapon; with nothing equipped the routine returns 0 at once, leaving the score at 0 and the other three globals holding whatever the previous actor left in them. Otherwise fdps_unit_get_item_id and fdps_get_item_record fetch the weapon's ITEM.DAT record for its reach -- range_min at +0x0b and range_max at +0x0c -- while the actor's tile (bytes +0x00 x, +0x01 y), movement allowance (+0x3b) and class byte (+0x20) come out of the unit record. fdps_get_class_record(class byte + 1) is that class's PROMAP.DAT terrain-cost row, the +1 skipping the default row that sits at index 0.

It then builds the candidate tile set. malloc hands out a 0x64-byte block that is never read and a 0x1900-byte tile buffer (3200 (x, y) byte pairs); fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control(side_select) blocks the opposing units' zones of control, fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range spreads the actor's movement allowance over its class costs, fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles(unit_index, side_select) takes back the tiles other units stand on, fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles copies what is left into the buffer and fdps_map_grid_reset wipes the grid. A third malloc of 0x64 bytes takes the target indices, room for 100, and nothing checks that against the unit count.

For each candidate tile, fdps_collect_targets_in_range gathers the units the weapon would reach from it -- range_code range_max, min_dist range_min, and a select_mode of 1 when side_select is 0 and 0 otherwise, which is what makes the filter pick out the units on the other side -- and the grid is reset again. Each target it finds is scored:
  - damage estimate = the actor's attack stat minus the target's defence stat (+0x4a of the target's record).
  - the score tier is 8 when that estimate is above 2, and 0 when it is not.
  - when the target's current HP (signed word at +0x40) is strictly below the estimate the blow counts as lethal: the estimate doubles and the tier becomes 0x12 (18).
  - fdps_check_can_counter_attack_from_tile(target index, tile x, tile y) returning 1 means the target would strike back from that tile, and the blow it would land comes off the estimate: estimate += the actor's defence stat minus the target's attack stat.
  - a target whose character index (record +0x08) is 0, the protagonist 蘭迪斯, multiplies the estimate by 3/2, so the AI leans on him.
The (tile, target) pair replaces the running best when its tier beats DAT_00063f78, or ties it and its estimate beats the running best estimate. A win writes the tier to DAT_00063f78, the tile to DAT_00063f80 (x) and DAT_00063f84 (y), and the target's unit index to DAT_00063f74; the estimate stays in a local and is never published. All three malloc blocks are freed on the way out.

fdps_map_actor_take_best_action ignores the returned value and reads the globals instead, but fdps_map_actor_behavior_step consumes it as a branch condition: ADD ESP,0x8 / TEST EAX,EAX / JNZ 0x0001015c at 00010149-0001014e. Because the result is always 0 the JNZ is never taken and that caller always falls through to the CALL 0x000120d0 at 00010154. fdps_map_actor_take_best_action weighs DAT_00063f78 against the spell score DAT_00063f88 of fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell and the item score DAT_00063f8c of fdps_map_actor_score_best_item, and needs 6 before it acts on any of them; fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on DAT_00063f78 alone. fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack is the routine that reads the tile and the target back.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the actor whose attack is being weighed. Passed straight through to fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot, fdps_unit_get_item_id and fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles. Both callers forward their own first argument, which reaches them from the phase sweep in fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase or fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase.
  side_select -- which side the actor is on, and so whose zones of control block its move and whose units count as targets: 0 on the enemy phase, 1 on the NPC phase. Passed unchanged to fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control and fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles, and turned into the select_mode of fdps_collect_targets_in_range as (side_select == 0), so an enemy actor looks for every non-zero side and an NPC actor looks for side 0.

Returns:
  0, always, on the no-weapon path and on the normal one alike. The result of the search is the four AI decision globals: DAT_00063f78 the score, DAT_00063f74 the chosen target's unit index, DAT_00063f80 and DAT_00063f84 the tile to attack from.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, hash unique in the image; it calls only in-image game routines and owns the AI decision globals at 0x63f74-0x63f84, with malloc/free used as a consumer of the CRT]

Rebuild note:
What reaches DAT_00063f78 is the coarse tier 0 / 8 / 0x12, not the damage estimate. Publishing the estimate -- the obvious thing, since it is the number the search actually ranks on -- puts a figure in the tens or hundreds onto the same scale as the spell and item scores of 8 and 18, and the AI attacks in preference to everything else it could do. The lethal test is strict, target HP < estimate, so a blow that exactly matches the target's HP is scored as a wound; writing <= for "this kills it" changes which target the AI picks. And fdps_check_can_counter_attack_from_tile returns 1 or -1 and never 0, which is why the counterattack penalty is gated on == 1 -- the natural if (fdps_check_can_counter_attack_from_tile(...)) applies the penalty to every target.

=== 00012550 [PLATE]
Is this unit a flying unit -- one that travels above the terrain instead of on it?

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index), reads the class code from the byte at record+0x20, and returns 1 when it is one of 0x16 (技師), 0x17 (機械伯爵), 0x18 (機械大師), 0x1f (飛兵) or 0x25 (惡靈), otherwise 0. The list is hard-coded here as a comparison chain, not read from the class table: those five are the same classes whose PROMAP.DAT record leaves the sixth terrain column passable, the terrain that can only be flown over. 0x26 (活屍) is deliberately not in the set.

Callers use the answer two ways. The combat resolvers at 0001c520 and 00019f80 skip the attacker's or defender's terrain modifier entirely when it is 1, so a flying unit gets neither the attack nor the defense percentage that fdps_map_load_tile_info's terrain type would select out of DAT_00060040 and DAT_00060058. fdps_spell_damage_unit and fdps_score_targets_for_spell consult it only for spell ids 0x0a and 0x0b, the two ground-shock spells, which fail outright against a flying target.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; whatever fdps_get_unit_record accepts, unchecked here as it is there

Returns:
  1 if the unit's class flies, 0 otherwise.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; only callee is the game function fdps_get_unit_record]

Rebuild note:
The flying set is a hard-coded list of five class codes in this function, not derived from the class record's sixth terrain column in PROMAP.DAT, even though the two agree for the shipped data file. Rewriting it as a lookup of the class record's fly-only terrain cost reads cleaner and gives the same answers today, but it silently makes the data file able to change which classes ignore terrain modifiers and which ones 裂地術 and 封神裂震 can hit -- behaviour the original binary does not have.

=== 000125b4 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs aligning FUN_000125c0 to 16 bytes.

=== 000125c0 [PLATE]
Reports whether one battle unit would strike back at an attacker standing on a given map tile: the same melee counterattack rule as fdps_check_can_counter_attack at 000137e0, but with the attacker named by the tile the blow would come from instead of by a unit index, which is the form the map AI needs before its own unit has moved.

Algorithm:
Resolves the record with fdps_get_unit_record(defender_unit) and rejects at once when the byte at record+0x26 is non-zero. That byte is the paralysis/immobilisation counter: fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome and fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit set it to rand()%2 + 2 when the attacking weapon's ITEM.DAT hit_effect byte is 01 (paralysis), fdps_cast_spell_on_targets clears it together with record+0x25 and record+0x27 on the cure effect, and fdps_battle_system_menu skips a unit whose counter is non-zero when looking for someone who can still act.
Next it takes the Manhattan distance between the unit's own tile -- the bytes at record+0x00 and record+0x01 -- and the passed tile, each delta through abs, and requires the sum to be exactly 1: orthogonal adjacency, so a diagonal never counts.
Then fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot(defender_unit, 0) looks for the slot holding the equipped weapon, and -1, nothing equipped, is a rejection; the slot goes through fdps_unit_get_item_id and fdps_get_item_record, and the ITEM.DAT range_min byte at item record +0x0b must be below 2, so that the weapon can reach an adjacent tile. range_max at +0x0c is never consulted.
Passing all four tests stores 1; each of the four failure paths stores -1, and all five join the single epilogue at 000126a1 that loads the result into EAX.

The sole caller, fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack, asks the question once per (candidate tile, candidate target) pair while scoring where to move: on 1 it adds the acting unit's defence (record+0x4a) minus the target's attack (record+0x48) to that pair's score at 000124a7, so a target that would hit back is worth less unless the actor can absorb the blow. The unit-index twin at 000137e0 is what the fight itself consults, through fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange, to decide whether to replay the exchange with the two roles swapped.

Parameters:
  defender_unit -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, the unit that might counterattack and the subject of every test but the adjacency one; unchecked here, as it is in fdps_get_unit_record. fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack passes an entry of the target list fdps_collect_targets_in_range filled in.
  attacker_x -- map tile x of the tile the attack would come from, in the same 0-based tile units as record+0x00. fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack passes the x of one of the tiles its acting unit can reach, the same pair it hands to fdps_collect_targets_in_range and publishes in DAT_00063f80.
  attacker_y -- map tile y of that same tile, matching record+0x01 and DAT_00063f84.

Returns:
  1 when the unit would counterattack, -1 on every failure -- not 0. The caller tests CMP EAX,1 at 000124a2.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; hash unique in the image, and the body calls four game routines and reads the game's own unit and item record fields]

Rebuild note:
Two traps, both shared with the twin at 000137e0. The result is 1 or -1 and never 0, so the obvious predicate call if (fdps_check_can_counter_attack_from_tile(...)) is true even when no counterattack is allowed. And this test accepts weapon range_min 0 as well as 1 (item record +0x0b < 2) while the otherwise identical twin requires exactly 1, so folding the two into one shared helper, or copying the == 1 across, changes what the map AI predicts for a unit carrying item 0x63 (光束砲), the only weapon-type entry in ITEM.DAT whose range is 0-0.

=== 000126ab [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligns next function to 0x126b0

=== 000126b0 [PLATE]
Map-AI action handler: walks one battle-map actor toward the opposing unit that is nearest to it over walkable terrain, rather than nearest in a straight line.

Algorithm:
fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) supplies the actor's tile -- column at record byte +0, row at +1 -- and its class byte at +0x20. fdps_get_class_record(class_byte) turns that byte into the class record whose first eight bytes are the per-terrain movement costs, and fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range(class_record, x, y, 100) floods the movement grid at DAT_00060144 outward from the actor's tile with a flat allowance of 100 movement points, i.e. as far over the map as the terrain lets the actor walk. No zone-of-control pass runs first, and no fdps_map_grid_reset runs before the fill: the grid is taken to be blank on entry.
fdps_move_path_trace(x, y, target, 0, 0, 2) then runs the tracer's mode 2, which ignores the goal tile it was handed and instead scans unit indices 0 through DAT_00060150-1, keeps the units whose side byte +6 is non-zero and whose status byte +5 has bit 0 clear, takes the one whose tile carries the lowest flooded cost, and writes that unit's column and row into target[0] and target[1]. It returns that cost, or -1 when no such unit sits on a tile the fill reached.
Either way fdps_map_grid_reset then blanks the grid again. On -1 the routine returns 0 and moves nothing. Otherwise, unless the winning tile is the tile the actor already stands on, it sets the map-cursor draw mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so no cursor is painted while the actor walks, parks the cursor on the actor with fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit, and calls fdps_battle_move_unit_toward(target_x, target_y, unit_index, side_select). The tile handed over is the target unit's own occupied tile; fdps_battle_move_unit_toward is what retargets the request to the reachable tile nearest it, so a non-zero result means the actor moved, not that it arrived. DAT_00069cd0 is then set to 1, the ordinary cursor mode, rather than restored to whatever it held on entry.
fdps_map_actor_behavior_step reaches this handler from behavior nibbles 0, 1, 3, 5, 9, 0xa and 0xb, in each case once the handler ahead of it in that nibble's chain has declined the actor; for nibbles 0, 3, 5 and 9 a 0 result falls through to fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent, which does the same job scored by Manhattan distance instead of by path cost.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8. fdps_map_actor_behavior_step forwards the actor it is stepping.
  side_select -- the acting side: 0 from fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase, 1 from fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase. Only forwarded to fdps_battle_move_unit_toward, which passes it on to fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control; the target search does not consult it (see the rebuild note).

Returns:
  1 when fdps_battle_move_unit_toward reported that the actor moved; 0 when no candidate unit stood on a tile the fill reached, when the winning tile is the tile the actor already occupies, or when the move produced no steps. fdps_map_actor_behavior_step reads the 0 as "this handler did not claim the actor" and falls through to the next handler in that nibble's chain.

Pool: fdps  [all callees are game routines; sole caller is fdps_map_actor_behavior_step; no Function ID hit in the watcom or ail sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
Two things here disagree with the neighbouring code and both have to be copied literally. The class record is fetched as fdps_get_class_record(unit[0x20]) with no +1, while fdps_battle_move_unit_toward, FUN_00012230 and fdps_battle_unit_turn all fetch fdps_get_class_record(unit[0x20] + 1) from the same byte of the same record, so this search floods the map with the neighbouring class's terrain costs and can pick a target the move itself would reach differently. And the side filter handed to fdps_move_path_trace is a hard-coded 0, not side_select, so on the NPC phase (side_select 1) the acting unit's own record passes the filter, wins the search with cost 0 on its own tile, and the handler returns 0 having moved nothing. Writing the obvious +1, or the obvious side_select, changes which unit the map AI walks at.

=== 000127c0 [PLATE]
Map-AI action handler: walks one battle-map actor toward the nearest unit of the side opposing it, nearness measured as straight-line tile distance.

Algorithm:
fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) supplies the actor's tile -- column at record byte +0, row at +1. The function then sweeps unit indices 0 through DAT_00060150-1, calling fdps_get_unit_record for each. A unit is a candidate only when the truth value of its side byte at +6 disagrees with side_select (side_select 0 accepts every unit whose side byte is non-zero, any non-zero side_select accepts only side byte 0) and when bit 0 of its flags byte at +5, the retired flag, is clear. The retired test is not open-coded: 00012856..00012884 is an inline expansion of fdps_unit_is_retired (000109b0), which is why fdps_get_unit_record is called a second time for the same index. See rebuild_info/build_flags.md on _inline expansion under -od. Each candidate is scored with the Manhattan distance abs(actor_x - x) + abs(actor_y - y) through the CRT abs, and the running best is replaced only on a strictly smaller distance, so a tie goes to the lower unit index. The search starts from a best distance of 0xffff and a best tile of -1, the sentinel that means nothing was found. The actor is not excluded from the sweep by index; it is excluded only when its own side byte fails the filter. That holds for every dispatcher path -- fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase passes 0 to actors whose side byte is 0, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase passes 1 to actors whose side byte is 1, and fdps_title_demo passes the actor's own side byte -- but not for fdps_icon_script_run, whose side_select is a byte out of the script stream: a value there that agrees with the actor's own side makes the actor its own zero-distance winner and this handler returns 0 without moving, the same dead end the sibling reaches with its hard-coded filter.

With no candidate found it returns 0 and moves nothing. Otherwise, unless the winning tile is the tile the actor already stands on, it sets the map-cursor draw mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 -- a value none of fdps_draw_map_cursor's cases 1 through 5 match, so no cursor is painted while the actor walks -- parks the cursor on the actor with fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit, and calls fdps_battle_move_unit_toward(target_x, target_y, unit_index, side_select). The tile handed over is the opposing unit's own occupied tile; fdps_battle_move_unit_toward is what retargets the request to the reachable tile nearest it, so a non-zero result means the actor moved, not that it arrived. DAT_00069cd0 is then set to 1, the ordinary cursor mode, rather than restored to whatever it held on entry.

Place in the map-AI chain:
fdps_map_actor_behavior_step calls this handler at five points (000100c6, 00010216, 000103ca, 00010568, 000105b2), and at every one of them the instructions just ahead are a call to fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent whose non-zero result jumps past this call. So this is the straight-line fallback the dispatcher tries once the path-cost search has declined the actor; where a 0 from here is not caught by a further handler, the dispatcher rests the actor with fdps_unit_rest (000100d6).

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8. fdps_map_actor_behavior_step forwards the actor it is stepping.
  side_select -- the acting side, used only as a truth value, selecting which side counts as opposing. fdps_map_actor_behavior_step forwards it untouched from its own callers: fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase passes 0, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase passes 1, fdps_title_demo passes the acting unit's own side byte +6, and fdps_icon_script_run passes a byte out of the script stream. Forwarded unchanged to fdps_battle_move_unit_toward, whose only use of it is to hand it on to fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control and fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles.

Returns:
  1 when fdps_battle_move_unit_toward reported that the actor moved; 0 when no opposing unit was found, when the winning tile is the tile the actor already occupies, or when the move produced no steps. fdps_map_actor_behavior_step reads the 0 as "this handler did not claim the actor" and falls through to the next handler in its chain.

Pool: fdps  [game battle logic; no library hit in either fid set]

Rebuild note:
The side filter compares truth values, never side numbers. Side byte +6 is 0 for the enemy side, 1 for neutral and 2 for the player, so the obvious record[6] != own_side is wrong in both directions: it would make neutral units targets for a player-driven actor, and player units targets for a neutral one. The original only ever asks whether the byte is zero.

=== 00012951 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea-form multi-byte NOPs aligning 00012960 to a 16-byte boundary.

=== 00012960 [PLATE]
Runs the enemy side's phase of one battle turn: every enemy unit that can still act has its best spell and its best item scored, and takes its map-AI turn when either score is worth acting on; a second sweep then gives a plain behaviour step to the enemies the score gate turned away.

Algorithm:
First sweep over unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1, re-reading the live unit count at DAT_00060150 every iteration. Each iteration clears the map-cursor overlay mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0, calls fdps_relocate_unit_array to re-seat the unit-record array at DAT_00069cd8 into a freshly allocated block, fetches this index's record with fdps_get_unit_record -- in that order, so the record pointer is taken after the relocation -- and arms the pending chapter-event slot DAT_00069d90 with its 0xff "no event" sentinel. A unit is eligible when its side byte +0x6 is 0 (0 = enemy, 1 = NPC, 2 = player), its flag byte +0x5 is clear of both 0x01 (retired) and 0x80 (already acted this turn), and the immobilising status-ailment byte +0x26 is zero. For an eligible unit it runs fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell(index, 0), which leaves its best spell score in DAT_00063f88, then fdps_map_actor_score_best_item(index, 0), which leaves its best item score in DAT_00063f8c; when either score is 6 or more, signed, it hands the unit to fdps_map_actor_behavior_step(index, 0), which runs that unit's whole AI turn and ends by OR-ing the 0x80 done bit into +0x5 (00010745). Both scores below 6 means the unit does nothing in this sweep.

The second argument is the acting unit's side, 0 for the enemy side: both scorers use it only to decide whether the spell's or the item's target-side byte is inverted before it becomes the side filter, which is what turns effect data authored from the player's point of view around for an enemy actor. fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase, the side-1 sweep, is the same construct with 1 in that position.

The physical-attack scorer fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack is not called here: the gate this phase applies is on the spell and item scores only, and the decision to close on somebody and hit them is left inside fdps_map_actor_behavior_step.

Whether or not the unit acted, if DAT_00069d90 is no longer 0xff the handler it selects out of the chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4 is called with the unit index as its single argument; the current chapter's post-action handler is then called out of the table at 0x0006028c, indexed by the chapter index DAT_00069cf4, with no argument. A non-zero battle-end code left in DAT_00069da0 returns from the function immediately.

Second sweep over the same index range with the same eligibility test, but without the relocation, without the cursor-mode clear and without the scorers: an eligible unit goes straight to fdps_map_actor_behavior_step(index, 0), and the same two dispatches and the same DAT_00069da0 abort check follow it. The units that acted in the first sweep now carry the 0x80 done bit, so this sweep picks up exactly the enemies the score gate passed over, and every enemy ends the phase having had one behaviour step. Enemies that an event handler deploys part-way through either sweep are still reached, because fdps_deploy_unit appends new records at the end of the array and the loop bound is re-read every iteration.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing. Whether the battle ended during the phase is left in DAT_00069da0, which the only caller, fdps_battle_advance_turn, tests immediately on return.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; every callee is game code, and it owns the battle-state globals 0x69cd0/0x69cf4/0x69d90/0x69da0 and the game's own dispatch tables at 0x601c4/0x6028c]

Rebuild note:
fdps_relocate_unit_array moves the unit-record array and erases the copy left behind, so the record pointer has to be re-fetched from fdps_get_unit_record after that call on every iteration, and the loop bound DAT_00060150 has to be re-read at the top of every iteration instead of being hoisted into a local; both loops are written that way. Folding the two sweeps into one shared loop also changes behaviour, because only the first sweep relocates the array, clears DAT_00069cd0 and runs the two scorers.

=== 00012b19 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte NOP (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) + 0x90, aligns next entry to 00012b20

=== 00012b20 [PLATE]
Runs the NPC side's phase of one battle turn: every side-1 unit that can still act takes its map-AI turn, one unit at a time, until the sweep runs out of units or the battle ends.

Algorithm:
Clears the map-cursor overlay mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 (0 = paint no cursor; none of fdps_draw_map_cursor's cases 1 through 5 match it), then sweeps unit indices upward, re-reading the live unit count at DAT_00060150 every iteration. Each iteration clears DAT_00069cd0 again, calls fdps_relocate_unit_array to re-seat the unit-record table at DAT_00069cd8 into a freshly allocated block, fetches this index's record with fdps_get_unit_record, and arms the pending chapter-event slot DAT_00069d90 with its 0xff "no event" sentinel. When the record is an NPC that can still act -- side byte +0x6 == 1 (0 = enemy, 1 = NPC, 2 = player), flag byte +0x5 clear of both 0x01 (retired, tested by fdps_unit_is_retired) and 0x80 (already acted this turn, set by fdps_battle_mark_unit_done), and the immobilising status-ailment byte +0x26 zero -- it hands the unit to fdps_map_actor_behavior_step(index, 1), which runs that unit's whole AI turn; the literal 1 is the acting side, against the literal 0 the twin sweep fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase passes. Then, if the unit's move armed a map event, DAT_00069d90 is no longer 0xff and that handler is called out of the chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4 with the unit index as its single argument; the same table fdps_battle_run_turn_events dispatches through. The current chapter's post-action handler is then called out of the table at 0x0006028c, indexed by the chapter index DAT_00069cf4 and taking no argument, and the sweep stops the moment that handler leaves a non-zero battle-end code in DAT_00069da0.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing. Whether the battle ended during the sweep is left in DAT_00069da0, which the only caller, fdps_battle_advance_turn, tests immediately on return.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; three fdps callees and a single fdps caller, and it owns the game-state globals 0x69cd0/0x69d90/0x69cf4/0x69da0 and the game's own dispatch tables at 0x601c4/0x6028c]

Rebuild note:
fdps_relocate_unit_array wipes the old unit-record table and re-allocates it at a different address on every single iteration, and the chapter event and post-action handlers called inside the loop can deploy reinforcements and grow the unit count at DAT_00060150 -- so the obvious C, hoisting the table base or the unit count into a local before the loop, gives a pointer into wiped memory and a bound that misses units brought on mid-sweep; the record must be re-fetched through fdps_get_unit_record after the fdps_relocate_unit_array call, in that order, every iteration.
