Ghidra's decompilation additionally drops the argument of the chapter-event dispatch (asm 00012bd2-00012bdc pushes the unit index, calls [EDX+0x601c4] and cleans with ADD ESP,0x4, while the decompiled C shows a bare `()`), so a rewrite copied from the decompiler calls the event handler with no unit index -- and the handlers do read it: fdps_chapter_26_event_deploy_waves_2_and_3 refuses to fire unless that unit's side byte is 2. The post-action dispatch at 0x6028c immediately below it genuinely takes no argument (no PUSH before the CALL, no ADD ESP after it), so the two indirect calls in this body do not share a signature.

=== 00012c05 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx, aligning FUN_00012c10 to 16 bytes.

=== 00012c10 [PLATE]
Picks and carries out the single best action for one battle-map actor under AI control, and reports whether it acted.

Algorithm:
Runs the three action scorers in turn, each passed (unit_index, side_select): fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack scores the actor's physical attack and leaves its best score in DAT_00063f78 with the chosen target's unit index in DAT_00063f74; fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell scores the actor's spells and leaves its best score in DAT_00063f88 with the chosen spell id in DAT_00063f90; fdps_map_actor_score_best_item scores the actor's usable items and abilities and leaves its best score in DAT_00063f8c. Each scorer zeroes its own score global on entry, so all three scores are fresh; DAT_00063f74 is not zeroed and is written only when an attack was actually found, at 00012504 inside the "better than the best so far" arm.
It then resolves two unit records through fdps_get_unit_record -- the actor's, and the one named by the attack target index DAT_00063f74 -- and precomputes, unconditionally and before any branch is taken, bit 0x40 of the actor's behaviour byte at record +0x34 and a physical damage estimate: the actor's attack stat (signed word at record +0x48) minus the attack target's defence stat (signed word at record +0x4a). Reading the target record before the threshold test is harmless even when the attack scorer found nothing: the estimate is used only in dispatch case 2 below, which requires the attack and spell scores to be equal and at least one score to have reached 6, so the attack score is 6 or more there and DAT_00063f74 is fresh.
When all three scores are below 6 nothing is done and 0 is returned; the caller fdps_map_actor_behavior_step then falls through to whatever fallback behaviours the actor's mode has -- mode 0 tries fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent, then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent, then fdps_unit_rest; mode 1 drops the second of those; mode 2 retries fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack alone; modes 3, 5 and 9 have their own chains.
Otherwise it dispatches through five comparisons taken in this order, writing A for the attack score, S for the spell score and I for the item score:
  1. A > S and A > I -- fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack moves the actor to the chosen tile and attacks.
  2. A == S and S > I -- the spell id breaks the tie. Below 0x12 the spell's power word (first field of the record fdps_get_spell_record returns) is compared with the physical damage estimate: a larger estimate takes fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, otherwise fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell. At 0x12 and above bit 0x40 decides instead -- set takes move_and_attack, clear takes cast_chosen_spell.
  3. A == I and I > S -- bit 0x40 set takes fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, clear takes fdps_map_actor_use_item.
  4. S > A and I <= S -- fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell.
  5. I > A and I > S -- fdps_map_actor_use_item.
Whichever branch ran, it clears DAT_00069cd0, the map-cursor overlay mode fdps_draw_map_cursor dispatches on, so no cursor is left drawn over the actor, and returns 1.

Behaviour-byte bit 0x40 is never set in the shipped game, so cases 2 and 3 always take their clear-bit arm: at spell id 0x12 and above the spell wins the tie, and an item tied with the attack always wins. Unit record +0x34 is initialised from exactly two places -- byte +0x11 of a map deployment record (fdps_deploy_unit at 0002379d) and the memset to 0 that fdps_build_map_unit_array gives each player-side record -- and across all 63 shipped MAP*.DAT files, 1,676 deployment records, that byte only ever holds 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 or 0x0b: nothing above the low nibble. Every later write to +0x34 anywhere in the image either stores an immediate with bit 0x40 clear (0x7 at 0001039a, 0 at 0003ac74) or is the read-modify-write (old & 0xf0) | n -- 29 inlined copies of it in the chapter event handlers plus fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range itself -- with n one of 0, 3, 4, 0x0a or 0x0b. Nothing can raise the bit. The same holds for bit 0x80, which fdps_score_targets_for_item reads to triple a healing item's weight.

The 0x12 constant in case 2 is not a boundary in the spell table. Spells 0x00..0x11 do carry plain HP power figures (0x11 excepted, whose power is 0), but so do 0x17 and 0x20..0x27; what lies wholly above 0x12 is the status-effect block 0x12..0x18, whose power is 0, and the attack-power-multiplier block 0x19..0x1f, whose power is a negative percentage. The cut is a literal the author chose, and its effect is that above it the tie is decided by a flag that is always clear, so the physical attack never wins it.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, the actor whose turn this is. Reaches here from the phase sweep in fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase or fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase by way of fdps_map_actor_behavior_step, so it is always a live, non-retired unit of the acting side. Passed unchanged to every callee.
  side_select -- which side counts as the opponent: 0 on the enemy phase, 1 on the NPC phase. Passed unchanged to every callee; the scorers use it to pick candidate targets and fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell uses it to flip a spell's target field.

Returns:
  1 when the dispatch was entered, that is when at least one of the three scores reached 6. The caller reads this as "the actor has acted" and stops looking for a fallback behaviour. 0 when all three scores were below 6 and nothing was done.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set, hash unique in the image; it calls only in-image game routines and touches only the game's own AI-decision globals]

Rebuild note:
The dispatch is a chain of five explicit comparisons, not a selection of the maximum. When all three scores are equal and at least one of them reaches 6, every one of the five conditions is false and no action routine runs at all -- yet DAT_00069cd0 is still cleared and 1 is still returned, so the caller believes the actor acted and skips its fallbacks, and the unit stands still for the turn. Writing the obvious "run whichever option scored highest" gives that case an action and changes enemy behaviour.

=== 00012e41 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 15 bytes of Watcom multi-byte NOP forms aligning 00012e50 to a 16-byte boundary.

=== 00012e50 [PLATE]
Map-AI action handler: walks one battle-map actor to the tile the AI scorer picked for it and carries out the melee attack on the target it picked there, counterattack, death scripts and experience award included.

Algorithm:
The tile and the target are not arguments; they arrive in the globals fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack wrote when it scored this actor's options -- the destination tile in DAT_00063f80 (x) and DAT_00063f84 (y), the chosen target's unit index in DAT_00063f74.
1. Clears the map cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so no cursor is painted over the walk, puts the cursor on the actor with fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit, and walks it with fdps_battle_move_unit_toward(DAT_00063f80, DAT_00063f84, unit_index, side_select).
2. Sets cursor mode to 1 (the plain cursor tile of fdps_draw_map_cursor), moves the cursor onto the target, turns the actor to face it with fdps_unit_face_target, and delay(100) holds for a tenth of a second.
3. Clears the pending experience total DAT_00069cec to 0. That global is where the blow-resolution path leaves the experience the exchange earned: on the map branch the accumulator is assigned by fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit itself at 0001ca68 -- an assignment, not an add, from its own figure of defender level * the enemy record's reward at +9 / attacker level (0001ca4c..0001ca66), prorated by damage/hp_max at 0001ca85 when the defender lived -- and on the full-screen branch by fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome at 0001a330. The ADD at 0002854b belongs to fdps_unit_apply_damage, which computes a different formula again and which this path does not reach.
4. DAT_00060010 chooses how the fight is shown. It is the game's animation setting: the third entry of the four-way settings ring fdps_options_menu draws -- music, sound effect, animation, window, entry index 2 -- which toggles it with XOR 1 at 000184bd. fdps_battle_system_submenu copies it into the settings record at +0xe (00015278) for fdps_load_savegame to restore, and fdps_save_game_screen stores it at +0x7 of its own record.
   When it is 0 -- animation off -- the fight is played on the map: cursor mode drops to 0 for one fdps_render_view_frame and goes back to 1; when fdps_check_can_counter_attack(unit_index, target) returns 1 the target is turned to face the actor; fdps_battle_show_combat_gauges(unit_index, target) puts the two HP bars on screen and returns their positions; fdps_unit_attack_target(unit_index, target, gauge_pos) strikes and returns the target's remaining HP. That HP and a second fdps_check_can_counter_attack are each reduced to a 0/1 temporary and ANDed together: when the target survived and may strike back, both units are turned to face each other and fdps_unit_attack_target(target, unit_index, gauge_pos + 2) plays the counterattack -- gauge_pos + 2 is the second of the two screen positions the gauge call returned, +8 bytes along.
   When it is non-zero -- animation on -- the whole exchange is played as the full-screen fight animation fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange(unit_index, target) instead; that routine runs its own counterattack test, so no counterattack is driven from here.
5. fdps_collect_death_scripts gathers the on-death records of every unit the exchange killed into a 12-byte stack buffer, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead plays the deaths out, and fdps_run_death_scripts(DAT_00063f74, count, records) runs those scripts against the target unit, which is what hands it the drops.
6. Scales the pending experience DAT_00069cec by 15/10 (signed, truncating) and passes it to fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up(DAT_00063f74) -- the target, not the actor -- which adds it to that unit's total and runs the level-up sequence once the total reaches 100.

fdps_map_actor_take_best_action dispatches to this function for the attack option, to fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell for the spell option and to fdps_map_actor_use_item for the item option. This is the only one of the three that walks the actor first: the spell handler casts from the tile the unit is already standing on. That is what the move_and_attack half of the name records.

Cursor mode is deliberately left at 1 on the way out; fdps_map_actor_take_best_action clears it to 0 at 00012e26 after the call returns.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8 of the actor taking the action; both callers pass the actor index they are working on.
  side_select -- which side the actor is on: 0 for a unit whose side byte is zero, non-zero for the rest. Only passed through, into fdps_battle_move_unit_toward and from there into fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control, where it decides whose zones of control block the walk.

Returns:
  The constant 1, always. Every call site discards it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game globals and game callers]

Rebuild note:
fdps_check_can_counter_attack returns 1 or -1 and never 0, and both tests here compare it against 1; writing the natural if (fdps_check_can_counter_attack(...)) lets every defender that may not strike back turn round and counterattack. The experience total goes to DAT_00063f74, the unit that was attacked, not to the acting unit -- that is how a player unit earns experience for surviving an enemy turn, and passing unit_index here instead would move the reward to the AI unit. The animation setting is tested here as a byte against 0 (CMP byte ptr / JNZ at 00012ecc) while fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell zero-extends the same byte and tests it against 1 at 00013d72; the menu only ever writes 0 or 1 so the two agree in play, but they were not written the same way and folding them into one shared helper is a behaviour change, not a tidy-up.

=== 0001303b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] / mov ecx,ecx to 16-byte boundary at 00013040

=== 00013040 [PLATE]
Scores every usable item in one map-AI unit's bag over every tile it could use it on, and leaves the best (bag slot, aim tile, score) in the AI item-decision globals.

Algorithm:
Clears the best score DAT_00063f8c, then calls fdps_get_class_record(0) and reads the unit's current MP from the signed word at record+0x44 -- both land in locals ([EBP-0x4c] and [EBP-0xc]) that are never read again. They are template leftovers, not a lost feature: fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell opens with the identical three steps and uses both, the class-0 record as the all-costs-1 movement table it hands to fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range (0001350b) and the MP word as what each spell's cost byte is weighed against (000134ee). Items cost no MP, and this routine gets its candidate tiles from a target sweep rather than a flood fill, so neither value has any work left to do here.

Resolves the acting unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and keeps its tile from record bytes +0 (x) and +1 (y), allocates a 0x190-byte scratch buffer for candidate tiles with malloc, and asks fdps_unit_item_count how many of the unit's eight bag slots are filled. A count of 0 returns straight away, which leaves that buffer allocated.

For each bag slot 0..count-1 it reads the item id from unit record byte 0xb + slot*2 and fetches the ITEM.DAT record with fdps_get_item_record. An item whose use_effect byte (record+0x0d) is 0 cannot be used and is skipped. The use_distance byte (record+0x10) carries the reach in its low nibble and the straight-line shape in bit 0x10: above 0x0f the aim search runs with reach 1 and minimum distance 1, so the candidate aim tiles of a line item are its passable orthogonal neighbours -- the reach is a terrain-blocked flood fill, not a Manhattan disc; otherwise the reach is use_distance itself and the minimum distance 0, which keeps the actor's own tile in the candidate set. fdps_collect_targets_in_range paints that reach into the map working grid with a NULL output array, fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles copies the marked tiles into the scratch buffer as (x, y) byte pairs, and fdps_map_grid_reset wipes the grid again.

For every one of those aim tiles it then works out the side filter. The item's use_target byte (record+0x11) is authored from the player's viewpoint, and fdps_collect_targets_in_range's select_mode reads 0 = side 0 (enemies), 1 = every non-zero side, 2 = side 1 (guest NPC), 3 = side 2 (the player's party). With side_select 0 -- the enemy phase -- use_target is inverted, 0 becoming 1 and anything else 0, so a damage item aims at everything that is not the enemy side and a support item at the actor's own side; with a non-zero side_select -- the NPC phase -- use_target is taken as it stands. fdps_map_actor_use_item repeats the identical inversion at 000271ea when it carries the choice out.

use_distance is reloaded from the record for the shape test: below 0x10 the affected units come from fdps_collect_targets_in_range over the item's use_radius (record+0x12) centred on the aim tile, at 0x10 and above from fdps_collect_targets_in_line swept from the unit's own tile toward the aim tile for use_distance - 0x10 tiles. Either collector writes the matching unit indices, one byte each, into a stack scratch at [EBP-0x70] with 0x20 bytes of room before the next local, and neither of them bounds-checks it. The grid is reset again, and when the target list is not empty fdps_score_targets_for_item scores the item against it.

A score strictly above the running best replaces it: DAT_00063f8c takes the score, DAT_00063f98 the aim tile x, DAT_00063f94 the aim tile y and DAT_00063f7c the bag slot. After the last slot the scratch buffer is freed. fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase, fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and fdps_map_actor_take_best_action read DAT_00063f8c back and treat 6 or more, signed, as worth acting on; fdps_map_actor_use_item carries the chosen item use out from the same four globals.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit array at DAT_00069cd8; passed on to fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_unit_item_count
  side_select -- the side the acting unit fights on, 0 on the enemy phase and 1 on the NPC phase; the only thing it changes is whether the item's use_target byte is mirrored before it becomes the side filter of the target collectors. fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase passes 0, the NPC phase reaches it with 1 through fdps_map_actor_behavior_step, and fdps_map_actor_take_best_action forwards its own side_select to this scorer and to its two siblings

Returns:
  Always 0, on the empty-bag path and on the normal one alike. Every caller ignores it; the result of the search is the four globals.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls and is called by game code, malloc/free are the only runtime calls]

Rebuild note:
The bag walk uses its loop counter directly as the bag slot index -- item id at unit record +0xb + slot*2 -- and never re-tests the +0xa empty bit that fdps_unit_item_count counted with, so it assumes the eight slots are packed. Writing the obvious defensive loop, walk all eight slots and skip the empty ones, picks a different item set and stores a different DAT_00063f7c the moment a bag has a hole in it. The use_distance byte is the second trap: the aim-tile search clamps it to reach 1 with minimum distance 1 for line items, and the raw value is reloaded from the record before the shape test, so keeping the clamped value in one variable takes the wrong branch. The 0x190-byte buffer is also leaked when the unit's bag is empty, because the early return sits between the malloc and the free.

=== 000132a6 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6-byte nop) + lea edx,[edx+0] (4-byte nop), aligns FUN_000132b0 to 16 bytes

=== 000132b0 [PLATE]
Scores one usable item against a list of candidate target units, so the map AI can weigh using that item against its other options.

Algorithm:
Fetches the item's ITEM.DAT record with fdps_get_item_record(item_id), keeps the use_amount word at record+0x0e sign-extended, and dispatches on the use_effect byte at record+0x0d; any code other than the two below is scored 0.
For use_effect 0x0b -- the four HP restoratives 藥草, 回復劑, 再生藥 and 神聖之水 -- it walks target_unit_indices[0 .. target_count-1], resolves each byte with fdps_get_unit_record, and reads the unit's current HP (record+0x40) and maximum HP (record+0x42) as signed words: 8 points when current HP is at or below max/3, 3 points when it is at or below max/2, otherwise 0 -- the more hurt the target, the more the heal is worth. That per-target score is then tripled when bit 0x80 of the AI behaviour byte at record+0x34 is set. The item's own use_amount, the amount it would actually restore, is never consulted, so all four restoratives score alike.
For use_effect 0x1e -- the two line-shaped damage items 光束砲 (use_amount 9999) and 火焰 (use_amount 300) -- it walks the same list and scores 8 when the target's current HP (record+0x40, read here as an unsigned word) is still above the item's use_amount, and 0x12 (18) when it is at or below it, so a hit that finishes the target outweighs one that only wounds it. Because 光束砲's use_amount of 9999 is above any HP total in the game, every one of its targets takes the kill score of 0x12.
The per-target scores are summed and the total returned.

Parameters:
  item_id -- ITEM.DAT item id, 0x00-0xe1. fdps_map_actor_score_best_item takes it from the acting unit's bag (unit record +0x0b, two bytes per slot) and only calls here for items whose use_effect byte is non-zero.
  target_count -- number of entries in target_unit_indices; the count the caller's target collector returned for the candidate aim tile.
  target_unit_indices -- array of target_count battle unit indices, one byte each, indexing the 0x50-byte unit records fdps_get_unit_record resolves.

Returns:
  The summed desirability of using this item on those targets; 0 for every use_effect code the AI does not weigh, which is every code but 0x0b and 0x1e. fdps_map_actor_score_best_item keeps the largest total seen in DAT_00063f8c along with the aim tile and bag slot that produced it, and fdps_map_actor_take_best_action treats 6 or more as worth acting on.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game routines fdps_get_item_record and fdps_get_unit_record and indexes game item/unit record fields; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The two branches read the same current-HP word at unit record+0x40 with different signedness -- MOVSX in the heal branch (00013329), MOV AX + AND 0xffff in the damage branch (000133dc) -- while the item's use_amount at +0x0e is always sign-extended (MOVSX at 000132d5). Declaring HP once as a signed short and writing both comparisons as plain field accesses reproduces the heal branch but not the damage branch: a negative HP would score 0x12 (killed) instead of 8 (wounded). The damage branch has to compare (unsigned short)hp against the signed use_amount.

=== 00013412 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov eax,eax (14 bytes to 16-byte boundary)

=== 00013420 [PLATE]
Picks the best spell one map-AI actor could cast this turn, together with the tile to centre it on, and publishes that choice in the AI decision globals.

Algorithm:
Zeroes the best-score global DAT_00063f88 on entry, so a caller always reads a fresh score even down the early-return paths. Fetches fdps_get_class_record(0) once -- record 0 of PROMAP.DAT, the default row whose eight terrain costs are all 1 (the table is indexed by class code + 1, and slot 0 is the all-1 row the calls that are not about a particular unit pass 0 for) -- and the actor's record through fdps_get_unit_record, keeping the actor's tile from record bytes +0x00 (x) and +0x01 (y) and its current MP from the signed word at +0x44. fdps_unit_collect_known_spells then expands the actor's 40-bit learned-spell mask at record +0x1a into a 20-byte stack list and returns how many ids it wrote. The routine returns at once, with the score left at 0, when the actor knows no spells or when the byte at record +0x27 is non-zero -- that is the status timer the ailment routine assigns to ailment id 0x11, spell 封魔咒術, so a sealed caster is skipped.

Otherwise it allocates a 0x190-byte tile buffer (200 (x, y) byte pairs) with malloc, without checking the result, and walks the known-spell list:
  - fdps_get_spell_record resolves the 7-byte MAGICDAT.DAT record for the id. The spell is skipped when its MP cost, byte +0x05, is above the actor's current MP.
  - fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range spreads out of the actor's tile over that all-1 cost table with the spell's distance byte +0x03 as its movement points, so the cast range is counted in walkable tiles and walls cut it short; fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles copies the tiles it reached into the buffer and fdps_map_grid_reset wipes the grid again. The actor's own tile is one of the candidates, and a distance of 0 leaves it as the only one. The byte goes in raw, including the 0x10 straight-line flag it can carry -- see the rebuild note.
  - For each candidate tile, fdps_collect_targets_in_range gathers the units the spell would catch when centred there, with the spell's radius byte +0x04 as its range_code, a min_dist of 0, and a select_mode derived from the spell's target byte +0x06: forwarded unchanged when side_select is non-zero, and inverted to (byte +0x06 == 0 ? 1 : 0) when side_select is 0, which is what turns a spell authored from the player's point of view around for an enemy caster. Across the 40 MAGICDAT.DAT records that byte holds only 0, 1 and -- on 0x16 神行術 alone -- 3, so the enemy phase can only produce select_mode 0 or 1 here and the NPC phase 0, 1 or 3; this routine never produces fdps_collect_targets_in_range's select_mode 2. The indices land in a 32-byte stack buffer and the grid is reset once more.
  - When that catches at least one unit, fdps_score_targets_for_spell scores the spell against them. The (spell, tile) pair replaces the running best when its score beats DAT_00063f88, or when the score equals it and the spell's power -- the signed word at record +0x00 -- beats the power of the current best. Power is signed and the eight 絕招 store it as a negative attack multiplier, so on a tie an ordinary spell always outranks a 絕招. A win writes the score to DAT_00063f88, the tile to DAT_00063f9c (x) and DAT_00063fa0 (y), and the spell id to DAT_00063f90.
The tile buffer is freed on the way out.

All three callers ignore the returned value and read the globals instead. Program-wide, DAT_00063f88 is written nowhere but here, and DAT_00063f90/DAT_00063f9c/DAT_00063fa0 are read only by fdps_map_actor_take_best_action and fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell, on paths that all require DAT_00063f88 >= 6: fdps_map_actor_behavior_step gates at 00010693, fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell re-checks at 00013cd9 before touching the tile globals, and every arm of fdps_map_actor_take_best_action that reads DAT_00063f90 has already established that DAT_00063f88 is the largest of the three action scores and that one of them reaches 6.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, naming the actor whose spells are being weighed. fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase passes its sweep index; fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and fdps_map_actor_take_best_action pass their own first argument straight through.
  side_select -- which side the actor is on, and so whose units its spells should look for. 0 means the actor is enemy-side and every spell's target byte is inverted; non-zero means the byte is used as authored, and the NPC phase reaches this with 1. The inversion is a boolean one, not a side swap, so the target byte of 3 that 0x16 神行術 carries comes out as 0 -- the same value a byte of 1 gives -- for an enemy caster.

Returns:
  0, always. The result of the search is the four AI decision globals: DAT_00063f88 the best score, DAT_00063f90 the chosen spell id, DAT_00063f9c and DAT_00063fa0 the tile to centre the cast on.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, hash unique in the image; it calls fdps_get_class_record / fdps_get_unit_record / fdps_unit_collect_known_spells and writes the AI decision globals its callers read back, and malloc/free are used as a consumer of the CRT]

Rebuild note:
The cast-range argument is the raw distance byte. That field carries the straight-line flag 0x10 in its top nibble with the reach in the low nibble, and the player's own targeting path decodes it -- fdps_battle_spell_command reads the same byte at 00027dbf, hands it to fdps_collect_targets_in_range as range_code, and tests it against 0xf at 00027e46 -- but this routine does not, so for the four records that set the flag the AI flood-fills 0x14, 0x17 or 0x1f movement points instead of tracing a line. The 0x190-byte tile buffer is sized for the decoded range and nothing else: the largest ordinary distance in MAGICDAT.DAT is 9, a 9-step diamond is at most 2*9*9 + 2*9 + 1 = 181 tiles, and fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles writes one pair per reached tile with no bound check whatever.

The 20-byte known-spell list at [EBP-0x5c] is unbounded in the same way and by a wider margin. fdps_unit_collect_known_spells (00027840) walks a 5-byte bitmap at record +0x1a, eight bits each, and writes one id byte per set bit with no cap, so a unit with more than 20 spells learned overruns the frame array -- which sits directly below the 32-byte target-index array at [EBP-0x7c] in the same frame.

The equal-score tie-break at 0001360a reads a stack slot ([EBP-0x8]) that nothing has written yet, because the current best's power is only stored inside the branch that accepts a new best. It is real but it cannot be observed: DAT_00063f88 starts at 0 and never decreases, the tie branch leaves it unchanged, so the garbage is only ever consulted while the best score is still 0; the first candidate that scores above 0 is taken through the JG path, which does not read that slot and does write it, and everything from there on is deterministic. So the slot can only change which spell id and tile are left in DAT_00063f90/9c/a0 on runs whose best score ends at 0, and every consumer of those globals is gated on DAT_00063f88 >= 6. Initialising that variable in the rebuild is therefore safe.

=== 0001366a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea eax,[eax+0x0] NOP form between FUN_00013420 and FUN_00013670

=== 00013670 [PLATE]
Collects the battle units standing on the straight line that a line-shaped item or spell effect sweeps out from the acting unit's tile toward the tile the player or the map AI is aiming at, and returns how many there are.

Algorithm:
Reads the map dimensions from the working-grid header at DAT_00060144 (signed word tile width at +0, signed word tile height at +2) and turns both into pixel extents by multiplying by the 0x18 tile size. Picks one orthogonal step: when origin_x == aim_x the step is (0, +/-0x18) taken from the sign of aim_y - origin_y, otherwise it is (+/-0x18, 0) taken from the sign of aim_x - origin_x, and on that second branch any difference in y is discarded, so the walk is never diagonal. Saves the global map cursor position DAT_00069cd4 (x in pixels) and DAT_00069ccc (y in pixels), points it at origin_x * 0x18, origin_y * 0x18, then repeats line_length times: adds the step to the two globals and, while the cursor is still inside the map extents (0 <= x < width * 0x18 and 0 <= y < height * 0x18), asks fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor which unit stands on that tile. Those two globals are the only channel into the finder, which takes no arguments and reads them itself, and that is why this routine drives them and then puts them back.

An index other than -1 is resolved with fdps_get_unit_record and kept when the side byte at record +6 agrees with select_enemy_side: zero keeps the records whose side byte is non-zero (guest NPC side 1 and the player's party side 2), non-zero keeps the records whose side byte is 0 (the enemy side). Every kept index is appended to out_indices as one byte, truncated from the int the finder returned. Nothing else is tested here. The retired-unit filter that the sibling collectors apply for themselves -- bit 0 of record byte +5 -- is already applied inside fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor, which calls fdps_unit_is_retired at 0002db22, so a retired unit standing on the line is never reported to this body at all.

The step is applied before the test, so the origin tile itself is never examined. That is not observable: the origin holds the acting unit, and in every reachable call the filter excludes that unit's own side -- the two player callers pass 1 while their caster is side 1 or 2, the enemy-side map actor passes 0 while it is side 0, and the NPC-side map actor passes 5 while it is side 1. A tile outside the map is skipped rather than ending the loop, which is likewise not observable, because the step is constant and the walk can never re-enter the map once it has left. Both cursor globals are restored before the count of written indices is returned.

Callers and data:
fdps_battle_item_menu and fdps_battle_spell_command are the player's two paths, and both pass select_enemy_side as the literal 1 (PUSH 0x1 at 00025516 and 00027e5f). fdps_map_actor_score_best_item and fdps_map_actor_use_item are the map AI's two, and both derive it as side_select ? use_target : (use_target == 0), at 0001319c-000131c5 and 000271ea-0002720b.
The line shape and its length come from one byte carrying the same encoding in two different tables: ITEM.DAT use_distance +0x10 on the three item paths, and MAGICDAT.DAT distance +0x03 on the spell path (fdps_get_spell_record at 00027d9c, byte +3 read at 00027dbf). Bit 0x10 marks the straight line and the low nibble carries the reach. Every caller gates on that byte being above 0x0f and passes the byte minus 0x10 as line_length. The shipped data holds three such items -- 0x63 光束砲 and 0xc7 火焰 at 14 tiles, 0xbe 高能量砲 at 6 -- and four such spells -- 0x19 魔龍霸炎 and 0x1a 強力衝擊 at 7, 0x1f 靈彈超必殺 at 4, 0x23 聖龍烈霸斬 at 15. All three items carry use_target 5, and the map AI's spell scorer fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell never calls this routine, so a line-shaped spell is a player-only ability.

Parameters:
  aim_x -- column of the tile the line is aimed at, 0-based. Only its direction from the origin is used, never its distance. fdps_battle_item_menu and fdps_battle_spell_command pass the live map cursor DAT_00069cd4 / 0x18, which the player is free to place diagonally; fdps_map_actor_score_best_item passes each candidate tile of its aim search in turn and fdps_map_actor_use_item passes the chosen target tile global DAT_00063f98, and both of those are orthogonal neighbours of the origin.
  aim_y -- row of that tile, 0-based, from DAT_00069ccc / 0x18 or from DAT_00063f94.
  out_indices -- caller-supplied byte array that receives one unit index per unit found. Every caller passes a small stack buffer, and neither its length nor a NULL is checked.
  origin_x -- column of the tile the line starts from, 0-based; the acting unit's record byte +0. The first tile examined is one step beyond it.
  origin_y -- row of that tile, 0-based; the acting unit's record byte +1.
  line_length -- how many tiles the line covers, counted from the tile next to the origin; the use_distance or distance byte above, minus 0x10.
  select_enemy_side -- which side of the battle to keep: non-zero keeps side 0, the enemy side, and zero keeps the two non-zero sides. The reachable values are 0, 1 and 5, and each selects the correct side for the caller that produces it. It is not the four-way select_mode enum of fdps_collect_targets_in_range and fdps_collect_targets_in_area, and on the two values they have in common it runs the opposite way round.

Returns:
  The number of unit indices written to out_indices, 0 when the line reached nobody.

Pool: fdps  [calls only game functions and shares the battle cursor state; no Function ID hit in either library set and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
select_enemy_side runs the opposite way round from the select_mode of the sibling collectors, which the same callers feed from the same source byte, so writing the family's "0 means the enemy side" test makes every line-shaped attack sweep the caster's own side instead. The walk is also strictly axis-priority: unless origin_x equals aim_x it goes horizontal and discards the y difference entirely, so deriving the step from the sign of both deltas draws a diagonal the original never draws. That one is reachable in play, because on the player's two paths the aim tile is the free-moving map cursor rather than an orthogonal neighbour chosen by the AI.

=== 000137de [EOL]
Alignment padding: mov eax,eax (8b c0) between FUN_00013670 and FUN_000137e0.

=== 000137e0 [PLATE]
Reports whether the defender may strike back after one unit attacks another on the battle map.

Algorithm:
Resolves both units through fdps_get_unit_record and applies four tests, returning -1 the moment one of them fails.
1. The defender's immobilising status byte at record +0x26 must be 0, so a disabled unit never counters.
2. The two units must stand on orthogonally adjacent tiles: the tile coordinate bytes at record +0x00 (x) and +0x01 (y) of both units give two deltas, each zero-extended from a byte and passed through the runtime abs, and their sum must be exactly 1.
3. fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot(defender_unit, 0) must find a slot holding an equipped weapon; it hands back -1 when the defender wears none.
4. The item in that slot, resolved with fdps_unit_get_item_id and fdps_get_item_record, must have range_min -- the ITEM.DAT byte at +0x0b -- equal to 1, so its reach covers an adjacent tile. Weapons whose range starts at 2, the bows and the cannons, therefore never counter, while 1-2 and 1-3 weapons do. range_max at +0x0c is never read.
Passing all four returns 1. Nothing about the attacker beyond its tile position is examined.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, the unit that just attacked; only its x/y bytes are read.
  defender_unit -- index into the same array, the unit that was attacked and the subject of every test but the adjacency one. fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack passes the map-AI's current target held in DAT_00063f74.

Returns:
  1 when the defender may counterattack, -1 in every other case. All six call sites, in four callers, compare the result against 1 explicitly.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record twice and operates on game unit records; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The result is 1 or -1 and never 0, so the natural C test "if (fdps_check_can_counter_attack(a, b))" is true even when no counterattack is allowed; every caller has to compare against 1. The weapon test is also range_min == 1 exactly rather than the in-range test range_min <= 1 <= range_max: fdps_check_can_counter_attack_from_tile, which is otherwise the same rule stated against a tile instead of a second unit, writes it as range_min <= 1, and folding the two into one helper would let a weapon whose range_min is 0 (光束砲, item 0x63, range 0-0) counterattack.

=== 000138e1 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / lea eax,[eax+0]

=== 000138f0 [PLATE]
Marks one unit as retired, taking it out of the battle for good.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit's record through fdps_get_unit_record (the 0x50-byte array based at DAT_00069cd8) and stores 1 into the status byte at record + 5. Bit 0 of that byte is the retired flag that fdps_unit_is_retired reads back. The store is a whole-byte assignment rather than a bit set, so it also clears bit 7 of the same byte -- the acted-this-turn flag that fdps_battle_mark_unit_done raises and fdps_units_clear_status_bit7 clears when a new turn opens. No other field of the record is touched and unit_index is not range-checked. The same two-step idiom appears inline elsewhere: fdps_map_actor_behavior_step retires a mode 7 actor this way at 000104b8, and fdps_chapter_23_end runs it at 0003b39f over every unit whose side byte +6 is 1 to clear the enemy side at the end of that scene. A sweep for the exact encoding c6 40 05 01 finds ten sites besides this function: 000104b8 fdps_map_actor_behavior_step, 0001d7f9 fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, 00022d36 fdps_build_map_unit_array, 00037724 fdps_chapter_08_event_villager_escapes, 00037c69 and 00037c7f fdps_chapter_15_event_boss_defeat, 00038c5b fdps_chapter_23_event_give_martial_artist_ring, 0003b064 fdps_chapter_19_post_action, 0003b39f fdps_chapter_23_end, 0003b5b9 fdps_chapter_24_post_action.

Nothing in the image calls this function or takes its address; it is compiled in but unreferenced.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, the same index fdps_get_unit_record takes; valid range 0 .. DAT_00060150 - 1, unchecked here and in the callee.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; the sole callee is the game symbol fdps_get_unit_record, which a compiled crt or ail object could not reference]

Rebuild note:
Retiring a unit assigns the whole status byte -- record[5] = 1 -- it does not OR bit 0 in. Writing the obvious record[5] |= 1, by analogy with fdps_battle_mark_unit_done which does OR 0x80 into the same byte, would leave the acted-this-turn flag (bit 7) standing on a retired unit instead of clearing it. The same assignment idiom is repeated inline in fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and in the chapter scene handlers, so getting it wrong here means getting it wrong in ten other places too.

=== 00013919 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (8d 80 00 00 00 00) + nop, aligning next function to 0x13920.

=== 00013920 [PLATE]
Scores one spell against a list of candidate target units, so the map AI can weigh casting that spell against its other options.

Algorithm:
Fetches the spell's MAGICDAT.DAT record with fdps_get_spell_record and keeps the signed word at record +0x00, the spell's damage figure. It then takes one branch per spell family, each summing a per-target score over target_unit_indices[0 .. target_count-1] with every unit resolved through fdps_get_unit_record:
  - healing spells, ids 0x0e-0x10 (恢復之光 / 治癒之風 / 痊癒之泉) and 0x21 (鎮魂之歌): 8 when the target's current HP at record +0x40 is below max HP (+0x42) / 3, 3 when it is below max HP / 2, otherwise 0; that score is doubled when bit 0 of the behaviour byte at +0x34 is set.
  - 0x11 封魔咒術: 6 for each target that knows at least one spell -- fdps_unit_collect_known_spells is called with a NULL output buffer, which asks it for the count only -- and is not already sealed, i.e. the status byte at +0x27 is 0.
  - 0x12 腐毒術: fdps_score_targets_without_status over status byte +0x25, 10 per target not already poisoned.
  - 0x13 麻痺術: the same over +0x26, 10 per target not already paralysed.
  - 0x14 神之祝福: fdps_score_targets_without_status three times, over the buff bytes +0x22, +0x23 and +0x24 at 4 per target, but each call's result is assigned over the previous one, so only the +0x24 pass reaches the total. See the rebuild note.
  - 0x18 甦癒術: 6 for each target already carrying one of the three ailments at +0x25, +0x26 or +0x27.
  - every other id, the damaging spells: 0x18 (24) when the target's current HP at +0x40 is below the spell's damage figure, i.e. the cast would kill it, and 8 otherwise; that score is then multiplied by the 1.5 stored at 0x00061571 and truncated back to an int through __CHP whenever the target's character index at record +0x08 is 0, which is 蘭迪斯, so the AI leans on the protagonist. Targets of the two ground-shaking spells 0x0a 裂地術 and 0x0b 封神裂震 are skipped entirely when fdps_unit_is_flying reports the unit is airborne. Spells whose damage word is negative (MAGICDAT.DAT stores the AP multiplier spells as a negated percentage) can never satisfy the kill test, so each of their targets scores the flat 8.
The accumulated total is returned.

Parameters:
  spell_id -- MAGICDAT.DAT spell id, 0x00-0x27. fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell passes each id of the caster's known-spell candidate list in turn.
  target_count -- how many entries of target_unit_indices to score, 0 or more. fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell passes the count fdps_collect_targets_in_range returned for this spell.
  target_unit_indices -- array of target_count byte unit indices into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, filled by fdps_collect_targets_in_range.

Returns:
  The summed desirability of casting this spell over that target set. Higher is better and 0 means there is nothing worth hitting; fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell keeps the highest score it has seen in DAT_00063f88 and records the winning spell id in DAT_00063f90.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game symbols fdps_get_spell_record, fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_unit_collect_known_spells and reads unit-record fields defined only by the game's own layout; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The 0x14 神之祝福 branch assigns the result of each of its three fdps_score_targets_without_status calls to the same total, so the +0x22 and +0x23 passes are computed and thrown away and only the +0x24 pass counts. Writing the obvious total += ... for the three calls trebles that spell's score and changes which spell the map AI picks; keep the three plain assignments.

The current-HP word at record +0x40 is widened with OPPOSITE signedness in the two arms that read it: the healing arm zero extends it -- XOR EAX,EAX / MOV AX at 00013996 -- while the damaging arm sign extends it -- MOVSX at 00013bce. Maximum HP at +0x42 is zero extended alongside the first, at 000139a4. Reading hp_current as the signed short the unit record declares in both places reproduces the damaging arm and breaks the healing one: a unit whose HP word had gone negative would look like the most hurt thing on the map to a healer, where the original sees 65535 and scores it 0. Keep the healing arm's unsigned cast.

=== 00013c1c [EOL]
4-byte Watcom alignment filler (8d 44 20 00, lea eax,[eax+eiz*1+0x0]) aligning FUN_00013c20 to 4/16.

=== 00013c20 [PLATE]
Scores a list of battle targets for a status-effect spell: adds a fixed per-target score for every target that is not already carrying the effect.

Algorithm:
Zeroes the running total, then loops i from 0 while i < target_count (signed, so a non-positive count returns 0 without touching the array). Each pass takes the byte target_ids[i] as a unit index, resolves the 0x50-byte unit record with fdps_get_unit_record, and tests the single byte at record + status_offset. Those bytes are the unit record's six status-effect timers at +0x22..+0x27, each holding the number of turns the effect still has to run: +0x22, +0x23 and +0x24 are the three 神之祝福 buff slots -- fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats scales attack by 1.15 while +0x22 runs, defence by 1.15 while +0x23 runs, and adds a flat 15 to the dexterity seed that feeds both hit and evade while +0x24 runs -- and +0x25, +0x26 and +0x27 are poison, paralysis and spell-seal, the slots fdps_unit_apply_status_effect writes for spell ids 0x12, 0x13 and 0x11. A zero byte means that effect is not running on the unit. Every target whose byte is zero adds score_per_target to the total; targets that already carry the effect add nothing. Neither the unit index nor the resulting pointer is checked, because fdps_get_unit_record checks neither.

Parameters:
  target_count -- number of entries in target_ids; fdps_score_targets_for_spell passes through the target-list length it was given.
  target_ids -- array of target_count unit indices, one byte each, into the record array based at 00069cd8; fdps_score_targets_for_spell passes its own target-id array unchanged.
  status_offset -- byte offset of the status-effect timer inside the unit record. fdps_score_targets_for_spell passes 0x25 for spell id 0x12 (腐毒術), 0x26 for spell id 0x13 (麻痺術), and 0x22, 0x23 then 0x24 for spell id 0x14 (神之祝福).
  score_per_target -- points contributed by one target that does not yet carry the effect: 0x0a for the two ailment spells, 4 for each of the blessing's three buff slots.

Returns:
  score_per_target multiplied by the number of targets whose status byte is zero; 0 when every target already carries the effect, and 0 for a non-positive target_count.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; its only callee is the game function fdps_get_unit_record and its only caller is game code]

Rebuild note:
The three calls in fdps_score_targets_for_spell's spell-id 0x14 (神之祝福) branch (00013b32, 00013b49, 00013b60) each store this function's result with MOV, not ADD, into the same accumulator at [EBP-0x14], so the scores for offsets 0x22 and 0x23 are computed and discarded and only 0x24 survives. Writing the obvious 'score += fdps_score_targets_without_status(...)' three times reproduces neither the original C nor the original scoring: the blessing's worth would treble and the map AI would choose that spell far more often.

=== 00013c88 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] (6-byte nop) + mov edx,edx (2-byte nop), aligning FUN_00013c90 to 16 bytes.

=== 00013c90 [PLATE]
Carries out the spell action the map AI's spell scorer chose for one actor: plays the cast over the battle map, applies it, and runs whatever the units it killed had scripted.

Algorithm:
Reads the chosen spell's record with fdps_get_spell_record(DAT_00063f90), the spell id fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell left behind at 00013635. From the record's byte +6 it derives the side filter it will hand to fdps_collect_targets_in_range: when side_select is 0 -- the enemy phase -- the filter is the inverted flag (rec[6] == 0), which turns a spell authored to hit side 0 into one that hits every non-zero side and collapses any other authored value to 0, so an enemy caster aims a player-facing spell at the player and a friendly-facing one at its own side; when side_select is non-zero -- the NPC phase, whose units are already on the player's side -- rec[6] is used unchanged.
It then gates on the spell score DAT_00063f88 that the same scorer left: below 6 it does nothing at all and returns 0.
Otherwise it puts the map cursor on the actor's own tile through fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit, and collects the units the spell reaches from the target tile the scorer chose (DAT_00063f9c, DAT_00063fa0) into a 32-byte stack array -- fdps_collect_targets_in_range with the spell record's reach byte +4 as range_code, min_dist 0 and the side filter above -- then wipes the working grid again with fdps_map_grid_reset, which is the contract every caller of that collector keeps.
It shows the area of effect while the cursor travels: DAT_00069cd0, the cursor overlay mode fdps_draw_map_cursor dispatches on, is set to rec[4] + 2, so reaches 1, 2 and 3 give that routine's radius-1, radius-2 and radius-3 diamonds (modes 3, 4, 5); fdps_map_cursor_move_to animates the cursor to the target tile scaled by the 0x18-pixel tile size, delay(200) holds it there, the mode is cleared again and fdps_render_view_frame paints one frame.
The cast itself goes one of two ways on DAT_00060010, the animation setting: the third of the four on/off entries of the settings ring fdps_options_menu draws (music, sound, animation, window), toggled there with XOR 1 at 000184bd, persisted by fdps_battle_system_submenu into the settings record at +0x0e and by fdps_save_game_screen at +0xa07 of the save image. Exactly 1 -- animation on -- plays the full-screen combat presentation through fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets; any other value runs the effect on the map through fdps_cast_spell_on_targets. Both are called as (unit_index, DAT_00063f90, target_count, targets). Only this function and fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack read that byte for behaviour: the player's own commands, fdps_battle_spell_command among them, never consult it, so the setting governs the AI side's actions alone.
The on-map route is taken for whatever spell id the scorer picked, with no filtering, while the full-screen route forwards only the ids that have no presentation of their own; fdps_cast_spell_on_targets records that MISC.VFS holds no Emg03, Emg04 or Emg12 animation, and this call site is the one that can reach it with those ids.
It then resolves the kills: fdps_collect_death_script_events gathers the 3-byte event records of the units the spell brought to 0 HP into a 12-byte (four-record) stack buffer that nothing bounds-checks, fdps_render_view_frame repaints, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead takes the dead off the map, and fdps_run_death_scripts executes the collected records.
Finally it zeroes DAT_00069cec, the pending battle experience, discarding it -- the AI's physical attack fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack instead scales that counter by 15/10 and awards it to the unit it struck -- clears DAT_00069cd0 once more and returns 1.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the AI-controlled actor doing the casting. Both callers pass their own actor index unchanged; it goes to fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit and on to fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets / fdps_cast_spell_on_targets as the caster unit id.
  side_select -- which side the actor is acting for: 0 on the enemy phase, 1 on the NPC phase, passed down unchanged from fdps_map_actor_take_best_action and fdps_map_actor_behavior_step. Its only use here is the inversion of the spell record's target-side byte described above.

Returns:
  1 when the spell was cast, 0 when DAT_00063f88 was below 6 and nothing was done. Both callers ignore it, and on both the 0 result is unreachable: fdps_map_actor_behavior_step applies the same DAT_00063f88 >= 6 test itself at 00010693 before calling, and each of fdps_map_actor_take_best_action's three call sites is guarded by comparisons that make DAT_00063f88 the largest of the three action scores, one of which its entry gate at 00012c8f already required to be at least 6.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; the body owns the game's AI-decision globals and calls only in-image game routines]

Rebuild note:
fdps_run_death_scripts is handed DAT_00063f74, a global that only the physical-attack scorer fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack ever writes (at 00012504): the melee target that scorer picked, which is neither the caster nor the unit whose death script is running, and which on the fdps_map_actor_behavior_step path was left over from an earlier actor because that scorer has not run yet this turn. It reaches the chapter event handler table at 000601c4 as the unit index for opcode-2 records, so passing the caster there instead -- the obvious reading, and what fdps_battle_spell_command does at its own matching call at 000280b1 -- hands chapter event handlers a different unit.

=== 00013e0a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte Watcom NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0], aligning FUN_00013e10 to 16 bytes.

=== 00013e10 [PLATE]
Locates the treasure-chest cell carrying a given cell code, so the map AI that sends a unit off to open a chest knows where to walk it.

Algorithm:
Reads the map dimensions out of the battle grid header behind DAT_00060144 -- width from the signed word at +0, height from the signed word at +2 -- then scans every cell in row-major order, y outer and x inner. For each cell it calls fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y), which republishes that cell's terrain attribute byte in DAT_00069d08 and the cell's per-cell code byte in DAT_00069d06. A cell matches when the 0x60 field of the attribute byte holds exactly 0x20 -- the treasure-chest kind -- and DAT_00069d06 equals cell_code. On the first match it stores x into out_xy[0] and y into out_xy[1] and returns 0; when the whole grid is walked without a match it returns -1. Nothing else is written, and there is no bounds checking: the scan trusts that the grid behind DAT_00060144 and the terrain layer behind DAT_00069cb0 that fdps_map_load_tile_info indexes carry the same width.
The other openable kind, 0x40 (the buried treasure the player digs up), is deliberately not matched, so an AI actor never goes after a buried-treasure cell -- only after a chest.

Parameters:
  cell_code -- the cell to look for, matched against the per-cell code byte that the map's third layer supplies through DAT_00069d06. fdps_map_actor_behavior_step passes byte 0x3d of the acting unit's 0x50-byte record, which is also the index it uses into the per-code already-taken flag array at DAT_000640d8 and into the 3-byte reward records at DAT_0006013c + 0x53. The code numbers the cell, not its kind, so the same numbering covers chest and buried-treasure cells alike.
  out_xy -- caller-supplied 2-byte buffer; on a hit out_xy[0] receives the column and out_xy[1] the row, both as bytes. Left untouched on a miss.

Returns:
  0 when a matching cell was found and out_xy was filled, -1 when no cell on the map matched. Note the sense: 0 is the success value, not the failure value.

Pool: fdps  [no library match: zero Watcom and zero ail Function ID candidates, hash unique in the image; its only caller, its only callee and every global it touches are game code]

Rebuild note:
The kind test is (attr & 0x60) == 0x20, an equality on a two-bit field, not a bit test. Writing the obvious (attr & 0x20) -- which is what fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes' pair of comparisons collapses to -- makes this scan also match kind 0x60 cells, so the AI would walk a unit to the wrong cell on any map that uses that kind. Widening it the other obvious way, to the pair 0x20/0x40 that fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor accepts, is equally wrong: the original never sends an AI actor to a buried-treasure cell, only to a chest. Also note the return sense: 0 means found and -1 means not found, so an obvious 'return 1 on success' rewrite inverts the caller's TEST EAX,EAX / JZ gate and the unit would head for an uninitialised coordinate.

=== 00013ec6 [EOL]
10-byte zero fill aligning FUN_00013ed0 to a 16-byte boundary

=== 00013ed0 [PLATE]
Draws one cell of a SAF tilemap: blits the tile that the cell names into the destination surface at the request's x/y, or draws nothing at all when the tile index is out of range or the cell would not sit wholly inside the surface.

Algorithm:
Reads the SAF base pointer from req+0x14 and the cell's tile index from req+0x18. Takes the cell width from the u16 at saf+0x07 and the cell height from the u16 at saf+0x09 (24x24 in every shipped .SAF), and the tile section's item count from the u16 at saf+0x20. Returns without drawing when the tile index is negative or not less than that count, when x (req+0x0c) or y (req+0x10) is not strictly positive, when pitch (req+0x04) minus the cell width is not strictly greater than x, or when the destination height (req+0x08) minus the cell height is not strictly greater than y; the placement test is all-or-nothing, nothing is clipped. Otherwise it resolves the tile's RLE pixel stream as saf + table[index], where table = saf + *(u32 *)(saf + 0x22) is the tile section's offset table and index is scaled by 4, forms the destination pointer as req+0x00 plus x plus y * pitch, and calls fdps_blit_dispatch(src, dst, cell width, cell height, pitch, req+0x1c, req+0x20) -- the last two carrying the blit mode's parameter block and the mode byte the request was built with.

Parameters:
  req -- pointer to the 0x24-byte draw request. fdps_draw_tilemap_layer, the only caller, passes its own stack copy of the request with +0x0c/+0x10 stepped to this cell's position in the grid and +0x18 replaced by the cell's signed i16 tile index. Fields used here: +0x00 destination base, +0x04 destination pitch, +0x08 destination height in rows, +0x0c x, +0x10 y, +0x14 SAF base, +0x18 tile index, +0x1c blit parameter block, +0x20 blit mode.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; unique hash, zero watcom and zero ail Function ID candidates, and both its caller and its callee are game graphics code]

Rebuild note:
The accept test is strict on all four sides -- x > 0, y > 0, pitch - cell_width > x, dest_height - cell_height > y -- and a cell that fails it is dropped whole, not clipped. Writing the obvious C bound (x >= 0 && x + cell_width <= pitch, and likewise for y) draws cells the original silently discards, so the outermost row and column of a tilemap that sits flush against the destination edge would appear where the original leaves the background showing.

=== 00013fca [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea eax,[eax+0x0] NOP before fdps_draw_tilemap_layer

=== 000140e0 [PLATE]
Returns a pointer to one frame record of a loaded .SAF animation, or NULL when the frame index is out of range.

Algorithm:
Reads the .SAF header's frame-section descriptor: the 16-bit item count at saf+0x0c and the 32-bit section start offset at saf+0x0e. Returns NULL when frame_index is negative or not less than that count. Otherwise it forms the address of the section's offset table as saf + *(unsigned int *)(saf + 0x0e), reads the frame_index-th 32-bit entry of that table, and returns saf + that value: every offset stored inside a .SAF is measured from the start of the file, so the stored offset is rebased onto the caller's base pointer. The routine calls nothing and reads no globals.

The header's four section descriptors are 10 bytes each (u16 count, u32 start, u32 size) starting at 0x0c, so the DWORD at 0x0e is only 2-byte aligned; the code reads it as a plain 32-bit load. Only the frame section (descriptor 0) is reachable through this function -- the tilemap, tile and sound sections have their descriptors at 0x16, 0x20 and 0x2a and are indexed by their own readers. No magic check is performed here.

Parameters:
  saf -- base of a complete .SAF image held in memory, as returned by fdps_vfs_load_entry; only the frame-section descriptor at +0x0c is looked at
  frame_index -- 0-based frame number, valid range [0, *(unsigned short *)(saf + 0x0c))

Returns:
  Pointer to the frame record (i16 sound id or -1, i16 duration in ticks, u8 lead-in count, u8 hit marker, u16 zero, i16 layer count, then that many 13-byte layers), or NULL when frame_index is outside the valid range.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; pure game-data container indexing]

Rebuild note:
The .SAF section descriptors are 10 bytes each (u16 count, u32 start, u32 size) packed from header offset 0x0c, so this routine's DWORD read at saf+0x0e is only 2-byte aligned. Declaring the header as an ordinary C struct makes the compiler pad the u16 to 4 bytes and every section field lands 2 bytes past where the file has it; the header must be laid out with Watcom's _Packed / #pragma pack(1) or addressed by byte offset.

=== 0001413f [EOL]
Single 0x90 NOP aligning fdps_draw_composite_sprite to a 16-byte boundary.

=== 00014140 [PLATE]

Name: game code, descriptive fdps_ name; no library symbol involved.
Boundary: 00014140-000142cb, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the entry, matching epilogue and RET at 000142cb; the 4 bytes after it are a LEA-form alignment nop before 000142d0.
Signature: __cdecl, void fdps_draw_composite_sprite(void *req, char flag) - both arguments read from the stack at [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], plain RET with caller cleanup.
Detail: image = req+0x14, frame index = req+0x18; the image is the loaded .SAF and holds a u16 frame count at +0x0C and a 32-bit section 0 offset-table displacement at +0x0E, and frame = image + table[index]. When flag is non-zero, fdps_sfx_play is called afterwards with the image pointer and the frame's leading i16, read sign-extended (MOVSX EAX,word ptr [EAX] at 000142b5): a frame with no sound stores -1, which fdps_sfx_play rejects on its own negative sound_index bound, where a zero-extended 65535 would not be caught.
Inline: 0001414c-000141bf is an inline expansion of fdps_saf_get_frame @ 000140e0 rather than open-coded arithmetic - argument temps at [EBP-0x50]/[EBP-0x54] are copied into the consecutive parameter-shaped slots [EBP-0x58]/[EBP-0x5c], the callee's body is replayed instruction for instruction under that substitution, and the result slot [EBP-0x64] is copied out to this function's own local [EBP-0xc].

=== 000144db [EOL]

=== 000144e0 [PLATE]
Returns the number of frames in a loaded .SAF animation image.

Algorithm:
Tests the three magic bytes at saf+0, saf+1 and saf+2 against 'S', 'A' and 'F'. The three tests are joined with OR, not AND: any single matching byte passes. On a pass, returns the 16-bit item count of section 0 (the frame section) out of the section descriptor at saf+0x0C, zero-extended to int. On a failure -- all three bytes wrong -- returns 0, which makes every caller's playback loop run zero times. No callees, no globals touched.

Parameters:
  saf -- base of a .SAF image in memory, as returned by the VFS loader. The 52-byte header starts here, and the four 10-byte section descriptors start at +0x0C; the first u16 of a descriptor is its item count.

Returns:
  Frame count, 0..0xFFFF. 0 also means the magic check failed, so the two cases are not distinguishable by the caller.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image, and it decodes the game's own resource tag; all six callers are ordinary game code]

Rebuild note:
The magic test is p[0]=='S' || p[1]=='A' || p[2]=='F' -- three ORs, so any one matching byte is accepted and the check is effectively no check. Writing the obvious && (or a memcmp) would start rejecting images the original plays, and the rejection is silent: the function just returns 0 and the animation renders nothing. Already recorded in rebuild_info/pitfalls.md; this is one of the two copies of that check, the other being fdps_saf_advance_tick.

=== 00014544 [EOL]
Watcom 16-byte alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs between FUN_000144e0 and fdps_saf_advance_tick.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; game resource-format state machine]
Evidence: No Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set (0 candidates in both), full_hash unique in the image and absent from ailv3.lib. All 12 callers are game code (fdps_title_screen, fdps_show_game_over, FUN_000196d0, FUN_0001a4c0, ...) and there are no callees, so nothing links it to a vendor module. The body tests the 'S','A','F' magic (0x53/0x41/0x46) at buffer offsets 0/1/2, reads the frame count from the u16 at header+0x0c, indexes the frame offset table based at the i32 in header+0x0e, and compares the i16 frame duration at frame+0x02 against a tick counter -- a format only this game knows, which no CRT, maths, emulator or Miles AIL routine contains. === 000146e0 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the four-entry icon array of the battle system ring menu: the Command.cel sprite ids 0x16, 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x13.

Rebuild note:
These bytes have no name in the original source. === 000146f0 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the four-entry disabled-flag array of the battle system ring menu: four zero ints, meaning every command in that menu is selectable.

Nothing writes it. It is read once per call, in the prologue of fdps_battle_system_menu, where four inline MOVSD copy all 0x10 bytes into that function's local array at EBP-0x38, immediately after the same idiom fills the paired icon array at EBP-0x48 from 0x146e0. The local is then handed by address as the second argument to fdps_menu_animate_open, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop and fdps_render_ring_menu_frame, and fdps_battle_system_menu never writes it afterwards, so all four entries stay zero for the whole life of the menu.

The four entries are in ring slot order up, left, right, down -- the same order fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop moves the menu cursor in. A zero entry means that slot may be chosen: fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop only moves the cursor to a direction whose entry is zero, and fdps_render_ring_menu_frame draws slot i with plate sprite (i == cursor_dir ? 0x1a : 0x1b) + cmd_disabled[i] and icon sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24, so a non-zero entry would take both the plate and the icon from the greyed-out bank 0x24 sprites further into the Command.cel sheet at DAT_000643ac. Because this image is all zeros and its copy is never written, none of that greying ever happens in the top-level menu; the submenu's own image at 0x14710 is the one whose copy does get set, at 00014ed8, when FDE.SAV is absent and the load entry has to be greyed out.

Pool: binary_artifact  [four inline MOVSD with no counter and no memcpy call are Watcom's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so these bytes are wcc386's output rather than a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
Sixteen zero bytes sitting between two initialiser images in read-only data look exactly like alignment filler, and dropping them is the obvious mistake; they are a live initialiser that fdps_battle_system_menu block-copies. The faithful rebuild writes `int cmd_disabled[4] = {0};` as a local of fdps_battle_system_menu and lets wcc386 regenerate the image. Because every entry is zero it is also tempting to delete the array and pass a null pointer or a file-scope const zero array instead: null crashes, since fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop and fdps_render_ring_menu_frame dereference all four entries on every frame, and a shared file-scope array is the wrong shape because the sibling image at 0x14710 fills the same role for fdps_battle_system_submenu and its copy is written.

=== 00014720 [PLATE]

Nothing writes it; it is read once per call, in the prologue of fdps_battle_unit_turn, where four inline MOVSD copy all 0x10 bytes into that function's local array at EBP-0x48, immediately before the same idiom fills the paired disabled-flag array at EBP-0x38 from the zero image at 00014730. The local is handed as the second argument of fdps_battle_action_menu, which forwards it to fdps_menu_animate_open, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop, fdps_menu_animate_close and fdps_render_ring_menu_frame, all of which read it as four ints and never write it. The four entries are in ring slot order up, left, right, down -- the order fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop moves the cursor in (scan code 0x48 selects slot 0, 0x4b slot 1, 0x4d slot 2, 0x50 slot 3) and the order fdps_battle_action_menu dispatches on: slot 0 (icon 3) attacks, collecting targets with fdps_collect_targets_in_range and running fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange; slot 1 (icon 2) enters fdps_battle_spell_command; slot 2 (icon 1) enters fdps_battle_item_menu; slot 3 (icon 0) ends the unit's turn and, when the caller passes flag 0, rests it through fdps_unit_rest. Each value is an index into the Command.cel sheet at DAT_000643ac; fdps_render_ring_menu_frame draws sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24, so a greyed-out slot takes its icon from a second bank 0x24 sprites further in. The paired zero image at 00014730 initialises the matching disabled array, which fdps_battle_unit_turn and fdps_battle_action_menu then both write: the caller pre-disables slot 1 for units whose class or state forbids spells, and fdps_battle_action_menu sets slot 0 when the unit has no usable weapon or no target in reach, slot 1 when it knows no spells, and slot 2 when it carries no items.

=== 00014730 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the four disabled flags of the per-unit battle action ring menu: sixteen zero bytes, one dword per ring slot.

Nothing writes the image; it is read once per call, in the prologue of fdps_battle_unit_turn, where four inline MOVSD at 00015490-00015493 copy all 0x10 bytes into that function's local array at EBP-0x38, immediately after the same idiom fills the paired icon array at EBP-0x48 from 00014720. The stack copy is what the game then writes. A flag of 1 means the slot is greyed out and cannot be chosen; 0 means it is selectable, and the image exists so that every unit's turn starts with all four slots live. Slots are in ring order up, left, right, down: slot 0 attack, slot 1 spell, slot 2 item, slot 3 end turn. fdps_battle_unit_turn itself sets slot 1 at 00015668 when the unit record's byte at +8 is neither 7 nor 3 -- the two values that permit casting -- and clears it again at 00015772 on the path that re-opens the menu after a cancelled move. fdps_battle_action_menu, which takes the array as its third argument (0001569d and 00015793 push &local_38), clears slot 0 on entry and then sets slot 0 when fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot finds no equipped weapon or no target lies in reach, slot 1 when the unit knows no usable spell, and slot 2 when it carries no usable item. Slot 3 is never written by anyone: end turn is always available, and its zero comes from this image alone. fdps_render_ring_menu_frame reads the array alongside the icon array and draws sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24, so a greyed-out slot takes its icon from a second bank 0x24 sprites further into the Command.cel sheet, and fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop refuses to settle the cursor on a slot whose flag is set.

Pool: binary_artifact  [four inline MOVSD with no counter and no memcpy call are Watcom's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so these bytes are wcc386's own output rather than a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
These sixteen zeros look like alignment padding between two initialiser images and are not. The faithful rebuild writes `int cmd_disabled[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};` as a local of fdps_battle_unit_turn and lets wcc386 regenerate the image. Hoisting it to a file-scope array and passing its address compiles and runs but is wrong: both fdps_battle_unit_turn and fdps_battle_action_menu write entries of the stack copy, so a file-scope array would carry one unit's greyed-out actions into the next unit's turn, and slot 3, which nothing ever writes, would stay whatever the previous turn left in it.

=== 00014740 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the red channel of the UI palette pulse: a 16-step intensity cycle with its first 8 steps repeated at the end, 24 bytes in all.

Nothing writes it. fdps_cycle_ui_palette reads it once per call, in its prologue, where MOVSD.REP with ECX=6 (00015bec-00015bf9) copies all 0x18 bytes into the local array at EBP-0x34, immediately before the same idiom fills the green ramp at EBP-0x4c from 00014758 and the blue ramp at EBP-0x1c from 00014770. The routine then waits for VGA vertical retrace on inp(0x3da) and, once per timer tick -- when the serviced-tick latch DAT_00063fbc differs from the tick counter DAT_00069d64 that fdps_timer_tick_handler increments -- rewrites DAC entries 8..15: for i = 0..7 it writes i + 8 to the DAC write-index port 0x3c8 and then red[phase + i], green[phase + i], blue[phase + i] to the data port 0x3c9, phase being DAT_00060014. Last it decrements the phase and wraps it from -1 back to 15, so the wave marches across colours 8..15 by one step per tick. All nine callers are modal UI loops (menus, lists, windows), which call it once per iteration, so it also paces those loops to the display refresh.

The values are 6-bit DAC intensities: 14, 11, 8, 5, 3, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 5, 8, 11, 14 for the 16-step cycle, then 14, 11, 8, 5, 3, 2, 0, 0 again. Green (00014758) has the same shape peaking at 42 and troughing at 14, blue (00014770) peaking at 26 and troughing at 0, so palette entries 8..15 pulse between a light green-cyan (14, 42, 26) and a near-black green (0, 14, 0). The duplicated tail is what lets the 8-entry window sit at any phase 0..15 without wrapping: the highest index reached is 15 + 7 = 22.

Pool: binary_artifact  [a fixed-count MOVSD.REP from rodata onto the frame, with no memcpy call and no write to the copy, is wcc386's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so these bytes are the compiler's output rather than a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
The faithful rebuild writes this as a 24-entry auto array inside fdps_cycle_ui_palette, not a 16-entry one. Writing `unsigned char red[16]` -- the natural way to spell a 16-step cycle -- and keeping the original's unmasked index red[phase + i] reads up to 7 bytes past the end; the original avoids that by storing the first 8 steps a second time rather than by masking. The three arrays are also autos, re-copied onto the stack on every call: hoisting them to file-scope const is functionally equivalent here, since nothing writes the copies, but it is not the shape the original was compiled from.

=== 00014854 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for a local char array: the printf format "%.3d" and its NUL, 5 bytes.

Read only by fdps_draw_number@00017530, which copies all 5 bytes onto its stack frame (MOVSD + MOVSB into EBP-0x18) on entry and then patches the copy in place, storing '0' + digit_count over the '3' at offset 2 to make "%.1d" .. === 0001485c [PLATE]
Frame-by-frame destination y for the four strips of the win/fail panel as it slides in: 4 strips x 19 frames of signed int, row-major, indexed strip * 19 + frame.

Read-only image, written by nothing at run time. fdps_battle_show_win_fail_window copies all 76 dwords onto its stack with a REP MOVSD at 00017cbc as its first act, and the 19-iteration slide-in loop then reads one entry per strip per frame to place that strip into the 360x240 scene buffer at row y + 0x14 before fdps_blit_rect presents it. Values are signed screen rows: a negative y means the strip has not fully entered the window yet, and the loop clips it by moving the source down by -y and shortening the strip by the same amount, so a strip whose y + height is still 0 or less is skipped for that frame. Row 0 (top strip) runs -8, 8, 20, 45, 75, 110, 156, 157 and then holds at 156 for the remaining frames; row 1 settles at 139, row 2 at 56, row 3 at 39, each after the same one-pixel overshoot on the settling frame. Rows 2 and 3 begin at -90 and -16, far enough off-screen that those two strips draw nothing for the first 8 and 13 frames respectively, which is what staggers the entrance. The matching slide-out table, 4 strips x 13 frames, is at 000149cc; the strips' x offsets, source y offsets, widths and heights are the four 4-int tables at 0001498c, 0001499c, 000149ac and 000149bc.

Pool: binary_artifact  [rodata initialiser image for an auto array in fdps_battle_show_win_fail_window, copied whole into the frame and never read in place -- the same construct as the local-array init images at 000146e0-000147ac]

Rebuild note:
The entries are signed and the slide-in loop depends on it: the y < 0 branch is what clips the strip against the top of the window. Declaring the table unsigned, or narrowing it to bytes because the settled values are small, turns the leading frames into blits at enormous y instead of clipped ones and the panel stops sliding in. The numbers are also hand-tuned, not a ramp -- each row overshoots its resting y by one pixel on the settling frame and comes back, and rows 2 and 3 start deep enough off-screen to be skipped for 8 and 13 frames -- so generating the keyframes from a formula loses both the bounce and the staggered entrance.
