Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the four-entry disabled-flag array of the in-game options ring menu: four zero ints, meaning all four settings are always selectable.

Nothing writes it. It is read once per call, in the prologue of fdps_options_menu, where four inline MOVSD at 000183e4-000183e7 copy all 0x10 bytes into that function's local array at [EBP + -0x18]. The local is then handed by address as the second argument to fdps_menu_animate_open, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop and fdps_menu_animate_close on every pass of the menu loop, and fdps_options_menu never writes it, so all four entries stay zero for the whole life of the menu.

The four entries are in ring slot order up, left, right, down -- the order fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop moves the cursor in. A zero entry means that slot may be chosen; fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop only moves the cursor to a direction whose entry is zero, and fdps_render_ring_menu_frame draws slot i with backdrop sprite (i == cursor_dir ? 0x1a : 0x1b) + cmd_disabled[i] and icon sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24, so a non-zero entry would take both from the greyed-out bank 0x24 sprites further into the Command.cel sheet at DAT_000643ac. This menu never greys anything: it reaches the same grey bank a different way. Unlike its siblings, fdps_options_menu builds its companion icon array at [EBP + -0x28] at runtime instead of copying a second image, picking per setting flag the ON icon or the ON icon plus 0x24 -- 0x0d/0x31 for the CD music flag at DAT_00060008, 0x0e/0x32 for DAT_00069d70, 0x0f/0x33 for DAT_00060010 and 0x18/0x3c for DAT_00060158 -- so the OFF state is drawn from the grey bank while the disabled flags remain zero and the entry stays selectable.

Pool: binary_artifact  [four inline MOVSD with no counter and no memcpy call are Watcom's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so these bytes are wcc386's output rather than a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
Sixteen zero bytes in read-only data immediately in front of four bytes of alignment filler and a function entry look exactly like tail padding, and reclaiming them is the obvious mistake; they are a live initialiser that fdps_options_menu block-copies on every call. The faithful rebuild writes `int cmd_disabled[4] = {0};` as a local of fdps_options_menu and lets wcc386 regenerate the image. Because every entry is zero it is also tempting to drop the array and pass a null pointer, or to share one file-scope const zero array with the other menus: null crashes, since fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop dereferences all four entries on every keypress and fdps_render_ring_menu_frame on every frame, and sharing aliases the submenu image at 0x14710, whose stack copy is written at 00014ed8.

=== 00015860 [PLATE]
Renders and presents one frame of the four-command ring menu: the battle-map view with the four command buttons standing at radius pixels around the map cursor, the one at cursor_dir highlighted.

Algorithm:
Allocates an 0x15180-byte (360x240, pitch 0x168) offscreen scene buffer with malloc and asks fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor which unit is standing on the cursor tile (-1 for none).

Places the four buttons. The float constant 0x3d860a8a is 2 * 3.14159 / 96 rounded to float -- the author's own six-digit pi, not a library one, so one value drives both the polar radius and the sweep: dx = (int)(cos(radius * 2*pi/96) * radius) and dy = (int)(sin(radius * 2*pi/96) * radius), each converted through __CHP, which truncates toward zero rather than rounding. The cursor's position in view coordinates is cx = DAT_00069cd4 - DAT_00069ce4 and cy = DAT_00069ccc - DAT_00069ce0, the cursor's pixel position minus the camera scroll. The four slots then sit at (cx - dx, cy - dy), (cx - dy, cy + dx), (cx + dy, cy - dx) and (cx + dx, cy + dy). At radius 0x18 the angle is 1.5707949, a shade under 90 degrees, so dx truncates to 0 and dy to 0x17: the slots rest 23 pixels up, left, right and down of the cursor, a pixel inside the 24-pixel tile -- the same 0 up / 1 left / 2 right / 3 down order fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop moves the menu cursor in. The 23 is the truncation and not the constant -- sin never exceeds 1, so radius * sin is below radius at every angle and CALL __CHP / FISTP chops it down whichever constant is used. Smaller radii put them on a quarter-turn spiral between the cursor and those resting places, which is how fdps_menu_animate_open and fdps_menu_animate_close animate the menu open and shut.

fdps_draw_scene_layers then composites the whole battle view -- map layers, map cursor and every unit -- into the buffer.

For each slot i whose position passes -0x18 <= x < 0x14f and -0x18 <= y < 0xd7, two 0x19 x 0x16 (25x22) Command.cel sprites go down at buffer + 0x18 + (y + 0x18) * 0x168 + x through fdps_blit_dispatch in mode 0, the RLE passthrough kernel: first the button plate, sprite (i == cursor_dir ? 0x1a : 0x1b) + cmd_disabled[i], then the command icon over it, sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24, so a greyed-out entry takes its icon from a second bank 0x24 sprites further into the sheet. Both resolve the sprite the way fdps_blit_command_sprite does, as DAT_000643ac + *(int *)(DAT_000643ac + 0xf + index * 4). That bounds test is an origin-only test against the 360x240 buffer; it takes no account of the sprite's own 25x22 extent. The camera clamp holds the ring centre inside 288 across and 168 down, and the largest radius any caller passes is 0x19 (PUSH 0x19 at 00016193), whose legs are -1 and 24, so the extreme slot origins are x = 312 for slot 2 and y = 192 for slot 3. Both pass the test. The y extreme puts its plate on buffer rows 216..237 of 240; the x extreme puts its 25 columns on 336..360, and 360 is one past the last column of a 360-byte row, so the rightmost plate's final column falls on the head of the following scanline -- still far inside the 0x15180 allocation and never over the adapter. Nothing in play is dropped by the test and nothing is written past the buffer, but the wrap is what the original does, so do not add a guard.

When a unit is standing on the cursor tile it is drawn a second time, fdps_draw_map_unit(unit_index, buffer, 0), so the unit whose menu this is sits on top of the buttons rather than under them.

delay(2) paces the frame, then fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x138 x 0xc0 window at buffer + 0x21d8 (buffer coordinate 24,24) straight to the mode-13h screen at 0xa0504 (screen coordinate 4,4) with destination pitch 0x140 -- the same framed 312x192 main view fdps_render_view_frame presents. free releases the buffer on the way out.

Parameters:
  cmd_icons -- four ints, the Command.cel sprite id of each slot's icon, in slot order up/left/right/down. fdps_battle_system_menu copies its four from the template at 0x146e0.
  cmd_disabled -- four ints, 0 when that slot's command may be chosen and 1 when it is greyed out. The flag is added to the plate sprite id and multiplied by 0x24 for the icon sprite id. It is the same array fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop reads to decide which directions the menu cursor may move to.
  radius -- pixel radius of the ring, and, multiplied by 2*pi/96, the angle of the sweep. 0x18 is the resting ring; fdps_menu_animate_open steps 1, 5, 9 ... 0x15 and then 0x18 and 0x19, fdps_menu_animate_close steps 0x17 down to 3.
  cursor_dir -- which slot is drawn highlighted: 0 up, 1 left, 2 right, 3 down. Any other value leaves all four slots on the unhighlighted plate.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Rebuild note:
The second fdps_draw_map_unit call paints the unit's sprite rather than its shadow only because the pass byte DAT_0006014c is 0 on its way out of fdps_draw_scene_layers. That byte is written only by fdps_draw_map_units, at 0002d24c and 0002d287, and fdps_draw_scene_layers leaves it at 0 by way of that call; if 0006014c is given a name during the data pass this note should use it, as src/mapdraw.h already calls it data_fdps_map_unit_shadow_pass_flag. === 00015b90 [PLATE]

=== 00015be0 [PLATE]
Advances the UI palette animation by one frame: waits for VGA vertical retrace, then once per timer tick rewrites DAC entries 8..15 from a sliding window over three colour ramps. Every modal menu, list and window loop in the game calls it once per iteration, so it is also what paces those loops to the display refresh.

Algorithm:
Copies the three 24-byte ramps at 0x14740 (red), 0x14758 (green) and 0x14770 (blue) onto the stack. Busy-waits on inp(0x3da), the VGA input status register, until bit 3 (vertical retrace active) is set -- this happens on every call, whether or not any colour changes. Compares the serviced-tick latch DAT_00063fbc against the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 that fdps_timer_tick_handler increments; equal means this tick has already been serviced and the routine returns without touching the DAC. Otherwise it latches the new tick into DAT_00063fbc and, for i = 0 to 7, writes palette index i + 8 to the DAC write-index port 0x3c8 via outp and then the red, green and blue bytes at ramp offset DAT_00060014 + i to the DAC data port 0x3c9. Last it decrements the phase DAT_00060014 and wraps it back to 15 when it reaches -1, so the wave marches across colours 8..15 by one step per tick.

Each ramp is a 16-step cycle with its first 8 bytes repeated at the end, which is why the 8-entry window at any offset 0..15 never has to wrap: red is 14,11,8,5,3,2,0,0,0,0,3,3,5,8,11,14 then 14,11,8,5,3,2,0,0; green and blue are exact mirrors -- 42,37,33,30,26,21,18,14 and back, 26,21,16,12,8,4,2,0 and back -- each with its trough as a repeated pair. Red is not: it holds 0 across indices 6..9 and climbs back through 3,3,5,8,11,14, which is not the reverse of its 14,11,8,5,3,2 descent. The colours therefore pulse between a light green-cyan (14,42,26) and a near-black green (0,14,0) in 6-bit DAC units. DAT_00060014 is initialised data and starts at 15.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the Watcom or AIL sets and the body hash is unique in the image; it owns the game globals 0x60014 and 0x63fbc and reads game-authored ramps at 0x14740..0x14787, and all nine callers are game UI loops]

Rebuild note:
The retrace busy-wait sits outside the once-per-tick guard, so the function blocks until vblank on every call even when it changes no colour; the obvious tidy-up of testing DAT_00063fbc == DAT_00069d64 first and returning early would remove the frame pace from all nine modal UI loops. Also, the three ramps are 24 bytes each although the cycle has only 16 steps -- the trailing 8 bytes repeat the first 8 so that ramp[phase + i] with phase up to 15 and i up to 7 never wraps -- so declaring them as 16-byte arrays and indexing [phase + i] reads past the end instead of doing the intended modulo.

=== 000160e0 [PLATE]
Returns the index of the first selectable entry of a four-entry menu, so the caller can put the menu cursor on it.

Algorithm:
Walks an index from 0 while it is below 4, testing cmd_disabled[index], and returns the first index whose entry is zero; falls out of the loop to return -1 when all four entries are non-zero. The four-entry bound is hard-coded, matching the 16-byte (four int) menu availability descriptors these menus use: fdps_battle_item_menu copies one from 0x00024d60 onto its stack and patches entry 1 before calling here, and fdps_battle_action_menu fills its own such array from the per-command legality probes. An entry of 0 means the command is selectable, non-zero means it is greyed out. The index doubles as the entry's position on the four-way menu -- 0 up, 1 left, 2 right, 3 down -- which is how fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop reads the same array when deciding which cursor moves are allowed.

Parameters:
  cmd_disabled -- pointer to four ints, one per menu entry, 0 selectable and non-zero greyed out. Only read, never written.

Returns:
  The index 0..3 of the first selectable entry, or -1 when every entry is disabled. fdps_battle_item_menu uses the value as the initial cursor index it hands to fdps_menu_animate_open and to fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; single static caller is game code, and a fixed four-entry availability scan over a caller-supplied menu descriptor is application policy, not CRT or AIL]

=== 00016130 [PLATE]
Plays the opening animation of the four-command ring menu: the command icons spiral out from the map cursor to their resting positions while the window sound effect plays.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_play_sfx with the asset name "OpWin.wav" once, then draws the animation frame by frame through fdps_render_ring_menu_frame, which renders and presents one whole ring from the same three menu descriptors plus a radius. The radius runs 1, 5, 9, 0xd, 0x11, 0x15 (loop from 1 while below 0x18, step 4), then one frame at 0x18 and one at 0x19. fdps_render_ring_menu_frame puts the four icons at distance r and angle r * 2*pi/96 from the map cursor, so distance and angle grow together and the icons sweep outward along a spiral; 0x18 is exactly a quarter turn, the resting layout in which the four entries sit on the up/left/right/down axes that fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop keeps repainting afterwards. Every frame forwards cmd_icons, cmd_disabled and cursor_dir untouched: fdps_render_ring_menu_frame draws entry i with Command.cel sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24 out of the sheet at 0x000643ac, and gives the entry at cursor_dir the highlighted backdrop sprite 0x1a instead of 0x1b. fdps_menu_animate_close is the counterpart that runs the radius back down.

  cursor_dir -- which entry is highlighted while the menu opens: 0 up, 1 left, 2 right, 3 down, or -1 when no entry is selectable. Callers pass 0 or the result of fdps_menu_find_first_enabled_entry, out of the same local they hand to fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop by address immediately afterwards.

Returns:

=== 000161b0 [PLATE]
Plays the closing animation of the four-command ring menu: the command icons spiral back in
toward the map cursor while the window sound effect plays.

Algorithm:
  Calls fdps_play_sfx("OpWin.wav") once, the same cue the opening animation fdps_menu_animate_open
  plays. Then runs a counter from 0x17 (23) down while it is greater than 0 in steps of -4, six
  frames in all (23, 19, 15, 11, 7, 3), and for each frame calls
  fdps_render_ring_menu_frame(cmd_icons, cmd_disabled, r, cursor_dir).
  That routine uses the third argument both as the radius in pixels and, times 2*pi/96
  (0.06544979), as the angle, placing the four 25x22 Command.cel icons at four points 90 degrees
  apart on a circle of that radius around the camera-relative cursor position, so a falling counter
  pulls the icons inward and unwinds them by about 75 degrees. The opposite direction is
  fdps_menu_animate_open, which drives the same helper up 1, 5, 9, 0xd, 0x11, 0x15 and then 0x18 and
  0x19; fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop holds it at 0x18 while the player is choosing.
  The loop stops at radius 3: it neither draws a radius-0 frame nor erases what it drew. What
  removes the icons differs by caller. fdps_battle_system_submenu (00014f7d),
  fdps_battle_action_menu (00015eb5) and fdps_battle_item_menu (00025395) call
  fdps_render_view_frame on the very next instruction after the ADD ESP,0xc, and that repaint clears
  them. fdps_options_menu does not: it tests the chosen entry straight away at 00018492 and either
  toggles a setting and jumps back to 000183ef, or returns to fdps_battle_system_menu, which jumps
  to 00014aec -- both paths reach fdps_menu_animate_open again, and its first frame recomposites the
  whole view through fdps_draw_scene_layers into a fresh buffer, so the stale icons go with it.

Parameters:
  cmd_icons -- pointer to four ints, one per menu entry, each the Command.cel sprite id of that
    entry's icon; fdps_render_ring_menu_frame draws sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24, so
    the second bank of 36 sprites holds the greyed-out icons. The callers pass the same four-int
    array they gave to fdps_menu_animate_open and fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop.
  cmd_disabled -- pointer to four ints, one per menu entry: 0 when the entry can be chosen, 1 when
    it is unavailable. fdps_render_ring_menu_frame adds it both to the icon id and to the plate
    sprite (0x1a highlighted / 0x1b normal), and fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop refuses to move the
    cursor onto an entry whose value is non-zero.
  cursor_dir -- which entry stays highlighted during the retraction: 0 up, 1 left, 2 right, 3 down.
    Callers pass by value the variable fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop filled in through its cursor_dir
    out-parameter, i.e. the entry the player was last on.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX is not set on the way out and no caller looks at it.

Pool: fdps  [game asset string "OpWin.wav"; game-only callers and callees, no Function ID hit in
either library set]

Rebuild note:
  fdps_battle_system_menu does not call this function. It carries its own copy of the loop inline at

  fdps_render_ring_menu_frame -- with no fdps_play_sfx call in front of it, so the top-level battle

2. The byte at +0x3c is displayed as 1000 when it holds the sentinel 0xff.
3. Before each print, the global colour selector 0x0006000c is set to 3 when the current value differs from its maximum, and to 1 or 0 according to whether the corresponding status byte (record+0x22, +0x23, +0x24) is non-zero. The current-versus-maximum test has NO else arm: the JZ at 00016453 and at 000164ad jump PAST the store, so a current equal to its maximum leaves whatever the caller left in 0x0006000c and the figure is drawn in it.   Nothing.

=== 000168e0 [PLATE]
Closes the unit status window and puts the screen back the way it was.

Algorithm:
Plays the "OpWin1.wav" window cue through fdps_play_sfx -- the same cue the open uses -- then mallocs an 0x15180-byte (360x240) scene scratch buffer and rebuilds the image that lies behind the window into background, choosing the branch on the still-screen flag DAT_00060070 (0 on the field/battle map, 1 while the town phase at fdps_run_village_phase is up):
  - flag 0: composites the live scrolling scene into the scratch buffer with fdps_draw_scene_layers, clears background to 0, and fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x138 x 0xc0 (312x192) view window from scratch+0x21d8 (x=24, y=24 at stride 0x168) to background+0x504 (x=4, y=4 at stride 0x140).
  - flag 1: memmoves the saved 320x200 page at DAT_00063fb4 into background. The fdps_blit_rect just before it copies the same rectangle into the scene scratch buffer, which is then freed without being read.
It then runs the close animation: fdps_draw_status_window_anim_frame(background, window_image, step) for step 5 down to 0. Each call composes one retreating position of the window's four panels over background and presents it to 0xa0000 on vertical retrace; step 0 is the closed position, and the open animation the callers run counts step 0 up to 8.
Finally it restores the visible screen. With DAT_00060070 == 0 it calls fdps_render_view_frame and then blanks the frame's four-pixel border directly in VGA memory: rows 0-3 with memset(0xa0000, 0, 0x500), rows 196-199 with memset(0xaf500, 0, 0x500), and then four pixels at each end of a row (offsets i*0x140 and i*0x140+0x13c from 0xa0000) once per iteration of a loop that runs 0x140 times. With the flag set it memmoves the saved page at DAT_00063fb4 back to 0xa0000 instead. It frees the scratch buffer and copies DAT_00063fb8 into DAT_00060159, restoring the cursor-info-panel flag that fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window saved and zeroed when the window opened; because that happens after the repaint above, fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel starts drawing again only from the caller's next frame.

Parameters:
  window_image -- the assembled status window image, as returned by fdps_load_status_cel_image and drawn into by the caller. Passed straight through as the window_image of fdps_draw_status_window_anim_frame.
  background -- a caller-owned 64000-byte (320x200) buffer. Its contents on entry are never read: this function fills it with the image behind the window before the first animation frame.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls game-only symbols; no Function ID hit, watcom and ail candidate counts both 0]

Rebuild note:
The border-clear loop after fdps_render_view_frame runs 0x140 (320) times -- the screen's width, not its height of 200 -- so its last 120 iterations write 4-byte zero runs from 0xa0000 up to 0xb8fff, past the end of the mode 13h frame. It is harmless only because the destination is raw VGA memory. Writing the obvious thing, a border clear over a 64000-byte offscreen page, overruns that page by 38 KB; keep the writes aimed at 0xa0000 directly.

=== 000170c0 [PLATE]
Frame-paced presentation and input-wait loop for the unit status window: redraws the window, the unit's walk-cycle sprite and an optional idle animation into an off-screen 320x200 buffer, presents it to VGA memory, and returns the first input code <= 0x7f.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game presentation code]
Evidence: writes the mode-13h framebuffer literals 0xa0000 / 0xa0504 and calls the game's own fdps_draw_scene_layers (0002bf60), fdps_blit_rect (0002f2f0), fdps_cel_blit_sprite (0002dba0) and fdps_blit_dispatch (000568db); reads and writes the battle globals 0x60138 (unit sprite table), 0x63fc0 / 0x69d64 (tick counters), 0x60070 (video mode flag) and 0x643dc (cel handle); called only by game code (fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window, and fdps_unit_item_select_loop from its call site at 00025bd5). Its library calls (malloc, free, memmove, memset, rand) all run outward into the CRT, which is the game using the runtime, not the reverse. Too large and stateful to be a linker or compiler product; no CRT or Miles AIL shape.
Name: fdps pool naming rule (fdps_ + snake_case); no vendor symbol is involved and no Function ID candidate exists to collide with.
Boundary: 000170c0-00017524, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the entry and the matching 89 ec 5d 5f 5e 5b c3 epilogue at the end; all branches stay inside, and the 11 bytes that follow are lea/mov alignment padding before the next function at 00017530.
Signature: __cdecl, int (uchar *window_image, int unit_index, char allow_idle_animation), confirmed by the assembly -- arguments read from [EBP+0x14], [EBP+0x18] and byte [EBP+0x1c], result in EAX, RET with no immediate and every call site cleaning its own arguments with ADD ESP,n.

Algorithm:
Copies a 15-entry sprite row table from 0x14818 (15, 30, 70, 105, 140, 170, 150, 130, 150, 170, 160, 165, 165, 160, 170 -- a drop from the top of the screen followed by two bounces) into a local array and sets the idle-animation frame counter to -1 (inactive). When allow_idle_animation is non-zero it calls rand and, when the value is a multiple of 200, arms the idle animation by setting the frame counter to 0.

It then loops: poll the input source at 0x178f0; a returned code greater than 0x7f means nothing has been selected yet, so a frame is drawn. The frame is skipped entirely unless the global tick at 0x69d64 differs from the last-drawn tick at 0x63fc0.

Per frame: allocate a 0x15180-byte backing buffer and a 0xfa00-byte 320x200 work buffer, zero the work buffer, capture the current screen into the backing buffer (from 0xa0504 when the mode flag at 0x60070 is set, otherwise via 0x2bf60), copy it back into the work buffer, then free the backing buffer. The walk-cycle frame index is (tick at 0x63fc0 % 16) / 4 with 3 folded back to 1, giving the 0,1,2,1 cycle; it indexes the 0x30-byte per-unit record at the table based at 0x60138, whose four 0x0c-byte groups (offsets 0x00, 0x0c, 0x18, 0x24) hold the four facings, and each stored value is an offset added back to 0x60138 to form the sprite pointer. A 0x240-byte 24x24 scratch buffer receives the decoded cel, is blitted into window_image at offset 0xd21 (row 10, column 161), and window_image is then blitted into the work buffer as a 0x123 x 0xc8 region at offset 0xf.

When the idle animation is armed the frame counter drives five phases: frames 0..14 draw the facing at offset 0x00 at the table's row positions (the drop and the bounces); frames 15..24 draw that same facing standing at row 170, column 161. Both of those first two phases push 0x8 as the last argument of fdps_blit_dispatch (00017302 and 0001734f), which is fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_vertical, the top-bottom mirror -- the unit is drawn upside down for the whole drop and for the ten frames it lies at row 170, which is the visible point of the animation. Frames 25..34 draw the facing at offset 0x24 and frames 35..44 the facing at offset 0x0c, both at the same standing position and both pushing 0x0. As a fifth phase, after frame 44 a separate row counter starting at 170 draws the facing at offset 0x18 walking upward in steps of 4, also pushing 0x0, until it passes row 10, at which point the frame counter returns to -1 and the sprite reverts to the plain walk cycle.

The work buffer is presented to VGA memory at 0xa0000 (whole 64000-byte copy when the mode flag is clear, otherwise a 0x138 x 0xc0 rect blit at 0xa0504), both remaining buffers are freed, and the last-drawn tick is updated.

Rebuild note:
(1) idle_rise_row ([EBP-0x10]) is initialised to 0xaa once on entry and is never reset when the animation disarms at 0001749c, so a second arming inside the same call would play the four counted phases and then end at once; resetting it beside the frame counter is the natural tidy-up and it lets the rise play twice.
(2) The walk frame is taken from data_fdps_unit_status_window_last_tick (0x63fc0, read at 000171ec) and not from the live data_fdps_timer_tick_counter (0x69d64); the last-drawn tick is only brought up to date at the end of the pass, so reading the live counter -- the obvious reading -- shifts the whole walk cycle by one tick.

Parameters:
  window_image -- pointer to the 320-pitch composed status window image; the unit sprite is stamped into it at offset 0xd21 each frame
  unit_index -- index into the 0x30-byte-per-entry sprite table at 0x60138; overridden by the global at 0x63fb0 when the mode flag at 0x60070 is set
  allow_idle_animation -- non-zero enables the randomly triggered drop/bounce/turn/rise idle sequence

Returns:
  The input code returned by the poller at 0x178f0 once it is <= 0x7f.
  Only one of the two callers uses the value. fdps_unit_item_select_loop stores it (00025bdd MOV [EBP-0x20],EAX) and compares it against 0x48, 0x50, 0x1c, 0x39, 0x1 and 0x53; fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window discards it -- 00016bff LEA EAX,[EBP-0x44] overwrites EAX on the instruction after the ADD ESP,0xc, and nothing in that function stores or compares it -- so the battle status window closes on any code at or below 0x7f whichever key it was.

=== 00017525 [EOL]

=== 00017530 [PLATE]
Draws an integer into an 8bpp surface as a run of 6x8 digit sprites from the Number.cel sheet.

Algorithm:
Copies the 5-byte format template "%.3d" from 0x00014854 onto the stack. When digit_count is 0 it
formats value straight through the "%d" literal at 0x000615a8. Otherwise it builds limit = 10^digit_count
by multiplying 1 by ten digit_count times; when value >= limit it does not format at all but fills the
buffer with digit_count '?' characters and a NUL, and otherwise it overwrites the template's '3' with
'0' + digit_count and sprintf()s value through the resulting "%.Nd", so the figure comes out zero-padded
to digit_count digits. When show_plus is non-zero and value is not negative it prepends the "+" literal
at 0x000615ac: strcpy()s the text aside, stores "+" over the head of the buffer as a 2-byte word, and
strcat()s the saved text back on.
It then walks the formatted string one character at a time, mapping '0'-'9' to sprite 0..9, '+' to 10,
'-' to 11, '?' to 12 and anything else to 0, and adds 13 times the colour-row selector held in the global
at 0x0006000c -- NUMBER.CEL holds 65 sprites, five rows of those thirteen glyphs, and callers set that
global to 0..3 before the call and put it back to 0 afterwards. The sprite's RLE stream is taken from the
CEL offset table at +0x0f of the sheet pointer in the global at 0x000643d8, and each glyph is drawn by
fdps_blit_dispatch in mode 0 at dest + 6 * character index, 6 pixels wide by 8 high, on the caller's
pitch. The 6x8 size is hardcoded; the sheet header's own width and height fields are never read.

Parameters:
  dest -- pointer at the first digit cell inside the destination 8bpp surface; callers form it as
    surface + row * pitch + column
  pitch -- destination stride in bytes, handed straight to fdps_blit_dispatch
  value -- the signed integer to draw
  digit_count -- fixed field width in digits, 1..9; 0 draws the number at its natural width with no
    padding and with no overflow guard. A value needing more than digit_count digits is drawn as
    digit_count '?' glyphs instead
  show_plus -- non-zero draws a leading '+' in front of a non-negative value

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no library byte match; calls fdps_blit_dispatch and reads the game's Number.cel globals]

Rebuild note:
The digit_count == 0 case is a separate sprintf with a plain "%d", not the padded template. Folding the
two branches into sprintf(buf, "%.*d", digit_count, value) looks equivalent but prints nothing at all for
value 0 with digit_count 0, and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel does call it that way. Keep the two format
strings apart.

=== 000176e6 [EOL]
10 bytes NOP padding, one unreferenced fdps gauge-fill helper at 000176f0 (ratio -> 117px bar length, forwards to FUN_00017740), 3 bytes NOP padding

=== 000176f0 [PLATE]
Draws one 117x8 gauge bar filled in proportion to current/max, for callers that hold a stat pair rather than a pixel width.

No CALL in the image reaches this body: its two call sites, the HP and MP bars of fdps_draw_unit_status_panel, were expanded inline by the compiler, and the out-of-line copy is emitted anyway. The expansions are at 0001655e..000165d4 (bar_index 1, dest + 0x9396) and 000165f9..00016689 (bar_index 2, dest + 0xab56); each stages the five arguments into a block of locals, copies them into a second block, runs this body verbatim and calls fdps_draw_gauge_bar.

Algorithm:
When max is 0 or negative the fill width is 0, so the bar is drawn empty; there is no division in that path. Otherwise the width is the signed division (current * 0x75 + max - 1) / max, that is ceil(current * 117 / max) over the bar's full width of 0x75 (117) pixels -- adding max - 1 to the numerator rounds up, so any current of 1 or more still leaves at least one filled pixel. It then calls fdps_draw_gauge_bar(dst, dst_stride, bar_index, width), which blits the first width columns of gauge graphic bar_index out of the Bar.cel sheet pointed to by DAT_000643c8 (0x3a8 = 117*8 bytes per graphic) and fills the remaining 0x75 - width columns from graphic 0 at the start of the sheet, both through fdps_blit_transparent_rect at height 8.

Parameters:
  dst -- pointer to the top-left pixel of the bar in the destination surface; passed straight to fdps_draw_gauge_bar. Both call sites pass the panel framebuffer plus a fixed byte offset, dest + 0x9396 for HP and dest + 0xab56 for MP.
  dst_stride -- destination pitch in bytes, added to the destination cursor once per row; 0x140 (320) at every call site.
  bar_index -- which gauge graphic supplies the filled part of the bar, 0x3a8 bytes apart in the Bar.cel sheet at DAT_000643c8; 1 for the HP bar and 2 for the MP bar.
  max -- the value at which the bar reads full; 0 or less draws it empty.
  current -- the value to show, scaled against max.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [shared data and link direction: the callee draws the unit-status panel's 117x8 bar out of the game's own Bar.cel sheet at DAT_000643c8, and no Watcom or AIL Function ID candidate matches]

Rebuild note:
Three things here would come out wrong if written the obvious way.

1. The fill width is a ceiling, not a truncation: (current * 0x75 + max - 1) / max in signed 32-bit arithmetic. Writing the obvious current * 117 / max drops the bar to zero pixels as soon as current falls below max/117, where the original still shows a one-pixel sliver -- 1 HP left is visibly not 0 HP. The guard is also max > 0, not max != 0: a negative max must draw an empty bar rather than reach the divide, and the operands must stay signed int (the body uses IDIV after SAR EDX,0x1f), so declaring them unsigned changes the result for negative inputs.

2. fdps_draw_unit_status_panel must be written as two calls to this function, not with the scaling copied into it twice. The decompiler shows the scaling inline at both of its bars, which invites exactly that, and it would leave this function dead in src/ with its logic duplicated in three places. The image says otherwise: both sites are compiler expansions of this body, complete with the argument staging an inliner emits and a caller never would.

3. Reproducing that shape needs `-oe` on top of the flag set rebuild_info/build_flags.md records; without it the rebuild emits a CALL here. Nothing about the observable behaviour changes either way, so this is not an equivalence problem under ADR-0001, but the documented flag set is incomplete and a shape comparison against the original will disagree at every such site until it is fixed. Two smaller source-form points fall out of the same probe: the test is written zero-case-first, `if (max <= 0) w = 0; else w = (current * 117 + max - 1) / max;` -- writing the positive case first flips the JG to a JLE and swaps the two blocks under -od -- and the width goes through a named local rather than being written into the call's argument list.

=== 00017740 [PLATE]
Draws one 117x8 gauge bar filled to a caller-supplied pixel width, for callers that already hold a width rather than a stat pair.

Algorithm:
The bar art is the three 117x8 graphics fdps_load_global_resources decodes out of "Bar.cel" into the 0xaf8-byte buffer pointed to by data_fdps_status_gauge_bar_sheet_ptr, 0x3a8 (117*8) bytes apart; graphic 0 is the empty track and the others are the filled colours (fdps_draw_unit_status_panel uses 1 for HP and 2 for MP). The filled part is drawn first: when fill_width is positive, fdps_blit_transparent_rect copies fill_width columns by 8 rows from data_fdps_status_gauge_bar_sheet_ptr + bar_index * 0x3a8 at source pitch 0x75 to dst at pitch dst_stride. fill_width is then clamped up to 0, and if it is still below 0x75 the remainder is drawn from graphic 0: source data_fdps_status_gauge_bar_sheet_ptr + fill_width, that is the empty track advanced by the same number of columns, into dst + fill_width for 0x75 - fill_width columns by 8 rows, again through fdps_blit_transparent_rect, so palette index 0 in the art reads as transparent in both halves. There is no upper clamp: a fill_width above 0x75 draws only the first blit, at that oversized width.

Parameters:
  dst -- pointer to the top-left pixel of the bar in the destination surface. fdps_draw_unit_status_panel passes its 320x200 panel page plus a fixed byte offset, dest + 0x9396 for HP and dest + 0xab56 for MP.
  dst_stride -- destination pitch in bytes, added to the destination cursor once per row; 0x140 (320) at every call site.
  bar_index -- which 0x3a8-byte graphic in the sheet at data_fdps_status_gauge_bar_sheet_ptr supplies the filled part, 0 to 2; only the filled half honours it, the remainder always comes from graphic 0.
  fill_width -- filled width in pixels out of the bar's 0x75 (117). Zero or less draws an empty bar, 0x75 or more draws no remainder.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set and a unique hash in the image; it reads the game's own Bar.cel sheet global at data_fdps_status_gauge_bar_sheet_ptr and hard-codes this game's UI geometry (117 wide, 8 high)]

Rebuild note:
The clamping is deliberately one-sided: fill_width below 0 is forced to 0, but nothing caps it at 0x75, so an over-full gauge (current > max at the caller) blits more than 117 columns from a 117-byte-pitch source and skips the remainder entirely -- adding the symmetric if (fill_width > 0x75) fill_width = 0x75 makes an over-full bar draw as a clean full bar where the original draws a smeared oversized one. Also, only the filled half is taken from bar_index: the unfilled remainder is always data_fdps_status_gauge_bar_sheet_ptr + fill_width, i.e. graphic 0, so writing the obvious "same graphic, later columns" for the second blit paints the whole bar in the filled colour.

=== 000177d0 [PLATE]
Loads one 125x100 portrait out of the game data file FACE.CEL, keeps it in the portrait buffer at DAT_00060120 and blits it once into the caller's surface; a portrait_index of -1 only releases the buffer.

Algorithm:
Frees whatever DAT_00060120 still points at and clears the global -- this happens on every call, so at most one portrait is ever resident. When portrait_index is exactly -1 the function returns there, leaving the buffer empty. Otherwise it opens "FACE.CEL" with fopen(name, "rb") and, if that fails, prints "File not found: 'FACE.CEL'" and calls exit(1). It then fseeks to 0xf + portrait_index * 4 and freads 8 bytes: the record's own file offset and the offset of the record after it. FACE.CEL's directory holds 161 dwords for its 160 portraits, the last of them being end-of-file, so the difference between the pair is the record's byte length. That many bytes are malloc'd into DAT_00060120, the file is seeked back to the record offset, the record is fread in and the file is fclosed. Finally fdps_blit_dispatch draws it with width 0x7d (125) and height 0x64 (100) -- the sheet-wide sprite size recorded in the FACE.CEL header -- destination pitch dest_pitch and mode 0, the plain RLE decode. The buffer is still allocated when the function returns.

Parameters:
  dest -- destination 8bpp surface, already offset to the top-left corner the portrait is drawn at; handed to fdps_blit_dispatch as its dst. fdps_draw_unit_status_panel passes its panel buffer + 0x513, the two cutscene callers pass 0xa708c, i.e. the mode-13h screen at row 90, column 12.
  dest_pitch -- bytes per row of dest, forwarded to fdps_blit_dispatch as its pitch. Every caller passes 0x140 (320).
  portrait_index -- which portrait of FACE.CEL to load, 0..159, used as the index into the sheet's offset directory at file offset 0xf. -1 means "no portrait": release the buffer and draw nothing. fdps_draw_unit_status_panel takes it from the byte at unit record + 0x07, which is a portrait id and not the character id at + 0x08.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [game data file 'FACE.CEL', game-owned buffer global, calls fdps_blit_dispatch]

Rebuild note:
The loaded record deliberately outlives the call: fdps_prompt_two_choice, fdps_draw_text and fdps_message_window_wait_key each repaint the same 125x100 image straight out of DAT_00060120 whenever it is non-NULL, so that the portrait survives a panel redraw. Reading the record into a local buffer, or freeing it after the blit, compiles and draws correctly once and then loses the portrait on the next redraw. The buffer is released only by the next call to this function, by a call with portrait_index -1, by fdps_village_animate_window_zoom and by fdps_shutdown_free_resources.

=== 000178e1 [EOL]

=== 000178f0 [PLATE]
Reads the keyboard scancode latch and applies the game's auto-repeat policy, so a modal input loop can poll it once per frame and see one event per key press plus a slow repeat while the key stays down.

Algorithm:
Reads the raw scancode byte through fdps_keyboard_scancode_ptr -- the latch that the INT 09h handler fdps_keyboard_isr writes, whose no-key state is 0xff -- and compares it with the code the previous poll saw, held in data_fdps_input_key_repeat_prev_scancode. When it differs the key is new: the repeat counter data_fdps_input_key_repeat_counter is reset to 0, data_fdps_input_key_repeat_prev_scancode takes the new code, and the code is returned unchanged. When it is the same the key is still down: if the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 has not moved since the tick recorded in data_fdps_input_key_repeat_last_tick, the poll yields 0xff and changes nothing, so the counter advances at most once per timer tick however often the caller polls. Otherwise the counter is incremented, the result is suppressed to 0xff unless the counter has reached 5 and is a multiple of 3 -- so the first repeat lands on tick 6 and further repeats every 3 ticks -- and data_fdps_input_key_repeat_last_tick records the current tick. Every path ends with a call to fdps_flush_keyboard_queue, which drops whatever the ISR has buffered, so this poll works off the latch alone and discards keystrokes that arrived between calls. data_fdps_input_key_repeat_counter, data_fdps_input_key_repeat_prev_scancode and data_fdps_input_key_repeat_last_tick are referenced by no other function in the image: they are this filter's own state.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  The raw scancode of the key the caller should act on, or 0xff when there is nothing this poll -- either no key is down or a held key is still inside the repeat delay. Callers test only for the scancodes they care about, so the two cases need not be told apart.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library and a unique hash in this image; the body is application input policy over the game's own globals, with no CRT and no AIL idiom]

Rebuild note:
Two ways an obvious rewrite diverges. First, data_fdps_input_key_repeat_last_tick (the tick the filter last acted on) is written only on the held-key path where the tick had advanced; hoisting that assignment to the top of the function, or adding it to the new-key branch, is the natural tidy-up and shifts the start of the repeat delay by one tick because the original deliberately compares the new key's first held poll against a tick left over from an earlier key. Second, the routine reads the ISR's single scancode latch and then calls fdps_flush_keyboard_queue on every path, so buffered keystrokes are thrown away by design; rewriting it to consume from the queue via fdps_read_keyboard_queue would deliver key presses the original never reports.

=== 0001798d [EOL]
Alignment padding: 3-byte NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0] before entry at 00017990.

=== 00017990 [PLATE]
Modal two-option (left/right) prompt loop; returns the chosen option or -1 if cancelled.
Pool: fdps  [game renderer callees and game menu callers; no Function ID hit]
Evidence: Calls only the game's own drawing entry points (fdps_blit_rect, fdps_blit_dispatch, fdps_cel_blit_sprite, fdps_draw_scene_layers, fdps_cycle_scene_palette) plus fdps_flush_keyboard_queue (000567B3), fdps_read_keyboard_queue (000567BE), malloc/free and inp for VGA status port 0x3DA; all 22 call sites are game menu/shop/battle routines. Reads game globals 00060070, 00060120, 000643DC, 00069D64 and hard-codes VGA frame addresses and PC keyboard scancodes. Function ID matched nothing in CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 or ailv3.lib (0 candidates on both sides), and 770 bytes of application UI logic is not a linker artifact.
Name: fdps pool, descriptive fdps_ + snake_case name; no library symbol identified and none applies.
Boundary: 00017990-00017c91, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 E5 at the entry, matching epilogue and single RET at the end; the following 14 bytes are LEA/MOV alignment padding before the next function at 00017ca0.
Signature: __cdecl int fdps_prompt_two_choice(void) - no argument is read from the frame or from EAX/EDX/EBX/ECX, and the result is returned in EAX.

Algorithm:
1. Calls fdps_flush_keyboard_queue (000567B3), which rewinds the scancode ring's
   write index onto its read index, so anything queued before the prompt opened is
   discarded and the key that opened it cannot answer it. Then allocates a 0x561E
   byte buffer and copies a 302x73 (0x12E x 0x49) region of
   VGA memory at 0xA9609 into it at stride 302. The caller has already drawn the
   prompt panel there, so this captures the panel bitmap. The four corner pixels
   (offsets 0, 0x12D, 0x54F0, 0x561D) are then cleared to 0 so the later masked
   blit renders the panel with transparent (rounded) corners.
2. Loops until a confirm or cancel key arrives. Each iteration:
   - calls fdps_cycle_scene_palette and allocates a 0x15180 byte (360x240)
     off-screen work buffer;
   - if the flag at 00060070 is zero, hands the work buffer to
     fdps_draw_scene_layers to draw the background; otherwise copies the current
     312x192 screen area at 0xA0504 into the work buffer at offset 0x21D8
     (x=24, y=24, stride 360);
   - masked-blits the captured panel into the work buffer at offset 0xC4FD
     (x=29, y=140) via 0002F390;
   - if the pointer at 00060120 is non-null, draws it through fdps_blit_dispatch
     at work buffer offset 0x9AD0 (x=32, y=110);
   - draws the two option graphics from the cel sheet at 000643DC at x=249 and
     x=275, y=123. The unselected side uses a fixed cel (13 for the right slot,
     8 for the left); the selected side cycles a 4-frame animation, cels 4..7 on
     the left and 9..12 on the right, indexed by ((frame/3)%4);
   - waits for vertical retrace by polling port 0x3DA (bit 3 set, then clear),
     blits the work buffer back to the screen at 0xA0504 (312x192), spins until
     the tick counter at 00069D64 changes, records it as the animation frame,
     and frees the work buffer;
   - reads a scancode via 000567BE: 0x1C (Enter) or 0x39 (Space) confirms and
     keeps the current selection; 0x01 (Esc) or 0x53 (Del) exits with -1;
     0x4B (Left) selects 0; 0x4D (Right) selects 1. Codes >= 0x7F are ignored.
3. Frees the captured panel buffer and returns the selection.

Selection starts at 0, so the left option is highlighted on entry.

Parameters: none.

Returns: 0 or 1 for the confirmed option (left or right), -1 if cancelled.

=== 00017ca0 [PLATE]
Shows the current chapter's victory and defeat conditions over the battle map, as entry 0 of the in-battle system submenu.

Algorithm:
Copies six geometry/keyframe tables out of rodata onto the stack: the slide-in destination y table at 0x0001485c (4 strips x 19 frames), the strip x offsets at 0x0001498c, the strip source y offsets at 0x0001499c, the strip widths at 0x000149ac, the strip heights at 0x000149bc, and the slide-out y table at 0x000149cc (4 strips x 13 frames). Opens "MISC.VFS" with fdps_vfs_open, printing "file not found: 'Misc.vfs'" and calling exit(1) when it is missing; reloads the nine global data tables through fdps_load_data_tables, pulls "WinFail.Cel" out with fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit, and frees the archive handle. Allocates and zeroes a 0x6c95-byte page (209 x 133, pitch 0xd1), paints sprite 0 of WinFail.Cel into it with fdps_cel_blit_sprite, then stamps six numbers into it with fdps_draw_number: the chapter number DAT_00069cf4 + 1 in 2 digits at page (85,4), the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 in 3 digits at (131,4), the party gold DAT_000643a4 in 8 digits at (87,121), and the units still standing on side 0, side 2 and side 1 from fdps_battle_count_remaining_units_on_side in 2 digits each at (47,104), (119,104) and (174,104). The message renderer at 0x0001ff60 then draws message 2 of the chapter's fdetxt text block DAT_00060124 -- the victory condition -- at (35,22), and message 3 -- the defeat condition -- at (35,59).

The finished page is presented in three phases, every frame paced the same way: malloc a 0x15180-byte scene buffer (360 x 240, pitch 0x168), composite the live battle map into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers, blit page strips into it with fdps_blit_rect at destination x = strip_x + 0x4c and y = strip_y + 0x14, wait on VGA port 0x3da until the retrace bit 0x08 goes high and then low again, present the 312 x 192 window at buffer offset 0x21d8 to the screen at 0xa0504 with fdps_blit_rect, spin until the timer tick DAT_00069d64 changes, and free the buffer.
  - 19 slide-in frames: each strip's y comes from its row of the 0x0001485c table, and a negative y is clipped against the top of the window by moving the source down by -y and shortening the strip by the same amount.
  - Hold: fdps_flush_keyboard_queue, then the four strips are redrawn at their resting positions -- page (55,0) 99x16, (0,17) 209x82, (0,100) 209x16 and (69,117) 71x16 -- for as long as fdps_read_keyboard_queue keeps returning a byte of 0x80 or more.
  - 13 slide-out frames from the 0x000149cc table, each strip shortened so that it stops at y 200.
Ends with a second fdps_flush_keyboard_queue and frees the page.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX at the RET is whatever free() left in it and the caller does not look at it.

Pool: fdps  [game resources and game call graph; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
Keep the fdps_load_data_tables call on every open: it overwrites the nine global data-table pointers with fresh allocations and nothing frees the old ones, so each visit to this panel leaks the previous set -- hoisting the call out of the function or adding frees changes behaviour. The hold loop runs while the scancode is 0x80 or more, not while it equals the queue-empty value 0xff, so a key-release break code keeps the panel up and any make code dismisses it. The two slide phases clip differently -- top clip with a matching source shift on the way in, bottom clip at y 200 on the way out -- so folding them into one shared strip-drawing helper draws the wrong rows.

=== 000184f0 [PLATE]
Offers the unit that has just finished acting the chance to search the special map cell standing under the map cursor, and hands over whatever that cell holds.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_map_load_tile_info with the map cursor pixel position -- x from 0x00069cd4, y from 0x00069ccc, each divided by the 24-pixel tile size -- and then reads the two globals that call publishes: the cell code (word at 0x00069d06) and the tile attribute byte at 0x00069d08. It returns without doing anything unless attribute & 0x60 is 0x20 or 0x40, the two searchable-cell classes (0x20 is the class fdps_map_find_chest_cell hunts for), and unless the per-cell already-searched flag at 0x000640d8[cell_code] is still 0.
Opens the message window on the searching unit's portrait (byte +7 of the record fdps_get_unit_record returns) and puts up the prompt: message id 0x20a for class 0x20, 0x20b for class 0x40. fdps_prompt_two_choice returning non-zero is "no", and the function closes and reopens the window on message 0x20c and returns.
On "yes" it plays Chess.wav and reads the cell's 3-byte record out of the loaded map data block at 0x0006013c, at offset 0x53 + 3 * cell_code: the byte at +0 is the kind, the word at +1 the payload.
  kind 0 (an item): publishes the item's name message id (payload + 0xc9) in the message argument global at 0x00064030, closes and reopens the window, shows message 0x20d and calls fdps_unit_add_item(unit_index, payload). When it fits, 0x000640d8[cell_code] becomes 1 and fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes turns the cell's tile over. When the bag is full (-1) it shows message 0x20e and prompts again; on "yes" fdps_unit_item_select_window(unit_index, 0, &slot) lets the player pick one inventory slot, and fdps_unit_get_item_id / fdps_unit_remove_item / fdps_unit_add_item trade that item for the cell's, write the discarded item id back into the cell record's payload word, and announce it with message 0x20f through the second message argument global at 0x00064034. Cancelling either prompt shows message 0x210 instead.
  kind 1 (money): puts the payload in the numeric message argument global at 0x00064038, shows message 0x211 when it is zero and 0x212 otherwise, adds it to the party gold at 0x000643a4, sets 0x000640d8[cell_code] and calls fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes.
  kind 2 and above (scripted): waits 200 ms in delay(), closes the message window and calls the handler at data_fdps_chapter_event_handler_table[payload] with unit_index, leaving the searched flag and the tile to that handler.
Every message goes through fdps_draw_text with the text base at 0x000643c4 and the same fixed layout arguments (destination 0xaa44a in the mode 13h screen, pitch 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d).

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the searching unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array at 0x00069cd8; its portrait is shown, its inventory receives the item, and it is what the scripted handler is called with. fdps_battle_action_menu passes the unit whose turn it is.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in image]

Rebuild note:
The item-for-item trade path deliberately does not consume the cell: it writes the discarded item id back into the cell record at 0x0006013c and never sets the searched flag at 0x000640d8 nor calls fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes, so the cell holds the traded-away item and can be searched again -- marking the cell searched whenever the player accepts an item, which is the obvious way to write it, loses that. Two smaller traps in the same body: the kind >= 2 branch indexes the handler table at data_fdps_chapter_event_handler_table with the payload word and not with the kind byte, and message 0x20d is emitted before fdps_unit_add_item is attempted, so the "found it" line appears even when the bag turns out to be full.

=== 00018b40 [PLATE]
Returns a pointer to one item record of the table loaded from Item.dat, computing base + item_id * 23.

Algorithm:
Multiplies item_id by 0x17, the 23-byte stride of an ITEM.DAT record, adds the table base pointer held in the global at 0x00063fe0, and returns the sum. fdps_load_data_tables fills that global at 0001896c-00018981 by passing &DAT_00063fe0 and the string "Item.dat" to fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit, so the pointer is live from startup until fdps_free_global_resource_buffers releases it. The 23 bytes are: type at +0x00; the signed stat words ap, hit, dp and ev at +0x01, +0x03, +0x05 and +0x07; hit_effect and hit_effect_rate at +0x09 and +0x0a; range_min and range_max at +0x0b and +0x0c; use_effect at +0x0d; use_amount at +0x0e; use_distance, use_target and use_radius at +0x10, +0x11 and +0x12; price at +0x13; select_mode at +0x15; +0x16 is zero in every record.

Parameters:
  item_id -- item number, the index shared by ITEM.DAT and the item id byte stored in a unit's equipment slots. Nothing here bounds it: the table's own ids are 0x00-0xFA, but a larger id is scaled like any other and the rebuild note below depends on 0xFF arriving. On the equipment path the callers zero-extend it out of a byte: fdps_unit_equip_slot and fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets read it from unit record + 0x0a + 2 * slot + 1, fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot and fdps_draw_unit_inventory from the same slot pair while scanning the eight slots, fdps_shop_buy_loop and fdps_village_item_sell_loop from a shop or sell list entry. That zero-extension is not a property of all 25 callers: fdps_unit_can_equip_item passes its own second parameter through unmasked (00026012 MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBP+0x18] / 00026015 PUSH EAX / 00026016 CALL 0x00018b40), which moves the range question up to that caller's own callers.

Returns:
  Pointer to the 23-byte item record for item_id. Never bounds-checked, and not guaranteed non-NULL: the base is only valid once fdps_load_data_tables has filled the global, and before that item_id 0 returns a null pointer. Callers read byte +0x00 to classify the item (weapon, armour, consumable, badge), the stat words to modify a unit's combat totals, byte +0x0d to dispatch the use effect, and word +0x13 for the shop price.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID match in the Watcom or ailv3 sets; every caller is game-side and the only data reference is a game-owned table pointer]

Rebuild note:
Two ways the obvious rewrite diverges. The record must stay 23 packed bytes: declaring an item struct with the i16 fields at +0x01/+0x03/+0x05/+0x07 laid out naturally makes sizeof 24 and every lookup past index 0 lands on the wrong item, because the stride is hard-coded here as 0x17. And the missing bounds check is load-bearing: item id 0xFF is reachable in play and reads past the end of ITEM.DAT, which is what makes the guide's "FF BUG item" behave differently every time -- clamping or rejecting ids above 0xFA removes that behaviour (rebuild_info/pitfalls.md).

Returns a pointer to one record of the class equipment table loaded from PROEQU.DAT: the item types the class is allowed to equip.

Algorithm:
Multiplies class_index by 6, the PROEQU.DAT record stride, adds the table base pointer held in the global at 0x00063fe4, spills the sum to a stack local and reloads it into EAX as the return value. fdps_load_data_tables@00018930 fills that global at startup by loading "ProEqu.dat" through fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit, so the pointer is valid from startup until teardown. There is no null check on the base pointer and no bounds check on the index: the table holds 36 records, covering class codes 0x00..0x23, while class codes run to 0x27, so 0x24-0x27 address memory past its end.

The record is six bytes from the same value space as byte +0 of an ITEM.DAT record, the item type. They are a variable-length set, stored in ascending order and right-padded with 0xff -- not six fixed slots: in the shipped table a given type sits at whichever position the sorting puts it in, and records run from one type used (classes 0x19 and 0x1a) to all six. The only caller, fdps_unit_can_equip_item, scans all six positions identically and returns 1 when one of them equals the type of the item it was asked about, which makes this table the "which item types may this class equip" list. The 0xff padding never matches because no ITEM.DAT record carries type 0xff; one code that does appear in the table, 0x2d in the records for classes 0x20 and 0x21, is carried by no item either.

Parameters:
  class_index -- the unit's class code, taken straight from byte +0x20 of its 0x50-byte unit record. Passed raw, not incremented: the PROMAP.DAT accessor fdps_get_class_record is fed class code + 1, this one is not.

Returns:
  Pointer to the class's 6-byte record, i.e. base + class_index * 6. It is address arithmetic only and is never NULL while the table is loaded, whether or not the index is in range.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only data reference is the game global at 0x00063fe4, written by the game's own table loader, and its only reference is a static call from game logic]

Rebuild note:
Two ways the obvious rewrite diverges. (1) PROEQU.DAT is indexed by the raw class code, while its neighbour PROMAP.DAT is indexed by class code + 1 -- callers of fdps_get_class_record INC the unit record's byte +0x20 before calling, the caller of this one does not. Writing the equipment lookup by analogy with the class lookup and adding 1 shifts every class's permitted-equipment list by one record. The table is also 36 records against 40 class codes, so classes 0x24-0x27 read past its end and this accessor does not check. (2) The unused positions of a record hold 0xff, not 0, and the scan in fdps_unit_can_equip_item has no sentinel test at all -- it compares all six. Treating 0 as the empty marker is the intuitive reading and it is wrong twice over: 0x00 is a live item type, carried by 25 of the 251 ITEM.DAT records, so a table or a comparison written that way would let every class equip all of them.

=== 00018bc5 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx, 11 bytes to the 0x18bd0 boundary.

=== 00018bd0 [PLATE]
Returns a pointer to one record of the spell table loaded from MagicDat.dat, computing base + spell_id * 7.

Algorithm:
Multiplies spell_id by 7 and adds the spell table base pointer held in the global at 0x00063ff0, which fdps_load_data_tables fills by loading "MagicDat.dat" through fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit. The stride of 7 is the MAGICDAT.DAT record: signed word power at +0x00, hit rate at +0x02, cast distance at +0x03 (bit 0x10 means straight line, low nibble the range), area radius at +0x04, MP cost at +0x05, target side at +0x06 (0 enemy, 1 own side, and 3 on spell 0x16). The table holds 40 records and the index is not checked against that count.

Parameters:
  spell_id -- spell number, 0x00-0x27, the index into MAGICDAT.DAT. Callers pass the spell or effect id they are working on; the caller at 0x00028f70 forces 0x14 for every effect code outside 0x11-0x13, and the caller at 0x00013c90 passes the AI's selected spell id from the global at 0x00063f90.

Returns:
  Pointer to the first byte of the record. Never NULL, and never range-checked, so an out-of-range spell_id yields a pointer past the end of the table.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set; called only by game code, and its one data reference is the game table base at 0x00063ff0, not a CRT or AIL state area]

Rebuild note:
The MAGICDAT.DAT record is 7 bytes with no padding even though it starts with a signed 16-bit field, so a C rewrite that declares the natural struct { short power; unsigned char hit, distance, radius, mp, target; } and writes spell_table[spell_id] gets stride 8 and reads the wrong record from spell 1 onward -- the record type has to be packed (or the address computed as base + spell_id * 7 by hand) to reproduce the original.

=== 00018c60 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the six-entry horizontal knockback ramp of the full-screen combat animation: the pixel x displacements {0, 4, 9, 14, 18, 14} of the sprite that has just been hit.

Nothing writes it. It is read once per call, at the top of fdps_combat_play_blow, where MOV ECX,0x6 / MOVSD.REP copies all 0x18 bytes into that function's auto array at EBP-0x80; the image at 00018c78 is copied to EBP-0x98 in the same breath and is the matching vertical ramp {0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10}. The index is the recoil counter that fdps_combat_play_blow keeps in its own frame: it starts at 0, a landed blow (hit outcome word 0 == 0) sets it to 5, and every composed frame that finds it non-zero decrements it by one, so the array is walked backwards from element 5 to element 0. Per frame the function computes x = sign * recoil_x[counter] + 0x18 and y = sign * recoil_y[counter] + 0x18 into the composite-sprite request it hands to fdps_draw_composite_sprite for the defender's Stand%03d.saf sprite; sign is -1 when the attacker's side byte (unit record +6) is non-zero and +1 when it is 0, so the struck unit is always thrown away from the striker. The vertical ramp is applied only when the attack has no travelling lead-in; the horizontal one is applied on every frame. Because the walk is backwards, the visible motion is 14, 18, 14, 9, 4, 0 -- the sprite is knocked out, overshoots by one frame, then slides back to rest. Element 0 being zero is what returns the sprite to its stand position when the counter reaches 0 and stays there for the rest of the blow.

fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets holds a byte-identical pair of images of its own at 00018c90 and 00018ca8 and uses them the same way for spell knockback.

Pool: binary_artifact  [the counted MOVSD.REP into a stack local, with no memcpy call and a second identical copy of the same six values for the other function, is wcc386's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so these bytes are the compiler's output rather than a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
The ramp is read from element 5 down to element 0, so it is stored in the opposite order to the motion it produces and its last element (14) is smaller than the one before it (18). Writing the visually obvious monotone ramp, or 'correcting' the final 14 to 18, changes the knockback animation. It is also an auto array of fdps_combat_play_blow, not a file-scope const: hoisting it and sharing one copy with fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets is the wrong shape.

=== 00018c78 [PLATE]

=== 00018ca8 [PLATE]
Six-entry y-offset table for the knockback shudder a landed spell hit gives its target, held as the rodata image of a local array initialiser: {0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10}.

Nothing writes it; it is read-only data in .object1. fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets copies all 24 bytes into a stack local on entry (0001a4fe MOV ESI,0x18ca8 / 0001a503 MOVSD.REP, six dwords) alongside the matching x table at 00018c90, and reads the copy in one place only, at 0001afea, once per drawn frame of phase 3: the target's composite-sprite origin y becomes 0x18 - table[frame] * knockback_sign. frame is the knockback counter at [EBP-0x48]; knockback_sign is the +1/-1 at [EBP-0x34], set at 0001a67b/0001a684 from byte +0x06 of the caster's unit record -- -1 for side 0 (enemy), +1 for any other side -- so the two sides are shoved in opposite directions.

The counter is armed only by a hit that landed: the main clip's hit frame (byte +0x05 of the SAF frame, tested at 0001aeee) sets it to 5 at 0001af00, but only when the miss flag [EBP-0x4] is clear, which fdps_spell_damage_unit's zero return sets at 0001ae6b. === 00018cc0 [PLATE]
Per-spell palette colour-band base for the recolour flash a landed spell hit gives its target on the combat screen: 40 dwords, one per spell id 0x00-0x27, held as the rodata image of a local array initialiser.

Nothing writes the image. fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets copies all 0xa0 bytes onto its stack at 0001a515 (MOVSD.REP, 0x28 dwords, destination EBP-0x26c) and reads the copy in one place, at 0001b00c, once per drawn frame: selector = 0x30000 + table[spell_id] * 0x100 + phase, where spell_id is the function's second parameter and phase is the counter at EBP-0x40 that steps (phase + 1) % 8 every frame. The selector goes into field +0x1c of the composite-sprite request, travels through fdps_draw_composite_sprite and fdps_draw_tilemap_cell into fdps_blit_dispatch, and is taken apart by the mode-3 kernel fdps_rle_blit_recolor as three bytes: +0x1c tint_offset = the cycling phase, +0x1d color_base = this table's entry, +0x1e band mask = 3. Every pixel the struck target's sprite writes therefore becomes ((src + phase) & 3) + table[spell_id], so the entry names the first index of the four-colour palette band the target is flashed in, and the phase rotates which of the four each pixel lands on.

Entries group by element rather than by spell: 0xd6 for the fire spells (0x00-0x02, 0x19, 0x1c, 0x1f, 0x23, 0x24), 0xe0 for the light spells (0x03, 0x04, 0x1a), 0x28 for the lightning spells (0x05-0x07, 0x1b, 0x1e, 0x20, 0x27), 0xa0 for the ice spells (0x08, 0x09, 0x25, 0x26), 0x48 for the two gravity spells (0x0c, 0x22), 0x20 for the dark spells (0x0d, 0x17) and 0xb4 for 0x1d alone. Thirteen entries are 0, and they are exactly the ids 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0e-0x16, 0x18 and 0x21 that fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets hands to fdps_cast_spell_on_targets at 0001a551 before it ever reaches this code -- the spells with no combat-screen presentation. A 0 here is unreachable filler, not a colour band at index 0.

Pool: binary_artifact  [compiler output, not a source-level global: both references are the address load and the block copy that plant the 40 dwords in a stack local, which is how Watcom 10.0a emits an initialised auto array]
