=== 00018d60 [PLATE]
Runs one attack on the game's full-screen combat screen: switches the shared palette and blend tables into fight mode, plays the attacker's blow and then the defender's counterblow with the two combatants' SAF sprites over their terrain backdrops, and puts the map's palette and tables back before returning. It is the alternative to the on-map attack that fdps_unit_attack_target plays; both callers pick one or the other for the same blow.

Algorithm:
1. Clears the pending-experience accumulator DAT_00069cec that fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up later banks into the acting unit.
2. Reads the fight-palette blend tables off disk: FMer1.tmp -> 0x4800 bytes at DAT_000653f0 (the 18-row brightness ramp table) and FMer2.tmp -> 0x1000 bytes at DAT_000643f0 (the 16x16x16 RGB-to-palette-index cube). fdps_load_global_resources writes that pair at startup from Fight.pal and the Mer1.tmp/Mer2.tmp pair from Fde.pal; step 12 reads the Fde pair back. Neither fopen result is checked.
3. Loads FigBar.cel from MISC.VFS into DAT_00064004 and composes the gauge-frame strip DAT_00064000 that fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges draws from: malloc of 0x9c4 (2500) bytes, then four fdps_cel_blit_sprite calls writing sheet entries 4..7 at pitch 0x7d (125), x 0, y = i*5.
4. fdps_get_unit_record on both indices, and takes the sprite-set byte at record+7 of each.
5. Formats "Stand%03d.saf" from the defender's record+7 byte, loads it from Fight.vfs into the playback cursor at [EBP-0x44], then does the same for the attacker into the cursor at [EBP-0x50]. Each cursor is a 12-byte stack record whose +8 field holds the clip pointer, primed by fdps_saf_advance_tick with mode 1.
6. Formats "Act%03d.saf" from the attacker's record+7 byte, loads it from FigAct.vfs, and takes the byte at offset 4 of its frame 0 (fdps_saf_get_frame(clip, 0)) as the clip's lead-in frame count. That is the frame+0x04 field resource_info/saf.md documents: fdps_combat_play_blow reads the same byte off the same frame at 000198b2 and runs that many lead-in frames of the Act clip before its main loop, and it is across those frames that fdps_combat_slide_backdrops moves the view from one terrain to the other. This body only tests the count against zero.
7. When fdps_check_can_counter_attack says the defender may strike back, loads the defender's Act%03d.saf as well; otherwise that slot stays NULL, and so does the second backdrop slot.
8. Spins on VGA input status port 0x3da until retrace bit 3 is set.
9. Resolves the defender's terrain backdrop: fdps_map_load_tile_info with the defender's tile x/y from record+0/+1, then takes the backdrop id the call leaves in DAT_00069d0b, decrements it in place when it is above zero (the tile carries the id 1-based, the file name is 0-based), formats "Back%02d.saf" and loads it from BackGrnd.vfs. When the lead-in count is non-zero, that backdrop is moved into the second slot at [EBP-0x30] and the same three steps run again for the attacker's tile, so the screen opens on the attacker's terrain and the blow's lead-in slides across to the defender's; a clip with no lead-in gets the defender's terrain alone and a NULL second slot.
10. fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643e4 = Fight.pal, 0, 0xff, 0, 0, 0), then fdps_combat_slide_in_attacker with the lead-in count handed straight to its attacker_only parameter -- a clip with a lead-in brings the attacker on alone, because the defender stands on the terrain the view has not reached yet -- then fdps_combat_play_blow with the attacker acting and the pair (opening backdrop, second slot) as its from/to backdrops. That call is what drains the defender's HP.
11. When fdps_combat_play_blow returns nonzero (the defender is still standing) and fdps_check_can_counter_attack still agrees, fdps_combat_play_blow runs again with the unit indices, the Act clips and the two SAF cursors swapped: that pass is the counterblow. The second fdps_check_can_counter_attack call is not a repeat of the first. fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome, reached from inside the blow, writes rand()%2 + 2 into the defender's record+0x26 at 0001a209 when the blow lands an ailment, and that byte is the first thing fdps_check_can_counter_attack rejects on -- so an ailment the attacker just inflicted cancels the counterblow. The write can only turn the answer from yes to no; nothing on the path clears the byte, so the defender's Act clip loaded in step 7 is always present when the counterblow runs.
12. Teardown: fdps_audio_stop_sample(-1); frees the backdrop, both Stand clips and the attacker's Act clip, plus the defender's Act clip and the second backdrop when they were loaded; frees DAT_00064004 and DAT_00064000; memsets the 64000 bytes of VGA memory at 0xa0000 to 0; fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc = Fde.pal, 0, 0xff, 0, 0, 0); and reads Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp back into DAT_000653f0 and DAT_000643f0.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit_index -- index of the striking unit into the 0x50-byte unit records at DAT_00069cd8; both callers pass the unit that is acting, and it goes to fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_check_can_counter_attack, fdps_combat_slide_in_attacker and fdps_combat_play_blow as the attacker.
  defender_unit_index -- index of the struck unit in the same array; fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack passes the AI's chosen target from DAT_00063f74, fdps_battle_action_menu the target the player picked.

Returns:
  Nothing. Neither caller reads EAX after the call.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; FDPS resource strings and game callees, with the C runtime used only as a consumer]

Rebuild note:
Two places where the obvious C is wrong.
  * In the counterblow pass every argument is swapped except the backdrops: fdps_combat_play_blow is handed the same backdrop pointer for both its from- and to-backdrop arguments. Writing that call as the mirror image of the first one -- giving it the (defender terrain, attacker terrain) pair the first pass got -- makes the combat view slide terrain during the counterblow, which the original never does.
  * fdps_check_can_counter_attack must be called twice, at 00018f73 and again at 000190ed. Hoisting the first answer into a local and reusing it -- which is what the two identical-looking calls invite -- lets a defender that this very blow has just disabled strike back, because the test reads record+0x26, which the blow writes.

=== 00019248 [EOL]
Watcom inter-function alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6-byte nop) + mov edx,edx (2-byte nop), aligning 00019250 to 16 bytes

=== 00019250 [PLATE]
Paints the filled run of one combat status gauge to an explicit pixel length, into a gauge frame the caller has already blitted.

Algorithm:
Resolves the gauge's fill artwork as data_fdps_gauge_fill_sheet_ptr + gauge_index * 0x271 (IMUL at 0001925c). data_fdps_gauge_fill_sheet_ptr is the malloc(0x9c4) scratch surface that fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange builds at 00018e15-00018e68 and fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets builds identically at 0001a603-0001a653: four passes of fdps_cel_blit_sprite(FigBar.cel, i + 4, data_fdps_gauge_fill_sheet_ptr, pitch 0x7d, x 0, y i * 5) for i = 0..3, i.e. sprites 4..7 of MISC.VFS's FigBar.cel decoded into one 125-pitch surface, five rows apart. 0x9c4 = 2500 = 4 * 0x271 = 4 * 125 * 5 exactly, so gauge_index * 0x271 is the top-left of band gauge_index and the 125x5 geometry is pinned rather than inferred. Clamps a negative fill_width up to 0. Then, when gauge_index is below 2, advances both the strip pointer and dest by (0x7d - fill_width), so those gauges fill from the right edge of their 125-pixel span inward and take the right-hand end of the strip artwork, while gauge_index 2 and above fill from the left; fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges picks the base index 0 or 2 from unit record byte +0x06, which is what makes the two panel layouts mirror each other. Finally, only when fill_width does not exceed 0x7d, calls fdps_blit_transparent_rect(strip, 0x7d, dest, dest_stride, fill_width, 5) -- palette index 0 of the strip reads as transparent, so the frame underneath shows through the bar's shaped edges. Nothing is drawn for the empty remainder of the span and nothing is erased, so a shortening gauge only reads correctly because the caller redraws the frame cel first. That is also what separates this routine from its two cousins, which do paint the remainder: fdps_draw_gauge_bar (117x8, Bar.cel) blits the unfilled run from image 0, and fdps_draw_unit_gauge (43x6, EasyBar.cel) does the same plus two end caps.

Parameters:
  dest -- pixel address of the fill run's top-left corner in the destination surface, at the left end of the gauge's 125-pixel span; shifted right by (125 - fill_width) internally for gauge_index below 2. fdps_draw_stat_gauge forwards it unchanged; fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges builds it as panel origin + dest_stride * row + column.
  dest_stride -- bytes per row of that destination surface, passed through to fdps_blit_transparent_rect untouched.
  gauge_index -- which of the four 125x5 fill strips in the data_fdps_gauge_fill_sheet_ptr scratch surface to use, at a 0x271-byte stride; strip N is FigBar.cel sprite N + 4, and fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges blits FigBar.cel sprite N as that gauge's frame, so frame N and fill N + 4 are a matched pair. It passes 0 and 1 for one panel layout and 2 and 3 for the other. Values below 2 additionally select right-to-left filling.
  fill_width -- how many pixels of bar to paint, 0 to 0x7d = 125. Negative is clamped to 0 (an empty bar); above 125 nothing is drawn at all.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX at the RET is whatever fdps_blit_transparent_rect left there, or untouched on the skipped path, and no caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in the Watcom or ailv3 sets and a unique body hash; its only data reference is the game global data_fdps_gauge_fill_sheet_ptr and its constants are game gauge geometry]

Rebuild note:
Two things a faithful rewrite gets wrong by writing the obvious C. First, fill_width above 0x7d skips the blit entirely (CMP [EBP+0x20],0x7d / JG at 00019297-0001929b), so an over-full gauge draws blank rather than full -- adding the natural min(125, fill_width) would make it read full, and both callers hand over an unclamped ceiling (cur * 125 + max - 1) / max that exceeds 125 whenever cur > max. Second, gauge_index below 2 fills right-to-left by adding (125 - fill_width) to the source pointer as well as to dest, so the bar shows the rightmost fill_width pixels of the strip at the right end of the span; writing the obvious left-aligned blit for all indices, or right-aligning the destination while still taking the strip's leftmost pixels, would each put the wrong artwork in the mirrored panel's two gauges. Both depend on data_fdps_gauge_fill_sheet_ptr being one contiguous 125-pitch surface of four stacked bands rather than four separate images: the source pointer walks within a band using src_stride 125, which is only the band width because the builders decode FigBar.cel sprites 4..7 into a single malloc(0x9c4) buffer five rows apart.

=== 000192c0 [PLATE]
Draws one unit status gauge filled to a current-over-maximum ratio, scaled onto the gauge's 125-pixel span.

Algorithm:
Computes the fill length in pixels first: 0 when max is not positive (the test is JG, so max == 0 and every negative max give an empty gauge and never divide), otherwise the signed ceiling (cur * 0x7d + max - 1) / max via IMUL / MOV EAX,EDX / SAR EDX,0x1f / IDIV. Because it rounds up, cur == max fills all 0x7d = 125 pixels and any cur >= 1 still leaves a one-pixel sliver showing. The length is not clamped at the top: cur > max produces more than 0x7d, and fdps_draw_gauge_fill skips its blit outright above 0x7d, so an over-full gauge disappears instead of reading full. Then pushes dest, dest_stride and gauge_index through unchanged together with that length to fdps_draw_gauge_fill, which resolves the gauge's 125x5 fill strip as *(char **)DAT_00064000 + gauge_index * 0x271 (0x271 = 625 = 125 * 5), right-aligns the fill for gauge_index < 2, and hands it to fdps_blit_transparent_rect with width = length and height = 5. The frame is a plain Watcom -4s frame with one local for the length; ADD ESP,0x10 after the call cleans the four arguments.

The artwork it draws through exists only while the full-screen combat animation is up: fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange mallocs the 0x9c4 = 2500 bytes at DAT_00064000 on the way in and composes them from FigBar.cel sheet entries 4..7 with fdps_cel_blit_sprite at pitch 0x7d and y = i * 5 -- the four 125x5 strips gauge_index selects -- then frees the buffer at teardown. Calling this outside a combat exchange would read a freed pointer.

The identical scaling and the same call appear twice inlined inside fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges, which draws one unit's two gauges from the unit record's stat pairs at +0x40/+0x42 (current/maximum HP) and +0x44/+0x46 (current/maximum MP); this out-of-line copy has no call sites of its own.

Parameters:
  dest -- pixel address of the gauge's top-left corner in the destination surface; passed straight to fdps_draw_gauge_fill, which offsets it and gives it to fdps_blit_transparent_rect as the destination pointer.
  dest_stride -- bytes per row of that destination surface; passed through to the same blit. The combat animation buffers in this cluster are 0x170 bytes wide.
  gauge_index -- which of the four 125x5 FigBar.cel fill strips to draw, indexing the sheet at *(char **)DAT_00064000 with a 0x271-byte stride; fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges uses 0 and 1 for one panel layout and 2 and 3 for the mirrored one. Values below 2 also select right-to-left filling inside fdps_draw_gauge_fill.
  max -- the stat's maximum, the divisor and the gate: not greater than 0 means draw nothing. Maximum HP (+0x42) or maximum MP (+0x46) at the inlined call sites.
  cur -- the stat's current value, numerator of the ratio; signed, and read as a signed 16-bit field of the unit record -- current HP (+0x40) or current MP (+0x44).

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX at the RET is whatever fdps_draw_gauge_fill left behind and no caller may use it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in Watcom 10.0x or ailv3.lib; game presentation logic that reaches the game global DAT_00064000 through its only callee]

Rebuild note:
The fill length is a ceiling, (cur*125 + max - 1)/max, not the obvious cur*125/max, so a unit on 1 HP out of 200 still shows a one-pixel sliver instead of an empty gauge; and there is deliberately no upper clamp -- when cur > max the length exceeds 125 and fdps_draw_gauge_fill skips the blit, leaving the gauge blank, so adding the obvious min(125, len) would make an over-full gauge draw full where the original draws nothing.

=== 0001930d [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] (8d 40 00), 3-byte NOP form

=== 00019310 [PLATE]
Draws one battle unit's HP and MP gauges into a combat animation frame: blits the pair of FigBar.cel gauge frames at the corner belonging to that unit's side, then fills each bar to its current-over-maximum share of the gauge's 125-pixel span.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads the record's four signed 16-bit stat fields: current HP at +0x40, maximum HP at +0x42, current MP at +0x44, maximum MP at +0x46. Byte +0x06 is the unit's side code (2 = player side, 0 = enemy side) and selects one of two panel layouts. A non-zero side moves the panel origin to dest_base + dest_stride * 0x20 + 0xc3, takes gauge strips 0 and 1, and starts the bars 1 pixel into the frame; side 0 moves it to dest_base + dest_stride * 0xc7 + 0x1e, takes strips 2 and 3, and starts the bars 0x13 pixels in. Strip indices below 2 also make fdps_draw_gauge_fill fill from the right, so the two panels are mirror images of each other, one in the upper right and one in the lower left of the 0x170-pixel-wide animation frame.
Blits the two gauge frames out of the FigBar.cel sheet held in data_fdps_combat_gauge_sprite_sheet_ptr with fdps_cel_blit_sprite: sprite index base at y 0 and index base+1 at y 10, both at x 0 relative to the shifted panel origin, both in blit mode 0.
Then paints the two bars. For each stat pair the fill length is 0 when the maximum is not greater than 0 (the test is JG, so a zero or negative maximum draws an empty bar and never divides), otherwise the signed ceiling (cur * 0x7d + max - 1) / max, 0x7d = 125 being the gauge's pixel span. Both lengths go to fdps_draw_gauge_fill, HP at panel origin + dest_stride * 2 + column with strip index base, MP at panel origin + dest_stride * 0xc + column with strip index base+1. Neither length is clamped at the top, and fdps_draw_gauge_fill skips its blit outright above 0x7d, so a current value above the maximum makes that bar disappear instead of reading full.

Parameters:
  dest_base -- base of the 8bpp destination surface the animation frame is being composed in; the panel origin is this plus the side-dependent row and column offsets. Handed to fdps_cel_blit_sprite as its dest_base. All three callers (0x000194e0, 0x000196d0, 0x0001a4c0) pass the 0x16480-byte off-screen frame buffer they allocated.
  dest_stride -- bytes per row of that surface, used both as the row multiplier for the panel offsets and as the pitch passed to fdps_cel_blit_sprite and fdps_draw_gauge_fill. Every call site passes the constant 0x170.
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array, passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, which does not bounds-check it. Callers pass the attacker's unit index, the defender's, or one entry of a target id list.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX at the RET is whatever fdps_draw_gauge_fill left behind and no caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_cel_blit_sprite and decodes game unit-record stat fields; no Function ID hit in the Watcom or ailv3 sets]

Rebuild note:
The bar length is a rounded-up ratio, not a truncated one: (cur * 125 + max - 1) / max, so any current value of 1 or more still shows a sliver of bar and cur == max fills all 125 pixels. Writing the obvious cur * 125 / max gives a bar one pixel short over most of its range and an empty bar at low HP, which is exactly the reading the player watches during the attack animation. The expression must also be left unclamped at the top: fdps_draw_gauge_fill draws nothing at all above 125, so adding the upper clamp a rebuilder would naturally add changes the picture whenever cur exceeds max.

=== 000194d9 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea NOP plus 0x90, aligning FUN_000194e0 to 16 bytes.

=== 000194e0 [PLATE]
Plays the entrance of the full-screen combat animation: the attacker slides onto the combat screen from his own side while the terrain backdrop rises into place under him.

Algorithm:
Allocates a 0x16480-byte off-screen surface of 0x170 (368) bytes per row by 0xf8 (248) rows -- the 320x200 screen plus a 24-pixel margin on every side -- and builds a composite-sprite draw request on the stack over it (dest, 0x170 stride, 0xf8 height, x, y, resource base, entry index, 0, 0), so request x/y (0x18,0x18) is screen (0,0). Takes the acting unit's record with fdps_get_unit_record and reads the side byte at record+6: side 0 gives a horizontal step of -15 per frame, any other side +15, so the attacker always comes in from his own edge of the screen.
Then, for a frame counter i running 8 down to 0, one pass per timer tick:
  - memset the surface to palette index 0;
  - draw entry 0 of backdrop with fdps_draw_composite_sprite at x = 0x18, y = i*0x14 + 0x18, so the backdrop starts 160 pixels low and rises 20 pixels a frame;
  - when attacker_only is 0, advance defender_saf_cursor with fdps_saf_advance_tick, draw its current entry at (0x18,0x18) -- the defender's final standing position, it never moves -- and paint the defender's HP/MP bars with fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges;
  - advance attacker_saf_cursor, set x = i*(+/-15) + 0x18 and draw its current entry, then paint the attacker's HP/MP bars. The request's y field is left as the previous draw wrote it: 0x18 when the defender was drawn, and the backdrop's own i*0x14 + 0x18 when attacker_only is set, so in that mode the attacker rides down with the backdrop instead of moving only sideways;
  - poll port 0x3da until the vertical retrace begins and then until it ends, blit the 320x200 window at surface+0x2298 (row 24, column 24) to the mode 13h frame buffer at 0xa0000 with fdps_blit_rect, then spin until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from the latched copy and re-latch it. That latch is not initialised before the loop, so the first frame's wait ends against whatever was on the stack.
Frees the surface and returns. At i = 0 every element is at its final position, which is the state the caller's own attack animation loop takes over.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array of the acting unit; its side byte decides the entry direction and its bars are drawn every frame. FUN_00018d60 passes its attacker, FUN_0001a4c0 its caster.
  defender_unit_index -- index of the unit on the receiving end; used only to draw its HP/MP bars, and only when attacker_only is 0. FUN_0001a4c0 passes the first entry of its target list.
  attacker_only -- when non-zero the defender is not drawn or gauged at all and the attacker slides in diagonally with the backdrop. FUN_00018d60 takes it from byte +4 of frame 0 of the attacker's Act%03d.saf and, when it is set, hands over the attacker's own terrain backdrop rather than the defender's; FUN_0001a4c0 always passes 0.
  attacker_saf_cursor -- SAF playback cursor for the attacker's Stand%03d.saf: dword 0 is the entry index, dword 2 the resource base, both read straight into the draw request.
  defender_saf_cursor -- the same cursor for the defender's Stand%03d.saf. Read only when attacker_only is 0, though both callers always pass a live cursor.
  backdrop -- the Back%02d.saf terrain resource loaded from BackGrnd.vfs; entry 0 of it is drawn as the backdrop.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [built on fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_saf_advance_tick, fdps_draw_composite_sprite, fdps_blit_rect; both callers are game code]

Rebuild note:
The composite-sprite request is one struct that is only partly rewritten between the three draws of a frame, and the motion depends on the leftovers: the attacker draw inherits its y from whichever draw ran before it, which is the backdrop's rising y when attacker_only is set. Filling in every field of the request before each draw -- the obvious way to write it -- pins the attacker at y = 0x18 and kills the diagonal entry.

=== 000196c1 [EOL]
Alignment padding: three Watcom multi-byte NOP forms filling 15 bytes to the 16-byte entry of FUN_000196d0.

=== 000196d0 [PLATE]
Plays one unit's blow on the full-screen combat animation and drains the damage out of the defender as the impact frames go by, handing the caller the defender's remaining HP.

Algorithm:
Copies the two const dword[6] recoil ramps at 00018c60 {0,4,9,14,18,14} and 00018c78 {0,2,4,6,8,10} onto the stack -- the horizontal and vertical displacement of the struck sprite, read through a counter that is set to 5 by a landed blow and walks back down to 0 one step per frame -- and mallocs the 0x16480-byte (368x248) offscreen surface that the 0x24-byte composite-sprite request on the stack draws into (stride 0x170 at req+4, height 0xf8 at req+8).

Counts the frames of act_clip whose byte at frame+5 is non-zero: those are the impact frames the damage is paid out over, and the count is forced to 1 when the clip has none. Resolves both unit records with fdps_get_unit_record and the attacker's equipped weapon with fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot(attacker, 0), fdps_unit_get_item_id and fdps_get_item_record. The blow is struck twice when that weapon's effect byte (item+9) is 2 -- the double-strike attribute of ITEM.DAT -- or when either of two independent rand() % 100 < 3 rolls comes up.

Each blow re-reads the defender's HP word (unit record +0x40), calls fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome into a six-dword outcome block, and primes the act_clip playback cursor with fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 1). Byte 4 of act_clip's frame 0 is the travelling-attack lead-in count: when it is non-zero, that many frames play over from_backdrop with only the attacker's gauges on screen, then fdps_combat_slide_backdrops carries the view across to to_backdrop with defender_stand_cursor riding in on it, and the two backdrop arguments are swapped in place.

The per-tick loop then composes each frame: memset of the surface, entry 0 of the current backdrop, the defender's sprite from defender_stand_cursor at x = sign * recoil_x + 0x18 and y = sign * recoil_y + 0x18, and act_clip's current frame at (0x18, 0x18). sign is -1 when the attacker's side byte (record+6) is non-zero and +1 when it is 0, so the defender is thrown away from the attacker; the vertical ramp is used only when there is no lead-in, and is 0 otherwise. On the first tick of an impact frame the defender's HP word becomes start_hp - blows_paid * outcome[5] / impact_frames, floored at 0. A landed blow (outcome[0] == 0) sets the recoil counter to 5 and puts 0x28000/3 in the request's blend fields (req+0x1c, req+0x20) so the struck sprite is drawn through blit mode 3 instead of each part's own mode; a miss instead clears the flag of the act_clip draw, which suppresses the clip's own impact sound, and plays Miss.wav through fdps_play_sfx. fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges paints the defender's gauges every frame and the attacker's only when there is no lead-in. Every frame waits for retrace bit 3 of port 0x3da to rise and fall, blits the visible 320x200 window (surface + 0x2298, stride 0x170) to 0xa0000 with fdps_blit_rect, then spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes. A critical blow (outcome[1] non-zero) also flashes DAC entry 0 to white through ports 0x3c8/0x3c9 (0x3f,0x3f,0x3f), holds it for delay(0x32) = 50 ms, and writes it back as black -- but the flash is gated on two further conditions beyond the critical: the current frame record's impact byte (frame+5) must be non-zero and the frame must be on its first tick. It therefore fires once per impact frame of a critical blow, not on every frame of one.

The blow ends on the tick fdps_saf_advance_tick reports the clip has run past its last frame. A defender left at 0 HP cancels any second blow; otherwise a travelling attack slides the view back to the attacker's backdrop with attacker_stand_cursor and the negated direction, and swaps the backdrops again.

Twelve settle frames close the animation: backdrop entry 0, the defender's advancing sprite and gauges, and -- only when there was no lead-in -- the attacker's sprite and gauges as well, each frame retrace-synced, blitted and tick-paced like the others. Frees the surface and returns the defender's remaining HP.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit_index -- index of the striking unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8. Its record supplies the side byte (+6) that signs the slide and the recoil, its equipped weapon decides the double strike, and its gauges are drawn while it is on screen. fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange passes the acting unit for the blow and the other unit for the counterblow.
  defender_unit_index -- index of the struck unit in the same array; its record's HP word at +0x40 is what this function writes, and its gauges are drawn on every frame.
  act_clip -- the attacker's Act%03d.saf attack animation, loaded from FigAct.vfs by fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange. Frame 0 byte 4 is the travelling-attack lead-in frame count, and byte 5 of each frame marks the impact frames.
  attacker_stand_cursor -- 3-dword SAF playback cursor over the attacker's Stand%03d.saf clip ([0] frame index, [1] tick counter, [2] clip pointer), primed by the caller. Drawn in the settle frames when the attack does not travel, and the sprite that rides in on the slide back.
  defender_stand_cursor -- the same cursor for the defender's Stand%03d.saf clip; advanced and drawn with the recoil offsets on every frame, and the sprite that rides in on the slide out.
  from_backdrop -- the Back%02d.saf terrain backdrop the animation opens on: the attacker's terrain for a travelling attack, the defender's otherwise. Entry 0 of it is the background of every frame, and it is the outgoing backdrop of both slides.
  to_backdrop -- the other terrain backdrop, the incoming one of both slides; only a travelling attack ever reads it, and fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange passes NULL when the attack does not travel. Both backdrop arguments are swapped in their own stack slots after every slide.

Returns:
  The defender's HP after the blow, as last written to unit record +0x40; 0 when the defender was killed. fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange plays the counterblow only when this is non-zero.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game strings, game callees, direct VGA output]

Rebuild note:
The double-strike test takes two separate rand() % 100 < 3 rolls, one before and one after the item+9 == 2 check, and takes both of them unconditionally -- even when the first already promoted the attack to two blows. Folding them into one roll, or skipping the second once the answer is known, changes the real double-strike rate (5.91%, not 3%) and consumes one rand() fewer, which shifts every later roll of the battle.

=== 00019f7e [EOL]
Alignment filler: mov eax,eax (8b c0), 2-byte NOP form padding to the 16-byte entry at 00019f80.

=== 00019f80 [PLATE]
Works out what one blow of a physical attack does to its target and hands the numbers back to the combat animation, without touching the defender's HP itself.

Algorithm:
Clears the caller's six-dword outcome block: outcome[0] = 1 (missed), outcome[1] = 0 (not critical), outcome[2..4] = 0 (written here, read by nothing), outcome[5] = 0 (damage). Resolves both unit records through fdps_get_unit_record and reads the figures the formula needs: attacker attack (+0x48), defender defense (+0x4a), defender current and maximum HP (+0x40, +0x42), attacker accuracy (+0x4c), defender evasion (+0x4e), and both levels (+0x21). The critical rate is byte 8 of the attacker's PROMAP.DAT class record, fetched with fdps_get_class_record(attacker +0x20 plus 1) -- that table is indexed by class code plus 1. The attacker's equipped weapon comes from fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot(unit, 0), fdps_unit_get_item_id and fdps_get_item_record, of which it keeps hit_effect (+9) and hit_effect_rate (+0xa).

Terrain: for each combatant that fdps_unit_is_flying reports is not flying, fdps_map_load_tile_info publishes the tile under it, its terrain attribute byte lands in DAT_00069d09, and the stat gains table[DAT_00069d09] * stat / 100 -- the per-terrain attack table at 00060040 for the attacker, the per-terrain defense table at 00060058 for the defender. Both are six signed dwords, attack {+5, 0, -5, -5, -5, 0} and defense {0, 0, +10, +10, -5, 0}, and the arithmetic is signed throughout (IDIV after a sign-extending SAR, not DIV). Both divisions truncate toward zero, so small stats come out of it unmodified in either direction.

Weapon effect, rolled before the blow is known to land: hit_effect 3 (critical) adds hit_effect_rate to the critical rate; hit_effect 4 (poison) and hit_effect 1 (paralysis) roll rand() % 100 < hit_effect_rate and, unless fdps_unit_is_ailment_immune vetoes it, write a duration of rand() % 4 + 2 into the defender's poison timer (+0x25) or rand() % 2 + 2 into its paralysis timer (+0x26).

Accuracy: rand() % 100 < attacker accuracy minus defender evasion. On a miss nothing more is computed and the outcome keeps missed 1 and damage 0. On a hit outcome[0] becomes 0, then rand() % 100 < the critical rate halves the defense and sets outcome[1]; damage = (attack - defense) * 9 / 10, floored at 0; a spread of rand() % (damage / 9) is added whenever damage / 9 is not zero; the defender's HP is reduced by the damage into a local only, floored at 0.

Experience, only when the attacker's side byte (+0x06) is 2 and the defender's is 0, i.e. a player unit hitting an enemy: with the defender's ENEMYDAT.DAT record from fdps_get_enemy_record(defender +0x07 minus 0x3c), DAT_00069cec = defender level * enemy record +9 (the per-level XP coefficient) / attacker level, where the attacker's level is first raised by 30 when its portrait id (+0x07) is above 10. When the defender's predicted HP is not zero -- it survived the blow -- the award is then scaled by damage / defender maximum HP. On any other pairing of sides DAT_00069cec is left holding whatever the previous action put there.

Finally stores the damage in outcome[5].

Parameters:
  attacker_unit_index -- index of the striking unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; its only caller fdps_combat_play_blow passes the same index it was given.
  defender_unit_index -- index of the unit being struck, same array.
  outcome -- caller's six-dword block, all of it written here: outcome[0] non-zero when the blow missed, outcome[1] non-zero when it was critical, outcome[5] the damage. outcome[2..4] are set to 0 and read by nothing in the program.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX holds the damage at the RET only because that is the register the last store passed through; the caller discards it.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record / fdps_get_class_record / fdps_map_load_tile_info and shares the battle globals DAT_00069cec and DAT_00069d09; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The weapon's poison and paralysis roll runs before the accuracy roll and writes the defender's timer byte whatever the blow then does, so an attack that misses can still inflict the status; folding the weapon effect into the hit branch, which is the natural way to write it, silently removes that. The experience divisor raises the attacker's level by 30 whenever its portrait id is above 10, which catches 蘭斯洛特 (id 0x0B) as well as every promoted form (0x0F and up) -- writing that test as "is a promoted class" hands him more experience than the original does. The stat locals the terrain modifier works on are signed int in the source, not the uint Ghidra shows: the tables hold -5 entries, and unsigned arithmetic would inflate the stat instead of trimming it. The six combat stat words are read ZERO extended here -- XOR EAX,EAX / MOV AX,word ptr at 00019fec, 0001a01e, 0001a02a, 0001a036, 0001a042 and 0001a04e -- where fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit sign extends the same six fields of the same records with MOVSX at 0001c562 and 0001c594. The fields are signed shorts in the settled layout, so a defender whose DP is -1 defends here with 65535 and one whose EV is -1 is never hit, while the map-side resolver reads both as -1.

=== 0001a362 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov eax,eax, 14 bytes aligning 0001a370 to 16.

=== 0001a370 [PLATE]
Slides the combat animation view from one combatant's terrain backdrop to the other's, bringing the incoming combatant's sprite in with it.

Algorithm:
Writes the surface's 24-pixel border margin 0x18 into the request's y field req[4] once, then runs eight steps, step = 1 through 8. Each step memsets the whole 0x16480-byte (368x248) offscreen surface req[0] to 0 and issues three fdps_draw_composite_sprite calls into it, all with the sound-effect flag clear: entry 0 of outgoing_backdrop at x = 0x18 + direction * step * 0x28, entry 0 of incoming_backdrop at x = 0x18 + direction * (step * 0x28 - 0x140), and then frame anim_cursor[0] of the bank anim_cursor[2], left at the x the incoming backdrop just used so the incoming combatant rides in on its own backdrop. 0x28 is 40 pixels and 0x140 is the 320-pixel screen width, so the eight steps carry one backdrop off and the other on across exactly one screen, and direction picks which way. The step then advances the sprite animation with fdps_saf_advance_tick(anim_cursor, 0), waits for the vertical retrace bit of port 0x3da to go high and then low again, blits the visible 320x200 window (req[0] + 0x2298, source stride 0x170) to the mode-13h screen at 0xa0000 with fdps_blit_rect, and spins until the timer tick counter data_fdps_timer_tick_counter changes. Only the x, y, bank and entry fields of the request are written; its surface pointer, strides and blend fields are left as the caller set them.

Parameters:
  outgoing_backdrop -- the Back%02d.saf backdrop image the combat animation is showing when the call is made; it slides off screen. fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange loads it from BackGrnd.vfs for the terrain the combatant stands on.
  incoming_backdrop -- the other combatant's Back%02d.saf backdrop; it slides on and comes to rest at (0x18, 0x18). fdps_combat_play_blow swaps its two backdrop arguments after every call, so the one that arrived here is the one that leaves next time. Never NULL: the caller only has two backdrops, and only calls this, when the attack's Act clip asks for the view to change sides.
  anim_cursor -- SAF playback cursor of the combatant that belongs to incoming_backdrop: [0] is the current frame index and [2] the sprite bank. Advanced one tick per step.
  req -- the composite-sprite draw request fdps_combat_play_blow keeps on its stack: [0] offscreen surface, [1] stride 0x170, [2] height 0xf8, [3] x, [4] y, [5] bank, [6] entry index.
  direction -- +1 or -1, the sign of the horizontal movement. fdps_combat_play_blow derives it from byte 6 of the acting unit's record and negates it for the slide back.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX holds no meaningful value at the RET and both call sites ignore it.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_draw_composite_sprite / fdps_saf_advance_tick / fdps_blit_rect; no library byte match]

Rebuild note:
The frame-pacing local the end-of-step spin compares against data_fdps_timer_tick_counter is read before it is ever written, so on the first of the eight steps it holds stack garbage and the spin normally falls straight through. Initialising it from the tick counter before the loop -- the obvious way to write that C -- adds a tick of delay to the first step.

=== 0001a4bb [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning FUN_0001a4c0 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001a4c0 [PLATE]
Plays one spell on the game's full-screen combat screen and applies its damage to every target in turn, draining each target's HP gauge across the hit frames of the spell's own animation.

Algorithm:
Spell ids 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0e-0x16, 0x18 and 0x21 have no combat-screen presentation of their own: they are handed straight to fdps_cast_spell_on_targets with the same four arguments, which plays them over the battle map instead, and this function returns. Everything else is set up and played here.
Setup:
  - Swaps the shared blend tables into fight mode: FMer1.tmp (0x4800 bytes) is read "rb" into DAT_000653f0 and FMer2.tmp (0x1000 bytes) into DAT_000643f0. Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp are read back into the same two buffers on the way out.
  - Loads FigBar.cel from MISC.VFS into DAT_00064004 and builds the 125x20 gauge strip DAT_00064000 out of its sprites 4..7 with fdps_cel_blit_sprite, five rows apart; fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges reads both globals.
  - Takes the caster's record from fdps_get_unit_record. Byte +0x07 is its fight-screen character id, byte +0x06 its side code. Side 0, the enemy side, gives the clip-name prefix "E" at 0x00061708 and a knockback sign of -1; the NPC and player sides give "M" at 0x00061704 and +1, so the target is always thrown away from its caster.
  - Loads the spell's three clips from MISC.VFS with fdps_vfs_load_entry: "%sB%02d.saf" (build-up), "%sL%02d.saf" (main) and "%sE%02d.saf" (finish), plus "%sS%02d.saf" as a fourth overlay clip for ids 0x0d, 0x1a-0x1f, 0x21-0x24 and 0x26-0x27 -- the only ids MISC.VFS ships an S clip for. 0x21 sits in that test but can never reach it, having been handed off at the top.
  - Loads Stand%03d.saf and Magic%03d.saf for the caster's character id from Fight.vfs, calls fdps_map_load_tile_info for the caster's tile (record bytes +0x00, +0x01), decrements the terrain backdrop byte DAT_00069d0b in place when it is non-zero and loads that Back%02d.saf from BackGrnd.vfs, then loads Stand%03d.saf for each of the target_count targets into a 40-slot array on the stack.
  - Uploads the combat palette DAT_000643e4 through fdps_set_palette_range and runs fdps_combat_slide_in_attacker for the caster and target 0.
  - Allocates the 0x16480-byte (368x248) drawing surface and fills in one composite-sprite request that every later draw reuses: surface, stride 0x170, height 0xf8, origin (0x18,0x18). The 24-pixel margin is why the visible 320x200 window sits at surface+0x2298.
Every animation frame is built the same way: memset the surface, then draw with fdps_draw_composite_sprite the backdrop, the S overlay where the phase uses it, the current target's Stand clip, the caster's Magic clip and the current effect clip; draw the caster's and the current target's gauges with fdps_draw_unit_hp_mp_gauges; advance the cursors with fdps_saf_advance_tick; spin on bit 3 of port 0x3da until vertical retrace starts and ends; blit the window to 0xa0000 with fdps_blit_rect; then spin until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from a latched copy and re-latch it. That latch is never initialised, so the very first frame's wait ends against whatever was on the stack.
The frames run in five phases:
  1. The caster's Magic clip plays until its cursor reaches the clip's marker frame, byte +0x04 of its frame 0.
  2. The build-up clip plays to its end, then fdps_spell_deduct_mp_cost takes the spell's MP.
  3. The main clip's frames are scanned for the hit flag, byte +0x05, and a clip with no hit frame prints "ERROR: No Hit Point !!!" and calls exit(1). Then, per target: fdps_spell_damage_unit rolls the spell (a 0 return means it missed), the pre-damage HP is written back over unit_record+0x40, and the main clip loops back to its marker frame until as many hit frames have gone by as the scan counted, each one stepping the target's HP down to before - (before-after)*hits_played/hit_count. Spell 0x0d also calls fdps_unit_inflict_random_ailments on a target it hit. A landed hit starts a knockback counted down from 5 to 0, over which the target's draw origin walks x = 0x18 - sign*{14,18,14,9,4,0} and y = 0x18 - sign*{10,8,6,4,2,0} out of the two 6-entry tables at 0x00018c90 (x) and 0x00018ca8 (y) -- thrown out and settling back onto its feet -- while its blend mode goes to 3 and its recolour selector to 0x03<<16 | band<<8 | phase, band being entry spell_id of the 40 dwords at 0x00018cc0 and phase a counter cycling 0..7 once per hit frame. That table holds 214,214,214,224,224,40,40,40,160,160,0,0,72,32, zero for 0x0e-0x16, 32,0,214,224,40,214,180,40,214,40,0,72,214,214,160,160,40; its zero entries are exactly the ids handed off at the top, so every id that reaches this code has a band of its own. Between targets the finished target slides out and the next slides in over 16 frames of 14 pixels, the outgoing one drawn in blend mode 9 through a {FMer1 table, 0x10-step, FMer2 table} descriptor built on the stack; those frames draw the gauge pair twice, once for target 0 and once for the target that just finished.
  4. The main clip plays out to its end, this time without looping back.
  5. The finish clip plays to its end.
Teardown: fdps_audio_stop_sample(-1), free of every clip, the gauge strip and the surface, memset of 64000 bytes at 0xa0000, the map palette DAT_000643bc back through fdps_set_palette_range, and the Mer1/Mer2 restore.

Parameters:
  caster_unit_index -- index of the casting unit in the 0x50-byte records at DAT_00069cd8; also the unit whose gauges are drawn on every frame.
  spell_id -- 0..39, the spell table index the callers picked. It selects the delegation above, supplies the %02d of every clip name and indexes the recolour-band table.
  target_count -- how many entries of target_unit_indices to play out. Not checked against the 40-slot stack array that holds the targets' Stand clips.
  target_unit_indices -- the caller's byte array of unit indices, resolved in array order.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library; calls the game's own named routines and loads game assets by name]

Rebuild note:
fdps_spell_damage_unit has already taken the damage off unit_record+0x40 when it returns; this routine reads the result, writes the pre-damage HP back over it, and re-drains it in (before-after)*hits_played/hit_count steps across the main clip's hit frames, so the obvious "damage the target, then play the animation" makes the HP gauge snap to its final value instead of draining. The per-frame pace latch is never initialised before its first read, so the first frame of the first phase does not wait on the timer tick DAT_00069d64 the way every later frame does.

Unreachable cdecl stack cleanup (add esp,4) after the noreturn crt_exit call at 0001add6; tail of FUN_0001a4c0.

=== 0001ba40 [PLATE]
Plays the game's ending credit roll: one animated card per party roster member, carrying that member's epilogue caption, and then the "End" movie.

Algorithm:
1. Asks for CD music track 1 through fdps_cd_set_music_track, then picks the caption block: message index base 0x20 when the chapter index DAT_00069cf4 is 0x1d (chapter 30, the last chapter), 0x19 otherwise (the only other caller is chapter 27's end handler, chapter index 0x1a). Clears the mode 13h framebuffer with memset(0xa0000, 0, 64000).
2. Swaps in the ending's blend tables: reads FMer1.tmp (0x4800 bytes) over the 18 x 256 shade-ramp table at DAT_000653f0 and FMer2.tmp (0x1000 bytes) over the 16 x 16 x 16 inverse colour cube at DAT_000643f0 -- the two tables fdps_build_palette_tables normally fills -- and uploads the ending palette at DAT_000643e4 through fdps_set_palette_range over indices 0..0xff with no channel bias. It also lays out the blend block {DAT_000653f0, level, DAT_000643f0} on the stack, the shape fdps_draw_composite_sprite consumes through request field +0x1c when request field +0x20 holds blit mode 9.
3. For each roster index i from 0 to the roster count DAT_00064114 inclusive: when the chapter index is 0x1a, i == 3 is bumped straight to 4, so that ending skips roster slot 3. The sprite id is the portrait id byte at offset 7 of fdps_get_roster_record(i), except on the extra pass past the end of the roster (i == DAT_00064114), where it is the fixed portrait id 12. Loads "Stand%03d.saf" from Fight.vfs and "Act%03d.saf" from FigAct.vfs by that id, and "Back%02d.saf" from BackGrnd.vfs by i * 3, all through fdps_vfs_load_entry, then mallocs a 0x16480-byte (368 x 248) offscreen buffer. The 0x24-byte composite-sprite request is destination = that buffer, stride 0x170, height 0xf8.
4. Each card plays in five stages. Every frame of every stage clears the buffer with memset, draws through fdps_draw_composite_sprite, waits out one full VGA vertical retrace on port 0x3da, blits the 320x200 window at buffer + 0x2298 to 0xa0000 through fdps_blit_rect with source stride 0x170, and then spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes:
   - slide-in, 9 frames with k counting 8 down to 0: the backdrop at (0x18, k * 0x14 + 0x18) and the standing sprite at (k * 0xf + 0x18, 0x18), so the two travel into their resting position (0x18, 0x18) from below and from the right.
   - hold, 0x32 frames: backdrop and standing sprite at rest, the standing clip ticked once per frame by fdps_saf_advance_tick.
   - action, however many frames the clip lasts: the backdrop plus the action clip, run until fdps_saf_advance_tick reports the clip finished.
   - caption, 0xfb frames: the standing animation plus the member's epilogue line, drawn by fdps_draw_text out of the message table DAT_00060124 at index (base + i) into buffer + 0x2578 with stride 0x170 and the glyph values 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d. Only the first 8 frames still draw the backdrop, at blend level k * 2, so the backdrop dissolves away over those eight frames and the rest of the hold is the character alone against black.
   - fade-out, 9 frames: the standing sprite at blend level k * 2, dissolving out.
   The backdrop, the action clip and the standing clip are freed at the end of the card.
5. After the last card: frees the offscreen buffer, restores the normal palette at DAT_000643bc through fdps_set_palette_range, reads Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp back over the shade-ramp table and the inverse colour cube, and hands the screen to fdps_play_movie("End").

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing

Pool: fdps  [game strings and game callees; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The 0x16480-byte offscreen buffer is allocated inside the per-member loop but freed only once after the loop ends, so every card except the last leaks about 89 KB; moving free() inside the loop is what a rewrite would naturally do and it changes the program's memory behaviour. Two smaller things a rewrite would tidy away and should not: the latch the frame loops compare against DAT_00069d64 is never initialised, so the very first frame of the very first card races on whatever the stack held, and the byte at offset 4 of frame 0 of the Act clip is read into a local that nothing ever uses.

=== 0001c272 [EOL]
14 zero bytes of alignment padding after FUN_0001ba40, filling up to the 0001c280 paragraph boundary

=== 0001c280 [PLATE]
Per-frame horizontal slide offset for the "Turn N" banner: 13 signed dwords, -60 -20 10 35 50 65 75 80 85 90 92 91 90.

Read-only image, written by nothing at run time. fdps_animate_turn_banner (0001e840) copies all 13 dwords onto its stack with a REP MOVSD at 0001e859 before it does anything else, and both of its animation loops read that copy, one entry per frame. The value is a pixel offset inside the 360x240 scratch buffer the function mallocs at 0001e860: the Turn.saf word is drawn at x = entry + 0x14 by fdps_draw_composite_sprite, and the turn number is drawn at the mirrored x = 0x12c - entry by fdps_draw_turn_number (0001ea80), so the two halves fly in from opposite edges and meet in the middle. The entries are signed and the first two are negative, putting the word at x = -46 and the digits at x = 360 on frame 0, both off the edges. The curve decelerates, overshoots its resting place by two pixels at entry [10] = 92, then settles back through 91 to 90. The forward loop runs entries [0] through [12]; the banner then holds for 500 ms (delay at 0001e983); the exit loop runs entries [10] down to [0], so the two settling frames are used only on the way in and the exit begins with a one-pixel jump back out to the overshoot. Every frame is composed into the scratch buffer and presented by fdps_blit_rect, then the loop spins on the tick counter at 00069d64 until it changes before starting the next one.

Pool: binary_artifact  [rodata initialiser image for an auto array in fdps_animate_turn_banner, copied whole into the frame and never read in place -- the same construct as the local-array init images at 000146e0-000149cc]

Rebuild note:
The entries are signed and the animation depends on it: the two leading negatives are what put the banner word and the digits off the left and right edges on the opening frames. Declaring the table unsigned, or narrowing it to bytes because the settled values are all under 100, makes the entrance start at an enormous x instead of off-screen. The numbers are also hand-tuned rather than an easing formula -- entry [10] overshoots the resting x by two pixels and entries [11] and [12] walk back to it -- and the exit loop deliberately starts at index 10, not 12, so writing the obvious symmetric reverse over all 13 entries replays the two settling frames and loses the snap back out to the overshoot.

=== 0001c2b4 [PLATE]
Initialiser image for the bounce curve of the floating battle indicators: 25 bytes of downward pixel displacement, one per animation frame, read with a per-cell phase stagger.

Nothing writes it. fdps_play_indicator_queue copies all 25 bytes into its stack array at [EBP-0x38] on entry (0001f34c MOV ECX,0x6 / 0001f354 MOV ESI,0x1c2b4 / 0001f359 MOVSD.REP / 0001f35b MOVSB) and reads it once per queued cell per frame. For frame f = 0..21 and queue index i, the entry taken is bounce[i % 4 + f] (0001f40a..0001f41d), zero-extended at 0001f421 and added to the glyph's screen y at 0001f431, so the blit lands at tile_y * 24 - DAT_00069ce0 + bounce[i % 4 + f] + 21. A larger value sits the glyph lower, so the value is displacement downward from the top of the hop, not height.

Values are 15,15,15,15, 7,3,1,0,0,1,3,7, 15,15, 11,9,8,8,9,11, 15,15,15,15,15: a rest at the baseline, a hop 15 pixels up and back down, a short rest, a smaller hop 7 pixels up and back, then a rest for the remainder. The i % 4 term staggers the four cells of a multi-digit popup by one frame each, so the digits ripple rather than move as a block. With f at most 21 and i % 4 at most 3 the index reaches exactly 24, the last byte of the table.

Pool: binary_artifact  [ECX=6 / REP MOVSD / MOVSB of a fixed 25-byte image from rodata into a stack frame at function entry, with no memcpy call, is wcc386's codegen for an initialised auto array rather than a global the programmer declared; only fdps_play_indicator_queue reaches it]

Rebuild note:
The table is 25 entries although the animation is only 22 frames. The three extra tail entries exist because the index is i % 4 + frame, not frame, so the highest index formed is 24. Declaring the obvious 22-entry table, one per frame, reads up to 3 bytes past the end for the second, third and fourth cell of every popup.

=== 0001c2cd [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for a local char array: four spaces and their NUL, 5 bytes.

Read only by fdps_show_number_indicator@0001f510, which copies all 5 bytes onto its stack frame (MOVSD + MOVSB into EBP-0x20) on entry, before it has decided whether the unit is even on screen. The copy is the text buffer the floated number is built in: once the unit passes the visible-tile-window cull, sprintf formats value through the "%d" literal at 000617bc straight over these bytes, strlen measures the result to drive the right-alignment countdown, and the individual characters are read out one at a time and turned into Number.cel glyph ids in the popup queue at DAT_000642b0. === 0001c2d2 [PLATE]
Initialiser image for the four Number.cel glyph ids that spell the MISS popup: 0x34 0x35 0x36 0x36.

Nothing writes it. fdps_show_miss_indicator@0001f690 loads all four bytes as one dword into its stack array at [EBP-0x4] on entry (0001f69c), before it has resolved the unit or decided whether the popup is visible at all.
