Flow: fdps_vfs_load_entry("MISC.VFS", name) yields the entry; two 64000-byte buffers are malloc'd and both are filled with the current VGA page from 0xa0000. Fade-out runs level 1..5, each step calling fdps_blit_tint_rect(saved, 320, 0xa0000, 320, 320, 200, data_fdps_inverse_palette_cube, data_fdps_palette_shade_ramp_table, 0, level) after waiting for the 0x3da retrace bit to go high then low and for data_fdps_timer_tick_counter to tick, so one step lands per frame. The now-dark screen is re-snapshotted into the first buffer, which becomes the animation's backdrop: for name "PLYPHASE.SAF" fdps_animate_turn_banner (0001e840) runs first, then fdps_saf_play_over_background (0001ecf0)(entry, backdrop) plays the animation and the backdrop is freed. fdps_animate_turn_banner does NOT preprocess or otherwise modify that backdrop -- it only READS its saved_screen argument, using it as fdps_blit_rect's source, and writes to its own work page and to the adapter at 000a0504, so the buffer the clip is then played over is untouched by it. Note also that the strcmp at 0001ec15 compares against the UPPER-CASE literal at 000617c0 while all three call sites pass a mixed-case name -- "EnyPhase.saf" at 00061790, "PlyPhase.saf" at 000617a0 and 00061acc -- so the branch is taken only because fdps_vfs_load_entry has already upper-cased the caller's buffer in place. Fade-in then runs level 5..1 over the second buffer, which still holds the untouched pre-call screen, and the entry and that buffer are freed.

=== 0001ecf0 [PLATE]
Plays one loaded .SAF animation through once, full screen, over a background image the caller supplies.

Algorithm:
Allocates a 0x16480-byte page with malloc -- a 368x248 8bpp surface, 48 pixels wider and taller than the 320x200 screen, so a frame may overhang the visible window without being clipped. Builds the 0x24-byte composite-sprite draw request on the stack: destination = that page, pitch 0x170 (368), height 0xf8 (248), x = y = 0x18 (24), SAF base (+0x14) = saf_image, blit parameter block (+0x1c) and blit mode (+0x20) both 0. Calls fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 1) to reset the three-dword playback cursor and stores saf_image in cursor[2], the slot fdps_saf_advance_tick reads the SAF header from. Then loops until fdps_saf_advance_tick reports the clip has ended: fdps_blit_rect copies the caller's 320x200 background_page into the visible window of the page at page+0x2298 (24 * 368 + 24), the request's index field (+0x18) takes the cursor's current frame number, fdps_draw_composite_sprite draws that frame with its flag argument 1 so the frame's own sound effect fires, fdps_blit_rect copies the 320x200 window from the page straight to the VGA framebuffer at 0xa0000, the routine spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes, and fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 0) advances the cursor by one tick. Mode 0 wraps the frame index back to 0 and returns 1 once the last frame has been held, so the animation plays exactly once and the loop exits there. The page is freed on the way out; the caller owns both saf_image and background_page.

Parameters:
  saf_image -- the loaded .SAF animation image to play. The only caller, fdps_play_vfs_animation, passes the MISC.VFS entry it loaded by name. Used as the composite-sprite bank at request+0x14 and as the SAF pointer in the playback cursor.
  background_page -- a 320x200 8bpp image, 320 bytes per row, repainted under every frame so the animation composites over a static picture. fdps_play_vfs_animation passes its snapshot of the VGA screen that was showing before the animation started.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; game call graph and mode 13h geometry -- calls only game workers plus malloc/free, and the 0xa0000 target, 320x200 window and 368-byte padded pitch are application geometry]

Rebuild note:
The dword holding the previously seen value of the tick counter DAT_00069d64 is never initialised: the first frame's wait loop compares the counter against whatever was left on the stack, so in practice it falls straight through and the first frame is displayed without waiting a tick. Writing the obvious C -- seeding that variable with 0 or with the current value of DAT_00069d64 -- makes the first frame wait a whole tick before it advances, lengthening every playback by one tick. Leave it reading the stale value, or start it from a value the counter cannot currently hold.

=== 0001ee0d [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_0001ee10 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001ee10 [PLATE]
Draws one battle-map unit's 24x24 walk sprite into a scene buffer, in a blit mode the caller picks, so a caller can paint the unit normally or as a flat silhouette.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and converts the record's tile position to buffer pixels the way fdps_draw_map_unit does: x = record[0] * 0x18 - data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_x + 0x18 and y = record[1] * 0x18 - data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_y + 0x12, where 0x18 is the tile size and data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_x / data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_y are the camera origin in world pixels. The 0x12 on y is fdps_draw_map_unit's one-tile border with that routine's fixed -6 sprite lift folded into the constant, because the sprites stand taller than their 24-pixel tile.

It draws nothing unless 0 < y < 0xd8 and 0 < x < 0x150. That is the same camera window fdps_draw_map_unit clips against, only tested after the conversion instead of before: its world-space bounds data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_x - 0x18 < x < data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_x + 0x138 and data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_y - 0x18 < y < data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_y + 0xc0 are these bounds rearranged. The test looks at the sprite origin alone, so a unit near an edge is either drawn whole or dropped, never clipped.

The walk-cycle phase is the shared map animation counter data_fdps_map_unit_walk_anim_counter -- which fdps_draw_map_unit steps modulo 16 once per frame tick, and nothing else in the program touches -- taken as data_fdps_map_unit_walk_anim_counter / 4 with the value 3 folded back to 1, giving the ping-pong 0, 1, 2, 1. The sprite index is record[2] * 0xc + record[3] * 3 + phase: record[2] is the unit's slot in the sprite cache at data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr that fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group filled, twelve sprites to a slot as four facings (record[3]: 0 down, 1 left, 2 up, 3 right) of three walk frames each. That index selects an entry of the cache's offset table, and the entry's value is measured from the base of the cache block: adding it back to that base -- never to the address the entry was read from -- gives the packed pixel stream. Finally it calls fdps_blit_dispatch(stream, scene_buffer + y * 0x168 + x, 0x18, 0x18, 0x168, blit_param, blit_mode).

Record byte 4, the unit's sub-tile step counter, is read and scaled by 4 into a local that nothing reads. The facing switch fdps_draw_map_unit uses to turn that counter into a displacement -- (0,+4), (-4,0), (0,-4), (+4,0) per step -- is absent from this body altogether, so a unit caught between tiles is drawn snapped to the tile it is leaving.

Parameters:
  scene_buffer -- the 360x240 8bpp scene buffer the caller allocated (0x15180 bytes) and filled with fdps_draw_scene_layers; the sprite is composited into it, not onto the VGA screen.
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, which bounds-checks nothing.
  blit_param -- forwarded as fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument; its meaning belongs to the kernel the mode selects, and mode 0 ignores it. All three callers pass a palette colour shifted left by 8, which fdps_blit_rle_recolor reads as add 0x00, base = the colour, mask 0x00, turning every pixel into that one palette index: 0xff00 from fdps_unit_rest and fdps_battle_advance_turn, and fdps_flash_units_in_color's own flash_color from there.
  blit_mode -- the kernel selector for fdps_blit_dispatch: 3 (fdps_blit_rle_recolor) from fdps_unit_rest and fdps_battle_advance_turn, alternating 0 (fdps_blit_rle_passthrough) and 3 every two frames from fdps_flash_units_in_color.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no fid hit in either library set; calls and is called by named game functions]

Rebuild note:
The routine computes the unit's sub-tile step offset (record[4] * 4) into a local and then never reads it, so a unit caught mid-step is drawn snapped to its tile. The sibling fdps_draw_map_unit does apply that counter, through a facing switch giving (0,+4)/(-4,0)/(0,-4)/(+4,0) per step, and the rest of this function's geometry is that routine's block trimmed -- same tile scale, same one-tile border, same -6 sprite lift folded into the y constant 0x12. Writing the obvious C, that is, finishing the offset the way the neighbour does, makes flashed and resting units drift up to 20 pixels off where the original puts them. The dead local has to survive into the rebuilt source, or the line has to be dropped, but the offset must not reach the destination address. Separately, the visibility test is strictly greater than zero on both axes, matching the strict comparisons fdps_draw_map_unit uses on the same window; writing >= 0 draws one extra row and column of units along the top and left edges that the original never shows.

=== 0001ef3b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligns FUN_0001ef40 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001ef40 [PLATE]
Plays the on-map animation of one blow landing on the defender, with both combatants' HP bars showing over the map.

Algorithm:
fdps_battle_compute_unit_gauge_position places the defender's bar into a stack position pair, then fdps_check_can_counter_attack(attacker_unit, defender_unit) decides whether the attacker's bar is wanted: when it returns exactly 1 the attacker's bar is positioned the same way into a second pair, otherwise that pair's x half is set to -1, which suppresses the attacker's bar for the whole run. Both unit records come from fdps_get_unit_record; from each it takes the side byte at +6 (side 0 selects EasyBar.cel image 2, anything else image 1) and the HP words at +0x40 (current) and +0x42 (maximum) -- the same reads fdps_battle_show_combat_gauges makes when it first puts the two bars on screen.

malloc gives it a 0x15180-byte (360x240) composite page -- no NULL test -- and each position pair becomes a destination pointer as page + (y + 0x18) * 0x168 + x + 0x18, the 0x18-pixel border the page carries on every side. The attacker's pointer is formed even when its pair is -1, out of a y half that was never written, but nothing dereferences it in that case.

It then builds the 0x24-byte composite sprite request on the stack over that page: page pointer at +0, width 0x168 and height 0xf0 at +4 and +8, the request origin at +0xc and +0x10 as defender_record[0] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 and defender_record[1] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0 - 6 (0x18 is the tile size, DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0 are the view's scroll origin in world pixels, and the -6 is the same sprite lift fdps_draw_map_unit applies), at +0x14 the "EasyAni.Saf" image that fdps_vfs_image_get_entry pulls out of the resident archive image at DAT_000643a8, and zero at +0x1c and +0x20. The entry size fdps_vfs_image_get_entry writes out is thrown away: the same local is immediately overwritten with fdps_saf_frame_count of that image, which is the frame count the loop runs to.

One pass per frame of the animation, frame number in request +0x18: fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the map -- layers, cursor and units -- into the page, fdps_draw_unit_gauge draws the attacker's bar (skipped while its pair is -1) and then the defender's, each filled to (current_hp * 0x29 + max_hp - 1) / max_hp pixels of the bar's 0x29-pixel span and to 0 when max_hp is not positive, and fdps_draw_composite_sprite draws the frame with its sound flag set, so the frame's sound effect fires. The frame is then presented in open code: spin on port 0x3DA bit 3 until vertical retrace starts and again until it ends, blit the 0x138 x 0xc0 window at page+0x21d8 -- pixel (24,24) of the 360-wide page -- with fdps_blit_rect to 0xa0504, the 4-pixel inset of the mode 13h screen, then wait for the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 to change. free releases the page after the last frame.

The same EasyAni.Saf animation is played for every attack; nothing here varies with the weapon or the damage.

Parameters:
  attacker_unit -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, the unit striking. Only its HP bar and its counter-attack eligibility are used here; the animation itself plays over the defender. fdps_unit_attack_target passes its own attacker_unit_index.
  defender_unit -- same index space, the unit being hit. Its tile fixes where the animation is drawn, and its bar is always drawn. fdps_unit_attack_target passes its own target_unit_index.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit; game call graph and game data -- unit records, the view-scroll globals and the "EasyAni.Saf" asset name]

Rebuild note:
The local the frame loop compares against the tick counter DAT_00069d64 is never initialised, so the first frame does not wait for a tick. Declaring it initialised from DAT_00069d64, which is what writing the loop cleanly in C invites, costs one extra tick of animation -- the same trap as in fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead and fdps_animate_turn_banner.

=== 0001f33b [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning FUN_0001f340 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001f340 [PLATE]
Plays back the queue of floating indicators standing over the battle map -- damage and healing numbers, "MISS", the status-cured mark -- bouncing every queued glyph over its unit for 22 frames, then emptying the queue.

Algorithm:
Copies the 25-byte bounce table at 0x0001c2b4 onto the stack: 15,15,15,15, 7,3,1,0,0,1,3,7, 15,15, 11,9,8,8,9,11, 15,15,15,15,15. The values are pixels of downward displacement, so read left to right the run is a rest at 15, a hop 15 pixels up and back, a short rest, a smaller hop 7 pixels up and back, and a rest. Returns immediately when the queue cursor DAT_00064378 is 0, so a playback with nothing queued costs nothing.

Otherwise it runs 22 frames. Each frame allocates a fresh 0x15180-byte (360x240) off-screen page with malloc -- no NULL check -- and repaints the scrolling map into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers. It then walks the DAT_00064378 queued cells. Cell i takes its glyph id from DAT_000642b0[i]; 0xff means a blank cell and is skipped, which is what fdps_show_number_indicator writes for the leading padding of a right-aligned number. For a live cell it resolves the owning unit with fdps_get_unit_record(DAT_000641e8[i]), reads the unit's tile x from record byte 0 and its tile y from record byte 1, and blits the glyph out of Number.cel (pointer in DAT_000643d8) with fdps_cel_blit_sprite in mode 0 at

  x = tile_x * 24 - DAT_00069ce4 + DAT_00064120[i] + 24
  y = tile_y * 24 - DAT_00069ce0 + bounce[i % 4 + frame] + 21

where 24 is the tile size in pixels, DAT_00069ce4 and DAT_00069ce0 are the camera's pixel scroll x and y, DAT_00064120[i] is the cell's x offset inside its own popup, and the +24 / +21 place the popup inside the scene page's border. The i % 4 term staggers consecutive queued cells by one frame each, so a four-digit number hops as a wave instead of as a block -- i is the absolute queue index, so a popup only starts on phase 0 when the cursor happened to be a multiple of four. With frame at most 21 and i % 4 at most 3 the table index reaches exactly 24, the table's last byte.

The frame is then presented: it spins on the VGA input status register (port 0x3da, bit 3) for a whole vertical retrace pulse, first until the bit sets and then until it clears, and blits the page's visible 312x192 window -- page + 0x21d8, i.e. 24 rows down and 24 pixels in -- to the mode-13h screen at 0xa0504 (row 4, column 4) with fdps_blit_rect. It then spins until the timer tick DAT_00069d64 differs from the tick it recorded on the previous frame, records the new tick, and frees the page.

After the 22 frames it waits 500 ms with delay and sets the queue cursor DAT_00064378 back to 0, leaving the queue empty for the next batch.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set, unique hash in the image; calls only game functions plus plain CLIB3S clients, and walks the game's own popup queue arrays]

Rebuild note:
The tick the frame loop waits on is read out of an uninitialized stack slot, so frame 0 compares against leftover stack contents and almost never waits; declaring it initialized, to 0 or to the current tick, adds a tick of delay to the first frame. And the bounce phase is the queue index modulo 4, not the cell's index inside its popup -- fdps_show_sprite_indicator advances the cursor by the number of cells it actually wrote rather than by 4, so a short indicator leaves the cursor off a multiple of four and every popup queued after it bounces out of phase; writing the phase as the per-popup cell index looks cleaner and loses that.

=== 0001f510 [PLATE]
Floats a number over one battle unit -- damage taken, HP healed, MP restored or a stat gain -- by queueing its digits into the shared indicator queue that 0x0001f340 plays back.

Algorithm:
Seeds a 5-byte stack buffer with the four-space string at 0x0001c2cd, sets the right-alignment countdown to 3 and the digit cursor to 0, then resolves the unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads its tile x from record byte 0 and its tile y from record byte 1.
Culls the request against the visible tile window derived from the camera scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 (pixel scroll x) and DAT_00069ce0 (pixel scroll y), each divided by 24, the tile size in pixels: tile x must satisfy scroll_x/24 - 1 < x < scroll_x/24 + 13, both edges exclusive, while tile y must satisfy scroll_y/24 - 1 <= y <= scroll_y/24 + 8, both edges inclusive. A unit outside that window queues nothing and leaves the queue untouched.
Otherwise it formats value into the stack buffer with sprintf against the "%d" format at 0x000617bc, the same format fdps_draw_turn_number prints the turn number with, and appends exactly four cells at the shared queue cursor DAT_00064378, one per digit position: DAT_00064120[cursor + i] takes the cell's pixel x offset within the popup, i*6 + 2 for all four cells, where the fixed-word popups fdps_show_miss_indicator and fdps_show_cure_indicator instead use i*6 + 1 with a kerning nudge on cell 1; DAT_000641e8[cursor + i] takes the unit index as a byte; DAT_000642b0[cursor + i] takes the Number.cel glyph id glyph_base + digit - '0', or 0xff for a blank cell, which the player skips.
The right alignment comes from the countdown, which starts at 3 and drops by one after every cell: cell i writes a digit only when strlen(buffer) > 3 - i, so a one-digit number lands in the last cell with the three before it blanked, and a four-digit number fills all four. The digit cursor into the formatted string advances only on the cells that emitted, so the digits stay in order. A value of five digits or more keeps only its first four; the fifth and later digits are formatted but never queued.
The cursor DAT_00064378 is then advanced by 4. The queue is drained by 0x0001f340, which blits each cell's glyph out of the Number.cel sheet at DAT_000643d8 over its unit for 22 bouncing frames and then clears the cursor.

Parameters:
  value -- the number to float, as a signed int. Callers pass the return of fdps_unit_apply_heal, of fdps_unit_restore_mp or of the damage helper at 0x00028460, or a literal stat-gain amount of 1, 7 or 0x0f.
  glyph_base -- base glyph id in Number.cel of the ten digit sprites the number is drawn with; each digit's ASCII code is added to it and '0' subtracted, in 8-bit arithmetic. Callers pass 0 for damage, 0x0d for MP restore and stat gains, and 0x27 for healing.
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, naming the unit the number floats over. Passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record and stored as a byte in DAT_000641e8.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record, which a pre-compiled library module could not; shares the battle popup queue globals DAT_00064120 / DAT_000641e8 / DAT_000642b0 / DAT_00064378 and the camera scroll globals with the rest of the battle display code; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The visible-window cull is deliberately asymmetric and writing it symmetrically changes which units get a number at the map edge: the x test rejects the column at scroll_x/24 - 1 (both edges exclusive, columns scroll_x/24 .. scroll_x/24 + 12) while the y test accepts the row at scroll_y/24 - 1 (both edges inclusive, rows scroll_y/24 - 1 .. scroll_y/24 + 8). Also, the x offset written into DAT_00064120 is i*6 + 2 for all four cells here, not the i*6 + 1 with a cell-1 nudge that the fixed-word siblings at 0001f690 and 0001f7d0 use, so folding the three producers onto one shared helper shifts the digits one pixel.

=== 0001f686 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6-byte nop) + lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0] (4-byte nop), aligning FUN_0001f690 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001f690 [PLATE]
Queues the four-glyph "MISS" indicator over one battle unit, for the effect code to report that a spell or item did nothing to that target.

Algorithm:
Copies the four Number.cel glyph ids held in the read-only dword at 0x0001c2d2 (0x34 0x35 0x36 0x36 = M, I, S, S) into a stack buffer, then resolves the unit with fdps_get_unit_record and reads its tile x from record byte 0 and tile y from record byte 1. Culls the request against the visible tile window, derived from the camera scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 (pixel scroll x) and DAT_00069ce0 (pixel scroll y) each divided by 24, the tile size in pixels: x must satisfy scroll_x/24 - 1 < x < scroll_x/24 + 13 (both edges exclusive, so columns scroll_x/24 .. scroll_x/24+12) while y must satisfy scroll_y/24 - 1 <= y <= scroll_y/24 + 8 (both edges inclusive). A unit outside that window queues nothing and leaves the queue count untouched. Otherwise it appends four cells at the shared indicator-queue cursor DAT_00064378, one per glyph: the cell's x offset in pixels into DAT_00064120 (i*6+1 for the 6-pixel-wide glyphs, except cell 1 which gets i*6+2 = 8 so the narrow I sits clear of the wide M), the unit index into DAT_000641e8, and the glyph id into DAT_000642b0. The cursor then advances by 4. fdps_play_indicator_queue later draws every queued cell out of Number.cel (pointer in DAT_000643d8) with fdps_cel_blit_sprite, at the unit's tile position minus the camera scroll plus a per-frame bounce offset, and zeroes the cursor when the animation ends. This is the fixed-word member of a four-producer family that shares that queue: fdps_show_number_indicator formats digits into it, fdps_show_sprite_indicator takes the glyph ids from its caller, and fdps_queue_status_cured_popup is the CURE counterpart of this one, queueing the adjacent glyph dword at 0x0001c2d6.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; the callers pass one entry of the target id list they are iterating.

Returns:
  Nothing. The indicator queue at DAT_00064120 / DAT_000641e8 / DAT_000642b0 and its count at DAT_00064378 are the output.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The viewport cull is asymmetric between the axes and the obvious symmetric rewrite changes which units get a popup: x is exclusive on both edges (scroll_x/24 - 1 < x < scroll_x/24 + 13) while y is inclusive on both (scroll_y/24 - 1 <= y <= scroll_y/24 + 8), so a unit one row above the top of the view still gets its MISS drawn but a unit one column left of the view does not. The per-cell x offsets carry the same trap: they are i*6+1 except cell 1, which is 8 rather than 7, and writing the uniform i*6+1 shifts the I of MISS one pixel left. Keep the divisions signed int divisions (the original uses IDIV, truncating toward zero) rather than shifts.

=== 0001f7c8 [EOL]

=== 0001f7d0 [PLATE]
Queues the four-glyph "CURE" indicator over one battle unit, for the effect code to report that a status ailment has just been lifted from that target.

Algorithm:
Copies the four Number.cel glyph ids held in the read-only dword at 0x0001c2d6 (0x37 0x38 0x39 0x3a = C, U, R, E) into a stack buffer, then resolves the unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads its tile x from record byte 0 and its tile y from record byte 1. Culls the request against the visible tile window derived from the camera scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 (pixel scroll x) and DAT_00069ce0 (pixel scroll y), each divided by 24, the tile size in pixels: x must satisfy scroll_x/24 - 1 < x < scroll_x/24 + 13 (both edges exclusive, so columns scroll_x/24 .. scroll_x/24 + 12) while y must satisfy scroll_y/24 - 1 <= y <= scroll_y/24 + 8 (both edges inclusive). A unit outside that window queues nothing and leaves the queue cursor untouched. Otherwise it appends four cells at the shared indicator-queue cursor DAT_00064378, one per glyph: the cell's x offset in pixels into DAT_00064120 (i*6 + 1, except cell 1 which gets i*6 + 2 = 8), the unit index into DAT_000641e8, and the glyph id into DAT_000642b0. The cursor then advances by 4. fdps_play_indicator_queue later draws every queued cell out of Number.cel (pointer in DAT_000643d8) with fdps_cel_blit_sprite, at the unit's tile position minus the camera scroll plus a per-frame bounce offset, and zeroes the cursor when the animation ends.

This is one of the two fixed-word producers of that queue, the same body as fdps_show_miss_indicator (0001f690) with only the glyph dword changed; the other two producers are fdps_show_number_indicator, which formats digits into it, and fdps_show_sprite_indicator, which takes the glyph ids from its caller.

All three call sites fire on the same shape: the caller has resolved the target, has found at least one of the status-ailment bytes at unit record +0x25, +0x26 or +0x27 non-zero, and is about to clear it and play "Cure.saf" over the target. fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets calls here for item effect code 0x16 when +0x25 is set (00026888-00026899, then MOV byte ptr [EAX + 0x25],0x0) and for code 0x18 when +0x26 is set (00026914-00026925); fdps_cast_spell_on_targets calls here when any of the three bytes is set (00028c4b-00028c73) and then memsets all three to 0. So the indicator marks a cure that actually took effect, never a cure applied to a unit that was not ailing.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; the callers pass one entry of the target id list they are iterating.

Returns:
  Nothing. The indicator queue at DAT_00064120 / DAT_000641e8 / DAT_000642b0 and its cursor at DAT_00064378 are the output; whether the indicator was queued or culled away is not reported.

Pool: fdps  [no library match in either Function ID set; calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record and writes only the game's indicator-queue and camera globals]

Rebuild note:
The viewport cull is asymmetric between the axes and the obvious symmetric rewrite changes which units get an indicator at the map edge: x is exclusive on both edges (JGE at 0001f821 rejects the column at scroll_x/24 - 1, JG at 0001f83e rejects scroll_x/24 + 13) while y is inclusive on both (JLE at 0001f85b accepts scroll_y/24 - 1, JGE at 0001f87a accepts scroll_y/24 + 8), so a unit one row above the view still gets its CURE drawn but a unit one column left of the view does not. The per-cell x offsets carry a second trap: they are i*6 + 1 except cell 1, which is 8 rather than 7 (0001f8a5 ADD AL,0x2 against 0001f8bf INC AL). That nudge is positional, not kerning -- it is the same code as the MISS producer, where cell 1 is the narrow I, and here it lands on the U regardless. Writing it as a per-letter kerning rule, or folding it away to a uniform i*6 + 1, moves the U by a pixel. Keep both divisions signed int divisions by 24 (IDIV with the dividend sign-extended by SAR EDX,0x1f), not shifts.

=== 0001f908 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] + mov edx,edx, aligning next function to 0x10.

=== 0001f910 [PLATE]
Flashes a list of battle-map units in one palette colour, over eight tick-paced frames, so the units an effect has just been applied to are marked out on screen.

Algorithm:
Runs eight frames, i = 0..7. Each frame allocates an 0x15180-byte (360x240) offscreen scene buffer with malloc and fills it with fdps_draw_scene_layers, which already paints every unit on the map through fdps_draw_map_units; it then redraws just the listed units on top, calling fdps_blit_unit_sprite(buf, unit_indices[j], flash_color << 8, mode) for j = 0..unit_count-1. The mode is 3 when (i / 2) & 1 and 0 otherwise, so frames 0,1 and 4,5 use mode 0 (fdps_blit_rle_passthrough), which redraws each sprite over the identical pixels already in the buffer and changes nothing visible, while frames 2,3 and 6,7 use mode 3 (fdps_blit_rle_recolor), which paints every pixel of the sprite as one palette index: the listed units go flat-coloured twice. flash_color is shifted left by 8 once at entry, which lands it in fdps_blit_rle_recolor's base field with the add and mask fields left at 0.
Presentation repeats fdps_render_view_frame's sequence without the cursor panel and without the palette cycling: poll port 0x3DA until bit 3 sets and again until it clears, spanning vertical retrace; fdps_blit_rect(buf + 0x21d8, 0x168, 0xa0504, 0x140, 0x138, 0xc0) to copy the 312x192 interior of the buffer into the mode 13h screen 4 pixels in from its top left; spin until the interrupt-driven tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from the value latched at the end of the previous frame; free the buffer. Unlike fdps_render_view_frame the latched tick is kept in a stack local rather than in DAT_00069d10.

Parameters:
  unit_count -- how many entries of unit_indices to flash. Zero is legal and turns the call into an eight-tick pause. Every caller passes the target count of the effect it has just applied.
  unit_indices -- array of unit_count byte indices into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8. Each index goes straight to fdps_blit_unit_sprite, which silently drops any unit whose sprite origin lies outside the visible view. Every caller passes the target id list of the effect it has just applied.
  flash_color -- the palette index every pixel of a flashed sprite becomes. fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets (the Cure/CureMP branches) and fdps_apply_heal_to_targets pass 0xff; fdps_cast_spell_on_targets passes 0x2b for effect id 0x11 and calls twice in a row, giving four flashes.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_draw_scene_layers, fdps_blit_unit_sprite and fdps_blit_rect, and drives the game's own VGA presentation geometry and tick global; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The per-frame tick wait compares the tick counter against a stack local that nothing writes before the first frame, so the first frame waits either not at all or a full tick depending on what that slot happened to hold. Initialising the local, or latching into DAT_00069d10 the way fdps_render_view_frame does, changes the pacing of the first flash frame -- and writing DAT_00069d10 would also perturb the next fdps_render_view_frame call. Leave the local uninitialised.

=== 0001fa2b [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0]) + 8b c9 (mov ecx,ecx), 5 bytes to 16-byte boundary.

=== 0001fa30 [PLATE]
Ticks the status effects running on one side's battle units once per turn: the poison damage first, then the countdown of all six effect timers.

Algorithm:
Sweeps unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 (the battle unit count) twice, taking each 0x50-byte record from fdps_get_unit_record.
First sweep, poison damage. A unit is hit when its poison timer -- record byte +0x25, the slot fdps_unit_apply_status_effect writes for effect id 0x12 -- is running, its side byte +0x06 equals side, and the retired bit 0x01 of byte +0x05 is clear (the test fdps_unit_is_retired makes, inlined here). The damage is the unit's maximum HP (unsigned word +0x42) divided by 10, published as a dword in the shared damage-value global DAT_00064038; it comes off current HP (word +0x40) and the result is floored at 0, so poison can leave a unit at 0 HP but never below it. Then the presentation: DAT_00069cd0, the map-cursor overlay mode fdps_draw_map_cursor dispatches on, is set to 0 so no cursor is drawn; fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit brings the view onto the unit; 0x00026e00(1, &unit_index_byte, "PosEff.saf") plays the poison animation over it; fdps_show_number_indicator(DAT_00064038, 0, unit_index) queues the damage figure and 0x0001f340 plays the indicator queue back; DAT_00069cd0 is set to 1.
Between the sweeps, 0x0001d6c0 plays the destruction sequence for anything the poison just brought to 0 HP, and the current chapter's post-action handler is called through the table at 0x0006028c indexed by the chapter index DAT_00069cf4 -- the same win/lose test the AI phases and fdps_battle_unit_turn run after a unit acts, so a poison death can end the battle.
Second sweep, countdown. For every unit whose side byte +0x06 equals side and whose retired bit is clear, each of the six status timers at record +0x22 .. +0x27 that is non-zero is decremented by one; that is the three buff slots fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats reads followed by the three ailment slots, poison's own +0x25 among them, so a poison timer ticks down after its damage has already been applied this turn. A timer that reaches zero sets DAT_00069cd0 to 0 and calls fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(unit_index) so the expired buff drops back out of the unit's derived stats. Nothing on that path puts DAT_00069cd0 back.

Parameters:
  side -- the side whose units are ticked, compared against unit record byte +0x06 as a zero-extended byte: 2 is the player side, 1 the NPC side, 0 the enemy side. fdps_battle_advance_turn is the only caller and passes 1, then 0, then 2, each call immediately after fdps_battle_run_turn_events for the same side.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX is not set on the exit path and the caller does not look at it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the watcom or ail sets, hash unique in the image; walks the game unit records through fdps_get_unit_record and is called only by fdps_battle_advance_turn]

Rebuild note:
The two sweeps are not symmetric about the cursor-mode global DAT_00069cd0: the poison sweep sets it to 0 and back to 1, but the timer-expiry branch sets it to 0 and leaves it there, so after any status effect runs out the map cursor is not drawn again until something else sets the mode. Writing the obvious restore, or deleting the write as pointless because fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats draws nothing, changes what the phase that follows looks like.

=== 0001fbff [EOL]
Alignment padding: single 0x90 NOP between FUN_0001fa30 and FUN_0001fc00.

=== 0001fc00 [PLATE]
Queues a floating indicator over one battle unit out of sprites the caller supplies: up to four Number.cel sprite ids that rise over the unit's tile when the indicator queue is played back. It is the member of the indicator-producer family whose message is an argument rather than a constant.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and takes the unit's tile x from record byte 0 and its tile y from record byte 1.
Culls the request against the visible map window derived from the camera scroll globals DAT_00069ce4 (pixel scroll x) and DAT_00069ce0 (pixel scroll y), each divided by 24, the tile size in pixels: nothing is queued unless tile_x > scroll_x/24 - 1 (0001fc4c) and tile_x < scroll_x/24 + 13 (0001fc67) and tile_y >= scroll_y/24 - 1 (0001fc86) and tile_y <= scroll_y/24 + 8 (0001fca3). The two lower edges are not written the same way -- x is exclusive, y inclusive -- so a unit one row above the window still gets its indicator while one column left of it does not. fdps_show_number_indicator and fdps_show_miss_indicator apply the identical predicate.
Then for each cell i of 0..3 it reads sprite_ids[i]. A zero id skips that cell and the loop moves straight on to the next one; it does not stop the loop. A non-zero id appends one entry at slot DAT_00064378 + i -- indexed by the loop counter, not by how many cells have been written -- of the three parallel byte queues: DAT_00064120 takes the cell's x offset in pixels within the unit's tile, i*6+1, except cell 1 which takes 8 so a narrow second letter sits clear of a wide first one; DAT_000641e8 takes unit_index as a byte; DAT_000642b0 takes sprite_ids[i].
Finally it adds the number of cells it actually wrote, not 4, to the queue cursor DAT_00064378.

fdps_play_indicator_queue drains the queue: for 22 frames it blits each entry's sprite out of Number.cel (pointer in DAT_000643d8, loaded by fdps_load_global_resources) with fdps_cel_blit_sprite at (tile_x*24 - DAT_00069ce4 + x_offset + 24, tile_y*24 - DAT_00069ce0 + bounce offset + 21), skipping any entry whose sprite id is 0xff, then zeroes the cursor. The sibling plates call the DAT_000642b0 bytes glyph ids -- Number.cel is a 65-sprite 6x8 font sheet of digits and letters, and each of those producers knows which word its own ids spell -- but they are the same bytes as this function's sprite_ids.

The other three producers sharing the queue are fdps_show_number_indicator, which formats digits into the cells, and fdps_show_miss_indicator and fdps_show_cure_indicator, which push the fixed words at 0x0001c2d2 and 0x0001c2d6.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit the indicator floats over, into the 0x50-byte record array behind DAT_00069cd8; passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record and stored as a byte in DAT_000641e8. Its one caller fdps_cast_spell_on_targets passes an id out of its target list.
  sprite_ids -- pointer to up to four Number.cel sprite ids for the indicator's four 6-pixel cells, a zero id marking an unused cell. fdps_cast_spell_on_targets passes one 4-byte row of the three-label table at 0x00027668, each row being three ids followed by a zero. Decoding Number.cel gives sprite 0x3b='A', 0x3c='t', 0x3d='D', 0x3e='e', 0x3f='f' and 0x40='x', so the three rows spell Att, Def and Dex -- the three 神之祝福 buff slots that fdps_unit_apply_status_effect writes to unit-record bytes +0x22, +0x23 and +0x24. Nothing in this body depends on that; the ids are copied unread.

Returns:
  Nothing. Whether the unit was on screen is not reported, so the caller cannot tell a culled request from a queued one.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record and touches only game draw-list and camera state]

Rebuild note:
The queue cursor DAT_00064378 advances by the number of non-zero sprite ids while the slots are indexed by the loop counter (cursor + i), so the two agree only while the non-zero ids form a prefix -- which holds solely because every label the caller passes is ids-then-zero. Writing the obvious DAT_00064378 += 4 that the sibling producers use leaves an unwritten slot inside the drawn range for a three-id label, and turning the skip into a blank-cell write is wrong too, because the consumer's blank marker is 0xff, not 0. The viewport cull is deliberately lop-sided as well: the x lower edge is exclusive but the y lower edge is inclusive, so writing the two range tests symmetrically changes which units get an indicator along the top and left edges of the view. Keep both divisions signed (the original uses IDIV, truncating toward zero) rather than shifts.

=== 0001fd4e [EOL]
Two zero bytes of alignment padding after FUN_0001fc00, aligning to 0001fd50.

=== 0001fd50 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the six-entry int array of screen rows that drives the slide-in of the game's message window.

fdps_message_window_open copies these 24 bytes with REP MOVSD into its local int[6] at [EBP-0x2c] in the prologue (MOV ECX,0x6 / LEA EDI,[EBP-0x2c] / MOV ESI,0x1fd50 / MOVSD.REP at 000205bc-000205c9), before any allocation happens, and thereafter reads only the stack copy, indexed by the animation step counter i = 0..5. Each entry is the top row on the 320x200 page at which the 302x73 Message.cel panel is composited that step: the panel is alpha-blended in place at work_page + row * 0x140 + 9 by fdps_blit_blend_rects, and the band height blended is min(200 - row, 0x49), so a row below 127 shows only the part of the panel that still fits above the bottom edge.

The six rows are 190, 170, 150, 135, 127, 120 -- the panel rises from the bottom of the screen to its resting row in decelerating steps (deltas 20, 20, 15, 8, 7), the visible band grows 10, 30, 50, 65, 73, 73 rows, and the blend weight run in parallel is i*2+5 = 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 out of the 16 that fdps_blit_blend_rects divides by, so the window fades in as it rises. After the loop the panel is drawn fully opaque at (9, 120) by fdps_cel_blit_sprite, matching the last entry. fdps_message_window_close holds its own byte-identical image at 0001fd68 and walks it from index 5 down to 0 to slide the window back off the bottom.

Pool: binary_artifact  [read-only image the compiler emitted for an auto-array initialiser and block-copies into the stack frame; nothing indexes it where it lies and the game never names it]

Rebuild note:
The rows are not a linear ramp and the last two steps are not redundant: 127 and 120 both clip to a 73-row band, so the geometry repeats while only the blend weight advances 13 -> 15, and that repeat is the final fade-in frame. Generating the rows as a computed ramp, or dropping the step whose height duplicates its neighbour, changes what the reveal looks like on screen. The image is also the initialiser of a per-call local array, not a file-scope const table, and fdps_message_window_close carries its own separate copy at 0001fd68 -- folding the two into one shared const table removes a copy the original has.

=== 0001fd54 [EOL]
interior of the object at 0001fd50

=== 0001fd58 [EOL]
Tail of the 6-dword const initializer at 0001fd50 that FUN_000205b0 copies to a stack local int[6]; the values drive a six-step scripted screen sequence.

=== 0001fd68 [PLATE]
Initialiser image for the message window's close animation: the six screen rows the Message.cel panel's top edge occupies as it slides off the bottom of the display.

Nothing writes it. fdps_message_window_close copies all six dwords into its stack array at [EBP-0x30] on entry (0002082c MOV ECX,0x6 / 00020834 MOV ESI,0x1fd68 / 00020839 MOVSD.REP) and reads one entry per animation step. The loop runs i = 5 down to 0, so the rows taken are 120, 127, 135, 150, 170, 190 -- the panel descends. Each step alpha-blends the 302x73 panel over the work page at (x=9, y=row) through fdps_blit_blend_rects with blend weight i*2+5, i.e. 15, 13, 11, 9, 7, 5 out of 16, and clips the band height to min(200 - row, 73), which bites from row 135 on and shortens the visible band to 10 rows by the last step.

Values are 190, 170, 150, 135, 127, 120: as stored the rows descend, i.e. the image is written in open order and read backwards by the close animation. The image at 0001fd50 is byte-identical and is the copy fdps_message_window_open walks forward (rows 190 down to 120, panel rising, blend weight 5 up to 15); the compiler emitted the two images separately rather than sharing one.

Pool: binary_artifact  [ECX=6 / REP MOVSD of a fixed 24-byte rodata image into a stack frame at function entry, with no memcpy call, is wcc386's codegen for an initialised auto array rather than a global the programmer declared; only fdps_message_window_close reaches it]

Rebuild note:
The stored order is the opening order. fdps_message_window_close indexes this array from the last element to the first; writing the obvious forward loop over the table as it reads in memory slides the panel up into place instead of down off the screen, and runs the fade backwards as well, because the blend weight is derived from the same descending index.

=== 0001fd70 [EOL]

=== 0001fd80 [PLATE]
Draws one glyph of the game's 1bpp font into an 8bpp surface together with its background cell and its outline or drop shadow, doing every actual pixel write through fdps_blit_glyph_1bpp.

Algorithm:
Advances the font_base parameter in place by glyph_index * data_fdps_font_glyph_stride_bytes (the bytes-per-glyph stride of the font sheet) to reach this glyph's bitmap. If bg_color is non-zero, fills the glyph cell at dst with it first: data_fdps_glyph_cell_height rows of data_fdps_font_glyph_width bytes, stepping one pitch per row -- both globals are read as zero-extended bytes and are the cell height and width in pixels, taken from the font, not from the caller. Then draws the decoration underneath the glyph, choosing between two styles on the flag byte data_fdps_font_outline_enabled_flag: when it is non-zero the glyph is blitted four times in outline_color at dst+pitch, dst-1, dst-pitch and dst+1, a 4-connected one-pixel outline; when it is zero a single drop shadow is blitted instead, and only if outline_color is non-zero, at dst + data_fdps_glyph_shadow_row_offset * pitch + data_fdps_font_shadow_offset_x, i.e. displaced by the row count in data_fdps_glyph_shadow_row_offset and the column count in data_fdps_font_shadow_offset_x. Finally, if fg_color is non-zero, the glyph itself is blitted at dst in fg_color, so the foreground lands on top of the decoration.

Parameters:
  dst -- destination pixel, the top-left corner of the glyph cell in an 8bpp surface; the caller at 0001ff60 walks it across the line one glyph advance at a time
  pitch -- destination row stride in bytes; also the one-row step used to place the outline and the shadow
  font_base -- base of the 1bpp font sheet, glyph n at font_base + n * data_fdps_font_glyph_stride_bytes; the caller passes the global font pointer data_fdps_font_sheet_ptr
  glyph_index -- which glyph of that sheet to draw; the caller passes a message token value, or a decimal digit reduced by '0'
  fg_color -- palette index of the glyph body; 0 suppresses the foreground blit
  bg_color -- palette index the cell is filled with before anything is drawn; 0 skips the fill
  outline_color -- palette index of the outline or of the drop shadow; 0 suppresses the shadow but not the outline

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no FID candidate in either library set, and neither the Watcom runtime nor Miles contains a glyph renderer; reads the game's font/display globals 0x6403c-0x6404a and its only callee is game rendering code]

Rebuild note:
The four outline blits at 0001fdfd-0001fe62 are NOT guarded by outline_color != 0, while the drop-shadow blit at 0001fe67 and the foreground blit at 0001fe9c both are. Writing the obvious symmetric C -- one `if (outline_color != 0)` around the whole decoration step -- silently drops the outline whenever a caller passes 0, where the original paints four palette-index-0 copies of the glyph around it. Also, the cell dimensions and the glyph stride come from the globals data_fdps_font_glyph_width/data_fdps_glyph_cell_height/data_fdps_font_glyph_stride_bytes, not from the glyph or from the caller, and the two size globals are byte-sized and zero-extended (XOR EAX,EAX; MOV AL,[...]), so declaring them as signed char breaks cells wider or taller than 127 pixels.

=== 0001fec1 [EOL]
Alignment padding: multi-byte LEA NOP forms aligning FUN_0001fed0 to 16 bytes.

=== 0001fed0 [PLATE]
Blits one 1bpp glyph bitmap into an 8-bit destination surface, painting a single palette colour wherever a source bit is set and leaving every other pixel untouched.

Algorithm:
Loops row from 0 while row is below the glyph cell height at data_fdps_glyph_cell_height, and inside it column from 0 while column is below the glyph cell width at data_fdps_font_glyph_width; both bounds are zero-extended bytes re-read from the globals on every iteration. A shift register -- a full dword local -- holds the current source byte: on each column whose low three bits are zero it takes the next byte from glyph_bits and advances that pointer, otherwise it shifts the register left by one. When bit 7 (0x80) of the register is set it stores the low byte of color at dst[column]; when it is clear it writes nothing, so unset bits leave the destination as it was. After each row dst advances by pitch, which is also what makes data_fdps_font_glyph_width the horizontal extent and data_fdps_glyph_cell_height the vertical one: the inner index is a byte offset inside a single destination row, the outer step is a whole row. Source rows are byte-aligned -- the fetch condition is true again at column 0 of every row, so one row consumes ceil(width/8) bytes and the spare bits of a row's last byte are skipped rather than carried into the next row. There is no clipping and no bounds check of any kind; the caller owns keeping the destination inside its surface.

Parameters:
  dst -- destination 8bpp pixel at the top-left corner of the glyph cell. fdps_draw_glyph passes its own destination offset by +pitch, -1, -pitch or +1 to lay down the four outline copies, by the shadow displacement for the drop-shadow style, and unoffset for the body pass.
  pitch -- bytes from one destination row to the next; added to the working destination pointer once per row. The values that reach it from fdps_draw_text are 0x140 for the visible screen and 0x138 for the 312-wide offscreen pages.
  glyph_bits -- start of this glyph's 1bpp bitmap, most significant bit first, rows padded to whole bytes. Only the local copy is advanced, so the caller's pointer survives and the same glyph can be blitted repeatedly; fdps_draw_glyph depends on that for its outline passes.
  color -- palette index stored for set bits; only the low byte is used.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX at RET holds the zero-extended data_fdps_glyph_cell_height height byte left by the final row test, which no call site reads.

Pool: fdps  [no match in either FID set and the body hash is unique in the image; it shares the glyph cell width/height globals data_fdps_font_glyph_width/data_fdps_glyph_cell_height with its application caller fdps_draw_glyph and touches no CRT, DOS or AIL state]

=== 0001ff56 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6) + lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0] (4), aligning FUN_0001ff60 to 16 bytes

=== 0001ff60 [PLATE]
Draws one entry of a game text block into an 8bpp surface, interpreting the control codes embedded in the entry, and hands back the destination cursor it stopped at. Every piece of text the game shows -- menu labels, item names, save-slot dates and the chapters' spoken lines -- is drawn by this one routine.

Algorithm:
Adds the signed 16-bit word text_base[text_id] to text_base as a byte offset, landing on that entry's token stream, and walks the stream word by word until the -1 terminator. The line height is read out of DAT_0006404f once, at entry. Each signed 16-bit token is handled as:
  -2  line break: bumps the line counter and puts the cursor at dest + pitch * DAT_0006404f * line_count.
  -3  page break: fdps_flush_keyboard_queue, then fdps_message_window_wait_key(1, 0x64), then composes a fresh panel in a malloc'd 0x15180-byte 360x240 scratch canvas -- on the battle map (DAT_00060070 == 0) fdps_draw_scene_layers rebuilds the map into it and the Message.cel sheet DAT_000643d0 is blitted at (0x1d, 0x8c); in the village (DAT_00060070 != 0) fdps_blit_rect copies the visible screen in at scratch (24, 24) and the ShopWin.Cel sheet DAT_00069d84 is blitted at (0x18, 0x8d). When a speaker portrait is loaded (DAT_00060120, the FACE.CEL image that fdps_load_and_draw_portrait keeps) its 125x100 picture goes in at scratch (32, 110) through fdps_blit_dispatch. It then sits out one whole vertical retrace pulse on port 0x3da (spins until bit 3 sets, then until it clears again), copies the 312x192 window back to screen address 0xa0504, frees the scratch, clears the line counter and restarts dest at the panel's text origin -- 0xaa44a on the battle map, 0xaa3d4 in the village.
  -4, -5  substitution: calls itself on the global text block DAT_000643c4 at the entry ids held in DAT_00064030 and DAT_00064034, always in the standard message colours 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d rather than the caller's, and carries on from the cursor that call returns.
  -6  number: sprintf's DAT_00064038 through the format at DAT_000617e8 into a 12-byte stack buffer, takes its strlen, and draws it one digit at a time with fdps_draw_glyph as glyph index (digit - '0'), advancing the cursor by 0x10 per digit rather than by the glyph width.
  -0x11  speaker by character id: closes the window this call has already opened, if any (fdps_message_window_wait_key(1, 0x64) then fdps_message_window_close), reads the character id from the following word, resolves it with fdps_battle_find_unit_by_character_id, and takes the portrait index from byte +0x07 of the record whenever that call handed one back. It then opens the window with fdps_message_window_open_from_tile at the speaker's tile (record bytes +0x00 and +0x01) or, when the character is not standing on the map, at (-1, 0). Clears the line counter, puts dest at 0xaa44a and steps the stream by two words.
  -0x12  speaker by unit index: the same, except the following word is a unit index passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, so the portrait always comes from byte +0x07 of that record.
  anything else  a glyph index: fdps_draw_glyph(cursor, pitch, DAT_000643cc, token, fg_color, bg_color, outline_color), then cursor += DAT_0006404b, the glyph advance.
On the -1 terminator it waits out and closes the message window if one of the speaker codes opened it, and returns the cursor.

Parameters:
  text_base -- start of a text block: a table of signed 16-bit byte offsets followed by the token streams those offsets point at. Callers pass the global game-text pointer DAT_000643c4, the current chapter's text at DAT_00060124, or a block they have just loaded themselves.
  text_id -- which entry of that table to draw, a 0-based index into the offset table. Callers pass literal ids and computed ones alike (fdps_shop_draw_item_entry passes item_id + 0xc9).
  dest -- the byte address the first glyph goes at, and the line origin that the -2 line break measures from. Either an offscreen surface or a raw VGA address; the -3, -0x11 and -0x12 codes overwrite it with a fixed screen address, so an entry carrying them only comes out right from a caller drawing straight to the screen at pitch 0x140.
  pitch -- bytes per row of dest: 0x140 for the visible screen, 0x138 for the game's 312-wide offscreen pages.
  fg_color -- glyph fill colour, handed to fdps_draw_glyph unchanged. 0xd0 for ordinary text, 0xc8 for a menu entry that is not available.
  bg_color -- glyph background colour for fdps_draw_glyph; 0 everywhere, which leaves the background untouched.
  outline_color -- glyph outline/shadow colour for fdps_draw_glyph; 0x6d everywhere.

Returns:
  The destination cursor one glyph past the last glyph drawn, so a caller can chain a second entry onto the end of the first.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game call graph and game globals]

Rebuild note:
dest is a parameter, but the body writes to it: the -3 page break and both speaker codes replace it with a fixed screen address (0xaa44a / 0xaa3d4) and the -2 line break then measures from that new value. The obvious rewrite -- leave the parameter alone and keep the cursor in a separate local -- drops every line after a page break or a speaker change back at the caller's original origin. The -4 and -5 substitution calls likewise hard-code the glyph colours 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d instead of forwarding fg_color / bg_color / outline_color, so a substituted string stays in the standard message colours even inside text the caller asked for in another colour.

=== 000203ce [EOL]
2-byte alignment padding (mov eax,eax) before 16-byte aligned entry FUN_000203d0

=== 000203d0 [PLATE]
Holds the message window that fdps_message_window_open left standing on screen, repainting it over a live background once per game tick, until the player presses a key or the tick budget runs out.

Algorithm:
Allocates a 0x561e-byte (302 x 73) buffer and copies the message window straight off the visible mode-13h screen into it with fdps_blit_rect, from 0xa9609 = 0xa0000 + 120*320 + 9 at pitch 320 -- the exact place and size fdps_message_window_open puts the Message.cel panel, so the copy carries whatever text fdps_draw_text has already written into it. The four corner pixels of that copy (offsets 0, 0x12d, 0x54f0 and 0x561d) are then set to palette index 0, so the window's corners read as transparent when it is put back.
One pass per game tick follows, at most timeout_ticks of them:
  - fdps_read_keyboard_queue takes the next scancode, and the loop ends as soon as that byte is below 0x80, i.e. a key-press make code. 0xff (the queue-empty report) and 0x80-0xfe (key-release break codes) let it carry on; the scancode itself is discarded either way.
  - Allocates a 0x15180-byte (360 x 240) frame. The frame carries the scene layer's 24-pixel margin: frame (24, 24), byte offset 0x21d8, is screen (4, 4), so a frame position is a screen position plus 20 rows and 20 columns.
  - Background. When the flag at 00060070 is clear -- the battle map, where fdps_run_village_phase has not set it -- fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the whole scrolling scene into the frame, so the map keeps animating behind the window. When it is set, the 312 x 192 viewport is copied off the visible page at 0xa0504 into the frame instead, leaving a static backdrop.
  - fdps_blit_transparent_rect puts the saved window back at frame offset 0xc4fd, screen (9, 120), with palette index 0 transparent.
  - When show_wait_indicator is set, fdps_blit_command_sprite draws Command.cel sprite 0x48 + (tick / 3 & 3) at frame offset 0x106bc, screen (280, 166) -- the bottom right corner of the window -- so the four-phase prompt indicator advances one phase every three ticks. The tick it divides is the value read from DAT_00069d64 on the previous pass, so the first pass always draws phase 0.
  - When a portrait is loaded, i.e. the FACE.CEL cache pointer at 00060120 that fdps_load_and_draw_portrait fills is not null, fdps_blit_dispatch mode 0 draws it 125 x 100 at frame offset 0x9ad0, screen (12, 90).
  - Waits on VGA input status port 0x3da for bit 3 to go high and then low -- for the vertical retrace to start and then finish -- then copies the frame's 312 x 192 viewport to 0xa0504 on the visible page.
  - Spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from the value recorded on the previous pass, records the new value, frees the frame and decrements timeout_ticks; the loop repeats while that count is not 0.
The saved window is freed on the way out. The 360 x 240 frame is allocated and freed inside the loop, once per pass.

Parameters:
  show_wait_indicator -- nonzero draws the blinking four-phase prompt indicator in the bottom right corner of the window, zero leaves it out. All nine call sites pass 1.
  timeout_ticks -- the most game ticks to keep waiting, decremented once per pass and tested against 0 at the bottom of the loop, so a key press can end the wait earlier. Callers pass 0x1e, 0x32 or 0x64. Nobody passes 0, which would wrap and spin for 2^32 ticks.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; both callers are game code, it reads the game's own globals at 00060070, 00060120 and 00069d64, and touches the C runtime only as a consumer of malloc, free and inp]

Rebuild note:
The frame pacing spins on DAT_00069d64, which nothing in this function writes -- fdps_timer_tick_handler increments it from the timer interrupt. Written as the obvious while (last_tick == g_frame_tick) ; over a plain int global, wcc386 loads the counter once into a register and the loop never ends. The counter has to be declared volatile.

=== 000205af [EOL]
Single 0x90 NOP aligning FUN_000205b0 to a 16-byte boundary.

=== 000205b0 [PLATE]
Opens the game's message window over whatever is on screen: slides the Message.cel panel up from the bottom while fading it in, then leaves it standing with the speaker's FACE.CEL portrait drawn in it.

Algorithm:
Copies the six-entry row table at 0001fd50 (190, 170, 150, 135, 127, 120) onto the stack. Allocates a 64000-byte work page, a 64000-byte screen backup and a 0x561e-byte (302 x 73) panel buffer; grabs the visible mode-13h screen from 0xa0000 into the backup, zeroes the panel buffer and renders Message.cel sprite 0 -- the sheet in the global at 000643d0, loaded by fdps_load_global_resources -- into it at pitch 302.
Six animation steps then run, i = 0..5: restore the work page from the backup, take row = table[i], clip the band height to min(200 - row, 73), and alpha-blend the panel over the work page in place at (9, row) through fdps_blit_blend_rect, passing the [18][256] weighted-palette table at 000653f0 (Mer1.tmp) as its blend_table and the 16x16x16 inverse-palette cube at 000643f0 (Mer2.tmp) as its rgb444_lut -- both filled by fdps_build_palette_tables -- with blend weight i*2+5. fdps_blit_blend_rect divides by 16, so the panel comes in at 5/16, 7/16, 9/16, 11/16, 13/16 and 15/16 of full strength. Each step waits on VGA input status port 0x3da for bit 3 to go high and then low -- for the vertical retrace to start and then finish -- and copies the work page to 0xa0000, so the copy starts at the top of active display rather than inside the blanking interval.
Finally it restores the work page once more, draws Message.cel sprite 0 fully opaque at (9, 120) through fdps_cel_blit_sprite -- the 16/16 step, done as a plain blit rather than a blend -- waits on the same retrace edge, presents that page and frees all three buffers. The window is left standing: callers write their text into it with fdps_draw_text at 0xaa44a and take it down again with fdps_message_window_close, which walks the identical row table at 0001fd68 backwards and runs the weight ramp in reverse.
The portrait is last. A face_index of 0 or more is handed to fdps_load_and_draw_portrait with destination 0xa708c (screen x 12, y 90) and pitch 320, which loads that FACE.CEL entry into the cache at 00060120 and blits it 125x100 over the left edge of the window. A negative face_index means no speaker: the cached portrait at 00060120 is freed and the pointer cleared in line, rather than through fdps_load_and_draw_portrait, whose own no-portrait test is == -1 and not < 0.

Parameters:
  face_index -- index of the speaker's portrait in FACE.CEL, or negative for a window with no portrait. Callers pass a fixed index (3, 0x23, 0x28, 0x77, 0x7a, 0x81), byte 7 or byte 8 of a unit record, or, by way of fdps_message_window_open_from_tile, a signed character id read out of a message token that stays negative when that speaker is not standing on the map.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the Watcom or AIL sets, unique hash in the image; all fourteen callers are game code and the C runtime appears only as callees]

Rebuild note:
The retrace wait is two-phase -- spin until 0x3da bit 3 is set, then spin until it is clear -- so the 64000-byte page copy begins at the start of active display, not inside the blanking interval. The usual single-phase wait-for-bit-3-set alone starts each copy one blanking period earlier and changes what the six-step reveal looks like on screen.

Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6-byte nop) + lea edx,[edx+0] (3-byte nop), aligning next function to 0x20820.

=== 00020820 [PLATE]
Closes the game's message window: slides the empty Message.cel panel down off the bottom of the screen while fading it out, over a freshly rebuilt map scene, and leaves that clean scene standing on the visible page. The counterpart of fdps_message_window_open, which every caller pairs it with.

Algorithm:
Copies the six-entry row table at 0001fd68 (190, 170, 150, 135, 127, 120) onto the stack -- byte-identical to the table fdps_message_window_open walks at 0001fd50, but read from the far end.
It builds its backdrop instead of grabbing it. It mallocs an 0x15180-byte (360x240) scene scratch buffer, composites the live scrolling scene into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers, mallocs a 64000-byte (320x200) base page and zeroes it, and fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x138 x 0xc0 (312x192) view window from scratch+0x21d8 (x=24, y=24 at stride 0x168) to base+0x504 (x=4, y=4 at stride 0x140), leaving the four-pixel border black. It then mallocs a 64000-byte work page, frees the scratch buffer, mallocs an 0x561e-byte (302x73) panel buffer, zeroes it and renders Message.cel sprite 0 -- the sheet in the global at 000643d0 -- into it at pitch 302. That panel carries no text and no portrait.
Six animation steps then run, i = 5 down to 0: restore the work page from the base page, take row = table[i], clip the band height to min(200 - row, 73), and alpha-blend the panel over the work page in place at (9, row) through fdps_blit_blend_rect, using the [18][256] weight table at 000653f0 and the 4096-entry inverse-palette lookup at 000643f0 that fdps_build_palette_tables fills, with blend weight i*2+5. Each step waits on VGA input status port 0x3da for bit 3 to go high and then low -- for the vertical retrace to start and then finish -- and copies the work page to 0xa0000, so the copy starts at the top of active display rather than inside the blanking interval.
Because i descends, row runs 120, 127, 135, 150, 170, 190 and the blend weight runs 15, 13, 11, 9, 7, 5 out of the 16 that fdps_blit_blend_rect divides by, so the panel drops toward the bottom of the screen and thins out as it goes. band_height is 200 - row, and the clamp at 0002094d fires on the first frame only, at row 120, where 200 - 120 = 80 exceeds the panel's own 73 rows; at 127 the band is exactly 73 and the JLE is taken, and at 135, 150, 170 and 190 it is already 65, 50, 30 and 10. The shortening from 80 to 10 across the animation is the subtraction at 00020946, not the clip, and what the clamp bounds is the READ of the 302 x 73 panel buffer, not the write to the 64000-byte page.
Finally it waits on the same retrace edge once more and presents the base page -- the bare scene, no panel -- then frees the work page, the base page and the panel buffer. Nothing else is released: the FACE.CEL portrait fdps_message_window_open cached at 00060120 is left in place.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in the Watcom or AIL sets, unique hash in the image; all fourteen callers are game code and the C runtime appears only as callees]

Rebuild note:
Two things the natural close animation gets wrong. It does not retract the window that is on screen: it throws the visible page away and recomposites the map with fdps_draw_scene_layers, and the panel it slides is a bare Message.cel with nothing drawn into it, so the message text and the speaker portrait are gone from the first animation frame instead of riding the window down. And the retrace wait is two-phase -- spin on port 0x3da until bit 3 is set, then spin until it is clear -- so each 64000-byte copy to 0xa0000 begins at the start of active display; the obvious single-phase wait starts every copy one blanking period earlier and changes what the six steps look like.

=== 00020a70 [PLATE]
Opens the game's message window for a speaker standing on the map: grows the Message.cel panel out of the speaker's tile over seven scaled steps until it reaches the window's resting place, then paints the speaker's FACE.CEL portrait into it.

Algorithm:
When tile_x is -1 the speaker is not on the map, so the zoom is skipped entirely and fdps_message_window_open plays its slide-up open instead; control then joins the portrait draw below.
Otherwise it clears the map-cursor draw mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so no cursor is painted, walks the view and the cursor onto the speaker with fdps_map_cursor_move_to(tile_x * 0x18, tile_y * 0x18) -- 0x18 is the tile size in pixels -- and then sets DAT_00069cd0 back to 1, the ordinary cursor mode, rather than restoring what it held on entry. The speaker's position in view pixels is taken after that scroll: vx = tile_x * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 and vy = tile_y * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0, the camera's pixel scroll x and y.
Seven steps then run with i = 0..6. Each one allocates a fresh 0x15180-byte (360 x 240) scene page, composites the scrolling map into it with fdps_draw_scene_layers, and derives the panel's destination size as width = i * 0x12e / 6 (forced to 4 when that comes out 0) and height = i * 0x49 / 6 (forced to 2 when 0), 0x12e x 0x49 being Message.cel's full 302 x 73 sprite size. The corner interpolates from the speaker to the window's resting place over the same six intervals: x = vx + 0x14 + (9 - vx) * i / 6 and y = vy + 0x14 + (0x78 - vy) * i / 6, so the last step lands on (9, 0x78) in view coordinates, exactly where fdps_message_window_open leaves the panel. The constant 0x14 converts view coordinates into page coordinates, because the visible window sits at page pixel (24, 24) and screen pixel (4, 4).
The panel is sprite 0 of the Message.cel sheet in the global at 000643d0, drawn by fdps_cel_blit_sprite at pitch 0x168 with the packed destination size height << 16 | width and blit mode 4, which is fdps_rle_blit_scaled in fdps_blit_dispatch. Each step then spins on bit 3 of VGA input status port 0x3da until the vertical retrace begins and again until it ends, blits the 0x138 x 0xc0 (312 x 192) window at page offset 0x21d8 to the screen at 0xa0504 with fdps_blit_rect, waits for the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 to change and latches the new value, and frees the page.
Both paths finish with fdps_load_and_draw_portrait(0xa708c, 0x140, face_index) -- mode-13h screen at column 12, row 90, pitch 320. On the tile_x == -1 path that repaints the portrait fdps_message_window_open has already drawn for the same face_index.

Parameters:
  tile_x -- column of the speaker's tile on the battle map, 0-based; FUN_0001ff60 passes byte 0 of the speaker's unit record. -1 means the speaker is not standing on the map and selects the slide-up open.
  tile_y -- row of the speaker's tile, 0-based, from byte 1 of the same unit record. Unread when tile_x is -1; the caller passes 0 there.
  face_index -- index of the speaker's portrait in FACE.CEL, forwarded unchanged to fdps_message_window_open and fdps_load_and_draw_portrait. FUN_0001ff60 supplies byte 7 of the unit record when the speaker was found on the map, and otherwise the signed character id read out of the message token; negative means no portrait, and -1 additionally releases the cached portrait buffer.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, hash unique in the image; its only caller and every non-runtime callee are game code]

Rebuild note:
The tick latch the end-of-step spin compares against DAT_00069d64 is read before it is ever written, so on the first of the seven steps it holds stack garbage and the spin normally falls straight through; declaring it initialised from DAT_00069d64 costs one extra tick on that step. The retrace wait is also two-phase -- spin on port 0x3da until bit 3 is set, then spin until it is clear -- so each blit to the screen begins at the start of active display, not inside the blanking interval; the usual single-phase wait starts every step one blanking period earlier.

=== 00020c60 [PLATE]
Shows the current chapter's title card: the chapter's graphic fades up out of black over a black screen, holds for a second, fades back down to black and leaves the screen cleared.

Algorithm:
Loads "Chapter.saf" and "Chapter.pal" from MISC.VFS through fdps_vfs_load_entry. Clears the mode-13h frame buffer at 0xa0000 with memset (0xfa00 = 320*200 bytes).
Allocates a 0x16480-byte off-screen surface with malloc -- 0x170 * 0xf8, i.e. 368x248 -- and fills the 0x24-byte composite-sprite request on the stack: surface pointer, destination stride 0x170, height 0xf8, draw origin (0x18, 0x18), sprite bank = the loaded Chapter.saf image, entry index = the current chapter index at data_fdps_chapter_current_chapter_id (0-based, 0..29), and zero in the request's last two dwords so fdps_draw_composite_sprite takes its per-part blend path. Only then does it black the DAC out, by re-uploading the game's current palette at data_fdps_vga_main_palette_ptr through fdps_set_palette_range over entries 0..0xff with a -0x40 bias on all three channels, which clamps every entry to 0. fdps_draw_composite_sprite renders that chapter's title graphic into the surface, and fdps_blit_rect copies the 320x200 window starting at surface+0x2298 -- 0x18*0x170 + 0x18, the draw origin -- to the VGA frame buffer at 0xa0000.
Fade up: for i from 0x10 down to 0 inclusive, spin on inp(0x3da) until VGA status bit 3 (vertical retrace) is set, upload Chapter.pal over entries 0..0xff with a bias of -4*i on every channel, then delay(0x50) = 80 ms. The last step, i = 0, leaves the card at full brightness. delay(0x3e8) holds it there for one second. Fade down is the same loop with i running 1 to 0x10, ending at a -0x40 bias, i.e. black again; the two loops are asymmetric on purpose so the full-brightness step is played once, not twice.
On the way out it clears the frame buffer again, reinstalls the game's palette at data_fdps_vga_main_palette_ptr at zero bias -- so the caller inherits a live palette over a black screen and has to repaint whatever comes next -- and frees the Chapter.saf buffer, the Chapter.pal buffer and the off-screen surface.

Parameters:
  none. The chapter is taken from the global chapter index at data_fdps_chapter_current_chapter_id, which the chapter-progress routines set before the chapter entry handler runs.

Returns:
  nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in the Watcom libs or ailv3.lib; game strings, game callees, and all 30 callers are the chapter entry handlers fdps_chapter_01_init .. fdps_chapter_30_init]

Rebuild note:
The off-screen surface is 368x248 with the sprite drawn at (24,24), and only the 320x200 window at that origin is blitted -- a deliberate 24-pixel margin on all four sides, because the composite sprite's part records carry signed dx/dy offsets and nothing clips them. Allocating a tight 320x200 surface and drawing at (0,0), which is the obvious rewrite, lets any part that hangs off the picture write outside the allocation.

=== 00021240 [PLATE]

  2. fdps_chapter_state_reset rebuilds the per-chapter runtime state block from the 0-based chapter index held in DAT_00069cf4, and through FUN_00022be0 rebuilds the chapter's 0x50-byte map unit records out of the roster array. What does the setting is nameable: the shipped ICON14.DAT is the ONLY Icon%02d.dat in the game carrying opcode 0x62, the scripted actor step, and it runs exactly one -- fdps_map_actor_behavior_step(35, 0) at script offset 229. Map unit 35 is MAP14.DAT's record 27, the LV16 光束砲座, and the tail of that step is fdps_battle_mark_unit_done, which raises bit 7. fdps_icon_script_run clears bit 7 when it STARTS (0002166e) and not when it finishes, so nothing else takes it off again. No other chapter entry handler makes this call.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing. The dispatch sites call it indirectly through the table and ignore EAX.

Pool: fdps  [game asset string "Icon14.dat" at 000618ac and six game callees including fdps_chapter_state_reset and fdps_roster_add_character; Function ID finds no Watcom or ailv3.lib candidate, and the body does no runtime work -- no FPU, DOS interrupt, allocator or AIL state]

Rebuild note:
Three traps in a six-line function. The opening script is "Icon14.dat", one less than the chapter number in the handler's name, because Icon%02d.dat is numbered by the 0-based chapter index -- emitting "Icon15.dat" from the name plays chapter 16's cutscene. The order of fdps_roster_add_character(5) and fdps_chapter_state_reset is NOT load-bearing here, contrary to what it looks like: MAP14.DAT declares NINE player slots and the party is ALREADY nine members when the handler runs (chapters 1 to 4, 7, 8, 9 twice and 11), so fdps_build_map_unit_array fills slots 0..8 from roster slots 0..8 whichever order the two calls run in, and the array is identical either way -- the order is not observable here. 瑪麗安 lands at roster slot 9, one past the last slot this map has, and gets no player slot in chapter 15 at all. The 瑪麗安 the player commands is MAP14.DAT's own record 0: side 2, character 5, LEVEL 20, keyed wave 1, equipped 0x47 狙擊弓 and 0x79 銀鱗甲 and carrying 0xb6 再生藥, deployed by the script's one DEPLOY_WAVE. What the roster add buys is the chapters after this one: MAP15.DAT and every later map declare TEN player slots. And the fdps_units_clear_status_bit7 call between the title card and the cursor move is not boilerplate shared with the sibling handlers -- it is unique to this one, and dropping it as a copy-paste leftover leaves units the opening cutscene moved unable to act on turn 1; what raises the bit is named in step 5, ICON14.DAT's single opcode 0x62 at script offset 229, the only scripted actor step in any Icon%02d.dat in the game.

Why unit 3 is 法蓮娜: unit slot i is roster slot i. fdps_build_map_unit_array memmoves the roster record at DAT_00064108 + i * 0x50 straight into unit slot i for every i below the roster count DAT_00064114, and the roster is in join order -- fdps_roster_add_character writes at index DAT_00064114 and then increments it (00023bcc, 00023e12), nothing in the image decrements or permutes the roster, and fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units matches battle units back to roster entries by the character id at +8 rather than by position, so a chapter cannot reorder it. The chapter handlers call fdps_roster_add_character with 0, 6, 4, 1, 3, 2, 8 and 9, 7, 5 in chapters 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 11, 15, which against the FRIAPRDA.DAT character ids gives the roster 蘭迪斯, 尤利安, 亞克, 法蓮娜, 裘娜, 費塔加, 布蘭多, 蓋亞, 琴琴, 瑪麗安. Slot 3 is character id 1, 法蓮娜.

The cursor argument is what separates this handler from most of the family: twenty-seven of the thirty park the cursor on unit 0, and only this one, fdps_chapter_22_init (00021410) and fdps_chapter_23_init (00021450) pass 3. Those three are exactly the three chapters that turn on 法蓮娜 -- chapter 17 is lost the moment she dies, and both fdps_chapter_22_event_boss_defeat and fdps_chapter_23_event_boss_defeat branch on whether she landed the killing blow -- so the family's one deviation is each of her chapters opening with the cursor already on her. Nothing else in the body differs from the plain four-step form.
