Unit slot i is roster slot i -- fdps_build_map_unit_array copies the roster record at DAT_00064108 + i * 0x50 over unit record i -- and the roster is append-only in join order, because fdps_roster_add_character writes at index DAT_00064114 and only ever increments it, with no function anywhere that removes or reorders a member. So slot 0 is 蘭迪斯 (added by chapter 1), 1 尤利安, 2 亞克 and 3 法蓮娜, whom chapter 4 adds as character id 1. Twenty-seven handlers of this family open the chapter on unit 0, 蘭迪斯; this one, chapter 17's at 000212d0 and chapter 23's at 00021450 open on unit 3, and those three are exactly the chapters the player loses when 法蓮娜 dies: fdps_chapter_22_post_action declares defeat on fdps_unit_is_retired(3) alone, and fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions substitutes unit 3 for unit 0 exactly when DAT_00069cf4 is 0x10 or 0x15. The rule behind the literal is therefore the same in every handler of the family -- the cursor opens on the unit the chapter is lost without.

The handler itself adds nobody and stores nothing, but the cut-scene it runs does change the board. Walked with the opcode ladder in src/icon.c, ICON21.DAT's 283 bytes hold fifty opcodes and exactly ONE unit-state opcode among them -- the RETIRE_UNIT at script offset 278 naming map unit 0, with no REVIVE behind it anywhere -- so chapter 22 is fought without 蘭迪斯, which is the strategy guide's 己方 line for the chapter (蘭迪斯以外的所有人) and what chapter 21's 說明 announces as 後面兩章蘭迪斯不會出場. The member carries no SWITCH_MAP and no DEPLOY_WAVE, so the board is the state reset's alone: MAP21.DAT declares eleven player slots and tags exactly ONE of its fifty-five deployment records wave 0 -- a level-20 character 73, 巫湯婆婆 -- which makes the opening array twelve units, the shortest of the family. The other fifty-four records are waves 1 to 5, the chapter's own turn-event reinforcements: wave 1 eight LV19 狼人戰士 (83) with eight LV18 蛇魔使 (75), wave 2 four of each, wave 3 four LV17 幽魂 (105), wave 5 four LV17 骷髏兵 (84), and wave 4 the last twenty-two. Because the script switches no map, step 4 parks the cursor on the tile the script's own walks reached, (6, 19), and not on MAP21.COD's player-slot-3 start tile (2, 24) four tiles away.

  none

  nothing. The dispatch sites call it indirectly through the table and ignore EAX.

Pool: fdps  [game asset string "Icon21.dat" and four game callees; Function ID finds no Watcom or ailv3.lib candidate, and the body does no runtime work -- no FPU, DOS interrupt, allocator or AIL state]

Rebuild note:
The IconAni script number is the 0-based chapter index, so chapter 22's entry handler opens "Icon21.dat" -- and the handler sitting immediately after it in the file, chapter 23's, opens "Icon22.dat". Writing the obvious fdps_chapter_22_init that loads "Icon22.dat" compiles, runs, and silently plays the next chapter's opening cutscene while the title card (selected from DAT_00069cf4, not from the filename) still shows chapter 22. The cursor argument is the same kind of trap in the other direction: chapters 17, 22 and 23 park the cursor on unit 3 (法蓮娜) rather than unit 0 (蘭迪斯) because those are the three chapters that are lost when she dies, so normalising the family to fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(0) opens those chapters looking at the wrong unit.

=== 00021450 [PLATE]
Chapter 23's entry handler: brings the game into chapter 23 by resetting the chapter state, playing the chapter's opening IconAni cutscene and its title card, then parking the map cursor on 法蓮娜. It is reached through slot 22 of the per-chapter entry-handler table at 00060074, which fdps_title_screen and fdps_run_village_phase both call as table[DAT_00069cf4].

Algorithm:
  1. fdps_chapter_state_reset rebuilds the per-chapter runtime state block and the chapter's unit roster from the chapter index held in DAT_00069cf4.
  2. fdps_icon_script_run("Icon22.dat") loads chapter 23's opening event script from the IconAni.vfs archive and interprets it. The script number is the 0-based chapter index, one less than the chapter number the player sees, so chapter 23's script is Icon22.dat; the neighbouring handlers use Icon21.dat (fdps_chapter_22_init) and Icon23.dat (fdps_chapter_24_init).
  3. fdps_show_chapter_title_card shows the chapter title card: Chapter.saf and Chapter.pal out of MISC.VFS, the graphic again selected by DAT_00069cf4, faded up, held, then faded back to black.
  4. fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit(3) leaves the map cursor sitting on the tile of unit 3.

Unit 3 is 法蓮娜. fdps_build_map_unit_array copies roster record i into map unit slot i for every i below the roster count DAT_00064114, so map unit 3 is roster slot 3; and a roster slot number is a join order, because fdps_roster_add_character forms the destination record as DAT_00064108 + DAT_00064114 * 0x50 (00023bcc-00023be6) and only increments DAT_00064114 afterwards (00023e12). The first four joins are fdps_chapter_01_init's character 0 (slot 0), fdps_chapter_02_init's character 6 (slot 1), fdps_chapter_03_init's character 4 (slot 2) and fdps_chapter_04_init's character 1 (slot 3), and character 1 is the 魔導士 法蓮娜. Nothing renumbers the slots between chapter 4 and chapter 23: no code path decrements DAT_00064114 or compacts the array, and the two save loaders restore the roster as one 0xa00-byte memmove into DAT_00064108 plus the stored count, so the order survives a save and reload.

The cursor argument is what separates this handler from most of the family: twenty-seven of the thirty park the cursor on unit 0 -- 蘭迪斯, roster slot 0 -- and only this one, fdps_chapter_17_init and fdps_chapter_22_init pass 3. All three of those chapters are lost the moment 法蓮娜 dies, so the cursor opens on the character the chapter is played around; that is not the whole rule, though, because chapters 14 and 20 carry the same defeat condition and still open on unit 0. Nothing else in the body differs from the plain four-step form -- no character is handed to the roster before the reset and no unit status bits are cleared after the title card.

=== 00021643 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 13 zero bytes aligning next function entry to 0x21650.

=== 00021650 [PLATE]
Runs one IconAni event script: loads the named entry out of IconAni.vfs and interprets its byte-opcode stream until the script says stop. Every scripted cutscene in the game is one of these -- each chapter's opening scene (Icon%02d.dat) and each chapter's victory scene (Win%02d.dat).

Algorithm:
Clears status bit 7 on every unit through fdps_units_clear_status_bit7, saves the current chapter id data_fdps_chapter_current_chapter_id, and opens "IconAni.vfs" with fdps_vfs_open; when that fails it prints "file not found: '%s'", waits for a key and carries on with the null handle anyway. fdps_vfs_load_file(script_name, archive) then reads the script into a buffer, and a null buffer waits for a key and gives up.
The interpreter loop clears data_fdps_map_cursor_draw_mode on every pass, reads the opcode byte at script[offset] and dispatches it through a compare ladder; each handler advances offset past its own operands. b1/b2/b3/b4 below are the operand bytes following the opcode, and the number in brackets is how far offset moves.
  0x00  end of script -- and so is every opcode the ladder does not recognise
  0x01  fdps_icon_script_walk_units
  0x02  fdps_icon_script_set_unit_facing
  0x03  fdps_draw_text: text entry b1 of the block at data_fdps_current_chapter_text_ptr, drawn straight onto the VGA screen at 0xa0000, pitch 0x140, colours fg 0xd0 / bg 0 / outline 0x6d [2]
  0x04  fdps_deploy_wave(data_fdps_chapter_current_chapter_id, b1, b2); b1 == 0xff means "the branch the player picked at opcode 0x63" instead of a literal wave number [3]
  0x05  fdps_icon_script_scroll_view_to_tile
  0x06  loads "Icon%04d.saf" b1 out of the archive, fdps_saf_play_over_scene, free [2]
  0x07  fdps_cd_set_music_track(b1), with 0xff turned into -1, i.e. silence [2]

  0x09  fdps_icon_script_blink_units_out

  0x12  writes b3 into unit b1's record byte 0x25 + b2 -- the one unit opcode with no bounds check on b1 [4]
  0x13  data_fdps_map_cell_event_triggered_flags[b1] = b2, then fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes [3]

On the way out it frees the script buffer and the archive handle, frees every .wav buffer it parked, and sets data_fdps_map_cursor_draw_mode back to 1.

Parameters:
  script_name -- name of the script entry inside IconAni.vfs, passed on to fdps_vfs_load_file. Every caller hands it a string literal: "Icon00.dat" is chapter 1's opening scene, "Win00.dat" chapter 1's victory scene.

Returns:
  Nothing. The epilogue does leave data_fdps_chapter_current_chapter_id in EAX and compare it against the copy saved on entry, but the flags are dead and no caller reads the result.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; it writes the game's own globals and its only vendor callees are free, memset, sprintf and printf]

Rebuild note:
The .wav buffers opcode 0x08 loads have to stay allocated until the whole script has finished. fdps_audio_start_wav only starts the voice, so freeing each buffer right after the call -- the way opcode 0x06 does for its .saf, which plays synchronously -- leaves the mixer reading freed heap. The 20-slot table is also a hard cap: the twenty-first and later sounds of one script are silently skipped, and the missing bounds check on opcode 0x12 is likewise original and must stay.

=== 00021e30 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 5: scrolls the map view to a scripted tile, one tile-step per rendered frame, and leaves it parked there with the map cursor just inside the new view.

Algorithm:
Reads two unsigned operand bytes -- script[offset+1] is the target tile x, script[offset+2] the target tile y -- and converts each to map pixels by multiplying by 0x18, the 24-pixel tile size. Takes the pixel distance from the current view origin (DAT_00069ce4 is the view's x, DAT_00069ce0 its y -- the pair fdps_draw_scene_layers scrolls the layer table by) through abs on each axis, and makes the step count the larger of the two divided by 0x18, i.e. the tile distance along the dominant axis. When that count is zero the view jumps straight to the target. Otherwise it computes one fixed per-axis increment, target_delta / step_count, from the origin as it stood on entry, and then loops step_count times: add the x increment to DAT_00069ce4, add the y increment to DAT_00069ce0, and call fdps_render_view_frame, which waits for vertical retrace before it presents -- so the scroll runs at one step per frame and the dominant axis advances exactly one tile per frame while the other axis advances by a truncated share of that. After the loop it first puts the map cursor globals DAT_00069cd4 (x) and DAT_00069ccc (y) at target + 0x18, one tile in from the new view's top-left corner, and then writes the exact target pixels into DAT_00069ce4 and DAT_00069ce0, which absorbs the truncation left on the minor axis. Unlike fdps_map_cursor_move_to it applies no clamping against the map extents; the tile the script names becomes the view origin as written.

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image; fdps_icon_script_run loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and passes the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this opcode within that image, so script[offset] is the opcode byte 5, script[offset+1] the target tile x and script[offset+2] the target tile y.

Returns:
  offset + 3, the stream offset one byte past this instruction's two operands. fdps_icon_script_run stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; it owns the game's view-origin and map-cursor globals and its only game callee is fdps_render_view_frame]

=== 00021f57 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] aligning 00021f60 to 16.

=== 00021f60 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 1: walks a list of battle units a scripted number of tiles, each in its own scripted direction, playing the six-step walk animation as they go.

Algorithm:
Clears the cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 and the cursor/info-panel flag DAT_00060159 to 0, so fdps_draw_map_cursor draws no cursor and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel draws no panel while the scripted walk is on screen. Reads three unsigned operand bytes: script[offset+1] is how many rendered frames each of the six walk sub-steps is held for, script[offset+2] is how many tiles the group walks, script[offset+3] is how many units follow; then skips the 4-byte opcode header. Each unit is a 2-byte pair of a unit index and a direction code.
Three nested loops follow: tile 0..tile_count-1 outermost, walk sub-step 1..6 inside it, hold 0..frame_delay-1 inside that. Every hold pass walks the whole unit list. fdps_get_unit_record turns the pair's first byte into a pointer to that unit's 0x50-byte record; the second byte is written to the facing code at record+3 (0 down/+y, 1 left/-x, 2 up/-y, 3 right/+x -- the codes fdps_unit_face_target writes); and for sub-steps 1 through 5 the sub-tile step counter at record+4 is set to the sub-step number. fdps_draw_map_unit displaces a unit by 4 pixels per step counter along its facing, so the six sub-steps carry it across one 0x18-pixel tile. On sub-step 6, and only on the first hold pass of it, the step counter is cleared to 0 instead and the tile is committed: facing 0 increments the tile y at record+1, 1 decrements the tile x at record+0, 2 decrements the tile y, and any other value increments the tile x. After each hold pass over the list it calls fdps_render_view_frame, which waits for vertical retrace before presenting, and fdps_cycle_scene_palette, so all the listed units advance on the same frame and the scene's colour cycling keeps running under them; one tile therefore costs 6 * frame_delay rendered frames.
Nothing here scrolls the view, tests the terrain or reports an arrival tile to fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event, which is what separates it from the interactive playback family reached through fdps_animate_move_path: the listed units walk straight through whatever is in the way for exactly the scripted number of tiles. Finally it writes the constants 1 into DAT_00069cd0 and DAT_00060159 -- cursor mode 1 is the bare cursor tile -- and returns the stream offset just past the operands it consumed.

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image; FUN_00021650 loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and passes the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this opcode within that image, so script[offset] is the opcode byte 1, script[offset+1] the frames held per walk sub-step, script[offset+2] the number of tiles walked and script[offset+3] the unit count.

Returns:
  The stream offset one byte past this instruction's last operand, i.e. offset + 4 + 2 * unit_count. FUN_00021650 stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in the watcom or ail sets and the body hash is unique in the image; every callee is game code, and the body walks the game's script stream while mutating unit records]

Rebuild note:
The exit path stores the literals 1 into DAT_00069cd0 and 1 into DAT_00060159 rather than restoring what they held on entry, so an area-of-effect cursor mode does not survive the opcode; writing it as the obvious save/restore pair changes behaviour. Separately, the tile commit and the record+4 write both sit inside the per-frame hold loop (the commit guarded by hold index 0), so hoisting the unit update out of that loop -- the natural way to write 'update the units, then render frame_delay frames' -- makes the units still move when the frames-per-sub-step operand is 0, where the original moves them not at all.

=== 000220f9 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea nop plus one 0x90, aligning FUN_00022100 to 16 bytes.

=== 00022100 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 2: turns a list of battle units to face given directions and holds the view there for a fixed number of rendered frames.

Algorithm:
Clears the map cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 and the cursor/info-panel display flag DAT_00060159 to 0, so fdps_draw_map_cursor draws no cursor and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel draws no panel while the scripted pose is on screen. Reads two unsigned operand bytes: script[offset+1] is how many frames the pose is held for, script[offset+2] is how many units follow; then skips the 3-byte opcode header. Each unit is a 2-byte pair: the first byte is a unit index, which fdps_get_unit_record turns into a pointer to that unit's 0x50-byte record, and the second byte is written to record+3, the unit's facing code (0/1/2/3, the same codes the walk handlers reached from fdps_animate_move_path set). Every listed unit is turned first, then fdps_render_view_frame is called frame_count times, each call waiting for vertical retrace before it presents, so all of them appear to turn on the same frame. Finally it writes the constants 1 back into DAT_00069cd0 and DAT_00060159 -- cursor mode 1 is the bare cursor tile -- and returns the stream offset just past the operands it consumed.

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image; fdps_icon_script_run loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and passes the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this opcode within that image, so script[offset] is the opcode byte 2, script[offset+1] the hold length in frames and script[offset+2] the unit count.

Returns:
  The stream offset one byte past this instruction's last operand, i.e. offset + 3 + 2 * unit_count. fdps_icon_script_run stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; both callees and the sole caller are game code, and the body walks the game's script stream and mutates unit records]

Rebuild note:
The exit path writes the literals 1 and 1 into DAT_00069cd0 and DAT_00060159; it does not save and restore them, even though the sibling opcode handler fdps_icon_script_animate_view_offset does save and restore DAT_00060159. Rewriting this as a save/restore pair -- the obvious way to write 'clear the flags for the duration' -- changes behaviour whenever the cursor mode was not 1 on entry.

=== 000221d7 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] multi-byte NOPs aligning next function to 0x10.

=== 000221e0 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 9: flashes a list of battle-map units on and off, then leaves them off.

Algorithm:
Reads the unit count from script[offset+1], then advances offset past the 2-byte opcode header so the count unit indices sit at script[offset] .. script[offset+count-1]. Clears the map-cursor shape selector data_fdps_map_cursor_draw_mode (0x00069cd0) and the cursor-panel flag data_fdps_ui_play_active_flag (0x00060159), so that fdps_draw_map_cursor and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel put nothing on top of the effect while it runs.
Then seven phases, phase = 1 to 7. Each phase stores phase & 1 into byte +5 of every listed unit's record -- fdps_get_unit_record turns each index into a record pointer -- and then calls fdps_render_view_frame three times, so each phase lasts three retrace-paced frames. Bit 0 of record byte +5 is the retired flag that fdps_draw_map_unit tests before drawing a unit at all, so odd phases hide the listed units and even phases show them: hidden, shown, hidden, shown, hidden, shown, hidden. Phase 7 is odd, so the units are left hidden, with byte +5 holding the value 1 that fdps_unit_mark_retired writes -- the listed units are retired from the battle, not merely blinked.
The write is a whole-byte store, not a bit operation, so every other bit of record +5 is cleared as a side effect. That includes bit 7, the flag fdps_battle_mark_unit_done sets to record that a unit has finished acting. The single-unit retire and un-retire opcodes 0x0b and 0x0c inside fdps_icon_script_run edit the same bit with OR 1 and AND 0xfe and do preserve it.
On exit data_fdps_map_cursor_draw_mode (0x00069cd0) and data_fdps_ui_play_active_flag (0x00060159) are both set to 1 -- the bare-cursor shape and the panel enabled -- rather than restored to whatever they held on entry.
The shipped IconAni.vfs scripts use this opcode with one unit index (ICON04.DAT, ICON11.DAT, WIN00.DAT, WIN26.DAT, WINGA26.DAT) or two (ICON28.DAT).

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image. fdps_icon_script_run loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and hands the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this opcode within that image. script[offset] is the opcode byte 9, script[offset+1] is the number of unit indices that follow, and script[offset+2] onward are those indices, each one an index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8.

Returns:
  The stream offset one byte past this instruction's last operand, offset + 2 + count. fdps_icon_script_run stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [both callees are game code (fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_render_view_frame) and the only state it touches is unit records and the game globals data_fdps_map_cursor_draw_mode (0x00069cd0) / data_fdps_ui_play_active_flag (0x00060159); no Function ID candidate in the watcom or ail sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
This opcode assigns unit record byte +5 outright (MOV byte [EDX+0x5],AL at 0002226b), where the neighbouring script opcodes 0x0b and 0x0c in fdps_icon_script_run set and clear the same retired bit with OR 1 / AND 0xfe. Writing the obvious `rec[5] |= 1` and `rec[5] &= ~1` for the blink phases, or calling fdps_unit_mark_retired, preserves bit 7 -- the finished-acting flag -- where the original clears it on every listed unit, so a unit blinked out and later un-retired comes back able or unable to act depending on which version is running. The second trap is the ending state: the phase counter runs 1..7 and stops on an odd phase, so the effect deliberately ends with the units hidden and retired; a rewrite that treats this as a pure blink and restores the units' previous visibility afterwards leaves scripted units standing on the map that the original removed.

=== 000222b4 [EOL]
Watcom 16-byte alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs before FUN_000222c0.

=== 000222c0 [PLATE]
Plays one loaded .SAF animation through once over the live scrolling scene, presenting it in the game's framed 312x192 main view.

Algorithm:
Allocates an 0x15180-byte page with malloc -- a 360x240 8bpp surface, wider and taller than the presented window so a frame may overhang it without being clipped. Builds the 0x24-byte composite-sprite draw request on the stack: destination = that page, pitch 0x168 (360), height 0xf0 (240), x = y = 0x18 (24), SAF base (+0x14) = saf_image, blit parameter block (+0x1c) and blit mode (+0x20) both 0. fdps_saf_frame_count(saf_image) gives the frame total; for each frame index i from 0 to count-1 the request's index field (+0x18) takes i, fdps_saf_get_frame(saf_image, i) resolves the frame record, and that frame is held for the tick count in the frame record's i16 at +0x02 (the SAF frame's dwell time, 1..45). On every held tick: fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the scrolling layer table into the page from scratch, fdps_draw_composite_sprite draws frame i over it with flag argument 1, so the frame's own sound effect fires -- a frame that carries a sound retriggers it once per tick it is held; the routine then spins on port 0x3da until vertical retrace begins and again until it ends; fdps_blit_rect copies the 312x192 (0x138 x 0xc0) window at page+0x21d8 (24 * 360 + 24) with source pitch 360 to 0xa0504, row 4 column 4 of the mode 13h framebuffer, so the animation origin lands at screen (4,4) and the outer 4-pixel border and the strip right and below the window keep whatever was on screen already; finally it spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes and latches the new value. free releases the page on the way out; saf_image belongs to the caller, and both callers free it immediately after the call returns. This is fdps_render_view_frame's presentation loop with a SAF frame in place of the cursor information panel: no panel is drawn and the scene palette is not cycled, so both are absent for the length of the animation.

Parameters:
  saf_image -- the loaded .SAF animation image to play, allocated and freed by the caller. 0x00021650, the IconAni script interpreter, passes the Icon%04d.saf entry it has just loaded from the VFS; 0x000288f0, the magic-effect executor, passes Emg33-1.saf. Used as the composite-sprite bank at request+0x14 and as the argument of fdps_saf_frame_count and fdps_saf_get_frame.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls game drawing routines and reads the game's frame counter; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The dword holding the previously seen value of the tick counter DAT_00069d64 is never initialised: the first tick-wait of the first frame compares the counter against whatever the stack happened to hold, so in practice it falls straight through and that tick is presented without waiting. Writing the obvious C -- seeding that variable with 0 or with the current value of DAT_00069d64 -- makes the animation start one tick late. Leave it uninitialised, or start it from a value the counter cannot currently hold.

=== 0002240a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte Watcom NOP (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_00022410 to 16 bytes.

=== 00022410 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 0x0e: fades the screen to black over sixteen retrace-paced steps, so a scripted scene can black out between pictures.

Algorithm:
Walks a counter i from 0 up to 0x3c in steps of 4 -- sixteen steps in all -- and hands the upload the bias -i, so the bias runs 0 down to -0x3c. Each step first waits for VGA vertical retrace, polling the input status register at port 0x3da through inp until bit 3 (mask 0x8) reads set; then calls fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, -i, -i, -i), which re-uploads all 256 DAC entries out of the game's master palette image (Fde.pal, loaded into DAT_000643bc at startup) with that bias added to every channel and clamped to 0..0x3f; then calls the Watcom CRT delay() for step_delay_ms milliseconds to hold the step. Because every step re-derives the DAC entries from DAT_000643bc, the ramp always runs from the master palette, not from whatever palette is on the DAC when the opcode is reached.
The last step's bias is -0x3c, not -0x40, so on the VGA's 6-bit DAC any entry brighter than 60 finishes at 1..3 rather than 0. The counterpart handler fdps_icon_script_fade_in, opcode 0x0f, runs the same ramp backwards from -0x40 up to 0 to bring the picture back.

Parameters:
  step_delay_ms -- how long each of the sixteen steps is held, in milliseconds, passed straight to the CRT delay(). fdps_icon_script_run reads it from the unsigned operand byte script[offset+1] of the 0x0e instruction, so 0..255.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only substantive callee is the game's fdps_set_palette_range acting on the game palette pointer DAT_000643bc, and its only caller is the game's IconAni script interpreter]

Rebuild note:
The loop bound is 0x40 with the last bias reached being -0x3c, one step short of the -0x40 its counterpart fdps_icon_script_fade_in starts from. Writing the symmetric loop (i <= 0x40, or mirroring the sibling's range) blacks the screen out completely instead of leaving it very dark, and changes what is on the DAC between the two opcodes.

=== 0002247e [EOL]
Alignment padding: mov eax,eax (8b c0) filling 2 bytes to the 16-byte entry at 00022480.

=== 00022480 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 0x0f: fades the screen up out of black over seventeen retrace-paced steps, bringing the picture back after a scripted scene has blacked out.

Algorithm:
Walks a darkening bias i from -0x40 up to 0 in steps of 4 -- seventeen steps in all, the loop counter at [EBP-0x4] counting down from 0x40 to 0 and the bias being its negation. Each step first waits for VGA vertical retrace, polling the input status register at port 0x3da through the CRT inp until bit 3 (mask 0x8) reads set; then calls fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, -i, -i, -i), which re-uploads all 256 DAC entries out of the game's master palette image (Fde.pal, loaded into DAT_000643bc at startup) with that bias added to every channel and clamped to 0..0x3f; then calls the Watcom CRT delay() for step_delay_ms milliseconds to hold the step. The first step's bias of -0x40 clamps every channel to 0, so the ramp always begins from true black whatever was on the DAC; the last step's bias of 0 uploads the master palette unmodified, so the handler always finishes with the DAC holding exactly Fde.pal. The counterpart handler fdps_icon_script_fade_to_black, opcode 0x0e, runs the ramp in the other direction, but not symmetrically: it takes sixteen steps and stops at -0x3c.

Parameters:
  step_delay_ms -- how long each of the seventeen steps is held, in milliseconds, passed straight to the CRT delay(). fdps_icon_script_run reads it from the unsigned operand byte script[offset+1] of the 0x0f instruction, so 0..255.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only substantive callee is the game's fdps_set_palette_range acting on the game palette pointer DAT_000643bc, and its only caller is the game's IconAni script interpreter]

Rebuild note:
The ramp is not the mirror of its 0x0e counterpart: this handler runs seventeen steps from bias -0x40 (which clamps every channel to 0, true black) up to and including bias 0, while fdps_icon_script_fade_to_black runs sixteen steps and stops at -0x3c. Writing the obvious mirror of the sibling loop -- starting at -0x3c, or stopping the loop before the bias reaches 0 -- costs the final step that re-uploads Fde.pal unmodified, so the screen stays permanently dimmed instead of returning to full brightness, and the fade takes one step less time than the original.

=== 000224ee [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8b c0 (mov eax,eax) two-byte no-op aligning the next entry to 16 bytes.

=== 000224f0 [PLATE]
IconAni script opcode 0x10: displaces the map view by a scripted list of pixel offsets, holding each one for a fixed number of rendered frames, then puts the view back.

Algorithm:
Saves the current view origin -- DAT_00069ce4 is the view's x in pixels and DAT_00069ce0 its y, the pair fdps_draw_scene_layers scrolls the layer table by -- and saves the display flag byte DAT_00060159, then clears that flag so fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel draws nothing while the effect runs. Reads two unsigned operand bytes: script[offset+1] is how many frames each step is held for, script[offset+2] is how many steps follow; then skips the 3-byte opcode header. For each step it takes two more bytes and sign-extends each by subtracting 0x100 when it exceeds 0x7f, writes saved_x + dx into DAT_00069ce4 and saved_y + dy into DAT_00069ce0 -- each step's offset is measured from the saved origin, not added to the previous step's -- and calls fdps_render_view_frame frame_count times, each call waiting for vertical retrace before it presents. After the last step it writes the saved origin and the saved flag byte back, and returns the stream offset just past the operands it consumed.
The shipped scripts use two shapes of offset list: an eight-entry circular wobble of one pixel repeated four times (ICON00.DAT, ICON02.DAT), and monotone ramps of 6 or 8 pixels a step that slide the view off its origin and let the restore snap it back (ICON06.DAT, ICON08.DAT). The separate opcode 5 handler fdps_icon_script_scroll_view_to_tile is the one that scrolls the view to a new tile and leaves it there.

Parameters:
  script -- base of the IconAni.vfs .DAT script image; fdps_icon_script_run loaded it with fdps_vfs_load_file and passes the same pointer to every opcode handler.
  offset -- byte offset of this 0x10 opcode within that image, so script[offset] is the opcode byte, script[offset+1] the per-step frame count (1 or 2 in the shipped scripts) and script[offset+2] the step count.

Returns:
  The stream offset one byte past this instruction's last operand, i.e. offset + 3 + 2 * step_count. fdps_icon_script_run stores it as its new script position.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit on either the watcom or the ail set; its only callee fdps_render_view_frame is game code, and it shares the view-origin globals and the display flag with the game's rendering layer]

Rebuild note:
The two operand bytes per step are offsets from the origin saved on entry, not increments: rewriting the loop as DAT_00069ce4 += dx turns ICON06.DAT's ramp of -6,-12,-18,-24 into -6,-18,-36,-60. And unlike its sibling opcode handlers fdps_icon_script_walk_units, fdps_icon_script_set_unit_facing and fdps_icon_script_blink_units_out, which all end by forcing DAT_00060159 to 1 and DAT_00069cd0 to 1, this one restores DAT_00060159 to whatever it was on entry and never touches DAT_00069cd0 at all -- writing the family uniformly makes the cursor panel reappear after a cutscene that had hidden it.

=== 00022e30 [PLATE]
Loads one numbered entry of an offset-table archive file into a buffer slot the caller owns, replacing whatever that slot held before.

Algorithm:
Frees *buffer when it is not NULL, then opens filename with fopen in mode "rb" (the mode string at 00061a00). A failed open prints the format at 00061a1c, "\n\n File not found %s!!! \a\n", with the file name and calls exit(1), so the routine does not come back from that path. On success it mallocs an 8-byte scratch block into *buffer, seeks to file offset 6 + entry_index * 4 and freads 8 bytes there: the archive's offset table begins at file offset 6 and holds one 32-bit absolute file offset per entry followed by a sentinel, so those two dwords are the start of entry entry_index and the start of the entry after it. Their difference is the entry's byte size. It frees the scratch block, mallocs the entry's size into *buffer, seeks to the entry's start offset, freads the whole entry into *buffer and fcloses the file. Neither malloc result is checked and no failure after the open is detected; the routine returns with *buffer holding the entry.

The 6-byte header plus u32 offset table is not the layout of the .VFS containers the rest of the game reads (those have a 35-byte header and a 26-byte named entry table, and are read by fdps_vfs_open, fdps_vfs_load_file and fdps_vfs_load_entry); it is the packed-archive layout the studio's previous game used, and this is that loader carried over. Nothing in the image calls this function or points at its entry, and no file shipped with the game has this layout. The previous game's canon gives that layout as a six-byte signature "LLLLLL" at +0x00, u32 LE offsets from +0x06 with the last one a sentinel equal to the file's own size, and entry i occupying file[offset[i]..offset[i+1]] -- which is exactly what this body hard-codes; there the container is shared by eleven resource files and its unified reader fd2_load_dat_resource @ 0x111BA does what this body does. Documented in fd2-anatomy resource_info/overview.md lines 12-18, which is where the 6-byte header and the sentinel convention can be checked, since no file here can confirm them.

Parameters:
  filename -- name of the archive file to open, handed straight to fopen and used as the %s of the not-found message. No search path of its own.
  buffer -- the caller's buffer pointer slot, both in and out. On entry it must hold NULL or a malloc'd block, because a non-NULL value is freed; on return it holds the malloc'd entry, which the caller then owns.
  entry_index -- 0-based index into the archive's offset table. Not range-checked, and the table must also hold the entry after it, because the loaded entry's size is the difference between the two offsets.

Returns:
  Nothing. The entry is handed back through *buffer. On a failed open the function never returns: it exits the process with status 1.

Pool: fdps  [no FID hit in either library set and the body hash is unique in the image; it hard-codes a game archive layout and exits with a game message, using the CRT only as a leaf service]

=== 000232b0 [PLATE]
Deploys one unit of a map's scripted deployment table onto the battle map, appending its 0x50-byte record to the end of the unit array.

Algorithm:
Grows the unit array first. With the unit count DAT_00060150 still 0 it mallocs one 0x50-byte record into DAT_00069cd8, otherwise it reallocs the array to (DAT_00060150 + 1) * 0x50, and fdps_get_unit_record(DAT_00060150) resolves the new last slot.

The anchor tile comes from the map%02d.cod placement table at DAT_00060140 that fdps_deploy_wave loaded: placement record deploy_index sits at DAT_00060140 + 0xb + deploy_index * 6 and holds two signed 16-bit tile coordinates.

When place_exact is non-zero the unit is put on that tile as it stands. When it is 0 the tile is searched for instead: fdps_map_grid_reset blanks the occupancy grid at DAT_00060144, fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control(0) and (1) between them mark every unit still in play, and the whole grid is scanned row by row -- cell (x, y) at DAT_00060144 + 4 + (y * width + x) * 2, width and height being the header words at +0 and +2. A cell whose byte 0 has bit 0x40 set has a unit standing on it and is skipped; the zone-of-control bit 0x80 is deliberately not tested, so a deployed unit may land beside an enemy but never on top of one. For each remaining cell whose Manhattan distance to the anchor is no greater than the best so far it calls fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) and keeps the cell when the terrain code that publishes at DAT_00069d09 -- the index class_move_cost is read with -- is below 5. The best-so-far distance starts at 0xff. fdps_map_grid_reset runs once more afterwards, leaving the grid blank for the movement code.

Everything else comes from deployment record deploy_index of the resident map%02d.dat table, at DAT_0006013c + 0x83 + deploy_index * 0x1a, 0x1a bytes wide: +0 side, +1 character id, +4 level, +5 and +6 the two equipped items, +7..+0xc six carried items, +0xd..+0x10 the four spell-mask bytes, +0x11 the AI behaviour byte whose low nibble fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on, +0x12..+0x14 three more per-unit bytes, +0x15 the wave number fdps_deploy_wave matched on, +0x16 the death-script opcode with its signed 16-bit operand at +0x17, and +0x19 one further byte.

Base stats are computed from the character id. Below 0x3c the unit is a roster-side character: fdps_get_character_base_record gives the 24-byte FRIAPRDA.DAT record and fdps_get_growth_record the 11-byte FriLevUp.dat record, and attack (+0x37) = ap_base + level * ap_min, defense (+0x39) = dp_base + level * dp_min, dexterity (+0x3e) = dx_base + level * dx_min, HP = hp_base + (level - 1) * hp_min, MP = mp_base + (level - 1) * mp_min -- the multiplier is level for the three combat stats but level - 1 for HP and MP. Race (+0x1f), class (+0x20) and movement (+0x3b) are copied straight out of the base record. At 0x3c and above the unit is an enemy: fdps_get_enemy_record(id - 0x3c) gives the 10-byte EnemyDat.dat record and every stat is a flat multiple of level -- HP = level * word[+2], MP = level * byte[+4], attack = level * [+5], defense = level * [+6], dexterity = level * [+7] -- with race [+0], class [+1] and movement [+8] copied over.

The record is then written out: tile column (+0) and row (+1) from the resolved tile; sprite cache slot (+2) from fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group(character id, fp), which pulls the unit's walk sprites out of the open ICON.CEL; facing (+3), sub-tile step (+4) and status flags (+5) cleared; side (+6); the character id in both +7 and +8; +9 cleared. The eight 2-byte inventory slots at +0xa each carry a flag byte and an item id: slot 0 takes deployment byte +5 flagged 0x40 (equipped) and slot 1 takes byte +6 flagged 0x40, except that when byte +5 is 0xff the item from byte +6 moves into slot 0, still flagged 0x40, and slot 1 is flagged 0x80 (empty) with its id byte left as the allocator returned it; slots 2..7 take bytes +7..+0xc, flagged 0 when the id is not 0xff and 0x80 when it is. The six status timers at +0x22 are memset to 0, the four spell-mask bytes memmoved to +0x1a, and +0x1e, +0x21 (level), +0x31 (death-script opcode), +0x32 (its operand word), +0x34 (behaviour byte), +0x35, +0x36 and +0x3d filled from the deployment record. +0x3c takes 0 when the side is 2, the player side, and 0xff otherwise. Current and maximum HP (+0x40, +0x42) and MP (+0x44, +0x46) all take the computed values, so the unit arrives at full health.

Last, fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(DAT_00060150) derives the four combat stats at +0x48..+0x4e from what was just written, and DAT_00060150 is incremented so the new record counts as in play.

Parameters:
  deploy_index -- index of the deployment record, 0 .. map%02d.dat header byte +2 minus 1. It selects both the 0x1a-byte record in DAT_0006013c and the 6-byte placement record in DAT_00060140. The only caller, fdps_deploy_wave, passes its loop variable over the deployment table.
  fp -- the ICON.CEL stream fdps_deploy_wave fopens before its loop and fcloses after it; used for nothing here but passing to fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group.
  place_exact -- non-zero puts the unit on the tile the placement record names; 0 searches the map for the nearest unoccupied walkable tile to it. fdps_deploy_wave hands its own third argument down unchanged.

Returns:
  Nothing. The new unit is the record at the index DAT_00060150 held before the call, and DAT_00060150 is one larger afterwards.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; shared game globals and game callees, with malloc, realloc, abs, memset and memmove used only as leaf services]

Rebuild note:
The nearest-tile search accepts a cell whose Manhattan distance merely ties the best so far (CMP EAX,[EBP-0x14] / JLE at 000233e6), so the tile actually used is the last tie in row-major scan order, not the first; writing the obvious "if (dist < best)" moves every searched-for deployment onto a different tile. And when the deployment record's weapon byte +5 is 0xff, the item from byte +6 still goes into inventory slot 0 with the equipped flag 0x40 even when it is 0xff too, which sends fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats into fdps_get_item_record(0xff), past the end of ITEM.DAT's 251 records; the guard that obviously belongs there is not in the original.

=== 00023830 [PLATE]
Deploys every unit of one wave of a map's scripted deployment table onto the battle map.

Algorithm:
fopens ICON.CEL in mode "rb" (the mode string at 00061a00) -- the sheet each deployed unit takes its walk sprites from -- and opens the Field.vfs archive with fdps_vfs_open. When that archive will not open it prints "file not found: '%s'", waits for a keypress through fdps_wait_any_key and carries straight on holding a NULL handle. It then formats "map%02d.cod" from map_no into a 20-byte stack buffer and loads that archive entry through fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit into DAT_00060140; that entry is the placement table fdps_deploy_unit reads, 6-byte tile-coordinate records after an 0xb-byte header.

Next it walks the resident map%02d.dat deployment table already held in DAT_0006013c: header byte +2 is the number of scripted deployment records, record i sits at DAT_0006013c + 0x83 + i * 0x1a, and for every record whose byte +0x15 -- its wave number -- equals wave_no it calls fdps_deploy_unit(i, icon_cel_stream, place_exact), which appends one 0x50-byte unit record to the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 and bumps the unit count DAT_00060150. The loop bound is re-read from DAT_0006013c on every pass, which changes nothing because fdps_deploy_unit grows the unit array, never the deployment table.

Finally it fcloses ICON.CEL, frees DAT_00060140 and sets it back to NULL, and releases the archive handle with a plain free -- the VFS has no close routine of its own.

Parameters:
  map_no -- map number, 0-based, selecting the "map%02d.cod" placement file; callers pass DAT_00069cf4, the map the chapter is playing, or a literal map number
  wave_no -- the wave tag matched against byte +0x15 of each deployment record. 0 is the group placed when the map opens; higher numbers are the reinforcement groups the chapter event handlers bring on, and the turn-scheduled events pass the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 here
  place_exact -- 0 lets fdps_deploy_unit search outward for the nearest unoccupied walkable tile around the recorded position; non-zero puts the unit exactly on the tile the record names

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [game strings, game VFS calls and the game's own unit record array; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The missing-archive branch is not an early exit. After the message and the keypress control falls through into fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit with a NULL archive handle, and the game does not survive that call; writing the obvious return after the message would instead leave the game running with the wave silently never deployed.

=== 00023945 [EOL]
Watcom alignment filler: multi-byte NOP forms padding FUN_00023830 up to the 16-byte-aligned entry of FUN_00023950.

=== 00023950 [PLATE]

Algorithm:
Multiplies roster_index by the 0x50-byte roster record stride and adds the array base pointer held in the global at 0x00064108 -- the same base and stride fdps_roster_add_character computes inline when it appends a member. The address is spilled to a stack local and reloaded into EAX as the return value. There is no bounds check: the index is not compared against the roster member count at 0x00064114, and callers do that themselves.

The array is a single 0xa00-byte heap block: fdps_load_global_resources does PUSH 0xa00 / CALL 0x0003d375 / MOV [0x00064108],EAX at 000296b8-000296c5. It is allocated once at startup, never reallocated, and released only by fdps_shutdown_free_resources (read at 0002944c), so 0xa00 / 0x50 fixes the block at 32 records and a pointer into the roster outlives a chapter load. fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units at 000239ed and fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members at 00039f8d form the identical base + index * 0x50 inline rather than calling this accessor.

Parameters:
  roster_index -- position in the roster array, 0 .. [0x00064114]-1. fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members and fdps_play_ending_credit_roll pass a loop counter bounded by the count at 0x00064114; fdps_church_select_promote_candidate passes an id out of its caller-supplied entry_ids array; fdps_village_select_member passes the grid's scroll base at 0x000601b8 plus the cursor offset; fdps_shop_draw_member_entry, fdps_roster_preview_combat_stats_with_item and fdps_shop_buy_loop @ 00033b80 (calling from 00033d0e) pass a roster position received from their own callers.

Returns:
  Pointer to the 0x50-byte roster record. Callers read 16-bit fields at the odd offsets 0x37 and 0x39 and at 0x3e (fdps_roster_preview_combat_stats_with_item), the status byte at 0x05 and the class byte at 0x20, and the current-HP word at 0x40 which fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members tests for zero and refills from the maximum-HP word at 0x42. Never NULL, never range-checked.

Pool: fdps  [no library match in the Watcom or ail Function ID sets; every caller is game code and the only data reference is the game's own roster base at 0x00064108]

Rebuild note:
The roster record is exactly 0x50 bytes with 16-bit fields at the odd offsets 0x37 and 0x39 (read as MOVSX word at 000335a7 and 000335ba). Declaring the obvious C struct for it lets the compiler insert padding, which pushes sizeof past 0x50 and shifts every field from 0x37 onward, so the stride this accessor multiplies by no longer matches the array the save file restores. Keep the record packed (or address it by byte offset) and keep the stride literal 0x50.

=== 00023975 [EOL]
Alignment padding: multi-byte NOP forms lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx

=== 00023980 [PLATE]
Banks the party at the end of a battle: copies every battle-map unit's record back over the party roster record of the same character, and resets the fields that must not survive the chapter.

Algorithm:
Outer loop over unit_index 0 .. [0x00060150]-1, the live battle unit count; each unit record comes from fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index). Inner loop over roster_index 0 .. [0x00064114]-1, the roster member count, addressing the roster record as [0x00064108] + roster_index * 0x50 -- the same base and stride fdps_get_roster_record uses. A roster slot is matched when its character id byte at +0x08 equals the unit's. There is no break on a match, so every slot carrying that id is written.
One case is exempt: when the character id is 0 (Randis) and fdps_unit_is_retired(unit_index) reports the unit has left the battle, the slot is left untouched and the scan moves on to the next slot.
For a matched slot the routine then, in order:
  1. memmove(slot, unit, 0x50) -- the whole record;
  2. memset(slot + 0x22, 0, 6) -- clears the six status-effect timers at +0x22..+0x27, so no buff or ailment carries out of the battle;
  3. slot[+0x05] &= 1 -- keeps only bit 0, the retired/dead flag that fdps_unit_is_retired returns, and drops every other status bit;
  4. when that byte is now 0, i.e. the member is not retired, copies maximum HP (word +0x42) into current HP (word +0x40) -- a full heal for every survivor, skipped for the dead;
  5. copies maximum MP (word +0x46) into current MP (word +0x44) unconditionally, dead members included;
  6. reads the experience byte at +0x3c as an unsigned byte and stores 0 when it is above 99, which catches both an experience count that has run past a level boundary and the 0xff sentinel the deployment path writes for units that are not roster characters;
  7. calls fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats(roster_index), rebuilding the four derived combat stat words at +0x48..+0x4e from the record just installed.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  Nothing. The result is the rewritten roster array at [0x00064108].

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record, fdps_unit_is_retired and fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats and works only on the game's own unit and roster globals; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail library set]

Rebuild note:
The experience byte at +0x3c must be read unsigned. The test is MOV AL,[slot+0x3c] / AND EAX,0xff / CMP EAX,0x63 / JLE, a zero-extended byte against 99; typing that field as a plain signed char makes the 0xff sentinel compare as -1, so it is not reset, it survives into the roster, and the status panel takes its 0xff branch and prints 1000 instead of an experience count.

=== 00023abd [EOL]
Alignment padding: 3-byte NOP form 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_00023ac0 to a 4-byte boundary.

=== 00023ac0 [PLATE]
Recomputes one roster member's four derived combat stats from the record's base stats and the items equipped in it.

Algorithm:
Forms the record pointer as [0x00064108] + roster_index * 0x50 -- the party roster array, the same base and 0x50 stride fdps_get_roster_record uses -- and seeds four running totals from the record's base stats: attack from the signed word at +0x37, defense from the word at +0x39, and both hit and evade from the single dexterity word at +0x3e (there is no separate evade base). It then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries starting at record+0x0a, and for every entry whose flag byte has bit 0x40 (equipped) set it looks the item id in that entry's second byte up with fdps_get_item_record and adds the item record's four signed word modifiers: +0x01 (ap) to attack, +0x05 (dp) to defense, +0x03 (hit) to hit, +0x07 (ev) to evade. Entries flagged empty (bit 0x80) or merely carried contribute nothing. The four totals are stored back as words at record +0x48 (attack), +0x4a (defense), +0x4c (hit) and +0x4e (evade) -- the fields fdps_draw_unit_status_panel prints.

This is the roster half of a pair. fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats is the battle half: it runs the identical seed-and-equipment sum over a record of the battle/map unit array at [0x00069cd8], and additionally adds 15 to the dexterity seed while the buff timer byte at +0x24 runs and scales the attack and defense totals by 1.15 while the timers at +0x22 and +0x23 run. This function makes neither adjustment and never reads +0x22..+0x24: base stats plus equipment is the whole computation on the roster side. The third member of the family is fdps_roster_preview_combat_stats_with_item, which derives the same four values for a candidate item in the shop without storing them.

Parameters:
  roster_index -- position in the party roster array, 0 .. [0x00064114]-1. fdps_roster_add_character passes the slot it has just filled in; fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units passes a loop counter bounded by the roster count at 0x00064114. Not range-checked.

Returns:
Nothing. The result is the four stat words written into the roster record.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; walks the game's 0x50-byte roster record through the game global at 0x00064108, and its only callee is the game's own item-record lookup]

Rebuild note:
Hit and evade are both seeded from the one dexterity word at record+0x3e; there is no separate evade base field (record+0x40 is current HP), so writing the obvious 'one base field per derived stat' version gives a wrong evade. In the same loop the equipped scan covers all eight inventory entries at record+0x0a, not just the two equipment slots that fdps_roster_add_character marks 0x40, so an item sitting in a later slot with bit 0x40 set does contribute to the totals. Third, the roster and battle recomputes are not interchangeable despite writing the same four fields from the same sources: this body applies none of the +0x22/+0x23/+0x24 status modifiers that fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats applies, so folding the obvious duplication into one shared routine changes roster stats wherever a roster record happens to carry a non-zero byte at those offsets.

=== 000241e0 [PLATE]
Runs the save-game screen: lets the player choose a slot and writes the current game state into FDE.SAV, over and over until the player backs out.

Algorithm:
Sets the save/load mode flag DAT_00064104 to 0 (0 = save, 1 = load; fdps_save_slot_select_loop reads it to decide whether an empty slot may be picked), builds the menu page with fdps_saveload_screen_build("Save.cel"), and mosaic-reveals that page onto the VGA screen at 0xa0000 with fdps_transition_random_blocks (320x200 at pitch 0x140, a 16x16 phase grid of 4x3 blocks, delay 1).
Then loops for as long as the last selection was 1:
  - fdps_save_slot_select_loop(page, &slot_index) returns 1 for a confirmed slot or -1 for Esc.
  - On 1, mallocs a 0x59cb-byte image of FDE.SAV. If fopen succeeds it freads the whole file, decrypts it in place with fdps_xor_crypt_buffer and fcloses; if the file is not there it memsets the whole image to 0xff instead, and that fresh image is deliberately not run through the cipher.
  - The slot record sits at image + 0x312b + slot_index * 0xa28. memmove copies 0xa00 bytes of live game state out of the block DAT_00064108 points at into that record, and then the last 0x14 bytes of that same 0xa00 region are overwritten with the stamp: month at +0x9fc and day at +0x9f8 from _dos_getdate, hour at +0x9f4 and minute at +0x9f0 from _dos_gettime, and DAT_00064110 at +0x9ec.
  - The header bytes follow the copied region: chapter index DAT_00069cf4 at +0xa00 (fdps_saveload_screen_build treats 0xff here as an empty slot), party member count DAT_00064114 at +0xa01, party gold DAT_000643a4 as a dword at +0xa02, then the four option bytes fdps_options_menu maintains -- DAT_00060158 at +0xa06, DAT_00060010 at +0xa07, the player's background-music toggle DAT_00060008 at +0xa08 and his sound-effect toggle DAT_00069d70 at +0xa09.
  - Reopens FDE.SAV for writing, stores fdps_compute_save_checksum(image, 0x59cb) at image + 0x59c7, encrypts all 0x59cb bytes with fdps_xor_crypt_buffer, fwrites them, fcloses, frees the image, then frees the menu page and rebuilds it with fdps_saveload_screen_build("Save.cel") so the slot list shows the save just made.
On leaving the loop it frees the menu page and mosaic-reveals restore_page onto the VGA screen with the same fdps_transition_random_blocks call.

Parameters:
  restore_page -- the caller's 64000-byte 320x200 8bpp page that the display is transitioned back to when the save screen closes. fdps_run_village_phase passes a freshly zeroed page, so the screen fades to black; fdps_run_bar_shop passes the page holding the bar screen.

Returns:
  Nothing. Whether anything was saved is not reported to the caller.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in the image, and it calls named game routines while using the CRT only as a consumer]

Rebuild note:
The timestamp fields and DAT_00064110 land inside the 0xa00-byte block that was just memmoved, at +0x9ec..+0x9ff, not after it; appending them after the copied block shifts every header field and breaks fdps_load_game_screen and fdps_draw_save_slot_panel. A missing FDE.SAV is initialised with memset 0xff and not 0, because 0xff in the record's chapter byte at +0xa00 is what marks a slot empty.

It fopen()s ICON.CEL, calls fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group with the leader's icon group slot_record[7], fclose()s the sheet, and takes the portrait as data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr + *(int *)(data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr + 4), that is sprite 1 of cache slot 0; the slot number fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group returns is discarded.
It paints the fixed captions with fdps_blit_command_sprite -- Command.cel sprites 0x2a and 0x2b at row 0x1a, columns 6 and 0x1f; 0x37 and 0x38 at row 0x13, columns 0x27 and 0x3c; 0x39 at row 0x14, column 0x5d -- and blits the 24x24 portrait through fdps_blit_dispatch in mode 0 at row 10, column 8.
What those five caption sprites are, decoded from the shipped COMMAND.CEL (MISC.VFS member, sprites 25x22, rendered through tools/cel_decode): 0x2a and 0x2b are the left and right halves of the scroll ornament along the panel's foot; 0x37 carries BOTH labels in one sprite, "LV" over "MAP", for the two figures at column 0x43; 0x38 carries the two arrow markers between those labels and their figures; 0x39 carries "/" over ":", the separators for the day-month pair on the upper row and the hour-minute pair on the lower one, which is why it alone is placed at row 0x14 -- its glyphs line up with the digits, not with the labels. Each caption sprite spans both text rows, so three sprites caption six figures, and the panel reads: row 0x13 "LV > level  day / month", row 0x1d "MAP > chapter  hour : minute".
It then copies out the fields it will print: the leader's level from slot_record[0x21], and the four dwords the save writer at 0x000241e0 leaves just below the chapter byte -- the month at +0x9fc, the day at +0x9f8, the hour at +0x9f4 and the minute at +0x9f0, each one byte of the _dos_getdate / _dos_gettime structures widened to a dword. The chapter number is the chapter byte plus one; it is both what the panel prints and what the routine formats through "fdetxt%02d.txt", the same 1-based naming fdps_field_load_chapter_resources uses. fdps_vfs_load_entry pulls that member out of Field.vfs, fdps_draw_text prints its message 1 -- the chapter title -- at dest+0x1ab5 (row 21, column 117), and the buffer is freed.
Six numbers follow, all two digits wide with no sign, drawn by fdps_draw_number and coloured through the Number.cel colour-row selector data_fdps_number_glyph_color_row: the level at row 0x13, column 0x43 in whatever colour row the global already holds; then data_fdps_number_glyph_color_row = 3 and the chapter number at row 0x1d, column 0x43; then data_fdps_number_glyph_color_row = 1 and the date, month at row 0x13, column 0x64 and day at row 0x13, column 0x51; then data_fdps_number_glyph_color_row = 2 and the time, minute at row 0x1d, column 0x64 and hour at row 0x1d, column 0x51. data_fdps_number_glyph_color_row is put back to 0 on the way out, which is what leaves it at 0 for the level of the next panel.

Parameters:
  dest -- top-left byte of this slot's panel inside the 8bpp page being built. fdps_saveload_screen_build forms it as page + 0xd + (slot * 0x34 + 0x1a) * 0x140, so the slot panels sit 52 rows apart. The two message destinations 0x1aa4 and 0x1ab5 are raw byte offsets that already assume a 320-byte pitch, unlike every other position here.
  pitch -- destination stride in bytes; 0x140 at the only call site. It multiplies every row constant and is handed straight through to fdps_blit_command_sprite, fdps_blit_dispatch, fdps_draw_number and fdps_draw_text.
  slot_record -- one 0xa28-byte save slot inside the decrypted FDE.SAV image, formed by the caller as save_buffer + 0x312b + slot * 0xa28. The roster copy is 31 entries of 0x50 bytes ending at +0x9b0, followed by 0x3c bytes of gap, a flag dword at +0x9ec, then the four timestamp dwords at +0x9f0..+0x9ff and the chapter index at +0xa00, where 0xff means the slot has never been written. slot_record[7] and slot_record[0x21] are the leader's icon group and level.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either Watcom or ail; game assets ICON.CEL and Field.vfs, game callees fdps_vfs_load_entry / fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group / fdps_blit_dispatch]

Rebuild note:
The portrait is fetched from the fixed address data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr + 4 -- sprite 1 of cache slot 0 -- and that is the right face only because the routine freed the ICON.CEL cache and zeroed data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_count immediately beforehand, forcing the group it loads into slot 0. Writing the obvious thing, indexing the cache by the slot number fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group hands back instead of throwing the cache away first, draws the wrong portrait from the second panel onward. The same teardown is why fdps_saveload_screen_build reloads every roster member's icon group after its slot loop finishes: drop that and the rest of the game paints from a one-entry cache.

=== 00024d50 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the four-entry icon array of the item ring menu: the Command.cel sprite ids 7, 4, 6, 5.

Nothing writes it; it is read once per call, at the top of fdps_battle_item_menu, where four inline MOVSD copy all 0x10 bytes into that function's local array at EBP-0x64. That local is then handed as the cmd_icons argument to fdps_menu_animate_open, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop and fdps_menu_animate_close, which read it as four ints and never write it. The four entries are in ring slot order up, left, right, down -- the same order fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop moves the menu cursor in and the same order fdps_battle_item_menu dispatches on: slot 0 (icon 7) uses an item, slot 1 (icon 4) hands one to an adjacent unit, slot 2 (icon 6) opens fdps_unit_equip_window, slot 3 (icon 5) discards. Each value is an index into the Command.cel sheet at DAT_000643ac; fdps_render_ring_menu_frame draws sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24, so a greyed-out slot takes its icon from a second bank 0x24 sprites further in. The paired image at 0x24d60 is the sixteen zero bytes that initialise the matching cmd_disabled array, whose entry 1 fdps_battle_item_menu then sets to 1 when fdps_collect_targets_in_range finds nobody adjacent to hand an item to.

Pool: binary_artifact  [the four inline MOVSD with no counter and no memcpy call are Watcom's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so these bytes are wcc386's own output rather than a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
These bytes have no name in the original source. The faithful rebuild writes `int cmd_icons[4] = {7, 4, 6, 5};` as a local of fdps_battle_item_menu and lets wcc386 regenerate the image; hoisting it to a file-scope const array and passing its address instead is the wrong shape here, and doing the same to the paired zero image at 0x24d60 is an actual bug, because fdps_battle_item_menu writes entry 1 of its stack copy of that array.

=== 00024d60 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the four-entry disabled-flag array of the in-battle item ring menu: four zero ints, meaning all four item commands start out selectable.

Nothing writes the image itself. It is read once per call, in the prologue of fdps_battle_item_menu, where four inline MOVSD copy all 0x10 bytes into that function's local array at EBP-0x54, immediately after the same idiom fills the paired icon array at EBP-0x64 from 0x00024d50. The local copy is then handed by address to fdps_menu_find_first_enabled_entry, fdps_menu_animate_open, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop and fdps_menu_animate_close on every pass of the menu loop at 000252db.

The four entries are in ring slot order up, left, right, down, the same order the menu cursor index runs in: 0 up = use an item, 1 left = give an item to an adjacent unit, 2 right = equip, 3 down = drop. A zero entry means the slot may be chosen; fdps_menu_find_first_enabled_entry returns the first zero as the starting cursor position and -1 if all four are non-zero, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop only moves the cursor onto a direction whose entry is zero, and the ring renderer draws slot i with icon sprite cmd_icons[i] + cmd_disabled[i] * 0x24 out of the Command.cel sheet at DAT_000643ac, so a non-zero entry also takes the greyed-out sprite bank.

Only entry 1 is ever changed, and only in the local copy: fdps_battle_item_menu calls fdps_collect_targets_in_range for range 1 around the acting unit and, when it returns no targets, stores 1 into element 1 at 00025340 so the give command is greyed out with nobody adjacent to give to. That store is one-way -- there is no path that puts the entry back to zero -- so once the give slot is greyed out it stays greyed out until fdps_battle_item_menu returns and a later call re-copies this image.

Pool: binary_artifact  [four inline MOVSD with no counter and no memcpy call are Watcom's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so these bytes are wcc386's output rather than a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
Sixteen zero bytes in read-only data immediately before the entry point of fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats look exactly like inter-function alignment filler, and dropping them is the obvious mistake; they are a live initialiser that fdps_battle_item_menu block-copies on every call. The faithful rebuild writes `int cmd_disabled[4] = {0};` as an ordinary auto of fdps_battle_item_menu. Because every entry is zero it is tempting to delete the array and pass a shared file-scope const zero array or a null pointer instead: null crashes, since the readers dereference all four entries every frame, and const or static is wrong because element 1 of the copy is written at 00025340 -- static would additionally leak the greyed-out give command into the next call of the menu, which the per-call re-copy is exactly what prevents.

=== 00024d70 [PLATE]
Recomputes one battle-map unit's four derived combat stats from its base stats, the items it has equipped and the buffs currently running on it, and writes them back into the unit record.

Algorithm:
Resolves the record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and seeds four 32-bit running totals from the record's base stats: attack from the signed word at +0x37, defense from the signed word at +0x39, and both hit and evade from the single dexterity word at +0x3e -- there is no separate evade base. When the buff timer byte at +0x24 is non-zero it adds 15 to that dexterity seed before it is copied into the second total, so that buff lifts hit and evade together. It then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries starting at record+0x0a, i from 0 to 7. An entry contributes only when its flag byte carries the equipped bit 0x40; its item id, the entry's second byte, is resolved through fdps_get_item_record and the ITEM.DAT record's four modifier words are added -- +0x01 (ap) to attack, +0x05 (dp) to defense, +0x03 (hit) to hit, +0x07 (ev) to evade. With the sum complete, if the buff timer byte at +0x22 is non-zero the attack total is multiplied by the double 1.15 held at 00061b1c and truncated toward zero by __CHP, and if the buff timer byte at +0x23 is non-zero the defense total is scaled the same way by the 1.15 held at 00061b24. The four totals are finally stored as words at record +0x48 (attack), +0x4a (defense), +0x4c (hit) and +0x4e (evade) -- the fields fdps_draw_unit_status_panel prints, highlighting attack while +0x22 runs, defense while +0x23 runs, and hit, evade and dexterity while +0x24 runs. Nothing is bounds-checked and no total is clamped.

Bytes +0x22 through +0x27 are the unit's six status timers, counted down one per turn by fdps_battle_tick_status_effects, which calls this function for the unit whenever one of them reaches zero so the expired buff drops out of the stats again. The roster-side counterpart is fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats, which runs the same equipment sum over a party roster record but applies neither the 15-point dexterity bonus nor the two 1.15 multipliers.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte battle/map unit array based at [0x00069cd8], 0 .. [0x00060150]-1; the index fdps_get_unit_record takes. Callers pass the unit whose equipment or status has just changed.

Returns:
Nothing. The result is the four stat words written into the unit record at +0x48, +0x4a, +0x4c and +0x4e.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ail set and the body hash is unique in the image; game domain logic over the FDPS unit record and ITEM.DAT, with all fifteen callers ordinary game bodies -- the one runtime contact, __CHP between FILD/FMUL and FISTP, is the Watcom float-to-int helper being consumed here]

Rebuild note:
The two buff multipliers are the double 1.15 applied as an x87 multiply followed by a truncate-toward-zero, i.e. exactly (int)(total * 1.15) in double precision; rewriting them as the obvious integer form total * 115 / 100 diverges wherever the double product lands just under an integer -- a buffed attack of 100 must come out 114, not 115, and 180, 200, 220, 340, 360 and 380 are wrong the same way. Second, hit and evade both seed from the one dexterity word at +0x3e: writing an evade base read at +0x40 because the other stats are consecutive would read the unit's current HP instead.

=== 00024e98 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] (6-byte nop) + mov edx,edx (2-byte nop), aligning next function to 16 bytes.

=== 00024ea0 [PLATE]
Draws one unit's eight-slot inventory list into an 8bpp surface: the selection bar on the highlighted row, then, for every filled slot, the item's category icon, its name and its headline number.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index). When selected_slot is 0..7 it blits sprite 0 of the SelBar.cel sheet held in DAT_000643c0 through fdps_cel_blit_sprite at x=0, y=selected_slot*0x11+8, so the highlight sits under the row drawn next; any other value leaves the list unhighlighted.
Then for each slot i of 0..7 it reads the slot pair at unit record offset 0xa+2*i: the flag byte at +0xa and the item id at +0xb. Flag bit 0x80 marks the slot empty and skips it; bit 0x40 marks the item equipped.
For a filled slot it fetches the item record with fdps_get_item_record(item_id) and picks the category icon from the record's type byte at +0x00: type 1..0x15 (weapons) gives 0x1d, type 0x16..0x27 (armour) gives 0x1e, everything else -- type 0 included -- gives 0x1f; an equipped item adds 4, giving 0x21/0x22/0x23. fdps_blit_command_sprite draws that Command.cel sprite at x=3, y=i*0x11+9.
The item name is message 0xc9+item_id out of the message table in DAT_000643c4, rendered by fdps_draw_text at x=0x13, y=i*0x11+8 with glyph arguments 0xd0, 0, 0x6d.
The right-hand column, at x=0x66, y=i*0x11+0xd, is one more Command.cel caption sprite plus a four-digit number drawn 0x16 pixels further right by fdps_draw_number: type 1..0x15 gives caption 0x40 with the record's ap (i16 at +0x01); type 0x27 or below -- which here also catches type 0 -- gives caption 0x41 with dp (i16 at +0x05); otherwise the use_effect byte at +0x0d decides, 0x0b (restore HP) giving caption 0x3e with use_amount (i16 at +0x0e), 0x0c (restore MP) giving caption 0x3f with the same field, and every other item giving caption 0x43 on its own with no number.
Rows are 0x11 = 17 pixels apart, and every coordinate is folded into the destination pointer as dest_base + y*pitch + x, so the routine never touches a surface descriptor.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, handed straight to fdps_get_unit_record; the callers pass on the unit they were opened for.
  selected_slot -- which inventory row carries the selection bar, 0..7; anything outside that range draws no bar. fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window passes -1, fdps_unit_item_select_window and fdps_unit_equip_window pass 0, fdps_unit_item_select_loop passes its live cursor position.
  dest_base -- base of the 8bpp destination surface. All four callers pass their 320x200 window buffer + 0x3b58, i.e. the list starts at pixel (0x98, 0x2f).
  pitch -- bytes per destination row; all four callers pass 0x140 (320).

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls and is called only by game code, and reads the game's own resource globals]

Rebuild note:
The item type byte is classified twice with two different tests, and type 0 falls in a different bucket each time: the icon test sends type 0 to the catch-all icon 0x1f, while the caption test lets it fall into the armour branch and print caption 0x41 with dp. A rewrite that computes the category once and reuses it changes what a slot holding an id past the end of Item.dat draws (the 0xFF bug item, or 0xE2..0xFA whose records are all zero) -- the original shows the plain item icon beside a DP figure. Keep the two tests apart. In the same vein only use_effect 0x0b and 0x0c print a recovery amount: 0x20, which also restores HP, falls through to caption 0x43 and no number.

Alignment padding: 3-byte NOP form 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning next function to 0x25140.

=== 00025140 [PLATE]
Finds which of a unit's eight inventory slots holds the weapon, or the armor, that the unit currently has equipped.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) to resolve the 0x50-byte record, then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries that start at record offset 0x0a, i from 0 to 7. For each entry it forms record + 0x0a + i*2 and tests bit 0x40 of that flag byte, the equipped bit -- the same bit FUN_00026070 writes when it equips a slot and FUN_00024ea0 reads to pick the equipped icon variant; a slot without it is skipped. For an equipped slot it passes the entry's second byte, the item id fdps_unit_get_item_id returns, to fdps_get_item_record and reads the record's first byte, the ITEM.DAT type field. When want_armor is 0 the slot matches if that type lies in 1..0x15, the whole weapon span of the type field; otherwise it matches if the type lies in 0x16..0x27, the armor span. The index of the first matching slot is returned immediately. Falling out of the loop after all eight entries returns -1. Neither argument is range-checked and no byte of the record is written.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the same index fdps_get_unit_record takes; the unit whose equipment is being looked up.
  want_armor -- which piece of equipment to look for: 0 for the equipped weapon (item type 1..0x15), non-zero for the equipped armor (item type 0x16..0x27). Every caller but the shop loop passes a literal 0; FUN_00033b80 passes 1 when the shop item under the cursor has a type above 0x15.

Returns:
The inventory slot index, 0..7, of the first equipped item of the requested kind, or -1 when the unit has no such item equipped. Callers feed the index back to fdps_unit_get_item_id or to the shop's trade-in price, and treat -1 as "nothing equipped".

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_get_item_record, and all nine references are direct calls from game code; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The weapon test rejects item type 0 as well as everything above 0x15, so it is `type != 0 && type <= 0x15`, not `type <= 0x15`. Writing the obvious single-sided comparison would make an equipped slot whose item record reads back type 0 -- the all-zero tail records of ITEM.DAT past id 0xe1, which a bad item id resolves to -- count as an equipped weapon, and the caller would then charge a trade-in price for, or attack with, a blank item.

Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning FUN_00025200 to 16 bytes.

=== 00025200 [PLATE]
Returns the item id held in one inventory slot of a unit.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) to resolve the 0x50-byte unit record in the array based at DAT_00069cd8, then returns the unsigned byte at record + slot*2 + 0x0b. The unit's inventory is eight 2-byte entries starting at record offset 0x0a: byte 0 of an entry is its flag byte (bit 7 set means the slot holds nothing, bit 6 means the item is equipped -- see fdps_unit_item_count and fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot) and byte 1, the byte this function returns, is the item id that fdps_get_item_record indexes with. Neither the unit index nor the slot is range-checked.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; the same index the callers use with fdps_get_unit_record.
  slot -- inventory slot, 0..7; usually the slot fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot found or a loop counter bounded by the count fdps_unit_item_count returns.

Returns:
The slot's item id, zero-extended to 32 bits. The value is meaningful only when the slot's flag byte says it is occupied; the caller is expected to have established that.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; its only callee is the game routine fdps_get_unit_record and all 14 references are direct calls from game code]

Rebuild note:
The slot index is not validated, and fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit at 0001c5d4 passes the result of fdps_unit_find_equipped_slot straight in without testing it for -1, so a unit with no equipped weapon reads record+0x09 -- one byte before the inventory -- and hands that to fdps_get_item_record. Writing the obvious C here, a bounds check on slot or an early return of 0/-1, changes what that path does. Keep the read unguarded.
