=== 00025240 [PLATE]
Returns how many of a unit's eight inventory slots are holding an item.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) to resolve the 0x50-byte unit record in the array based at DAT_00069cd8, then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries that start at record offset 0x0a, i from 0 to 7. For each entry it forms the address record + i*2 + 0x0a and tests bit 7 of that flag byte; bit 7 set means the slot holds nothing (the item id itself is the second byte of the entry, which fdps_unit_get_item_id returns), so every entry whose bit 7 is clear adds one to the running total. All eight entries are examined -- the scan does not stop at the first empty slot -- and neither the unit index nor the returned record pointer is checked.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, 0-based; the same index the callers use with fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_unit_get_item_id. It is a battle unit index on the battle side (fdps_battle_action_menu, fdps_map_actor_score_best_item) and a party member index on the village/shop side, where fdps_chapter_26_end and fdps_chapter_15_post_action pass the constants 0 and 4.

Returns:
The number of occupied inventory slots, 0 to 8. 0 means the unit is carrying nothing, which is how fdps_village_item_sell_loop and fdps_village_item_transfer_loop refuse a sale or a transfer; 8 means the inventory is full, which is how fdps_shop_buy_loop, fdps_village_item_transfer_loop, fdps_chapter_22_event_boss_defeat, fdps_chapter_23_event_give_martial_artist_ring, fdps_chapter_25_event_marian_buys_wind_god_bow, fdps_chapter_15_post_action and fdps_chapter_26_end refuse to hand the unit another item. fdps_unit_find_item_slot uses it as the bound of a 0..count-1 sweep over fdps_unit_get_item_id.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its sole callee is the game routine fdps_get_unit_record and every call site is game code, including fdps_battle_action_menu]

=== 000252af [EOL]

=== 000252b0 [PLATE]
Runs the item command of the battle action menu for one unit: a four-entry ring menu that uses, hands over, equips or discards the items in that unit's bag.

Algorithm:
Copies the four-entry icon template at 0x00024d50 and the matching disabled-flag template at 0x00024d60 onto the stack and sets the result accumulator to -1; both copies happen once, outside the loop. Then it loops:
  - fdps_unit_item_count(unit_index); when the bag is empty it returns the accumulator.
  - Probes for a neighbour with fdps_collect_targets_in_range over the cursor tile, followed by fdps_map_grid_reset. DAT_00069cd4 and DAT_00069ccc hold the map cursor's pixel x and y and are divided by the 0x18-pixel tile size everywhere they are read. When nothing is adjacent it marks entry 1 unselectable in the stack copy of the disabled-flag table.
  - fdps_menu_find_first_enabled_entry, fdps_menu_animate_open, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop, fdps_menu_animate_close, fdps_render_view_frame; then it saves the cursor pixel position for the branches below. A cancel (-1) returns the accumulator.
  - Entry 0, use: fdps_unit_item_select_window(unit_index, 1, &slot) picks a usable item and fdps_get_item_record turns the slot's item id into an Item.dat record. It publishes use_radius (record +0x12) + 2 in the cursor-footprint global DAT_00069cd0, sweeps the reachable targets with fdps_collect_targets_in_range at use_distance (+0x10), passing 1 in the minimum-distance slot only when use_effect (+0x0d) is 0x1c, and runs fdps_map_cursor_select_loop in the record's select_mode (+0x15). It then re-collects the units the effect actually covers: fdps_collect_targets_in_range at use_radius when use_distance is below 0x10, otherwise fdps_collect_targets_in_line along a line of use_distance - 0x10 tiles from the saved cursor tile. For use_effect 0x19 and 0x1c a second pick, fdps_map_cursor_select_loop mode 6, supplies a destination tile, written as tile coordinates to DAT_0006437c (x) and DAT_00064380 (y). On confirm it applies the effect through FUN_000262a0(unit_index, slot, target_count, target_ids), calls fdps_battle_mark_unit_done and returns 1; on cancel it puts the cursor back on the acting unit with fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit and reopens the item list.
  - Entry 1, hand over: picks any item, mallocs a 100-byte candidate buffer, collects the adjacent units, lets the player pick one with fdps_map_cursor_select_loop mode 3, identifies it with fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor, restores the cursor with fdps_map_cursor_move_to, frees the buffer and calls fdps_flush_keyboard_queue. fdps_unit_add_item puts the item in the recipient's first free slot; when the recipient's bag is full it opens fdps_unit_item_select_window on the recipient and trades the two items instead, removing and re-adding on both sides. Either way it runs fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats on every unit it touched and sets the accumulator to 2.
  - Entry 2, equip: fdps_unit_equip_window(unit_index) and nothing else.
  - Entry 3, discard: picks any item, fdps_unit_remove_item, fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats. The accumulator is left as it was.
DAT_00069cd0, the map cursor's overlay footprint, is set to 0 across every fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit call and put back to 1 afterwards, so the cursor does not paint while it snaps.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; fdps_battle_action_menu passes the unit whose action menu it is running.

Returns:
  1 when the unit used an item and its turn is over, 2 when an item changed hands, -1 when the player backed out with neither having happened. fdps_battle_action_menu reads 1 as "the command was carried out" and 2 as "count a later cancel of the whole action menu as an action anyway".

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in the image]

Rebuild note:
Only the hand-over branch sets the result to 2. Equipping (entry 2) and discarding (entry 3) leave it at -1, so backing out of the action menu after only equipping or throwing something away still leaves the unit free to move and attack, while doing so after a hand-over spends its turn. Writing the obvious "every branch that changed the bag returns 2" costs the unit its turn for an equip.

=== 000259c0 [PLATE]

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game asset string and game-only callees, with malloc/memmove/free used as an ordinary consumer]

Rebuild note:
The list backdrop has to be copied out of the window image before fdps_draw_unit_inventory paints the item rows into it. Writing it in the intuitive order -- draw the panel and the item list, then snapshot the rectangle you will erase with -- captures the rows and the slot-0 selection bar as part of the backdrop, and every redraw inside fdps_unit_item_select_loop then leaves the old highlight showing under the new one.

=== 00025b17 [EOL]

=== 00025b20 [PLATE]
Modal item-list cursor loop of the unit status window: lets the player move a highlight over one unit's eight inventory slots and either confirm a slot or back out.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and caches the unit's sprite cache slot, the byte at record+2. Counts the slots in use once, before the loop, applying the same test fdps_unit_item_count applies: for i = 0..7 the flag byte at record[0xa + 2*i] with bit 0x80 clear means that slot holds an item. That count is the cursor's wrap point and is never recomputed, so the loop assumes the inventory does not change under it.
Each iteration does three things in order. fdps_blit_rect copies the untouched 0x97 x 0x95 list panel out of list_backdrop over window_image + 0x3b58 (pitch 0x140, i.e. row 47, column 152 of the 320x200 window) to erase the previous highlight. The routine at 0x00024ea0 then redraws the eight item rows into the same place, putting the selection bar on the row named by *selected_slot (rows are 0x11 pixels tall). Finally fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input(window_image, sprite cache slot, 0) presents the frame and blocks until it has one keyboard scancode.
The scancode is dispatched: 0x48 (up) plays Beep.wav and steps *selected_slot back, turning 0 into count-1; 0x50 (down) plays Beep.wav and steps it forward, turning count-1 into 0. 0x1c (Enter) and 0x39 (Space) confirm -- with usable_only zero the routine returns 1 immediately, otherwise it reads the item id at record[0xb + 2 * *selected_slot], looks the record up with fdps_get_item_record and returns 1 only when the ITEM.DAT use_effect byte at +0x0d is non-zero; an item that cannot be used is refused silently, with no sound and no message, and the loop starts over. 0x01 (Esc) and 0x53 (Del) return -1. Every other scancode falls through and repaints.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the 0x50-byte record in the unit array based at DAT_00069cd8; the unit whose inventory is on show. Callers pass the same index they opened the status window with.
  usable_only -- 0 lets confirm accept any slot; non-zero lets it accept only an item whose use_effect is non-zero. Only the battle "use item" path (0x000252b0, through 0x000259c0) passes 1; the equipment screen, the shop sell loop, the item-transfer loop and the script handlers all pass 0.
  window_image -- base of the 320x200 status window image being shown; the item list occupies the rectangle at +0x3b58. Handed on unchanged to fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input.
  list_backdrop -- 0x57e3-byte copy (0x97 x 0x95, stride 0x97) of that list rectangle as it looks with no highlight on it, blitted back over the list at the top of every iteration. 0x00025da0 allocates it with malloc(0x57e3) and fills it with the reverse fdps_blit_rect.
  selected_slot -- in and out: the inventory slot the highlight sits on, 0..count-1. The caller seeds it and reads it back afterwards to learn which item was picked.

Returns:
  1 -- the player confirmed; the chosen slot is in *selected_slot.
  -1 -- the player cancelled; *selected_slot is left wherever the cursor had got to.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; every caller and callee is game code and the only string is the asset name "Beep.wav"]

Rebuild note:
The cursor wraps by comparing against count-1, not by taking a remainder, and 0x00025da0 enters this loop without first checking that the unit carries anything -- so count can be 0. Writing the wrap the obvious way, *selected_slot = (*selected_slot + 1) % count, divides by zero on the equipment screen for a unit with an empty bag; the original simply lets the index walk out of 0..7, draws no highlight for it and does no harm, because 0x00025da0 tests fdps_unit_item_count after the loop returns.

=== 00025cb9 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0x0] + nop, 7 bytes to align next entry at 00025cc0

=== 00025cc0 [PLATE]
Removes one item from a unit's eight-slot inventory, closing the gap so the items that are left stay packed at the front.

Algorithm:
Resolves the record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index). The inventory is eight 2-byte slots starting at record+0x0a: byte 0 of a slot is a flag whose bit 0x80 means "slot empty", byte 1 is the item id -- the layout fdps_unit_add_item fills and fdps_unit_get_item_id reads. memmove then copies the (7 - slot) slots above the removed one down by one slot, from record+0x0c+slot*2 to record+0x0a+slot*2, so slots slot+1..7 become slots slot..6. Finally it stores 0x80 into the flag byte of the last slot at record+0x18, marking it empty. Only that single byte is written: the item id byte at record+0x19 keeps whatever the shift left there. Nothing bounds-checks slot -- slot 7 makes the move zero-length, and anything above 7 hands memmove a negative, therefore huge unsigned, byte count.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array whose base is at 0x00069cd8; callers pass the same index they hand to fdps_unit_item_count and fdps_unit_get_item_id.
  slot -- which inventory slot to drop, 0..7; the shop sell loop at 00034000 and the item transfer loop at 00034210 pass the slot the player just selected and read back with fdps_unit_get_item_id.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX still holds the unit record pointer at the RET, and no caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and edits the returned game record; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The empty marker is written as a single byte -- record[0x18] = 0x80 -- so the item id byte at record+0x19 is left holding the value the memmove shifted into it. Writing the obvious `slots[7] = 0x0080` or clearing the whole 2-byte slot zeroes that id byte, and since fdps_unit_get_item_id returns the id byte without checking the empty flag, any consumer that reads slot 7 unguarded would then get 0 instead of the original's stale id. Keep the store one byte wide.

=== 00025d14 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs aligning FUN_00025d20 to 32 bytes.

=== 00025d20 [PLATE]
Adds one item to a unit's inventory, filling the first empty slot.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) to resolve the 0x50-byte unit record in the array based at DAT_00069cd8, then walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries that start at record offset 0x0a, i from 0 to 7. For each entry it forms the address record + i*2 + 0x0a and tests bit 7 of that flag byte; bit 7 set means the slot holds nothing, the same test fdps_unit_item_count uses. At the first such entry it stores 0 over the whole flag byte -- clearing bit 7 so the slot counts as occupied and bit 6 so the item is not marked equipped -- writes item_id into the entry's second byte, the byte fdps_unit_get_item_id returns, and returns 1. If all eight entries are occupied the loop runs out and it returns -1 without touching the record. Neither the unit index nor the item id is range-checked, and the slot is taken as found: nothing is shifted or compacted (removal is the side that compacts, in fdps_unit_remove_item).

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the same index fdps_get_unit_record takes; the unit that is to receive the item.
  item_id -- item id to store, 0..0xff; only the low byte of the pushed argument is read. Comes from a shop line (fdps_shop_buy_loop), another unit's inventory slot (fdps_village_item_transfer_loop), a map cell's contents (fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor) or a script record's operand (fdps_run_death_scripts).

Returns:
1 when the item was stored, -1 when all eight inventory slots were already full. fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor and fdps_run_death_scripts branch on -1 to withhold the reward or to offer the player a replacement; the other callers ignore the result.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only callee is the game routine fdps_get_unit_record and its references are 27 direct calls from 21 distinct functions in game code]

Rebuild note:
Filling a slot means writing 0 over the entry's flag byte, not just storing the id: the obvious C, record[0x0a + i*2 + 1] = item_id with the flag byte left alone, leaves bit 7 set, so fdps_unit_item_count keeps counting the slot as empty and the next add overwrites the item. Two more things a rewrite must copy verbatim: the empty test is flags & 0x80, not flags == 0x80, and the failure return is -1, not 0 -- fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor tests the result with CMP EAX,-1.

Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning FUN_00025da0 to 16 bytes.

=== 00025da0 [PLATE]
Unit equipment window: opens the status window on one unit's inventory and equips whatever the player picks, one item after another, until they back out.

Algorithm:
fdps_load_status_cel_image loads the 320x200 Status.cel window image. malloc(0xfa00) plus memmove from 0xa0000 saves the visible mode 13h screen so fdps_close_status_window can put it back afterwards. Two more buffers take pristine copies of the two rectangles that get repainted later: malloc(0x57e3) for the item list (0x97 x 0x95 = 151 x 149 pixels at window_image + 0x3b58, i.e. row 47, column 152 of the 320x200 image) and malloc(0x2981) for the stats block (0x7d x 0x55 = 125 x 85 at window_image + 0x8ad3, row 111, column 19, the area holding the HP and MP gauges and the stat figures). fdps_blit_rect copies both out of the image while it is still unpainted. Only then does it paint: fdps_draw_unit_status_panel(unit_index, window_image) fills in the stats side and fdps_draw_unit_inventory(unit_index, 0, window_image + 0x3b58, 0x140) draws the eight item rows with the selection bar on row 0. "OpWin1.wav" plays through fdps_play_sfx, and fdps_draw_status_window_anim_frame(saved_screen, window_image, step) runs for step = 0..8, the nine-frame slide-in of the window over the saved screen.

The rest is one loop. fdps_unit_item_select_loop(unit_index, 0, window_image, list_backdrop, &selected_slot) runs the modal cursor loop over the eight inventory slots; the usable_only argument is the literal 0, so confirm accepts any occupied slot. fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) then resolves the record and the item id byte at record + 0xb + 2 * selected_slot is read, whichever way the loop ended. The loop stops when the select loop returned -1 (the player cancelled) or when fdps_unit_item_count(unit_index) is 0 -- that count test is the only way out for a unit carrying nothing. Otherwise fdps_unit_can_equip_item(unit_index, item_id) decides. When the unit's class may not wear that item, nothing at all happens -- no sound, no message -- and the select loop is entered again. When it may, "Equip.wav" plays, fdps_unit_equip_slot(unit_index, selected_slot) puts the item on in place of whatever was worn in the same category, fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats(unit_index) refreshes the derived stats, fdps_blit_rect copies the stats backdrop back over window_image + 0x8ad3 to erase the old figures, and fdps_draw_unit_status_panel redraws them. The item list is not repainted here; fdps_unit_item_select_loop redraws it from list_backdrop at the top of every one of its own passes.

On the way out fdps_close_status_window(window_image, saved_screen) takes the window away and puts the screen back, and the four buffers are freed in the order window image, list backdrop, stats backdrop, saved screen.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the 0x50-byte record in the unit array based at DAT_00069cd8; the unit whose equipment is being changed. Handed on unchanged to every callee that takes a unit index. fdps_village_member_equip_loop passes the party member the player picked, fdps_battle_item_menu passes the unit whose battle turn it is.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_load_status_cel_image / fdps_draw_unit_status_panel / fdps_get_unit_record / fdps_play_sfx and the game's own "OpWin1.wav" and "Equip.wav" strings, using malloc/memmove/free only as services; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
Both backdrops have to be copied out of the window image before fdps_draw_unit_status_panel and fdps_draw_unit_inventory paint into it. Allocating and snapshotting after the drawing -- the intuitive order -- captures the item rows and the stat figures as part of the backdrops, and every later erase then leaves the old highlight, and the old digits, showing under the new ones. The empty-bag path is load-bearing too: the window opens and plays its slide-in even for a unit carrying nothing, and the fdps_unit_item_count test that closes it runs only after fdps_unit_item_select_loop has returned, so an early "nothing to equip" guard would change what the player sees.

=== 00025fe0 [PLATE]
Reports whether one unit's class is allowed to equip a given item.

Algorithm:

=== 00026070 [PLATE]
Equips the item held in one of a unit's eight inventory slots, unequipping whatever the unit already wore in the same category.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit record twice through fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) -- both calls return the same 0x50-byte record out of the array based at DAT_00069cd8 -- and reads the item id of the slot being equipped from record + slot*2 + 0x0b. fdps_get_item_record turns that id into an ITEM.DAT record and its byte at +0 is the item's type code. Then it walks the eight 2-byte inventory entries that start at record offset 0x0a, i from 0 to 7. An entry whose flag byte has bit 0x40 clear is skipped, so only entries currently equipped are considered. For an equipped entry it looks its item id up with fdps_get_item_record too and compares the two type codes against the threshold 0x15: type codes 0x01-0x15 are the weapon kinds and 0x16 upward are armour and the non-weapon items, so the two items are in the same category exactly when both are <= 0x15 or both are > 0x15. In that case the entry's whole flag byte is stored back as 0, taking the equipped bit off it (bit 7, the slot-is-empty bit, is already clear on an occupied slot). An equipped entry whose item record type byte is 0 -- which no real item has -- is left alone. Finally it stores 0x40 into the flag byte at record + slot*2 + 0x0a unconditionally, marking that slot equipped. Nothing is range-checked and nothing verifies that the slot is occupied or that the unit's class may wear the item; fdps_unit_can_equip_item is the check the status screen runs first.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8, the same index fdps_get_unit_record takes.
  slot -- inventory slot to equip, 0..7. fdps_unit_equip_window passes the slot under the menu cursor; fdps_shop_buy_loop passes fdps_unit_item_count(unit_index) - 1, the slot fdps_unit_add_item has just filled.

Returns:
Nothing. Both callers discard EAX.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_get_item_record; no Function ID hit in the Watcom or Miles sets, and its call site plays s_Equip.wav]

Rebuild note:
Only one item per broad category may be worn, and the category test is the coarse split at item type 0x15 (weapons 0x01-0x15, armour and the rest 0x16 up) -- not equality of the type byte and not the class's PROEQU.DAT equip list. Writing the obvious 'unequip the other slot holding an item of the same type' gives the wrong answer: equipping a 刀 (type 0x02) must unequip an already equipped 劍 (type 0x01), and equipping any armour must unequip any other armour whatever its sub-kind.

=== 00026174 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte LEA NOP forms filling to the 16-byte-aligned entry at 00026180.

=== 00026180 [PLATE]
Collects the death-script record of every battle unit the action just carried out has reduced to zero HP, so the caller can pay out and fire those scripts once the death sequence has played.

Algorithm:
Walks unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 (the unit count of the map currently in play), resolving each record with fdps_get_unit_record. A unit contributes when all three tests pass: bit 0 of the flag byte at record+0x05 is clear, i.e. the unit has not already been taken off the map (the same bit fdps_unit_is_retired returns and fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead sets); the opcode byte at record+0x31 is not 0xff, the "no script" sentinel; and the signed hit-point word at record+0x40 is <= 0 (CMP word ptr [EAX + 0x40],0x0 / JLE to the copy block at 000261e9). For each qualifying unit it memmoves the 3 bytes at record+0x31 -- an opcode byte followed by a signed 16-bit operand -- to out_scripts + 3*n, then bumps n. n is returned.

Where the record comes from: fdps_deploy_unit fills record+0x31 and +0x32 from bytes +0x16 and +0x17 of the map%02d.dat deployment record, so only the map's scripted units carry a script, while fdps_build_map_unit_array stamps 0xff into +0x31 of every player-roster slot it lays out, which is why the party never pays a reward for its own losses.

What the records mean is settled by the consumer, fdps_run_death_scripts, which the same callers hand this array to: opcode 0 gives the operand to the acting unit as an item, 1 adds it to the party gold at DAT_000643a4, 2 calls slot operand of the chapter-event handler table at 000601c4, and 3 or above paints line operand of the chapter text table, with 4 additionally setting the battle-end code DAT_00069da0 to 2 (chapter cleared) and 5 setting it to 1 (defeat). All four callers -- fdps_battle_action_menu, fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets and fdps_battle_spell_command -- use the same three-step idiom: this function into a stack buffer, then fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead to play the destruction sequence and retire the dead units, then fdps_run_death_scripts to run the collected records against the acting unit. The sibling fdps_collect_death_script_events reads the same field under the same retired and hit-point tests but accepts only opcodes 2..5, so the map-AI path that reaches it hands out no item or gold rewards.

Nothing bounds the write: the loop can emit one record per unit on the map, while the tightest caller, fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, has only 0x0c bytes -- four records -- between its buffer at EBP-0x18 and its next live local.

Parameters:
  out_scripts -- caller-supplied array that receives the collected records, three bytes each, packed from the front with no gaps. Every caller passes the address of a local stack buffer; the buffer's capacity is never communicated to this function.

Returns:
  int -- how many 3-byte records were written; 0 when no unit qualifies. The callers pass it straight to fdps_run_death_scripts as its record count, and that function does nothing at all when it is 0.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and reads the game's unit-count global DAT_00060150; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the AIL set]

Rebuild note:
The collect must run before fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, not after: that function stores 1 into record+0x05 for every unit at zero HP, which sets the retired bit this function's first test rejects, so reordering the two -- play the death animation, then hand out the rewards, which reads as the natural order -- silently returns 0 and every item, gold and scripted chapter event owed for those kills is lost. All four callers already have it in the right order. Second, the routine writes one 3-byte record per qualifying unit with no capacity check at all, and the caller buffers are sized by nothing but the original's frame layout -- fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack leaves it four records -- so a rebuild must keep each caller's buffer at least as large as the original's rather than trust this routine to stop, and must not add the bound check that obviously belongs here.

=== 00026225 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx, aligning FUN_00026230 to 16 bytes.

=== 00026230 [PLATE]
Applies one damaging item or spell effect to a list of battle-map targets: damages each target, floats the damage number over it, then plays all of those numbers out at once over the unit shake animation.

Algorithm:
Loops i from 0 to target_count-1. For each i it zero-extends target_ids[i] to a unit index and calls FUN_00028460(unit_index, base_damage), which rolls base_damage*9/10 + (rand()%100)*base_damage/1000, subtracts that from the unit record's current HP (word +0x40, clamped at zero) and returns the rolled amount. The returned amount goes straight into FUN_0001f510(amount, 0, unit_index), which queues a four-cell floating number over that unit in the popup tables at 00064120 / 000641e8 / 000642b0 and advances the queue counter at 00064378; the glyph base 0 selects the damage digit sprites, where the healing path at FUN_00026fd0 passes 0x27 for its own digit set. After the loop it calls FUN_0001f340 once, which plays the 22-frame unit shake with the queued numbers riding over it and clears the queue counter at the end -- so every target's number appears together, after all the damage has already been applied. FUN_0001f340 is gated on that counter being non-zero, so a target_count of 0 leaves the screen alone.

Parameters:
  target_count -- how many entries of target_ids to hit; the size of the area-of-effect target list FUN_000262a0 was given.
  target_ids -- array of target_count bytes, each a unit index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8.
  base_damage -- the effect's power before the damage roll; FUN_000262a0 reads it from the signed word at offset 0x0e of the item record of the item or spell being used.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image, and every callee is unit-record game code]

Rebuild note:
The number floated over each target is the rolled damage FUN_00028460 returns, not the HP actually removed: a unit on 3 HP hit for 20 has its HP clamped to 0 but still shows 20. Recomputing the popup value as (HP before - HP after), which is the obvious way to write it, changes what the player sees on every overkill.

=== 0002629c [EOL]

=== 000262a0 [PLATE]
Applies the effect of one item out of a unit's inventory to a list of battle-map targets, and settles the deaths that effect causes.

Algorithm:
Clears the floating-indicator queue count at data_fdps_indicator_queue_count, reads the acting unit's record through fdps_get_unit_record, and takes the item id from the inventory entry at record + 0xb + 2 * item_slot. fdps_get_item_record turns that id into an ITEM.DAT record, from which it reads use_effect (byte at +0x0d) and use_amount (signed word at +0x0e), then dispatches on use_effect:

  0x01/0x07, 0x02/0x08, 0x03/0x09 -- plays EMg00.saf, EMg05.saf or EMg08.saf over the targets with fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units, then fdps_apply_damage_to_targets with use_amount.
  0x04/0x0a -- loads EarQu.wav out of MISC.VFS with fdps_vfs_load_entry, starts it with fdps_audio_start_wav, shakes the view over 25 fdps_render_view_frame passes by offsetting the scroll globals data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_x and data_fdps_battle_view_window_origin_y by rand() % 4 - 2 each frame, restores both globals, then fdps_apply_damage_to_targets.
  0x0b/0x20 -- fdps_apply_heal_to_targets with use_amount.
  0x0c -- CureMP.saf over the targets and a fdps_flash_units_in_color flash in colour 0xff, then for every target either fdps_show_miss_indicator when its maximum MP (record +0x46) is 0, or fdps_unit_restore_mp followed by the restored figure floated over it.
  0x0f, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14 -- the permanent stat-up items, all under Cure.saf and all applied to target_ids[0] only: +15 maximum HP (+0x42), +15 maximum MP (+0x46), +7 AP (+0x37), +7 DP (+0x39), +7 DX (+0x3e), +1 MV (+0x3b). The three that move a combat stat follow with fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats. Every amount is a constant here, not use_amount.
  0x16, 0x18 -- clears the poison byte (+0x25) or the paralysis byte (+0x26) of target_ids[0], queueing the cured popup through fdps_show_cure_indicator first when the byte was set, then Cure.saf and a 0xff flash over the targets.
  0x1e -- damages every target directly through fdps_unit_apply_damage with use_amount and floats the figure over it, with no effect animation and without consuming the item. The loop calls fdps_get_unit_record at 00026a96 and stores the pointer to [EBP-0x20] without ever reading it, so this branch works purely through unit indices and that call is a dead store -od keeps.
  0x21 -- 蓋亞's 強化套件: opens the message window on the target's form id (record +0x07), and when that id is 9 draws text 0x21e, adds +30 AP, +30 DP and +1 MV, grants the 轟神砲 spell with fdps_set_flag_bit bit 0x1d, and recomputes the combat stats; any other form id gets the refusal text 0x21d.
  0x22 -- the other 強化套件: the same shape, text 0x21f and +100 maximum HP when the form id is 9.
  0x23 -- 布蘭多's 高能量裝置: opens the message window on the target's original character id (record +0x08) and acts only when that id is 8. With no 金屬礦 (item 0xa3) in the target's bag it draws text 0x220; otherwise text 0x221, then it removes the device, looks the 金屬礦 slot up a second time, removes that too and hands over the 高能量砲 (item 0xbe). That first fdps_unit_remove_item removes from the TARGET unit's bag using the ACTING unit's item_slot -- 00026d56 pushes [EBP+0x18], then target_ids[0] -- and not from the actor's bag; the two coincide only because the shipped path has 布蘭多 use the device on himself.

Each consumable branch calls fdps_unit_remove_item on the acting unit's slot; the weapon-borne codes paired with them -- 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x20 and 0x1e -- leave the item alone. use_effect values 0x05, 0x06, 0x0d and 0x1b reach no branch at all, so the items carrying them do nothing when used. All the message text goes through fdps_draw_text against the text block pointer in data_fdps_all_game_text_ptr, between fdps_message_window_open and fdps_message_window_close.

Finally it clears data_fdps_battle_pending_xp_credit, collects the death scripts of everything the effect killed into a stack buffer with fdps_collect_death_scripts, plays those deaths out with fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, and runs the scripts with fdps_run_death_scripts so the acting unit collects the rewards.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit using the item, into the 0x50-byte unit array whose base is at data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr. Both callers pass the unit whose turn it is.
  item_slot -- which of that unit's eight inventory slots holds the item. fdps_battle_item_menu gets it from fdps_unit_item_select_window, fdps_map_actor_use_item from the slot the map AI picked.
  target_count -- how many entries target_ids holds; the callers get it from fdps_collect_targets_in_range or fdps_collect_targets_in_line.
  target_ids -- array of target unit indices, one byte each. Several branches only ever touch target_ids[0].

Returns:
  Nothing. Both callers ignore EAX.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit; game unit records, ITEM.DAT records, view globals and named .saf/.wav resources]

Rebuild note:
The 0x23 branch deliberately looks the 金屬礦 slot up a second time after fdps_unit_remove_item has already removed the device: removing an item compacts the eight-slot inventory, so reusing the index from the first fdps_unit_find_item_slot would delete the wrong item. The permanent stat-up amounts (15, 15, 7, 7, 7, 1, 30/30/1, 100) are constants in this function and not the item's use_amount, which is 0 for every one of those items, so the obvious `stat += use_amount` silently does nothing. Effects 0x21/0x22 test the current form id at unit record +0x07 while 0x23 tests the original character id at +0x08; unifying them onto +0x07 would break the 高能量砲 trade for a 布蘭多 who has already class-changed, and onto +0x08 would change which portrait the message window shows. The earthquake jitter is rand() % 4 - 2, i.e. -2..+1, not a symmetric shake.

=== 00026dfb [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + mov ecx,ecx, aligning to 00026e00

=== 00026e00 [PLATE]
Plays one named MISC.VFS animation over a list of battle-map units, drawing a copy of the animation on each listed unit's map cell over the live scrolling scene and presenting it in the game's framed 312x192 main view.

Algorithm:
malloc(0x15180) takes a 360x240 8bpp page -- wider and taller than the presented window, so a frame may overhang it without being clipped. That page becomes field +0x00 of the 0x24-byte composite-sprite draw request built on the stack; the request's pitch (+0x04) is 0x168 (360), its height (+0x08) 0xf0 (240), and its blit parameter block (+0x1c) and blit mode (+0x20) are both 0. fdps_vfs_load_entry("MISC.VFS", anim_name) loads the animation into a fresh buffer, which becomes the request's SAF base at +0x14, and fdps_saf_frame_count gives the frame total.

Each frame index from 0 to that total minus 1 is played for exactly two timer ticks; the dwell field the SAF frame record carries is not consulted, unlike fdps_saf_play_over_scene. On every one of those ticks:
  - fdps_draw_scene_layers repaints the scrolling layer table into the page from scratch;
  - the request's frame index (+0x18) takes the current frame number;
  - for each i from 0 to unit_count - 1, fdps_get_unit_record(unit_ids[i]) resolves the unit's 0x50-byte record and the request origin is set from its tile position and the camera: x (+0x0c) = record[0] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce4 - 0x18, y (+0x10) = record[1] * 0x18 - DAT_00069ce0 - 0x1e, where record[0] and record[1] are the unit's tile column and row, 0x18 is the 24-pixel tile size, and DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0 are the view origin in map pixels. fdps_draw_composite_sprite then draws the frame there. Its sound flag is 1 only when i == 0 and this is the first of the frame's two ticks, and 0 otherwise, so a frame that carries a sound effect fires it once per animation frame instead of once per unit per tick. Nothing culls a unit that has scrolled outside the visible window;
  - the routine spins on port 0x3da until vertical retrace begins and again until it ends, then fdps_blit_rect copies the 0x138 x 0xc0 (312x192) window at page + 0x21d8 -- row 24, column 24 of the 360-wide page -- with source pitch 0x168 to 0xa0504, row 4 column 4 of the mode 13h framebuffer;
  - it then spins until the frame-tick global DAT_00069d64 differs from the value latched at the end of the previous tick, and latches the new value.

When the last frame has been played it frees the page and then the loaded animation.

Parameters:
  unit_count -- how many entries of unit_ids to draw the animation over. 1 from the poison and status-effect call sites, the effect's target count from the item and spell effect handlers.
  unit_ids -- array of unit_count unit indices into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; each element is zero-extended and passed to fdps_get_unit_record. Callers pass either their target-id list or the address of a single-byte local.
  anim_name -- name of the entry to play inside MISC.VFS, such as "Cure.saf", "CureMP.saf", "Posion.saf", "PosEff.saf" or "EMg00.saf". Handed straight to fdps_vfs_load_entry, which ends the program if the archive holds no entry of that name.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library; game callees and game globals]

Rebuild note:
The frame-tick value this routine spins against is a stack local that is never initialised, so the first tick of the animation compares against whatever the frame happened to hold and in practice skips its wait entirely. Giving that local an initialiser -- 0, or the current DAT_00069d64, either of which is the obvious thing to write -- adds a tick of delay to the start of every effect animation. Leave it uninitialised.

=== 00026fc9 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte NOP (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) plus 0x90, aligning next entry to 0x26fd0.

=== 00026fd0 [PLATE]
Applies one HP-restoring item effect to a list of battle-map targets, animation included: plays the effect animation over them, heals each one, floats the restored amount over it, then plays all of those numbers out at once over the unit shake animation.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units(target_count, target_ids, "Posion.saf") to play that MISC.VFS animation over the battle scene with the listed units drawn into every frame; the string literal sits at 00061b98 and is spelled "Posion", not "Poison". Then fdps_flash_units_in_color(target_count, target_ids, 0xff) flashes the same targets for eight frames -- that function shifts the 0xff left by 8 and hands it to fdps_blit_unit_sprite as the blit parameter, so the targets pulse in that colour while the scene keeps rendering.
Loops i from 0 to target_count-1. For each i it zero-extends target_ids[i] to a unit index and calls fdps_unit_apply_heal(unit_index, base_heal), which rolls base_heal*9/10 + (rand()%100)*base_heal/1000, adds it to the unit record's current HP (word +0x40) clamped at maximum HP (word +0x42), credits the experience earned for the heal into DAT_00069cec and returns the rolled amount. That amount goes straight into fdps_show_number_indicator(amount, 0x27, unit_index), which queues a four-cell floating number over that unit; the glyph base 0x27 selects the healing digit sprites of Number.cel, where fdps_apply_damage_to_targets passes 0 for the damage digits and the MP path passes 0x0d.
After the loop it calls fdps_play_indicator_queue once, which plays the 22-frame unit shake with the queued numbers riding over it and clears the queue cursor at DAT_00064378. fdps_play_indicator_queue's work is gated on that cursor being non-zero, so a target_count of 0 floats nothing -- but the two animations ahead of the loop still run in full.

Parameters:
  target_count -- how many entries of target_ids to heal; the size of the area-of-effect target list fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets was given. The loop guard is a SIGNED compare, so a count of zero or below is accepted and simply heals nothing, while both animations ahead of the loop still run in full.
  target_ids -- array of target_count bytes, each a unit index into the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8.
  base_heal -- the effect's power before the healing roll. fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets reads it from the signed word at offset 0x0e of the item record (use_amount) and reaches this function for use_effect 0x0b, the consumable HP restores B4 藥草 / B5 回復劑 / B6 再生藥 / C2 神聖之水, and for use_effect 0x20, the healing staves, spears and bows such as 1C 女神之杖 and 34 天使之杖. Both codes arrive here with identical arguments.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [feeds a game resource filename to a MISC.VFS loader, no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image]

Rebuild note:
The asset name really is the misspelled "Posion.saf", and this is the healing effect, so the spelling looks doubly wrong. Writing the obvious "Poison.saf" makes the MISC.VFS lookup miss the entry and the heal plays no animation. The same misspelled literal is emitted a second time at 0006155c for the map-AI callers, so it is written that way in more than one source module.

=== 00027067 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6-byte nop) + lea edx,[edx+0] (3-byte nop), aligning next function to 0x10

=== 00027070 [PLATE]
Applies one healing effect to a battle unit's HP and credits the battle experience earned for it.

Algorithm:
Resolves the 0x50-byte unit record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads its current HP (signed word +0x40) and maximum HP (signed word +0x42). Rolls the heal as amount*9/10 plus (rand()%100)*amount/1000, so a request of N restores between 0.900*N and 0.999*N. Adds the roll to current HP, clamps the total to maximum HP, and stores it back to +0x40. Then, when the record's portrait/character id byte +0x7 is below 0x3c -- the unit is a roster character rather than an EnemyDat entry -- it adds (effective level * 25 * HP actually restored) / maximum HP to the pending experience accumulator data_fdps_battle_pending_xp_credit, where the effective level is the unit's level byte +0x21 plus 30 for portrait ids 0x0f..0x21, the promoted character forms whose levels restart at 1. fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up is what later clamps data_fdps_battle_pending_xp_credit to 99 and awards it to the acting unit. The value handed back is the rolled heal, not the HP that was actually restored.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr; the callers pass the battle target's unit index.
  amount -- the requested heal. fdps_apply_heal_to_targets passes the item record's use_amount word (+0x0e) for the use_effect 0x0b consumables and 0x20 healing staves; fdps_spell_heal_unit and fdps_cast_spell_on_targets pass the power word (+0x00) of a spell record.

Returns:
  The heal that was rolled -- amount*9/10 + (rand()%100)*amount/1000 -- before the clamp against maximum HP. fdps_apply_heal_to_targets passes it straight to fdps_show_number_indicator as the number to float over the target.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and writes the game global data_fdps_battle_pending_xp_credit; no Function ID hit against the Watcom 10.0x libraries or ailv3.lib, and the only library callee is rand]

Rebuild note:
The return value is the heal that was rolled, not the HP actually restored, and fdps_apply_heal_to_targets prints it as the floating number over the target -- writing the obvious `return new_hp - old_hp` would make a near-full-HP target display a smaller number than the original does. Separately, the +30 effective-level bonus is tested here as portrait id 0x0f..0x21 while fdps_battle_spell_command tests portrait id > 8 for the same +30 (000280cf), so folding the two into one shared helper changes the experience awarded.

=== 0002717a [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0] before FUN_00027180.

=== 00027180 [PLATE]
Carries out the item action the map AI has just chosen for one battle-map actor: re-collects the target list for the chosen item, plays the map-side presentation of the hit, then applies the effect.

Algorithm:
The item comes out of the acting unit's own inventory. fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) gives the record, and the byte at record + 0xb + DAT_00063f7c * 2 is the item id of the slot the map-AI scorer at 00013040 picked; fdps_get_item_record turns that id into an ITEM.DAT record. The side filter comes from the item's use_target byte +0x11: with side_select non-zero (an NPC-side actor) it is passed on as written, with side_select 0 (an enemy-side actor) it is replaced by (use_target == 0), which mirrors the item's normal player-side sense onto the enemy side.
fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit puts the cursor on the actor, then the item's use_distance byte +0x10 chooses the shape. Below 0x10 it is an area item and the targets come from fdps_collect_targets_in_range(DAT_00063f98, DAT_00063f94, targets, use_radius +0x12, 0, side filter). At 0x10 and above it is a straight-line item and they come from fdps_collect_targets_in_line(DAT_00063f98, DAT_00063f94, targets, record +0 = actor tile x, record +1 = actor tile y, use_distance - 0x10, side filter). DAT_00063f98 and DAT_00063f94 are the x and y of the target tile the scorer chose; targets is a 32-byte stack array whose length neither collector checks.
fdps_map_grid_reset then wipes what the collector painted on the working grid, delay(200) holds, and the cursor overlay mode DAT_00069cd0 is set to use_radius + 2 -- the area-of-effect diamond fdps_draw_map_cursor draws at that mode.
  Area item: fdps_map_cursor_move_to(DAT_00063f98 * 0x18, DAT_00063f94 * 0x18) walks the cursor to the target tile carrying that diamond, and the routine drops straight to the effect. It leaves the cursor mode at use_radius + 2. Only fdps_map_actor_take_best_action clears it, at 00012e26, the shared exit both of its call sites (00012db0 via JMP 00012dca, and 00012e1e by fallthrough) reach. fdps_map_actor_behavior_step does not: its four stores of 0 into DAT_00069cd0 are at 000101ee, 00010239, 0001029e and 000103f1, every one of them on an earlier behaviour branch than the call at 000105fa, and the path from 000105ff to its single RET at 00010754 contains none. The mode is put back by whichever action runs next -- fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack at 00012e5c, fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent at 0001276d, fdps_unit_rest at 0001212e -- or by the phase loop, fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase at 0001298b and fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase at 00012b2c and 00012b55.
  Straight-line item: fdps_unit_face_target turns the actor toward targets[0], delay(200) holds, and the screen flashes white and fades back -- fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, i, i, i) applies the same bias to all three channels with i counting 0x40 down to 0 and delay(4) between steps, so 0x40 saturates the whole DAC to white and 0 restores it. Cursor mode becomes 6, the mode in which fdps_draw_map_cursor draws nothing and instead clears the marked byte of every grid cell the cursor crosses, so the sweep leaves the beam's path highlighted behind it. The far end of the beam is extrapolated from the actor's own tile -- the cursor globals DAT_00069cd4 (x) and DAT_00069ccc (y) divided by the 0x18 pixel tile size -- along the direction of the target tile, (use_distance - 0x10) times over, then clamped (see the rebuild note). DAT_0006015c is reset to 0x14 so the highlight blend ramp starts from a fixed phase, fdps_map_cursor_move_to sweeps the cursor out to that tile, cursor mode goes back to 0, eight calls to fdps_render_view_frame hold the trail on screen, fdps_map_grid_reset wipes it and the cursor returns to targets[0].
Finally fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets(unit_index, DAT_00063f7c, target count, targets) applies the item's effect to every unit collected, and DAT_00069cec -- the pending experience accumulator fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up hands to the acting unit -- is zeroed, so a map-AI actor is credited nothing for the action.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte record array at DAT_00069cd8; both callers, fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, pass the actor they are stepping.
  side_select -- which side the actor stands on, and with it how the item's use_target byte +0x11 is read: 0 for an enemy-side actor, reaching here from fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase, and 1 for an NPC-side actor, from fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase. Both callers pass their own second argument straight down.

Returns:
  0 on every path. Both callers discard it.

Pool: fdps  [no FID hit in either library set; game call graph and game globals]

Rebuild note:
The clamp on the extrapolated sweep tile reads its bounds from the wrong place. It takes signed words at +0 and +2 of layer 0's .MPL blob (the pointer at DAT_00069cb0), but an .MPL carries its dimensions at +7 and +9 and its first four bytes are the magic "MPL\0" -- so the bounds it actually gets are 0x504d = 20557 for x and 0x004c = 76 for y. On x the bound is 0x504d = 20557 and the extrapolated tile cannot exceed roughly 900 -- the longest beam in the shipped ITEM.DAT is 14 tiles (records 0x63 and 0xc7) and no shipped .MPL is larger than 64 by 64 (measured over the 68 .MPL members of FIELD1.VFS, width 13..64, height 9..64) -- so the x upper arm at 00027407 is unreachable and only the lower clamp to 0 ever fires on x. On y the bound is 0x004c = 76 and the extrapolated tile reaches 14 * (aim_y - actor_y), so the upper arm at 0002742f fires from six rows of aim difference down and pins the sweep at row 75. Either way a beam aimed right or down off the edge of a map sweeps the cursor past the edge, where cursor mode 6 marks grid cells of the following row. Clamping against the real map size -- the words at +0 and +2 of the working grid DAT_00060144, which is what fdps_collect_targets_in_line uses -- stops the sweep at the map edge and does not reproduce the original.

=== 000274df [EOL]
Single 0x90 NOP aligning FUN_000274e0 to a 16-byte boundary.

=== 000274e0 [PLATE]
Collects the event half of the death scripts carried by every battle unit the action just resolved has brought to 0 HP, so the caller can run them once the kill has been played out: the scripted chapter events and battle-end verdicts, but not the item and gold rewards.

Algorithm:
Walks unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 (the battle unit count), fetching each 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record. A unit contributes when all three tests pass: bit 0 of the flag byte at record+0x05 is clear -- not retired, the same bit fdps_unit_is_retired returns and fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead sets; the signed hit-point word at record+0x40 is <= 0; and the opcode byte at record+0x31 is between 2 and 5 inclusive, which also excludes the 0xff "no script" sentinel. For each accepted unit the three bytes at record+0x31 -- an opcode byte followed by a signed 16-bit operand, the same death-script record fdps_collect_death_scripts copies -- are memmoved to out_events + 3*count, and count is bumped. count is returned.

Why the opcode window is 2..5:
fdps_run_death_scripts, which the caller hands the collected array to, splits its opcodes in exactly this place. Opcodes 2 (call slot operand of the chapter-event handler table at 000601c4), 3 (paint scripted line operand of the chapter text table), and 4 / 5 (the same line plus the battle-end code at DAT_00069da0 set to 2 for cleared or 1 for defeat) run unconditionally. Opcodes 0 (item drop) and 1 (gold) first require the unit index that executor was given to be player-side (its record byte +6 == 2) and not retired, and on failure return from the whole executor rather than skipping the one record. The sole caller here, fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell, is the map AI casting a spell, and it passes DAT_00063f74 -- the melee target the physical-attack scorer picked, which on this path is left over from an earlier action -- as that unit index; immediately after the call it zeroes the pending-experience accumulator DAT_00069cec instead of awarding it. Both halves of the same policy: an AI spell kill pays the player nothing. Withholding the reward opcodes here rather than letting the executor reject them is what keeps that suppression from also truncating the list, since the executor's rejection is a return and would take opcodes 4 and 5 -- the battle-end verdicts -- down with it. The sibling fdps_collect_death_scripts keeps every opcode except 0xff, and each of its four callers hands the executor a unit that can satisfy the guard: the AI's melee path fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack passes that same DAT_00063f74, but there it is the live player-side unit the AI just struck, the one it also awards the accumulated experience to.

Parameters:
  out_events -- caller-supplied array that receives the collected 3-byte records back to back, packed from the front with no gaps; the only caller passes a 12-byte (four-record) stack buffer, and nothing here checks that bound.

Returns:
  The number of 3-byte records written to out_events; 0 when no defeated unit carries an event record. fdps_run_death_scripts does nothing at all when handed 0.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the AIL set; the loop bound is the game's unit-count global DAT_00060150, the per-unit fetch is fdps_get_unit_record, and its only caller is game code]

Rebuild note:
Three things a rebuild gets wrong by writing the obvious C. (1) The collect must run before fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, never after: that routine stores 1 into record+0x05 for every unit at zero HP, setting the retired bit this function's first test rejects, so the natural-reading order -- play the deaths, then settle what they owed -- silently returns 0 and every scripted chapter event and battle-end verdict owed for those kills is lost. The caller's order at 00013db1 / 00013dc1 is collect, repaint, then mark dead. (2) This and fdps_collect_death_scripts differ only in the +0x31 test, so folding them into one shared helper, or copying the sibling's "opcode != 0xff" condition here, makes this path hand out the item and gold rewards it deliberately drops -- and because fdps_run_death_scripts *returns* instead of skipping when a reward record's player-side guard fails, and the unit index this call site gives it is a stale melee target, letting one through also abandons every record behind it, including the opcodes that end the battle. (3) There is no capacity check: one 3-byte record is written per matching unit into a caller buffer that holds four, so the buffer must stay at least as large as the original's rather than the routine be trusted to stop.

=== 00027595 [EOL]
Watcom 16-byte alignment padding (lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov ebx,ebx)

=== 000275a0 [PLATE]
Restores magic points to one battle unit: adds a slightly randomised fraction of the requested amount to the unit's current MP, clamps the result to the unit's maximum MP, and hands back the amount it rolled rather than the amount it actually applied.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and zero-extends the record's two 16-bit MP fields, current MP at +0x44 and maximum MP at +0x46. Splits the restore in two: a fixed part, amount * 9 / 10, and a random part, (rand() % 100) * amount / 1000, so the total lands between 90% and just under 100% of amount. Adds both to current MP; if the sum exceeds maximum MP it is replaced by maximum MP. Re-reads the +0x44 field, subtracts it from the clamped result to get the gain actually applied, and stores that gain in a stack local it never reads again. Stores the clamped result back into the +0x44 field as a 16-bit word, then returns the fixed part plus the random part. Nothing else in the record is touched and no experience is credited, which is what separates it from its HP twin fdps_unit_apply_heal, whose roll formula is otherwise identical.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array reached through fdps_get_unit_record; no bounds check. fdps_battle_advance_turn passes the fixed indices 4 and 8 and its loop index over every unit holding item 0xb3; fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets passes a target id out of the target list it was given.
  amount -- nominal MP to restore, in MP points. fdps_battle_advance_turn passes the constant 15 at all three of its call sites; fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets passes the signed word at offset 0x0e of the item record, the item's use_amount.

Returns:
  The restore the routine rolled, amount * 9 / 10 + (rand() % 100) * amount / 1000. This is the value before the clamp against maximum MP, so it overstates the gain whenever the unit was already near full MP. All four call sites -- 0001e6bc, 0001e746 and 0001e7d7 in fdps_battle_advance_turn, 00026a1b in fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets -- store the return value and pass it straight to fdps_show_number_indicator with glyph base 0xd, so the rolled value is exactly the number the player sees float over the unit; the CALL 0x0001f510 instructions that consume it are at 0001e6d9, 0001e763, 0001e7f8 and 00026a3a. The three turn-based sites refuse to call at all when current MP already equals maximum MP; the item site guards only against a maximum MP of 0, sending those targets to fdps_show_miss_indicator instead.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image; called only by game code and its only non-CRT callee is fdps_get_unit_record]

Rebuild note:
The routine computes the MP it actually applied (clamped result minus the old +0x44 value) at 0002763b and then throws it away, returning the unclamped amount*9/10 + (rand()%100)*amount/1000 instead. The discarded delta is not a harmless dead store: every call site feeds the return value to fdps_show_number_indicator, so the figure the player sees is the roll and not the gain. Writing the obvious C -- returning the real gain, which the HP twin fdps_unit_apply_heal also declines to do -- makes the CureMP popup show a smaller number than the original whenever the target was near full MP, and show 0 where the original shows the full roll when an effect-0x0c item is used on a unit already at full MP, a case fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets does not filter out. Keep the dead local and return the pre-clamp amount.

=== 00027660 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the eight single-bit masks 1, 2, 4, 8, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80 -- the value 1u << n for n = 0..7.

Nothing writes it. It is read once per call, in the prologue of fdps_set_flag_bit, where two inline MOVSD copy all 8 bytes into that function's local array at EBP-0x14; every later access goes to the stack copy, never here. fdps_set_flag_bit then resolves a unit record through fdps_get_unit_record and does record[0x1a + n/8] |= mask[n % 8], i.e. it sets bit n of the 5-byte known-spell bitmap that starts at offset 0x1a of the 0x50-byte unit record. n is a spell id and runs 0x00..0x27, 40 spells over 40 bits: fdps_unit_collect_known_spells walks the same field with an outer loop of 5 bytes and an inner loop of 8 bits and reports each set bit as spell id byte_idx * 8 + bit_idx. The four call sites all mean 'this unit has learned a spell': fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up passes the spell id it just read from the class growth row and drew as text page id + 0x1be; fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets grants spell 0x1d to the unit named by the effect record; fdps_title_demo grants 0x27 and 0xb to its demo units; fdps_chapter_01_end grants spell 0 to unit 0 as a story event. Because the table is exactly 1 << n, the mask lookup is equivalent to a shift and carries no other meaning.

Pool: binary_artifact  [two inline MOVSD with no counter and no memcpy call are Watcom's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so these bytes are wcc386's own output rather than a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
None. The bytes are read-only and the stack copy is never written, so hoisting them to a file-scope const changes shape but not behaviour; the faithful shape is still a local `uchar mask[8] = {1,2,4,8,0x10,0x20,0x40,0x80};` inside fdps_set_flag_bit.

=== 00027668 [PLATE]
Initialiser image for the three-row sprite-id table fdps_cast_spell_on_targets copies onto its stack: the floating indicator labels for the three 神之祝福 buff slots.

Read once, at 00028906-0002890d, where fdps_cast_spell_on_targets copies all 12 bytes to EBP-0x30 with three MOVSD before it plays any spell; nothing else references it. The stack copy is used only on the spell 0x14 (神之祝福) path: for each buff slot 0, 1, 2 that fdps_unit_apply_status_effect lands on a target, that slot's row is passed to fdps_show_sprite_indicator as the sprite_ids argument, which queues up to four sprites out of the indicator sheet at DAT_000643d8 to float over the target's tile.

Pool: binary_artifact  [compiler-emitted initialiser image for a function-local array, copied wholesale to the stack by MOVSD and never read in place -- the same pattern as binary_artifact_local_array_init_spell_bit_mask_lookup_27660 four bytes below]

Rebuild note:
The zero byte ending each 4-byte row is a sentinel, not padding. Declaring the local as uchar tbl[3][3] = {{0x3b,0x3c,0x3c},{0x3d,0x3e,0x3f},{0x3d,0x3e,0x40}} both breaks the 4-byte stride the slot index uses and drops the terminator fdps_show_sprite_indicator stops on, so it would run into the next row and draw a fourth glyph. === 000278e0 [PLATE]
Frame-paced presentation and input-wait loop for the spell-list window: once per game tick it repaints the caster's spell page, its scroll arrows and his animated sprite over a live background, presents the result to VGA memory, and returns the first input code the keyboard poller reports as a real key.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_unit_collect_known_spells(unit_index, <stack buffer>) once on entry and keeps only the returned spell count, which is what decides whether the down arrow is drawn. It then loops on fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat: a code <= 0x7f leaves the loop and becomes the result, anything above it is the poller's no-key sentinel and means another frame is due. The frame is skipped entirely unless the live tick at DAT_00069d64 differs from the tick of the last drawn frame latched in DAT_00064390.

Per frame: fdps_cycle_ui_palette advances the UI palette; the blink phase is (DAT_00064390 / 8) & 1, taken from the latch, which at this point still holds the previous frame's tick. fdps_blit_rect restores the 0x97 x 0x95 panel background from panel_src into window_buf + 0x3b58 (column 152, row 47) and fdps_draw_spell_list_page redraws the eight rows over it. fdps_blit_command_sprite then paints Command.cel sprite blink + 0x44 at window_buf + 0x3e1c (column 220, row 49) when list_top is non-zero, and sprite blink + 0x46 at window_buf + 0xef9c (column 220, row 191) when list_top + 8 is below the spell count -- the up and down scroll arrows, each alternating between two sprites every 8 ticks.

It allocates a 0x15180-byte scene buffer and a 0xfa00-byte 320x200 frame buffer. With the mode flag DAT_00060070 clear it composites the live scrolling map into the scene buffer with fdps_draw_scene_layers, zeroes the frame and blits the 0x138 x 0xc0 view window (source stride 0x168) into frame + 0x504 (column 4, row 4); with the flag set it copies the saved 320x200 page at DAT_00063fb4 into the frame instead, after blitting that same page into the scene buffer, which is freed without ever being read. The scene buffer is freed on both paths.

The walk-cycle frame index is (DAT_00064390 % 16) / 4 with 3 folded back to 1, giving the 0, 1, 2, 1 cycle; the clamp to 0 that follows cannot fire for a non-negative tick. A 0x240-byte 24x24 scratch buffer receives cel sprite 3 of the sheet at DAT_000643dc as its backdrop, and fdps_blit_dispatch draws the walk frame over it in blit mode 0. The sprite row is unit_index itself when DAT_00060070 is set, and otherwise byte +2 of the record fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) returns; row * 0x30 + walk * 4 indexes the table based at DAT_00060138 and the dword found there is an offset added back to that same base to form the sprite pointer. fdps_get_unit_record is called on both paths, so its result is fetched and dropped when the flag is set.

The scratch buffer is blitted into window_buf + 0xd21 (column 161, row 10), window_buf + 0xf is blitted into frame + 0xf as a 0x123 x 0xc8 region, the whole 0xfa00-byte frame is copied to the VGA aperture at 0xa0000, the frame and scratch buffers are freed, and DAT_00064390 is set to DAT_00069d64.

Parameters:
  window_buf -- the composed 320-pitch window image the spell page lives in; the list area at +0x3b58, the two arrow positions at +0x3e1c and +0xef9c and the caster's sprite at +0xd21 are rewritten in it every frame, and it is then stamped into the presented screen at column 15
  panel_src -- the pristine 151 x 149 (0x97 x 0x95) spell-panel background, source stride 0x97; blitted over the list area first each frame so the previous frame's rows are erased before the new ones are drawn
  unit_index -- index of the battle unit whose spells are listed; handed to fdps_unit_collect_known_spells, fdps_draw_spell_list_page and fdps_get_unit_record, and used directly as the row in the sprite table at DAT_00060138 when DAT_00060070 is set

  cursor_index -- index of the highlighted spell row, passed straight through to fdps_draw_spell_list_page

Returns:
  The first code fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat hands back that is <= 0x7f, i.e. a BIOS scancode; the caller maps it to cursor movement, confirm or cancel. Codes above 0x7f are the poller's no-key sentinel and are never returned.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set; calls only game routines and uses the CRT as a client]

Rebuild note:
Both animation phases -- the arrow blink (DAT_00064390 / 8) & 1 and the walk-cycle frame (DAT_00064390 % 16) / 4 -- are computed from the latch DAT_00064390 while it still holds the tick of the previously drawn frame; the latch is only advanced to DAT_00069d64 on the last line of the frame. Writing the obvious loop, which latches the new tick at the top and derives the phases from the live counter, shifts both animations by one tick.

=== 00027c20 [PLATE]
Battle "spell" command: runs one player-controlled unit's whole cast -- opens the caster's known-spell list over the battle map, walks the player through target selection, and plays the chosen spell out on the targets it settles on.

Algorithm:
Zeroes the spell list's scroll position and cursor row once, then repeats this cycle until a spell is actually cast:
  - fdps_load_status_cel_image builds the status window page. A 0xfa00-byte malloc'd buffer takes a memmove copy of the live VGA screen at 0xa0000, and a second 0x57e3-byte buffer takes a fdps_blit_rect copy of the pristine 0x97 x 0x95 list area at window+0x3b58, which is what fdps_spell_list_select_loop erases each frame's list with.
  - fdps_draw_unit_status_panel and fdps_draw_spell_list_page paint the caster's panel and the first page of its spell list, fdps_get_unit_record caches the caster's record (the byte at record+0x02 is loaded into a local that nothing reads), and nine fdps_draw_status_window_anim_frame steps slide the window in.
  - fdps_spell_list_select_loop takes the player's choice, fdps_close_status_window puts the screen back and the three buffers are freed. -1 from that loop is the player backing out of the spell list, and the function returns -1 with the unit not having acted.
  - fdps_unit_collect_known_spells rebuilds the id list and fdps_get_spell_record looks the chosen id up in the MagicDat.dat table: byte +3 is the cast distance (bit 0x10 set means a straight line, the low nibble its length), byte +4 the blast radius, byte +6 the target side. The map cursor mode at 00069cd0 is set to radius + 2, which is how fdps_draw_map_cursor picks the diamond footprint painted round the cursor.
  - distance != 0: fdps_collect_targets_in_range lists what is in reach of the cursor tile (00069cd4 is the cursor's map pixel x and 00069ccc its y, 0x18 = 24 pixels to the tile) and fdps_map_cursor_select_loop, in the mode the spell's target-side byte names, lets the player aim. The hit list is then recomputed about the confirmed tile: distance <= 0x0f takes fdps_collect_targets_in_range again with the blast radius in place of the distance, distance >= 0x10 takes fdps_collect_targets_in_line from the caster's own tile (unit record +0 and +1) for distance - 0x10 tiles and plays "Chess.wav".
  - distance == 0 (the map-wide spells): the radius is read back out of 00069cd0, the cursor drops to mode 1, fdps_collect_targets_in_range gathers every enemy within the radius of the caster's tile, and fdps_map_cursor_select_loop runs as mode 4 -- or as mode 5, which never confirms, when the radius caught nobody.
  - Spell 0x15 (傳送術) then takes a second pick: when the first unit of the hit list is the caster itself the pick is thrown away, otherwise fdps_map_cursor_select_loop mode 6 asks for a tile that unit may stand on and the answer is left in tiles in the destination globals 0006437c (x) and 00064380 (y), after which fdps_map_cursor_move_to_unit walks the cursor back to the caster.
  - On a confirmed cast, 0x0001a4c0 plays the animation and applies the spell (the MP cost comes off in there), fdps_collect_death_scripts, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead and fdps_run_death_scripts settle whatever died, and the experience banked in 00069cec is divided by the caster's level (unit record +0x21, plus 0x1e when the class byte at +7 is above 8, i.e. a promoted class) before 0x0001dd30 awards it.
  - The cursor returns to the caster and the loop ends. Cancelling target selection instead reopens the spell list, still on the same page with the same spell highlighted.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array based at 00069cd8, handed straight down from fdps_battle_action_menu.

Returns:
  1 when the unit cast a spell, -1 when the player backed out of the spell list without acting. No other value is produced; fdps_battle_action_menu marks the unit done for anything that is not -1.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set; hash unique in the image, and the sole caller plus every non-CRT callee are game routines]

Rebuild note:
The spell list's scroll position and cursor row are initialised before the retry loop, not inside it, so a cancelled target selection reopens the menu on the same page with the same spell still highlighted; declaring the two locals inside the loop body -- the obvious C -- sends the player back to the top of the list every time. The experience award is an integer division of 00069cec by the caster's level, so a haul smaller than the divisor rounds away to nothing.

Algorithm:

  - 0x000276f0 draws the page of the list that begins at *list_top with row *cursor_index highlighted, into window_buf + 0x3b58 with pitch 0x140.
  - 0x000278e0 runs the animated window redraw and the input poll, and returns a BIOS scancode.
  - 0x48 (up): when *cursor_index is not 0, steps the cursor up one row and pulls *list_top down to it once the cursor has scrolled off the top of the window.
  - 0x50 (down): while *cursor_index is below count-1, steps the cursor down one row and, when *list_top + 8 <= *cursor_index, scrolls to *cursor_index - 7. The visible window is eight rows tall.
  - 0x1c (Enter) or 0x39 (Space): looks the selected id up with fdps_get_spell_record and compares that spell's MP cost (record byte +5) with the caster's current MP (signed word at unit record +0x44). Returns 1 when the MP covers the cost; when it does not, it drops back into the loop with no sound, message or cursor change of any kind.
  - 0x01 (Esc) or 0x53 (Del): returns -1.
  - any other scancode: redraw and poll again.
Those two keys are the only exits. Nothing here spends MP; the deduction is fdps_spell_deduct_mp_cost's job, later in the caller.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the casting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array; the caller passes the unit whose battle turn is running.
  window_buf -- the 320x200, 0x140-pitch status-window page the menu is composed into; the spell list occupies the 151x149 block at +0x3b58.
  panel_src -- 151x149 copy of that block as it looked before the list was drawn over it, taken by the caller with fdps_blit_rect; used to erase the list ahead of every redraw.
  list_top -- in/out. Index of the first list row shown in the eight-row window. The caller initialises it to 0 and keeps it across repeat entries into the menu.
  cursor_index -- in/out. Index of the highlighted row, and the way the choice comes back: on a confirm the caller re-runs fdps_unit_collect_known_spells and reads ids[*cursor_index] to recover the spell id.

Returns:
  1 -- the player confirmed a spell whose MP cost the caster can pay.
  -1 -- the player cancelled with Esc or Del.
  No other value is ever returned.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_unit_collect_known_spells, fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_blit_rect; no Function ID hit in either library set]
