=== 00028313 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / nop, aligning next function to 0x28320

=== 00028320 [PLATE]
Damages one battle unit with one spell: rolls the spell's hit rate and, when it lands, works out what that spell does to that target and takes it off the target's HP.

Algorithm:
fdps_get_unit_record(target_unit_index) resolves the target's 0x50-byte record, and the class code in its byte +0x20 plus one indexes fdps_get_class_record for the target class's 10-byte PROMAP.DAT record, whose byte +0x09 holds 100 minus that class's magic resistance. fdps_get_spell_record(spell_id) then supplies the 7-byte MAGICDAT.DAT record, and the signed word at its +0x00 -- the spell's power -- selects the damage formula:
  - power >= 0: a flat magic figure. damage = power * (100 - target class magic resistance) / 100. Neither the caster's stats nor the target's defense enters it, so the same spell hits for the same amount whoever casts it.
  - power < 0: power is the negative of an attack multiplier in percent, -250 meaning 2.50x. fdps_get_unit_record(caster_unit_index) supplies the caster's derived attack word at +0x48, and damage = attack * -power / 100 minus the target's derived defense word at +0x4a, floored at 0. Those two words are the ones fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats writes.
Byte +0x02 of the spell record is the hit rate in percent. rand() % 100 is drawn and compared against it; a draw that is not below the rate returns 0 with the target untouched. On a draw that lands, spell ids 0x0a (裂地術) and 0x0b (封神裂震), the two ground-shaking spells, also return 0 when fdps_unit_is_flying says the target travels above the terrain. Every other case hands the figure to fdps_unit_apply_damage(target_unit_index, damage), which rolls the final 90.0%-99.9% of it into the target's HP word and credits the battle experience.

Parameters:
  caster_unit_index -- index of the acting unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8. Read only on the power < 0 path, and only for the attack word at +0x48. fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets and fdps_cast_spell_on_targets both pass the unit that is casting.
  target_unit_index -- index of the unit being hit, in the same array. Both callers pass one entry of their target id list.
  spell_id -- MAGICDAT.DAT record index, 0..0x27; the spell being cast. 0x0a and 0x0b additionally select the flying-target immunity.

Returns:
  The damage fdps_unit_apply_damage rolled, or 0 -- 0 covering all three of a failed hit roll, a flying target under spell 0x0a/0x0b, and a computed damage floored at 0. fdps_cast_spell_on_targets floats a non-zero return over the target as the damage number through fdps_show_number_indicator and paints fdps_show_miss_indicator on 0. fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets takes the target's HP word +0x40 before the call and puts that old value back afterwards, keeping only the two endpoints, so its combat animation can interpolate the drop frame by frame -- the HP write this function makes through fdps_unit_apply_damage is real and has to happen here for that to work.

Pool: fdps  [game logic over the unit, class and spell records with a literal 0x64 percent divisor; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ail set and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
rand() is drawn before the flying-target test, so a target that is immune to spell 0x0a or 0x0b still consumes one value from the PRNG. Hoisting that test into a guard clause at the top of the function -- the obvious shape, since it is an immunity -- leaves the draw untaken and shifts every later damage roll of the battle.

=== 00028453 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / nop, aligning next function to 0x28460

=== 00028460 [PLATE]
Applies one damaging effect to a battle unit's HP and credits the experience the party earns for it.

Algorithm:
Resolves the target through fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads its current HP (word +0x40) and
maximum HP (word +0x42). Rolls the damage actually dealt as base_damage * 9 / 10 plus
(rand() % 100) * base_damage / 1000, each term truncated on its own, so the roll lands between 90.0%
and 99.9% of base_damage. Subtracts the roll from current HP, clamps the result at 0, and stores it
back into word +0x40.
When the target is enemy-side (byte +0x6 == 0) it also credits experience. fdps_get_enemy_record is
called with the target's portrait id byte +0x7 biased down by 0x3c, and byte +0x9 of that EnemyDat.dat
record -- the enemy's base experience value -- is multiplied by the target's level (byte +0x21). A
target still standing after the hit (clamped HP non-zero) has that award prorated by
damage / maximum HP; a target just killed keeps the whole of it. The award is added into the pending
battle-experience accumulator at 00069cec, the same counter fdps_unit_apply_heal adds to and
0x0001dd30 clamps to 0x63 before handing it to the unit that acted.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the target in the 0x50-byte unit record array at DAT_00069cd8; used only as
    the argument to fdps_get_unit_record. Callers read it out of a target id list.
  base_damage -- nominal damage of the item, spell or skill effect before the roll.
    fdps_apply_damage_to_targets and 0x000262a0 pass the effect's damage figure; 0x00028320 passes
    the magnitude it computed from the effect record.

Returns:
  The rolled damage. All three callers hand it to 0x0001f510, which floats it over the target as the
  damage number. It is the amount rolled, not the HP the unit actually lost, so an overkill reports
  more than the target had left.

Pool: fdps  [game data structures and game rules; no fid hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The value returned is the damage rolled, not the HP the unit actually lost: the clamp at 0 happens to the stored HP only, and the callers float the returned figure over the target. Writing the obvious 'return hp_before - hp_after' changes every overkill's on-screen damage number. The roll itself is also never the full nominal figure -- base*9/10 + (rand()%100)*base/1000 tops out at 99.9% of base_damage and each division truncates separately, so folding it into one expression such as base*(900 + rand()%100)/1000 gives different numbers.

=== 00028561 [EOL]
15 bytes alignment filler, one cdecl 2-arg wrapper function at 00028570 (65 bytes, ends RET at 000285b0), then 15 bytes filler to 000285c0

=== 00028570 [PLATE]
Heals one battle unit by the power value of a spell record.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_spell_record(spell_id) for the 7-byte MagicDat.dat record, sign-extends the signed 16-bit power field at record+0x00 (the spell's damage-or-heal amount; it is signed because the eight special attacks store an attack-power multiplier there as a negative percentage), and calls fdps_unit_apply_heal(unit_index, power). That routine rolls the heal as power*9/10 + (rand()%100)*power/1000, adds it to the unit record's current HP at +0x40, clamps the total to the maximum at +0x42, and -- only when the record's portrait id byte +0x7 is below 0x3c, i.e. a roster character rather than an EnemyDat entry -- credits (effective level * 25 * HP actually restored) / maximum HP into the pending battle-experience accumulator DAT_00069cec. Its return value is passed back unchanged. Nothing else happens here: no hit-rate roll against the record's +0x02 chance byte, no MP deduction of the +0x05 cost (that is the sibling fdps_spell_deduct_mp_cost), and no test of the +0x06 target field, so a spell whose power is negative would subtract HP rather than add it.

Nothing in the image reaches this entry: no call, no data word and no other reference. The two live heal paths bypass it -- fdps_cast_spell_on_targets calls fdps_unit_apply_heal on each target itself, and fdps_apply_heal_to_targets does the same for item effects -- so this is an unused packaged form of that step, unlike its counterpart fdps_spell_damage_unit, which has two callers.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at the global 0x00069cd8; forwarded unchanged to fdps_unit_apply_heal, which resolves it through fdps_get_unit_record. Not bounds-checked anywhere on the path.
  spell_id -- MagicDat.dat record index, 0..0x27; selects the record whose power field is read and is not used for anything else.

Returns:
  int -- what fdps_unit_apply_heal returns: the heal it rolled, power*9/10 + (rand()%100)*power/1000, before the clamp. This is not the HP actually restored, which is smaller whenever the clamp at maximum HP bites.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in any library; both callees are game code over game globals]

Rebuild note:
The power field at spell record +0x00 is a signed 16-bit value and eight spells store it negative (an attack-power multiplier percentage, see assets/tables/spells.md); the body sign-extends it with MOVSX and passes it through with no sign test, so writing the field as unsigned short/uint16 in C -- the obvious choice for a byte-packed table -- turns a -250 into 65286 and heals for tens of thousands of HP instead of behaving as the original does.

=== 000285b1 [EOL]
Watcom alignment filler after the RET, up to the next function at 000285c0: same three multi-byte LEA NOP forms

=== 000285c0 [PLATE]
Deducts a spell's MP cost from the caster's current MP.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_spell_record(spell_id) for the 7-byte MAGICDAT.DAT record and fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) for the caster's 0x50-byte record in the array based at the global 0x00069cd8. Sign-extends the caster's current MP out of the signed 16-bit field at record+0x44, subtracts the record's MP cost byte at spell+0x05 (read unsigned) from it, and stores the low 16 bits back into record+0x44. That is the whole body: there is no test that the caster can afford the cost, no floor at zero, and no reference to the maximum MP at record+0x46, so a cost larger than the current MP leaves the field negative.

The one caller, fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets, runs this once after the action's animation loop has finished. It is reached only through fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets, whose own callers are fdps_battle_spell_command @ 00027c20 (call site 00028083) and fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell @ 00013c90 (call site 00013d89), so every action that gets here is a cast.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at the global 0x00069cd8, identifying the unit that just acted. Forwarded unchanged to fdps_get_unit_record, which bounds-checks nothing.
  spell_id -- MAGICDAT.DAT record index, 0..0x27, the action just performed. Forwarded unchanged to fdps_get_spell_record and used only to reach the cost byte at record+0x05.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game-only fdps_get_spell_record and fdps_get_unit_record and mutates the game's unit record array; no Function ID hit in either library set]

=== 0002860f [EOL]
Single 0x90 NOP aligning next function entry to 0x28610.

=== 00028610 [PLATE]
Plays spell 11 (封神裂震)'s full-screen Mag11.saf animation, then hands the screen back to the battle map through a white flash.

Algorithm:
fdps_vfs_load_entry("MISC.VFS", "Mag11.saf") loads the animation and malloc gives a 0x16480-byte page -- a 368x248 8bpp surface, 48 pixels wider and taller than the 320x200 screen, so a frame may overhang the visible window without being clipped. A 0x24-byte composite-sprite draw request is built on the stack over that page: pitch 0x170 (368) at +0x04, height 0xf8 (248) at +0x08, x = y = 0x18 (24) at +0x0c/+0x10, the SAF image at +0x14, blit mode 9 at +0x20 -- fdps_rle_blit_translucent -- and at +0x1c a three-dword blend descriptor holding the shade-ramp table DAT_000653f0, the blend level, and the inverse colour cube DAT_000643f0. The three-dword playback cursor is set up by hand -- cursor[2] takes the SAF image at 00028683 -- and fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 1) then zeroes the frame index and the dwell accumulator. A second malloc of 0xfa00 takes a memmove snapshot of the mode 13h screen at 0xa0000, the picture the spell was cast over.

Fade-in, 31 ticks, counter i running 0x1f down to 1: the blend level is i / 2, stepping 15 down to 0, and since fdps_rle_blit_translucent reads level 0 as an opaque source and level 16 as an invisible one, the animation comes up out of the frozen screen. Each tick copies the 320x200 snapshot into the page's visible window at page+0x2298 (24 * 368 + 24) with fdps_blit_rect, takes the current frame number from cursor[0] into request+0x18, draws it with fdps_draw_composite_sprite, and advances the cursor with fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 0), discarding the result -- so the clip wraps rather than stopping when it reaches its end. It then spins on port 0x3da until vertical retrace begins and again until it ends, blits the page's 320x200 window to 0xa0000, and spins until the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 changes. The snapshot buffer is freed at the end of the phase.

Main phase, running until fdps_saf_advance_tick reports the clip has ended: the same tick, except that memset clears the whole 0x16480-byte page to 0 first, so the rest of the animation plays on black instead of over the frozen screen, and the return of fdps_saf_advance_tick(cursor, 0) is kept as the loop's exit condition. Mode 0 wraps the frame index back to 0 and returns 1 once the last frame has been held, so this phase runs from wherever the fade-in left the cursor to the end of the clip, exactly once.

Clip timing: Mag11.saf holds 22 frames and every one of them dwells for a single tick, so the 31-tick fade-in outlasts it. The fade-in shows frames 0 through 21 on its first 22 ticks, wraps, and shows frames 0 through 8 again on the remaining 9, leaving the cursor on frame 9; the main phase then runs frames 9 through 21, 13 ticks. The presentation is 44 ticks long and the clip is played through exactly twice, with the seam between the two passes falling inside the fade-in rather than at the phase boundary.

The flag argument to fdps_draw_composite_sprite is 0 in both phases, and that callee only reaches fdps_sfx_play when the flag is non-zero (000142ac), so neither of the two sound effects embedded in Mag11.saf -- frame 0 fires sound 0 and frame 15 fires sound 1 -- is ever played. The audio for this spell comes from the caller, which starts EarQu.wav itself.

Exit: the SAF image and the page are freed. fdps_set_palette_range(DAT_000643bc, 0, 0xff, 0x3f, 0x3f, 0x3f) re-uploads the game palette with the maximum per-channel bias, which clamps every DAC entry to white, and memset blanks the 0xfa00-byte frame buffer at 0xa0000. Six steps then run, i = 5 down to 0: fdps_set_palette_range with bias i * 10 -- 50, 40, 30, 20, 10, 0 -- each followed by fdps_render_view_frame, which repaints and presents the live battle view. The screen therefore whites out and fades back into the map at its true palette over six frames; the opening 0x3f bias is not part of that arithmetic progression.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [references the game's own strings, data tables and helpers: it calls fdps_vfs_load_entry, fdps_saf_advance_tick, fdps_draw_composite_sprite, fdps_blit_rect, fdps_set_palette_range and fdps_render_view_frame, which a compiled library object could not, and Function ID matched nothing in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set]

Rebuild note:
The dword both frame loops compare against DAT_00069d64 is never initialised: on the first tick of the fade-in it holds stack garbage, so that wait falls straight through and the frame is presented without waiting a tick. Seeding it with 0 or with the current value of the counter -- the obvious C -- costs an extra tick there and lengthens the fade-in. DAT_00069d64 is written only by the timer interrupt, so it also has to be declared volatile, or wcc386 loads it once into a register and neither spin ever ends.

The fade-in's 31 ticks against Mag11.saf's 22 are also not to be reconciled. The cursor is deliberately not reset between the two phases, so the main phase picks the clip up mid-way at frame 9; resetting it, or shortening the fade-in to the clip's length, or letting the fade-in stop at the end of the clip, each changes what the player sees.

=== 000288e4 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs between FUN_00028610 and FUN_000288f0.

=== 000288f0 [PLATE]
Applies one spell to a list of battle-map targets and plays that spell's presentation over the map, instead of on the full-screen combat screen: MP is deducted from the caster, the spell's Emg animation runs on every target's map cell, and the spell's actual effect -- damage, healing, a status ailment, a buff, a teleport -- is resolved target by target.

Algorithm:
Copies the 12-byte buff-indicator sprite table at 00027668 onto the stack as three 4-byte groups, one per buff slot, and clears the map-cursor mode global DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so no cursor is drawn while the spell plays. fdps_play_spell_palette_flash(spell_id) flashes the screen in the spell's colour.

It then deducts the cost: the caster's current MP, the signed word at unit-record +0x44, minus the spell record's cost byte at +0x05, written back as a word. That is the same read-modify-write fdps_spell_deduct_mp_cost performs; the sequence is repeated inline here rather than called.

The map animation's name is formatted into a stack buffer as "Emg%02d.saf" with the spell id in decimal -- except for spell 0x0b (封神裂震), which formats spell_id - 1 and so plays Emg10.saf, 裂地術's animation, because MISC.VFS has no EMG11.SAF. Spell 0x0b then plays its own full-screen cutscene through fdps_play_spell_11_cutscene; spell 0x21 (鎮魂之歌) instead loads Emg33-1.saf out of MISC.VFS with fdps_vfs_load_entry, plays it with fdps_saf_play_over_scene and frees it.

Spells 0x0a (裂地術) and 0x0b shake the ground: EarQu.wav is loaded from MISC.VFS and started with fdps_audio_start_wav(buf, 1, -1, -1), then 25 iterations of fdps_render_view_frame run with the scene view origin globals DAT_00069ce4 and DAT_00069ce0 each offset from their saved values by rand() % 4 - 2 -- a range of -2..+1, not a symmetric jitter -- and both globals are put back to the saved values when the loop ends.

fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units(target_count, target_unit_indices, name) draws that animation on every listed target's cell. The spell is then resolved, dispatching on spell_id:

  0x0e-0x10 and 0x21 -- the healing spells 恢復之光, 治癒之風, 痊癒之泉 and 鎮魂之歌. Each target gets fdps_unit_apply_heal by the spell record's power word at +0x00, and the amount it returns floats over the target through fdps_show_number_indicator with glyph base 0x27.

  0x15 (傳送術) -- fdps_map_cursor_move_to takes the cursor tile globals DAT_0006437c (x) and DAT_00064380 (y) scaled by the 0x18-pixel tile size, those two tile coordinates are written into target 0's record bytes +0x00 and +0x01, and the animation is replayed so it appears at the tile the target arrived on. Only the first target is moved.

  0x16 (神行術) -- clears bit 7 of each target's record byte +0x05, the bit fdps_battle_mark_unit_done sets, so the target may act again this turn.

  0x18 (甦癒術) -- for each target whose ailment bytes at +0x25..+0x27 are not all zero, fdps_show_cure_indicator queues the cured mark; then memset clears those three bytes.

  0x11 (封魔咒術) -- fdps_flash_units_in_color(target_count, target_unit_indices, 0x2b) runs twice back to back, then fdps_unit_apply_status_effect(0x11, target) is rolled on each target, with fdps_show_miss_indicator on the targets it fails against.

  0x12 and 0x13 (腐毒術, 麻痺術) -- fdps_unit_apply_status_effect(spell_id, target) per target, MISS on failure.

  0x14 (神之祝福) -- three passes, one per buff slot 0, 1, 2. Each pass rolls fdps_unit_apply_status_effect(slot, target) on every target and, where it lands, floats that slot's four sprites from the stack copy of the 00027668 table over the target with fdps_show_sprite_indicator and calls fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats; fdps_play_indicator_queue plays the pass out before the next slot starts.

  anything else -- fdps_spell_damage_unit(caster_unit_index, target, spell_id) per target. A non-zero result floats over the target with glyph base 0, and for spell 0x0d (鬼動死靈陣) fdps_unit_inflict_random_ailments is rolled on that target as well; a zero result shows MISS instead.

Every path converges on a final fdps_play_indicator_queue, sets DAT_00069cd0 to 1 so the plain map cursor is drawn again, and frees the EarQu.wav buffer if one was loaded.

The two callers both reach it with the same four arguments. fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell calls it directly when the battle-animation option byte DAT_00060010 is not 1, and otherwise goes through fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets, which forwards to this function anyway for spell ids 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0e-0x16, 0x18 and 0x21 -- the spells that have no full-screen presentation of their own.

Parameters:
  caster_unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit array at DAT_00069cd8 of the unit casting the spell. Its MP pays the cost and it is the attacker fdps_spell_damage_unit scores the damage from. Both callers pass their own unit index straight through.
  spell_id -- MagicDat.dat spell id, 0x00..0x27; selects the record fdps_get_spell_record returns, the Emg%02d.saf animation and the branch that resolves the effect. In practice only 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0d-0x16, 0x18 and 0x21 reach here.
  target_count -- how many entries of target_unit_indices are valid; the bound of every per-target loop, and the unit count handed to fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units and fdps_flash_units_in_color.
  target_unit_indices -- caller-owned byte array of unit indices, one per target, built by fdps_collect_targets_in_range. Each byte is widened to a full index for fdps_get_unit_record and the per-target callees.

Returns:
  Nothing. Every branch falls into the single epilogue at 00028ed6; EAX at the RET is whatever free left there and neither caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [game strings and game call graph; no Function ID hit in either set]

Rebuild note:
Spell 0x0b's animation name is built from spell_id - 1 on purpose: it shares 裂地術's Emg10.saf because MISC.VFS holds no EMG11.SAF. Writing the obvious sprintf(name, "Emg%02d.saf", spell_id) for every spell -- or "fixing" the -1 as an off-by-one -- makes 封神裂震 ask for Emg11.saf, and fdps_vfs_load_entry ends the process when the entry is not in the archive.

=== 00028edd [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8d 40 00 (lea eax,[eax+0x0]) aligning FUN_00028ee0 to 4 bytes.

=== 00028ee0 [PLATE]
Inflicts the status ailments that ride on 鬼動死靈陣 (spell id 0x0d) onto one battle unit: each of the unit's three ailment slots is rolled independently at a flat 20% chance.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) once to resolve the unit's 0x50-byte record, then loops i from 0 to 2 over the three ailment timer bytes at record offsets 0x25 (腐毒術), 0x26 (麻痺術) and 0x27 (封魔咒術). Each pass calls the CRT rand() and takes the result modulo 100; when the remainder is below 0x14 -- the flat 20% chance -- it calls fdps_unit_is_ailment_immune(unit_index), and only when that reports the unit is not immune it calls rand() a second time and writes rand() % 2 + 2 into the byte at record + 0x25 + i, i.e. an ailment duration of 2 or 3, the same duration formula fdps_unit_apply_status_effect writes. The immunity test sits inside the loop and is reached only after the chance roll has already succeeded, so the first rand() is drawn three times per call whatever the unit is. Unlike fdps_unit_apply_status_effect, which lands one named effect, this routine consults no hit rate -- the 20% is a hard-coded literal, not a MAGICDAT.DAT lookup; it does not test whether a slot already holds an ailment, so an existing ailment is overwritten and its duration refreshed; and it touches no global at all, so nothing is credited to the pending battle experience at DAT_00069cec that fdps_unit_apply_status_effect adds to. Ailments landed this way therefore earn the party no experience.

Both callers reach it only for spell id 0x0d and only after that spell landed: fdps_cast_spell_on_targets tests spell_id == 0xd at 00028e7c on the branch where fdps_spell_damage_unit returned non-zero, and fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets tests spell_id == 0xd at 0001ae89 together with its own hit flag.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, in 0 .. unit count at 0x00060150 - 1. The callers pass one entry of the target id byte array they are iterating. Not range-checked.

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX is not set on the exit path and neither caller looks at it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls fdps_get_unit_record and writes a game record field]

Rebuild note:
The immunity test must stay inside the loop and stay second in the &&. It depends only on unit_index and on record fields this loop never writes, so it is loop-invariant and reads as an obvious hoist, but hoisting it -- or writing the condition as !immune && rand() % 100 < 20 -- skips rand() calls the original makes and desynchronises the shared RNG stream. The absent already-afflicted check is likewise load-bearing: the sibling has one and this does not, so refreshing an ailment already on the unit is the original behaviour.

=== 00028f64 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs between FUN_00028ee0 and FUN_00028f70.

=== 00028f70 [PLATE]
Applies one status effect to a battle unit, rolling the effect's hit rate and crediting the experience the party earns when it lands.

Algorithm:
Resolves the target's 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index), then maps effect_id onto one of the six status-effect timer bytes of that record: 0x11 (封魔咒術) selects +0x27, 0x12 (腐毒術) selects +0x25, 0x13 (麻痺術) selects +0x26, and any other id selects +(0x22 + effect_id) and rewrites the id to 0x14 -- the only caller passes 0, 1 or 2 there, the three 神之祝福 buff slots at +0x22, +0x23 and +0x24 that fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats reads as a 1.15x attack multiplier, a 1.15x defence multiplier and a flat +15. fdps_get_spell_record(effect_id) then supplies the effect's hit rate in byte +2 of its MAGICDAT.DAT record, and rand() % 100 is compared against it. The effect lands only when that roll passes, when the chosen timer byte is still 0, and -- for ids 0x11 through 0x13 only -- when fdps_unit_is_ailment_immune(unit_index) reports the unit is not immune; the 神之祝福 slots skip the immunity test. Landing writes rand() % 2 + 2 into the timer byte, so every effect runs for two or three turns, sets the result to 1, and adds ten times the target's level (record byte +0x21) to the pending battle experience at DAT_00069cec, the same accumulator fdps_unit_apply_damage and fdps_unit_apply_heal credit and fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up later clamps to 99 before awarding it.

Parameters:
  effect_id -- selects the status effect. 0x11, 0x12 and 0x13 are the spell ids of the three ailment spells and double as the MAGICDAT.DAT index of the hit-rate lookup; 0, 1 and 2 are the three 神之祝福 buff slots, whose hit rate always comes from spell 0x14 instead. fdps_cast_spell_on_targets is the only caller and passes nothing else.
  unit_index -- index of the target unit in the 0x50-byte unit record array based at 00069cd8, taken from the caller's array of target id bytes. Not range-checked.

Returns:
  1 -- the timer byte was written and the effect is now running on the unit.
  0 -- the hit-rate roll failed, the unit already carries this effect, or the unit is immune. The two ailment call sites in fdps_cast_spell_on_targets, 00028cec (id 0x11) and 00028d4c (id 0x12 or 0x13), call fdps_show_miss_indicator on a 0; the 神之祝福 loop at 00028dc4 draws nothing on a 0, and on a 1 calls fdps_show_sprite_indicator (0001fc00) and fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats (00024d70).

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls fdps_get_unit_record and writes a game global]

Rebuild note:
effect_id is a spell id only on the 0x11-0x13 paths; for the 神之祝福 slots it arrives as a 0-2 index and the body overwrites it with 0x14 before calling fdps_get_spell_record. Writing the obvious fdps_get_spell_record(effect_id) reads spells 0, 1 and 2 (業火 / 狂暴巨燄 / 烈獄之火, hit rate 95) instead of 神之祝福's 100 and makes the blessing miss one time in twenty. The ailment offset table is not sequential either: 0x11 maps to +0x27, not to +0x25.

=== 00029076 [EOL]
Alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] (6) + lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0] (4), aligning FUN_00029080 to 16.

=== 00029080 [PLATE]
Reports whether one battle unit is immune to the three status ailments, so the code that inflicts them can skip it.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and reads two bytes out of the 0x50-byte record: the class code at +0x20 and the portrait/template id at +0x7. Returns 1 when the class code is 0x19 (機兵), 0x21-0x22 (守護獸, 將軍) or 0x24-0x26 (？？, 惡靈, 活屍), or when the template id falls in 0x3c-0x44; template ids of 0x3c and up index ENEMYDAT.DAT as id - 0x3c, so that range is the first nine enemy records. Anything else returns 0. The two class ranges are not contiguous: 0x23 (傭兵) sits between them and is not immune, and 0x1a (魔神) is below the first range and is not immune either.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; the callers pass the index of the unit that is about to be afflicted.

Returns:
  1 when the unit cannot be given a status ailment, 0 when it can. All three callers use it as a gate on a zero result: fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome writes the poison byte at record+0x25 for weapon effect 4 and the paralysis byte at +0x26 for weapon effect 1 only when this returns 0; fdps_unit_apply_status_effect applies the same gate before writing any of the ailment bytes for spells 0x11-0x13 (封魔咒術 -> +0x27, 腐毒術 -> +0x25, 麻痺術 -> +0x26); fdps_unit_inflict_random_ailments checks it before seeding all three bytes at +0x25..+0x27.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game function fdps_get_unit_record and compares hard-coded ids at fixed offsets of the game's unit record; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The immune class set has a deliberate hole and a rewrite that tidies it away changes the game: the code tests +0x20 == 0x19, then 0x21-0x22, then 0x24-0x26, so class 0x23 (傭兵) is NOT immune even though it sits between the two ranges. Writing the obvious `c >= 0x21 && c <= 0x26` makes mercenaries immune to poison, paralysis and 封魔咒術. The second half of the test is on a different field (+0x7 template id, 0x3c-0x44), not on the class, so it cannot be folded into the class comparison either.

=== 000290ff [EOL]
Single-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler between FUN_00029080 and FUN_00029100

=== 00029100 [PLATE]
Flashes the screen in one spell's signature colour, four times, while the spell is being cast.

Algorithm:
Copies three 40-byte colour planes out of read-only data onto the stack -- red from 0x00027674, green from 0x0002769c, blue from 0x000276c4 -- one entry per spell id 0x00-0x27. Then loops four times. Each pass selects VGA DAC entry 0 by writing 0 to port 0x3c8 through outp, writes red[spell_id], green[spell_id] and blue[spell_id] to port 0x3c9, and calls fdps_render_view_frame to paint and present one frame with that palette in force; it then selects DAC entry 0 again, writes (0,0,0), and calls fdps_render_view_frame once more. Eight presented frames in all, alternating the spell's colour with black, so everything drawn in palette index 0 strobes four times at the render loop's frame rate. The stored values are 6-bit VGA DAC levels and follow the spell's element: (63,0,0) for 0x00-0x02, 0x0c, 0x14, 0x1e and 0x1f, (57,42,25) earth brown for 0x0a-0x0b 裂地術/封神裂震, (0,63,0) green for 0x18 甦癒術, (63,9,0) for 0x20 審判之雷, and full white (63,63,63) for every remaining spell. DAC entry 0 is left black on return; the routine never puts back whatever colour it held before.

Parameters:
  spell_id -- MAGICDAT.DAT spell table index, 0x00-0x27. Comes straight from the caller at 0x000288f0, which passes the same value to fdps_get_spell_record. Used unchecked as the index into all three colour planes.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Rebuild note:
DAC entry 0 is left black and is NOT put back. The entry is never read before it is written -- there is no IN from port 0x3c7 or 0x3c9 anywhere between 00029100 and 00029201 -- and the last pass ends on the black burst at 000291b5..000291e9, so whatever colour index 0 held before the call is gone when the routine returns. Saving the entry first and restoring it at the end, the obvious courtesy for a routine that borrows one palette slot, changes what the map is drawn over once the cast is finished. A rebuild must not add that save-and-restore.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, hash unique in the image; calls the game symbol fdps_render_view_frame, which no compiled vendor object could reference]

=== 00029210 [PLATE]
Initialiser image for the title screen's four per-entry menu state bytes: { 0, 2, 2, 0 }.

Read once, at the top of fdps_title_screen, into a 4-byte stack array; nothing writes it. Element i is the state of title menu entry i (0 = New Game, 1 = Load Game screen, 2 = Continue/load savegame, 3 = Quit). 0 means the entry is selectable, non-zero means greyed out, so entries 1 and 2 start disabled and become selectable only when FDE.SAV opens, its checksum at buffer+0x59c7 matches fdps_compute_save_checksum and the byte at buffer+0x30c5 is not 0xff -- fdps_title_screen then stores 0 into elements 1 and 2 of the stack copy (0002a394, 0002a398). The value is also the cel frame variant: the menu draw loop passes frame index i*3 + (i == selection ? 1 : state[i]) to fdps_cel_blit_sprite, so 0 is the normal frame, 1 the highlighted frame and 2 the greyed frame. Enter (0x1c) and Space (0x39) accept the selection only while state[selection] is 0.

Pool: binary_artifact  [compiler-emitted initialiser image for a local array, copied wholesale into a stack slot; no game code ever addresses it in place]

Rebuild note:
The non-zero value has to be 2, not 1. It is both the 'disabled' flag and the cel frame variant, so spelling the array as booleans { 0, 1, 1, 0 } still greys out the right entries but draws them with the highlighted frame.

=== 0002af20 [PLATE]
Packs three colour channels into one 0x00RRGGBB colour word: the constructor counterpart of fdps_get_rgb_red, fdps_get_rgb_green and fdps_get_rgb_blue, which take that word apart again.

Algorithm:
Zero-extends the low byte of r and shifts it left 16, ORs in the low byte of g shifted left 8, ORs in the low byte of b unshifted, spills the word to a stack local and reloads it as the return value. Only the low byte of each argument contributes; anything above bit 7 of a channel is dropped, so the result never has bits above 23 set. There are no globals, no callees and no bounds or range checks.

Nothing in the image calls this function and no data word points at it, so it is unused game code the linker kept because the object defining it is linked whole. The packing it performs is the one fdps_build_palette_tables (0002af60) open-codes inline for each of the 256 palette entries it reads.

Parameters:
  r -- red channel, 0..255, taken from the low byte of the argument slot; lands in bits 16-23.
  g -- green channel, 0..255, low byte only; lands in bits 8-15.
  b -- blue channel, 0..255, low byte only; lands in bits 0-7.

Returns:
  The packed colour word (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b, in the same 0x00RRGGBB layout that fdps_get_rgb_red, fdps_get_rgb_green and fdps_get_rgb_blue decode.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID match in the Watcom 10.0x or ailv3 library sets, and it sits inside one game object's run of colour helpers alongside the three accessors and fdps_build_palette_tables]

=== 0002af54 [EOL]
alignment padding: two 6-byte lea NOP forms, aligns fdps_build_palette_tables at 0002af60

=== 0002af60 [PLATE]
Builds the game's palette lookup tables from a 256-entry VGA palette: packs each entry into a nibble-per-channel RGB word at 000657f0, scales that row by 16 brightness coefficients into 000653f0, and fills a 16x16x16 RGB-to-palette-index cube at 000643f0.
Pool: fdps  [no library match; game-owned globals and call graph]
Evidence: Called only by fdps_load_global_resources and calls fdps_palette_find_nearest_color plus three local component extractors (0002ae90/0002aec0/0002aef0); writes the game tables 000643f0, 000653f0 and 000657f0 and reads the 18-dword coefficient table at 0002ae40. Function ID finds no match in the Watcom or ail sets and the hash is unique in the image; no CRT or AIL entry point, no driver state, and far too large for a linker artifact.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case describing what the body builds; no vendor symbol involved.
Boundary: 0002af60-0002b1a3, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 to the matching MOV ESP,EBP/POP/RET epilogue; the 12 bytes after it are LEA-form alignment padding before fdps_palette_find_nearest_color at 0002b1b0.
Signature: __cdecl, void fdps_build_palette_tables(fdps_palette_entry *palette) -- the single argument is read from [EBP+0x14], the RET purges nothing, and the calls it makes clean up with ADD ESP,n.
Algorithm:
1. Copies the 18-dword brightness coefficient table at 0002ae40 onto the stack, indexed by shade level.
2. For each of the 256 palette entries: reads the three bytes (r,g,b) of the source palette (6-bit VGA components, scaled by 4 to 8 bits), packs them as r<<16|g<<8|b, then calls the three component extractors. Each result is masked with 0xF0 and repositioned so red lands in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11 and blue in bits 0-3. Row 0 of the ramp table (000653f0) is zeroed and the packed value is stored into row 1 (000657f0 = 000653f0 + 0x400).
3. For levels 2..17, each of the 256 row-1 values is multiplied by the level coefficient and stored at 000653f0[level*256 + index]. Because each channel occupies only the low nibble of its own byte, one multiply scales all three channels without carrying between them.
4. Fills the 16x16x16 inverse lookup cube at 000643f0: for every (r,g,b) triple of 4-bit components (passed as component*4) it calls fdps_palette_find_nearest_color with the source palette and stores the returned index as a byte, written sequentially over 4096 entries. The outer loop supplies target_green, the middle one target_red and the innermost one target_blue, so the cell for a quantised (r, g, b) is at green * 256 + red * 16 + blue.

Alignment padding: two 6-byte Watcom NOP forms (lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0]).

=== 0002b1b0 [PLATE]
Returns the index of the palette entry closest to a target colour, by minimum squared RGB distance over a 256-entry, 3-bytes-per-entry table.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in the image; called only by game graphics code]
Evidence: fid.watcom and fid.ail are both empty and same_hash_in_image is 1, so there is no library byte match. Its only reference is a static call from fdps_build_palette_tables@0002af60, which writes the returned index into the game's 16x16x16 colour lookup table at DAT_000643f0. Nearest-colour matching is not a CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 or Miles AIL service, and 202 bytes of real loop logic cannot be a linker thunk or merged epilogue.
Name: game code, so fdps_ + snake_case describing the algorithm; no vendor symbol claimed or available.
Boundary: 0002b1b0-0002b279, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the call target through the matching MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP,EDI,ESI,EBX / RET; no body holes, and the gap after 0002b27a is defined data with no instructions.
Signature: __cdecl, int (int r, int g, int b, uchar *palette). Arguments are read from [EBP+0x14/0x18/0x1c/0x20], RET takes no immediate, and the caller cleans with ADD ESP,0x10; result in EAX.
Algorithm: best distance seeded with 10000000 and best index with 0x100, then 256 fixed iterations over an advancing byte cursor forming dr = r - pal[0], dg = g - pal[1], db = b - pal[2] and dr*dr + dg*dg + db*db in signed 32-bit arithmetic. The strict less-than test makes the first of several equally close entries win. The palette buffer must therefore hold at least 768 bytes. The palette bytes are zero-extended but the target components are not masked, so the caller is responsible for keeping r/g/b in range; with in-range targets the 0x100 seed can never survive and the result is always 0..255.

=== 0002c220 [PLATE]
Builds the draw-order list for the scrolling scene layer table: the layer slot indices sorted by ascending depth key.

Algorithm:
Fills draw_order[0 .. data_fdps_scene_layer_count-1] with the identity permutation 0,1,2,..., where data_fdps_scene_layer_count is the number of active layer slots. Then bubble-sorts that index list in place: the outer index i runs while i < data_fdps_scene_layer_count-1, the inner index j while j < data_fdps_scene_layer_count-i-1, and each step compares the depth bytes data_fdps_scene_layer_draw_depth[draw_order[j]] and data_fdps_scene_layer_draw_depth[draw_order[j+1]] as unsigned and exchanges the two entries when the first is the greater. The result is ascending by depth. The sort is a bubble sort, so slots that share a depth value keep their slot-index order. There are no callees.

Parameters:
  draw_order -- out; base of an int array with room for at least data_fdps_scene_layer_count entries, receiving the layer slot indices in draw order. No bound is checked; fdps_draw_scene_layers passes a 6-element stack array, matching the 6-slot width of the layer table.

Returns:
  Nothing. The sorted list is the caller's array.

Pool: fdps  [hard-coded game globals data_fdps_scene_layer_count and data_fdps_scene_layer_draw_depth; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ail set, and the only caller is game rendering code]

Rebuild note:
The sort is a hand-written bubble sort and is therefore stable: scene layer slots that share the same depth byte at data_fdps_scene_layer_draw_depth stay in slot-index order, and fdps_draw_scene_layers blits them in exactly that order, so equal-depth layers overlap in a fixed way. Rewriting this as a call to qsort (unstable) would silently reorder equal-depth layers and change what covers what.

=== 0002c327 [EOL]

=== 0002c330 [PLATE]
Draws one layer of the scrolling scene: fills the visible 14x9 window of 24x24 map tiles into the scene buffer, animating the tiles the layer's attribute table marks and pulsing the tiles the movement grid has marked.

Algorithm:
Copies the 14-byte blend-level ramp at 0002b280 (02 03 04 05 06 07 07 07 06 05 04 03 02 02) onto the stack, advances tile_attr past its 0x11-byte header, and steps the highlight phase counter DAT_0006015c to (DAT_0006015c + 1) % 0x38 -- once per call, so once per layer rather than once per frame. If the global tick counter DAT_00069d64 has moved more than 3 ticks past the latch DAT_00060164, flips the two-frame animation phase DAT_00060160 with XOR 1 and re-latches the tick. Builds on the stack the four-dword blend descriptor that fdps_blit_dispatch modes 9 and 0x0a read: shade-ramp table 000653f0, blend level, inverse colour cube 000643f0, and the tint colour DAT_00060154.

Reads the layer's map size out of map_layer (tile width word at +7, tile height word at +9) and splits each pixel scroll offset into a whole tile count and a 0..23 remainder, decrementing the count and adding 24 to the remainder by hand when the offset is negative so the division floors. Then walks rows 0..8 and columns 0..13. The destination row base is scene_buf + (row * 24 + 24 - scroll_y remainder) * 0x168 + 24 - scroll_x remainder, so the window is inset 24 pixels into the 360-pixel-pitch buffer and each cell is blitted 24 pixels further right. Cell coordinates are wrapped into range modulo the map width and height (a negative remainder gets the dimension added back), giving cell = y * width + x, the signed 16-bit tile index at map_layer + 0xb + cell * 2 (sign-extended, MOVSX at 0002c4f9, like the width and height words at +7 and +9), and the tile's pixel stream at tileset + *(int *)(tileset + 0xf + tile * 4).

When layer_mode is 0 every tile is blitted opaque through fdps_blit_dispatch mode 0 and neither tile_attr nor move_grid is touched. Otherwise the flag byte tile_attr[tile * 4] decides the draw. Its low three bits pick the tile animation: 1 adds the phase DAT_00060160 (0 or 1) to the tile index, a two-frame animation; 2 adds ((DAT_00069d64 >> 2) & 3) * 0x60, a four-frame animation whose frames sit 0x60 tiles apart in the tileset; every other value leaves the tile index alone. Then, if bit 0x80 of the flag byte is set, the tile is drawn translucent (mode 9) at the fixed level in tile_attr[tile * 4 + 1]. If it is clear, byte 1 of the movement grid cell (move_grid + 4 + cell * 2 + 1) decides: 0xff, the value fdps_map_grid_reset writes into every cell, means the cell is unmarked and the tile is blitted opaque; any other value means the cell is marked and the tile is drawn blended at ramp[DAT_0006015c / 4] -- mode 0x0a for layer_mode 1, mode 9 for any other non-zero layer_mode -- so marked tiles pulse between blend levels 2 and 7 out of 16.

Parameters:
  scene_buf -- the 360x240 8bpp scene buffer being composited, from fdps_draw_scene_layers; every blit goes into it and nothing else is written through it.
  map_layer -- this layer's map image, DAT_00069cb0[slot]: tile width word at +7, tile height word at +9, then width * height 16-bit tile indices from +0xb.
  tileset -- this layer's tile graphic sheet, DAT_00069c20[slot]: a dword offset table at +0xf indexed by tile index, each entry the offset from the sheet base to that tile's 24x24 RLE stream.
  move_grid -- the battle map working grid DAT_00060144 (word width, word height, then width * height 2-byte cells). Only byte 1 of a cell is read, and the cell is picked with map_layer's dimensions rather than the grid's own header.
  scroll_x -- the layer's view origin in pixels along x, may be negative; the caller derives it from the layer's scroll accumulator and the global scroll factor.
  scroll_y -- the same along y.
  tile_attr -- this layer's per-tile attribute table, DAT_00069c98[slot]: 0x11 bytes of header, then 4 bytes per tile of which byte 0 is the flag byte and byte 1 the fixed blend level. Read only when layer_mode is non-zero, but advanced past the header on every call.
  layer_mode -- the layer's mode byte, DAT_00069cf8[slot]: 0 draws the layer opaque and ignores tile_attr and move_grid; 1 draws marked and translucent tiles tinted toward DAT_00060154; any other non-zero value blends them with what is already in the buffer instead.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image; its only caller and only callee are game draw code, and it owns the game's scene rendering globals]

Rebuild note:
The highlight phase counter DAT_0006015c is advanced at the top of this function, so it steps once per drawn layer, not once per frame: the pulse of the movement-range highlight runs faster on maps with more active scene layers. Writing the obvious thing -- advancing the counter once per frame beside the DAT_00060160 tile-animation phase, which really is tick-gated here -- changes the pulse rate and decouples it from the layer count.

=== 0002c694 [EOL]
Watcom 16-byte alignment padding: two 6-byte lea-form NOPs before FUN_0002c6a0.

=== 0002c6a0 [PLATE]
Draws the map cursor overlay into the scene buffer being composited: either the bare cursor tile, or the diamond-shaped footprint of an ability's area of effect centred on the cursor, whichever the cursor-mode global selects.

Algorithm:
Dispatches on the cursor mode at 00069cd0 with a chain of equality tests; every mode draws by calling fdps_blit_cursor_tile(map_x, map_y, sprite_index, dest) once per cell, at the cursor pixel position (x = 00069cd4, y = 00069ccc) displaced by whole tiles of 0x18 = 24 pixels. The call list is hand-unrolled, one call per cell, and fdps_blit_cursor_tile itself drops any cell that falls outside the visible viewport.
  mode 1 -- the cursor tile alone, sprite 0.
  mode 2 -- the cursor tile alone, sprite 1.
  mode 3 -- radius-1 diamond: sprite 0x0e on the centre, sprites 2/3/4/5 on the tiles above/left/right/below.
  mode 4 -- radius-2 diamond, all 13 tiles: sprite 1 on the centre, 2/3/4/5 on the four tips two tiles out, 6/7/8/9 on the four diagonal tiles, a/b/c/d on the four tiles one out.
  mode 5 -- radius-3 diamond: sprite 1 on the centre, 2/3/4/5 on the four tips three tiles out, 6/7/8/9 each used twice for the eight (1,2)- and (2,1)-offset tiles of that outer ring, a/b/c/d on the four tips two tiles out, and 0x0e/0x0f on the two upper diagonal tiles with 0x11/0x10 on the lower-left and lower-right ones -- that last pair emitted out of numeric order. The four tiles orthogonally adjacent to the centre get no call at all.
  mode 6 -- draws nothing. It divides both cursor coordinates by 0x18 to get a tile position, indexes the battle grid whose base pointer is DAT_00060144 (word width, word height, then width*height 2-byte cells) as base + 4 + ((y/0x18) * width + x/0x18) * 2, and clears byte 1 of that cell -- the byte fdps_map_grid_reset fills with 0xff and fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles reads to decide a cell is marked. fdps_map_cursor_move_to renders a frame at every step of a cursor move while the mode is non-zero, so this marks every tile the cursor travels across.
Mode 0, and any value above 6, falls through to the epilogue having done nothing. The mode is 0 while the cursor is hidden and 1 for the plain cursor almost everywhere in the game; the ability code sets it to the ability's area-of-effect code plus 2 -- spell record byte +4 at 00013d32 and 00027db5, item record byte +0x12 at 00025461 -- and 00027356 sets 6 just before it scrolls the cursor across the map.

Parameters:
  dest -- the scrolling scene buffer being composited this frame, 0x168 bytes per row; fdps_draw_scene_layers hands over its own buffer and it is passed straight through to fdps_blit_cursor_tile.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game globals and game state]

Rebuild note:
The six shapes are hand-unrolled call lists, not loops, and they are not the shapes a loop would produce: mode 5 skips the four tiles orthogonally adjacent to the centre, and its lower two diagonal cells take sprites 0x11 (left) and 0x10 (right) in that order, so rewriting the dispatch as a loop over a diamond, or assuming the sprite ids run in reading order, changes what appears on screen. Mode 6 is a second trap: this draw routine, called from the frame compositor, draws nothing and instead clears the marked-cell byte of the battle grid at DAT_00060144 for the tile under the cursor, so hoisting that branch out of the renderer -- or rendering a different number of frames during a cursor move -- silently changes which tiles end up marked.

=== 0002cc17 [EOL]
Watcom inter-function alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] + lea edx,[edx+0]

=== 0002cc20 [PLATE]
Draws one 24x24 sprite of the global Cusor.cel overlay sheet into the scrolling scene buffer at a map pixel position, skipping the draw entirely when that position is outside the visible viewport.

Algorithm:
Clips first and does nothing else if the clip rejects: the position must satisfy DAT_00069ce4 <= map_x < DAT_00069ce4 + 0x138 and DAT_00069ce0 <= map_y < DAT_00069ce0 + 0xc0. DAT_00069ce4 and DAT_00069ce0 are the viewport origin in map pixels, the pair fdps_battle_player_phase_loop scrolls in 0x18-pixel steps, and 0x138 x 0xc0 is the 312x192 visible window. Converts the accepted position to a scene-buffer offset as ((map_y - DAT_00069ce0) + 0x18) * 0x168 + (map_x - DAT_00069ce4) + 0x18: the scene buffer that fdps_draw_scene_layers composites is 0x168 (360) bytes per row and carries a 0x18 (24) pixel border on all four sides, so the visible window starts at pixel (24, 24). Resolves the source pixels out of the Cusor.cel image whose pointer fdps_load_global_resources leaves in DAT_000643b8, through the CEL sprite offset table of dwords at cel + 0x0f: src = cel + *(int *)(cel + sprite_index * 4 + 0xf). Passes the two pointers to fdps_blit_dispatch with width 0x18, height 0x18, pitch 0x168 and mode 0, which selects fdps_blit_rle_passthrough; transparency is structural in that kernel, an opcode that advances the destination pointer without writing, so the sheet's uncovered pixels leave whatever the map layers already put there and no colour index is treated as a key.

Cusor.cel is not a set of eighteen cursor pictures but one box-outline kit of 24x24 pieces, which is what lets the caller assemble an arbitrary tile region's outline one cell at a time: sprite 0 is a closed box and sprite 1 the same box with a gap in the middle of each side (the two cursor styles); 2, 3, 4, 5 are the box missing its bottom, right, left, top side, the caps that go on the tips of a run; 6, 7, 8, 9 are the two-sided corner pieces top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right; 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0d are pairs of 3x3 corner nubs (the two top corners, the two left, the two right, the two bottom) that close the concave joints of a stepped outline; 0x0e, 0x0f, 0x10, 0x11 are those nubs singly, top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. The sheet's last two sprites, 0x12 and 0x13, are blank and unreferenced.

Parameters:
  map_x -- horizontal position in map pixels, a multiple of 24, in the same space as the viewport origin DAT_00069ce4. fdps_draw_map_cursor forms it from the cursor X global DAT_00069cd4 plus or minus multiples of 0x18.
  map_y -- vertical position in map pixels, same space and stride, from the cursor Y global DAT_00069ccc.
  sprite_index -- which piece of the kit above to draw, 0 through 0x11. Not bounds checked.
  dest -- the 360x240 scene buffer being composited, handed down from fdps_draw_scene_layers through fdps_draw_map_cursor.

Returns:
  Nothing. There is no failure path; an off-screen position is simply not drawn.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the watcom or the ail set and the body hash is unique in the image; its only callee is fdps_blit_dispatch and its only caller is game rendering code]

Rebuild note:
The viewport test compares only the tile's top-left corner against the 312x192 window, but the blit unconditionally writes a full 24x24 block at a 360-byte pitch, so a tile accepted at the right or bottom edge writes up to 23 pixels into the scene buffer's 24-pixel border margin -- the margin is what makes that safe (max column 0x137+0x18+23 = 358 of 360, max row 0xbf+0x18+23 = 238 of 240), and it is also why cursor tiles vanish whole rather than clipping as they leave the view. Writing the obvious thing (adding extent-based partial clipping, or compositing into a tight 312x192 buffer) both changes what the player sees at the map edges and can run past the end of the destination.

=== 0002ccd0 [PLATE]
Chooses which status-effect icon to show over one battle-map unit this cycle, or reports that the unit has none.

Algorithm:
Copies the 5-byte field-offset table at 0002b28e -- 0x23, 0x22, 0x24, 0x25, 0x27, the unit record's status-effect timer bytes in icon order -- onto the stack, and forms the record pointer as [00069cd8] + unit_index * 0x50. First pass: walks the five offsets and counts how many of those record bytes are non-zero; if none are, returns -1 at once. Second pass: replaces cycle with (cycle % count) + 1, walks the same five offsets again and decrements that counter at every non-zero byte, returning the table slot whose byte drives it to zero; if the walk ends without reaching zero it returns -1. Selecting modulo the number of active effects is what makes an advancing cycle rotate through the effects a unit is carrying. The unit record's sixth status timer, +0x26, has no entry in the table and is never shown.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at 00069cd8; fdps_draw_map_unit passes the unit it is drawing. Not range-checked.
  cycle -- rotation counter, reduced modulo the number of active effects to pick one of them. fdps_draw_map_unit passes the global at 00060168, which it advances once every 25 unit-draw ticks. The modulo is signed, so a negative cycle yields -1 unless the remainder happens to be 0.

Returns:
  0..4 -- the slot of the effect to show, i.e. record offsets 0x23, 0x22, 0x24, 0x25 and 0x27 respectively. fdps_draw_map_unit uses it directly as the frame index into the IconSts.cel sheet held at 000643d4 and blits a 0x18 x 0x0b strip 13 scanlines below the unit's cell.
  -1 -- the unit carries no active status effect, so no icon is drawn.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; game global array with 0x50-byte stride]

Rebuild note:
The five status timers are visited in the order 0x23, 0x22, 0x24, 0x25, 0x27: the first two are swapped relative to the record layout, and the sixth timer at +0x26 is deliberately absent. Writing the obvious loop over offsets 0x22..0x27 swaps two icons on the map and invents a sixth frame index that IconSts.cel does not have.

=== 0002cd9e [EOL]
Alignment padding: 8b c0 (mov eax,eax), 2-byte no-op aligning next function to 0002cda0.

=== 0002cda0 [PLATE]
Draws one unit of the battle map into the scene buffer -- either its shadow or its sprite, depending on which pass fdps_draw_map_units is running -- and steps the map's shared walk-animation clock on the way past.

Algorithm:
Whenever the frame tick DAT_00069d64 differs from the value latched in DAT_00069d18, the routine latches it and steps two counters it owns outright: the walk counter DAT_00069cc8 modulo 0x10 and the icon counter DAT_00069d1c modulo 0x19, and every time the second wraps to 0 it bumps the icon cycle DAT_00060168. The latch is what keeps this to once per tick even though fdps_draw_map_units calls the routine twice for every unit on the map.

It then forms the unit record as DAT_00069cd8 + unit_index * 0x50 and reads the portrait id at +7; 0x80 marks a record with no map sprite and returns at once. Tile position comes from the bytes at +0 and +1 multiplied by 0x18, facing from +3, the sub-tile step counter from +4 and the status byte from +5, whose bit 0 is the retired flag -- a retired unit draws nothing. Facing 0/1/2/3 selects a per-step displacement of (0,+4)/(-4,0)/(0,-4)/(+4,0), multiplied by the step counter and added to the tile position, so a unit walking between tiles is drawn 4 pixels along for each of the six steps that make up a tile; y additionally takes a fixed -6, because the sprites stand taller than their 24-pixel tile.

The walk frame is DAT_00069cc8 / 4 with 3 folded back to 1, so the three sprites of a facing play 0, 1, 2, 1. A unit carrying the paralysis counter at record +0x26 is pinned to frame 0 and displaced by DAT_00069cc8 % 2 pixels in x instead, which makes it shiver in place.

Nothing is drawn unless DAT_00069ce4 - 0x18 < x < DAT_00069ce4 + 0x138, the camera's horizontal window. The destination pointer is dest_base_offset + (y - DAT_00069ce0 + 0x18) * 0x168 + (x - DAT_00069ce4 + 0x18): pitch 0x168, with a one-tile border on both axes.

With the pass byte DAT_0006014c set, fdps_draw_map_units is in its shadow pass. The vertical window is DAT_00069ce0 - 0x1a < y < DAT_00069ce0 + 0xbe, two pixels lower than the sprite pass because the shadow is laid down two scanlines below the cell (dst + 0x2d0). Portrait ids 0x8e, 0x69, 0x6a, 0x24-0x27 and 0x3c-0x3e cast no shadow and return here. The shadow sprite comes from the global Shadow.cel sheet at DAT_000643dc through the standard CEL offset table at +0x0f, indexed by the walk frame -- or fixed at sprite 1 when status bit 0x80 says the unit has already acted this turn. Either way it goes down through fdps_blit_dispatch mode 9 (translucent) with the blend descriptor { shade ramps at 0x000653f0, level 0xa, inverse colour cube at 0x000643f0 }.

With the pass byte clear it is the sprite pass, windowed at DAT_00069ce0 - 0x18 < y < DAT_00069ce0 + 0xc0. The sprite index is record[2] * 0xc + facing * 3 + frame: record +2 holds the unit's slot in the sprite cache at DAT_00060138, which fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group filled from the portrait id, twelve sprites to a slot as four facings of three frames, and the cache's own offset table starts at its base rather than at +0x0f. A unit that has already acted (status bit 0x80) is drawn at frame 1 through mode 11, alpha-blended half-way into palette colour 0 with the descriptor's level set to 8, so it reads as greyed out; portrait ids 0x69, 0x6a and 0x24-0x27 go through mode 9 at level 7, so they read as semi-transparent; everything else is an opaque mode 0 blit. Then fdps_unit_select_status_icon(unit_index, DAT_00060168) picks an ailment icon, and any answer other than -1 blits a 0x18 by 0x0b strip out of the global IconSts.cel sheet at DAT_000643d4, 13 scanlines below the top of the unit's cell.

Every sprite blit is 0x18 by 0x18 at pitch 0x168; only the status icon is smaller.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8, 0 .. DAT_00060150 - 1. fdps_draw_map_units passes every live index in turn, once per pass; fdps_render_ring_menu_frame passes the single unit standing under the map cursor.
  dest_base_offset -- base address of the destination surface, pitch 0x168. fdps_draw_map_units forwards the scene buffer it was handed; fdps_render_ring_menu_frame passes its own 360x240 page.
  flag -- overwritten with 0 at 0002cdba before any read, so no value passed here can be observed. fdps_draw_map_units forwards its own second argument, fdps_render_ring_menu_frame passes 0.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set and a hash unique in the image; its whole state is game globals and the game's 0x50-byte unit record, and every callee is game code]

Rebuild note:
The map's walk-animation clock lives inside this per-unit draw: DAT_00069cc8, DAT_00069d1c and DAT_00060168 are stepped here and nowhere else in the program, and only when the frame tick DAT_00069d64 has moved since the previous call (the latch is DAT_00069d18). Writing the obvious thing -- stepping the counter at the top of the function without the tick latch, or hoisting the step out into the frame loop -- runs the walk cycle at twice the unit count per frame, or stops it on the frames where only fdps_render_ring_menu_frame draws. Separately, the two passes clip against vertical windows two pixels apart (DAT_00069ce0-0x18 .. +0xc0 for the sprite, -0x1a .. +0xbe for the shadow, which is blitted two scanlines lower); folding them into one shared test makes shadows appear and disappear a row early or late along the top and bottom edges of the view.

=== 0002d240 [PLATE]
Draws every unit on the map into the scene buffer, all the shadows first and then the unit sprites.

Algorithm:
Walks the unit table twice, each pass running index 0 up to the live unit count in DAT_00060150 and calling fdps_draw_map_unit(index, dest_base_offset, flag), which draws one unit out of the 0x50-byte record array based at DAT_00069cd8. Which of the two things fdps_draw_map_unit draws is selected by the pass byte DAT_0006014c, which this function is the only writer of and fdps_draw_map_unit the only reader of. The first pass sets it to 1, so fdps_draw_map_unit blits the unit's shadow from the global Shadow.cel sheet at DAT_000643dc, translucently and two scanlines below the unit's cell. The second pass clears it to 0, so fdps_draw_map_unit blits the unit's own 0x18 by 0x18 sprite from the map sprite sheet at DAT_00060138 and, above it, whatever status icon fdps_unit_select_status_icon picks. Both arguments are forwarded unchanged on every call. The pass byte is left at 0 on the way out.

Splitting the work this way is what keeps a unit drawn later in the table from casting its shadow over a unit drawn earlier: every shadow is on the surface before the first sprite goes down.

Parameters:
  dest_base_offset -- base address of the destination scene buffer, whose pitch is 0x168 bytes; forwarded to fdps_draw_map_unit, which turns it into a per-unit destination pointer. The only caller, fdps_draw_scene_layers, passes the buffer it was handed.
  flag -- forwarded as fdps_draw_map_unit's third argument; only its low byte is read. The only caller passes 0, and fdps_draw_map_unit overwrites that argument with 0 before ever reading it, so nothing passed here has any effect.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ail set; its whole state is two game globals and its only callee is game code]

Rebuild note:
The two sweeps must stay separate sweeps. Collapsing them into one loop that draws each unit's shadow and sprite together -- the obvious simplification, since the pass byte is only read inside the callee -- lets a unit further down the table drop its translucent shadow on top of a unit already drawn, which the original never does because every shadow is blitted before the first sprite.

=== 0002d353 [EOL]

=== 0002d360 [PLATE]
Walks one battle-map unit one tile down the screen, playing the six-step walk animation and scrolling the view to keep up.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit's 0x50-byte record as DAT_00069cd8 + unit_index * 0x50, then takes two pixel measurements before it starts: the map's full height, from the tile-height word at [DAT_00069cb0]+9 times 0x18, and the unit's starting pixel row, from its tile y at record+1 times 0x18. Writes 0 into the facing byte at record+3 -- the code fdps_unit_face_target uses for facing down. Then runs six passes with the walk sub-step counter at record+4 holding 1..6; six passes of 4 pixels make one 0x18-pixel tile. Each pass scrolls the view down by 4 (DAT_00069ce0) while the unit is more than 0x78 pixels below the top of the view and the view has not yet hit the bottom of the map (map height in pixels minus the 0xc0-pixel view height), advances the map cursor pixel row DAT_00069ccc by 4, and calls fdps_render_view_frame unless the scancode latch that fdps_keyboard_scancode_ptr points at holds 2 or 3, the two keys that fast-forward movement. After the loop it draws one catch-up frame if the latch holds 2 -- but not if it holds 3, which skips drawing entirely. It then commits the move by incrementing the tile y at record+1, clears record+4, and reports the arrival tile to fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event as (DAT_00069cd4 / 0x18, DAT_00069ccc / 0x18, 0), so a scripted chapter event sitting on that tile is queued for the battle loop.

One of the four per-direction step routines fdps_animate_move_path dispatches to; the others are fdps_animate_move_step_up (0002d480), 0002d590 (direction 1, -x) and 0002d6a0 (direction 3, +x).

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; fdps_animate_move_path passes its own unit_index through unchanged.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no fid candidate in either library; called only by fdps_animate_move_path]

Rebuild note:
Two places where the obvious rewrite is not what the original does. === 0002d480 [PLATE]
Walks one battle-map unit one tile up the screen, playing the six-step walk animation and scrolling the view to keep up.

Algorithm:
Resolves the unit's 0x50-byte record as DAT_00069cd8 + unit_index * 0x50, and reads the unit's starting pixel row once, before anything moves, as the tile y at record+1 times 0x18. Writes 2 into the facing byte at record+3 -- the code fdps_unit_face_target uses for facing up, and the one fdps_draw_map_unit turns into a per-step displacement of (0, -4). Then runs six passes with the walk sub-step counter at record+4 holding 1..6; six passes of 4 pixels make one 0x18-pixel tile. Each pass scrolls the view up by 4 (the scroll-y global DAT_00069ce0) while that starting row sits less than 0x30 pixels -- two tiles -- below the view's top edge and the view has not reached row 0; moves the map cursor pixel row DAT_00069ccc back by 4, which is the moving unit's own on-screen position; and calls fdps_render_view_frame unless the scancode latch that fdps_keyboard_scancode_ptr points at holds 2 or 3, the two keys that fast-forward movement. After the loop it draws one catch-up frame if the latch holds 2 -- but not if it holds 3, which skips drawing entirely. It then commits the move by decrementing the tile y at record+1, clears record+4, and reports the arrival tile to fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event as (DAT_00069cd4 / 0x18, DAT_00069ccc / 0x18, 0), so a scripted chapter event sitting on that tile is queued for the battle loop. Like the leftward step at 0002d590 and unlike the downward one at 0002d360, this direction needs no map extent to clamp against: running off the top edge is stopped by the DAT_00069ce0 >= 4 test alone.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at DAT_00069cd8; fdps_animate_move_path passes its own unit_index through unchanged.

Returns:
  Nothing; EAX is not loaded before the epilogue.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, unique hash in the image; indexes the game's own 0x50-byte unit records and shares the map cursor and viewport globals with the rest of the map code]

Rebuild note:

=== 0002dc20 [PLATE]
Finds the battle unit standing on the map for a given character id, handing back both its index in the unit array and a pointer to its record.

Algorithm:

The roster fallback at 0002dc95-0002dcd5 is dead code and must stay dead. Its guard at 0002dc8f compares the out_record pointer with 0, but out_record was already dereferenced at 0002dc34, so a null pointer would have faulted long before; the intent was plainly *out_record == 0 (no unit found). === 0002df90 [PLATE]
Moves the battle unit-record array to a fresh, randomly displaced heap address and erases the copy left behind, so nothing outside the game can keep a fixed address on the unit records.

Algorithm:
1. Calls rand() and mallocs (rand() % 0x400) + 1 bytes as a scratch block, which it holds for the rest of the routine. The remainder is taken with a signed IDIV by 0x400 after SAR EDX,0x1f, so over the 0..0x7fff that rand() returns the scratch size is 1..0x400.
2. Reads the unit count at 0x00060150 and mallocs (count + 1) * 0x50 bytes -- one 0x50-byte unit record more than the live array. The scratch block is still held, so this allocation lands a random distance away from wherever the old one sat.
3. memmove(new_block, DAT_00069cd8, (count + 1) * 0x50): the full length of the NEW block, not the length of the source.
4. memset(DAT_00069cd8, 0, count * 0x50), wiping the old array before it goes back to the heap.
5. free(DAT_00069cd8), then free(scratch).
6. Publishes the new block in DAT_00069cd8. The count at 0x00060150 is never written, so the array does not gain an entry: this is a move, not a resize.

The two mechanisms only make sense together -- holding a randomly sized block across the allocation moves the array on every call, and zeroing the old storage destroys the stale copy that would otherwise survive in the freed block. fdps_battle_unit_turn, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase and fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase all call it at the top of each unit iteration and immediately re-resolve their record pointer through fdps_get_unit_record, so the array never sits at one address for long.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX still holds the new block pointer at the RET, but the address is published through DAT_00069cd8 and every call site overwrites EAX on the next instruction.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library and the body hash is unique in the image; the whole body is bookkeeping over two FDPS globals -- the unit count at 0x00060150 and the unit array pointer at 0x00069cd8 -- with the game's hard-coded 0x50-byte record stride, consuming malloc/memmove/memset/free/rand as a stack-convention client]

Rebuild note:
The copy length and the wipe length deliberately disagree by one record, and neither may be "corrected". When fdps_deploy_unit or fdps_build_map_unit_array sized the old block last it is exactly count * 0x50 bytes, so the memmove reads 0x50 bytes past the end of that allocation and fills the spare tail slot with heap garbage; after fdps_load_savegame the block is instead a flat 0x1e00 bytes, which is 96 records, so the over-read stays inside it for any saved count below 96; when this routine itself sized it, the old block is (count + 1) * 0x50 and the memset leaves its final record unzeroed. Writing memmove(new, old, count * 0x50) or memset over the whole allocation is the obvious C and is a behaviour change. Callers must also re-read every unit record pointer after this call: a pointer held across it points into freed, zeroed memory.

Reports that a unit is on a map tile and, if that tile carries a scripted chapter event that fires on the reported occasion, leaves the event's handler index in the battle loop's pending-event slot.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y), which republishes the cell's terrain attribute byte in the global at 0x00069d08 and the cell's event code in the word at 0x00069d06. Returns without doing anything more unless both gates pass: bits 0x60 of the attribute byte must be clear -- a cell whose 0x60 field holds 0x20 or 0x40 is a searchable cell, investigated from the action menu by FUN_000184f0 through a different table, and 0x60 is excluded there too -- and the event code must be non-zero, code 0 meaning the cell carries no event. Otherwise it reads the cell's 2-byte entry out of the tile-event table of the chapter script image "map%02d.dat", whose base pointer is the global at 0x0006013c (filled by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources from "Field.vfs"). The entry address is formed as base + code * 2 + 0x31, that is, the table beginning at image offset 0x33 indexed by code - 1; offset 0x33 is where the 16 three-byte turn-event records that fdps_battle_run_turn_events walks end, and 0x33 + 16 * 2 = 0x53 is where the searchable-cell table FUN_000184f0 uses begins. Byte [0] of the entry is the event's index into the chapter-event handler pointer table at 0x000601c4, with 0xff meaning the cell has no handler; byte [1] is the occasion the entry fires on. When byte [0] is not 0xff and byte [1] equals trigger_kind, byte [0] is stored into the pending-event global at 0x00069d90. No other global is written and no handler is called here: the slot is seeded with 0xff by the four turn drivers -- fdps_battle_system_menu (00014ceb), fdps_battle_unit_turn (000154f4), fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase (000129a9 and 00012a8e) and fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase (00012b73) -- before a unit is let act, and read back by those same four (CMP against 0xff at 00014d0b, 0001581c, 00012a16, 00012acd, 00012bb9) to dispatch 0x000601c4[pending](unit_index). This function's own callers do not seed it: none of fdps_map_actor_behavior_step or the four walk-step animations touches 0x00069d90 at all.

Parameters:
  x -- tile column of the cell the unit is on, 0-based, forwarded unchanged to fdps_map_load_tile_info. Comes either from the map cursor pixel global 0x00069cd4 divided by 24 (the walk animations at 0002d360/0002d480/0002d590/0002d6a0) or from byte 0 of the unit's 0x50-byte record (fdps_map_actor_behavior_step, fdps_battle_unit_turn).
  y -- tile row, same two sources: 0x00069ccc divided by 24, or byte 1 of the unit record.
  trigger_kind -- which occasion is being reported, matched against byte [1] of the tile's event entry. 0 is passed as a unit finishes stepping onto the tile during movement; 1 is passed when a unit ends its turn on the tile, immediately after fdps_battle_mark_unit_done. No other value is passed anywhere in the image.

Returns:
  Nothing. The result is the handler index left in the pending-event global at 0x00069d90, which the caller dispatches through the table at 0x000601c4.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only callee is the game function fdps_map_load_tile_info and all six callers are game code]

=== 0002e0c0 [PLATE]
Runs the chapter script's turn-scheduled events for one side's phase of the current battle turn.

Algorithm:
Walks all 16 entries of the fixed turn-event table that starts at offset 3 of the chapter script image "map%02d.dat", whose base pointer is the global at 0x0006013c (loaded by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources; bytes 1 and 2 of that image are a header the loader publishes elsewhere). Each entry is 3 bytes: [0] the turn number the event is scheduled for, [1] the index of its handler, [2] the side whose phase fires it. An entry fires when [0] equals the battle turn counter at 0x00069ce8 -- set to 1 by fdps_chapter_state_reset and bumped once per turn cycle by fdps_battle_advance_turn -- and [2] equals the side argument. Firing loads the handler pointer from the chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4 indexed by [1] (index scaled by 4, unchecked) and calls it with a literal 0 as its argument; that is the same handler table the AI phase loops and fdps_battle_unit_turn call through with a unit index. The scan does not stop at the first match, so every entry carrying the same turn and side fires, in table order. The function writes no global and returns nothing.

Parameters:
  side -- the side whose phase is about to run, in the encoding of unit record byte 0x6: 0 enemy, 1 friendly NPC, 2 player. fdps_battle_advance_turn passes 1 ahead of the NPC pass, 0 ahead of the enemy pass, and 2 as it opens the next player phase.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game globals and game-only callers]

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; reads battle globals and calls game code]

Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code, descriptive; no library symbol is involved.
Boundary: 0002e160-0002e5d5, Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the entry and the matching 89 ec 5d 5f 5e 5b c3 at the end; the 10 bytes after it are lea-based alignment padding, and the next function begins at 0002e5e0.
Signature: __cdecl, no parameters, no return value - it reads nothing from the stack or from incoming registers, and its caller adjusts no stack and discards EAX.

Algorithm:
1. Allocates a 64000-byte (320x200) off-screen frame buffer and a 0x4000-byte array of 64x64 tile-graphic pointers, and calls fdps_cel_expand_sheet_24x24 for the shared tile source.
2. Marker scale defaults to 4 px per tile (virtual width 0x280); maps taller than 40 tiles drop to 3 px per tile (virtual width 0x380).
3. Fills the pointer array: for each tile (x,y) calls fdps_map_load_tile_info, then takes the resulting tile index from DAT_00069d04 and stores tilesrc + 6 + index * 0x240 (24*24 bytes per tile).
4. Plays a 7-step zoom animation: each step interpolates the source rect and scale between the camera view and the full map, calls fdps_render_map_overview_scaled into the off-screen buffer and copies 64000 bytes to 0xa0000.
5. Flushes the keyboard (000567b3) then loops on 000567be until it returns a value <= 0x7f. Each time the frame counter DAT_00069d64 has moved by two or more, or has moved backwards, it redraws all DAT_00060150 units from the array at DAT_00069cd8: units with bit 0 of byte +5 set are skipped; bytes +0 / +1 are tile x / y and byte +6 selects a colour base from the three-dword table copied from 0002b294. Each marker is drawn by 0002e5e0 at (0xa0 + x*scale - width*scale/2, 0x64 + y*scale - height*scale/2). The map cursor (DAT_00069ccc / DAT_00069cd4 divided by 24) is drawn last with colour base 0x82. A shared brightness offset ping-pongs between 0 and 7 each frame, making every marker pulse.
6. Plays the reverse 6-step animation and frees the frame buffer, the pointer array and the tile source.
