Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_get_unit_record and read-modify-writes the packed nibble field of the game's own unit record, paints the chapter's text bank onto the VGA screen, and is reached only through a game-owned dispatch table; no Function ID candidate in the Watcom or ailv3.lib sets and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
The write is rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, not rec[0x34] = 0. Writing the obvious "reset the behaviour mode" as a plain store also wipes bits 0x40 and 0x80 of the same byte, which are separate per-unit flags that fdps_map_actor_take_best_action (00012c6f) and fdps_score_targets_for_item (0001337d) test, and the twenty released units would take a different AI path afterwards. The loop bound is inclusive as well -- i <= 0x2d -- so a rewrite using i < 0x2d silently leaves unit 0x2d holding position.

=== 0003922d [EOL]
Alignment padding: 3-byte lea eax,[eax+0x0] NOP form aligning 00039230 to 16 bytes.

=== 00039230 [PLATE]
Chapter 26's mid-map ambush trigger: the first time a player-side unit walks onto the marked tile, the map's enemy reinforcements and its allied relief force both come onto the battlefield and the tower garrison stops holding position and charges the party.

Algorithm:
Resolves the acting unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and does nothing at all unless the one-shot guard byte DAT_000640e8 is still 0 and that record's side byte at +6 is 2. Side 2 is the player, 0 the enemy and 1 the allied/neutral side, so an enemy or an ally crossing the same tile changes nothing. When both gates pass it runs, in this order:
  1. FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 2, 0) -- deploys every deployment record of the current map whose wave byte (record offset +0x15) equals 2. In map25.dat those are records 73..79: seven side-0 enemies, the wave whose death script is fdps_chapter_26_event_wave_2_defeated_line.
  2. FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0xa, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) -- paints line 10 of the chapter text image (fdetxt26.txt, held at DAT_00060124) straight onto the visible mode-13h screen at 0xa0000, 320 bytes per row.
  3. Clears the map-cursor mode DAT_00069cd0 to 0 so fdps_draw_map_cursor draws nothing, pans the view with fdps_map_cursor_move_to(0xf0, 0x378) -- pixel (240, 888), which at 0x18 pixels per tile is tile column 10, row 37, the bottom of the map where both waves arrive -- then calls fdps_render_view_frame twelve times to hold that view, and restores the cursor mode to 1.
  4. Paints line 11, then FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 3, 0) deploys the wave-3 records -- in map25.dat records 62..66, five side-1 allied units, the guide's 英雄索爾 and his four 侍衛 -- then paints line 12.
  5. Walks unit indices 0x0c through 0x4f inclusive and stores (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0 back into each record's byte 0x34. The low nibble of +0x34 is the AI behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on: the garrison carries mode 2 from the scenario file, which only strikes what is already in reach and never leaves its tile, while mode 0 also advances along a traced path and closes on the nearest opposing unit. The four high bits are separate flags and are preserved. Unit indices 0x0c..0x4f are the map's 68 wave-0 deployment records exactly -- the tower garrison -- and unit indices 0x50..0x5b are the twelve units this handler has just appended, seven wave-2 enemies followed by five wave-3 allies, all of which keep the behaviour mode their deployment records gave them. So the sweep releases the garrison alone; neither the enemy wave nor the allied relief force starts moving with it.
  6. Sets DAT_000640e8 to 1, so the whole sequence runs at most once. fdps_chapter_state_reset memsets the 0x20-byte block at 0x000640d8, which is what clears this flag when the chapter is entered again.

The entry is never called by name. Its address is the pointer at 0x00060268, slot 41 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the shipped data the only thing that selects slot 41 is the tile-event table of map25.dat -- map 25, chapter 26 -- whose entry for cell event code 1, the two bytes at file offset 0x33, is {slot 41, occasion 0}. fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event arms DAT_00069d90 with that slot when the cell a unit occupies carries a non-zero event code and the entry's second byte equals its own trigger_kind argument; the single-tile movement steppers pass 0 while the end-of-turn callers pass 1, so this fires as a unit walks across the tile rather than when it stops on it. The turn driver then calls the armed handler with the index of the unit that just moved, through PUSH index / CALL [0x601c4 + slot*4] / ADD ESP,4.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit whose movement armed the trigger, 0x00..0x5b on this map (0x00..0x0b are the twelve party slots, 0x0c upward the map's 80 deployment records). Read from [EBP+0x14], passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record, and only the side byte of that record is looked at. The frame slot holding it is reused as the 0..11 counter of the twelve-frame hold afterwards.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; every callee and every global is game code, and its only reference is a slot of the game's own chapter-event handler table at 0x000601c4]

Rebuild note:
Update the behaviour byte as rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0, never as rec[0x34] = 0. The OR operand is the constant 0, so the whole store looks like a plain zeroing, but bits 0x40 and 0x80 of that byte are independent unit flags that other map-AI code reads; clearing them changes how those units behave. The release range is likewise 0x0c..0x4f inclusive, not "every deployed unit": units 0x50..0x5b are meant to go on holding position.

=== 000393aa [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte NOP form lea eax,[eax+0x0] aligning FUN_000393b0 to 16 bytes.

=== 000393b0 [PLATE]
Chapter 26's wave-2 wipe line: the death script of the seven enemy reinforcements the chapter's tile trigger brings on runs it, and once the last of them is gone it paints the guest hero's line onto the screen and latches itself off.

Algorithm:
Clears its local flag, then falls straight through to the epilogue if the one-shot latch DAT_000640ea is already non-zero. Otherwise it runs i = 0 .. 6, calling fdps_unit_is_retired(0x50 + i) on each, and raises the flag as soon as one of those seven units answers 0. If the flag is still 0 -- every one of the seven is retired -- it calls fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0x17, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d), which walks message 0x17 of the chapter's text image and paints it straight onto the mode-13h screen at 0xa0000 with a 0x140-byte pitch; 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the foreground, background and outline colours it forwards unchanged to fdps_draw_glyph. It then stores 1 into DAT_000640ea so the line is drawn once. DAT_00060124 is the "fdetxt%02d.txt" entry fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads out of Field.vfs at 0002286f-00022894 for the chapter index DAT_00069cf4 plus one, here fdetxt26.txt. The incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] is overwritten with 0 at 000393cc and reused as the loop counter; the value the dispatcher pushed is never read.

Unit indices 0x50 .. 0x56 are the chapter's seven wave-2 enemy reinforcements. fdps_build_map_unit_array opens the battle with DAT_00064118 player slots -- map25.dat header byte 1, which is 12 -- at 0x00 .. 0x0b, then lays the map's 68 wave-0 records into 0x0c .. 0x4f; when a player-side unit walks across the map's trigger tile, fdps_chapter_26_event_deploy_waves_2_and_3 calls fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, 2, 0), which appends map25.dat's seven wave-2 records (records 73 .. 79, enemy id 0x64, level 0x12) at 0x50 .. 0x56, and only afterwards brings the five allied wave-3 records on behind them at 0x57 .. 0x5b. 12 + 68 + 7 + 5 is the map's whole complement, and 0x50 .. 0x56 is exactly the range this body polls.

Those same seven records carry the death script 02 2a 00 at record + 0x16, and that is what reaches this entry. fdps_run_death_scripts walks the 3-byte scripts fdps_collect_death_scripts copied out of the units a battle action has just killed, and its opcode 2 calls table[operand] through 0x000601c4 at 0001dcae with operand 42.

The all-retired test can only ever succeed because of the order fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack runs the three steps in: fdps_collect_death_scripts at 00012fde takes the script of every unit at 0 HP whose retired bit is still clear, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead at 00012fe9 then stores 1 into record + 5 of each of them, and only then does fdps_run_death_scripts at 00012ffc dispatch the collected scripts. So the seventh unit already reads as retired on the pass that kills it.

The entry is never called by name; its address is slot 42 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4, the relocated pointer at 0x0006026c. Nothing else in the shipped data selects slot 42: over all 63 MAP*.DAT, the number 42 appears in none of the turn-event tables (header + 3, stride 3) and none of the tile-trigger tables (header + 0x31, stride 2), and as a death-script operand (opcode 2 at record + 0x16, signed operand at + 0x17) only in map25.dat records 73 .. 79.

Message 0x17 of fdetxt26.txt opens with the -0x11 portrait token carrying character id 0x0c, and 0x0c is map25.dat's single wave-3 ally, deployment record 62 -- the guide's LV40 英雄索爾, the level-40 guest hero it says can take the wave-2 group on by himself. So the line is his. What it actually says has not been read: the rest of the entry is 16-bit indices into the Fdetxt.fon glyph sheet rather than Big5 code points, and no index-to-character mapping exists yet.

DAT_000640ea is not private to this handler. It is one of the 0x20 bytes fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) when a chapter starts, and fdps_chapter_27_event_deploy_wave_1 latches the same byte in the chapter that follows.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the dword every slot of the table at 0x000601c4 is called with. The dispatcher that reaches this entry, fdps_run_death_scripts, forwards its own first argument at 0001dcaa-0001dcad: the index of the unit that made the killing action -- the same value it hands to fdps_get_unit_record at 0001d9aa, pays the drops and the gold to, and tests for player side and not-retired -- not the index of the dead unit whose script is running. Overwritten with 0 at 000393cc and used as the 0 .. 6 loop counter, so its incoming value has no effect here.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own handler table, both callees are fdps game routines, and the state it touches is game state -- the chapter latch DAT_000640ea and the chapter text pointer DAT_00060124; no Function ID candidate in either library set and the hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
Keep the guard a chapter-scoped byte in the block fdps_chapter_state_reset clears, not a function-local static: a static fires the line once per process and would skip it on a replay of chapter 26. And keep the caller's collect / mark-dead / run-scripts order, because this handler's all-retired test depends on the dead already carrying the retired bit when it runs.

=== 00039440 [PLATE]
Chapter 27's four-generals death script: once the last of the Mage King's four 魔戰將軍 is gone it speaks his line, brings the map's wave-1 reinforcements onto the battlefield and takes the Mage King himself out of hold-position behaviour.

Algorithm:
Clears its local "one of them is still standing" flag at [EBP-0x4], then falls straight through to the epilogue when the one-shot latch DAT_000640ea is already non-zero. Otherwise it runs i = 0 .. 3, calling fdps_unit_is_retired(i + 0xd) on each -- unit indices 0x0d .. 0x10, the chapter's four generals -- and raises the flag as soon as one of them answers 0. All four calls are made whether or not the flag is already up; there is no early exit.

If the flag is still 0, i.e. every one of the four is retired, it does three things in this order and then latches itself off:
  1. fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 0x14, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) walks message 0x14 of the chapter's text image and paints it straight onto the mode-13h screen at 0xa0000 with a 0x140-byte pitch; 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the foreground, background and outline colours it forwards unchanged to fdps_draw_glyph. DAT_00060124 is the "fdetxt%02d.txt" image fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads out of Field.vfs for the current map number plus one, here fdetxt27.txt. Entry 0x14 of that file opens with the -0x11 portrait token carrying character id 0x3f, the chapter's boss, so the line is spoken by him.
  2. fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, 1, 0) runs fdps_deploy_unit on every deployment record of the resident map%02d.dat table whose wave byte at +0x15 equals 1, which puts the map's thirty wave-1 units on the battlefield. DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, 26 here. The third argument is place_exact and it is 0, so each arrival is placed on the nearest free walkable tile around its recorded position rather than exactly on it.
  3. An inline expansion of fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range over the one-element range (0x0c, 0x0c, 0x0b): the three constants are staged at [EBP-0x24], [EBP-0x20] and [EBP-0x1c], copied into the inlined callee's own slots [EBP-0x10], [EBP-0x14] and [EBP-0x18], and the counter at [EBP-0xc] runs the inclusive range, so for unit index 12 alone it fetches the record with fdps_get_unit_record and stores (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0x0b back into rec[0x34]. The four high bits are left alone because they are separate per-unit flags.
Finally it stores 1 into DAT_000640ea, so the whole sequence happens once.

The low nibble of record +0x34 is the behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step masks out at 00010062 and dispatches on. Unit 12 carries mode 2 from the scenario file (map26.dat deployment record 0, byte 0x11, which fdps_deploy_unit copies into record +0x34 at 0002379d). Mode 2, dispatched at 00010122, calls fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, then fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack only if that returned 0, then fdps_unit_rest if that returned 0 as well -- three calls with no movement routine among them, so the unit strikes whatever is already in reach but never leaves its tile. Mode 0x0b, dispatched at 00010652, runs fdps_map_actor_score_best_spell, then fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell once DAT_00063f88 has reached 6, then fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack, and finally fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack when DAT_00063f78 has reached 6 or fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent -- falling back to fdps_unit_rest when that finds nowhere to go -- otherwise; every one of those tails moves the unit. Mode 0x0b's extra fdps_chapter_30_revive_wave_4_undead call at 0001067e is gated on record +7 lying in 0x3c .. 0x3e; record +7 is the deployment record's character id (fdps_deploy_unit copies deployment byte 1 into record +7 at 00023675) and unit 12 carries 0x3f there, so that branch does not fire for this unit.

The entry is never called by name; its address is slot 43 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4, the relocated pointer at 0x00060270. Slot 43 is selected in exactly one place in the shipped data: map26.dat deployment records 1 .. 4 carry the 3-byte death script 02 2b 00 at record +0x16, which fdps_run_death_scripts dispatches at 0001dcae. map26.dat schedules no turn events and no tile triggers at all, so this is the chapter's only scripted event. Map 26 is chapter index 26, the player's chapter 27. With that file's 12 player slots at indices 0 .. 11 (header byte 1) and its 25 wave-0 records deployed into 12 .. 36, records 1 .. 4 are unit indices 0x0d .. 0x10, exactly the range this body tests, and record 0 -- the map's only level-40 unit, the boss -- is unit index 12, the same unit fdps_chapter_27_post_action reads to declare the chapter cleared.

All four generals carry the same script, so this handler is entered once per general killed. The all-retired test throws away the first three entries and the latch throws away any later one, which is why the body is written as a test over the whole group rather than as a counter.

DAT_000640ea is not private to this handler. It is one of the 0x20 bytes fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) when a chapter starts, and fdps_chapter_26_event_wave_2_defeated_line latches the same byte in the chapter before this one.

The incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] is overwritten with 0 at 00039460 and reused as the 0 .. 3 loop counter; the value the dispatcher pushed is never read.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the dword every dispatcher of the table at 0x000601c4 pushes; the table has no single contract for it. fdps_run_death_scripts, the dispatcher that reaches this entry, forwards its own actor_unit_index at 0001dcaa -- the unit whose action caused the deaths, i.e. the killer, not the general whose script is running -- while the turn phases push their unit sweep counters and fdps_battle_run_turn_events pushes a literal 0. Overwritten with 0 at 00039460 and used as the loop counter, so its incoming value has no effect here.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own scripted-event handler table at 0x000601c4; every callee is an fdps game routine and every piece of state it touches is game state -- the chapter latch DAT_000640ea, the chapter text pointer DAT_00060124 and the map number DAT_00069cf4; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
The all-retired test only ever succeeds because the dead are retired before their scripts are run. Every caller of fdps_collect_death_scripts uses the same three-step idiom -- collect the 3-byte scripts, then fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, which stores 1 into record+5 at 0001d7f9, the very bit fdps_unit_is_retired reads back, then fdps_run_death_scripts -- so by the time slot 43 is dispatched the fourth general already reads as retired. Writing the death handling in the obvious order, run the dying unit's script and then mark it retired, leaves him unretired when this handler looks and the reinforcements never come. Second, DAT_000640ea is a chapter-scoped byte inside the block fdps_chapter_state_reset clears with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20), not a private one: writing the guard as a function-local static char fires the event only once per process, so replaying chapter 27 after a Game Over or a save load would silently skip both the wave and the boss's release.

=== 00039541 [EOL]
Alignment padding: three Watcom multi-byte NOP forms (lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / lea eax,[eax+0]).

=== 00039550 [PLATE]
Chapter 28's turn-scheduled reinforcement event: brings on the wave of the current map's units due for the turn just played, then pans the view up to the spawn point so the player sees them arrive.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with an empty local area (SUB ESP,0x0).

First it calls fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, DAT_00069ce8 / 2, 0) and cleans the 12 argument bytes itself. DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, the value that names "map%02d.dat" and "map%02d.cod". DAT_00069ce8 is the battle turn counter: fdps_chapter_state_reset sets it to 1, fdps_load_savegame restores it from the save image, and fdps_battle_advance_turn raises it once per turn cycle. The halving is a signed divide by 2 (SAR EDX,0x1f / SUB EAX,EDX / SAR EAX,1), so it truncates toward zero. fdps_deploy_wave reloads "map%02d.cod" for that map number and runs fdps_deploy_unit over every deployment record of the loaded "map%02d.dat" image at DAT_0006013c -- 0x1a-byte records from +0x83, count in byte +0x2 -- whose wave byte, record + 0x15, equals turn / 2, so each unit of that wave is appended as a new 0x50-byte record on the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 with the unit count DAT_00060150 raised once per unit. The trailing 0 makes fdps_deploy_unit put each unit on the free walkable tile nearest its scripted spawn point from "map%02d.cod" instead of using those coordinates verbatim.

Then it shows the arrival. It stores 0 into DAT_00069cd0, the map-cursor draw mode fdps_draw_map_cursor dispatches on, so nothing of the cursor is painted while the view moves. fdps_map_cursor_move_to(0x120, 0) walks the cursor to map pixel (288, 0) -- tile (12, 0), the rightmost of the three spawn tiles -- dragging the viewport origin with it and rendering a frame at every step the viewport actually moves. Twelve calls to fdps_render_view_frame then hold the picture there for twelve TIMER TICKS -- about 0.66 s, not a sixth of a second: fdps_render_view_frame straddles the retrace to do its palette work, but it spins on data_fdps_view_frame_last_tick until data_fdps_timer_tick_counter differs, so the hold is paced by the 18.2 Hz timer tick and not by the 70 Hz retrace; the loop counter lives in the incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14], which the body zeroes at 00039599 and never reads as an argument. Last it stores 1 into DAT_00069cd0, the plain-cursor mode -- a fixed value, not the mode that was there before.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x00060274, slot 44 of the chapter-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the shipped data the only thing that selects slot 44 is the turn-event table of MAP27.DAT -- map 27, chapter 28 -- which holds the nine entries {turn 2, slot 44, phase 0}, {4,...}, {6,...}, {7,...}, {10,...}, {12,...}, {14,...}, {16,...}, {18,...} and 0xff in its remaining seven slots. fdps_battle_advance_turn dispatches the phase-0 events at 0001e5bc, after the "EnyPhase.saf" banner and before the INC of the turn counter at 0001e5fd, so the counter still holds the turn whose player phase has just ended. MAP27.DAT carries 65 deployment records: 37 in wave 0, nine waves of three records each, and one 0xff filler; the nine scheduled turns select waves 1, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9, because turn 7 divides down to 3, so wave 3 is deployed a second time and wave 4 is never deployed at all. All 27 wave records take their spawn points from MAP27.COD at tiles (10,0), (11,0) and (12,0) along the top edge of the map, which is where the pan goes.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- the single dword every slot of the handler table at 0x000601c4 is called with; the unit-driven dispatchers forward the acting unit's index into the array at DAT_00069cd8, and fdps_battle_run_turn_events, the only dispatcher that reaches this slot, has no unit and pushes a literal 0. Overwritten with 0 at 00039599 and reused as the frame counter, never read as an argument.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom 10.0x or the ailv3.lib set; it shares the game state at 00069cd0 / 00069ce8 / 00069cf4 with its callees, all three of which are named fdps_ routines, and every dispatcher of its handler table is game code]

Rebuild note:
Two ways a faithful-looking rewrite diverges. (1) The wave key is DAT_00069ce8 / 2 read while the counter still names the player turn that has just ended -- fdps_battle_advance_turn calls fdps_battle_run_turn_events(0) at 0001e5bc, before the INC of the counter at 0001e5fd -- so making the counter 0-based, or hoisting the increment ahead of the phase-0 dispatch, shifts every reinforcement wave by a turn. (2) The division truncates and MAP27.DAT schedules turn 7, so the shipped game deploys wave 3 twice and never deploys wave 4; rounding the division, or correcting the schedule entry to 8, adds three enemies chapter 28 never spawns. Keep the plain signed integer divide and the data as it is.

=== 000395c6 [EOL]
Alignment padding: 6-byte lea eax,[eax+0] plus 4-byte lea edx,[edx+eiz*1+0], aligning 000395d0 to 16 bytes.

=== 000395d0 [PLATE]
Chapter 29's mid-map ambush trigger: once a player unit walks across the marked line of tiles, the enemy groups holding the right, lower-right and upper-middle of the map stop guarding their ground and start hunting the party.

Algorithm:
Resolves the acting unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and returns immediately unless that record's side byte at +6 is 2. Side 2 is the player, 0 the enemy and 1 the neutral side (fdps_roster_add_character writes 2 into +6; fdps_deploy_unit copies it from byte 0 of the scenario deployment record), so an enemy or neutral unit crossing the same tile changes nothing.

For a player unit it runs the body of fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range inline with the constants (0x24, 0x59, 0): for every unit index i from 0x24 to 0x59 inclusive it fetches the record with fdps_get_unit_record and stores (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0 back into rec[0x34], clearing the low nibble and leaving the four high bits untouched -- fdps_map_actor_take_best_action reads bit 0x40 of that byte and fdps_score_targets_for_item reads bit 0x80 as separate flags. The expansion keeps both sets of the helper's frame slots: 0x24, 0x59 and 0 land in [EBP-0x24], [EBP-0x20] and [EBP-0x1c], are copied into the formals at [EBP-0x10], [EBP-0x14] and [EBP-0x18], and the loop counter at [EBP-0xc] is seeded from the first of those; the value slot is OR'd into the byte even though it holds 0. Every function of the chapter-event block that touches the behaviour nibble carries the same expansion rather than a call -- fdps_chapter_02_event_enemies_advance four times, fdps_chapter_29_event_activate_all_enemies twice, and fdps_chapter_05_event_enemies_advance, fdps_chapter_07_event_enemies_pursue, fdps_chapter_13_event_enemies_advance, fdps_chapter_event_clear_unit_behavior_1d_25 and fdps_chapter_16_event_enemies_advance_for_turn once each -- while the out-of-line copy at 00036b60 is reached only from outside that block, by fdps_title_demo and fdps_chapter_20_post_action.

The low nibble of record +0x34 is the AI behaviour mode that fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on. Mode 2, which these units carry from the scenario file, tries fdps_map_actor_take_best_action (strike something already in reach) and then fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack, which only scores candidate tiles and always returns 0, so the unit never leaves its tile. Mode 0 tries fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent (advance one step along the traced path) and then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent (move toward the nearest opposing unit), so the unit closes on the party.

The entry is never called by name. Its address is the pointer at 0x00060278, slot 45 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4. In the shipped data the only thing that selects slot 45 is the tile-trigger table of map28.dat -- map 28, chapter 29 -- whose entry 1, the two bytes at file offset 0x33, is {slot 45, pass-mode 0}. fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event arms DAT_00069d90 with that slot when the tile a unit occupies carries trigger index 1 in its attribute byte at +0x10 and the entry's second byte equals fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event's own third argument; the four single-tile movement steppers fdps_walk_step_down, fdps_animate_move_step_up, fdps_animate_move_step_left and fdps_animate_move_step_right pass 0 while fdps_battle_unit_turn and fdps_map_actor_behavior_step pass 1, so this trigger fires as a unit walks over the tile, not when it stops on it. fdps_battle_unit_turn then calls the armed handler with the index of the unit that just acted, and resets DAT_00069d90 to 0xff at the start of the next unit's turn.

map28.dat declares 12 player slots in byte 1 and 80 scenario units in byte 2, so unit indices 0x00..0x0b are the party and 0x0c..0x5b are deployment records 0..79. The range 0x24..0x59 is records 24..77. Records 24..59 carry behaviour byte 2 (deployment record offset 0x11, copied to unit record +0x34 by fdps_deploy_unit) and are the 36 units this event releases; records 60..77 already carry 0 and are the group that advances from the first turn. Records 0..23 and the two Guardian Dragons at records 78..79 stay in place until the map's second trigger, fdps_chapter_29_event_activate_all_enemies, fires.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit whose action armed the trigger, 0x00..0x5b on this map. Passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record; supplied by fdps_battle_unit_turn and the other turn drivers that dispatch through the table at 0x000601c4 as the index of the unit that just finished acting.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; its only callee is fdps_get_unit_record, it edits game unit-record fields, and its only reference is a slot of the game's own handler table at 0x000601c4]

Rebuild note:
The store is a read-modify-write: rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | mode, not rec[0x34] = 0. The obvious C for 'put these units into behaviour mode 0' clears the whole byte, which also wipes the high-nibble flags bit 0x40 (read by fdps_map_actor_take_best_action) and bit 0x80 (read by fdps_score_targets_for_item) and changes how the released units are scored. Ghidra's decompilation feeds that mistake: it folds the OR with the constant 0 away and prints the store as a bare '& 0xf0', so transcribing it loses the third argument and turns an expansion of fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range(0x24, 0x59, 0) into a hand-written loop -- read the assembly at 00039651-00039656, where the value is fetched into DH and OR'd in. The loop bound is inclusive at both ends as well -- i <= 0x59, through unit index 89 -- so writing the more natural i < 0x59 leaves map28.dat's deployment record 77 guarding its tile forever.

=== 00039662 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / mov eax,eax, 14 bytes to align next function entry to 16

=== 00039670 [PLATE]
Chapter 29's final ambush trigger: once a player unit walks onto the entrance tile of the map's upper room, every enemy on the map stops holding its ground -- the army starts hunting the party, and the two Guardian Dragons switch to the breath-then-strike routine instead.

Algorithm:
Resolves the acting unit with fdps_get_unit_record(unit_index) and returns immediately unless that record's side byte at +6 is 2. Side 2 is the player side (fdps_roster_add_character writes 2 into +6; fdps_deploy_unit copies the value from byte 0 of the scenario deployment record), so an enemy or neutral unit crossing the same tile changes nothing.

For a player unit it runs two inline expansions of fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range back to back. The first carries the constants (0x0c, 0x59, 0), staged at [EBP-0x24], [EBP-0x20] and [EBP-0x1c], copied into the inlined callee's own slots [EBP-0x10], [EBP-0x14] and [EBP-0x18], with the counter at [EBP-0xc] seeded from the first of them: for every unit index i from 0x0c to 0x59 inclusive (CMP [EBP-0xc],[EBP-0x14] / JLE at 000396cc-000396d2) it fetches the record with fdps_get_unit_record and stores (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0 back into rec[0x34]. The second carries (0x5a, 0x5b, 0x0a) through the parallel slots [EBP-0x28]/[EBP-0x2c]/[EBP-0x30] and [EBP-0x34]/[EBP-0x38]/[EBP-0x3c] with the counter at [EBP-0x40]: for unit indices 0x5a and 0x5b it stores (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | 0x0a. Both loops leave the four high bits of the byte alone, because they are separate per-unit flags.

The low nibble of record +0x34 is the behaviour mode fdps_map_actor_behavior_step dispatches on, masking the byte with 0xf at 00010062. The three modes involved are all now readable end to end:

  mode 2 (00010122-0001015c), what these units carry from the scenario file: fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, then fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack -- which only scores and returns 0 -- then fdps_unit_rest. No movement call of any kind, so the unit never leaves its tile.

  mode 0 (00010090-000100de): fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent, then fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent, then fdps_unit_rest. The third of those scores every candidate by plain |dx|+|dy| with no regard for what the unit can reach this turn, so a mode-0 unit closes on the party from anywhere on the map.

  mode 0x0a (000105cf-0001064d), the mode the two dragons get: fdps_map_actor_score_best_item, and if the score it leaves in DAT_00063f8c has reached 6, fdps_map_actor_use_item; then, separately and unconditionally, fdps_map_actor_score_best_attack, and if DAT_00063f78 has reached 6, fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, otherwise fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent with fdps_unit_rest as the last resort. Two things separate it from mode 0. The item and the attack are sequential rather than a choice: mode 0 goes through fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, which scores attack, spell and item and dispatches to exactly one of them, while mode 0x0a fires the item and then still takes its attack. And it never calls fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent, so its movement is limited to what the flood fill in fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent can reach -- a mode-0x0a unit works from where it stands instead of crossing the map.

Which is exactly what the two units at 0x5a and 0x5b are for. map28.dat's deployment records 78 and 79 are the only two records in the file whose equipped item (record byte 5, which fdps_deploy_unit writes to unit record +0x0a/+0x0b with the 0x40 equipped flag at 0002369a-000236aa) has a non-zero ITEM.DAT use_effect: item 0xc7 火焰, use_effect 0x1e, use_amount 300, use_distance 0x1e -- the line flag 0x10 plus reach 14. fdps_map_actor_score_best_item skips any item whose use_effect byte is 0 at 0001311f, so on this map its scoring loop finds something only for those two units, and fdps_score_targets_for_item weighs use_effect 0x1e as line-shaped damage. The guide's chapter 29 page states the same behaviour from the player's side: 注意魔龍的火焰具有無視障礙的直線14格攻擊範圍（直接傷害300），使用後還可再近身攻擊一次 -- the dragon's 火焰 has a 14-tile straight-line range that ignores obstacles for 300 direct damage, and after using it the dragon can still make one melee attack. That second clause is the mode-0x0a arm: the item branch and the attack branch in sequence.

The entry is never called by name. Its address is the pointer at 0x0006027c, slot 46 of the chapter-event handler table based at 0x000601c4; the base is visible in the indirect calls CALL dword ptr [reg + 0x601c4] at 0002e140, 00012a33, 00012bd6, 00014d28, 00015839, 000188d8 and 0001dcae. In the shipped data the only thing that selects slot 46 is the tile-event table of map28.dat -- map 28, chapter index 28, the player's chapter 29 -- whose entry 2, the bytes 2e 00 at file offset 0x35, names slot 46 with occasion byte 0. fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event arms DAT_00069d90 with that slot when the cell a unit occupies carries event code 2 and the entry's occasion byte equals its own trigger_kind argument; the four single-tile walk animations fdps_walk_step_down, fdps_animate_move_step_up, fdps_animate_move_step_left and fdps_animate_move_step_right pass 0 while fdps_battle_unit_turn and fdps_map_actor_behavior_step pass 1, so this trigger fires as a unit steps over the tile, not when it ends its turn on it. The unit's turn driver then calls the armed handler with the index of the unit that just acted and resets DAT_00069d90 to 0xff before the next unit acts.

map28.dat declares 12 player slots in byte 1 and 80 scenario units in byte 2, all of them wave 0, so unit indices 0x00..0x0b are the party and 0x0c..0x5b are deployment records 0..79. The two ranges together are all 80 of them, every enemy of the map and nothing else. The record census matches the guide's roster head for head -- 34 骷髏兵 (id 84), 25 地獄犬 (id 107) and 19 幽魂 (id 105), all level 27, in records 0..77, and 2 守護魔龍 (id 112), level 30, in records 78..79 -- and splits by behaviour byte +0x11 as: records 0..59 at mode 2, records 60..77 already at mode 0 and attacking from the first turn, records 78..79 at mode 2. The map's other trigger, entry 1 -> slot 45 -> fdps_chapter_29_event_activate_enemy_groups, releases only records 24..77, so the 24 units of records 0..23 (9 骷髏兵, 8 地獄犬, 7 幽魂) and both dragons are held until this handler fires.

Parameters:
  unit_index -- index of the unit whose movement armed the trigger, 0x00..0x5b on this map. Passed straight to fdps_get_unit_record; supplied by the turn drivers that dispatch through the table at 0x000601c4 as the index of the unit that just acted. Only the side byte at +6 of its record is read.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set; its only callee is the game symbol fdps_get_unit_record, it read-modify-writes a packed nibble field of the game's unit-record struct, and its only reference is a slot of the game's own handler table at 0x000601c4]

Rebuild note:
Both stores are read-modify-write: rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xf0) | value, not rec[0x34] = value. The obvious C for "put these units into behaviour mode 0" or "into mode 0x0a" is a plain store, which also wipes the high-nibble flags in the same byte and changes how the released units are scored afterwards.

Both loop bounds are inclusive -- i <= 0x59 and i <= 0x5b -- so the natural i < 0x59 / i < 0x5b leaves map28.dat's deployment record 77 and one of the two 守護魔龍 guarding their tiles forever.

The two ranges must keep their two different values. Writing one loop over 0x0c..0x5b with value 0, which is the obvious way to say "release every enemy", is wrong in two visible ways: mode 0 reaches fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent, which scores by raw |dx|+|dy| and ignores what the unit can actually reach, so the two MV2 dragons would leave the upper room and crawl at the party across the map; and mode 0 dispatches through fdps_map_actor_take_best_action, which picks exactly one of attack, spell or item, whereas mode 0x0a uses the item and then also attacks. The guide describes the shipped behaviour as 使用後還可再近身攻擊一次 -- after the 火焰 the dragon still gets a melee attack -- so collapsing the two loops loses a visible half of the boss fight.

The ranges are hard-coded index literals, not a sweep of the live unit table. Rewriting this as "every unit not on the player's side" would catch units outside 0x0c..0x5b and would drop the deliberate split.

Alignment padding: 8d 80 00 00 00 00 + 8d 54 22 00, aligns FUN_00039770 to 16 bytes

=== 00039770 [PLATE]
Chapter 30's reinforcement ambush: the first time a unit steps onto one of the map's trigger tiles it brings on the map's four wave-4 enemies, pans the view over both of their arrival points, and speaks the chapter's line about them.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with an empty local area (SUB ESP,0x0) and returns immediately unless the byte at DAT_000640e8 is still 0, so everything below happens once per chapter. DAT_000640e8 is element 0x10 of the 0x20-byte chapter-event flag block based at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset clears with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) and that fdps_load_savegame restores from save-image offset 0x30a3; it is shared with a dozen other chapters' event handlers, not private to this one.

First it calls FUN_00023830(DAT_00069cf4, 4, 0) and cleans the 12 argument bytes itself. DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, the value that names "map%02d.dat" and "map%02d.cod". FUN_00023830 reloads "map%02d.cod" for that number and runs FUN_000232b0 over every deployment record of the loaded "map%02d.dat" image at DAT_0006013c -- 0x1a-byte records from +0x83, count in byte +0x2 -- whose wave byte, record + 0x15, equals 4, appending each as a new 0x50-byte record on the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 and raising the unit count DAT_00060150 once per unit. The trailing 0 makes FUN_000232b0 place each unit on the nearest free walkable tile to its scripted spawn point in "map%02d.cod" rather than on that tile verbatim.

Then it shows the arrival twice. Both loops keep their 0..11 counter in the incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14], which the body zeroes and never reads as an argument. It then stores the literal 1 into DAT_00069cd0, the plain-cursor mode, rather than the mode that was there before.

The entry is never called by name. Its address sits in the pointer at 0x00060280, slot 47 of the scripted-event handler table based at 0x000601c4 -- (0x60280 - 0x601c4) / 4 = 47 -- the base pinned by the indirect calls CALL dword ptr [reg + 0x601c4] at 00012a33 and 00012aea in FUN_00012960, 00012bd6 in fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase, 00015839 in fdps_battle_unit_turn, 0002e140 in fdps_battle_run_turn_events, 0001dcae in FUN_0001d990 and 000188d8 in FUN_000184f0. In the shipped data slot 47 is selected in exactly one place: the tile-event table of map29.dat, whose entry for cell event code 1 (image offset 0x33, the bytes 2f 00) names handler 0x2f with occasion 0, the occasion fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event reports as a unit finishes stepping onto a tile during movement. Map 29 is chapter index 29, the player's chapter 30. map29.dat's wave-4 records are two of character id 0x55 and two of character id 0x6a, all level 0x14, whose spawn points in map29.cod are tiles (5, 12) for the first pair and (15, 13) and (16, 13) for the second -- the two clusters the pan visits. The strategy guide's chapter 30 entry lists exactly those four as LV20 死靈 x2 and LV20 白骨戰士 x2 and describes the event as "進入平衡之神攻擊範圍時（不包括傳送），右下與左下各出現兩個幽靈和白骨戰士"; the parenthesis matches occasion 0, which a teleported unit never reports.

Parameters:

Rebuild note:
Two ways the obvious rewrite diverges. DAT_000640e8 is not this handler's private flag: it is element 0x10 of the 0x20-byte chapter-event block at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes with memset(0x640d8, 0, 0x20) at every chapter start and that fdps_load_savegame restores from save-image offset 0x30a3, and a dozen handlers in other chapters latch the same byte -- writing the guard as a function-local static char fires the ambush once per process, so replaying chapter 30 after a Game Over or loading a save would silently skip the reinforcements. Chapter 30's "first form has fallen" event: paints the chapter's line, applies the map's scripted terrain change, and brings on the second form of 平衡之神 by deploying the current map's wave-2 unit.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard Watcom four-push frame with an empty local area and stores 0 into its own incoming argument slot [EBP+0x14] at 0003984c; nothing reads that slot afterwards, so the source reuses the parameter as a scratch variable.

Calls the message renderer at 0x0001ff60 with (DAT_00060124, 0x0f, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d). DAT_00060124 is the chapter text image fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads as "fdetxt%02d.txt" for map number + 1, here FDETXT30.TXT, whose 54-entry 16-bit offset table makes 0x0f its sixteenth message; 0xa0000 with pitch 0x140 aims the glyphs at the visible mode-13h screen, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the three colour values the renderer forwards unchanged to fdps_draw_glyph.

DAT_00069cf4 is the current map number, and the loader places every deployment record of the already-loaded "map%02d.dat" at DAT_0006013c whose wave byte -- record + 0x15 -- equals 2. The store at 00039876 looks like a standalone flag because Ghidra labels the target DAT_000640da, but 0x000640da is element 2 of the per-cell trigger table based at 0x000640d8 that fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes indexes by cell code (0002e9b0 CMP byte ptr [EAX + 0x640d8],0x0). === 000398ee [EOL]

=== 000398f0 [PLATE]
Reads the entry count out of a VFS container file on disk, without opening the container or building a handle for it.

Algorithm:
Presets a stack local to 0, then fopen(path, "rb") with the mode string at DAT_0006201c; when the open fails it falls straight through and returns that 0. Otherwise fseek(fp, 7, SEEK_SET) onto the VFS header's entry-count field, fread's it as one 4-byte little-endian value into the local, fclose's the file, and returns the local. Nothing else in the header is inspected -- not the "VFS" magic at offset 0, the version at offset 3 or the entry-table offset at offset 5 -- so any file at all will be probed and no format check can reject one. The fread result is discarded, so a file too short to hold 11 bytes returns whatever fread managed to store. This is the header half of fdps_vfs_open lifted out on its own: that function issues the identical fopen / fseek(7) / fread(4) sequence, on the same mode-string constant, before going on to read the entry table and malloc a handle. This one keeps all 32 bits of the field, unlike its two siblings, which each see only the low 8 -- and they do not truncate the same thing: fdps_vfs_image_entry_count takes the low byte of the file image's own offset-7 field, while the count read inside fdps_vfs_find_entry takes the low byte out of an open handle, where fdps_vfs_open had already stored it as a dword. Between them that is what caps a container at 255 usable members. Nothing in the image calls this function or takes its address; it reaches the link as part of the VFS module object that also holds fdps_vfs_image_entry_count, fdps_vfs_find_entry, fdps_vfs_find_entry_size, fdps_vfs_open, fdps_vfs_load_file and fdps_vfs_image_get_entry.

Parameters:
  path -- NUL-terminated path of the VFS container file to probe, handed unchanged to fopen as the filename. No caller in the image supplies one.

Returns:
The container's entry count as the full 32-bit header field, or 0 when the file cannot be opened. Zero is therefore ambiguous between a failed open and an empty container.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; application-level stdio glue over CLIB3S, sitting at the head of the contiguous VFS module block]

=== 0003995e [EOL]
Alignment filler: mov eax,eax (8b c0) padding to the 16-byte entry at 00039960.

=== 00039960 [PLATE]
Returns the entry count of a VFS container image held in memory, read as a single byte out of the header field at offset 7.

Algorithm:
Zero-extends the byte at image + 7 into EAX (XOR EAX,EAX / MOV AL,[EDX+7]), spills it to the frame local at [EBP-4], reloads it and returns it. Offset 7 of a VFS header is the 32-bit entry count of the container, so this accessor sees only its low 8 bits: a container with 256 entries reports 0. fdps_vfs_image_get_entry reads that same field off the same kind of pointer as a full dword, so the truncation is this function's own and not a property of the format. It matches instead the habit of the two handle scanners, fdps_vfs_find_entry and fdps_vfs_find_entry_size, which both take the count back out of an open handle with MOV AL,[EDX] although fdps_vfs_open stored it there as a dword. No validation of any kind: the "VFS" magic at offset 0, the version at offset 3 and the entry-table offset at offset 5 are never looked at.

Nothing in the image calls this function or takes its address; it reaches the link as part of the VFS module object that also holds fdps_vfs_read_entry_count, fdps_vfs_find_entry, fdps_vfs_find_entry_size, fdps_vfs_open, fdps_vfs_load_file and fdps_vfs_image_get_entry. It is the in-memory counterpart of fdps_vfs_read_entry_count, which fopen/fseek(7)/fread's the same field as a full 4-byte value out of a container on disk.

Parameters:
  image -- base of a VFS container image resident in memory: the 35-byte header, then the 26-byte entry table, then the member bytes. Not a handle from fdps_vfs_open -- offset 7 of a handle falls inside the archive path string it keeps at handle+4 -- so the argument is a whole container image, the same thing fdps_vfs_image_get_entry takes, such as the nested BASEANI.VFS / BASEWAV.VFS images the game keeps in DAT_000643a8 and DAT_000643a0.

Returns:
The container's entry count truncated to 8 bits, 0..255.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unoptimised stack-argument game codegen, inside the contiguous VFS block]

Rebuild note:
The container's entry count is a u32 at header offset 7, and this routine returns only its low byte -- the obvious C, `return *(unsigned int *)((char *)image + 7);` or a struct field read of a u32 entry_count, silently differs for any container with 256 or more entries (it would report 256, the original reports 0). Emit it as a byte load. The same 8-bit truncation appears in fdps_vfs_find_entry and fdps_vfs_find_entry_size, which read the count out of a handle where fdps_vfs_open stored it as a dword, and it is what caps VFS containers at 255 usable members (resource_info/vfs.md). Note the truncation is not uniform across the module: fdps_vfs_read_entry_count and fdps_vfs_image_get_entry keep all 32 bits, so a shared helper or a single `entry_count` type for the whole module would change behaviour.

=== 00039981 [EOL]
Alignment padding: three multi-byte LEA NOP forms filling 15 bytes to the 16-byte entry boundary of fdps_vfs_find_entry.

=== 00039a13 [EOL]

=== 00039a20 [PLATE]
Reports the size in bytes of one named member of an open VFS archive, or -1 when the archive holds no member of that name.

Algorithm:
Initialises the result to -1 and reads the directory handle's entry count as a single byte out of dir[0] (fdps_vfs_open stores it there as a dword). Walks the entries from 0 upward: for each one it memcpy's the entry's 13-byte name field at dir+0x11+i*0x1a into a stack buffer, calls strupr on the caller's name and strcmp's the two. On a match it returns the dword at dir+i*0x1a+0x1e -- the entry's size field, the same field fdps_vfs_load_file passes to malloc and fread as the member's byte count -- and otherwise falls out of the loop with the -1 still in place. 0x1a is the VFS entry stride, 0x11 the size of the handle header (entry count plus container path) that fdps_vfs_open lays down in front of the entry table, and 0xd the 8.3 name field width including its NUL.

That 0x1e is a folded base, not a field offset: it is the entry table's own 0x11 plus 0x0d, so the field being read is the member size at offset 0x0d of the 26-byte entry -- a displacement larger than one whole entry only because the table offset is folded into it. The same loop's memcpy adds the 0x11 explicitly, and fdps_vfs_open lays down 0x11 bytes of handle header before the table. The entry also carries a duplicate copy of the size at offset 0x11 and the member's start at 0x16, neither of which this function reads; the two size copies agree in every shipped container, so nothing but this decomposition distinguishes them. fdps_vfs_load_file at 00039bd0 shows the same fold twice over off the same base -- +0x1e at 00039c3b feeding malloc and the fread count, +0x27 at 00039c5d feeding the seek, and 0x27 - 0x11 is 0x16, the member start.

Parameters:
  name -- member name to look up, e.g. "Fight.pal"; any writable NUL-terminated string, upper-cased in place by this call.
  dir -- archive directory handle returned by fdps_vfs_open.

Returns:
The member's size in bytes, or -1 if no entry matches.

Pool: fdps  [shares the VFS record layout with fdps_vfs_find_entry at 00039990; no FID hit in the watcom or ail sets]

Nothing in the image calls this function or refers to its address; it is an unused member of the VFS reader's interface.

Rebuild note:
Both hazards of fdps_vfs_find_entry are reproduced here: the entry count is loaded with MOV AL,byte ptr [EDX], so an archive with more than 255 members silently searches only the first 255, and the name match is one-way -- strupr rewrites the caller's buffer and the entry name is taken raw -- so writing the loop bound as a u32 count or the comparison as stricmp(entry, name) both diverge from the original.

=== 00039bca [EOL]

=== 00039bd0 [PLATE]
Loads one named entry out of a VFS archive into a freshly allocated buffer, returning NULL and printing a diagnostic on any failure.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; game-private VFS record layout]
Evidence: Calls fdps_vfs_find_entry@00039990, then indexes the directory with IMUL 0x1a and reads the entry length from [entry+0x1e] and the file offset from [entry+0x27] -- a project-specific layout no CRT or Miles routine has. It uses the runtime only as a client (malloc, fopen, fseek, fread, fclose, printf) and its three format strings are game diagnostics, not library API names. fid.watcom and fid.ail are empty with zero candidates. All five static callers are fdps_ resource-loading functions, and nothing touches AIL driver state.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code; no vendor symbol claimed and none matches.
Boundary: 00039bd0-00039ce6, canonical Watcom prologue 53 56 57 55 89 e5 at the entry and the matching mov esp,ebp / pop / ret at the end; the 9 bytes after it are alignment padding before FUN_00039cf0.
Signature: __cdecl, void * fdps_vfs_load_file(char * name, void * vfs) -- both arguments read from [EBP+0x14]/[EBP+0x18], RET with no immediate, callers clean 8 bytes; result in EAX.

Algorithm:
1. fdps_vfs_find_entry(name, vfs) gives the entry index; on -1 it prints "Can't find the string: %s" and returns NULL.
2. memcpy 13 bytes of the archive path stored at vfs+4 into a local buffer and fopen(path, mode at 0006201c); on failure prints "Can't open the source VFS_file: %s" and returns NULL.
3. Takes the entry byte length from [vfs + index*0x1a + 0x1e] and malloc()s it; on failure prints "Can't allocate memory for VFS_file: %s(%dbytes)", still fcloses the file and returns NULL.
4. Takes the entry file offset from [vfs + index*0x1a + 0x27], fseek(fp, offset, 0), fread(buf, length, 1, fp), fclose(fp).
5. Returns the allocated buffer, which the caller owns.

Handle layout: a 0x11 byte header (u32 member count at 0, 13-byte archive path at 4) followed by 26-byte directory entries starting at 0x11, each holding the 13-byte name at +0, the member size at +0x0d, a duplicate size at +0x11, a reserved byte at +0x15 and the member start at +0x16. The 0x1e at 00039c3b and the 0x27 at 00039c5d are folded bases: 0x11 + 0x0d and 0x11 + 0x16.

=== 00039ce7 [EOL]
Watcom multi-byte NOP alignment padding to 16-byte boundary at 00039cf0

=== 00039cf0 [PLATE]
Finds one named member of a VFS container image held in memory and hands back a pointer to that member's bytes inside the image.

Algorithm:
Copies the container's 0x0b-byte header onto the stack with memmove, then walks entry indices from 0 while the index is below the u32 entry count at header+7, compared unsigned. For each index it memmoves the 0x1a-byte directory entry at image + (u16 entry-table offset at header+5) + index*0x1a into a stack copy, then memmoves that entry's first 13 bytes -- the member's 8.3 name -- into a second stack buffer. It calls strupr on the caller's name, which uppercases the caller's own buffer in place, and compares the result with strcmp against the entry-name copy; the entry's own name is never case-folded, so the match is a one-way uppercase normalisation and not a case-insensitive compare. On a match it writes the u32 at entry+0x0d, the member's size, through out_size and returns image + the u32 at entry+0x16, the member's start measured from the front of the container. The result variable is seeded with 0 before the loop, so falling out of the loop returns 0. Nothing is allocated and nothing is copied out: the returned pointer aims into the container image itself and stays valid only as long as the caller keeps that image.

This is the memory-image counterpart of fdps_vfs_find_entry, which scans the directory handle fdps_vfs_open builds and returns an index instead.

Parameters:
  image -- base of a whole VFS container image already resident in memory. fdps_play_sfx passes the sound pack held in DAT_000643a0; fdps_baseani_get_entry_or_exit, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead and fdps_play_attack_animation pass the BaseAni.vfs image held in DAT_000643a8.
  name -- name of the member to look up, in the container's 8.3 form. It is uppercased in place before every comparison, so the buffer behind it must be writable and it stays uppercased after the call returns.
  out_size -- receives the member's size in bytes when the member is found; left untouched when it is not. All four call sites pass a stack slot and discard it.

Returns:
  Pointer to the member's data inside the container image, or 0 when the container holds no member of that name.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; the VFS header and directory constants are game-specific, and it touches the runtime only as a consumer through memmove, strupr and strcmp]

Rebuild note:
strupr(name) uppercases the caller's buffer in place and the entry name is compared as stored, so this is one-way normalisation, not a case-insensitive lookup: writing stricmp(entry_name, name), or uppercasing into a scratch copy, changes behaviour twice over. Entry names that are not already uppercase would start matching, and the caller's string stays uppercased after the call -- fdps_baseani_get_entry_or_exit relies on that, printing the same buffer in its "File not found: %s" message, which therefore reports the uppercased name. It also means every name literal handed to this function must live in writable storage.

=== 00039d9d [EOL]
3-byte zero fill aligning the 00039d9c function tail up to the dword-aligned start of the read-only table at 00039da0

=== 00039da0 [PLATE]
Compiler-emitted initialiser image for the 26-entry revival price list of fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members: one dword per class code, giving the gold charged per experience level to bring a fallen party member back.

Nothing writes it. It is read once per call, in the prologue of fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members, where REP MOVSD with ECX=0x1a copies all 104 bytes into that function's local int[26] at EBP-0xb0; the stack copy is then only ever read, never modified. The function is called from the chapter-end handlers (0003a410 for chapter 1, 0003a470, 0003a520, 0003a600, 0003a670 and the rest, one per chapter), so this is the bill the party settles between chapters, not a shop price.

The index is the class code byte at +0x20 of the 0x50-byte roster record returned by fdps_get_roster_record, and the entry is multiplied by the level byte at +0x21; the product is subtracted from the party's gold total at DAT_000643a4 and is also what fdps_draw_number prints as the six-digit figure on each row of the Relive.cel panel, next to the two-digit level. The 26 slots are class codes 0x00 through 0x19 in the order of PROMAP.DAT (assets/classes.md), which is exactly the range a party member's class can take -- every starting and promoted form of the twelve recruitable characters falls inside it, and 0x1a upward are the monster and boss classes. Read against that table the entries are: 0x00 swordsman 50, 0x01 sword saint 100, 0x02 sword emperor 100, 0x03 hero 120, 0x04 warrior 70, 0x05 holy warrior 120, 0x06 berserker 110, 0x07 knight 70, 0x08 paladin 100, 0x09 earth knight 120, 0x0a archer 40, 0x0b sharpshooter 80, 0x0c sniper king 90, 0x0d mage 40, 0x0e sorcerer 80, 0x0f warlock 70, 0x10 priest 40, 0x11 high priest 100, 0x12 pontiff 90, 0x13 monk 40, 0x14 martial saint 110, 0x15 martial god 100, 0x16 engineer 70, 0x17 mecha count 100, 0x18 mecha master 120, 0x19 mecha soldier 80. Base classes sit at 40-70 and promoted classes at 80-120, so a promotion roughly doubles the cost of dying.

There is no range check on the class byte and no affordability check on the fee: the whole bill is subtracted first, and fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members clamps the gold total back up to 0 only after the player dismisses the panel.

Pool: binary_artifact  [REP MOVSD of a fixed dword count into a stack frame, with every element read from the copy rather than from these bytes, is Watcom's codegen for an auto-array initialiser, so this image is wcc386's own output and not a global the programmer declared]

Rebuild note:
An entry is the price per level, not the price. Reading these as flat revival fees and writing `gold -= rate[unit->class]` bills a level-30 hero 120 instead of 3600 -- the original multiplies by the level byte at +0x21 (IMUL at 00039f1a) and prints the product as a six-digit number, which only makes sense once the level is folded in.

=== 00039e10 [PLATE]
Destroys every enemy still standing on the battle map. Each of the post-battle and scripted scene handlers calls it first, before loading its scene script, so the map is cleared of enemies before the scene plays.

Algorithm:
Walks unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1, the live unit count, fetching each 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record. Where the record's side byte at +0x6 is 0 -- the enemy side; 1 is the neutral side and 2 the player side -- it writes 0 into the current-HP word at +0x40, leaving max HP at +0x42 and every flag byte alone. It then calls fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead once, which plays the destruction sequence over every unit that is not retired and whose HP word is 0: it animates each one away, marks it removed and plays Explo.Saf over the map positions. Removing the units, updating their flags and redrawing the map are therefore all done by that one call, not by this loop.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  Nothing; every call site is a bare CALL that ignores EAX.

Pool: fdps  [reads the game's unit-count global at 0x00060150 and calls the game accessor fdps_get_unit_record; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set, and all 27 references are direct CALLs from game-logic scene handlers]

Rebuild note:
The HP field is 16-bit: the instruction at 00039e53 is MOV word ptr [EAX+0x40],0x0, and the max-HP word sits immediately after it at +0x42. Declaring the field as int or long in the rebuild and writing rec->hp = 0 zeroes max HP as well, and the same scene handlers then run restore-current-from-maximum passes (fdps_chapter_24_end does one explicitly) which would bring every enemy back with a maximum of zero.

=== 00039e67 [EOL]
Watcom multi-byte NOP alignment padding to 16-byte boundary at 00039e70

=== 00039e70 [PLATE]
Revives every fallen member of the party roster at the cost of the party's gold, and shows the player the bill.

Algorithm:
Copies the 26-entry revive-rate table at 0x00039da0 onto the stack (one dword per class code: 50, 100, 100, 120, 70, 120, 110, 70, 100, 120, 40, 80, 90, 40, 80, 70, 40, 100, 90, 40, 110, 100, 70, 100, 120, 80), then sweeps roster indices 0 .. DAT_00064114-1 through fdps_get_roster_record. A member whose current HP (word at +0x40) is 0 is revived in place: its roster index is appended to a 20-entry list on the stack, current HP is set from the maximum HP at +0x42, the status byte at +0x05 is cleared, and rate[class byte at +0x20] * level byte at +0x21 is subtracted from the party's gold at DAT_000643a4. When the sweep finds no fallen member the routine does nothing further and returns.
Otherwise it rebuilds the icon sprite cache: frees DAT_00060138 when the cache count DAT_00069cf0 is non-zero, zeroes that count, opens ICON.CEL and calls fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group once per roster member in roster order with that member's portrait index (byte at +0x07 of the 0x50-byte record at DAT_00064108), so cache slot n ends up belonging to roster member n. It then loads "Relive.cel" out of MISC.VFS through fdps_vfs_load_entry and drains the keyboard queue with fdps_flush_keyboard_queue.
The bill is animated until a key arrives: while fdps_read_keyboard_queue reports the queue empty (0xff; a real make code is 0x01..0x7f) it allocates and clears a 0xfa00-byte 320x200 page, blits sprite 0 of Relive.cel over it, and draws one row per revived member at y = row * 0x10 + 0x17 -- Command.cel captions 0x2a at x 0x3e, 0x2b at x 0x57, 0x3a at x 0xb4 and 0x29 at x 0xd6 from the UI sheet at DAT_000643ac, the member's name through FUN_0001ff60 from the message table at DAT_000643c4 with text index (character id at +0x08) + 1, the level as two digits and the fee as six digits through fdps_draw_number, and the member's 24x24 map icon through fdps_blit_dispatch, taken from cache slot (roster index) * 0x30 at walk frame (DAT_00069d64 >> 2) & 3 with 3 folded back to 1, so the icon cycles 0, 1, 2, 1. The finished page is presented by polling the VGA input status register 0x3da until one vertical retrace has begun and ended and then memmove-ing 0xfa00 bytes to 0xa0000; the loop then spins until the timer tick DAT_00069d64 differs from the value held in a stack local (uninitialised on the first pass) and frees the page.
On the key press it drains the keyboard queue again, raises the gold at DAT_000643a4 back to 0 if the fees overdrew it, and frees the Relive.cel buffer.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  Nothing. The revived roster members, the reduced gold total and the rebuilt icon sprite cache are the whole result.

Pool: fdps  [game resource strings ICON.CEL / MISC.VFS / Relive.cel; walks the party roster and spends the game's gold total; every callee is either a named game routine or a CRT leaf service]

Rebuild note:
The row guard at 0003a0b2 tests the number of revived members against 7, not the row index, so from seven fallen members upward the panel draws no rows at all -- an empty Relive.cel frame that still waits for a key. Writing the obvious "if (row < 7)" to cap the panel at seven rows shows the player a screen the original never shows. The fee is also charged unconditionally, with the gold total clamped back up to 0 only after the panel is dismissed, so there is no affordability check to add. Finally, the spin on DAT_00069d64 and the two 0x3da polls only terminate if the tick counter and the port read are treated as volatile.

=== 0003a2d3 [EOL]
Watcom alignment padding: lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0] / nop, aligning 0003a2e0 to 16 bytes.

=== 0003a2e0 [PLATE]
Applies the game's standard battle end conditions, leaving the verdict in the battle-end code at DAT_00069da0.

Algorithm:
Returns at once unless DAT_00069da0 is still 0, so an outcome already recorded by a chapter event or by an earlier handler is never overwritten. Otherwise it stores 2 (chapter cleared) up front, then sweeps unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 (the live unit count), fetching each 0x50-byte record with fdps_get_unit_record: a record whose side byte at +6 is 0 -- the enemy side -- and whose retired bit is still clear -- bit 0 of byte +5, the bit fdps_unit_is_retired reads -- puts the code back to 0, meaning an enemy is still standing and the battle continues. The sweep runs to the end of the table rather than stopping at the first survivor. It then runs the defeat test unconditionally, whatever the sweep concluded: with the 0-based chapter id DAT_00069cf4 equal to 0x10 or 0x15 (chapters 17 and 22) it asks fdps_unit_is_retired(3), for every other chapter fdps_unit_is_retired(0), and stores 1 (defeat) when that unit is retired. Because that store is not guarded, a defeat outranks a victory recorded moments earlier in the same call.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  Nothing; the verdict is left in DAT_00069da0, where 0 means the battle continues, 1 defeat and 2 chapter cleared. main reads it after each pass of fdps_battle_player_phase_loop: 1 runs fdps_show_game_over and returns to fdps_title_screen, 2 dispatches the chapter's post-battle scene handler out of the table at 0x00060304 and then fdps_run_village_phase.

Pool: fdps  [unit records and chapter-state globals: it reaches the unit table only through the game accessors fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_unit_is_retired and writes the game's battle-end global, and no Function ID candidate exists in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set]

Rebuild note:
The victory sweep and the defeat test are sequential, not an if/else pair, and the defeat store carries no 'only while the code is still 0' guard -- so when the last enemy falls in the same action that retires the must-survive unit, the original records defeat (1), not victory (2). Writing the obvious 'if (all enemies retired) code = 2; else if (lord retired) code = 1;' inverts that case. The outer 'only while DAT_00069da0 == 0' gate must be kept too, or a scripted Game Over set by fdps_chapter_event_set_game_over gets recomputed away.

=== 0003a3a1 [EOL]

=== 0003a3b0 [PLATE]
Chapter 1's post-action handler: the win/lose test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 0 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area (SUB ESP,0x0), then runs two tests in sequence and returns. First it calls fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions, which refreshes the chapter-event/battle-end code at DAT_00069da0 only while it is still 0: it presets 2 (victory), knocks it back to 0 for every unit record whose side byte +6 is 0 -- an enemy -- that still has bit 0 of its flag byte +5 clear, and finally forces 1 (defeat) when fdps_unit_is_retired reports unit 0, Randis, gone. Then, unconditionally, it calls fdps_unit_is_retired(2) and on a non-zero answer calls FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 15, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) and stores 1 into DAT_00069da0 without first reading it.

Unit index 2 is the allied hero Sol. map00.dat, the chapter's deployment file, declares one player slot in its header byte +1, so the roster pass in FUN_00022be0 fills only unit 0, Randis; the opening script ICON00.DAT then deploys wave 2 (the map's lone level-2 enemy, record 0) into unit 1 and wave 1 (record 21, side 1, character id 0x0c, level 10 -- Sol) into unit 2, which is the unit the same script immediately repositions with its retire / place at (14,14) / unretire trio. DAT_00060124 is the chapter's dialogue bank, the "fdetxt%02d.txt" image fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads, here FDETXT01.TXT; its message 15 is the last of the bank's sixteen and opens with the portrait token -0x11 carrying character id 0x0c, which FUN_0001ff60 resolves through fdps_battle_find_unit_by_character_id, so the line drawn is Sol's own. 0xa0000 with pitch 0x140 aims the glyphs at the visible mode-13h screen, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d are the foreground, background and outline colours FUN_0001ff60 forwards unchanged to fdps_draw_glyph.

The pair of tests is chapter 1's stated rule set: win when every enemy is wiped out, lose when Randis dies or Sol dies. Because the second store is unconditional rather than guarded on DAT_00069da0 still being 0, Sol's death is recorded as a defeat even over a victory the enemy sweep recorded earlier in the same call.

Parameters:
  none -- every dispatch site (FUN_00012960 at 00012a48 and 00012aff, FUN_00012b20 at 00012beb, fdps_battle_unit_turn at 0001584e, FUN_0001fa30 at 0001fb50) scales the 0-based chapter id DAT_00069cf4 by 4 and does CALL dword ptr [EAX + 0x6028c] with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  Nothing. The outcome is left in DAT_00069da0, where 0 means the battle continues, 1 defeat and 2 chapter cleared. The callers compare it against 0 immediately after the call to decide whether to break out of the phase loop.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set, hash unique in the image; it is a slot of the game's per-chapter handler table at 0x0006028c, calls game code and reads/writes the game globals DAT_00060124 and DAT_00069da0 -- symbols no separately compiled vendor object could reference]

Rebuild note:
The Sol test stores 1 into DAT_00069da0 without reading it first, so it overwrites the 2 (victory) that fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions may have just written in the same call -- killing the last enemy and losing Sol in one action is a defeat, not a win. Writing the obvious C, an else-if chain after the default check or a `if (code == 0 && retired) code = 1;` guard, gives the opposite verdict in that case. The FUN_0001ff60 message draw is inside the same unguarded branch and is likewise not conditioned on the battle-end code.

=== 0003a410 [PLATE]
Chapter 1's chapter-end handler: grants Randis his starting spell, banks the party, plays chapter 1's victory scene and hands the game on to chapter 2. Reached through slot 0 of the chapter-end handler table based at 0x00060304.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area (SUB ESP,0x0), then runs five steps in order.
1. fdps_set_flag_bit(0, 0) ORs bit 0 into the per-unit spell-learned bitfield at unit record +0x1a of battle unit 0, which in chapter 1 is Randis. Bit 0 is spell 00, 業火. Randis's FRIAPRDA.DAT record carries an empty spell mask, so this call is the only place he ever acquires that spell; the rest of the family has no equivalent step.
2. FUN_00023980 writes every active battle unit record back into the persistent roster table with a 0x50-byte memmove and resets the per-battle fields at +0x22..+0x27. Offset 0x1a is inside the copied block and outside the cleared range, so the spell bit set in step 1 is what carries into the roster. The order matters: the bit is set on the live unit record, then copied.
3. FUN_00021650, the IconAni.vfs event-script interpreter, is called with the ASCIIZ resource name "Win00.dat" at 0x000620b0 and plays chapter 1's victory scene.
4. FUN_00039e70 revives every party unit left at 0 HP, restoring it from its maximum and charging the per-class revive cost.
5. The chapter index at DAT_00069cf4 is set to 1, so the village phase main runs next, and the chapter loaded after it, are chapter 2's.
Like fdps_chapter_02_end it does not call fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies first.

Parameters:
  none -- main dispatches through the table at 0x000293a1 with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing; the effects are the spell granted to unit 0, the roster writeback, the scene it played, the revived party and the advanced chapter index in DAT_00069cf4.

Pool: fdps  [calls only game code; its one data operand is the game resource name "Win00.dat"; it is reached from main through the game's own chapter-end handler table]

Rebuild note:
The fdps_set_flag_bit(0,0) call must stay ahead of the roster writeback FUN_00023980 and must target the live battle unit record, not the roster record: FUN_00023980 memmoves the unit's 0x50 bytes onto the roster, so setting the bit afterwards (or on the roster copy, which is then overwritten) silently loses it. It is also easy to drop the call as a stray one-off while emitting the family from the chapter_NN_end template -- Randis's FRIAPRDA.DAT record has an empty spell mask, so this single line is the only place he acquires 業火, and without it the protagonist has no spells for the rest of the game.

=== 0003a4b0 [PLATE]
Chapter 3's post-action handler: the win/lose test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 2 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area, then runs two tests as a strict else-if chain and returns. fdps_unit_is_retired(0) tests unit 0, Randis; when it returns non-zero the handler stores 1 -- defeat -- into the battle-end code DAT_00069da0 and jumps straight to the epilogue, so the second test never runs. Only while unit 0 is still in play does it call fdps_unit_is_retired(4).

Unit index 4 is this chapter's boss, the mage. fdps_build_map_unit_array sizes the party half of the unit array at DAT_00069cd8 from map02.dat header byte +1, which is 3, so unit indices 0, 1 and 2 are the roster slots; it then calls fdps_deploy_wave(2, 0, 1), which appends the map's wave-0 deployment records in table order. map02.dat has exactly two of them: record 0, side 1, character id 0x0c at level 10 -- the NPC ally Sol -- becomes unit 3, and record 1, side 0, character id 0x66 at level 8 -- the mage -- becomes unit 4. The mage is the only enemy on the map when it opens; all 78 remaining deployment records are level-6 stone giants (enemy template 0x47) tagged for later waves.

When unit 4 is retired the handler calls fdps_draw_text(DAT_00060124, 13, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d). DAT_00060124 is the chapter's dialogue bank, the "fdetxt%02d.txt" image fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads, here FDETXT03.TXT; its entry 13 opens with the token pair -0x11, 102 -- the portrait control code followed by character id 0x66 -- so the line played on victory is the mage's own. 0xa0000 with pitch 0x140 aims the glyphs at the visible mode-13h screen, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d land in fdps_draw_text's fg_color, bg_color and outline_color parameters, which it forwards to fdps_draw_glyph. Unlike the handlers of the neighbouring chapters this one never calls the shared default end-condition check fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions, so wiping out every enemy does not clear chapter 3: the only victory is the mage's death, and the map's reinforcement waves keep arriving until it happens. The chapter's twenty-two-turn deadline is not enforced here either. map02.dat's 16-entry turn-event table at file offset 3 ends its live records with (22, 5, 0), and fdps_battle_run_turn_events matches that against the turn counter DAT_00069ce8 and calls slot 5 of the chapter-event table at 0x000601c4 -- fdps_chapter_03_event_turn_limit_game_over -- which is what writes the defeat code when the deadline expires. This handler only ever reports the two states it can see after an action.

Returns:
  nothing; the outcome is left in DAT_00069da0, where 0 means the battle continues, 1 defeat and 2 chapter cleared. The callers compare it against 0 immediately after the call to decide whether to break out of the phase loop.

Rebuild note:
The two tests are one else-if chain, not two independent ifs. 0003a4d4 JMP 0x0003a511 skips the unit-4 test outright once unit 0 is found retired. The sibling fdps_chapter_04_post_action does write its extra test as an unguarded if, but there the override runs in the safe direction -- it stamps defeat over a victory the default check had just recorded. Copying that shape here reverses it: an action that retires Randis and the mage together would overwrite the defeat code 1 with 2, print the mage's death line and clear a chapter the original loses.
