=== 0003a640 [PLATE]
Chapter 6's post-action handler: the win/lose test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 5 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area, calls fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions -- the rule set most slots of the table share -- and then adds chapter 6's own extra defeat condition on top of it. The shared check refreshes the battle-end code at DAT_00069da0 only while it is still 0: it stores 2 (chapter cleared), puts the code back to 0 again for every unit record whose side byte +6 is 0, an enemy, whose retired bit (bit 0 of byte +5) is still clear, and then forces 1 (defeat) when fdps_unit_is_retired reports unit 0 gone. Afterwards this handler calls fdps_unit_is_retired(3) and, when that returns non-zero, stores 1 into DAT_00069da0 without first reading it, so unit 3's death is recorded as a defeat even over a victory the enemy sweep has just recorded in the same call.

Unit 0 is 蘭迪斯 and unit 3 is 法蓮娜. The map unit array is only as long as the map's player-slot count (map%02d.dat header byte +1), and its leading entries are the party roster in roster order up to that length: fdps_chapter_state_reset rebuilds them through fdps_build_map_unit_array, which sizes the array to that player-slot count, fills each record from the roster table at DAT_00064108 and the map's 6-byte deployment records, zeroes every unit at or past the roster count DAT_00064114, and then appends the wave-0 deployments past the player slots. A map fielding fewer player slots than the roster has members therefore cuts the roster short and its wave-0 deploys start at a lower index. The chapter entry handlers grow that roster one character at a time -- fdps_chapter_01_init appends character 0 (蘭迪斯), fdps_chapter_02_init character 6 (尤利安), fdps_chapter_03_init character 4 (亞克) and fdps_chapter_04_init character 1 (法蓮娜) -- and MAP05.DAT fields four player slots, so by chapter 6 slots 0 to 3 are 蘭迪斯, 尤利安, 亞克, 法蓮娜 and chapter 6's rule set reads: win when every enemy is wiped out, lose when 蘭迪斯 or 法蓮娜 dies. fdps_chapter_04_post_action and fdps_chapter_05_post_action are this same routine instruction for instruction, but chapter 4 does not carry the same pair: MAP03.DAT fields three player slots, so there index 3 is the first appended wave-0 deployment and the 3 reaches the guest 索爾, making chapter 4 enforce 蘭迪斯 and 索爾 while chapters 5 and 6 enforce 蘭迪斯 and 法蓮娜. fdps_chapter_17_post_action has the identical shape for the chapter whose only stated loss is 法蓮娜.

The chapter's third stated loss, the guest hero 索爾, is not tested here. 索爾 is a map-placed guest rather than a roster member, so he has no fixed roster slot and sits past the roster count at an index the chapter's deployment data decides; the sibling slots that do enforce him name that index directly -- fdps_chapter_01_post_action tests map unit 2, which fdps_chapter_01_init also reaches by index to set his poisoned opening HP, and fdps_chapter_26_post_action tests map unit 0x5b behind DAT_000640e8 == 1 -- and no such index appears in this body.

Parameters:
  none -- every dispatch site (fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase at 00012a48 and 00012aff, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase at 00012beb, fdps_battle_unit_turn at 0001584e, fdps_battle_tick_status_effects at 0001fb50) loads DAT_00069cf4, scales it by 4 and calls through the table with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:

Rebuild note:
The store at 0003a65f carries no "only while the code is still 0" guard and runs after the shared check rather than as its else branch, so 法蓮娜 dying on the same action that kills the last enemy turns a cleared chapter into a Game Over. === 0003a710 [PLATE]
Chapter 8's post-action handler: the win/lose test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 7 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c. Chapter 8 is the underground-prison map, where the party escorts four villagers off the battlefield while keeping Randis and the guest mage 費塔加 alive.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area and writes the chapter-event/battle-end code DAT_00069da0 itself. Unlike most of the family it never calls fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions, the shared default end check, so chapter 8 has no "every enemy is dead" victory rule at all; it applies three rules of its own, in order.
1. fdps_unit_is_retired(0) -- Randis gone from the battle -- stores 1, defeat.
2. Once the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 is greater than 3, fdps_unit_is_retired(0x13) -- the guest mage 費塔加 gone -- stores 1, defeat. The gate is there because unit 0x13 is not on the map before that: fdps_chapter_08_event_send_guest_mage_to_cells is what puts it into play, and the chapter script fires it at the end of the player's third turn.
3. When fdps_unit_is_retired reports units 0x0f, 0x10, 0x11 and 0x12 -- the chapter's four villagers -- all off the battlefield, the chapter is over. fdps_chapter_08_event_villager_escapes, the handler that runs when one of those four walks out, counts the ones that got out alive in the chapter-scratch byte DAT_000640e9 of the per-chapter event flag block fdps_chapter_state_reset clears on entry. A count of 0 means none was rescued and all four were killed instead, so this stores 1, defeat, and paints message 0x1b, 「計劃失敗，村民全部遭到毒手了！」; any other count stores 2, victory, and paints message 0x23, 「村民全逃了，我們也該溜了。溜吧！溜吧！」. Both go through fdps_draw_text against the chapter text block at DAT_00060124, straight onto the mode-13h VGA screen at 0xa0000 with pitch 0x140, text colour 0xd0, background 0 and shadow colour 0x6d -- this family's fixed trailing arguments.

Parameters:
  none -- takes void.

Returns:
  Nothing. The outcome is left in DAT_00069da0: 0 the battle continues, 1 defeat, 2 victory.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit on either the Watcom or the ail side; game globals, per-chapter battle state and a literal VGA framebuffer address]

Rebuild note:
Chapter 8 ends the moment all four villagers (units 0x0f-0x12) are off the battlefield, and the outcome is victory whenever at least one of them left alive -- the guide's 失敗條件 村民全滅 is only the DAT_000640e9 == 0 case, so writing the obvious "victory when all four escaped" turns a partial rescue into a defeat. The second trap is the turn gate: the 費塔加 death test is armed only once DAT_00069ce8 is greater than 3, so writing it ungated reports defeat on turns 1-3, before he has been deployed onto the map. The third is the argument list of the two fdps_draw_text calls: 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d are pitch, text colour, background and shadow colour, not a width-by-height rectangle -- 0xd0 is a palette index, and reading it as 208 rows of screen is how the call gets rewritten into a clipped blit that does not exist.

=== 0003a8c0 [PLATE]
Chapter 10's post-action handler: the escape/defeat test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 9 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Counts, over the eight player-side unit slots 0 through 7, how many units are accounted for. For each index it takes the record from fdps_get_unit_record and counts the unit when byte +1 -- the unit's tile y -- equals 0x17, the bottom row of the chapter's map, or when fdps_unit_is_retired reports it gone; a retired unit therefore counts as accounted for, so casualties do not block the escape. It then calls fdps_unit_is_retired with unit index 0: when unit 0, 蘭迪斯, is gone it stores 1 (defeat) into the chapter-event/battle-end code DAT_00069da0 and returns without looking at the count; otherwise it stores 2 (victory) only when the count reached all eight. Both stores are conditional, so when neither end condition holds DAT_00069da0 keeps the value the battle loop gave it and the battle goes on. Unlike the other chapters' handlers this one never calls the shared default end-condition check at FUN_0003a2e0, so wiping out the enemies is not a victory here. These are the strategy guide's chapter 10 (宗教法庭) rules: win by getting everyone off the bottom of the battlefield, lose if 蘭迪斯 dies.

Parameters:
  none -- the dispatch sites call through the table with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing; the outcome is the chapter-event/battle-end code left in DAT_00069da0 -- 0 battle continues, 1 defeat, 2 victory. The boolean fdps_unit_is_retired leaves in EAX is dead residue.

Pool: fdps  [dispatch-table entry among the per-chapter handlers, all of them fdps; calls fdps_get_unit_record and fdps_unit_is_retired and writes the game global DAT_00069da0; no Function ID hit in either library set]

Rebuild note:
The escape count ORs the tile-row test with fdps_unit_is_retired, so a dead unit counts as having escaped and chapter 10 stays winnable after losses; writing the obvious "all eight units are standing on the bottom row" makes the chapter unwinnable the moment any unit other than 蘭迪斯 dies. The handler also deliberately omits the shared default end-condition check FUN_0003a2e0 that its sibling chapter handlers call, so copying the sibling pattern would wrongly add a wipe-out-all-enemies victory.

=== 0003ab30 [PLATE]
Chapter 15's post-action handler: while the chapter's optional duel is running it settles the duel instead of applying the normal battle end conditions, handing the 妖刀村雨 to 裘娜 when she wins; at every other moment of the chapter it defers to the shared end-condition check. Reached through slot 14 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area (SUB ESP,0x0), then branches on the per-chapter event flag DAT_000640e8 -- one byte of the 0x20-byte block at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset memsets to 0 when a chapter starts.

Flag clear, the ordinary case: it calls fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions and returns, writing nothing to DAT_00069da0 itself. That check presets 2 (victory), knocks the code back to 0 while any unit record with byte +6 == 0 still has bit 0 of byte +5 clear, and forces 1 (defeat) when unit 0, Randis, is retired.

Flag set: chapter 15's duel is running. The event at 0x00037b70 raised the flag when the fortress cannon fell on turn 25 or earlier and the player accepted the challenge; it had already destroyed the rest of the map, deployed the challenger as the map's wave-2 unit, and retired unit records 0..8 except record 4 and unit record 0x34 by writing 1 into byte +5 of each, so the only two units still standing are unit 4, 裘娜, and unit 0x35, the challenger. From there:
  1. fdps_unit_is_retired(4), and when that returns 0, fdps_unit_is_retired(0x35). While both duellists are still standing it returns immediately, leaving DAT_00069da0 exactly as it found it, so the battle loop keeps running the duel.
  2. Once one of them is down it calls fdps_unit_is_retired(4) a second time to see which one. 裘娜 gone: FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x16, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) renders message 0x16, the line for the duel lost.
  3. 裘娜 still standing -- so it is the challenger who fell: message 0x17 the same way, then fdps_unit_item_count(4). When that is not 8, i.e. at least one of her eight inventory slots is free, message 0x18 is rendered and fdps_unit_add_item(4, 0xa5) puts the 妖刀村雨 into the first empty slot. With all eight slots full both the message and the item are skipped and nothing is said about it.
  4. On both outcomes DAT_00069da0 is set to 2, the code that means the chapter is cleared, so the chapter ends whichever way the duel went and fdps_chapter_15_end runs next.

DAT_00060124 is the chapter's dialogue resource, fdetxt15.txt (the chapter index plus one), loaded out of Field.vfs by fdps_load_field_chapter_resources; 0xa0000 is the mode-13h frame buffer FUN_0001ff60 draws into, 0x140 the destination pitch, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d the three colour arguments it forwards to fdps_draw_glyph.

While the duel runs no defeat condition is tested at all. That is deliberate: unit 0, Randis, is one of the records the duel setup retired, so the shared check would see him gone.

Parameters:
  none -- every dispatch site loads DAT_00069cf4 * 4 and does CALL dword ptr [EAX + 0x6028c] with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup (FUN_00012b20 at 00012beb, fdps_battle_unit_turn at 0001584e, FUN_0001fa30 at 0001fb50).

Returns:
  nothing; the outcome is left in DAT_00069da0, which the callers compare against 0 to decide whether to break out of the phase loop.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; it is reached only from the game's own per-chapter handler table at 0x0006028c, and every callee is proven game code]

Rebuild note:
While DAT_000640e8 is set this handler must not fall back on fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions. The duel setup at 0x00037b70 retires unit records 0..8, unit 0 -- Randis -- among them, so that check would force the defeat code 1 into DAT_00069da0 the moment the player accepts the duel: writing the obvious "run the default check first, then add the duel test" turns chapter 15's duel into an instant Game Over. The silent skip when 裘娜's eight inventory slots are all full is original behaviour too -- no swap prompt, no forced grant, and message 0x18 goes with the item.

=== 0003ac20 [PLATE]
Chapter 15's chapter-end handler: puts the party back on the map after the chapter's optional duel, plays chapter 15's victory scene and hands the game on to chapter 16. Reached through slot 14 of the chapter-end handler table based at 0x00060304.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with two local dwords, then runs five steps in order.
  1. Tests the per-chapter event flag DAT_000640e8, one byte of the 0x20-byte flag block at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset memsets to 0 when a chapter starts. In chapter 15 the flag is set by the event at 0x00037b70: when the fortress cannon falls on turn 25 or earlier and the player accepts the challenger's duel, that event retires unit records 0..8 except record 4 and unit record 0x34 by writing 1 into byte +5 of each, leaving only the two duellists on the map. When the flag is clear the duel never ran and the whole block below is skipped.
  2. When it is set: for i = 0 to 8 it calls fdps_get_unit_record(i) and stores 0 into byte +5 of the returned record, clearing the retire bit that fdps_unit_is_retired tests (bit 0x01) so those party members count as standing again; it then calls fdps_get_unit_record(0x34) and stores 0 into byte +0x34 -- the behaviour-mode byte -- of that one record. Note the offset: 0x00037b70 retired record 0x34 by setting its byte +5, and byte +5 of that record is not the byte cleared here, so unit 0x34 stays retired and it is its behaviour byte that is reset.
  3. FUN_00023980 writes every active battle unit record back into the persistent roster table, resetting the per-battle fields as it goes; step 2 is what decides which records are still active when it runs.
  4. FUN_00021650, the IconAni.vfs event-script interpreter, is called with the ASCIIZ resource name "Win14.dat" at 0x00062158 and plays chapter 15's victory scene. The Win%02d.dat scene scripts are numbered by the 0-based chapter index, so chapter 15's is Win14.dat. (Ghidra's label for the string starts two bytes early, over stray "EL" bytes in the inter-string padding, which is why the decompiler renders the argument as s_Win14.dat_00062156 + 2; the characters the callee sees are "Win14.dat".) The uint it returns is discarded.
  5. FUN_00039e70 revives every party unit left at 0 HP, restoring it from its maximum and charging the per-class revive cost, and finally 0xf is stored into the chapter index at DAT_00069cf4 -- chapter index 15, i.e. the player's chapter 16 -- so the village phase main runs next, and the chapter loaded after it, are chapter 16's.

Unlike most of the family it does not call fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies first: chapter 15 reaches victory through 0x00037b70, which already clears the map before the duel can start.

Parameters:
  none -- main dispatches through the chapter-end handler table with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing; the effects are the un-retired party, the roster writeback, the victory scene it played, the revived party and the advanced chapter index in DAT_00069cf4.

Pool: fdps  [calls only game code; its one data operand is the game resource name "Win14.dat"; it is reached from main through the game's own chapter-end handler table, and matches no Watcom or AIL library symbol]

Rebuild note:
Chapter 15's duel event (0x00037b70) retires unit records 0..8 (skipping 4) and unit record 0x34 by writing 1 into byte +5, but this end handler only un-retires records 0..8: for record 0x34 it clears byte +0x34, the behaviour-mode byte, not byte +5. Writing the obvious mirror image of the duel event -- clearing byte +5 for record 0x34 as well -- leaves unit 52 un-retired and its behaviour byte untouched, the reverse of what the original leaves behind, and changes which records FUN_00023980 treats as active in the roster writeback that runs immediately afterwards.

=== 0003ad10 [PLATE]
Chapter 17's post-action handler: the win/lose test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 16 (0-based chapter id 0x10) of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area, then calls fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions, the shared end-condition check, and adds one test of its own. fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions refreshes the chapter-event/battle-end code at data_fdps_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code only while it is still 0: it stores 2 (chapter cleared), clears it back to 0 if any unit record whose side byte +6 is 0 still has bit 0 of byte +5 clear -- i.e. an enemy is still standing -- and then, because the chapter id data_fdps_chapter_current_chapter_id is 0x10, tests unit 3 rather than unit 0 and stores 1 (game over) when that unit is retired. Returns:
  nothing; the outcome is left in data_fdps_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code, where 0 means the battle continues, 1 game over and 2 chapter cleared. The callers compare it against 0 immediately after the call to decide whether to break out of the phase loop.

Rebuild note:
The final data_fdps_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code = 1 store looks like dead code and is not safe to delete. For chapter id 0x10 fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions already ends with the same fdps_unit_is_retired(3) test, so on the normal path -- the code still 0 on entry -- this handler's own test can only store the 1 that is already there. The two are not equivalent: fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions writes only while the code is 0, while this store is unguarded, so it still forces game over when the code was already non-zero on entry. Writing the obvious simplification -- drop the duplicate, fold the two tests into an if/else, or copy the guard over from fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions -- silently changes behaviour in that case.

That callee refreshes the battle-end code at DAT_00069da0 only while it is still 0: it leaves 2 (chapter cleared) when every unit record whose side byte +6 is 0, the enemy side, has been retired (bit 0 of byte +5), and forces 1 (defeat) when unit 0, Randis, is retired.

Why nothing more is needed: the strategy guide gives chapter 18 咆哮的獅王 exactly one win condition, 敵人全滅, and exactly one lose condition, 蘭迪斯死亡 -- the shared check's pair verbatim. Chapter 18 is also not one of the two chapters for which that check substitutes unit 3, Farlena, for unit 0 (chapter ids 0x10 and 0x15, the player's chapters 17 and 22). And no deployment record of map17.dat, chapter 18's map, carries death-script opcode 5 at record +0x16 -- the opcode that stores 1 into DAT_00069da0 -- so unlike chapter 2 this chapter has no data-side lose condition either.

Parameters:

=== 0003ada0 [PLATE]
Chapter 18's chapter-end handler, and the gate on the hero (英雄) class-change route: when 蘭迪斯 is still carrying the 神的聖印 and none of the first nine party members has changed class, the seal is traded for the 勇者徽章 and the chapter plays its alternative victory scene; otherwise the ordinary one plays. Reached through slot 17 of the chapter-end handler table based at 0x00060304.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with 0x14 bytes of locals and clears two byte flags: has_promoted at [EBP-0x8] and got_emblem at [EBP-0x4].
1. fdps_unit_find_item_slot(0, 0xa9) searches the eight inventory slots of unit 0 for item 0xa9, the 神的聖印. The chapter's 0x50-byte unit records are materialised from the roster array in join order, so unit 0 is 蘭迪斯. A return of -1 means he is not carrying it and the entire bonus branch is skipped.
2. Otherwise unit indices 0 through 8 -- a literal nine, not the live battle unit count at DAT_00060150 -- are resolved one at a time with fdps_get_unit_record, and has_promoted is set for any record whose form id byte at +0x07 differs from its character id byte at +0x08. fdps_roster_add_character seeds both bytes with the same character id, and the only routine that rewrites +0x07 is the class-change animation at 0x00034c10, which takes the new form id from the character's RankUp.dat promotion record; the two bytes therefore differ exactly for a character who has already been promoted. The sweep runs all nine slots with no early exit.
3. When has_promoted is still clear, fdps_unit_remove_item(0, slot) takes the 神的聖印 off 蘭迪斯 -- closing the gap in his inventory -- and fdps_unit_add_item(0, 0xdb) puts the 勇者徽章 in his first free slot, so the emblem does not necessarily occupy the slot the seal did. got_emblem is set.
4. Four steps then run unconditionally, whichever way the branch above went. fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies wipes every enemy still standing on the battle map, so the scene plays over a cleared map. fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units copies every battle unit record back over the roster record of the same character. The IconAni.vfs event-script interpreter at 0x00021650 is then handed the ASCIIZ resource name "Win17-1.dat" at 0x0006217c when got_emblem is set and "Win17.dat" at 0x00062188 when it is not; the Win<NN>.dat scenes are numbered by 0-based chapter index, so 17 is the player's chapter 18. The revive routine at 0x00039e70 restores every party member still at 0 HP and charges the per-class revive cost. Last, the chapter index global DAT_00069cf4 is set to 0x12; that global is 0-based, so 0x12 selects the player's chapter 19, and it is the index every per-chapter handler table -- chapter init, post-action, chapter end -- is dispatched through afterwards.

Parameters:
  none -- the chapter-end handler table is dispatched through with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing. The effects are the conditional 神的聖印 to 勇者徽章 trade in unit 0's inventory, the cleared map, the roster writeback, one of the two chapter 18 victory scenes, the paid revive screen and the advanced chapter index in DAT_00069cf4.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own chapter-end handler table; every callee is game code and the data operands are the game resource names "Win17-1.dat" and "Win17.dat"; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the AIL library set]

Rebuild note:
The promotion sweep is a literal nine iterations over the unit array, with no side test and no reference to the live battle unit count at DAT_00060150 that the neighbouring chapter-end code loops over. Those nine slots are the roster in join order, 蘭迪斯 through 琴琴; 瑪麗安 joins in chapter 15 at slot 9 and is never inspected. Writing the obvious loop -- over every live unit, or over the whole roster -- lets a promoted 瑪麗安 disqualify the trade and denies the 勇者徽章 on playthroughs where the original grants it.

=== 0003ae80 [PLATE]
Chapter 19's post-action handler: the win/lose test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, which on the way out of the chapter offers 裘娜 the wandering swordsman's duel and, when she wins it, trades her 妖刀村雨 (item 0xa5) for the 妖刀村正 (item 0xa6). Reached through slot 18 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with a 0xc-byte local area, then branches on DAT_000640e9, chapter 19's duel flag -- one byte of the 0x20-byte per-chapter event flag block at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset clears when a chapter starts. Chapter 19's other event, the tile-triggered wave 6, uses the neighbouring byte DAT_000640e8.

Flag clear, the ordinary case: it calls fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions and adds no condition of its own. That check leaves 2 (chapter cleared) in the battle-end code DAT_00069da0 once every enemy-side unit is retired, and forces 1 (game over) when unit 0, 蘭迪斯, is retired.

Flag set, the duel is running: fdps_unit_is_retired(4) -- 裘娜's battle-map slot -- and fdps_unit_is_retired(0x4d), the challenger the accept branch deployed as the map's wave 2. While both are still standing it writes nothing at all, so the battle loop keeps running the duel. Once one of them is down it calls fdps_unit_is_retired(0x4d) a second time to see which:
  - challenger gone: message 0x11 through 0x0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x11, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d); then fdps_unit_find_item_slot(4, 0xa5), and when 裘娜 is still carrying the 妖刀村雨 fdps_unit_remove_item takes it off her, before fdps_unit_add_item(4, 0xa6) hands her the 妖刀村正 either way.
  - 裘娜 gone: message 0x12, the line for the duel lost, and no item changes hands.
Both outcomes set DAT_00069da0 to 2, so the chapter ends whichever way the duel went.

Then, on every entry, the offer test -- all five of: the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 is 0x14 (20) or less, DAT_00069da0 is 2 (the chapter has just been cleared), DAT_000640e9 is still clear, unit 4 is not retired, and fdps_unit_find_item_slot(4, 0xa5) finds the 妖刀村雨 in her bag. When they all hold:
  1. fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, 2, 0) appends the challenger to the unit array as the current map's wave-2 unit.
  2. message 0xd, then fdps_message_window_open(0x23) slides the message panel up carrying portrait 0x23, then message 0xe drawn at 0xaa44a -- the frame buffer plus (138, 131), inside the open panel.
  3. fdps_prompt_two_choice() takes the answer; 0x00020820 retracts the panel.
  4. Answer 0, accepted: message 0x10, then a sweep of unit indices 0 through 0x4c that writes 1 into byte +5, the retired flag, of every record except index 4 -- fdps_get_unit_record is called for index 4 as well, its result simply discarded -- and DAT_00069da0 goes back to 0 so the phase loop resumes. Only 裘娜 and the challenger are left on the map.
  5. Answer non-zero, declined: message 0xf and nothing else; DAT_00069da0 stays 2 and the chapter ends.
  6. Either answer sets DAT_000640e9 to 1. fdps_chapter_19_end keys its un-retire and full HP/MP restore of the twelve roster characters on that same flag, so declining the duel still buys the party the free recovery.

DAT_00060124 is the chapter's FDETXT dialogue resource; DAT_00069cf4 is the map the chapter is playing, which is also the index the handler table is walked with; 0xa0000 is the mode-13h frame buffer 0x0001ff60 draws into, 0x140 its pitch, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d the three colour arguments it forwards to fdps_draw_glyph.

Parameters:
  none -- every dispatch site loads DAT_00069cf4, scales it by 4 and calls through the table at 0x0006028c with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup afterwards.

Returns:
  nothing; the outcome is left in DAT_00069da0, which the callers compare against 0 to decide whether to break out of the phase loop.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set; reached only through the game's own per-chapter handler table at 0x0006028c, and every callee is proven game code]

Rebuild note:
Two things here have to be written literally. While DAT_000640e9 is set this handler must not fall back on fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions: the accept branch retires unit 0, 蘭迪斯, along with everyone else but unit 4, so the shared check would force the defeat code 1 into DAT_00069da0 the moment the duel starts -- writing the obvious "run the default check first, then add the chapter's extra" turns chapter 19's duel into an instant Game Over. And 0x4d is a hard-coded unit index, not a handle on the unit fdps_deploy_wave has just appended: it names the challenger only while the array already holds exactly 0x4d units, that is after both the turn-6 wave-1 arrival (fdps_chapter_19_event_lancelot_joins) and the tile-triggered wave 6 have deployed. Finish the chapter before turn 6 and the challenger is appended at 0x4c instead, where the retire sweep kills him off, and the settle test on 0x4d never fires -- the chapter can no longer be ended. That is shipped behaviour and the strategy guide records it; resolving the challenger from the deployment instead would quietly fix a bug the original has.

=== 0003b0b0 [PLATE]
Chapter 19's chapter-end handler: closes the chapter out by undoing the duel staging with a free full recovery for the roster whenever the chapter's duel flag is up, banking the party back into the roster, playing chapter 19's victory scene and handing the game on to chapter 20. Reached through slot 18 of the chapter-end handler table based at 0x00060304, which main indexes with the chapter index in DAT_00069cf4.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with 8 bytes of locals.
The first step is conditional on DAT_000640e9, chapter 19's duel flag -- byte 0x11 of the 0x20-byte per-chapter event flag block at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset memsets to 0 on chapter entry and that fdps_load_savegame restores from the save file. fdps_chapter_19_init calls that reset, and inside chapter 19 the only writer of the byte is fdps_chapter_19_post_action, which raises it to 1 once it has put 裘娜's duel to the player -- on both answers, accepted and declined. On accept the same post-action stages the duel by writing 1 into the status byte at +0x05 of every unit record from 0 to 0x4c except index 4, 裘娜's slot, leaving the whole party (and every enemy) marked retired while she fights the challenger alone.
When the flag is zero this routine jumps straight past the sweep. When it is non-zero it walks battle unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 (the live battle unit count), resolves each record with fdps_get_unit_record, and for every unit whose character id byte at +0x08 is 0x0b or lower -- read as an unsigned byte; ids 0x00-0x0b are the permanent roster characters, the only ids fdps_roster_add_character is ever passed, of which chapter 19 has eleven on the roster once its own init adds id 0x0b -- writes 0 over the whole status byte at +0x05, then copies max HP at +0x42 into current HP at +0x40 and max MP at +0x46 into current MP at +0x44. Bit 0 of that status byte is the retired/dead flag fdps_unit_is_retired reads, so clearing the byte undoes the staging and revives anyone who genuinely fell during the chapter; since the flag does not record which answer the player gave, declining the duel buys the party the same free revival. The HP and MP stores are belt and braces: once the status byte is clear, fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units restores both by itself. Chapter 15, which runs the same duel one chapter earlier, undoes its own staging the same way but only clears the status byte and restores nothing.
Four steps then run unconditionally. fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units copies every battle unit record over the roster record carrying the same character id, resetting the per-battle fields as it goes. fdps_icon_script_run, the IconAni.vfs event-script interpreter, is handed the ASCIIZ resource name "Win18.dat" at 0x00062194 and plays chapter 19's victory scene -- the same 0-based 18 that fdps_chapter_19_init passes as "Icon18.dat". fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members then runs the revive screen over every roster member still at 0 HP, restoring it from its maximum and charging the party gold. Last, the chapter index global DAT_00069cf4 is set to 0x13; that global is 0-based, so 0x13 selects the player's chapter 20, and it is the index every per-chapter handler table -- chapter init, post-action, chapter end -- is dispatched through afterwards.
Unlike most of the family this handler never calls fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies, so the map is not swept of enemies before the scene plays; chapters 1, 2 and 15 are the only others that skip it.

Parameters:
  none -- the chapter-end handler table is dispatched through with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing; the effects are the conditional free full recovery of the roster, the roster writeback, the victory scene, the paid revive screen and the advanced chapter index in DAT_00069cf4.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own chapter-end handler table; every callee is game code and the one data operand is the game resource name "Win18.dat"; Function ID matches no Watcom 10.0x or AIL library symbol and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
Three things about the conditional sweep. (1) It must run before fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units: that routine masks the unit status byte at +0x05 down to bit 0 and skips restoring current HP from max whenever the bit survives, so the natural "bank the party, then heal it" ordering carries the party into chapter 20 recorded as dead -- and after an accepted duel, which stamps that bit on every unit but index 4, fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members then bills the player gold to revive the entire party. (2) The character id at +0x08 is compared as an unsigned byte (MOV AL / AND EAX,0xff before CMP EAX,0xb); Watcom's plain char is signed, so declaring that field char in C would let ids 0x80 and up pass the <= 0x0b test and be healed as well. (3) The gate is "the duel offer was made", not "the duel was fought": fdps_chapter_19_post_action raises DAT_000640e9 on its decline branch too, so a player who refuses 裘娜's duel still gets the free full recovery. Rewriting the condition as "if the duel happened" -- the obvious reading of a step whose job is to undo duel staging -- silently takes that free revival away.

Chapter 20's post-action handler: releases three of the tunnel map's held enemies every turn and then applies the standard win/lose test. Reached through slot 19 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Reads the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 (fdps_chapter_state_reset sets it to 1, fdps_battle_advance_turn raises it once per turn cycle). While it is 0x11 (17) or less it calls fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range three times, each time with first_index == last_index so exactly one unit is touched, and with value 0, at unit indices turn+0xc, turn+0x1d and turn+0x2e. So over turns 1 through 17 the three runs take unit indices 13..29, 30..46 and 47..63 out of hold and send them at the party -- three per turn, 51 in all, which is the batch-by-batch enemy advance the strategy guide describes for this map. It then falls through, on every turn, to fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions: while the battle-end code DAT_00069da0 is still 0 that routine writes 2 (chapter cleared), puts it back to 0 if any unit whose side byte +6 is 0 is not yet retired, and -- chapter 20's 0-based index 0x13 being neither 0x10 nor 0x15 -- overwrites it with 1 (game over) when unit index 0, Randis, is retired. The three constants line up with the shipped map data. map19.dat's header gives 11 player slots (byte +1) and 55 deployment records (byte +2, 0x1a bytes each from +0x83); fdps_build_map_unit_array lays the party at indices 0..10, and fdps_deploy_wave(map, 0, 1) then appends, in record order, the 54 records tagged wave 0 at indices 11..64. Neither this function nor fdps_object_set_field34_low_nibble_range bounds the index against DAT_00060150, and neither has to.
Three of the 54 are never released. Index 11 is deployment record 0, the map's only unit deployed in behavior mode 5 -- the scripted event walker -- standing on the bottom-left chest at tile (4,22); it is the unit the guide warns leaves that chest to go and take the treasure at (21,2), and writing mode 0 over it would cancel that script, so the schedule starts one index above it. Index 12 (record 1, tile (22,3)) and index 64 (record 54, tile (20,12)) are ordinary mode-2 units the arithmetic simply does not reach. Record 40, the one record of the 55 tagged wave 1: map19.dat schedules no turn event at all and its one tile trigger is chapter 20's sword upgrade, fdps_chapter_20_event_upgrade_randis_sword, so that unit arrives only if the opening IconAni script Icon19.dat deploys the wave, and it would take index 65, past everything this handler writes.

=== 0003b270 [PLATE]
Chapter 22's post-action handler: the defeat test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 21 (chapter index 0x15) of the per-chapter handler table based at 0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area, calls fdps_unit_is_retired(3), and when that returns non-zero stores 1 -- defeat -- into the chapter-event/battle-end code at DAT_00069da0. That is the whole body: the code is not read before it is written, so a defeat overwrites a victory already recorded there, and no other value is ever stored. Unlike most slots of this table, this one does not forward to the shared end-condition check at 0003a2e0, so it declares no victory of its own; chapter 22 is won by a scripted event rather than by a sweep of the unit list. Unit index 3 is the unit that must survive this chapter, and 0003a2e0 makes the same substitution independently, testing unit 3 instead of unit 0 exactly when the chapter id DAT_00069cf4 is 0x10 or 0x15.

Parameters:
  none -- every dispatch site indexes the table with DAT_00069cf4 and calls the slot with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing; the outcome is left in DAT_00069da0, where 0 means the battle continues, 1 defeat and 2 chapter cleared. The callers test it against 0 immediately after the call to decide whether to leave the phase loop.

Pool: fdps  [slot of the game's per-chapter handler table at 0006028c; its one callee reaches fdps_get_unit_record and it writes the game's battle-end global, and no Function ID candidate exists in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set]

Rebuild note:
The handler writes DAT_00069da0 = 1 unconditionally once unit 3 is retired, without the "only while the code is still 0" guard that the shared checker at 0003a2e0 puts around its own writes. Adding that guard by analogy -- the obvious defensive rewrite -- changes behaviour: in the original a defeat detected on the same action that produced a victory overwrites the 2 with a 1, and the player gets a Game Over where the guarded version would clear the chapter. Note also that no handler reachable during chapter 22 calls 0003a2e0 -- this function is the sole entry for slot 21 and it does not forward there -- so the 0x15 arm of that function's CMP dword ptr [DAT_00069cf4],0x15 at 0003a35f is unreachable, and chapter 22's entire defeat rule is this handler's own store rather than two independent defeat tests.

=== 0003b2e0 [PLATE]
Chapter 23's post-action handler: the defeat test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 22 (chapter index 0x16) of the per-chapter handler table based at 0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area, then tests the two units this chapter can be lost with, in order. First fdps_unit_is_retired(3): when that unit is gone it stores 1 -- defeat -- into the chapter-event/battle-end code at DAT_00069da0 and returns having drawn nothing. Otherwise it calls fdps_unit_is_retired(0x1f), and only when that second unit is gone does it paint a message before declaring the same defeat: 0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x14, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) renders string 0x14 of the chapter's message table straight into the mode-13h VGA frame buffer at pitch 320, in the same seven-argument full-screen form the chapter-script event handlers use (00036f70 issues it twice, with indices 0x17 and 0x18); the trailing 0xd0, 0, 0x6d are the three glyph parameters 0001ff60 forwards to fdps_draw_glyph, not a rectangle. DAT_00060124 is the buffer fdps_field_load_chapter_resources loads from Field.vfs as "fdetxt%02d.txt" with chapter index + 1, so the string drawn is fdetxt23.txt's number 0x14. Like chapter 22's handler, this slot never forwards to the shared end-condition check at 0003a2e0, so it declares no victory of its own -- chapter 23 is cleared by a scripted scene, the routine at 0003b350 that wipes the remaining enemies, loads "Win22.dat" and moves DAT_00069cf4 on to 0x17. DAT_00069da0 is not read before it is written and 1 is the only value ever stored, so a defeat found here overwrites a victory already recorded.

Parameters:
  none -- every dispatch site indexes the table with DAT_00069cf4 and calls the slot with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing; the outcome is left in DAT_00069da0, where 0 means the battle continues, 1 defeat and 2 chapter cleared. The callers test it against 0 immediately after the call to decide whether to leave the phase loop.

Pool: fdps  [slot of the game's per-chapter handler table at 0006028c; it reaches fdps_get_unit_record through fdps_unit_is_retired, renders the game's own chapter message text into the VGA frame buffer and writes the battle-end global, and no Function ID candidate exists in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set]

Rebuild note:
The second test sits in the else arm, not beside the first: when unit 3 is already retired the handler declares defeat without ever drawing message 0x14, even if unit 0x1f is gone too. Writing the natural "lose if A or B" -- two independent ifs, or one if with ||, followed by the message -- changes what the player sees on the losing turn. The store of 1 into DAT_00069da0 is also unguarded in both arms, unlike the shared checker 0003a2e0 which only refreshes the code while it is still 0, so adding that guard by analogy would let a victory recorded on the same action survive where the original turns it into a Game Over.

=== 0003b350 [PLATE]
Chapter 23's chapter-end handler: clears the battle map of both the surviving enemies and the chapter's NPC-side units, banks the party, plays chapter 23's victory scene and hands the game on to chapter 24, reached through slot 22 of the chapter-end handler table based at 0x00060304.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an 8-byte local area, then runs five steps in order.

1. fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies zeroes the HP word at +0x40 of every side-0 (enemy) unit and then retires everything left at 0 HP, so the victory scene plays over a map cleared of enemies.

2. The chapter's own sweep: unit indices 11 through DAT_00060150-1 (the live battle unit count), each record taken with fdps_get_unit_record. Where the side byte at record+0x06 is 1 -- the NPC side; the codes are 0 enemy, 1 NPC, 2 player -- it stores 1 into the flag byte at record+0x05, setting the retired bit and clearing every other flag in that byte, including the 0x80 already-acted bit. Unlike step 1 it does not touch HP. Indices 0 through 10 are the eleven player units this chapter deploys and are left alone, which is where the literal 11 comes from.

3. FUN_00023980 writes every active battle unit record back into the persistent roster table, matching unit to roster member on the character id byte at +0x08. It keeps only bit 0 of the roster copy's flag byte at +0x05 and refuses to restore HP from the maximum at +0x42 when that bit is set, so the NPC units step 2 just retired are banked as out of play rather than as live members.

4. FUN_00021650, the IconAni.vfs event-script interpreter, is called with the ASCIIZ resource name "Win22.dat" at 0x000621c4 -- the Win%02d.dat form named by the 0-based chapter index 22 -- and plays chapter 23's victory scene; the uint it returns is discarded.

5. FUN_00039e70 runs the revive screen over the roster, restoring every member left at 0 HP from its maximum and charging the per-class revive cost against the party gold at 0x000643a4.

Finally the chapter index at DAT_00069cf4 is set unconditionally to 0x17, so the village phase main runs next, and the chapter loaded after it, are chapter 24's -- the chapter index is 0-based, so 0x17 is the player's chapter 24.

Parameters:
  none -- main dispatches through the table at 0x00060304 with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing; the effects are the cleared map, the retired NPC-side units, the roster writeback, the victory scene it played, the revived party and the advanced chapter index in DAT_00069cf4.

Pool: fdps  [calls only game code; its one data operand is the game resource name "Win22.dat"; it is reached from main through the game's own chapter-end handler table, and the ordinary Watcom C frame rules out binary_artifact]

Rebuild note:
The NPC sweep assigns the whole flag byte -- record[0x05] = 1 -- it does not OR bit 0 in. Writing the natural record->flags |= UNIT_RETIRED leaves the 0x80 already-acted bit and any other flag bits standing on those records while FUN_00021650 runs Win22.dat against them, and the script interpreter edits unit records. The sweep must also stay where it is, before FUN_00023980: run it afterwards and the NPC units are banked into the roster as live members with their HP restored from maximum, because the roster writeback reads that same flag bit to decide.

=== 0003b3d0 [PLATE]
Chapter 24's post-action handler: the win/lose test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, which on the way out of the chapter offers 裘娜 the wandering swordsman's duel and, when she wins it, trades her 妖刀村正 (item 0xa6) for the 妖刀正宗 (item 0xa7). Reached through slot 23 of the per-chapter handler table based at 0x0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with a 0xc-byte local area, then branches on DAT_000640e9, chapter 24's duel flag -- one byte of the 0x20-byte per-chapter event flag block at 0x000640d8 that fdps_chapter_state_reset clears when a chapter starts.

Flag clear, the ordinary case: it calls fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions and adds no condition of its own. That check leaves 2 (chapter cleared) in the battle-end code DAT_00069da0 once every enemy-side unit is retired, and forces 1 (game over) when unit 0, 蘭迪斯, is retired.

Flag set, the duel is running: fdps_unit_is_retired(4) -- 裘娜's battle-map slot -- and fdps_unit_is_retired(0x52), the challenger the accept branch deployed as map 23's wave 7. While both are still standing it writes nothing at all, so the battle loop keeps running the duel. Once one of them is down it calls fdps_unit_is_retired(0x52) a second time to see which:
  - challenger gone: message 0x19 through FUN_0001ff60(DAT_00060124, 0x19, 0xa0000, 0x140, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d); then fdps_unit_find_item_slot(4, 0xa6), and when 裘娜 is still carrying the 妖刀村正 fdps_unit_remove_item takes it off her, before fdps_unit_add_item(4, 0xa7) hands her the 妖刀正宗 either way.
  - 裘娜 gone: message 0x1a, the line for the duel lost, and no item changes hands.
Both outcomes set DAT_00069da0 to 2, so the chapter ends whichever way the duel went.

Then, on every entry, the offer test -- all five of: the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 is 0x19 (25) or less, DAT_00069da0 is 2 (the chapter has just been cleared), DAT_000640e9 is still clear, unit 4 is not retired, and fdps_unit_find_item_slot(4, 0xa6) finds the 妖刀村正 in her bag. When they all hold:
  1. fdps_deploy_wave(DAT_00069cf4, 7, 0) appends the challenger to the unit array as the current map's wave-7 record. Wave 7 is the one wave of map 23 that fdps_chapter_24_event_deploy_wave_for_turn never brings on; the waves it schedules are 2, 6, 4, 3 and 5, on turns 5, 7, 10, 13 and 15.
  2. message 0x15, then fdps_message_window_open(0x23) slides the message panel up carrying portrait 0x23, then message 0x16 drawn at 0xaa44a -- the frame buffer plus (138, 131), inside the open panel.
  3. fdps_prompt_two_choice() takes the answer; fdps_message_window_close() retracts the panel.
  4. Answer 0, accepted: message 0x17, then a sweep of unit indices 0 through DAT_00060150 - 2 that writes 1 into byte +5, the retired flag, of every record except index 4 -- fdps_get_unit_record is called for index 4 as well, its result simply discarded. The bound stops one short of the end of the array, which is where fdps_deploy_wave has just put the challenger, so 裘娜 and the challenger are the only two left standing. DAT_00069da0 then goes back to 0 and the phase loop resumes.
  5. Answer non-zero, declined: message 0x18 and nothing else; DAT_00069da0 stays 2 and the chapter ends.
  6. Either answer sets DAT_000640e9 to 1.

The retire sweep stores 1 into byte +5 rather than ORing into it, the way fdps_battle_mark_unit_done does: one store raises the retired bit 0x01 and clears the acted-this-turn bit 0x80.

DAT_00060124 is the chapter's FDETXT dialogue resource, fdetxt24.txt; DAT_00069cf4 is the map the chapter is playing, map 23, and is also the index the handler table is walked with; DAT_00060150 is the live unit count; 0xa0000 is the mode-13h frame buffer FUN_0001ff60 draws into, 0x140 its pitch, and 0xd0, 0 and 0x6d the three colour arguments it forwards to fdps_draw_glyph.

Parameters:
  none -- every dispatch site loads DAT_00069cf4, scales it by 4 and calls through the table at 0x0006028c with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup afterwards.

Returns:
  nothing; the outcome is left in DAT_00069da0, which the callers compare against 0 to decide whether to break out of the phase loop.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ail set; reached only through the game's own per-chapter handler table at 0x0006028c, and every callee is proven game code]

Rebuild note:
0x52 is a hard-coded unit index for the challenger fdps_deploy_wave has just appended, while the retire sweep that stages the duel is bounded by the live unit count DAT_00060150 - 1. The two name the same unit only while the array holds exactly 0x52 units at the moment the offer is accepted, that is after all five of map 23's turn waves have deployed (turns 5, 7, 10, 13 and 15). Clear the chapter earlier and the settle test reads a slot the challenger never occupied: the strategy guide records the shipped result, that finishing before turn 7 makes the swordsman forfeit at the end of the first turn of the duel and hand 裘娜 the 妖刀正宗 for nothing. Resolving the challenger from what the deployment actually appended would quietly fix that. Second, while DAT_000640e9 is set this handler must not fall back on fdps_battle_check_default_end_conditions first: the accept branch retires unit 0, 蘭迪斯, along with everyone else but unit 4, so the shared check would force the defeat code 1 into DAT_00069da0 the moment the duel starts.

=== 0003b600 [PLATE]
Chapter 24's chapter-end handler: closes the chapter out by giving the twelve roster characters a free full recovery when the shared branch flag is set, clearing the battle map, banking the party back into the roster, playing chapter 24's victory scene and handing the game on to chapter 25. Reached through slot 23 of the chapter-end handler table based at 0x00060304, which main indexes with the chapter index in DAT_00069cf4.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with 8 bytes of locals.
The first step is conditional on the shared one-shot byte flag at DAT_000640e9; when it is zero the routine jumps straight past it. In chapter 24 that flag is raised by FUN_0003b3d0, the chapter's post-action handler, which stages the chapter's optional one-on-one duel by writing 1 into the unit status byte at +0x05 of every battle unit except index 4 -- so if the duel was fought, the whole party bar that one unit reaches the end of the chapter marked down. Bit 0 of that status byte is the dead flag, so clearing the byte revives as well as heals. There is no side test and no retired test, and the sweep runs before the enemies are cleared, so it passes over the whole unit array and the character id is the only filter.
Four steps then run unconditionally. fdps_battle_destroy_remaining_enemies retires every enemy still standing on the battle map, so the victory scene plays over a cleared map. FUN_00023980 writes every active battle unit record back into the persistent roster table, resetting the per-battle fields as it goes; it keeps only bit 0 of the status byte (AND byte ptr [rec+0x5],0x1) and skips the restore of current HP from max for any record that still has that bit set, which is why the recovery sweep has to run ahead of it. Last, the chapter index global DAT_00069cf4 is set unconditionally to 0x18; that global is 0-based, so 0x18 selects the player's chapter 25, and it is the index every per-chapter handler table -- chapter init, post-action, chapter end -- is dispatched through afterwards.

Parameters:
  none -- main dispatches through the table at 0x00060304 with nothing pushed and no stack cleanup.

Returns:
  nothing; the effects are the conditional free full recovery of the twelve roster characters, the cleared map, the roster writeback, the victory scene it played, the paid revive pass and the advanced chapter index in DAT_00069cf4.

Pool: fdps  [reached only through the game's own chapter-end handler table; every callee is game code and the one data operand is the game resource name "Win23.dat"; Function ID matches no Watcom 10.0x or AIL library symbol and the body hash is unique in the image]

Rebuild note:
The recovery sweep has to stay ahead of FUN_00023980: that routine carries bit 0 of the unit status byte through into the roster and refuses to restore current HP from max for any record whose bit 0 is still set, so writing the order that reads more naturally -- bank the party, then heal it -- leaves the whole party recorded as dead going into chapter 25. Read the character id at +0x08 as an unsigned byte too: the original zero-extends it (MOV AL,[EAX+8] / AND EAX,0xff) before the <= 0x0b test, and Watcom's plain char is signed, so declaring that field char would let every id from 0x80 up pass the test and be healed.

=== 0003b8a0 [PLATE]
Chapter 27's post-action handler: the win/lose test the battle loop runs after a unit has acted, reached through slot 26 (chapter index 0x1a) of the per-chapter handler table based at 0006028c.

Algorithm:
Builds the standard four-push Watcom frame with an empty local area, then runs two independent tests against the chapter-event/battle-end code at DAT_00069da0. First fdps_unit_is_retired(0xc): when unit 12 -- the chapter's boss -- is retired it stores 2, chapter cleared. Then fdps_unit_is_retired(0): when unit 0, Randis, is retired it stores 1, defeat. Neither store is guarded on the current value, so this slot overwrites whatever was already recorded there, and because the defeat store comes second it wins over the victory store when one action retires both units. Unlike most slots of this table, chapter 27 does not forward to the shared end-condition check at 0003a2e0: it declares victory on one named unit's death rather than on a sweep of the whole unit list, matching the chapter's stated pair -- win when the Mage King dies, lose when Randis dies.

Returns:

Pool: fdps  [slot of the game's per-chapter handler table at 0006028c, a table the game's own data section builds; it calls the game-only accessor fdps_unit_is_retired and writes the game's battle-end global, and no Function ID candidate exists in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set]

Rebuild note:
The two stores into DAT_00069da0 are unguarded and ordered victory-then-defeat, and both details are load-bearing. Adding the "only while the code is still 0" guard that the shared checker at 0003a2e0 puts around its own writes, or collapsing the two ifs into an if/else, or testing defeat first, all change the outcome of the one action that retires both unit 12 and unit 0: the original leaves 1 and gives the player a Game Over, while every one of those rewrites can leave 2 and clear the chapter.

Three things a rewrite has to keep.
