=== 0003bade [PLATE]
Allocates two 512-byte DOS real-mode buffers via DPMI INT 31h function 0100h and publishes their real-mode segments and flat linear addresses in the CD-ROM/MSCDEX globals.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; called only by fdps_cdrom_detect; writes the game's own CD state block]
Evidence: Link direction and shared data. The sole reference to the entry is the call from fdps_cdrom_detect at 0003c698, and its callees are the CRT helpers __CHK, memset and int386x - game code using the runtime, not runtime code. Function ID is empty against both the Watcom 10.0x libraries and ailv3.lib (0 candidates on each), so no vendor module owns these bytes. Every write lands in the 0x00069da4-0x00069e54 CD-ROM state area that fdps_cd_device_request reads; nothing touches CRT or AIL state. It is a full compiled body with a stack probe, so not binary_artifact.
Name: no library symbol identified; fdps_ + snake_case name describing what the body does, consistent with fdps_cdrom_detect and fdps_cd_device_request around it.
Boundary: 0003bade-0003bb7c, PUSH 0x14 / CALL __CHK is the Watcom stack-probe prologue at a real entry, the RET at 0003bb7c ends it, gap_after is empty, and 0003bb7d opens the identical prologue of fdps_cd_device_request.
Signature: void (void), __watcall. No argument register is read before being written and nothing is fetched from the caller's frame; each PUSH group is balanced by the function's own ADD ESP before a plain RET. For a zero-argument void function __watcall and __cdecl are indistinguishable in code, and the compilation unit in fact uses the stack convention (-4s), like the rest of the game - 0003c87d PUSH dword ptr [0x00069de4] / 0003c883 PUSH dword ptr [0x00069dec] / 0003c889 CALL 0x0003c452 / 0003c88e ADD ESP,0x8, and 0003c86a MOVSX EAX,word ptr [ESP + 0x4] reads a parameter off the frame; void (void) simply makes the argument side unobservable here.

Algorithm:
1. memset the 12-byte struct SREGS at 0x00069df0 to zero.
2. Fill the input REGS at 0x00069dc8 with AX = 0x0100 and BX = 0x0020, then call int386x(0x31, in, out, sregs). DPMI 0100h allocates 0x20 paragraphs (512 bytes) of DOS memory below 1MB; the returned AX is the real-mode segment and DX the protected-mode selector, which is discarded.
3. Store the first block's segment as a word at 0x00069e54 and its flat linear address (segment << 4) at 0x00069de8. DOS/4GW identity-maps the first megabyte, so segment << 4 is directly dereferenceable.
4. Repeat the identical DPMI 0100h call for a second 512-byte block; store its segment shifted left 16 bits at 0x00069da8 (a pre-packed seg:0000 real-mode far pointer for the MSCDEX request header's transfer address) and its flat linear address at 0x00069da4.

The input REGS block is not re-initialised before the second call because int386x leaves the caller's input structure untouched.

No error handling: a failed DPMI allocation returns with the carry flag set and garbage in AX, and the resulting addresses are used unchecked by the CD driver functions.

=== 0003bb7d [PLATE]
Sends the currently prepared MSCDEX request header to the CD-ROM device driver via real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h, issued through DPMI Simulate Real Mode Interrupt.
Pool: fdps  [no FID hit in either library set; game-owned CD state area at 0x00069dac-0x00069e54]
Evidence: All 13 callers are the CD-ROM cluster at 0003bce2-0003c6f9 (including fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info and fdps_cd_stop_audio) and it shares their state block, so it is the game's own CD request primitive. Callees (memset, printf, int386x, __CHK) are generic CRT and identify nothing. Not AIL: no AIL module references it and it touches MSCDEX, not AIL state. Not crt: no runtime module builds MSCDEX headers against game globals. Not binary_artifact: full compiler-emitted body with a __CHK prologue.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code; no library symbol identified, and none can be (watcom and ail candidate counts are both 0).
Boundary: 0003bb7d-0003bc3e, entry is the PUSH 0x14 / CALL __CHK stack probe, body ends at the RET at 0003bc3e; gap_after is empty and 0003bc3f is the next function's own __CHK prologue.
Signature: void fdps_cd_device_request(void). No argument register or stack slot is read on entry and no value is returned; every input is a file-scope global (drive letter index of the first CD-ROM drive at 0x00069dfe, real-mode segment of the request header at 0x00069e54, the header itself). Callers fill the header before calling. __watcall and __cdecl are indistinguishable for a zero-argument void function.
Algorithm: clears the SREGS block at 0x00069df0 (12 bytes) and the DPMI real-mode call structure at 0x00069e22 (0x32 bytes); fills the real-mode structure with EAX=0x1510 (MSCDEX Send Device Request), ECX = the drive letter index byte at 0x00069dfe, EBX=0 and ES = the word at 0x00069e54, so the driver sees ES:BX pointing at the request header; then fills the protected-mode input REGS block at 0x00069dc8 with EAX=0x0300 (DPMI Simulate Real Mode Interrupt), BL=0x2f (the interrupt number, 2Fh), BH=0, CX=0 (no words copied from the stack) and EDI = 0x00069e22, sets SREGS.es to DS, and calls int386x(0x31, &in, &out, &sregs). If the output REGS carry flag at 0x00069dc4 is set it prints "DEVICE REQUEST FAILED!!!" and returns anyway; the MSCDEX status word inside the request header is not inspected here, so the caller must read it.
Note: the MOV EAX,0x69e22 at 0003bbf9 stores nowhere but is not dead code -- it is the parameter setup of FP_SEG, which <i86.h> declares under __386__ as #pragma aux FP_SEG = parm caller [eax dx] value [dx], so the near-to-far conversion of &data_fdps_cd_real_mode_call loads the offset into EAX and DS into DX and only DX is consumed. That is why the SREGS.es assignment is FP_SEG rather than a hand-written segment read.
Note on 0x00069dfe: its only writer is 0003c689, MOV [0x00069dfe],AL with AL from MOV AL,[0x00069db4] at 0003c684, and 0x69db4 is data_fdps_cdrom_int_out_regs+8 (ECX) from the INT 2Fh AX=1500h call at 0003c663. CX from MSCDEX 1500h is the drive-letter index of the first CD-ROM drive -- the drive count is the separate store at 0003c67e from BX at 0x69db0 -- and MSCDEX 1510h likewise reads CX as a drive letter, not a device subunit.

=== 0003bc3f [PLATE]
Splits a packed Red Book CD-ROM address (0x00MMSSFF) into its three separate byte fields, for callers that need minutes, seconds and frames one at a time.

Algorithm:
After the Watcom stack probe __CHK(4) the whole body is three byte stores taken straight out of the packed argument: the low byte of msf_packed to *frame, bits 8-15 to *second, bits 16-23 to *minute. Bits 24-31 are ignored. No globals are read or written and nothing is returned; the two callers own the results. fdps_cd_msf_to_sector turns them into a logical sector number (minute*4500 + second*75 + frame - 150, the 75-frames-per-second Red Book rate less the 150-frame pregap); fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info drops them into the CD lead-out globals DAT_00069e08 (minute), DAT_00069e09 (second) and DAT_00069e0a (frame).

Parameters:
  msf_packed -- packed Red Book address, 0x00MMSSFF, as the MSCDEX device driver reports track and lead-out positions; only the low 24 bits are used
  minute -- out; receives bits 16-23, the minutes field (0-99)
  second -- out; receives bits 8-15, the seconds field (0-59)
  frame -- out; receives bits 0-7, the frames field (0-74)

Returns:
  Nothing. The three results leave through the out-parameters.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in image; called only by game CD-ROM code]

Rebuild note:
The parameter order is (packed, minute, second, frame) -- most-significant field first -- while the body stores least-significant field first; writing the call with the pointers in the order the stores appear, or in packed-bit order, silently swaps minutes and frames and the LBA computed from them is wrong by a factor of 4500. Nothing in the code range-checks the fields, so the swap does not fault, it just seeks to the wrong place on the disc.

=== 0003bc78 [PLATE]
Converts a packed Red Book CD-ROM address into the logical sector number of that position on the disc.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_cd_unpack_msf to split the packed argument into its minute, second and frame bytes, written into three separate stack bytes. Then forms minute * 4500 + second * 75 + frame; both multiplies are open-coded shift/add chains, 4500 being 75 frames per second times 60 seconds per minute and 75 being frames per second. Finally subtracts 0x96 = 150 frames, the two-second lead-in that Red Book addressing places before logical sector 0, and returns the result.

Parameters:
  msf_packed -- a Red Book disc address packed as 0x00MMSSFF, minutes in bits 16-23, seconds in bits 8-15, frames in bits 0-7. fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info passes the lead-out address out of the MSCDEX disk-information reply; fdps_cdrom_read_track_info passes the start address of the audio track it queried.

Returns:
  The logical sector number of that address, counted with 00:02:00 as sector 0. An address below 00:02:00 yields a negative value; neither caller checks for it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; called only by game CD-ROM code]

Rebuild note:
The routine subtracts 150 frames before returning, so it yields a logical sector number and not the plain frame count of the address; writing the obvious minute*60*75 + second*75 + frame gives a value 150 too large, which would shift every CD-DA track start and the lead-out that fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info and fdps_cdrom_read_track_info publish. It also returns a signed value that goes negative for addresses under 00:02:00, and the callers rely on that not being clamped.

=== 0003bce2 [PLATE]
Reports where the CD-ROM drive's head is sitting, as a logical (HSG) sector number on the disc.

Algorithm:
Builds an MSCDEX IOCTL-input device request on the stack: header length 0x1e, subunit 0, command code 3 (IOCTL input), media descriptor 0, transfer address taken from DAT_00069da8 (the real-mode seg:0000 far pointer to the second DOS staging buffer), byte count 6, starting sector 0, volume-ID pointer 0. Only the 26 documented header bytes are filled in; the declared length is 0x1e and the four bytes past the documented end, along with the status and reserved fields, go to the driver as whatever was on the stack. Alongside it builds the 6-byte control block: byte 0 = 1 (location of head), byte 1 = 0 (HSG addressing, so the answer comes back as a sector number rather than minute/second/frame). memcpy puts the header into the DOS request buffer at DAT_00069de8 and the control block into the DOS transfer buffer at DAT_00069da4, then fdps_cd_device_request hands the packet to the CD-ROM device driver. Both blocks are copied back out of the DOS buffers -- the header for as many bytes as its own length field says, the control block for 6 -- the request status word at header+3 is published in DAT_00069e20, where fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy reads it, and the dword the driver wrote at control block +2 is returned.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  The location of the drive head as an HSG logical sector number. The call's success is not folded into the return value; a caller that needs it reads the status word left in DAT_00069e20.

Pool: fdps  [no FID hit in either library set, and it calls the game routine fdps_cd_device_request, which a library object could not do]

=== 0003bd99 [PLATE]
Reads the CD-ROM drive's audio channel routing and volume settings into the caller's 9-byte MSCDEX control block.

Algorithm:
Builds a 26-byte DOS device-driver request header in a 0x1c-byte stack buffer: length 0x1a, subunit 0, command 3 (MSCDEX IOCTL Input), media descriptor 0, transfer address taken from the real-mode far pointer at DAT_00069da8, transfer count 9, starting sector 0, volume-ID pointer 0. The status word at header offset 3 and the eight reserved bytes at offsets 5..0x0c are deliberately left as they lie on the stack, since the driver overwrites the first and ignores the rest. Stamps control-block code 4 (Audio Channel Info) into channel_info[0], then memcpy's the header into the DOS-addressable request buffer whose flat linear address is in DAT_00069de8 and the 9-byte control block into the DOS-addressable control-block buffer whose flat linear address is in DAT_00069da4 -- the same DOS block DAT_00069da8 names as a real-mode segment, both published by fdps_cd_alloc_dos_buffers. Calls fdps_cd_device_request, which hands the packet to the CD-ROM device driver through real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h. On return it copies the header back out of DAT_00069de8 (header[0] = 0x1a bytes), copies the nine answered control-block bytes back from DAT_00069da4 into channel_info, and latches the header's status word into DAT_00069e20. That last copy and the status latch are reached by a tail jump into the shared epilogue at 0x0003c590, which the function at 0x0003c51c also owns; in C it is straight-line code.

Parameters:
  channel_info -- pointer to a caller-owned 9-byte MSCDEX Audio Channel Info control block. The routine writes the function code into byte 0 itself; the driver fills bytes 1..8 with four (input channel, volume) pairs, one pair per output channel. The caller's bytes 1..8 are handed to the driver on the way in and are overwritten on the way out.

Returns:
  Nothing. Whether the request succeeded is reported only through the device request-header status word left in DAT_00069e20, where bit 15 is the driver's error flag.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game's own fdps_cd_device_request and shares the game's CD state block at 0x00069da4/0x00069da8/0x00069de8/0x00069e20; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the AIL library set]

Rebuild note:
DAT_00069da4 and DAT_00069da8 are two views of the SAME DOS real-mode block: fdps_cd_alloc_dos_buffers writes the flat linear address (segment << 4) to 0x69da4 and the real-mode far pointer (segment << 16) to 0x69da8. This routine memcpy's through 0x69da4 but puts 0x69da8 into the request header's transfer-address field. Writing the obvious C -- one pointer for the buffer, used for both the copy and the header field -- breaks it either way round: the driver gets a far pointer it cannot resolve, or the memcpy writes to a protected-mode address that is not the buffer. The same split applies to every MSCDEX request builder in this family.

=== 0003be36 [PLATE]
Sets the CD-ROM drive's audio channel routing and volume, by issuing the MSCDEX IOCTL Output request whose control block code is 3 (Audio Channel Control).

Algorithm:
Stamps control block code 3 into byte 0 of the caller's 9-byte control_block; the eight bytes after it are the four (input channel, volume) pairs the caller already filled in for output channels 0 through 3. Builds a 24-byte DOS device driver request header in the stack frame: length 0x18 at offset 0, subunit 0 at 1, command 0x0c (IOCTL Output) at 2, media descriptor 0 at 0x0d, transfer address at 0x0e taken from DAT_00069da8, and byte count 9 at 0x12. The status word at offset 3, the eight reserved bytes, and the start-sector and volume-ID-pointer fields at 0x14 and 0x16 are all left uninitialised; the driver fills the status in, and because the header declares itself 0x18 long against a 26-byte record, offsets 0x14 through 0x17 reach the driver as live stack -- unlike the IOCTL Input siblings, which zero both fields (0003bdb4 and 0003bdbc in 0003bd99). Copies the header into the DOS request-header buffer at *DAT_00069de8 and the nine control bytes into the DOS control-block buffer at *DAT_00069da4 -- the pair of real-mode buffers fdps_cd_alloc_dos_buffers allocated, DAT_00069da8 being the same control-block buffer expressed as a real-mode seg:0000 far pointer for the driver, DAT_00069da4 its flat linear address for memcpy. Calls fdps_cd_device_request, which hands the header to the CD-ROM device driver through real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h. Copies the header back out of *DAT_00069de8 over the stack copy, using the length byte at offset 0 as the count, and latches the returned status word (header offset 3) into DAT_00069e20, where fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy reads it. The nine control bytes are not copied back. The copy-back stretch from 0003bea0 on is shared code: fdps_cd_seek and fdps_cd_play_audio_range jump into it after pushing their own header length.

Parameters:
  control_block -- pointer to a writable 9-byte MSCDEX Audio Channel Control block. Byte 0 is overwritten with 3; bytes 1..8 are four (input channel, volume) pairs, one per output channel 0..3, each volume 0..0xff. Supplied by the caller; no caller exists in the image.

Returns:
  Nothing. The driver's verdict is left in the request-header status word copied to DAT_00069e20.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; calls the game's own fdps_cd_device_request and shares the CD transfer-buffer globals 00069da4 / 00069da8 / 00069de8 and the status global 00069e20 with the other MSCDEX packet builders]

Rebuild note:
The DOS control-block buffer is addressed through two different globals in the same function and they are not interchangeable: the request header's transfer-address field takes DAT_00069da8 (the buffer's real-mode segment shifted into the high half, i.e. a seg:0000 far pointer for the driver) while the memcpy that fills the buffer takes DAT_00069da4 (the same buffer's flat linear address). Writing the obvious C -- one pointer variable used for both -- either hands the driver a protected-mode address it cannot follow or memcpy's into linear address seg<<16, and in both cases the request goes out over uninitialised bytes with no error reported.

=== 0003bea0 [PLATE]
Pool: fdps
Shared epilogue of the MSCDEX/CD-ROM device request routines: takes the request-header length on the stack, copies the header back out of the real-mode request buffer at [0x00069de8] into the caller's 0x18-byte stack block via crt_memcpy, extracts the 16-bit MSCDEX status field at header+3 and stores it into the game global at 0x00069e20, then releases the caller's block and returns.
Evidence: Every path into this address comes from the game's CD-ROM driver glue, and every one of them is already judged fdps: FUN_0003c452 (Play Audio, command 0x84) and FUN_0003c3fa (Seek, command 0x83) each end with PUSH <len> / JMP 0x0003bea0, and FUN_0003be36 (IOCTL Output, command 0x0c) falls straight through into it after MOVZX EAX,[ESP] / PUSH EAX. All three build MSCDEX request packets and dispatch them through fdps_cd_device_request@0003bb7d. The work done here is the matching read-back half of that protocol: the word at request-header offset 3 is the MSCDEX status field, and it is stashed in a game global. That is application logic about a game-specific driver protocol, so crt is excluded -- no runtime routine knows the MSCDEX header layout. Not ail: nothing touches the .DIG driver structures or the 0x70000 sound state area. Not binary_artifact: it is not a thunk or jump island, it performs real work on game state; it is a compiler-outlined common epilogue whose instructions correspond directly to the tail of the game's own C source. The sole callee 0x000435bc is crt_memcpy (settled separately, CLIB3S.LIB Function ID hit), and a memcpy call says nothing about its caller's origin. No Function ID hit on this body at all.

=== 0003bec1 [PLATE]
Reads the CD's media catalog number (UPC) out of the CD-ROM drive and publishes it in the CD state globals.

Algorithm:
Builds a 0x1a-byte DOS device request header in the 0x28-byte stack frame -- length 0x1a, subunit 0, command 3 (MSCDEX IOCTL Input), media descriptor 0, transfer address = the real-mode far pointer of the control-block buffer held in DAT_00069da8, transfer count 0x0b, starting sector 0, volume-ID pointer 0 -- and above it an 11-byte IOCTL control block whose byte 0 is 0x0e (UPC Code) and whose byte 1, the CONTROL/ADR byte, is preset to 2 (ADR = media catalog number). Header bytes 3..4 (status) and 5..0x0c (reserved) are left holding whatever was on the stack; the driver overwrites the first and ignores the rest. memcpy copies the header into the real-mode request buffer whose flat linear address is in DAT_00069de8, and the control block into the buffer whose flat linear address is in DAT_00069da4 -- the same DOS block DAT_00069da8 names as a real-mode far pointer, both published by fdps_cd_alloc_dos_buffers. fdps_cd_device_request then hands the packet to the CD-ROM device driver through real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h. On return the control block is copied back from DAT_00069da4 and the header from DAT_00069de8 (0x1a bytes, the count taken from the local header's own length byte), the request header's status word at header offset 3 is latched into DAT_00069e20, and the CONTROL/ADR byte is tested: when the driver answered 0 there the disc carries no catalog number, and the block's 7-byte UPC/EAN field at block offset 2 is zeroed with memset. That 7-byte field is then copied into the global at DAT_00069e0f, which no other code in the image reads. The status word is recorded but never tested, so DAT_00069e0f is rewritten whether or not the driver accepted the request.

Parameters:
  None.

Returns:
  1, always; the value carries no information. What the routine produces is DAT_00069e0f (the 7-byte packed UPC/EAN, all zero when the disc has none) and DAT_00069e20 (the driver request's status word, bit 15 being the driver's error flag).

Pool: fdps  [calls the game's own fdps_cd_device_request and shares the CD state block at 0x00069da4/0x00069da8/0x00069de8/0x00069e20 with the neighbouring fdps_cdrom_* functions; no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the AIL library set]

Rebuild note:
The control block's CONTROL/ADR byte is deliberately preset to 2 before the request and tested against 0 after it, so the zero test fires only when the driver actively reports "no catalog number"; a rewrite that clears the whole control block first would blank DAT_00069e0f on every drive that leaves that byte alone. DAT_00069da4 and DAT_00069da8 are two views of the same DOS block -- flat linear address for the memcpy, real-mode far pointer for the header's transfer-address field -- and using one pointer for both breaks the request in one direction or the other.

=== 0003bfa5 [PLATE]
Reads the CD-ROM disk information summary (lowest/highest track and lead-out address) through the MSCDEX device driver. It builds a 26-byte device request header on the stack (length 0x1a, subunit 0, command 3 = IOCTL Input, media descriptor 0, transfer address from 0x00069da8, byte count 7, sector 0) and a 7-byte IOCTL control block whose subcommand byte is 0x0A (Read Disk Info), copies both into the DOS-addressable staging buffers pointed to by 0x00069de8 and 0x00069da4, calls fdps_cd_device_request@0003bb7d, then copies both blocks back and distributes the reply: 6 payload bytes to 0x00069e16, lowest track to 0x00069e06, highest track to 0x00069e07, the lead-out address split into MSF at 0x00069e08/09/0a by 0003bc3f and converted to a frame/LBA count at 0x00069e0b by 0003bc78, and the request header status word from offset 3 to 0x00069e20.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; unique hash in the image]
Evidence: link direction in both directions. It calls fdps_cd_device_request@0003bb7d and the CD helpers 0003bc3f and 0003bc78, all of which are game code, and a linked library object cannot reference the game's own symbols; its four static callers (fdps_cdrom_detect@0003c636, 0003c1a1, 0003c27c, 0003c8e6) are game code too, and 0003c636 is reached from main. It writes the game's CD-ROM globals at 0x69e06..0x69e20 and shares the low-memory staging pointers with the rest of the CD module. memcpy, memset and __CHK are CRT callees, which is the normal direction and not evidence against fdps. Every reference to this address is a direct call, so no pointer table dispatches it. 291 bytes of real logic rules out binary_artifact; nothing touches AIL structures.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code; confirmed by the IOCTL subcommand byte 0x0A (Read Disk Info) and the track/lead-out fields the body unpacks. No library symbol involved, and no other address claims the symbol.
Boundary: 0003bfa5-0003c0c7, own __CHK prologue at the start, balancing ADD ESP,0x24 / RET at the end, zero gap before the next function's identical prologue at 0003c0c8.
Signature: void (void). No register or stack argument is read and no call site passes one. The return is void on the callers' own evidence: all four discard EAX at once, and 0003c636 re-reads the status word from DAT_00069e20 rather than from the register the function left it in. Stack convention (__cdecl), the binary's -4s default, with no deviation signal present: this unit calls its game helpers with pushed arguments and caller cleanup (ADD ESP,0x10 / ADD ESP,4), and both helpers are themselves __cdecl.

=== 0003c0c8 [PLATE]
Reads the MSCDEX Audio Track Info block for one CD-ROM track and publishes that track's start position and control field in the CD state globals.

Algorithm:
Builds a 0x1a-byte DOS device request header on the stack -- length 0x1a, subunit 0, command 3 (IOCTL Input), media descriptor 0, transfer address = the real-mode far pointer of the control-block buffer held in data_fdps_cd_ioctl_buffer_real_mode_ptr, transfer count 7, starting sector 0, volume ID pointer 0 -- together with a 7-byte IOCTL control block whose byte 0 is 0x0b (Read Audio Track Info) and whose byte 1 is the low byte of track. memcpy copies the header into the real-mode request buffer at data_fdps_cd_request_header_buffer and the control block into the buffer at data_fdps_cd_ioctl_buffer; fdps_cd_device_request hands the request to the CD-ROM device driver; memcpy copies both blocks back. The reply is then unpacked into the CD state globals: the request header's status word (header offset 3) into data_fdps_cd_last_request_status, the control block's packed Red Book start address (block offset 2) through fdps_cd_msf_to_sector into data_fdps_cd_track_start_sector as a logical sector number, the caller's track number into data_fdps_cd_track_info_track_number, and the control block's track control byte (block offset 6) masked with 0xd0 into data_fdps_cd_track_info_control_flags. The 0xd0 mask keeps the ADR/control bits that distinguish data from audio and mark four-channel audio and drops the copy-permitted bit; fdps_cd_track_is_audio compares the stored value against 0x40. The status word is recorded but never tested here, so the track globals are overwritten whether or not the driver accepted the request. Bytes 5..12 of the header (the reserved area) are left holding whatever was on the stack.

Parameters:
  track -- CD-ROM track number to query; 1 through the highest track number on the disc, which fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info leaves in data_fdps_cd_highest_track_number. Callers pass a zero-extended byte or a sign-extended 16-bit track number. Only the low byte reaches the driver; the low 16 bits reach data_fdps_cd_track_info_track_number.

Returns:
  Nothing. The results are the globals data_fdps_cd_track_info_track_number (the track just queried), data_fdps_cd_track_start_sector (its start sector), data_fdps_cd_track_info_control_flags (its masked control byte) and data_fdps_cd_last_request_status (the driver request's status word).

Pool: fdps  [builds MSCDEX device request packets by hand; no Function ID match, watcom and ail candidate counts both 0]

Rebuild note:
The track control byte is masked with 0xd0, not the 0xf0 that the obvious 'take the control nibble' rewrite would use. 0x20 is the copy-permitted bit, and fdps_cd_track_is_audio decides audio-vs-data by comparing the stored value against 0x40 exactly; masking with 0xf0 would make every audio track that permits copying read back as 0x60 and be reported as a data track, so the game would refuse to play it.

=== 0003c1a1 [PLATE]
Reports the playing length of one CD audio track as a count of CD frames (sectors).

Algorithm:
Refreshes the disc summary with fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info, which republishes the disc's highest track number in the byte at 00069e07 and its lead-out sector in 00069e0b. Saves the track number that the CD track-info globals currently describe, from the word at 00069dff. Calls FUN_0003c0c8 (MSCDEX Read Audio Track Info) for the requested track and takes that track's start sector from 00069e01. When track is below the highest track number at 00069e07, compared unsigned, it queries track + 1 the same way and uses that track's start sector as the end point; when track is the last track on the disc it uses the lead-out sector at 00069e0b instead. It then calls FUN_0003c0c8 once more with the track number saved on entry, so the shared track-info globals 00069dff, 00069e01 and 00069e05 are left describing the same track they described before the call. Finally it returns end sector minus start sector. Both sector numbers come out of fdps_cd_msf_to_sector, which subtracts the 150-frame (2-second) lead-in, so that offset cancels in the subtraction and the result is a plain frame count at 75 frames per second.

Parameters:
  track -- CD-ROM track number, from the disc's lowest track at 00069e06 to its highest at 00069e07. Only the low byte of the argument slot is read. fdps_cd_get_track_length_msf passes its own track parameter through unchanged.

Returns:
  The track's length in CD frames: the number of sectors between the start of this track and the start of the next one, or between the start of the last track and the disc's lead-out.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library; calls fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info and shares the disc-info globals the game's own CD-ROM layer owns]

Rebuild note:
The final FUN_0003c0c8 call at 0003c205 is not redundant: it re-queries the track that was selected on entry so that the shared track-info globals (00069dff track number, 00069e01 start sector, 00069e05 control byte) are restored, and fdps_cd_resolve_track_range reads exactly those globals to decide which track's range to publish. Writing the obvious C -- query this track, query the next, return the difference -- drops that restoring call and leaves the CD layer pointing at the wrong track, so a following play/seek can address the next track instead of the current one.

=== 0003c217 [PLATE]
Reports the playing time of one CD audio track as a Red Book minute/second/frame triple.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors for the length of the requested track in CD frames -- that routine returns the difference between the next track's start sector and this track's, or between the lead-out sector at DAT_00069e0b and this track's start when the track is the last one. Subtracts 0x96 = 150 frames, the two-second lead-in pre-gap, from that length; see the note below, the value it subtracts from carries no pre-gap term. Divides the result by 0x4b = 75, the number of frames in one CD second: the remainder is stored through frames and the quotient is the whole number of seconds. Divides that by 0x3c = 60: the remainder is stored through seconds and the quotient through minutes. Each division is written as (value - remainder) / divisor rather than as a bare quotient, so the same quotient is computed twice. Both divisions are unsigned -- four DIV instructions, never IDIV, since each quotient is computed twice -- and all three results are stored as single bytes. Nothing is returned and no global is touched here; fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors refreshes the disc-info globals at 00069dff-00069e0b as a side effect of the query and puts the previously selected track back afterwards.

Parameters:
  track -- audio track number on the disc, 1..the highest-track byte at DAT_00069e07; passed straight through to fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors
  minutes -- out: whole minutes of the track's playing time
  seconds -- out: seconds within the minute, 0..59
  frames -- out: frames (sectors) within the second, 0..74

Returns:
Nothing. The three results leave through the out-pointers.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; the only real callee, fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors, is game code that reaches fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info and the game's own MSCDEX disc-info globals, and Red Book track timing is not a CLIB3S, MATH387S or AIL service]

Note: the 150-frame subtraction is applied to a duration, not to an absolute Red Book address, so it takes off two seconds that are not there. fdps_cd_msf_to_sector (0003bc78) already ends on SUB EAX,0x96 when it converts a packed Red Book address into a sector number, and every value in the disc-info globals passes through it, so the difference fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors returns has no pre-gap term left and this routine reports every track two seconds short. The subtraction is the module's fixed convention rather than an adjustment chosen for track lengths: the identical SUB 0x96 opens the same /75, /60 chain in fdps_cd_sector_to_msf, which receives its input as a plain sector argument and so cannot be encoding anything about tracks, and in fdps_cd_get_disk_info_msf, which applies it to the absolute lead-out sector. None of the three has a caller or a data reference anywhere in the image, so the short value never reaches the player.

Rebuild note:
The routine subtracts 150 frames from a value that is already a duration: fdps_cd_msf_to_sector removes the two-second pre-gap when it converts each Red Book address into a sector number, so the difference fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors returns has no pre-gap term left and every track comes out two seconds short. Writing the obvious duration conversion -- frames/75 and /60 with no subtraction -- gives a different answer, so the 0x96 must be kept. The divisions are also unsigned: for a length below 150 frames the subtraction wraps and the triple becomes a huge value, where signed C int arithmetic would give a small negative one, so the intermediate must be an unsigned type. The same pre-gap convention is inlined in fdps_cd_get_disk_info_msf and stands alone in fdps_cd_sector_to_msf, so all three must be reproduced the same way.

=== 0003c27c [PLATE]
Reports the two facts the game can want about the CD as a whole: the highest track number on the disc, and the disc's total playing time as a Red Book minute/second/frame triple.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info, which issues the MSCDEX Read Disk Info IOCTL and republishes the answer in the CD globals. The refresh republishes those globals whether or not the driver accepted the request -- nothing here tests data_fdps_cd_last_request_status -- so the values used below are that call's answers, which on a refused request are the cleared control block coming back unchanged rather than anything the drive said. Copies the highest-track byte DAT_00069e07 out through highest_track_out. Then takes the lead-out sector count DAT_00069e0b and subtracts 0x96 (150 sectors, two seconds). That subtraction is NOT a Red Book lead-in removal: DAT_00069e0b has already had the lead-in taken off, by fdps_cd_msf_to_sector at 0003bc78, before fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info stores the sector at 0003c0b5. What this second subtraction produces is therefore the playing length less a further 150 frames, so every triple this function reports is two seconds short. Do not "fix" it: the double subtraction is this module's convention, shared with fdps_cd_get_track_length_msf. The unsigned value is then split into the triple: remainder modulo 0x4b (75 sectors, one second of CD audio) is the frames field, the quotient's remainder modulo 0x3c (60) is the seconds field, and the final quotient is the minutes field. Each of the three is stored as a single byte through its pointer.

Parameters:
  highest_track_out -- where to store the number of the last track on the disc, taken from the disk-info block's highest-track byte; 1..99 on a Red Book disc the drive answered for, and 0 when the request was refused, since the block is cleared before it is sent and comes back unchanged. Written first, before the time conversion.
  minutes_out -- where to store the minutes field of the total playing time.
  seconds_out -- where to store the seconds field, 0..59.
  frames_out -- where to store the frames field, 0..74; one frame is 1/75 second.

Returns:
Nothing. All four results come back through the caller's pointers.

Pool: fdps  [calls fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info and reads the CD globals that routine fills; no Function ID hit in any library, and a compiled vendor object could not call a symbol defined in the game's own source]

=== 0003c2e8 [PLATE]
Converts a CD sector count into a minute/second/frame triple, writing the three fields as separate bytes through caller-supplied pointers. The reverse-direction conversion of fdps_cd_msf_to_sector, but not its exact inverse: fdps_cd_msf_to_sector returns 4500*m + 75*s + f - 150 and this routine decomposes sector - 150, so composing the two yields a triple four seconds earlier than the one that went in. An exact inverse would decompose sector + 150.

Algorithm:
Subtracts 0x96 (150 frames, the two-second lead-in pregap) from sector, then decomposes what is left with unsigned 32-bit divisions: value % 0x4b (75 frames per second) is stored through frame, (value - frame) / 0x4b is the total second count, that count % 0x3c (60 seconds per minute) is stored through second, and (count - second) / 0x3c is stored through minute. Each division is written as (value - remainder) / divisor rather than as a bare quotient, which is why the same quotient is computed twice; the first divisor is spilled to a stack local and read back by DIV dword ptr [ESP]. Calls __CHK(0x10) on entry for the Watcom stack probe, reads no global and writes none.

sector is a count in the unit the whole CD module uses: the pregap-corrected number fdps_cd_msf_to_sector returns, which fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info stores in DAT_00069e0b and fdps_cdrom_read_track_info stores in DAT_00069e01. The 0x96 is therefore taken off a second time and the triple comes out two seconds earlier than a plain decomposition of the same count would give. That is the module's uniform convention, not a quirk of this routine: fdps_cd_get_track_length_msf and fdps_cd_get_disk_info_msf inline the identical arithmetic, over a track length and over the lead-out sector, and subtract 0x96 the same way.

No call site in the image reaches this entry and no data reference points at it.

Parameters:
  sector -- unsigned CD frame (sector) count to convert. Values below 0x96 wrap the unsigned subtraction and yield a meaningless triple; nothing in the body guards against it.
  minute -- out: receives the minute field.
  second -- out: receives the second field, 0-59.
  frame -- out: receives the frame field, 0-74.

Returns:
  Nothing. All three results leave through the pointers.

Pool: fdps  [no library match; a member of the game's MSCDEX/CD-DA object, whose other members call fdps_cd_device_request and fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info and share the CD state globals at 00069da4-00069e54, so the block is the game's own source]

Rebuild note:
The pregap is subtracted, not added, and it is subtracted from a value that has already had it taken off. The textbook conversion decomposes sector + 150; the plain duration conversion decomposes sector with no adjustment at all; this routine decomposes sector - 150, because its input is the pregap-corrected count fdps_cd_msf_to_sector produces. Writing either obvious formula shifts every result by two or four seconds against the original, so the 0x96 must be kept exactly where it is. sector must also stay unsigned: the subtraction and all four divisions are unsigned 32-bit (SUB then DIV, never IDIV), so an input below 150 wraps to a huge frame count instead of going negative, and declaring the parameter int changes what the divisions produce in exactly that case. The same convention is inlined in fdps_cd_get_track_length_msf and fdps_cd_get_disk_info_msf, so all three must be reproduced the same way.

=== 0003c34f [PLATE]
Reads the CD-ROM drive's device status from MSCDEX, leaving both the driver's device status dword and the status word of the request that carried it in the CD globals.

Algorithm:
Builds a 0x1a-byte MSCDEX device request header in the stack frame: header length 0x1a, subunit 0, command code 3 (IOCTL Input), media descriptor 0, transfer address = the real-mode segment:offset of the CD data buffer held in DAT_00069da8, transfer byte count 5, starting sector 0, volume id pointer 0. Beside it it lays out the 5-byte IOCTL Input control block, setting only its first byte to control block code 6 (Device Status); the four bytes behind it are left as they lie, since the driver is the one that fills them. memcpy copies the header into the real-mode request buffer at the linear address in DAT_00069de8 and the control block into the data buffer at the linear address in DAT_00069da4, then fdps_cd_device_request hands the packet to the CD-ROM device driver through real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h. Two more memcpy calls read both buffers back into the stack copies. The four device status bytes the driver returned at control block offset 1 are stored in DAT_00069e1c. The body then falls into the tail at 0x0003c0ba, an epilogue Watcom merged with fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info, which stores the request header's status word (header offset 3) into DAT_00069e20 -- the word whose BUSY bit (0x0200) fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy tests.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  Nothing. Both results leave through globals: DAT_00069e1c takes the MSCDEX device status dword, DAT_00069e20 the request header status word.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; it calls fdps_cd_device_request and is called by fdps_cd_audio_is_idle, and shares the CD state globals 0x00069da4 / 0x00069da8 / 0x00069de8 with the rest of the CD subsystem]

Rebuild note:
The body's last instruction is JMP 0x0003c0ba, an epilogue Watcom merged with fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info, and that shared tail is part of this function's C source: it stores the request header's status word into DAT_00069e20. Rewriting the function from the listing and stopping at the store to DAT_00069e1c drops that store, and since fdps_cd_audio_is_idle ignores everything this function publishes except that one global's BUSY bit, the idle test would then answer from whatever the previous CD request left behind and the game would stop waiting correctly for CD audio to finish.

=== 0003c3fa [PLATE]
Issues an MSCDEX Seek to the CD-ROM drive, moving the drive head to one logical sector without transferring any data.

Algorithm:
Builds a 24-byte MSCDEX device request header in a stack local: length 0x18 at offset 0, subunit 0 at offset 1, command code 0x83 (Seek) at offset 2, addressing mode 0 (HSG logical sector) at offset 0x0d, transfer address 0 at offset 0x0e, sector count 0 at offset 0x12, and the caller's sector at offset 0x14 (the request's starting sector number). Offsets 3 to 0x0c -- the status word and the eight reserved bytes -- are left as they lie; the driver fills the status. memcpy copies the 0x18 bytes into the DOS real-mode transfer buffer whose linear address is held in data_fdps_cd_request_header_buffer, then fdps_cd_device_request hands the request to the CD-ROM device driver through real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h. The routine finishes through the shared epilogue at 0003bea0, reached by a tail JMP with the header size 0x18 already pushed as the memcpy count; that epilogue is the cross-jumped tail of fdps_cd_set_audio_channel_control and copies the header back out of the transfer buffer, stores the driver's status word from header offset 3 into data_fdps_cd_last_request_status, drops the 0x18-byte frame and returns. data_fdps_cd_last_request_status is the status word fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy and fdps_cd_audio_is_idle test.

Parameters:
  sector -- HSG logical sector to seek to, counted from the start of the disc; the units fdps_cd_msf_to_sector produces (minutes*4500 + seconds*75 + frames - 150). Nothing in the image calls this routine, so no caller pins the value further.

Returns:
  Nothing. The driver's status reaches the caller only through data_fdps_cd_last_request_status; the EAX left by the shared epilogue is the raw dword read at header offset 3 and is not a result.

Pool: fdps  [no FID candidate in either library set; calls the game routine fdps_cd_device_request and shares the CD transfer-buffer global data_fdps_cd_request_header_buffer with the rest of the game's MSCDEX wrappers]

=== 0003c452 [PLATE]
Issues the MSCDEX Play Audio request that starts CD-DA playback over one range of disc sectors.

Algorithm:
Builds a 22-byte (0x16) MSCDEX device request header in a 0x18-byte stack frame: header length 0x16 at +0, subunit 0 at +1, command code 0x84 (Play Audio) at +2, addressing mode 0 (HSG / logical sector) at +0x0d, start_sector as a dword at +0x0e, and the sector count end_sector - start_sector as a dword at +0x12. The status word and reserved area at +3..+0x0c are not written; the driver fills them in. memcpy copies the packet into the real-mode transfer buffer whose flat address is held in DAT_00069de8, then fdps_cd_device_request hands it to the CD-ROM device driver through real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h. The routine finishes by pushing the header length 0x16 and tail-jumping to the shared CD request epilogue at 0x0003bea0 (the merged tail inside FUN_0003be36), which copies the packet back out of the transfer buffer, records the driver's status word in DAT_00069e20 and releases the 0x18-byte frame. Playback is asynchronous: the request completes as soon as the driver accepts it, and fdps_cd_audio_is_idle reports when the range has finished playing.

Parameters:
  start_sector -- first disc sector to play, as a logical (HSG) sector number. fdps_cd_play_track passes DAT_00069dec, the track start published by fdps_cd_resolve_track_range.
  end_sector -- one past the last sector to play; the packet carries end_sector - start_sector as its sector count. Callers pass DAT_00069de4, the start of the following track or the disc's lead-out address.

Returns:
  Nothing. The driver's status word is left in DAT_00069e20 by the shared epilogue, and both callers discard whatever the epilogue leaves in EAX.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit; it builds the game's own MSCDEX request packets and shares the request-buffer pointer DAT_00069de8 with the neighbouring fdps_cd_* wrappers]

Rebuild note:
The sector-count field at packet offset +0x12 is written as a full dword (MOV dword ptr [ESP+0x12],EAX at 0003c482), which is what makes the header exactly 0x16 bytes long; Ghidra's decompilation renders it as a 16-bit store (local_6 = (undefined2)(end_sector - start_sector)). Emitting the obvious C from that decompilation gives a 2-byte count with two bytes of uninitialised stack garbage above it, so the driver is asked to play a wildly wrong number of sectors. The count must be a 32-bit field.

=== 0003c4ff [PLATE]
Resumes CD-DA playback that was halted earlier, by issuing the MSCDEX Resume Audio Play command to the CD-ROM device driver.

Algorithm:
  Probes 0x20 bytes of stack through __CHK, then opens a 0x10-byte frame that holds a 13-byte MSCDEX device request header. It fills three header fields and nothing else: byte 0 = 0x0d (header length), byte 1 = 0x00 (subunit), byte 2 = 0x88 (Resume Audio Play command code); the status word at +3 and the reserved bytes from +5 are left holding whatever was in the frame, which is what the driver expects for this command.
  It then jumps to 0003c4c2, the epilogue it shares with fdps_cd_stop_audio -- the two routines are identical apart from the command byte (0x88 here, 0x85 Stop Audio there) and the compiler tail-merged them. That shared trailer memcpy's the 13-byte header into the real-mode transfer buffer whose flat address is held in DAT_00069de8, calls fdps_cd_device_request to hand the request to the driver via real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h, memcpy's the 13 bytes back out of the transfer buffer, stores the header's status word (offset +3) into DAT_00069e20, releases the frame and returns.

Parameters:
  none.

Returns:
  nothing. The driver's reply is published in the CD status global DAT_00069e20, where fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy reads it.

Pool: fdps  [game CD-audio code; no Function ID hit in either library set]

=== 0003c51c [PLATE]
Issues one MSCDEX IOCTL Output request whose control block is a single command byte, for the drive commands that carry no data of their own.

Algorithm:
Builds a 0x18-byte DOS device-driver request header in a stack local: header length 0x18, subunit 0, command code 0x0c (IOCTL Output), media descriptor 0, transfer address = the real-mode segment:offset of the IOCTL control-block buffer held in DAT_00069da8, transfer byte count 1. The status word at header+3 and the eight reserved bytes are left as they lie; the driver fills the status in. The start-sector and volume-ID-pointer fields at struct offsets 0x14 and 0x16 are left as they lie too -- there is no store at [ESP+0x14] or [ESP+0x16] anywhere in 0003c51c..0003c5a5 -- and because the header declares itself 0x18 long against a 26-byte record, offsets 0x14 through 0x17 reach the driver as live stack, unlike the IOCTL Input siblings, which zero both (0003bdb4 and 0003bdbc in 0003bd99). Stores command_code into a one-byte stack local, then memcpy's the header into the real-mode request-header buffer at DAT_00069de8 and that one byte into the real-mode control-block buffer at DAT_00069da4. Calls fdps_cd_device_request, which hands the header to MSCDEX through real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h. memcpy's the 0x18 header bytes back out of DAT_00069de8 and stores the returned status word (header+3) into DAT_00069e20, the global that fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy reads.

Everything from the control-block copy onward is a tail shared with fdps_cd_set_door_lock: that function builds its own two-byte control block, pushes a count of 2 and jumps to 0x0003c56b.

Parameters:
  command_code -- MSCDEX IOCTL Output control block code, used as a byte. fdps_cd_close_tray passes 5 (Close Tray); the same request shape also carries 0 (Eject Disk) and 2 (Reset Drive).

Returns:
  Nothing. The outcome is the driver's request-header status word, left in DAT_00069e20.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit on either library set; calls fdps_cd_device_request, a function of the game's own source]

=== 0003c5a6 [PLATE]
Fetches the CD-ROM drive's audio Q-channel into a caller-supplied 11-byte control block, so the caller can see which track is playing and how far into that track the drive has got.

Algorithm:
Writes MSCDEX IOCTL-input control code 0x0c (Audio Q-Channel Info) into q_channel[0], then builds a 26-byte DOS device request header on the stack: length 0x1a, subunit 0, command 3 (IOCTL input), media descriptor 0, transfer address = the real-mode seg:0000 far pointer of the CD control-block buffer published in data_fdps_cd_ioctl_buffer_real_mode_ptr by fdps_cd_alloc_dos_buffers, byte count 6, starting sector 0, volume-ID pointer 0. Rebuild note:
The request header asks for a 6-byte transfer while the control block it points at is 11 bytes, and the caller reads the frame field at offset 6 -- one byte past the declared count. Writing the obvious C, i.e. setting the byte count to sizeof the Q-channel block (11) or to the 0x0b both memcpy's use, changes what the game asks the CD driver for; keep the literal 6.

=== 0003c6bc [PLATE]
Closes the CD-ROM drive tray and reports whether the drive came back not busy.

Algorithm:
Probes 8 bytes of stack through the Watcom __CHK stub, then calls the MSCDEX IOCTL-Output request builder fdps_cd_ioctl_output_command with control block code 5, which is Close Tray in the MSCDEX IOCTL Output control block table, and cleans that one stacked argument off with ADD ESP,4. The body has no RET of its own: it ends at 0003c6cf and runs straight on into fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy at 0003c6d0, which supplies the return value by testing bit 0x0200 -- the DOS device-driver request-header BUSY bit -- of the status word fdps_cd_ioctl_output_command latched into DAT_00069e20. That run-on is this routine's tail call to the predicate, with the JMP dropped because the target happens to be the next function; fdps_cd_audio_is_idle makes the same tail call from further away and still carries an explicit JMP 0003c6d0.

Nothing in the image calls this entry or references its address. That is the norm for this CD layer rather than a sign of misidentification: most of its entry points are equally unreferenced and the module survives because it was linked whole.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  ushort -- 1 when the BUSY bit of the status word that the Close Tray request left in DAT_00069e20 is clear, 0 when it is still set.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit on either library set; its only real callee is game code that marshals MSCDEX device requests, which a third-party library object could not reference]

Rebuild note:
This function has no RET of its own -- the 20 bytes at 0003c6bc end in ADD ESP,4 and run into the predicate at 0003c6d0. Emitting only what Ghidra shows inside the body gives void fdps_cd_close_tray(void) { fdps_cd_ioctl_output_command(5); }, which silently drops the 0/1 status the original hands back. The rebuilt source must end in that value: either return fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy(); -- the reading fdps_cd_audio_is_idle's explicit tail JMP to the same address supports -- or the DAT_00069e20 BUSY-bit test written out again. Both are functionally equivalent; a void body is not.

=== 0003c6d0 [PLATE]
Predicate on the CD-ROM driver's last request: returns 1 when the BUSY bit of the saved MSCDEX request-header status word is clear.

Algorithm:
Loads the 16-bit status word that the CD request routines saved at data_fdps_cd_last_request_status, masks it down to bit 9 alone (XOR AL,AL drops the error-code byte, AND AH,0x2 keeps 0x0200, the BUSY bit of the DOS device-driver request-header status word), and returns SETZ of that mask: 1 when the bit is clear, 0 when it is set. It touches no other memory and calls nothing.

The body is also the shared tail of the two routines that lead into it, both of which end with this same test in their C source. fdps_cd_close_tray issues its IOCTL Output request through fdps_cd_ioctl_output_command and then falls straight through at 0003c6d0, having no RET of its own; fdps_cd_audio_is_idle calls fdps_cdrom_read_device_status for the device-status IOCTL and tail-jumps here at 0003c6f7. data_fdps_cd_last_request_status itself is written by fdps_cd_ioctl_output_command at 0003c59c and on the path out of fdps_cdrom_read_device_status, in each case from the request header copied back out of the real-mode transfer buffer at data_fdps_cd_request_header_buffer after fdps_cd_device_request.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  1 when the saved status word's BUSY bit (0x0200) is clear -- the driver reports no request or audio playback in progress -- and 0 when it is set.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit on either the Watcom or the AIL set, and the one datum it touches is the CD status global that the game's own CD layer writes]

Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code; the callee/predicate pair implements the documented MSCDEX 'is audio still playing' query, and the caller is the CD music repeat poll.
Boundary: 0003c6e8-0003c6f8, ends at the JMP tail call at 0003c6f7; gap_after is empty and 0003c6f9 opens the next function with its own PUSH/CALL __CHK prologue.
Signature: __watcall, no arguments (the pushed 4 is the Watcom __CHK stack-probe size at 0004361a, not a request code); returns a 16-bit 0/1 flag in AX -- 1 = BUSY clear, audio idle.

=== 0003c6f9 [PLATE]
Asks the CD-ROM driver whether the disc has been swapped since the last time it was asked, and hands back MSCDEX's media-change byte.

Algorithm:
Builds a 26-byte MSCDEX device request header in its 0x20-byte stack frame: length 0x1a, subunit 0, command code 3 (IOCTL Input), media descriptor 0 at +0x0d, transfer address at +0x0e taken from DAT_00069da8 (the real-mode seg:off of the control-block buffer), transfer byte count 2 at +0x12, start sector 0 at +0x14 and volume-ID pointer 0 at +0x16. Beside the header, at frame+0x1c, it builds the 2-byte IOCTL Input control block whose first byte is subcommand 9, Media Changed; the second byte is the driver's answer and is not initialised on the way out. memcpy copies the header into the real-mode request buffer at DAT_00069de8 and the control block into the real-mode data buffer at DAT_00069da4, fdps_cd_device_request issues the driver call, and two further memcpy calls copy both blocks back out of those buffers. The header's returned status word (header+3) is then stored into DAT_00069e20 -- the same global fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy tests for the BUSY bit -- and the control block's answer byte is returned.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  The MSCDEX media-change byte, zero-extended into AX: 1 means the disc has not been changed, 0 means the driver cannot tell, 0xff means the disc has been changed. It is not a boolean and it is not a 0/1 predicate. The upper half of EAX still holds header bytes 5 and 6 left over from the status-word load and carries no meaning.

Pool: fdps  [calls the game function fdps_cd_device_request, which a compiled library object could not; no Function ID hit in the Watcom or ail sets]

Rebuild note:
The returned byte is MSCDEX's tri-state media-change value, where 1 means the disc has NOT changed, 0 means unknown and 0xff means it has changed -- writing the obvious 'return changed != 0;' or treating the result as a boolean inverts the common case. Separately, the epilogue is MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESP+0x3] followed by a 16-bit MOVZX AX,byte ptr [ESP+0x1d], so only AX is meaningful and the top half of EAX still holds request-header bytes 5 and 6; the return type must stay a 16-bit type or a rewrite will hand callers a cleanly zero-extended EAX the original never produced.

=== 0003c7aa [PLATE]
Locks or unlocks the CD-ROM drive door, so the disc cannot be swapped while the game is using it.

Algorithm:
Builds a 0x18-byte MSCDEX device-driver request header in a 0x1c-byte stack frame: byte 0 = header length 0x18, byte 1 = subunit 0, byte 2 = command 0x0c (IOCTL Output), byte 0x0d = media descriptor 0, dword 0x0e = the real-mode address of the control-block transfer buffer taken from data_fdps_cd_ioctl_buffer_real_mode_ptr, word 0x12 = transfer length 2. Directly behind the header, at frame offset 0x18, it lays down the 2-byte IOCTL Output control block { 0x01 = Lock/Unlock Door, lock }. memcpy copies the 0x18-byte header into the real-mode request buffer whose flat address is held in data_fdps_cd_request_header_buffer; the routine then pushes the control-block length 2 and jumps to 0x0003c56b, the shared request tail it has in common with fdps_cd_ioctl_output_command. That tail memcpys the control block into the real-mode transfer buffer at data_fdps_cd_ioctl_buffer, calls fdps_cd_device_request to hand the request to the CD-ROM driver, copies the header back out of data_fdps_cd_request_header_buffer, latches its status word (header offset 3) into data_fdps_cd_last_request_status -- which is what fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy reads -- and returns.
The header fields this routine never writes (the status word at +3, the reserved bytes 5..0x0c, the start sector at +0x14 and the low half of the volume-ID pointer at +0x16..+0x17) reach the driver holding whatever the stack frame happened to contain; MSCDEX ignores them for an IOCTL Output request. The staging memcpy copies 0x18 bytes and stops there, so the volume-ID pointer's high half at +0x18..+0x19 is never staged at all -- in this frame those two bytes are the Lock/Unlock Door control block, not part of the header.

Parameters:
  lock -- door state to request: 1 locks the drive door, 0 unlocks it. Taken as a single byte from the first stack argument and written straight into the second byte of the MSCDEX Lock/Unlock Door control block.

Returns:
  Nothing. Whether the drive accepted the command is left in the request status word at data_fdps_cd_last_request_status.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the ailv3.lib symbol set, and the body reaches fdps_cd_device_request, the game's own MSCDEX plumbing, which no vendor library object could call into]

Rebuild note:
The terminating JMP looks like a tail call to a helper, but 0x0003c56b is a label inside fdps_cd_ioctl_output_command, so a rewrite cannot call it -- both C functions must carry their own copy of that tail, including the part that latches the request header's status word into data_fdps_cd_last_request_status. Drop that latch from either one and fdps_cd_status_is_not_busy afterwards reports on whatever request ran before, silently.

=== 0003c803 [PLATE]
Resolves the disc address range of the CD-ROM track that fdps_cdrom_read_track_info queried last, publishing it in the play-range globals so the caller can hand that range to the Play Audio request.

Algorithm:
Copies the queried track's start address out of DAT_00069e01 into the range-start global DAT_00069dec. Reads the queried track number from DAT_00069dff and the disc's highest track number from DAT_00069e07, the latter published by fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info. When track + 1 is past the highest track the queried track is the last one on the disc, so the range end DAT_00069de4 takes the lead-out address DAT_00069e0b and the routine returns. Otherwise it calls fdps_cdrom_read_track_info for track + 1, which republishes DAT_00069e01 as the next track's start address; that value becomes the range end in DAT_00069de4, and a second call to fdps_cdrom_read_track_info for the original track number puts the track-info globals (DAT_00069e01, DAT_00069dff, DAT_00069e05) back on the track the caller had selected. The range end is exclusive: fdps_cd_play_audio_range takes the pair as (start, end) and sends end - start as the sector count of the Play Audio request. Every fdps_cdrom_read_track_info call is a real MSCDEX IOCTL-Input request, so the non-last-track path costs two extra device requests.

The closing restore call is state hygiene, not a dependency: no reader anywhere in the program observes what it republishes. DAT_00069e01 is read only here and in fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors, DAT_00069dff only here and at fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors:0003c1b4, DAT_00069e05 only in fdps_cd_track_is_audio -- and each of those reads follows that function's own track query. fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors runs the same idiom, saving the selected track at 0003c1b4 and restoring it at 0003c1ff, so the shared CD state block is treated throughout as caller-owned state a helper must put back.

Parameters:
  none -- the track acted on is whichever one fdps_cdrom_read_track_info queried last, held in DAT_00069dff.

Returns:
  Nothing. The result is the pair DAT_00069dec (range start) and DAT_00069de4 (range end, exclusive), and the two globals are read separately rather than consumed as a pair: fdps_cd_play_track reads both -- DAT_00069dec at 0003c883 as the range start and DAT_00069de4 at 0003c87d as the range end -- into fdps_cd_play_audio_range, while fdps_cd_play_track_range calls this routine twice and takes only the range start from the first call (0003c8b6) and only the range end from the second (0003c8cf).

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom libraries or ailv3.lib; shares the CD track-state globals with fdps_cd_play_track and fdps_cd_stop_audio, and carries the PUSH n / CALL __CHK prologue of compiled game code]

Rebuild note:
The second fdps_cdrom_read_track_info call at 0003c851 must be kept even though nothing reads the globals it restores. It is a real MSCDEX IOCTL-Input request to the drive, so dropping it as dead code -- the obvious simplification once you notice DAT_00069e01/DAT_00069dff/DAT_00069e05 have no surviving reader -- changes how many device requests a track change costs. The same restore appears in fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors at 0003c205 and is equally unobserved; both are the CD block's convention of putting the shared track selection back, and both stay.

=== 0003c85b [PLATE]
Starts CD-DA playback of a single track: halts any audio in progress, selects the requested track, resolves its start and end positions, then issues the play request for that range.
Pool: fdps  [no library match; game CD-audio module]
Evidence: Function ID is empty against both the Watcom libraries and ailv3.lib (0 candidates either side, hash unique in the image), so no vendor bytes. Its four call sites sit in three game CD routines (fdps_cd_set_music_track at 00030c34, fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll at 00030c9f, and fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track at both 00030ed4 and 00030f23) and it calls fdps_cd_stop_audio plus the FUN_0003c0c8 / FUN_0003c803 / FUN_0003c452 cluster that shares the globals at 00069de4 and 00069dec. Neither CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 nor Miles AIL 3.02 does red-book track control, and 55 bytes of parameterised logic is no linker island. The only vendor symbol touched is __CHK, the Watcom stack probe.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code, describing the observed sequence; no library symbol identified.
Boundary: 0003c85b-0003c891, entry is the PUSH 0xc / CALL __CHK probe, the RET follows the ADD ESP,0x8 that balances the frame, and 0003c892 opens the next function with the same probe prologue; gap_after is empty.
Signature: __cdecl void fdps_cd_play_track(short track) - the argument is read with MOVSX from [ESP+4] and the plain RET leaves cleanup to the caller; EAX is never set deliberately, so the return is void.
Body: 1. PUSH 0xc; CALL __CHK, the stack-overflow probe for 12 bytes (it pops its own argument, so ESP is unchanged on return). 2. CALL fdps_cd_stop_audio to halt any track currently playing. 3. MOVSX of the 16-bit track argument, passed to fdps_cdrom_read_track_info which selects/queries the requested track (caller cleans the 4 bytes). 4. CALL fdps_cd_resolve_track_range, the only writer of 00069dec and 00069de4; it derives the playback start and end positions for the selected track (00069de4 is written on two paths, so the end position is conditional). 5. PUSH [00069de4] then [00069dec] and CALL fdps_cd_play_audio_range, which therefore receives (start, end) and performs the actual play request; the 8 bytes are cleaned here.

=== 0003c892 [PLATE]
Starts CD-DA playback of a run of consecutive CD tracks, from the start of the first track through to the end of the last, and reports how long that run is.

Algorithm:
Halts whatever is playing with fdps_cd_stop_audio. Selects first_track with fdps_cdrom_read_track_info and calls fdps_cd_resolve_track_range, which publishes the selected track's start sector in data_fdps_cd_play_range_start_sector (00069dec) and its end sector in data_fdps_cd_play_range_end_sector (00069de4); the start sector is latched out of data_fdps_cd_play_range_start_sector here, because the second resolve overwrites both globals. Repeats the same pair for last_track and keeps only the end sector from data_fdps_cd_play_range_end_sector. Hands the two latched sector numbers to fdps_cd_play_audio_range(start_sector, end_sector) as one continuous play request, then returns end minus start.

Parameters:
  first_track -- 1-based CD track number playback starts at, the same numbering fdps_cd_play_track and fdps_cdrom_read_track_info take; read sign-extended from a 16-bit stack slot.
  last_track -- 1-based CD track number playback stops at. Its end sector bounds the range, so this track is played in full. Not checked against first_track.

Returns:
  The length of the play range in CD sectors (frames), end sector minus start sector. It comes out negative when last_track precedes first_track, since neither argument is validated.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom 10.0x or the ailv3.lib set; game-side CD audio sequencing over the CD state globals shared with fdps_cd_play_track]

Rebuild note:
fdps_cd_resolve_track_range rewrites both data_fdps_cd_play_range_start_sector and data_fdps_cd_play_range_end_sector on every call, so the start sector has to be read after the first resolve and before the second. Issuing both resolve calls and then reading the two globals -- the obvious way to write it -- yields last_track's start sector and plays the wrong range.

=== 0003c8e6 [PLATE]
Plays the whole game CD as audio: everything from the first sector of the disc through to the lead-out.

Algorithm:
Probes 12 bytes of stack with __CHK, then silences any playback in progress with fdps_cd_stop_audio. Asks the drive for track 1's audio track info through fdps_cdrom_read_track_info(1), which refreshes the track-info globals -- track number in data_fdps_cd_track_info_track_number, track start sector in data_fdps_cd_track_start_sector, control byte in data_fdps_cd_track_info_control_flags -- none of which this routine reads back. Calls fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info to refresh the disc summary; that leaves the highest track number in data_fdps_cd_highest_track_number and the lead-out address, converted to a logical sector number, in data_fdps_cd_leadout_sector. Finally hands (0, data_fdps_cd_leadout_sector) to fdps_cd_play_audio_range, which issues MSCDEX Play Audio (command code 0x84) starting at sector 0 for data_fdps_cd_leadout_sector sectors: the whole disc from its very first sector, not from where track 1's audio begins. That last call is reached by a JMP to 0x0003c889 -- the identical three-instruction tail of fdps_cd_play_track, which the compiler merged with this one. No code in the program calls this routine.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no library match in either the watcom or the ail Function ID set; its callees, the CD state globals it shares and its merged tail are all game CD code]

Rebuild note:
The obvious C rewrite passes track 1's start sector as the beginning of the play range, because the call that resolves it sits two lines above; the original passes the literal 0, so playback starts at the very first sector of the disc (the data track on this game's mixed-mode CD) rather than where track 1's audio begins. Write the 0 literally and keep the fdps_cdrom_read_track_info(1) call whose result is discarded.

=== 0003c911 [PLATE]
Reports whether one CD-ROM track holds CD-DA audio rather than data.

Algorithm:
Probes 8 bytes of stack through the Watcom __CHK stub, then calls fdps_cdrom_read_track_info with the track number. That routine issues the MSCDEX IOCTL-Input request with control block 0x0b (Read Audio Track Info) for the track and leaves the track's Q-channel ADR/control byte, masked with 0xd0, in DAT_00069e05. This function reads DAT_00069e05 back and returns whether it differs from 0x40, the masked control value of a data track; every audio-track control value survives the mask as something else. The other fields fdps_cdrom_read_track_info publishes for the track -- its Red Book start address at DAT_00069e01 and its track number at DAT_00069dff -- are left for other callers and are not looked at here.

Nothing in the shipped image calls this: it is part of the unused API surface of the CD-ROM module, half of whose functions are linked in but never referenced.

Parameters:
  track -- CD-ROM track number, as the MSCDEX audio-track-info control block takes it; a signed 16-bit value, the same argument fdps_cd_play_track forwards to fdps_cdrom_read_track_info.

Returns:
1 when the track is an audio track, 0 when it is a data track.

Pool: fdps  [no FID hit in either library set and the body hash is unique in the image; the PUSH 0x8 / CALL __CHK prologue is what the compiler emits for game source, and the body reads the game's CD globals]

Rebuild note:
The function has no result of its own to hand back: it depends on fdps_cdrom_read_track_info having just written DAT_00069e05, so a rewrite must keep both the call and the global. Folding the two into one function that returns the control byte would break fdps_cd_get_track_length_sectors and fdps_cd_resolve_track_range, which call the same routine and pick different fields (DAT_00069e01, DAT_00069dff) out of the same globals. The test is also an exact equality against the masked byte -- CMP 0x40 after the callee's AND 0xd0 -- not a bit test; write the equality the binary writes rather than the `(control & 0x40) == 0` that reads more naturally, which is equivalent only for the Red Book-legal control values and only while the callee's mask stays 0xd0.

=== 0003c93a [PLATE]
Reads how far CD-DA playback has got: asks the CD-ROM driver for the audio Q-channel and hands the caller the track now playing and the running time inside that track.

Algorithm:
Calls fdps_cd_read_q_channel on the 11-byte MSCDEX IOCTL-input control block at 0x00069e56; that routine stamps control code 0x0c (Audio Q-Channel Info) into the block, wraps it in a 26-byte DOS device request (length 0x1a, subunit 0, command 3) and issues it through fdps_cd_device_request, so the driver's reply comes back in the same block. Four byte fields of the reply are then copied out through the caller's pointers, in the order the code writes them: block+2 (TNO, the track playing now) to *track, block+6 (FRAME) to *frame, block+5 (SEC) to *second, and block+4 (MIN) to *minute. The MIN store is not spelled out here: AL is loaded with block+4 and the body jumps to 0x0003bc71, the shared "MOV EDX,[ESP+8] / MOV [EDX],AL / RET" tail that sits inside fdps_cd_unpack_msf, which stores through the same second-argument slot and returns. The MIN/SEC/FRAME triple is the position within the current track; the driver reports the absolute position on the disc at block+8..+10 and this routine does not read it. Nothing in the program calls this entry.

Parameters:
  track -- pointer to the byte that receives the number of the track playing now (Q-channel TNO field).
  minute -- pointer to the byte that receives the minutes of the running time within that track.
  second -- pointer to the byte that receives the seconds of that running time, 0-59.
  frame -- pointer to the byte that receives the frames of that running time, 0-74 (1/75 second each).

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; it drives MSCDEX through fdps_cd_device_request, and no CRT or AIL routine does that, and it is compiled project C: a standard-shape body reading its four arguments from the stack, calling fdps_cd_read_q_channel and touching only game globals. Separately, the PUSH 0x8 / CALL __CHK prologue records that this function belongs to the 0003bade-0003c96x block, the one part of the game code built without -s]

Rebuild note:
This routine reads the Q-channel FRAME field at block+6 even though the request its callee issues declares a 6-byte transfer, so block+6 is one byte past what the driver was asked to fill. Both halves of that mismatch have to survive a rebuild untouched: do not 'fix' the count on the fdps_cd_read_q_channel side (the owner of that literal 6), and do not drop or guard the frame read here on the grounds that the byte looks untransferred. Writing either the obvious count or the obvious validity check changes what the game asks the CD driver for and what it reports back.

=== 0003c97c [PLATE]
Initialiser image for the four-byte local signature buffer of AIL_internal_lx_image_size: the C string "  " (0x20 0x20 0x00 0x00).

Read exactly once, by the first instruction of AIL_internal_lx_image_size's body (MOV EAX,[0x0003c97c] at 0003cbca), which copies all four bytes into the stack slot at ESP+0xc8. That slot is then handed to AIL_internal_read_block as a 2-byte destination for the bytes at the file's e_lfanew offset, and then to strcmp against the "LX" literal at 00062258 to decide whether the file is a linear executable. The two trailing zeroes are what terminates the string for that strcmp -- the read fills only bytes 0 and 1 -- and the two spaces are a value that cannot compare equal to "LX", so a file whose header could not be read is rejected rather than accepted. Nothing writes this image; it is read-only data sitting in .object1 among the code, four bytes ahead of the twin image at 0003c980 that serves the matching load pass FUN_0003ccf8 and eight ahead of AIL_internal_read_block itself.

Pool: binary_artifact  [compiler output backing a local aggregate initialiser, not a variable the source declared; the owning function is ail, but naming.md puts emitted images in binary_artifact whoever owns them]

Rebuild note:
The declaration must keep both the length and the initialiser: the signature buffer is four bytes and is initialised before use, while only two of them are ever read from the file. Writing the obvious `char sig[2];` or an uninitialised `char sig[4];` leaves no NUL after the two signature bytes, and the strcmp against "LX" then runs into whatever the stack held; the spaces also matter, because they are the value strcmp sees when the header read fails and are what makes that case return 0 instead of matching by accident.

=== 0003c980 [PLATE]
Initialiser image for the LX-signature scratch buffer in the driver-image loader: the four bytes "  \0\0".

Nothing writes it; it is read once, by the prologue of FUN_0003ccf8 (the load-and-relocate pass of the AIL linear-executable driver loader), which copies the dword into its local 4-byte buffer at ESP+0x28c before doing anything else. FUN_0003ccf8 then reads the 2-byte executable signature from the file at offset e_lfanew into that buffer and calls strcmp against the "LX" literal at 00062258; a match lets the loader go on to the 0xac-byte header, the object table and the fixups, a mismatch makes it close the file and return 0. The two leading spaces are a value that can never equal "LX", so a read that does not happen leaves the compare failing; the two trailing zero bytes are what terminates the string for strcmp, since the read itself deposits only 2 bytes and its return value is ignored. The identical image at 0003c97c is the same initialiser emitted separately for the sizing pass, AIL_internal_lx_image_size.

Pool: binary_artifact  [compiler output -- the constant image of a function-local array initialiser, consumed by value and never addressed; the enclosing function is ail, the datum is not]

Rebuild note:
The trailing 00 00 is not padding. FUN_0003ccf8 reads only 2 bytes into this buffer and then calls strcmp on it, so the NULs from the initialiser are the terminator; declaring the local as an uninitialised char[4], or as char sig[2] = "  " (legal C, no terminator), makes strcmp run into adjacent stack and the signature check stop being reliable. Keep it as char sig[4] = "  ";.

=== 0003c9eb [PLATE]
Installs a new memory-release callback into the AIL free-hook slot at 0x00060384 and returns the previously installed one.
Pool: ail  [shared data with ail_code.obj; every reader of the slot is AIL, one of them a Function ID hit]
