=== 0003ca49 [PLATE]
Allocates a block of DOS conventional memory through DPMI INT 31h function 0100h and page-locks it, handing the caller the block's linear address, its real-mode far pointer and its protected-mode selector.

Algorithm:
Builds a Watcom union REGS on the stack with eax = 0x100 (DPMI Allocate DOS Memory Block) and ebx = paragraphs, and issues it with int386(0x31, &in, &out). When out.cflag is non-zero the allocation failed: the routine leaves every out-parameter untouched and returns 0. Otherwise it publishes the returned real-mode segment (out.eax) three ways -- *out_real_mode_ptr = seg << 16, the far pointer seg:0000; *out_linear = (seg & 0xffff) << 4, the flat linear address of the same byte; *out_selector = out.edx & 0xffff, the protected-mode selector DPMI created alongside the block and the handle fdps_dpmi_free_dos_memory needs to give it back. It then locks the whole block into physical memory with fdps_dpmi_lock_region(linear, linear + paragraphs * 16 - 1), recomputing the start as *out_real_mode_ptr >> 12 and the byte size as paragraphs << 4, and discards that call's result. Returns 1.

Parameters:
  paragraphs -- size of the block in 16-byte paragraphs, passed to DPMI in BX and multiplied by 16 to get the byte size of the locked range. Comes from the Miles AIL driver loaders, sized from a driver image.
  out_linear -- receives the flat linear address of the block (segment * 16). Written only on success.
  out_real_mode_ptr -- receives the block as a real-mode far pointer, segment in the high half and offset 0 in the low half. Written only on success.
  out_selector -- receives the protected-mode selector DPMI allocated for the block, the argument fdps_dpmi_free_dos_memory takes. Written only on success.

Returns:
  1 when the DPMI allocation succeeded, whether or not the page lock did; 0 when DPMI returned with CF set, in which case none of the three out-parameters has been written.

Pool: fdps  [game-written DPMI wrapper module -- the fn 0x100/0x101/0x600/0x601 group that the AIL vendor objects reach through EXTDEF; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the AIL set]

Rebuild note:
The result of fdps_dpmi_lock_region is thrown away: this routine returns 1 whenever DPMI fn 0100h succeeded, even if the page lock failed, and on the failure path it leaves all three out-parameters untouched rather than zeroing them. Writing the obvious C -- return fdps_dpmi_lock_region(...), or clearing the out-parameters up front -- changes what the AIL driver loaders see.

=== 0003cad2 [PLATE]
Frees a DOS conventional-memory block that DPMI function 0100h allocated, by handing DPMI back the block's selector.

Algorithm:
Reserves 0x38 bytes for an adjacent pair of Watcom union REGS -- the input register set at ESP+0x00 and the output set at ESP+0x1c, 0x1c bytes each (eax, ebx, ecx, edx, esi, edi, cflag). Stores 0x101, the DPMI Free DOS Memory Block function code, into the EAX slot, and selector & 0xffff into the EDX slot at ESP+0x0c, which is where fn 0101h expects the selector. Calls int386(0x31, &in, &out) to issue the DPMI services interrupt and drops its three arguments with ADD ESP,0xc. No other slot of the input set is written, so the remaining registers enter the interrupt holding whatever the stack already contained; fn 0101h reads only AX and DX. The output set is never examined -- the carry flag at ESP+0x34 is discarded, so a failed free is silent. The prologue is a bare SUB ESP with no stack probe.

Only the third argument is read. The first two are the linear address and the real-mode far pointer of the same block, carried for symmetry with the three-output allocator at 0x0003ca49. There are eight call sites, and every one of them pushes the three values out of driver descriptor fields the allocator filled -- but from two different descriptors. AIL_internal_install_driver_inner and AIL_internal_uninstall_driver_inner use +0x08 (linear address), +0x00 (real-mode far pointer) and +0x04 (selector). AIL_internal_dig_driver_setup_full, which holds five of the eight call sites, and AIL_internal_dig_driver_teardown use +0x28, +0x20 and +0x24 of the larger dig-driver descriptor.

Parameters:
  linear_unused -- protected-mode linear address of the block, as the allocator at 0x0003ca49 wrote it (real-mode segment << 4). Never read.
  segment_unused -- the block's real-mode far pointer, segment in the high 16 bits and offset zero, as the allocator at 0x0003ca49 wrote it (real-mode segment << 16). Never read.
  selector -- the DPMI selector that fn 0100h returned for this block. Masked to 16 bits and loaded into DX; the only argument the body uses.

Returns:
  Nothing. The DPMI carry flag is discarded, so callers cannot distinguish a failed free from a successful one.

Pool: fdps  [the game's own DPMI service module, which the AIL vendor objects reach across the EXTDEF seam; no Function ID hit in either library, and it reaches the interrupt through the public int386 API rather than an inline INT, which is how a client uses the runtime and not how the runtime is built]

Rebuild note:
The vendor AIL objects call this with three pushed dwords and ADD ESP,0xc, so the rebuild must define all three parameters even though only the third is read. Writing the obvious one-argument free(selector) still links and, being __cdecl, still balances the stack -- but the body then reads the block's linear address where the selector should be, and because the DPMI carry flag is discarded every DOS low-memory free fails silently instead of reporting an error.

=== 0003cb01 [PLATE]
Locks a range of linear memory into physical memory through DPMI function 0x0600, so the pages stay resident while interrupt-time code touches them.

Algorithm:
Reserves a 0x38-byte stack frame holding a Watcom union REGS in/out pair (in block at ESP+0, out block at ESP+0x1c). Normalizes the two endpoints with an unsigned compare (CMP start,end and the two JNC arms), so callers may pass them in either order: base = min(start, end) lands in EAX and size = max(start, end) - base + 1 in EDX. The +1 means end is read as the address of the last byte of the range, not one past it. Stores 0x600 -- DPMI Lock Linear Region -- into the in block's EAX slot, then base>>16 and base&0xffff into the EBX and ECX slots and size>>16 and size&0xffff into the ESI and EDI slots, which is how fn 0x0600 takes its starting linear address in BX:CX and its byte count in SI:DI. The EDX slot is never written. Calls int386(0x31, &in, &out), then tests the out block's carry-flag word at ESP+0x34 and returns 1 when it is zero.

The stretch from 0x0003cb24 to the RET is a shared tail: fdps_dpmi_unlock_region at 0x0003cb6e does the same endpoint arithmetic, stores 0x601 instead, and jumps into 0x0003cb24 rather than carrying an epilogue of its own.

Parameters:
  start -- one endpoint of the linear byte range to lock, a flat address inside the LE image or in BSS. Callers pass the first byte of a code extent (0x4478c, 0x4b370, 0x477f4), the address of an AIL module static, or, from fdps_dpmi_lock_size, that function's base argument.
  end -- the other endpoint, also a flat linear address. The larger of the two is treated as the last byte of the range. fdps_dpmi_lock_size passes base + size here, so a block requested as (base, size) is locked as size + 1 bytes.

Returns:
  int -- 1 when the DPMI host returned with the carry flag clear, i.e. the range is locked; 0 when the call failed. fdps_dpmi_lock_size passes it straight back to its own caller; the AIL module-init routines and FUN_0003ca49 discard it.

Pool: fdps  [the game's own DPMI service module, which the vendored AIL objects reach across the EXTDEF seam -- no FID hit in either the Watcom or the AIL library set, and FD2 carries the same six-wrapper module in the same order at the same sizes]

Rebuild note:
end is the last byte of the range, not one past it: the byte count sent to DPMI is (max - min) + 1, so writing the obvious size = end - start locks one byte less than the original. It bites through fdps_dpmi_lock_size, which passes end = base + size and therefore makes the original lock size + 1 bytes -- when base + size falls exactly on a page boundary the original pins one page more than the caller asked for, and a rebuild that drops the +1 leaves that page pageable under an interrupt handler. Also keep the return sense inverted from the hardware: 1 means carry clear, i.e. success.

=== 0003cb6e [PLATE]
Unlocks a DPMI-locked range of linear memory so its pages may be paged out again; the counterpart of the fn 0x0600 lock primitive fdps_dpmi_lock_region.

Algorithm:
Normalizes the two endpoints with an unsigned min/max (CMP start,end then the two JNC arms reading the same flags), so callers may pass them in either order: base = min(start, end) in EAX, size = max(start, end) - base + 1 in EDX. The +1 means end is treated as the address of the LAST byte of the range, not one past it. Stores 0x0601, DPMI Unlock Linear Region, into the EAX slot of a 0x38-byte union REGS in/out pair built on the stack, then jumps to 0x0003cb24, the shared tail inside fdps_dpmi_lock_region: that tail writes base>>16 and base&0xffff into the EBX and ECX slots and size>>16 and size&0xffff into the ESI and EDI slots (DPMI fn 0x0601 takes the starting linear address in BX:CX and the size in SI:DI), calls int386(0x31, &in, &out), and returns 1 when the out block's carry-flag word came back zero.

This body has no epilogue of its own. The ADD ESP,0x38 and the RET that end the call both belong to fdps_dpmi_lock_region; the only instruction that distinguishes the two entries is the 0x0601 store here versus the 0x0600 store there.

The in block is never cleared before use: only the EAX, EBX, ECX, ESI and EDI slots are written, so the EDX slot reaches the DPMI host holding stack garbage. Fn 0x0601 ignores EDX, so this is harmless. Like the rest of this module the body carries no __CHK stack probe and no EBP frame, and it destroys EBX without saving it.

Parameters:
  start -- one endpoint of the linear byte range to unlock, a flat address in the LE image or in BSS. Callers pass the start of a code extent (0x477f4, 0x45203) or, through fdps_dpmi_unlock_size, the base of a static data block.
  end -- the other endpoint, also a flat linear byte address. The larger of the two is taken as the last byte of the range. fdps_dpmi_unlock_size passes base + size here, so a range requested as (base, size) is unlocked as size + 1 bytes.

Returns:
  int -- 1 when the DPMI host cleared the carry flag, i.e. the range was unlocked; 0 on failure. The six AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_* callers discard it; fdps_dpmi_unlock_size passes it back to its own caller unchanged.

Pool: fdps  [the game's own DPMI service module, which AIL reaches across the EXTDEF seam -- no FID hit in either the Watcom libraries or ailv3.lib, and FD2 carries the same six-wrapper module in the same order and the same sizes]

Rebuild note:
Three ways the obvious C diverges here. (1) end is the address of the last byte of the range, not one past it: the size sent to DPMI is (max - min) + 1, so writing the obvious size = end - start unlocks one byte less than the original. It matters because fdps_dpmi_unlock_size passes end = base + size, which makes the original unlock size + 1 bytes -- when base + size lands exactly on a page boundary the original releases one page more than the caller asked for, and a rebuild that drops the +1 leaves that page locked. (2) The return sense is inverted from the hardware: 1 means the carry flag came back CLEAR, i.e. success. (3) The module must be compiled with stack checking off (#pragma off (check_stack), as FD2 does for the same six functions): no member has a __CHK probe, and they run on the AIL driver-setup path where the probe must not fire. What need NOT be reproduced is the missing EBX save -- the original destroys EBX in a __cdecl body, but only AIL vendor code and the module's own wrappers call in, and they treat EBX as scratch anyway, so letting the compiler preserve it is strictly safer.

=== 0003cb93 [PLATE]
Locks a memory block described as base address plus byte size into physical memory, so DPMI will not page it out while interrupt-time code touches it.

Algorithm:
Adds size to base to form the far endpoint of the block, then calls fdps_dpmi_lock_region with (base, base + size). That primitive takes two inclusive endpoints and asks DPMI function 0x0600 (Lock Linear Region) for (max - min) + 1 bytes, so the extent actually locked here is size + 1 bytes, one more than the caller named. Its return value is left in EAX untouched and becomes this function's result.

Every caller is an AIL vendor object reaching across the EXTDEF seam: the four once-only module bring-up routines page-lock their own code extent and their interrupt-touched statics through it, and AIL_internal_alloc_and_commit locks each block it allocates. The (start, end) form of the same operation is fdps_dpmi_lock_region; the undo is fdps_dpmi_unlock_size at 0x0003cbaa, a byte-identical twin over fdps_dpmi_unlock_region.

Parameters:
  base -- linear address of the first byte to lock. Callers pass the address of an AIL static block, of a heap block just allocated, or the first byte of a code range.
  size -- length of the block in bytes. Callers pass plain object sizes (4, 0x18, 0x40, 0x48, 0x80, 0x100) or, for code ranges, end minus start.

Returns:
  The lock primitive's success flag, passed through unchanged: 1 when the DPMI call returned with the carry flag clear, 0 when it failed.

Pool: fdps  [the game's own DPMI service module; every caller is an AIL vendor object referencing it across the EXTDEF seam, which does not make it library code -- the bytes are absent from ailv3.lib and its primitive at 0x0003cb01 is game code]

Rebuild note:
fdps_dpmi_lock_size(base, size) locks size + 1 bytes, not size: it hands fdps_dpmi_lock_region the endpoint pair (base, base + size), and that routine locks (max - min) + 1 bytes. Writing the obvious base + size - 1 in the rebuild, or reimplementing the wrapper over a half-open range, locks one byte fewer than the original and can leave the last byte of an interrupt-touched buffer pageable. Second, the routine has no stack-probe prologue, matching every other member of the module; it is reached only from AIL driver-setup paths that must be safe outside a normal stack context, so a rebuild has to suppress the __CHK probe explicitly (#pragma off (check_stack)) rather than let the compiler insert one.

=== 0003cbaa [PLATE]
Unlocks a DPMI-locked block of linear memory described as (base, size), for callers that hold an address and a byte count rather than a pair of endpoints.

Algorithm:
Adds size to base to form the end address, pushes (base, base + size) and calls fdps_dpmi_unlock_region, then drops the two arguments with ADD ESP,8 and returns. EAX is not touched after the call, so fdps_dpmi_unlock_region's status is the return value. That callee orders the endpoint pair, computes end - start + 1 as the byte length, loads DPMI function 0x0601 (Unlock Linear Region) into a union REGS frame and falls into the shared int386 tail at 0x0003cb24, which is owned by the fn 0x0600 lock primitive at 0x0003cb01 and turns the returned carry flag into 0 or 1. Because the end address is inclusive, the region actually unlocked is size + 1 bytes long. No frame is set up and no stack probe runs.

Parameters:
  base -- linear address of the first byte of the block to unlock; callers pass either a malloc'd block pointer or the address of a module static.
  size -- size of the block in bytes; the values seen at the call sites are small object sizes such as 4, 0x40 and 0x80.

Returns:
  int, passed through from fdps_dpmi_unlock_region: 1 when the DPMI call returned with carry clear (the pages are unlocked), 0 when it failed. All four callers ignore it.

Pool: fdps  [the game's own DPMI service module, defined by the game and reached by the vendored AIL objects across the EXTDEF seam; no FID hit in either the Watcom or the AIL library set]

Rebuild note:
The end address handed to fdps_dpmi_unlock_region is inclusive -- it computes end - start + 1 -- so this wrapper unlocks size + 1 bytes, not size. Writing the obvious 'return fdps_dpmi_unlock_region(base, base + size - 1);' would change the region by one byte; keep the arithmetic as base + size. The routine also has no stack-probe prologue, matching its siblings at 0x0003cb01 and 0x0003cb6e; it is reached from AIL driver-setup paths, so a rebuild must suppress the __CHK probe (#pragma off (check_stack)) rather than let the compiler add one.

=== 00042c30 [EOL]
x87 tbyte constant 2*pi, loaded by FLD TBYTE PTR CS:[00042c30] at 00042c5f

=== 00042c30 [PLATE]
The 80-bit x87 extended constant 2*pi (6.283185307179586477), the modulus the trig387 module uses to bring an out-of-range argument back into FSIN/FCOS range.

Read-only, never written, and reached by exactly one instruction: `FLD extended double ptr CS:[0x42c30]` at 00042c5f inside FUN_00042c4e, the module's range-reduction helper. IF@COS (00042c3a) and IF@SIN (00042c44) each execute FCOS/FSIN and then CALL that helper; the helper reads the x87 status word, and if C2 is clear -- the argument was in range and the result is already on the stack -- it returns with CF set and the caller's `JNC` falls through to RET. If C2 is set, the argument was outside the instruction's +-2^63 range, so the helper loads this constant, runs FPREM until C2 clears, drops the modulus with FSTP ST(1), clears CF, and returns; the caller's `JNC` then jumps back and re-executes FCOS/FSIN on the reduced argument. IF@TAN (00042ca0) does not reduce and never reaches this constant. The public wrappers cos (00042c7a), sin (00042c8d) and tan (00042ca5) load their double argument from the stack and call the IF@ entry points.

It lives in the code segment of its own object, which is why the load carries a CS: override; in the flat 32-bit model CS and DS alias the same memory, so the override has no effect beyond encoding.

Pool: crt  [only trig387's own helper reaches it, and these 10 bytes plus every PUBDEF offset in the surrounding code match Watcom 10.0a MATH387S trig387.obj byte for byte]

Rebuild note:
This is a 10-byte x87 extended value, not a double. Transcribing it as an 8-byte `double` (the obvious C type for 6.283185307179586) makes the FLD read two bytes of the following instruction as the exponent and returns a nonsense modulus, so sin/cos silently produce garbage for arguments large enough to need reduction. Preferred fix is not to emit it at all: sin/cos/tan here are stock vendor code and should be resolved out of MATH387S by wlink.

Pool: crt  [MATH387S.LIB(trig387.obj IF@COS), Function ID score 10, single candidate, hash unique in image]
Evidence: The entire body is FCOS / CALL 0x42c4e / JNC back to the FCOS / RET, verbatim the Watcom 387 cosine kernel: FCOS sets C2 when the operand magnitude exceeds the reducible range, the helper at 0x42c4e performs one FPREM reduction step and returns carry clear so the FCOS is retried, and returns carry set once the operand is in range so control falls through to the RET. The byte-identical FSIN twin IF@SIN sits immediately after at 0x42c44 and shares the same helper, which is how trig387.obj is laid out. Not fdps: no game data or string references, pure x87 numerics reached only from the maths wrapper cos at 0x42c7a. Not ail: no ail library hit, no interrupt or driver path. Not binary_artifact: a real library routine carrying a real library symbol, not a jump island or shim.
Name: Function ID byte match against trig387.obj in Watcom 10.0/10.0a/10.0b, one candidate, no other function in the image shares the hash; spelled as the library spells it, with no project prefix.
Boundary: 00042c3a-00042c43, the entry is the target of the function's own JNC at 0x42c41 and the RET at 0x42c43 is the last byte; no gap follows and 0x42c44 is the entry of IF@SIN.

=== 00042c4e [PLATE]
80387 trig argument range-reduction helper for the inline FSIN/FCOS entries: it reads the FPU status word left by the caller's trig instruction and, if C2 says the operand was out of range, loads the extended-double 2*pi from CS:[0x42c30] and loops FPREM until C2 clears, pops the divisor with FSTP ST1 and returns CF=0 so the caller retries; when C2 was already clear it returns immediately with CF=1 (OR AH,1 before SAHF) to say no reduction was needed.
Pool: crt  [Watcom 387 inline-trig module, no Function ID hit]
Evidence: Called only by IF@SIN (00042c44) and IF@COS (00042c3a), and its single data reference is the module's own extended-precision 2*pi constant at 00042c30 read through a CS override - callers and shared constant pool put it inside the Watcom 387 math module. It touches no game globals, no driver structures and no AIL state, so neither fdps nor ail fits; 44 bytes with a real FPREM loop is not a jump island or shim, so not binary_artifact.
Name: no library symbol identified - an internal label of the trig module, no Function ID candidates in either library set.
Boundary: 00042c4e-00042c79, PUSH EBP/MOV EBP,ESP entry that both call sites target, RET at 00042c79 matching the POP EAX/POP EBP epilogue, no gap before the entry of cos at 00042c7a.
Signature: hand-written x87 assembly with no C calling convention - input is ST(0) plus the caller's FPU status word, output is ST(0) and CF; EAX is pushed only as scratch for the FSTSW slot and restored, so no register or stack argument is consumed. Ghidra's __watcall(undefined2 in AX) is an unconfirmed guess and is not recorded.

=== 00043310 [PLATE]
Watcom C/C++ 10.0a 32-bit DOS startup body: identifies the host DOS extender, shrinks the DOS memory block, copies the PSP command tail and the program name, records the NO87 flag, zeroes BSS, then runs the registered initializers and enters __CMain.
Pool: crt  [cstrt386.obj, _TEXT offset 0x78, from CLIB3S.LIB]
Evidence: module cstrt386 in CLIB3S.LIB publishes _cstart_@0x000, __exit@0x28f, __do_exit_with_msg__@0x292 and __GETDS@0x2cc in _TEXT; anchoring _cstart_ at 00043298 puts those at 00043527, 0004352a and 00043564, all real function starts here, and the module's code resumes at offset 0x78, which is this address. Corroborated by the runtime state it owns - the whole Watcom low-globals block at 0006041c-00060458 (initial ESP, PSP and environment selectors, DOS version, host type, NO87 flag, command line and program name pointers) - and by its callees __InitRtns (0004dfa6) and __CMain (0004df4c). Raw INT 21h/INT 31h probing and segment-register juggling with no C prologue rule out fdps; no AIL data or driver structures rule out ail; 535 bytes of real work rule out binary_artifact.
Name: no public symbol of its own. cstrt386 publishes nothing at offset 0x78, and being hand-written assembly it emits no LPUBDEF static name to recover, so the file-static form L$N_<module>_<purpose> applies, ordinal 1 as the module's only unnamed body ahead of the first public. No Function ID hit exists (0 candidates in both the Watcom and the ail sets).
Boundary: 00043310-00043526, ending at the CALL __CMain at 00043522, which never returns; the bytes at 00043527 are the module's public __exit. The entry proper is the 2-byte JMP at 00043298 that wears _cstart_, with the copyright data at 00043299-0004330f between it and this body.
Signature: no C convention. Hand-written assembly entered by JMP, never called; takes no stack arguments, cleans nothing up and never returns. The only incoming state read is loader-supplied: EDX (Intel Code Builder info block) and GS (DPMI selector). Any recorded void(void) prototype is a placeholder, assumed.

Algorithm:
  1. STI, align ESP down to a dword boundary, record the initial stack pointer
     at 00060434 and 00060420, preload selector 0x24 into 0006042c and EBX with
     'PHAR' for the Phar Lap probe.
  2. INT 21h AH=30h (get DOS version); AL/AH are stored as DOS major/minor at
     00060457/00060458. The high half of EAX selects the host:
       - 0x4458 ('DX'): Phar Lap 386|DOS-Extender. Version digit from BL; read
         the PSP memory-block end at ES:[5Ch] through selector 0006042c, round
         up to 4K, store at 00060420 and shrink the block with INT 21h AH=4Ah.
         Environment selector 0x2C.
       - 0x4243 ('CB'): Intel Code Builder. EDX points at the info block, saved
         at 000603ac; shrink memory by [EDX+1Ch] (INT 21h AH=4Ah), PSP pointer
         from [EDX+10h] (command tail at PSP+81h), environment segment from
         [PSP+2Ch] shifted left by 4.
       - otherwise: INT 21h AX=FF00h, DX=78h. If a host answers, this is the
         DPMI/DOS-4G path: a non-zero GS is saved at 000603b0, INT 31h AX=0006h
         fetches the DS segment base, the PSP selector comes from ES and the
         environment selector from ES:[2Ch]. If nothing answers, fall back to
         the fixed selectors (PSP 0x24, environment 0x2C, flat data 0x17).
     The host type/subtype pair goes to 0006044e/0006044f, the environment
     pointer to 00060451 and its selector to 00060455.
  3. Self-modifying step: with the flat data selector in ES, store DS into the
     code at 0004356d, the operand of the MOV DS,CS:[4356Dh] in the exit path.
  4. Command line: read the tail length from PSP:80h, skip leading spaces with
     REPE SCASB, copy the rest with REP MOVSB to the 16-byte aligned buffer
     past the end of BSS (0006a3bc rounded up), append two NUL bytes. That
     aligned buffer address is recomputed at the end and stored at 00060424,
     so 00060424 is the pointer to the copied command line.
  5. Environment scan: a string whose first four bytes lowercase to "no87" and
     whose fifth byte is '=' increments the no-x87 flag at 0006044c. After the
     terminating double NUL, skip the word count and copy the program name over
     the last NUL of the command line buffer; the address of that copy goes to
     00060428 and the first free byte past it to 00060430, the stack pointer to
     0006041c.
  6. Zero BSS from 00063930 to 0006a3bc with REP STOSD plus a byte tail; when
     the host type byte at 0006044e is 1 the cleared span is clamped to 0x1000
     bytes.
  7. CALL __InitRtns (0004dfa6) with EAX=0FFh to run every registered
     initializer up to priority 255, clear EBP, then CALL __CMain (0004df4c),
     which builds argc/argv, calls main and exits. __CMain does not return, so
     this call is the last instruction of the routine.
Open question: FD2 records the same vendor routine as one 557-byte function including the entry JMP and the copyright data; here it is split into _cstart_ at 00043298 and this body. That is an entity-layout difference only - both describe the same stock cstrt386 code, which is vendor-linked and not rebuilt from C.

=== 0004356d [PLATE]
The flat data (DS) selector that __GETDS reloads, kept inside cstrt386's own code segment.

Written exactly once, by L$1_cstrt386_start_body at 0x43432: MOV word ptr ES:[0x4356d],DS, where ES has just been loaded from BX with a writable alias selector for the code segment -- the store patches the code object at run time. Read only by __GETDS at 0x43564: MOV DS,word ptr CS:[0x4356d] followed by RET, whose whole body is those two instructions and whose only job is to put a valid flat data selector back into DS. The word occupies the last two bytes of cstrt386's _TEXT (segment offset 0x2d5, segment length 0x2d7); 0x4356f is linker alignment padding, and kbhit begins at 0x43570. Its image value is 0x0000, so the selector is meaningless until the startup patch has run; loading it before that faults. No game code and no AIL code reaches it.

Pool: crt  [both references are in CLIB3S module cstrt386, and these two bytes are the tail of that module's own _TEXT segment]

Rebuild note:
This is a variable that lives in the code segment, not in DGROUP, and that is load-bearing. __GETDS exists to restore DS when DS is not yet usable, so its selector must be reachable CS-relative; declaring it in C as a static unsigned short would put it in DGROUP/_BSS and make the routine depend on the very register it is there to reload. The startup write also needs the writable code-segment alias in ES -- plain C cannot express it. __GETDS and this word have to stay as hand-written assembly in cstrt386.

=== 0004b170 [EOL]
Miles AIL wave-synthesizer (HWAVE) module: a 128-entry note-to-Hz table followed by 10 functions that render XMIDI events on the AIL digital sample API -- DPMI lock/unlock guards, channel state, voice volume/pitch, event and timbre callbacks, open/close

=== 0004b170 [PLATE]
Equal-temperament note-frequency table for the AIL sample-based MIDI synthesizer: 128 dwords, one per MIDI note number 0..127, holding that note's frequency an octave above concert pitch (entry 57 = 440, entry 69 = 880, entry 60 = 523), rising monotonically from 8 to 25088.

Read-only; nothing in the image writes it. The only reader is AIL_internal_dig_apply_pitch_bend@0004b5f0, which loads three entries per call at 0004b682/0004b689/0004b690: the voice's sample root note (synth_state +0x558), the note currently sounding (+0x518), and the note the channel's pitch wheel bends towards. The bend target is formed from the 14-bit wheel value (MSB<<7 | LSB) against centre 0x2000 scaled by the channel bend range (+0x414), then clamped to 0..0x7f at 0004b671-0004b67a, so the index never leaves the table. The routine takes the difference between two entries, scales it by the 13-bit bend fraction and shifts right 13, giving a frequency linearly interpolated between two semitones; the ratio of that against the root-note entry becomes the sample playback rate handed to AIL_set_sample_playback_rate. Channel 9 (percussion) skips the root-note ratio and applies the bend ratio alone. Only ratios between entries are ever used, so the octave-up scaling cancels out and exists to keep resolution at the low end of the integer table.

Pool: ail  [referenced from exactly one function, AIL_internal_dig_apply_pitch_bend, which ticket 14.2 matched byte-for-byte to /ail_lib/ail_code.obj in ailv3.lib; no game or CRT code reaches it. FD2 named the same table data_ail_dig_pitch_bend_freq_scale_lookup_uint32_127 at its 0x45120.]

Rebuild note:
Emit the 128 values literally; do not generate them. Entry 0 is 8, half the 16 the equal-temperament progression demands (it is note 0's un-doubled frequency), and entries 123..125 sit 2-3 counts below the formula because the original generator accumulated float error at the top of the range. The routine interpolates differences between adjacent entries, so a regenerated table changes the bend curve at both extremes.

=== 0004e326 [PLATE]
256 three-byte INT nn / RET stubs, one per interrupt vector, executed to raise an arbitrary software interrupt with the register set the caller supplied.

Initialised data in .object1, built into the vendor object intxa386.obj next to __int386x_ (0004e248) and _DoINTR_ (0004e2a5); nothing ever writes it. Entry n sits at base + n*3 and holds CD nn C3, except entry 3, which holds CC 90 C3 -- INT 3 has a one-byte encoding, and the NOP filler keeps the stride uniform. FUN_0004e2f2 masks the interrupt number to 0..255 (AND EAX,0xff), scales it by 3 (LEA EAX,[EAX+EAX*0x2]), forms the stub address and PUSHes it; FUN_0004e280 does the same starting from ESI (LEA ESI,[ESI+ESI*0x2]). Both then load the segment and general registers from the caller's REGS/SREGS block and transfer to the stub, whose RET comes straight back so the resulting registers can be stored. The index is the interrupt number itself, so the table has no gaps, no sentinel and no terminator; the mask is the only bound check.

Pool: crt  [both referencing functions are pool_crt bodies of Watcom CLIB3S module intxa386.obj, whose only public symbols are __int386x_ and _DoINTR_; game code raises interrupts through int386/int386x and never touches this table]

Rebuild note:
Regenerating the table from a loop of int n mnemonics breaks it: an assembler encodes int 3 as the one-byte CC, so entry 3 has to be padded the way the original pads it (CC 90 C3) or every later entry shifts down by one and base + n*3 lands in the middle of an instruction.

=== 0004e6ab [PLATE]
sbrk(increment): extends the program's data area, returning the address of the new space or -1 with errno set.
Pool: crt  [Watcom CLIB3S sbrk386.obj, Function ID score 144.07, single candidate, hash unique in image]
Evidence: Branches on the C runtime's extender/os-mode byte at 0006044e (1 = DPMI with the subtype at 0006044f, 9 = the other direct-allocation case, 2..8 = extender). === 0004e830 [PLATE]
The 80-bit x87 extended constant +0.0 that the 80x87 emulator compares against when it emulates FTST.

Read-only, never written, and reached by exactly one instruction sequence: 0004f8f6 inside FUN_0004ec3c, the EMU387 instruction dispatcher. Control arrives there only through slot 4 of the jump table at 0004f8bc, which decodes the D9 E0..E7 escape group (slot 0 FCHS at 0004f8dc, slot 1 FABS at 0004f8e9, slot 4 FTST, slot 5 FXAM at 0004f927, slots 2/3/6/7 the invalid-opcode entry 0004f770) -- so this constant belongs to FTST alone. The handler copies all ten bytes (dword, dword, word) into the scratch operand slot at [EBP + 0x6c] of the emulator state block, then loads EAX with the address of ST(0) at [EDI + EBP*0x1 + 0x1c] and EDX with the address of the scratch, and calls the shared extended-precision compare at 00050524; the tail it returns to writes the C3/C2/C0 result into the emulated status word at [EBP + 0x4]. In that state block EBP is the base, [EBP + 0x4] is the status word (its TOP field is bits 11-13, masked with 0xc7ff), [EBP + 0x8] is the tag word, and [EBP + 0x1c] starts the eight 10-byte emulated registers, which is why the scratch lands at 0x6c.

All ten bytes are zero: sign 0, exponent field 0x0000, significand 0, i.e. +0.0. The CS: override on the load is only an encoding artifact -- the constant sits at offset 0 of the emu387 module's own _TEXT segment, and in the flat 32-bit model CS and DS alias the same memory.

Pool: crt  [its only reader is 0004ec3c, which matches Watcom EMU387.LIB module emu387 byte for byte; that match puts the module's _TEXT base at 0004e830, so this is the module's first datum]

Rebuild note:
This is a 10-byte x87 extended zero, not a double and not padding. Ten zero bytes at the front of a module read like alignment fill or like something the loader could leave in BSS, and the obvious C spelling of the value -- `static double ftst_zero = 0.0;` -- is only 8 bytes; the handler copies 10, so it would take the two high exponent bytes from whatever follows and FTST would report a comparison against a denormal or a NaN instead of zero, silently flipping C3/C0 and every FP branch that depends on them. Emit the full ten zero bytes, or better, do not re-emit this module at all: resolve the emulator out of EMU387.LIB with wlink.

=== 0004e83a [EOL]
Watcom 80x87 emulator state tables: the 8-slot circular register-stack ring (with its TOP field values) and the parallel tag-word 2-bit field masks; the trailing 14 bytes belong to sibling block 0004e8da

=== 0004e83a [PLATE]
Navigation table for the emulated 80x87 register stack: eight 10-byte records, one per ST slot, giving the byte offsets of the neighbouring slots and the status-word TOP encoding for that slot.

Read-only, never written. It lives in _TEXT of the Watcom emu387 module, so every access is a CS-override load of the form word ptr CS:[reg + 0x4e83a] where reg holds a slot's byte offset (0, 10, 20 ... 70); the same value doubles as the offset of that slot's 10-byte temp-real value inside the emulator state block at [EBP+0x1c], which is why the record stride is 10 and not 8. Record fields: +0 the next slot's offset (TOP+1, the pop direction; slot 7 wraps to 0), +2 the previous slot's offset (TOP-1, the push direction; slot 0 wraps to 70), +4 the slot number pre-shifted into bits 11-13 of the x87 status word (0x0000, 0x0800, 0x1000, 0x1800, 0x2000, 0x2800, 0x3000, 0x3800), +6 the slot number itself (0..7), +8 always zero. Only +0, +2 and +4 have readers in this image.

The emulator's main ESC dispatcher FUN_0004ec3c and its opcode arms FUN_0004edde (compare-and-pop tail), FUN_0004fcac, FUN_0004fd9a (FUCOMPP) and FUN_000502d1 use it to move TOP: they fetch the new offset from +0, then rewrite the saved status word with AND word ptr DS:[EBP+4],0xc7ff followed by OR of the +4 word. The parallel table crt_x87_emu_tag_field_masks at 0004e88a supplies the matching tag-word clear and set masks for the same slot offsets.

Pool: crt  [Reached only by 80x87-emulator code; FUN_0004ec3c is a zero-mismatch match for module emu387 of EMU387.LIB, _TEXT+1036, and this table's words appear in that same library module.]

Rebuild note:
This table belongs to EMU387.LIB and must come from the linked library, not from a C source file: it sits in the code segment and is only ever read through a CS segment override, which flat-model Watcom C cannot emit. If it is ever regenerated by hand, note that the links wrap -- slot 7's +0 is 0x0000, not 0x50, and slot 0's +2 is 0x0046 -- and that the trailing zero word at +8 is load-bearing padding that keeps the record stride at 10 so the stored offsets also index the 10-byte ST register file.

=== 0004e88a [EOL]
8 records x 10 bytes for the emulated x87 tag word, same stride-10 slot index: +0 clear mask ~(3<<2i), then the tag values shifted into bit position 2i in the order 1<<2i, 0, 2<<2i, 3<<2i for i=0..7, i.e. the eight 2-bit tag fields covering a full 16-bit word

=== 0004e88a [PLATE]
Per-register masks for the emulated 80x87 tag word: eight 10-byte groups, one per stack register, indexed by the same byte offset (0, 10, 20, ... 70) that indexes the emulator's stack ring at 0004e83a.

Read-only; it lives in object 1, which is not writable, and nothing writes it. It is read by the EMU387 emulator body FUN_0004ec3c and by the handlers that share its state frame: FUN_0004edde, FUN_0004f95d, FUN_0004f9a0, FUN_0004f9e5, FUN_0004fa2a, FUN_0004fa6f, FUN_0004fab4, FUN_0004faf9, FUN_0004fcac, FUN_0004fd00, FUN_0004fd9a. The emulated tag word is the word at [EBP+8] of that frame.

Group i (i = offset/10, the stack register number, taken from field +6 of the matching ring record) holds: +0 = ~(3 << 2i), the AND mask that clears register i's two tag bits; +2 = 1 << 2i, tag 01 = zero; +4 = 0, tag 00 = valid; +6 = 2 << 2i, tag 10 = special (NaN/Inf/denormal); +8 = 3 << 2i, tag 11 = empty. So group 0 is fffc 0001 0000 0002 0003 and group 7 is 3fff 4000 0000 8000 c000.

The standard idiom is AND [EBP+8] with CS:[idx + 0x4e88a] then OR with CS:[idx + 0x4e892], i.e. mark that register empty -- a stack pop, usually followed by MOVZX EDI,CS:[EDI + 0x4e83a] to advance TOP. FUN_0004faf9 instead ORs CS:[idx + 0x4e88c] after storing a zero significand, i.e. mark it zero (FLDZ). Only the +0, +2 and +8 slots are reached by any instruction in the image; +4 and +6 are the valid and special entries of the same four-value set and are never loaded here.

Pool: crt  [only the Watcom 80x87 emulator reaches it; the body that owns the references, 0004ec3c, matches EMU387.LIB module emu387 at _TEXT+1036]

Rebuild note:
The 10-byte stride is shared with the stack ring at 0004e83a, because one byte offset indexes both. The zero word at +4 of every group is a live table entry, not padding, and dropping it (an OR with 0 is a visible no-op) would shrink the stride to 8 and send every ring offset into the wrong group.

=== 0004e8da [PLATE]
Four x87 status-word bit patterns, one per outcome of an emulated compare: less, equal, greater, unordered.

Read-only initialised data among the code in .object1, built into the Watcom vendor object emu387.obj and read CS-relative; nothing writes it. Every compare the emulator implements funnels through the same three steps. The interpreter FUN_0004ec3c (and FUN_0004fd9a, the D9 F0..F7 group) points EAX and EDX at the two 10-byte extended operands, calls the compare helper at 00050526, and jumps to one of two shared tails: FUN_0004ee30 for the forms that leave the register stack alone -- the FCOM/FICOM memory and register forms, and FTST at 0004f922, which compares against the zero constant L$1_emu387_ftst_zero -- and FUN_0004edde for the popping forms, which does the identical condition-code update and then also rewrites the popped register's tag field through L$1_emu387_tag_field_masks and advances the stack top through L$N_emu387_stack_ring. Both tails do INC EAX, clear C3/C2/C1/C0 out of the emulated status word at [EBP+4] with AND DX,0xb8ff, OR this table's byte into DH, and store the word back before rejoining the dispatcher at 0004ec3c.

The index is the compare helper's return value plus one, and the helper at 00050526 returns exactly four values: -1 when ST is below the source, 0 when they are equal, +1 when ST is above, and 2 when either operand has an all-ones exponent with a non-zero significand, i.e. unordered. INC EAX maps that onto 0..3 and there is no other index path, so all four slots are live and none is a sentinel. The entries are 01 40 00 45, and because they are ORed into DH, which covers status-word bits 8..15, 0x01 is C0 (bit 8), 0x04 is C2 (bit 10) and 0x40 is C3 (bit 14). Less therefore sets C0 alone, equal sets C3 alone, greater sets nothing, and unordered sets C3|C2|C0 -- the encoding the 387 defines for FCOM. C1 is cleared by the 0xb8ff mask and no entry ever sets it.

Pool: crt  [both referencing bodies are pool_crt tails of the 80x87 emulator, and the four bytes appear verbatim in Watcom 10.0a's emu387.obj immediately before the FPREM quotient table; the game reaches floating point only through emulated instructions and never touches an emulated status word]

Rebuild note:
These are high-byte patterns, not status-word values. They are ORed into DH, so 0x01 means C0 (bit 8) and 0x40 means C3 (bit 14); writing the obvious status |= cc_bits[result] against the 16-bit word sets the invalid-operation flag (bit 0) and the stack-fault flag (bit 6) instead of the condition codes. The index is also biased: the compare result runs -1..2 and the table is indexed by result + 1, so cc_bits[result] reads the byte before the table for the less-than case.

=== 0004e8de [EOL]

=== 0004e8de [PLATE]
Eight status-word bit patterns, one per value of the low three quotient bits, used to report an FPREM / FPREM1 result in the emulated 80x87 condition codes.

Read-only initialised data in .object1, built into the vendor object emu387.obj alongside the INT 7 handler; nothing writes it. Two callers use it, and both do the identical three steps: FUN_0004fc82 (slot 0 of the D9 F8..FF opcode table at 0004fc62, i.e. FPREM) and the arm at 0005028f inside the interpreter FUN_0004ec3c (slot 5 of the D9 F0..F7 table at 0004fb58, i.e. FPREM1) point EAX and EDX at two 10-byte register slots at [EBP+0x1c], CALL the shared remainder helper at 00050ff5, mask its returned quotient with AND EAX,0x7, clear C3/C2/C1/C0 out of the emulated status word at [EBP+4] with AND DX,0xb8ff, then OR DH with this table's entry and store the word back before rejoining the dispatcher via JMP DS:[EBP+0x76].

The index is the quotient modulo 8 and the entries are 00 02 40 42 01 03 41 43. In DH, which covers status-word bits 8..15, 0x01 is C0 (bit 8), 0x02 is C1 (bit 9), 0x04 is C2 (bit 10) and 0x40 is C3 (bit 14), so the table scatters quotient bit 0 into C1, bit 1 into C3 and bit 2 into C0 -- the placement the 387 specifies for FPREM and FPREM1. No entry sets C2, and the 0xb8ff mask has already cleared it, so the emulator always reports C2 = 0, meaning reduction complete: it computes the whole remainder in one call instead of the hardware's partial-remainder steps. There is no sentinel and no terminator; every one of the eight slots is a live value.

Pool: crt  [both referencing functions are pool_crt bodies of the 80x87 emulator, and the 8 bytes are present verbatim in Watcom's EMU387 vendor object emu387.obj; game code reaches floating point only through emulated instructions and never touches this table]

Rebuild note:
The quotient bits do not go where they look like they should. Writing the obvious 'status |= quotient & 7' packs them into C0/C1/C2 contiguously, but the 387 puts Q0 in C1, Q1 in C3 and Q2 in C0, so an fmod or an argument reduction that inspects the quotient bits gets the wrong quotient. Worse, that spelling can set C2, which means 'reduction incomplete' -- callers that loop while C2 is set would then spin forever on a remainder this emulator has already finished computing.

=== 0004e8e8 [PLATE]
Effective-address handler table for the memory forms of an emulated 80x87 instruction: 24 code pointers indexed by (mod << 3) | r/m taken from the ModR/M byte.

Read-only, never written, and reached by exactly one instruction: CALL dword ptr CS:[EBX*0x4 + 0x4e8e8] at 0004ec86 inside FUN_0004ec3c, the EMU387 instruction dispatcher. Control gets there only after FUN_0004ec3c has skipped any prefixes and FWAIT, confirmed the trapped opcode is D8..DF (MOV BL,AL / AND BL,0xf8 / CMP BL,0xd8), and found the ModR/M byte below 0xc0 (CMP AH,0xc0 / JNC 0x0004ed25 at 0004ec6c) -- the register forms are handled elsewhere and never index this table. The index is built by MOV BL,AH / MOV BH,AH / SHR BH,0x3 / AND EBX,0x1807 / OR BL,BH: r/m lands in bits 0-2, mod in bits 3-4. So the rows are mod=0 in slots 0-7, mod=1 in slots 8-15, mod=2 in slots 16-23, and there is no row for mod=3.

Each slot is a 6- to 11-byte stub that returns the operand offset in EBX and leaves ESI pointing past whatever displacement it consumed. The base register comes out of the trap frame's PUSHA block: [EBP+0x28] EAX, +0x24 ECX, +0x20 EDX, +0x1c EBX, +0x18 ESP, +0x14 EBP, +0x10 ESI, +0x0c EDI. Row mod=0 takes no displacement (0004ee9a: XOR EBX,EBX / ADD EBX,[EBP+0x28] / RET), row mod=1 sign-extends a disp8 (0004eecc: MOVSX EBX,byte ptr [ESI] / INC ESI / ADD EBX,[EBP+0x28]), row mod=2 takes a disp32 (0004ef10: MOV EBX,[ESI] / ADD ESI,0x4 / ADD EBX,[EBP+0x28]). Slot 5 of row 0 is the architectural special case mod=0, r/m=5 -- absolute disp32 with no base, 0004eeba. Slot 4 of every row is r/m=4, meaning a SIB byte follows, and all three rows point at the SIB decoder FUN_0004ef5c, which reads that byte and re-dispatches its base field through the sibling table at 0004e948 before applying the index and scale.

On return FUN_0004ec3c does MOV ES,CX and MOV ESI,EBX, so ES:EBX addresses the memory operand; it then saves the advanced instruction pointer to [EBP+0x38], forms the 6-bit opcode index as (ModR/M & 0x38) | (opcode & 7), points EBP at the emulator state block at 000613c8 and vectors into the per-opcode memory-form handler table at 0004e9a8.

Pool: crt  [only the Watcom 80x87 emulator reaches it; its one reader 0004ec3c matches EMU387.LIB module emu387 at _TEXT+1036, which puts this table at module offset 0xb8]

Rebuild note:
This table and the one at 0004e948 agree in 21 of their 24 slots and differ only at slot 4 of each row, and that difference is the whole point: r/m = 4 here means "a SIB byte follows" and vectors to the SIB decoder 0004ef5c, while base = 4 in the sibling table means ESP is the base register. Merging the two, the obvious tidy-up once a diff shows only three differences, makes every [ESP + disp] x87 memory operand swallow one more instruction byte as a second SIB, so both the operand address and the instruction length come out wrong.

=== 0004e948 [PLATE]
Dispatch table of 24 effective-address helper routines used by the 80x87 emulator when the ModR/M byte says a SIB byte follows.

Read only by FUN_0004ef5c, the SIB decoder, at 0004ef6f: it fetches the SIB byte, masks its base field into BL, folds the ModR/M mod field in as bits 3-4 (MOV BH,AH / SHR BH,3 / AND BH,0x18 / OR BL,BH) and does CALL dword ptr CS:[EBX*0x4 + 0x4e948]. Rebuild note:

=== 0004eaa8 [PLATE]
Dispatch table for the 64 register-form (ModR/M mod = 11b) 80x87 instructions: one dword code address per (ESC opcode, ModR/M reg) pair.

Read-only data in .object1, assembled into Watcom's EMU387 emulator module; nothing writes it. === 0004eba8 [PLATE]
INT 7 (coprocessor-not-available) entry of the Watcom 80x87 emulator, privilege-level-3 variant. It re-enables interrupts, PUSHADs the client's general registers to form the emulator's context block, then fills from the incoming trap frame the four fields it cannot take from its own registers, calls the emulator core at 0004ec3c, and restores DS/ES and the registers before IRETD.
Pool: crt  [Function ID __int7_pl3 from emu387.obj (EMU387.LIB), score 17.02, sole candidate, hash unique in the image]
Evidence: STI / PUSHAD / trap-frame fixup / POP DS / POP ES / POPAD / IRETD is hand-written interrupt-gate code that wcc386 cannot emit from C. Its only reference is a DATA reference from FUN_000445bc, which installs it on protected-mode vector 7 (INT 21h AX=2504h) during floating-point startup; its only callee is the emulator decode loop FUN_0004ec3c; and the sibling entries __int7_X32VM (0004ebcc) and __int7 (0004ec18) sit immediately around it, sharing that callee. Not fdps: no game data, string or call-graph contact. Not ail: no ailv3.lib hit, no audio state. Not binary_artifact: a real library routine with a body.
Name: pl3 is privilege level 3, not a guess from the Function ID score -- FUN_000445bc dispatches on the mode byte at 0x0006044e and installs THIS address on the level >= 3 branch (the branch that also takes the ring-3 CR0 route), installing __int7 at 0x0004ec18 otherwise.
Frame: the argument block handed to 0004ec3c is identical to the one __int7 at 0004ec18 hand-builds, which decodes every offset used here. PUSHAD lays down EAX..EDI; the two PUSHes add the ES and DS dwords on top; word [EBP-6] is the high half of the DS dword, exactly where __int7 stores SS (MOV word ptr [ESP+2],SS); and [EBP+0x0c] is the ESP slot of the PUSHAD block, exactly where __int7 stores the interrupted ESP. So the incoming frame holds, at entry ESP, +0x18 the interrupted ESP, +0x1c the interrupted SS (word), +0x20 ES and +0x24 DS, above the EIP/CS/EFLAGS that POPAD leaves ESP pointing at for the IRETD. These are values the extender's frame supplies because a ring-3 client's ESP and segments cannot be read out of the handler's own registers -- which is why this variant exists at all, and why the offsets reach past a plain same-privilege frame. The two pushed dwords do double duty: arguments to the core on the way in, and the values popped back into DS and ES on the way out.
Boundary: 0004eba8-0004ebc8, ends at the IRETD; the 3 bytes after it (87 db 90) are alignment padding before __int7_X32VM.
Signature: No C calling convention. Entered on vector 7, it reads nothing from EAX/EDX/EBX (all saved by PUSHAD, restored by POPAD), takes its inputs from the trap frame, and leaves via IRETD. The recorded __watcall(EAX, EDX, EBX) was Ghidra's guess and is not what the assembly does.

=== 00050360 [PLATE]
Memory-operand front end of the 80x87 emulator's 80-bit extended-precision ADD: loads the two 10-byte temp-reals pointed to by EAX and EDX into the register form the core expects (operand 1 mantissa in EDX:EAX with its sign/exponent word in SI, operand 2 mantissa in ECX:EBX with its sign/exponent word in the high half of ESI), calls the adder at 000503ba, and stores the 10-byte sum through the destination pointer that arrived in EBX.
Pool: crt  [80x87 emulator (EMU387 family); no Function ID hit on this body, identified by caller and data format]
Evidence: Both operands are read and the result written as dword/dword/word at +0/+4/+8, the 10-byte 80387 temp-real layout, through a private register protocol no C compiler emits for user code. All three callers live in the emulator's INT 7 path: FUN_0004ec3c is the opcode dispatcher directly after __int7 at 0004ec18, entered from __int7_X32VM at 0004ebcc -- both of those are Function ID byte matches naming emu387.obj -- and it decodes a saved interrupt frame and branches through tables of 0x0004fxxx handlers; FUN_0004ef99 and FUN_0004f7a2 sit in the same block and re-enter the dispatcher through JMP [EBP+0x76]. The core at 000503ba is shared by five further routines of the same family. There are no data or string references and no driver state, so nothing points at AIL, and the 42-byte body does real work with no unconditional jump elsewhere, so it is neither a jump island nor a convention shim. Game code has no reason to drive 80-bit temp-reals through the library's private register protocol.
Operation: addition, established at the core. 000503ba shortcuts a zero operand by returning the other one unchanged (0 + b = b, which multiply and divide could not do), then differences the two exponents with SUB CX,DI, aligns the smaller mantissa with SHRD by CL while keeping a sticky word in EDI, and combines with ADD EAX,EBX / ADC EDX,ESI before renormalising and saturating to the 0x7fff / 0x8000000000000000 infinity encoding. The callers agree: FUN_0004f7a2 is the register-register form (both operands are slots of the emulated FP register file at [EBP+0x1c], destination the first of them) and FUN_0004ef99 is the memory form, converting the memory operand into the scratch at [EBP+0x6c] via FUN_00050b8a first. The sibling wrapper FUN_00050794, called at 0004f7c3 with a byte-identical argument setup, is a different operation of the same family.

=== 00050bcf [EOL]

=== 00050bcf [PLATE]
Thirty-two low-bit masks used by the x87 emulator's round-to-integer helper; entry i is the low (31 - i) bits set, i.e. 0x7fffffff >> i, ending at 0 for i = 31.

Read-only, and read only by FUN_00050c4f, which rounds the 80-bit temporary real at [EDI] in place under the rounding-control field passed in DX (0x000 nearest, 0x400 down, 0x800 up, 0xc00 truncate; down and up are exchanged at 00050c6a when the operand's sign bit is set, and 0xc00 is folded to 0x400 at 00050c76). The helper computes BX = (exponent word at [EDI+8] & 0x7fff) - 0x403f, returns immediately when that is not negative because the value is already integral, and otherwise adds 0x20 to form the index. At 00050c90 the entry masks the fraction bits held in the low significand dword at [EDI]; when even that index is still negative the code falls to 00050cde, zeroes the low dword, adds a further 0x20 and at 00050cee masks the fraction bits in the high significand dword at [EDI+4]. In both places the mask is ANDed with the significand word and XORed back to truncate it, and INC EAX then turns the mask into the single ulp bit that the round-up paths add to the significand, propagating into the exponent at [EDI+8] on carry. Index runs 0..31 and is guarded on both sides; both loads carry a CS override because the table sits inside the code object, between FUN_00050b8a and FUN_00050c4f.

Pool: crt  [the sole referencing function is FUN_00050c4f, which byte-matches EMU387.LIB module emu387 in all of Watcom 9.5 through 10.6a; no game or AIL code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
Entry 0 is 0x7fffffff, not 0xffffffff. The table is 0x7fffffff >> i, one bit narrower than the 0xffffffff >> i that a 32-entry low-bit mask table is usually written as, because the significand's explicit integer bit is never part of the fraction. Since the consumer does INC EAX on the loaded mask to build the rounding ulp bit, a 0xffffffff entry would wrap to 0 and silently stop the round-up path working. Linking EMU387 rather than re-emitting this module avoids the question.

=== 00050d82 [PLATE]
The nine 80-bit x87 extended coefficients of the arctangent power series that the 80x87 emulator evaluates for FPATAN.

Read-only, never written, and reached by exactly one instruction: `LEA EDX,[0x50d82]` at 00050f9a inside FUN_00050e92, the emulator's internal arctangent helper. That routine first folds the operand: an operand of exactly 1.0 returns pi/4 outright, and when |x| exceeds 0.267949 (2 - sqrt(3) = tan(pi/12), tested at 00050f0a as exponent 0x3ffd with high mantissa 0x8930a2f4) it applies x' = (x*sqrt(3) - 1)/(x + sqrt(3)) -- sqrt(3) is built inline as the immediates 0xddb3d742:0xc265539e with exponent 0x3fff, not read from memory -- and adds pi/6 to the result. The reduced argument, EDX = this table and EBX = 8 then go to the odd-power-series evaluator at 00051a0e, which squares the argument, runs eight Horner steps over the table and multiplies by the argument once at the end; eight steps over nine coefficients is why the table has 9 entries and why it is stored highest degree first. FUN_00050ddc, the emulator's FPATAN/atan2 handler, is what calls FUN_00050e92 and applies the quadrant correction afterwards with its own inline pi/2 and pi constants.

Entry i occupies table + i*10 in the emulator's 80-bit extended format. The values are +0.04438952, -0.06483194, +0.07679369, -0.09090371, +0.11111098, -0.14285714, +0.20000000, -0.33333333, +1.0. Only the last two are the exactly rounded odd reciprocals; from entry 6 downwards each one drifts further from 1/(2k+1) -- 1e-11 at +0.2, 1.3e-7 at +0.111111, 1.3e-4 at +0.0767937, 0.014 at +0.0443895 -- because the tail is minimax-fitted for the reduced range rather than taken from the Taylor series. The table ends at 00050ddb and the next byte is the first instruction of FUN_00050ddc.

Pool: crt  [its only reader matches EMU387.LIB module emu387 byte for byte; with that module's _TEXT base at 0004e830 this table is module offset 9554, ending exactly where the module-offset-9644 routine begins]

Rebuild note:
Do not regenerate these coefficients from the arctangent Taylor series and do not spell them as doubles. Only +1 and -1/3 are the exactly rounded reciprocals; writing the obvious 1.0/5.0, -1.0/7.0 ... 1.0/17.0 tail replaces a minimax fit whose last entry differs by 0.014, which changes the emulated FPATAN result near the reduction boundary. The elements are 10-byte extendeds, so `static double atan_coef[9]` gives a 72-byte object with an 8-byte stride while the evaluator at 00051a0e strides 10 and would read its exponent out of the neighbouring coefficient. The safe route is not to re-emit this module at all: resolve the emulator out of EMU387.LIB with wlink.

numerator P(w) of the natural-log rational approximation: 3 x 80-bit x87 extended reals in Horner (descending) order, p2=-0.78956112887491258778, p1=16.383943563021535539, p0=-64.12494342374557732; loaded by LEA ECX,[0005117e] with EBX=2 at 0005130a in FUN_00051220

=== 0005117e [PLATE]
Numerator coefficients A2, A1, A0 of the rational approximation to ln(x) used by the 80x87 emulator, three 80-bit x87 extended values stored leading-coefficient-first.

Read-only, never written, and reached by exactly one instruction: `LEA ECX,[0x5117e]` at 0005130a inside FUN_00051220, the emulator's software natural logarithm. FUN_00051220 rewrites the exponent of its argument so the significand lies in [0.5,1) and keeps the exponent as n, compares that significand against the inline sqrt(0.5) (0005125a..0005126b) to select the interval, then builds z = (x - 0.5) / (x*0.5 + 0.5) and w = z*z. It evaluates the denominator table at 0005119c with EBX=3, then this table with EBX=2, divides one by the other, multiplies by w and by z, and adds z -- Cody & Waite's ln(x) = z + z*w*A(w)/B(w) -- and finally adds n*ln(2), split into a high and a low part for extra precision, when n is non-zero. Both evaluations go through 000519bc, a Horner loop that loads a 10-byte coefficient through a CS: override, multiplies by the argument, advances by `LEA EDI,[EDI+0xa]` and adds the next coefficient; its EBX operand is the polynomial degree, so a table of degree+1 entries is read.

The entries are: +0x00 = -0.78956112887491257266 (coefficient of w^2), +0x0a = +16.383943563021534222 (coefficient of w), +0x14 = -64.124943423745581147 (constant term).

FUN_00051220 has one caller, 000511dd, which multiplies its result by log2(e) (loaded as an immediate at 00051202) and then by the second operand -- that is FYL2X. 000511c4 is the FYL2XP1 entry: it adds 1.0 to the operand and falls straight into 000511dd. Those two are reached only as slot 1 of the D9 F0-F7 and D9 F8-FF escape groups, through binary_artifact_x87_emu_switch_table_4fb58 and binary_artifact_x87_emu_switch_table_4fc62, with EAX pointing at emulated ST(0) and EDX at ST(1) in the register file at state+0x1c. So this table is live only on a machine with no 387, when FDPS executes an FYL2X or FYL2XP1.

The CS: overrides on the coefficient loads are an encoding artifact: the table sits in the emu387 module's own _TEXT segment, immediately in front of the code that uses it, and in the flat 32-bit model CS and DS alias the same memory.

Pool: crt  [its only reader is FUN_00051220, and these 30 bytes plus the 40 that follow match Watcom 10.0a EMU387.LIB module emu387 at _TEXT offset 0x294e byte for byte]

Rebuild note:
Each entry is a 10-byte x87 extended value and the order is the reverse of the published constants. Writing the obvious `static double a[3] = {-64.124943423745581, 16.383943563021534, -0.789561128874913};` gets both wrong at once -- 24 bytes where 30 are read, and A0 first where A2 is expected -- and the emulator then returns a silently wrong logarithm rather than faulting.

=== 0005119c [PLATE]
Denominator polynomial of the rational approximation the 80x87 emulator uses for the natural logarithm: four 80-bit x87 extended reals, highest-degree coefficient first.

Read-only, never written, and reached by exactly one instruction: 000512f3 in FUN_00051220, the extended-real natural log, which does MOV EBX,0x3 / LEA ECX,[0005119c] / CALL 000519bc. FUN_000519bc is the shared Horner evaluator for this format -- it loads a coefficient as two dwords plus a word through a CS: override, advances with LEA EDI,[EDI+0xa], and alternates the soft-float multiply 000507be with the soft-float add 000503ba for EBX iterations after the leading term, so EBX=3 consumes the four entries stored here. Fourteen instructions later FUN_00051220 evaluates the matching three-entry numerator at 0005117e (L$N_emu387_ln_rational_num) with EBX=2 and divides one by the other at 000505e9. FUN_00051220 first reduces its argument to [sqrt(2)/2, sqrt(2)) by rebiasing the exponent to 0x3ffe and comparing the mantissa against 0x3ffe:b504f333_f9de6484 = sqrt(2)/2, then reconstructs ln(x) = ln(m) + k*ln2 from the two-part ln2 split. Its only caller is FUN_000511dd, the FYL2X emulation, which turns ln into log2 by multiplying with 0x3fff:b8aa3b29_5c17f0bd = log2(e).

The stored values are the Cody & Waite ALOG denominator coefficients b3, b2, b1, b0 in descending order: 1.0, -35.66797773903464617, +312.0322209192453284, -769.4993210849487978. The leading 1.0 is stored explicitly rather than assumed, which is why the table holds one more entry than the term count the caller passes. The CS: override on the loads is only an encoding artifact: the table sits at offset 0x296c of the emu387 module's own _TEXT segment, and in the flat 32-bit model CS and DS alias the same memory.

Pool: crt  [its only reader, FUN_00051220, matches Watcom EMU387.LIB module emu387 byte for byte at module offset 10736, and these 40 bytes appear verbatim in emu387.lib]

Rebuild note:
These are 10-byte extended reals, not doubles. Watcom 10.0a's long double is 8 bytes, so the obvious C spelling -- an array of four long double constants -- gives a 32-byte table with an 8-byte stride, and the evaluator's LEA EDI,[EDI+0xa] would then walk off into the neighbouring numerator and return garbage for every logarithm on a machine without a 387. Emit the raw byte image, or better, do not re-emit this module at all: resolve the emulator out of EMU387.LIB with wlink.

=== 000513f2 [PLATE]
Nine 80-bit x87 extended constants: the Maclaurin coefficients of sin, highest order first -- 1/17!, -1/15!, 1/13!, -1/11!, 1/9!, -1/7!, 1/5!, -1/3!, and finally 1.0.

Read-only, never written, and reached by exactly one instruction: LEA EDX,[0x513f2] at 00051609 inside FUN_000514b8, the 80x87 emulator's sine/cosine core. The core adds n*10 to the base and calls FUN_00051a0e(value, coeff_table, 8 - n), a Horner evaluator that performs coeff_count multiply-add steps and therefore consumes elements n through 8 inclusive, always finishing on the trailing 1.0. n is the number of leading (tiniest) terms to skip, chosen from the argument's magnitude: FUN_000514b8 reduces the argument modulo pi/2 (the exponent 0x3ffe with significand 0xC90FDAA2_2168C235 pushed at 000514e5, 00051518 and 00051539), builds an octant code in AL, clamps -(exponent - 0x3ffe) to 0..8 and reads n from the nine-word table at 000514a6, whose entries are 0,1,2,3,4,4,5,5,6 -- so a smaller reduced argument evaluates fewer terms, and n never exceeds 6 (three coefficients minimum).

The octant parity decides which series runs: the branch at 000515ed reaches this sine table, while the branch at 000515c9 reaches the cosine table at 0005144c, which holds the matching even coefficients 1/16!, -1/14!, 1/12!, -1/10!, 1/8!, -1/6!, 1/4!, -1/2!, 1.0 in the same nine 10-byte slots. Bits of the octant code then flip the sign of the result at 0005163c and 00051672.

It sits in the code segment of its own object among the emulator's other read-only tables.

Pool: crt  [only the 80x87 emulator reaches it; these 90 bytes appear verbatim at segment offset 0x2bc2 of the emu387 module in Watcom 10.0a lib386/DOS/emu387.lib, whose segment base maps to 0004e830 in FDPS -- the already-named L$1_emu387_ftst_zero]

Rebuild note:
The elements are 10-byte x87 extended values, not doubles. Declaring the obvious `static const double sin_coeff[9] = { ... };` gives an 8-byte stride, and the emulator's index-times-10 addressing then walks straight off the ends of the elements and feeds the series garbage. This module is stock vendor code and should be resolved out of EMU387.LIB by wlink rather than re-emitted.

=== 000514a6 [PLATE]
Number of leading Taylor coefficients the 80-bit sine/cosine kernel drops, indexed by the magnitude of the reduced argument.

Read only at 00051595, in FUN_000514b8 -- the extended-precision sin/cos/tan kernel that the 387 emulator's FSIN/FCOS/FSINCOS/FPTAN handlers reach through the mode wrappers 000516af (sine), 000516b9 (cosine) and 000516c6 (tangent). === 000516d4 [PLATE]
Four 80-bit x87 extended constants; entry k holds 2^(2^k / 16), i.e. 2^(1/16) = 1.0442737824, 2^(1/8) = 1.0905077327, 2^(1/4) = 1.1892071150, 2^(1/2) = 1.4142135624.

Read-only, never written, and reached by exactly one instruction: LEA ESI,[0x516d4] at 00051871 inside FUN_000516fc, the 80x87 emulator's F2XM1 (2^x - 1) core. That routine strips the sign at 0005170a and folds a negative argument with 2^x = 2^(1+x)/2 (00051728 adds -1.0, 0005173d flips the sign, and ESI is left at -1 so 000518b0 can decrement the result's exponent by one). It then splits the folded argument at 00051741: BX = exponent + 4 and the mantissa is shifted left until BX drops below 0x3fff, so ECX collects floor(16*y) while EDX:EAX keeps the renormalised remainder, which is stored back to [EDI] and run through the rational approximation of 2^r at 0005178a..00051866 (inline coefficients 20.8137712, 0.0577611358, 7.2135034108). The loop at 00051877 then multiplies that partial result back up: it walks ECX bit by bit (SHR ECX,1 / JNC 000518aa) and, for every set bit, calls the soft-float multiply 000507be with the entry the walking pointer is on -- reading mantissa low from CS:[ESI], mantissa high from CS:[ESI+4] and the exponent word from CS:[ESI+8] at 00051896 / 00051892 / 0005188d -- before stepping 10 bytes with LEA ESI,[ESI+0xa] at 000518aa. Bit k therefore contributes 2^(2^k/16) and the whole product is 2^(ECX/16). Adding -1.0 at 000518c4 finishes F2XM1.

Each element is Watcom's 10-byte in-memory extended real: mantissa low dword at +0, mantissa high dword at +4, sign bit plus 15-bit biased exponent word at +8. The exponent word is 0x3fff in all four entries, so every factor lies in [1,2). Four entries cover ECX = 0..15, that is |x| < 1; an argument of exactly 1.0 makes ECX 16, and the fifth step would read the ten bytes at 000516fc, which are the routine's own prologue.

Pool: crt  [its only reader is a routine of the EMU387.LIB emu387 module that owns the whole soft-float package around it, and that module exports no name for this table]

Rebuild note:
The four entries are 10-byte x87 extended reals while Watcom 10.0a's long double is 8 bytes, so the obvious static long double t[4] = { 1.04427378, 1.09050773, 1.18920712, 1.41421356 }; emits a 32-byte table at 8-byte stride with truncated values; the multiply loop steps LEA ESI,[ESI+0xa] and reads an exponent word at +8, so it would walk off the table and F2XM1 -- and with it exp/pow on a machine with no coprocessor -- would return nonsense. Emit the raw 40-byte image, or link the emulator from EMU387.LIB instead of re-emitting the module.

=== 0005285c [PLATE]
128-slot dispatch table of the Miles AIL software mixer's output-converter routines: slot N holds the entry of AIL_internal_mix_finalize_<N>, the loop that packs the 32-bit mix accumulators into the DIG driver's DMA buffer in one particular PCM output format.

Statically initialised in the image and never written at run time -- the LE loader's relocations supply the 60 live entries, and the other 68 slots are genuine NULL holes of the index, not padding. Read only by AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_format (00054765), as CALL dword ptr [EAX*4 + 0x5285c] with EAX taken from the mixer-variant selector word at 000614f8 that the same function builds from the DIG_DRIVER's output format at +0x18 and its flags at +0x1c; that dispatcher is entered from the DIG driver install, DMA-buffer rebuild, interrupt-time mix service and teardown paths (000469f0, 000463c0, 000461d0, 00046940). AIL_internal_register_mix_globals (00054823) mentions this address a second time for a different reason: it is the low end of the linear range 0005285c..00054823 handed to the DPMI lock primitive at 0003cb01, because the table and the converter bodies behind it must stay resident for interrupt-time mixing.

The index is a 7-bit format mask: 0x01 = signed output (no sign-bias XOR), 0x02 = reversed channel order, 0x04 = MSB-first samples, 0x08 = split output (two de-interleaved destination buffers), 0x10 = stereo, 0x20 = 16-bit, 0x40 = saturating clamp for multi-voice accumulator overflow. Combinations that cannot occur are NULL: byte-swap on 8-bit output, and channel-reverse or split on mono. Live slots are 0x00-0x01, 0x10-0x13, 0x18-0x1b, 0x20-0x21, 0x24-0x25, 0x30-0x3f, 0x40-0x41, 0x50-0x53, 0x58-0x5b, 0x60-0x61, 0x64-0x65 and 0x70-0x7f, and their bodies run contiguously from 00052c5c to 00053899. The 128-slot sibling table immediately after this one at 00052a5c holds the AIL_internal_mix_loop_* voice-mixing kernels and is indexed by the same selector word.

Pool: ail  [both referencing functions are AIL DIG-driver internals with ailv3.lib byte matches, every live entry is an ailv3.lib-matched AIL_internal_mix_finalize_* body, and no game or CRT code reaches the table]

Rebuild note:
The 68 NULL slots are addressed by the same mask as the live ones, so this must be emitted as one 128-entry array with the holes left in place; writing the 60 live converters as a dense initialiser list, or replacing the table with a switch, shifts every index. It also has to be the first object of the AIL mixer module, because AIL_internal_register_mix_globals DPMI-locks the fixed linear range from this table's address up to its own entry -- letting the linker place the table after the converter bodies leaves part of the interrupt-time code unlocked.

=== 00052a5c [PLATE]
128-slot dispatch table of the Miles AIL software mixer's voice mix-in kernels: slot N holds the entry of AIL_internal_mix_loop_<N>, the hand-written loop that reads one voice's PCM samples and accumulates them into the 32-bit mix accumulator buffer in one particular combination of source format, resampling rate and volume scaling.

Statically initialised in the image and never written at run time -- the LE relocations supply the 72 live entries and the other 56 slots are genuine NULL holes of the index, not padding. The single read is CALL dword ptr [EBP*0x4 + 0x52a5c] at 000546a0 in AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample, with EBP loaded two instructions earlier from the mixer-variant selector data_ail_mix_format_flags (000614f8) that the same function assembles from the voice's format fields; the sibling table at 0005285c is indexed by the same word and holds the output-format converters that run after all voices are summed. AIL_internal_register_mix_globals (00054823) never names this address, but it falls inside the linear range 0005285c..00054823 that function hands to the DPMI lock primitive at 0003cb01, because table and kernels must stay resident for interrupt-time mixing.

The index is the 7-bit format mask, read here as a description of the source voice: 0x01 = stereo destination (accumulate into the left/right dword pair, 8 bytes per output frame), 0x02 = stereo source frame, 0x04 = take the second channel of that frame, 0x08 = 16-bit source samples, 0x10 = source samples are already signed (no XOR 0x8000 offset-binary bias), 0x20 = resample through the 16.16 position whose fraction is at 0006150c and whose two-entry integer step is at 00061510, 0x40 = translate each source byte through the caller's 256-entry dword volume/pan table (a second table at +0x400 for the right channel). A slot is NULL exactly where the combination cannot arise: bit 0x04 without bit 0x02 (16 slots), and bit 0x10 together with bit 0x40 -- the whole 0x50-0x5f and 0x70-0x7f blocks, 40 further slots -- because the volume table already carries the source's signedness. The 72 live bodies run contiguously from 0005389a to 00054563, ending where AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample itself begins.

The kernels are entered on a private register contract, not a C calling convention: the dispatcher loads EDI with the mix-buffer cursor from 00061504, ESI with the source cursor from 000614fc, EDX with the voice's volume/pan table at sample+0x48, ECX with 0x80000000 and EAX/EBX with 0, and after the call reads the advanced ESI back to update the voice's play position and compares EDI against the mix-buffer end at 00061508 to decide whether the buffer is full. Each kernel also stops on the source end pointer at 00061500.

Pool: ail  [only the AIL DIG mixer reaches it, every live entry is an ailv3.lib-matched AIL_internal_mix_loop_* body, and no game or CRT code refers to the table]

Rebuild note:
The 56 NULL slots are addressed by the same mask as the live ones, so this must be emitted as one 128-entry array with the holes in place; writing the 72 live kernels as a dense initialiser list, or replacing the table with a switch, shifts every index. The entries are hand-written assembly with a private register contract (ESI/EDI/EDX/ECX in, ESI and EDI back out), so giving them ordinary C prototypes and letting the compiler choose registers breaks the dispatcher. The table also has to stay between the converter bank at 0005285c and the kernel bodies, because AIL_internal_register_mix_globals DPMI-locks that one linear range.
