=== 00056799 [PLATE]
Returns the address of the keyboard scancode byte the game's INT 09h handler writes, so input loops can read the current key and clear it.

Algorithm:
Loads the address of the byte at 0x00070006 into EAX and returns; it touches nothing else. That byte is written by fdps_keyboard_isr, which stores the raw scancode it read from port 0x60 there on every key event, break codes (>= 0x80) included, and by fdps_uninstall_keyboard_isr, which sets it to 0xff when it restores the original INT 09h vector. 0xff is not a scancode; it is the no-key-pending value, and callers store it through this pointer themselves to discard a stale key -- fdps_battle_player_phase_loop and fdps_map_cursor_select_loop both do so before entering their loops.

Parameters:
  none.

Returns:
  Pointer to the one-byte scancode slot. *p is the last scancode the ISR saw, or 0xff when no key is pending.

Pool: fdps  [reads state defined by the game's own keyboard ISR; no hit in the Watcom or AIL Function ID sets, and LEA EAX,[imm32] / RET is code for 'return &g;', not a linker island]

=== 000567a0 [PLATE]
Blocks until the player presses a key, then discards every scancode still queued by the keyboard ISR.

Algorithm:
Spins re-reading the scancode ring's read index at 0x00070019 and comparing it against the write index at 0x0007001d, looping while the two are equal, which is the queue-empty condition. fdps_keyboard_isr advances the write index every time it queues a make code, so the loop falls through on the first key press. The routine then stores the read index into the write index, rewinding the queue to empty: the key that ended the wait and anything else pending are thrown away, so the screen that follows does not inherit them. That is the same single store the flush-without-waiting routine at 000567b3 makes. The ring itself is the 10-entry byte buffer at 0x0007000f, dequeued by the routine at 000567be.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  void. EAX is left holding the read index as a by-product of the compare; no caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [shares the scancode ring with the game's own INT 09h handler; no Function ID hit in any library]

=== 000567b3 [PLATE]
Discards every keyboard scancode still queued by the game's INT 09h handler, without waiting for one.

Algorithm:
Loads the read index of the keyboard ring from 0x00070019 and stores it into the write index at 0x0007001d, leaving the two equal. fdps_keyboard_isr advances 0x0007001d as it appends scancodes to the 10-entry byte ring at 0x0007000f, and the queue-pop function at 000567be advances 0x00070019 as it takes them out, reporting an empty queue (0xff) whenever the two indices match; rewinding the write index onto the read index therefore makes every scancode already in the ring unreachable. Nothing else is touched -- the ring bytes, the last-scancode byte at 0x00070006 and the ISR's repeat-suppression byte at 0x00070021 keep their values. The sibling at 000567a0 is the blocking form of the same operation: it spins until the indices differ and only then performs this identical store.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  nothing; EAX is left holding the read index as a side effect of the load and no caller reads it.

Pool: fdps  [shares the keyboard ring globals with the game's own INT 09h handler, which the Watcom CRT and AIL never own; no Function ID hit in either library set]

=== 000567be [PLATE]
Takes the next scancode out of the keyboard queue that fdps_keyboard_isr fills, or reports the queue empty.

Algorithm:
Sets the no-key marker 0xff in AL first, then loads the queue's read index from 0x00070019 and compares it with the write index at 0x0007001d; equal indices are the queue-empty condition and the routine returns the marker untouched. Otherwise it reads the byte at 0x0007000f + read index -- the 10-entry ring that fdps_keyboard_isr appends make codes to -- then increments the read index and stores 0 back when the increment reaches 10, the ring length. Only the read index is written, so it never contends with fdps_keyboard_isr, which owns the write index and the ring bytes. 0xff cannot collide with a real entry because fdps_keyboard_isr queues nothing with bit 7 set, i.e. no break codes. The same ring is emptied without reading by fdps_flush_keyboard_queue, and by fdps_wait_any_key after it has blocked for one key.

Parameters:
  none

Returns:
  The dequeued scancode, 0x01..0x7f, or 0xff when nothing is queued. Only AL is set; the upper 24 bits of EAX keep whatever the caller left in them, and every call site masks the result with AND EAX,0xff before using it.

Pool: fdps  [shares the scancode ring globals with the game's own INT 09h handler; no Function ID hit in either library set, and all callers are game-side interactive loops]

Rebuild note:
The ring has no fullness test: fdps_keyboard_isr advances the write index unconditionally, so after ten unread scancodes the write index catches up to the read index and this routine reports the queue empty while ten bytes sit in it. Writing the obvious ring buffer -- a pending count, or a full check that drops the incoming byte instead -- changes which keystrokes the game sees; keep the two bare indices with 'equal means empty' and the 0xff marker.

=== 00056898 [PLATE]
Computes the FDE.SAV integrity checksum: the unsigned sum of every byte of the save image except its trailing 4-byte checksum field.

Algorithm:
Hand-written assembly. Loads save_image into ESI (and, unused, into EDI), sets ECX = size - 4 so that the trailing 4-byte checksum field is left out of the sum, zeroes EBX (the accumulator) and EAX, then loops LODSB / ADD EBX,EAX for ECX iterations, adding each byte zero-extended to 32 bits. Moves EBX into EAX and returns. EBX is used as the accumulator without ever being saved or restored, and the MOV EDI,ESI is dead: both are consequences of sharing its shape with fdps_xor_crypt_buffer, which sits immediately after it at 000568b7 and does use EDI, for STOSB. ECX is a LOOP count, so a size of exactly 4 would iterate 2^32 times; every call site passes 0x59cb.

Parameters:
  save_image -- pointer to the plaintext (descrambled) 0x59cb-byte FDE.SAV image. All four callers pass that buffer.
  size -- total size of the image in bytes, counting the trailing 4-byte checksum field; 0x59cb at every call site.

Returns:
  The 32-bit sum of the first size-4 bytes. fdps_load_savegame and fdps_title_screen compare it with the dword stored at save_image+0x59c7 and treat a mismatch as a corrupt save; fdps_save_game_screen and fdps_battle_system_submenu write it to that dword before scrambling the image with fdps_xor_crypt_buffer and writing the file out.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in any library, hash unique in the image, four game callers and no callees; the hardcoded 'length minus 4' skip is a game data-format detail no CRT routine has, and 31 bytes of loop logic is neither a thunk nor a linker island]

Blit mode dispatcher: publishes pitch, width and height into the shared graphics globals, loads src/dst into ESI/EDI with EDX = pitch - width as the end-of-row advance, and calls one of thirteen blit kernels chosen by the mode byte (0-12); any other mode draws nothing.
Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; all callers and all callees are game code]
Evidence: fid.watcom and fid.ail are both empty, full_hash unique in the image and absent from ailv3.lib, so no library byte match. 46 call sites over 27 distinct callers, all game routines (fdps_cel_blit_sprite, fdps_draw_unit_status_panel, fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input, fdps_load_global_resources, ...) and all thirteen callees are private to this dispatcher; the 16-bit words at 0x00070022/0x00070024/0x0007002e written here are read back by those kernels, making writer and readers one game-owned module. Too large and stateful for binary_artifact; the C runtime has no blit-parameter block, and nothing here touches AIL state.
Name: fdps_ + snake_case for game code, describing the dispatch this body actually performs; no vendor symbol involved.
Boundary: 000568db-00056a0c, frame prologue at the entry and every arm converging on POP EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP; RET at 00056a08; empty gap after, and 00056a0d is the separate mode-0 kernel. Thirteen four-byte runs of 0x90, one between each JNZ and the CALL it guards, at 00056916, 00056929, 0005693c, 0005694f, 00056962, 00056975, 00056988, 0005699b, 000569ae, 000569c1, 000569d4, 000569e7 and 000569fa -- 52 bytes in total, all of it padding belonging to this body.
Signature: __cdecl, seven stack arguments (src, dst, width, height, pitch, arg6, mode) with a plain RET and stack_purge 0 -- confirmed by the assembly, not a guess. arg6 at [EBP+0x1c] is unused here but is read out of this frame by ten of the thirteen kernels (all but 00056a0d, 00057551 and 000575ed), in four different shapes: a pointer (fdps_rle_blit_remap_sprite_and_backdrop at 00056a8d, and 00056b25, 00057114), three packed bytes (00056bb7), two packed words (00056c5e, 00056e2a) and a descriptor pointer (0005761b, 00057793, 00057916, 00057a74) -- so the kernels are hand-written assembly that shares this frame. The sharing is not read-only: 0005761b, 00057793, 00057916 and 00057a74 also WRITE this frame's argument slots [EBP+0x8] through [EBP+0x1c] as their own scratch (MOV [EBP+0x8],EBX at 00057627, MOV [EBP+0xc],EAX at 0005764f, MOV [EBP+0x10],EDX at 00057654, MOV [EBP+0x14],EAX at 0005765c, MOV [EBP+0x18],EAX at 00057664, MOV [EBP+0x1c],EDX at 00057696).

=== 00056a05 [EOL]

=== 00056a0d [PLATE]
Blit mode 0: decodes an RLE 4-op pixel stream into an 8bpp destination surface, writing every pixel it draws through unchanged.

Algorithm:
Per row it loads the row width from DAT_00070024 into BX, then reads one command byte from ESI at a time until that counter reaches exactly zero. The top two bits of the command byte select the op, the low six bits carry len-1, so len = (cmd & 0x3f) + 1, i.e. 1..64:
  00 fill      -- reads one pixel byte from the stream and REP STOSB writes it over len destination bytes; width -= len.
  01 stretched -- reads one pixel byte and writes it into every second destination byte across a 2*len span (INC EDI then STOSB, so the second byte of each pair is written and the first is left holding whatever was already there); width -= 2*len.
  10 literal   -- REP MOVSB copies len bytes straight out of the stream; width -= len.
  11 skip      -- EDI += len with no write, i.e. a transparent run; width -= len.
When the row width hits zero it adds the end-of-row advance in EDX to EDI, decrements the row counter at DAT_00070022, and restarts at the entry, which reloads a fresh row width. It returns once that row counter reaches zero.

Op 01 is not a half-tone: replaying all 99 .CEL sheets shipped with the game (28,467 sprites) finds only 791 of these runs, 746 of them one pixel long, and their start column is even 462 times and odd 329 times, so nothing aligns them to a pixel pair. What they actually produce is a single untouched column immediately left of the pixel they write -- and 642 of the 838 untouched columns have a written pixel on their other side too, i.e. a one-pixel hole punched into otherwise solid content (M050.CEL sprite 17 row 2 is a fully painted tile row with one such hole at column 11). Two bytes buy what a skip-then-literal pair would cost three, so this is the encoder's packing of 'leave one column, then one pixel', and the hole it leaves is part of the original's output.

This is the kernel fdps_blit_dispatch calls for mode 0, the plain sprite and tile blit. fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_vertical (mode 8) reuses this same body bottom-up: it points EDI at the last raster line and tail-jumps here with a negated row stride in EDX. fdps_rle_blit_remap_sprite_and_backdrop (mode 1) and fdps_rle_blit_with_palette_remap (mode 2) decode the identical four ops but push every pixel through a 256-entry remap table.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. This is hand-written assembly; every input arrives in a register or a global, all of them set up by fdps_blit_dispatch immediately before the call:
    ESI          -- RLE command stream, advanced in place past the bytes it consumes
    EDI          -- destination pixel pointer, advanced in place
    EDX          -- end-of-row advance, computed by the caller as pitch - width
    ECX          -- must be zero on entry; the body writes only CL but reads all of CX/ECX
    DAT_00070024 -- u16 row width in pixels, reloaded at the top of every row
    DAT_00070022 -- u16 rows remaining, decremented to zero by this routine

Returns:
  nothing. EAX, EBX, ECX, ESI and EDI are all destroyed.

Pool: fdps  [no fid hit in either library, and it shares the blit width/height globals with fdps_blit_dispatch, which calls it as blit mode 0]

Rebuild note:
This kernel cannot be written as an ordinary C function: it takes ESI (stream), EDI (destination) and EDX (row advance) in registers, destroys EBX, ESI and EDI, which Watcom's convention says a callee preserves, and it requires the upper 24 bits of ECX to be zero on entry -- fdps_blit_dispatch does XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d for exactly that. The body only ever writes CL, but then uses the whole of CX in SUB BX,CX and the whole of ECX in REP MOVSB / REP STOSB / LOOP, so a caller that skips the zeroing gets runaway runs that overrun the destination. A second trap is the row terminator: OR BX,BX / JNZ ends a row only on an exact zero, so hardening it to 'width <= 0' changes behaviour on any stream whose last run overshoots the row. A third is op 01: the obvious reading of a 'stretched fill' is that it doubles each pixel across the 2*len span, and writing it that way paints the columns the original leaves alone. The original writes only the second byte of each pair (INC EDI before STOSB) and the gaps really do stay as they were -- measured on the shipped sheets, most of those gaps are one-pixel holes inside painted content, so filling them changes what the game draws.

=== 00056a8d [PLATE]
RLE sprite blit kernel, mode 1 of fdps_blit_dispatch: draws one RLE 4-op pixel stream through a 256-entry palette remap table and puts the destination pixels showing through the sprite's transparent runs through the same table, so every pixel of the width x height rectangle ends up as remap[...].

Algorithm:
Entered by a plain CALL from fdps_blit_dispatch (0005692d, the CMP BH,0x1 arm) with that function's registers still live: ESI = the RLE command stream, EDI = the destination pixel, EDX = pitch - width (the end-of-row advance), EAX and ECX zeroed, and EBP still the dispatcher's frame pointer. The first instruction overwrites EBP with [EBP+0x1c], the dispatcher's sixth argument, which here is the base of the 256-byte palette remap table. Each row starts by loading BX with the row width from DAT_00070024, then decodes command bytes until BX is exactly zero. A command byte's low six bits give len = (byte & 0x3f) + 1 (1..64) and its top two bits select the op:
  0b00 RLE fill -- read one stream byte, write remap[byte] to len destination pixels with REP STOSB; BX -= len.
  0b01 stretched fill -- read one stream byte, write remap[byte] to len pixels spaced two apart, the first landing at EDI+1; BX -= 2*len.
  0b10 literal copy -- for each of len stream bytes write remap[byte]; BX -= len.
  0b11 backdrop recolour -- consume no stream byte; for len pixels read the pixel already at EDI, write remap[that pixel] back and advance; BX -= len. This is the op that the kernels at 0x00056a0d (mode 0) and 0x00056b25 (mode 2) implement as a transparent skip (ADD EDI,ECX).
Every lookup is MOV AL,byte ptr [EAX + EBP*0x1] with EAX holding nothing but the pixel byte, so the table index stays in 0..255 only because the dispatcher zeroed EAX; ECX likewise carries the run length for REP/LOOP only because the dispatcher zeroed it. When BX reaches zero the row ends: EDI += EDX, the remaining-row counter DAT_00070022 is decremented, and the outer loop reloads BX for the next row. The routine returns when DAT_00070022 reaches zero.

Place in the kernel family:
The thirteen kernels split into pairs on this one op. fdps_rle_blit_with_palette_remap (mode 2) applies the same remap table but leaves the transparent runs alone; fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop (mode 0xa) and fdps_rle_blit_tint (mode 0xb) are that same pair with a tint blend in place of the table lookup. This kernel is the remap half of the "affect the backdrop too" side.

Nothing in the shipped executable selects mode 1. Every path that can reach the dispatcher's mode argument resolves to a constant: 31 direct call sites pass 0, eight pass 9, two pass 8, one passes 0xb; fdps_draw_scene_layer passes 9 or 0xa; fdps_blit_unit_sprite passes its caller's 3 or 0; fdps_cel_blit_sprite passes its own eighth argument, a literal 0 at 50 call sites and 4 at the other four; and fdps_draw_tilemap_cell passes the draw request's +0x20 field, which the eighteen callers of fdps_draw_composite_sprite set to 0, 3 or 9 and which fdps_draw_composite_sprite itself replaces with 0 or 9 per part when it arrives as 0. No entry in that chain has a non-call reference, so no function pointer can bypass the census. The modes that reach the dispatcher are 0, 3, 4, 8, 9, 0xa and 0xb; 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and 0xc are compiled in and unreachable.

Parameters:
  none on the stack -- the inputs arrive in registers and globals prepared by fdps_blit_dispatch:
  ESI -- base of the RLE command byte stream, pointing past the caller's header.
  EDI -- destination address of the first pixel of the first row, in an 8bpp linear surface.
  EDX -- pitch - width, added to EDI at the end of every row.
  EBP -- on entry the dispatcher's frame pointer; [EBP+0x1c] is its sixth argument, the 256-byte palette remap table, and EBP is replaced by that pointer for the rest of the body.
  DAT_00070024 -- row width in pixels, reloaded once per row.
  DAT_00070022 -- number of rows still to draw, decremented once per row.

Returns:
  nothing. EAX, EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI and EBP are all left modified; in particular the caller's frame pointer is destroyed, which fdps_blit_dispatch survives only because it unwinds through ESP-relative POPs.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; the only caller is fdps_blit_dispatch, and 0x00070022/0x00070024 are that dispatcher's blit parameter block, not library state]

Rebuild note:
The row terminates only on the width counter hitting exactly zero (SUB BX,CX then OR BX,BX / JNZ), so a stream whose runs overshoot the row width does not stop -- BX wraps and the decoder keeps painting past the end of the row; writing the obvious while (remaining > 0) in C would end the row early and silently change what a malformed or deliberately over-long stream draws. The stretched-fill op writes its first pixel at dst+1, not dst (INC EDI before STOSB at 00056ad1), so the run occupies the odd columns of its 2*len span; the obvious for (i = 0; i < len; i++) { dst[0] = c; dst += 2; } shifts the whole run one pixel left. And the 0b11 op is not the transparent skip it is in most of the family: copying the mode-0 or mode-2 body and only swapping the table in leaves the backdrop inside the sprite's bounding box unremapped.

=== 00056b25 [PLATE]
Blit mode 2 of fdps_blit_dispatch: draws one RLE-coded sprite into the destination surface, passing every pixel it writes through a 256-byte palette translation table. No call site in the shipped program ever asks for mode 2, so this kernel is unreachable in FDPS.LE; see Reachability.

Algorithm:
Takes the translation table base out of the caller's frame slot [EBP+0x1c] (fdps_blit_dispatch's arg6) into EBP, destroying its own EBP for the rest of the call. Then, per destination row, it loads the row width from the 16-bit global at 0x00070024 into BX and decodes control bytes from ESI until BX reaches exactly zero. A control byte's low six bits are a length minus one, so len = (b & 0x3f) + 1 (1..64), and its top two bits select the run:
  00 -- fill: read one source byte, write table[byte] to len consecutive destination pixels (REP STOSB); charges len columns.
  01 -- stretched fill: read one source byte, write table[byte] to len pixels at stride 2 starting at dst+1 (INC EDI / STOSB / LOOP), leaving the pixels in between untouched; charges 2*len columns.
  10 -- literal: read len source bytes and write table[byte] for each; charges len columns.
  11 -- skip: advance the destination by len pixels without writing, i.e. transparency; charges len columns.
At the end of a row EDI advances by EDX, the end-of-row slack (pitch - width) that fdps_blit_dispatch computed, and the 16-bit row counter at 0x00070022 is decremented in place; the routine returns when that counter reaches zero, leaving the global at 0. The stream format is the game's four-opcode RLE, the same one the untranslated mode-0 kernel fdps_blit_rle_passthrough decodes; the mode-1 kernel fdps_rle_blit_remap_sprite_and_backdrop uses the same table but spends its 11 opcode recolouring the pixels already in the destination instead of skipping them, and the mode-3 kernel fdps_blit_rle_recolor replaces the table lookup with an arithmetic recolour of every pixel.

Reachability:
Mode 2 is never selected. Every one of the 26 static callers of fdps_blit_dispatch was enumerated; the literal mode bytes pushed are 0, 8, 9 and 0x0b, and the four call sites that pass a variable resolve as follows:
  fdps_cel_blit_sprite -- forwards its eighth stack argument (the argument at [EBP+0x2c] becomes the dispatcher's arg6, not the mode). Across all 54 of its call sites that eighth argument is the literal 0 (50 sites) or the literal 4 (4 sites).
  fdps_blit_unit_sprite -- forwards its blit_mode argument, which is the literal 3 at two call sites and 3 or 0 in fdps_flash_units_in_color.
  fdps_draw_scene_layer -- never forwards its layer_mode at all: it only compares it with 0 and 1, and pushes 0x0a when it is 1 and 9 otherwise. The layer_mode byte itself comes from byte +0x1c of the 0x20-byte per-layer record in dscNN.dat (Field2.vfs), which across the shipped data holds 1 for 62 layers, 0 for 3 and 2 for one (DSC07.DAT layer 1) -- but that 2 is a layer flag, not a blit mode, and never reaches the dispatcher.
  fdps_draw_tilemap_cell -- forwards field +0x20 of the 0x24-byte SAF draw request, and every one of the seventeen builders of that record writes that field with the literal 0, 3 or 9.
Nothing takes the address of fdps_blit_dispatch, so there is no indirect path into it. The modes the game actually asks for are 0, 3, 4, 8, 9, 0x0a and 0x0b; modes 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and 0x0c are compiled in and unreached. Consequence for the rebuild: this kernel cannot be exercised by playing the game, so a transcription error in it will not surface in playtesting.

Parameters:
  none in the C sense -- the routine takes no stack arguments. Its inputs are registers set up by fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI = the RLE stream, EDI = the destination pixel address, EDX = pitch - width, and EBP = the caller's frame pointer, whose +0x1c slot holds the translation table base. EAX and ECX must arrive with their upper 24 bits clear (the dispatcher's XOR EAX,EAX / XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d), because the table index is the whole of EAX and REP STOSB, LOOP and ADD EDI,ECX use the whole of ECX. Row width and row count come from the 16-bit globals at 0x00070024 and 0x00070022 that the dispatcher wrote. The table is 256 entries: the index is a zero-extended source byte.

Returns:
  nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either the Watcom or the ailv3 set; the sole caller is the game's blit dispatcher, and this body reads back the same 0x00070022/0x00070024 blit-geometry words that dispatcher writes, so writer and reader are one module]

Rebuild note:
The stretched-fill run (opcode 01) writes its first pixel at dst+1, not at dst -- the loop is INC EDI then STOSB -- so the obvious rewrite `for (i = 0; i < len; i++) dst[i*2] = c;` shifts every stretched span one pixel to the left. The row is also terminated by a 16-bit counter tested for exactly zero (SUB BX,CX / OR BX,BX / JNZ), and opcode 01 subtracts len twice, so a run that overshoots the remaining row width wraps through 65535 and keeps decoding; rewriting the test as `while (width > 0)` on an int quietly changes that behaviour. Neither mistake can be caught by playing the game: no call site in the program selects mode 2, so this kernel has to be got right by reading rather than by testing.

=== 00056bb7 [PLATE]
Blit mode 3 of fdps_blit_dispatch: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface, recolouring every pixel it writes by arithmetic on the palette index rather than through a lookup table.

Algorithm:
Entry state is whatever fdps_blit_dispatch set up before the CALL at 00056953 (the CMP BH,0x3 arm): ESI = the packed pixel stream, EDI = the first destination pixel, EDX = pitch - width (the end-of-row advance), ECX = 0, and EBP still pointing at the dispatcher's own stack frame. The first three instructions lift the recolour operands out of that frame -- tint_offset = [EBP+0x1c], color_base = [EBP+0x1d], band mask = [EBP+0x1e], the three low bytes of the dispatcher's sixth argument -- into DH, DL and AH; only then does PUSH EDX / POP EBP replace EBP with the row advance, which is why those reads come first.
Each row begins by loading BX from the width word at 00070024, the count of destination columns still to fill. A token byte is read from ESI and its top two bits pick one of the four ops of the RLE 4-op stream, the run length in every case being (token & 0x3f) + 1:
  00 -- fill: one source byte, recoloured, REP STOSB'd len times; BX -= len.
  01 -- stretched fill: one source byte, recoloured, written to every other destination byte starting at EDI+1 (the INC EDI at 00056c09 precedes the STOSB), EDI advancing by 2 per pixel; BX -= 2 * len, so the run covers 2 * len columns and leaves the even ones untouched.
  10 -- literal copy: len source bytes, each recoloured and stored in turn; BX -= len.
  11 -- skip: EDI += len with nothing written, leaving the destination pixels as they were; BX -= len.
The recolour applied before every store is AL = ((src + tint_offset) & mask) + color_base, each step in 8 bits (00056be5 / 00056be7 / 00056be9, and the same three instructions on each of the other two writing paths). It never reads the pixel already on the destination, so nothing here blends. This is the construct the predecessor project settled as ((src + tint_offset) & 7) + color_base (fd2_tile_blit_24x24_with_tint_offset, and the 'translucent overlay' palette_op mode of fd2_rle_blit_sprite), generalised here by making the band mask a parameter instead of a literal 7: with mask 7 the sprite is folded into the 8-colour palette band anchored at color_base while tint_offset rotates which colour of the band each pixel lands on; with mask 0 the whole sprite collapses to the single index color_base.
A row ends when BX reaches exactly zero -- the test is OR BX,BX / JNZ, not a bound -- whereupon EDI += the row advance held in EBP, the row counter at 00070022 is decremented, and the next row starts by reloading BX. The routine returns when that counter reaches zero, so the blit consumes the counter and leaves it at zero.
Every call site that selects mode 3 with a literal reaches it through fdps_blit_unit_sprite with 0x0000ff00 as the dispatcher's sixth argument -- tint_offset 0, color_base 0xff, mask 0 -- which is the collapsing case: the unit is painted as a flat silhouette in palette index 0xff. fdps_unit_rest and fdps_battle_advance_turn both use that for the white rest flash. Other call sites take the mode from data (fdps_draw_tilemap_cell reads it out of a draw-request record, fdps_cel_blit_sprite from its own argument), so other tint_offset / color_base / mask triples can reach this kernel.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. The contract is by register and through the caller's frame: ESI = packed 4-op RLE pixel stream, EDI = destination pixel pointer, EDX = end-of-row advance (pitch - width), ECX = 0, EBP = fdps_blit_dispatch's frame pointer, whose bytes at +0x1c, +0x1d and +0x1e supply tint_offset, color_base and the band mask. Width and height come from the 16-bit words at 00070024 and 00070022, which fdps_blit_dispatch writes from its own width and height arguments.

Returns:
  nothing. It destroys EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI and EBP without saving them; fdps_blit_dispatch restores EBX, ESI, EDI and EBP from its own prologue after the call.

Pool: fdps  [called only by fdps_blit_dispatch; shares the blitter's state globals at 00070022 and 00070024; no library byte match on either the Watcom or the ail set]

Rebuild note:
Three things a straight rewrite gets wrong. (1) The 01 stretched-fill run writes the odd destination columns: INC EDI precedes STOSB at 00056c09, so the pixels land at dst[1], dst[3], ... while the run still charges 2*len against the column budget; the obvious `for (i = 0; i < len; i++) dst[2*i] = px;` puts every pixel one column to the left of the original. (2) The three recolour bytes are the low bytes of fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument, read straight out of the dispatcher's frame as an immediate value, but that same argument is a 256-byte remap table pointer for modes 1 and 2 and a descriptor pointer for the blend modes, so giving it one C type across all thirteen kernels is wrong. (3) The byte packing is not the predecessor's. FD2 packs this same recolour as color_base = op & 0xff and offset = (op >> 8) & 0xff with the mask hardcoded to 7; FDPS packs the offset in the low byte (+0x1c, added before the mask), color_base in byte 1 (+0x1d, added after it) and the band mask in byte 2 (+0x1e). Carrying FD2's expression or its packed constants across swaps the two operands, and because the observed FDPS constant 0x0000ff00 relies on mask 0 to collapse the output to one index, the swap turns a flat white silhouette into a scrambled sprite rather than into an obvious crash.

=== 00056bf4 [EOL]

=== 00056c14 [EOL]

=== 00056c38 [EOL]

=== 00056c5e [PLATE]
Blit mode 4 of fdps_blit_dispatch: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface rescaled to an arbitrary destination width and height.

Algorithm:
Reads its two scale words straight out of the caller's stack frame -- [EBP+0x1c] is the destination width and [EBP+0x1e] the destination height, the low and high halves of fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument -- and publishes them into the shared graphics parameter block as DAT_00070028 and DAT_0007002a. It then zeroes EBP and reuses it as a Bresenham accumulator for the rest of the routine. DAT_0007002c is seeded with the destination height as the count of destination rows still to write, DAT_00070026 with the same value as the vertical accumulator, and DAT_00070030 with the destination pitch (DAT_0007002e) minus the destination width, the advance from the end of one destination row to the start of the next.

The source width is loaded into DX once, at 00056c9f, above the row loop's entry; each destination row then loads BX and BP with the destination width and pushes ESI, which points at the first control byte of the current source row. It then decodes control bytes until BX destination pixels have been written. The top two bits of a control byte select the operation and the low six bits plus one give its length: 00 is a run of the one following byte, 01 is a half-tone run of the one following byte written to every other pixel over twice the length, 10 is a literal copy of length bytes, 11 skips length pixels and leaves the destination untouched. Every operation drives the same horizontal Bresenham inner loop: while BP is below the source width it adds the destination width and consumes one pixel of the run (for op 10 that also advances ESI, for op 01 it flips the half-tone phase held in AH); once BP has reached the source width it subtracts the source width and emits one destination pixel, decrementing BX. A source pixel is therefore emitted more than once when scaling up and dropped when scaling down, and a run may be abandoned part-way when the destination row fills.

At the end of a destination row ESI is popped back to the start of the source row, and the vertical Bresenham runs: while the accumulator is not above the source height (DAT_00070022) it calls fdps_rle_skip_row to step ESI over one whole encoded source row and adds the destination height; then it subtracts the source height once and stores the accumulator back into DAT_00070026. EDI advances by DAT_00070030 and DAT_0007002c is decremented; the routine returns when no destination rows are left. A source row is thus re-decoded from its start as many times as the vertical scale calls for.

Parameters:
  none in C terms -- the routine takes no stack arguments. Its inputs arrive in registers and in the parameter block fdps_blit_dispatch fills: ESI = the source RLE stream, EDI = the destination surface, EBP = the caller's own frame pointer, from which the packed destination width and height are read; DAT_00070022 = source height in rows, DAT_00070024 = source width in pixels, DAT_0007002e = destination pitch in bytes.

Returns:
  nothing.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in Watcom 10.0x or ailv3.lib; shares the graphics parameter block at 0x00070022-0x00070033 with its caller fdps_blit_dispatch and its callee fdps_rle_skip_row]

Rebuild note:
The kernel reads its two scale words out of fdps_blit_dispatch's own stack frame at [EBP+0x1c]/[EBP+0x1e], then zeroes EBP at 00056c74 and uses it as the Bresenham accumulator for the whole routine without ever restoring it, so it destroys the caller's frame pointer and only survives because fdps_blit_dispatch's epilogue pops EBP off ESP instead of relying on it -- a rewrite that keeps this as inline assembly must not assume EBP is live across the call, and one that turns it into a real C function must have the dispatcher unpack that argument and pass it. Second, the source cursor is pushed at the top of every destination row and popped back at 00056d84, so a row whose decode stopped part-way (the destination row filled before the run was exhausted) still advances to the next source row only through fdps_rle_skip_row: writing the obvious C that carries one source pointer straight on from wherever the decode stopped desynchronises the stream, and re-decoding the same row for vertical upscaling stops working. Third, the destination row advance is computed sixteen bits wide and stored zero-extended -- MOV BP,[0x0007002e] / SUB BP,[0x00070028] / MOV dword ptr [0x00070030],EBP at 00056c8b-00056c99, with EBP's top half still holding the zero from XOR EBP,EBP at 00056c74 -- so a destination wider than the pitch stores 65534 rather than -2, and the global is signed and does hold genuine negative advances when fdps_rle_blit_translucent and its three neighbours write the dispatcher's full 32-bit EDX into it at 0005761b, 00057793, 00057916 and 00057a74. Fourth, the three sixteen-bit exact-zero terminators are unguarded, and that is the routine's degenerate-input behaviour: a destination width of zero makes DEC BX / JNZ at 00056ce4 (and its three copies) run the row for 0x10000 pixels rather than none; a destination height of zero makes DEC word ptr [0x0007002c] / JNZ at 00056dbb ask for 0x10000 rows; and a destination height of zero additionally never leaves the vertical loop at 00056d8c, because the accumulator is seeded from 0x0007002a at 00056c84 and grown by 0x0007002a at 00056d9e, so it stays at zero, CMP BP,[0x00070022] / JA never takes, and fdps_rle_skip_row is called for ever. A rewrite may not add a zero check: the check would be a behaviour change, and fdps_blit_dispatch, the only thing that reaches this kernel, cannot be assumed to screen its arguments.

=== 00056d25 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler inside the FUN_00056c5e address range

=== 00056d5b [EOL]
Three 0x90 NOP bytes: alignment filler, not reachable code.

=== 00056dc9 [PLATE]
Advances a source pointer past one encoded scanline of a 4-op RLE pixel stream without drawing anything, so a scaling blitter can drop the source rows it is not going to show.

Algorithm:
Loads the source bitmap width in pixels from the word at 0x00070024 into BX, the count of source pixels still unaccounted for in this row. Then repeats: LODSB one control byte from ESI and dispatch on its top two bits, the run length in every case being count = (control & 0x3f) + 1, obtained as SHL CL twice to test the two flag bits followed by SHR CL,2 and INC CL.
  00 fill:    one pixel byte follows and covers count pixels -- ESI ends two bytes on, BX -= count.
  01 stretch: one pixel byte follows and covers 2*count columns, the blitters writing it into the second pixel of each pair -- ESI ends two bytes on, BX -= count twice.
  10 literal: count pixel bytes follow -- ESI ends 1 + count bytes on (ADD ESI,ECX after the LODSB), BX -= count.
  11 skip:    no bytes follow, count transparent columns -- ESI ends one byte on, BX -= count.
That is the op table resource_info/cel.md records for this encoding, under the names fill / stretch / literal / skip.
After each op the loop continues while BX is non-zero, so it stops when the width counter lands on exactly zero, with ESI then on the first control byte of the next row. The four NOP runs are branch-target padding, not code.

Both call sites drive it the same way: fdps_rle_blit_scaled (00056d99) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (000574d1) restore ESI to the start of the row they have just blitted and then call this routine once per source row that the vertical Bresenham accumulator, compared against the source height word at 0x00070022 and stepped by the destination height at 0x0007002a, says to consume.

What the stream is: the pixel payload of a .CEL sprite or of a .SAF tilemap tile. fdps_cel_blit_sprite computes sheet + *(i32 *)(sheet + index * 4 + 0x0f) and passes it to fdps_blit_dispatch as the source argument that becomes ESI, and fdps_draw_tilemap_cell hands a tile's stream to the same dispatcher; the encoding is the same in both cases.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register contract: ESI is the pointer to the first control byte of an encoded row, and the row width in pixels is read from the word at 0x00070024, which the caller's blit parameter block already holds.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the side effect: ESI is left just past the encoded row. BX and CL are destroyed. The literal case adds all of ECX to ESI while only CL is ever loaded, and what makes that safe is upstream: fdps_blit_dispatch does XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d before every one of its thirteen mode calls, and neither blitter ever writes above CL -- the one 16-bit write in each, SHL CX,1 at 00056cf2 and 000572f9, doubles a value of at most 0x40 and so never carries into CH.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in any library; shares the game's blit parameter globals at 0x00070022/0x00070024 with its two callers, and no runtime or Miles AIL routine takes a program global as an implicit argument]

Rebuild note:
Register contract rather than a stack one: ESI is both the argument and the result, and BX and CL are destroyed. Emitted as unsigned char *fdps_rle_skip_row(unsigned char *rle_stream), the register that carries information both ways becoming the parameter and the return value; the register destruction is a property of the contract and not of what the routine does, so it does not carry over (ADR-0001). Both callers already treat ESI that way, restoring the row start with POP ESI at 00056d84 and 000574bc and never reloading it between calls.

Second, the loop ends only when the 16-bit counter reaches exactly zero; writing the obvious while (width > 0) changes behaviour on a row whose runs overshoot its width, where the original wraps BX and keeps decoding. resource_info/cel.md records the same wrap on the drawing side, where it walks off the end of the destination instead.

Third, if this is ever rewritten in C, the literal case must add a count narrowed to 8 bits. The original adds the whole of ECX while only ever loading CL, relying on fdps_blit_dispatch's XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d having cleared the rest once at the top of the whole blit; a rewrite that reaches this routine by any other path, or that keeps a wider count variable live across rows, loses that guarantee silently and corrupts the source pointer.

=== 00056e2a [PLATE]
Blit mode 5: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface rotated (and uniformly shrunk), by walking the destination along two perpendicular fixed-point vectors built from the single (dx, dy) pair the dispatcher's sixth argument carries.

Algorithm:
Setup. Clears the two row-to-row fractional accumulators at 0x00070048 and 0x0007004a, reads dx from the word at [EBP+0x1c] and dy from the word at [EBP+0x1e] -- the low and high halves of fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument, still live in the dispatcher's frame -- and loads the destination pitch from the word at 0x0007002e into EBP. It then branches on the signs of dx and dy into four arms that write the same four quantities with the signs of that quadrant folded in, and store the absolute values of dx and dy at 0x0007004c and 0x0007004e:
  0x00070034 = sign(dx)          -- x step taken while walking along a source row
  0x00070038 = -sign(dy) * pitch -- y step taken while walking along a source row
  0x0007003c = sign(dy)          -- x step taken when moving to the next source row
  0x00070040 = sign(dx) * pitch  -- y step taken when moving to the next source row
So one source pixel advances the destination by (dx, -dy) / 0x1000 and one source row advances it by (dy, dx) / 0x1000. Those two vectors are perpendicular and of equal length, which is what makes this a rotation: with dx = k*cos and dy = k*sin, k = 0x1000 is unit scale and a shorter k shrinks the image. The four sign arms are the four quadrants of that vector, not four mirroring modes.

Row loop, entered at 0x00056f19. Each pass reloads BX from the sprite width at 0x00070024 (the source columns still to be consumed on this row), zeroes the two within-row accumulators DX and BP, and pushes EDI so the row's origin can be restored at the end.

Within a row it LODSBs one control byte from ESI and dispatches on its top two bits, the run length in every case being count = (control & 0x3f) + 1, obtained as two SHL CL,1 that test the flag bits followed by SHR CL,2 and INC CL. These are the four ops of the CEL pixel encoding, decoded exactly as fdps_blit_rle_passthrough decodes them:
  00 fill:    one pixel byte follows and is stored count times; BX -= count.
  01 stretch: one pixel byte follows and covers 2*count columns, an AH flag toggled each step suppressing the store on the first column of every pair so only the second is painted; BX -= 2*count.
  10 literal: count pixel bytes follow, one LODSBed and stored per step; BX -= count.
  11 skip:    no bytes follow and nothing is stored, the destination merely advances count steps; BX -= count.
Every step of every op advances the destination the same way: DX += |dx| and, if DX reaches 0x1000, DX -= 0x1000 and EDI += the x step at 0x00070034; then BP += |dy| and, if BP reaches 0x1000, BP -= 0x1000, the pixel is stored a second time at the current EDI, and EDI += the y step at 0x00070038. That second store is the gap filler: on a diagonal step it paints both the horizontal and the vertical neighbour so the rotated run stays connected. A single 0x1000 is subtracted per step, not a modulo, so an accumulator increment larger than 0x1000 still advances at most one destination pixel -- the routine can shrink but never magnify.
A row ends when BX reaches exactly zero.

Row advance, at 0x000570a8. EDI is popped back to the row origin, then 0x00070048 += |dy| stepping EDI by 0x0007003c on carry, and 0x0007004a += |dx| stepping EDI by 0x00070040 on carry -- the perpendicular vector, accumulated across the whole blit rather than reset per row. The row counter, the word at 0x00070022, is then decremented and the routine returns once it reaches zero.
The MOV DX,[0x00070026] at 0x000570a9 is dead: DX is reloaded from 0x00070048 at 0x000570b0 before any use. 0x00070026 is written only by the scaling kernel FUN_00056c5e. The four-NOP runs after conditional jumps and the three-byte fillers after unconditional ones are assembler padding, not code.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register-and-frame contract established by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI is the encoded pixel stream, EDI is the destination pixel the source's top-left corner maps to, EBP still points at the dispatcher's frame so that dx = word [EBP+0x1c] and dy = word [EBP+0x1e] can be read out of its sixth argument, and ECX must have its upper 16 bits clear because only CL is ever loaded while LOOP consumes all of ECX. The geometry comes from the blit parameter words the dispatcher has just published: sprite width at 0x00070024, row count at 0x00070022, destination pitch at 0x0007002e. Unlike fdps_blit_rle_passthrough it ignores the EDX = pitch - width end-of-row advance, because it restores EDI to the row origin itself.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the drawn, rotated image. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI, EDI and EBP are all destroyed, the row counter at 0x00070022 is left at zero, and the eight blit parameter words at 0x00070034-0x0007004e are left holding this call's step vectors.

Reachability: no code path in FDPS.LE selects mode 5. Every operand that can reach the mode byte at fdps_blit_dispatch's [EBP+0x20] was enumerated -- the 46 direct call sites pass the literals 0, 8, 9 and 0xb or forward a wrapper's own argument; fdps_cel_blit_sprite's mode argument (its eighth, not its seventh) is a literal 0 at 50 sites and a literal 4 at four; fdps_blit_unit_sprite is given 0 or 3; fdps_draw_scene_layer passes 9 or 0xa; and the draw request that fdps_draw_tilemap_cell forwards carries 0, 3 or 9 in its +0x20 field, with no store of 5 into any +0x20 field anywhere in the image. The kernel is compiled in and called from the dispatcher's mode-5 arm, but that arm is not taken in the shipped game.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the Miles AIL set and the body hash is unique in the image; it shares the game's blit parameter block at 0x00070022-0x0007004e with fdps_blit_dispatch, its only caller, and 737 bytes of sprite decode logic is neither a runtime primitive nor a linker artifact]

Rebuild note:
Three things a faithful rewrite has to keep. First, each accumulator subtracts a single 0x1000 on carry rather than taking a modulo, so an increment larger than 0x1000 still advances at most one destination pixel per step: the obvious 'pos += dx; dst += pos >> 12; pos &= 0xfff' magnifies where the original clamps, and the mode silently becomes a different transform. Second, the vertical carry stores the pixel a second time at the current EDI before stepping (00056f79, 00056fe1, 00057043); dropping that as a redundant write leaves one-pixel holes along every diagonal run. Third, the two row-to-row accumulators at 0x00070048/0x0007004a are cleared once at entry and deliberately carry across rows, unlike the within-row DX/BP pair which is zeroed at the top of every row -- resetting them per row turns the rotation into a shear. As with its sibling kernels it also cannot be given a real C signature: it takes its inputs in ESI, EDI and the caller's own EBP frame, requires the upper 16 bits of ECX to be clear (fdps_blit_dispatch's XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d supplies that), destroys EBX, ESI, EDI and EBP, and ends its row loop only when BX reaches exactly zero, so a stream whose ops overrun the width wraps the counter and keeps writing. One more thing the re-read adds: no call site in the image selects mode 5, so a rewrite of this kernel cannot be validated by playing the game -- the three rules above have to be transcribed from the assembly and taken on the assembly's authority, and the dispatcher's mode-5 arm has to keep calling it even though nothing exercises that arm.

=== 00056eb5 [EOL]
3 bytes of 0x90 NOP filler, no references

=== 00056ee7 [EOL]

=== 00057058 [EOL]
3-byte NOP filler inside FUN_00056e2a, after JMP at 00057056, before code resuming at 0005705b

=== 00057114 [PLATE]
Blit mode 6: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface both resampled to a caller-chosen destination width and height and rotated, the geometry arriving in a four-int record that fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument points at.

Algorithm:
Setup. EBP still points at fdps_blit_dispatch's frame, so MOV EBP,[EBP+0x1c] replaces it with the parameter record pointer and the four fields are read out before EBP is destroyed: the word at record+0 becomes the destination width at 0x00070028, the word at record+4 the destination height at 0x0007002a, and the words at record+8 and record+0xc become the rotation vector (dx, dy) held in DX and AX. The two row-to-row fractional accumulators at 0x00070048 and 0x0007004a are cleared, and the destination pitch is loaded from the word at 0x0007002e into EBP.
It then branches on the signs of dx and dy into four arms (00057162, 0005718f, 000571c3, 000571eb) that write the same four step quantities with that quadrant's signs folded in, and store |dx| at 0x0007004c and |dy| at 0x0007004e as the fractional increments:
  0x00070034 = sign(dx)          -- x step taken between two destination pixels of a row
  0x00070038 = -sign(dy) * pitch -- y step taken between two destination pixels of a row
  0x0007003c = sign(dy)          -- x step taken when moving to the next destination row
  0x00070040 = sign(dx) * pitch  -- y step taken when moving to the next destination row
So one destination pixel advances by (dx, -dy) / 0x1000 and one destination row advances by (dy, dx) / 0x1000. Those two vectors are perpendicular and of equal length, which makes the walk a rotation with a uniform scale on top of the resampling the row and column counters already do. This is the same vector construction fdps_rle_blit_rotated (mode 5) uses; what mode 6 adds is that the rectangle being walked is destination-sized rather than source-sized.
The row counter at 0x0007002c and the vertical resampling accumulator at 0x00070026 are both seeded with the destination height.

Row loop, entered at 0005722f. Each pass reloads BX from the destination width at 0x00070028 -- the number of destination pixels still to be emitted on this row -- copies it into BP as the horizontal resampling accumulator, zeroes the two within-row fractional accumulators at 0x00070044 and 0x00070046, and pushes ESI and EDI so the row's stream position and origin can be restored at the end.

Within a row it LODSBs one control byte from ESI and dispatches on its top two bits, the run length in every case being count = (control & 0x3f) + 1, obtained as SHL CL,1 twice to test the flag bits followed by SHR CL,2 and INC CL. These are the four ops of the CEL pixel encoding, the same four fdps_blit_rle_passthrough decodes:
  00 fill    (0005726a): one pixel byte follows in the stream and is the value for all count source columns.
  01 stretch (000572f4): one pixel byte follows and covers 2*count source columns, an AH flag toggled on every source column consumed suppressing the store on the first column of each pair so only the second is painted.
  10 literal (000573a5): count pixel bytes follow; the current one is read with MOV AL,[ESI] when a pixel is emitted and ESI is advanced with INC ESI when a source column is consumed.
  11 skip    (00057438): no bytes follow and nothing is stored; the destination merely advances over count source columns' worth of destination pixels.
Every op runs the same two interleaved counters. BP holds the horizontal resampling accumulator: while BP is below the source width at 0x00070024 the run's next source column is consumed (BP += destination width, CL decremented, and the run ends into the next control byte when CL reaches zero); once BP reaches the source width, BP -= source width and one destination pixel is emitted, decrementing BX. So count source columns are stretched or squeezed into however many destination pixels the width ratio calls for.
Each emitted destination pixel then walks the destination: 0x00070044 += |dx| and, on reaching 0x1000, 0x00070044 -= 0x1000 and EDI += the x step at 0x00070034; then 0x00070046 += |dy| and, on reaching 0x1000, 0x00070046 -= 0x1000, the pixel is stored a second time at the current EDI, and EDI += the y step at 0x00070038. That second store is the diagonal gap filler; in the stretch op it is suppressed on the same AH parity as the main store, and in the skip op it is absent along with the main store.
A row ends when BX reaches exactly zero.

Row advance, at 000574bb. EDI is popped back to the row origin and ESI back to the start of the source row just drawn. The vertical resampling accumulator at 0x00070026 then advances: while it is still at or below the source height at 0x00070022 the routine calls fdps_rle_skip_row to step ESI over one whole encoded source row and adds the destination height, and when it passes the source height it subtracts the source height and is stored back. A destination taller than the source therefore skips no rows and redraws the same source row; a shorter one drops rows.
EDI is then moved to the next destination row by the perpendicular vector: 0x00070048 += |dy| stepping EDI by 0x0007003c on carry, and 0x0007004a += |dx| stepping EDI by 0x00070040 on carry. Unlike the within-row pair these two are cleared once at entry and deliberately carry across rows.
The row counter at 0x0007002c is decremented and the routine returns once it reaches zero. The four-NOP runs after conditional jumps and the two three-byte fillers at 000571b6 and 000571e8 after unconditional ones are assembler padding, not code.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register-and-frame contract established by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI is the encoded pixel stream, EDI is the destination pixel the source's top-left corner maps to, EBP still points at the dispatcher's frame so that [EBP+0x1c] yields the parameter record pointer, and ECX must have its upper 16 bits clear because only CL is ever loaded; the dispatcher's XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d supplies that. The record is four 32-bit slots of which only the low words are read: +0 destination width in pixels, +4 destination height in rows, +8 dx and +0xc dy, the rotation vector in 1/0x1000 units. The rest of the geometry comes from the blit parameter words the dispatcher has just published: source width at 0x00070024, source height at 0x00070022, destination pitch at 0x0007002e. Like the other transforming kernels it ignores the EDX = pitch - width end-of-row advance, because it restores EDI to the row origin itself.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the drawn, resampled and rotated image. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, EBP, ESI and EDI are all destroyed, the row counter at 0x0007002c is left at zero, and the blit parameter words at 0x00070026-0x0007004e are left holding this call's destination size, step vectors and accumulator residues.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the Miles AIL library set and the body hash is unique in the image; it shares the game's blit parameter block at 0x00070022-0x0007004e with fdps_blit_dispatch, its only caller, and 1079 bytes of sprite decode logic is neither a runtime primitive nor a linker artifact]

Rebuild note:
Four things a faithful rewrite has to keep. First, the two fixed-point accumulators subtract a single 0x1000 on carry rather than taking a modulo, so an increment larger than 0x1000 still advances at most one destination pixel: the obvious 'pos += dx; dst += pos >> 12; pos &= 0xfff' magnifies where the original clamps. Second, the vertical carry stores the pixel a second time at the current EDI before stepping (000572dc, 00057381, 0005741c); dropping that as a redundant write leaves one-pixel holes along every diagonal run. Third, the row-to-row accumulators at 0x00070048/0x0007004a are cleared once at entry and deliberately carry across rows, unlike the within-row pair at 0x00070044/0x00070046 which is zeroed at the top of every row -- resetting them per row turns the rotation into a shear. Fourth, the horizontal loop is bounded only by the destination pixel count BX and the vertical loop only by the row counter at 0x0007002c, and the source row's own ops are never counted out: the decoder deliberately under-consumes the stream and relies on POP ESI plus fdps_rle_skip_row to find the next row, so a rewrite that advances one shared source pointer through the decode loop desynchronises the stream. A destination width or height of zero means 65536 iterations, not none. The register-and-frame contract itself is real -- the inputs arrive in ESI, EDI and the caller's own EBP frame, the upper 16 bits of ECX must be clear, and EBX, EBP, ESI and EDI are destroyed -- but it does not force the routine to stay in the assembly module with its dispatcher: src/rlerot.c re-expresses it as three ordinary stack parameters, rle_stream being the dispatcher's argument 1 (loaded into ESI at 000568e1), dest_pixel its argument 2 (loaded into EDI at 000568e4), and blit_geometry the argument 6 pointer read from [EBP+0x1c]. The ECX precondition and the destruction of EBX, EBP, ESI and EDI are register allocation rather than observable behaviour (ADR-0001).

=== 000571b6 [EOL]

=== 00057551 [PLATE]
Blit mode 7: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface mirrored left to right, so art drawn facing one way can be shown facing the other. The other axis is mode 8, fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_vertical.

Algorithm:
Reads the destination pitch once from the word at 0x0007002e into EDX, then runs one pass per destination row. Each pass reloads the sprite width in pixels from the word at 0x00070024 into BX -- the number of destination columns still to be covered on this row -- saves the row's left edge with PUSH EDI, and moves EDI forward by width-1 to the row's right-hand column, from which the whole row is decoded leftwards.

Inside a row it LODSBs one control byte from ESI and dispatches on its top two bits, the length in every case being count = (control & 0x3f) + 1, obtained as two SHL CL,1 that test the flag bits followed by SHR CL,2 and INC CL:
  00 fill:    one pixel byte follows; STD then REP STOSB writes it into count columns walking left, then CLD; BX -= count.
  01 stretch: one pixel byte follows; a DEC EDI / store / DEC EDI loop writes it into every other column across 2*count columns, leaving the columns it steps over untouched; BX -= count twice.
  10 literal: count pixel bytes follow, each LODSBed and stored with EDI walking left; BX -= count.
  11 skip:    no bytes follow; SUB EDI,ECX leaves count columns transparent; BX -= count.
These are the four ops of the CEL pixel encoding, and they consume the stream identically to the mode-0 kernel at 0x00056a0d; only the starting column and the direction of travel differ, so the output is the exact left-right reflection of that kernel's output within the same width-by-height destination rectangle.

A row ends when BX reaches exactly zero. EDI is then restored to the saved left edge and advanced by one full pitch, and the row counter -- the word at 0x00070022 -- is decremented; the routine returns once that reaches zero. The three four-NOP runs after the conditional jumps and the three-byte fillers after the unconditional ones are assembler padding, not code.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register contract established by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI is the encoded pixel stream, EDI is the top-left corner of the destination rectangle, and the geometry comes from the blit parameter words the dispatcher has just published -- sprite width at 0x00070024, row count at 0x00070022, destination pitch at 0x0007002e. Unlike most of its sibling kernels it reads nothing out of the dispatcher's frame, and it ignores the EDX = pitch - width end-of-row advance the dispatcher leaves in EDX, reloading the full pitch instead because it restores EDI to the row origin itself.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the drawn rectangle. EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are destroyed, and the row counter at 0x00070022 is left at zero. ECX must have its upper 24 bits clear on entry, since the skip op subtracts all of ECX from EDI while only CL is ever loaded; the dispatcher's XOR ECX,ECX at 0005690d supplies that.

Pool: fdps  [shares the game's blit parameter globals at 0x00070022/0x00070024/0x0007002e with fdps_blit_dispatch, which is its only caller; no Function ID hit in either the Watcom or the Miles AIL set, no runtime idiom, no interrupt or driver structure, and 147 bytes of real decode logic rather than a linker artifact]

Rebuild note:
The mirror is about the sprite's own box, not about EDI. EDI arrives pointing at the top-left corner exactly as it does for the mode-0 kernel, and this routine adds width-1 to it itself, so the mirrored image lands in the same destination rectangle; writing the obvious 'start at dst and walk backwards' draws it one whole width to the left. Two more things a faithful rewrite must keep: it deliberately ignores the EDX = pitch - width that the dispatcher hands every kernel and re-reads the full pitch from 0x0007002e, because it restores EDI to the row origin with PUSH/POP instead of letting it run off the row end, so reusing the siblings' end-of-row advance double-counts the width; and both loops are exit-tested, the row on BX becoming exactly zero and the pass count on a pre-decrement of 0x00070022, so a row whose ops overrun the width wraps BX and keeps writing past the row end, and a height of zero means 65536 rows rather than none. The stretch op is the one place where the reflection is not a simple index flip: mode 0 does INC EDI and then STOSB, painting the odd columns of its 2*count run, while this does DEC EDI and then the store, painting the columns that are the reflections of those, so a rewrite that mirrors mode 0's loop body without moving the decrement ahead of the store paints the complementary set of columns and the sprite comes out one pixel off. The routine's inputs arrive in ESI and EDI plus three globals and it destroys EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI along with the row-count global, so its register contract is not expressible as a C prototype; the rebuild replaces that contract with two ordinary parameters under ADR-0001, as fdps_rle_blit_passthrough at 00056a0d does.
