=== 000575ed [PLATE]
Blit mode 8: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream vertically mirrored, by aiming the destination pointer at the bottom row of the target rectangle and handing the decoding itself to fdps_rle_blit_passthrough with an upward row step.

Algorithm:
Reads the three blit geometry words that fdps_blit_dispatch has just published: the destination pitch at 0x0007002e, the sprite width in pixels at 0x00070024 and the row count at 0x00070022. It zero-extends the pitch into EAX and the row count into EDX, decrements the row count with DEC DX, and multiplies them, so EAX = pitch * (rows - 1); adding that to EDI moves the destination pointer from the top-left corner of the rectangle to the left edge of its last row. It then builds its own end-of-row advance in EDX as -(pitch + width): the two words are added as 16 bits into a zeroed EDX and the sum is negated as 32 bits. Finally it tail-jumps to fdps_rle_blit_passthrough at 0x00056a0d.

That kernel is mode 0, the unmodified pass-through blit, and it decodes each row left to right, so EDI has already advanced by one full width by the time the kernel adds EDX at the end of a row (0x00056a81). Adding -(pitch + width) therefore lands EDI one pitch higher than the row started, and the kernel climbs the rectangle row by row -- its DEC word [0x00070022] / JNZ 0x00056a0d at 0x00056a83 re-enters at the very top, reloading the per-row pixel budget from 0x00070024 -- while consuming the source stream in its normal forward order. The result is the exact top-to-bottom reflection of mode 0's output inside the same width-by-height destination rectangle: the vertical counterpart of the left-to-right reflection fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_horizontal performs for mode 7.

Nothing after the JMP belongs to this routine: the plain RET at 0x00056a8c that ends fdps_rle_blit_passthrough returns straight to the call site in fdps_blit_dispatch.

What mode 8 is for:
Exactly two call sites in the whole program select it, both inside fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input (the CALL at 0x0001732e and the CALL at 0x00017369), and both pass a 24x24 sprite, a pitch of 0x140 and the unit's front-facing walk-cycle frame. They are the opening phases of that window's randomly armed idle animation: frames 0..14 stamp the sprite upside down at column 161 on the row given by the 15-entry drop-and-bounce table the function copies from 0x14818, and frames 15..24 hold it upside down at the resting position (destination offset 0xd521 = row 170, column 161). From frame 25 the animation switches back to mode 0 and the character is the right way up again. So the vertical mirror in this game draws a unit head-down, and that is its only use.
No other path reaches mode 8: every other call site of fdps_blit_dispatch passes a literal 0, 4, 9 or 0xb, the three that compute the mode at run time yield 9 or 0xa (fdps_draw_scene_layer at 0x0002c603), 0 or 3 (fdps_blit_unit_sprite, whose three callers pass 3, 3 and 0-or-3) and the caller's own value (fdps_cel_blit_sprite forwards [EBP+0x30] unchanged, and every one of its call sites passes a literal 0 or 4), and nothing references the dispatcher's entry other than by CALL.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. This is hand-written assembly carrying the blit family's register contract, set up by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch (CALL at 0x000569b2, reached when the mode byte at [EBP+0x20] equals 8): ESI is the encoded pixel stream, EDI is the top-left corner of the destination rectangle, and the geometry arrives in the three globals above. It discards the EDX = pitch - width end-of-row advance the dispatcher leaves in EDX for its sibling kernels and substitutes the negative step described above.

Returns:
  nothing; the result is the drawn rectangle. It destroys EAX, EDX and EDI itself, and inherits everything fdps_rle_blit_passthrough destroys -- EBX, ECX, ESI, EDI, and the row count at 0x00070022, which is left at zero.

Pool: fdps  [shares the game's blit geometry globals at 0x00070022/0x00070024/0x0007002e with fdps_blit_dispatch, its only caller, as one of that dispatcher's thirteen mode kernels; no Function ID hit against the Watcom libraries or against ailv3.lib and the body hash is unique in the image, and it performs real raster arithmetic on program globals rather than merely redirecting control, so not binary_artifact]

Rebuild note:
The upward row step is -(pitch + width), not -pitch. fdps_rle_blit_passthrough adds it only after EDI has already walked one whole width across the row, so a rewrite that does the intuitive thing and steps the destination back by one pitch per row staggers the image one width further left on every row. The starting displacement is likewise pitch * (rows - 1) and not pitch * rows: the mirrored image has to occupy the very same rectangle an unmirrored blit of the same sprite would, and the off-by-one puts it a row too low. Both counts are 16-bit -- DEC DX on the row count means a row count of zero displaces the destination by 65535 pitches and then draws 65536 rows from there, far outside the surface, rather than drawing nothing. Getting any of that wrong will most likely survive playtesting: mode 8 is selected from exactly two call sites, both in fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input's idle animation, which arms itself only when a rand draw comes out a multiple of 200, so the only picture this kernel ever draws is a rarely seen easter egg. It has to be checked deliberately, not waited for.

=== 0005761b [PLATE]
Blit mode 9: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream translucently, blending every pixel it draws with the destination pixel underneath it at a caller-chosen 16-step level and resolving the blended colour back to a palette index.

Algorithm:
Entered by a plain CALL from fdps_blit_dispatch with that function's registers and stack frame still live: ESI = the RLE command stream, EDI = the first destination pixel, EDX = pitch - width (the end-of-row advance), EBP = the dispatcher's own frame pointer. EDX is parked in the scratch global at 0x00070030 straight away because the blend needs the register back, then the dispatcher's sixth argument [EBP+0x1c] is read as a pointer to a three-dword blend descriptor:
  +0x00  base of the shade-ramp table that fdps_build_palette_tables fills at 0x000653f0 -- 18 rows of 256 dwords, row k holding every palette colour packed as red in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11, blue in bits 0-3 and multiplied by the coefficient at 0x0002ae40[k], which is k for rows 0-8 and 16-(k-9) for rows 9-17.
  +0x04  blend level, 0 = opaque source through 16 = source invisible.
  +0x08  base of the 16x16x16 inverse colour cube at 0x000643f0, one palette index per 4-bit rgb triple.
From the level it picks the pair of ramp rows whose coefficients sum to 16, so the source always carries weight (16 - level)/16 and the destination level/16: at level <= 8 source pixels are looked up in row level+9 and destination pixels in row level; above 8 the same two weights are only available the other way round, so source reads row 16-level and destination row 25-level. Both row pointers, the cube base and the two constants 0x000f0f0f and 0x0000ffff are cached in the dispatcher's argument slots [EBP+0x08] through [EBP+0x18], which this kernel uses as its scratch area for the rest of the call.

Each row reloads the row width from the word at 0x00070024 into BX and decodes command bytes from ESI until BX is exactly zero. A command byte's low six bits give len = (cmd & 0x3f) + 1, i.e. 1..64, and its top two bits select the op:
  00 blended fill -- one pixel byte follows; its ramp value is held in EDX and blended into len consecutive destination pixels; BX -= len.
  01 stretched blended fill -- one pixel byte follows; blended into every other destination pixel starting at dst+1, across a 2*len span whose in-between pixels are left as they were; BX -= 2*len.
  10 blended literal -- len pixel bytes follow, each blended with the destination pixel under it; BX -= len.
  11 skip -- no bytes follow; EDI advances by len with nothing written, i.e. transparency; BX -= len.
All three drawing ops share the same blend: sum = src_row[src_pixel] + dst_row[dst_pixel], then (sum >> 4) & 0x000f0f0f, which cannot carry between the three channel bytes precisely because the two coefficients sum to 16 and no channel can exceed 15*16; the 12-bit cube index is then formed as (v >> 12) | (v & 0x0000ffff), putting green in bits 8-11, red in bits 4-7 and blue in bits 0-3, and the byte written out is cube[index].

At the end of a row EDI advances by the end-of-row value saved at 0x00070030, the 16-bit row counter at 0x00070022 is decremented in place, and the routine returns once that counter reaches zero, leaving the global at 0.

The level is a real per-call fade parameter rather than a fixed effect: the mode 9 call sites that build the descriptor in view pass 8 and 12 (0x00032209, 0x0003228b) and 10 (0x000332e6, 0x000339d3), and three more compute it -- fdps_draw_composite_sprite sets it to 16 minus the word at +7 of a sprite-part record (0x0001424e), so that record field is the source's own opacity and this level is its complement.

Where the three kernels that follow it stand: 0x00057793 (fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop, mode 10) and 0x00057916 (fdps_rle_blit_tint, mode 11) open with the same descriptor decode and end in the same masked add and cube lookup, but they take a fourth dword at +0x0c, fetch it once through the ramp row as a constant palette colour, and blend each source pixel against that constant instead of against the destination -- their level weights the constant colour, and mode 11 never reads [EDI] at all. Only 0x00057a74 (fdps_rle_blit_blend_color_range, mode 12) blends against the destination the way this one does, and it does so only for source pixels inside the colour band its descriptor carries at +0x0c/+0x10, storing the rest verbatim. So this kernel is the one that makes a whole sprite see-through.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. Hand-written assembly with a register contract set up by its sole caller fdps_blit_dispatch: ESI is the RLE pixel stream, EDI the top-left destination pixel, EDX the end-of-row advance pitch - width, EBP the dispatcher's live frame, out of which [EBP+0x1c] supplies the blend descriptor pointer; the rectangle geometry comes from the words the dispatcher has just published, width at 0x00070024 and row count at 0x00070022.

Returns:
  nothing. The result is the blended rectangle. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are destroyed, the caller's argument slots [EBP+0x08]..[EBP+0x1c] are overwritten with scratch, the row counter at 0x00070022 is left at zero and 0x00070030 holds the end-of-row advance. Unlike the mode 0 kernel it does not rely on the caller for a clean ECX: it zeroes ECX itself at 00057667.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; shares the graphics state block at 0x00070022/0x00070024/0x00070030 with fdps_blit_dispatch, its only caller, and blends through the game's own palette tables at 0x000653f0 and 0x000643f0 -- work no C runtime, maths library or audio driver ships]

Rebuild note:
The 12-bit index into the inverse colour cube at 0x000643f0 is built as (v >> 12) | (v & 0xffff) from a value carrying red in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11 and blue in bits 0-3, which lands green in bits 8-11, red in bits 4-7 and blue in bits 0-3: the cube is green-major, then red, then blue, so the obvious cube[(r << 8) | (g << 4) | b] returns a wrong colour for every pixel that is not grey. The level > 8 branch is not a second blend rule either -- it is the same two weights fetched from the other half of the ramp table, because rows 0-8 and 9-17 only carry the coefficients 0..8 and 16..8 -- so writing it as a special case, or picking any two rows whose coefficients do not sum to 16, breaks the masked add: a channel byte then exceeds 255 and carries into the next channel. The level's polarity is the third trap: 0 draws the source opaque and 16 makes it invisible, the opposite of the opacity the callers hold -- fdps_draw_composite_sprite stores 16 - opacity at 0x0001424e -- so passing an opacity straight through inverts every fade. Two family traps also apply here: the stretched op writes its first pixel at dst+1 and steps by 2, so for (i = 0; i < len; i++) dst[2*i] = px shifts the run one column left, and both loop terminators test for exactly zero (OR BX,BX after the subtraction, and a DEC of the word at 0x00070022), so a stream whose runs overrun the row width wraps BX and keeps painting, and a height of zero draws 65536 rows instead of none.

=== 0005771a [EOL]
3-byte NOP filler inside the address span of FUN_0005761b

=== 00057769 [EOL]
3-byte 90 90 90 alignment padding gap inside the 0005761b function range

=== 00057793 [PLATE]
Blit mode 0x0a of fdps_blit_dispatch: draws one RLE 4-op sprite stream with every pixel it writes alpha-blended toward a single constant palette colour, and blends that same colour into the destination pixels showing through the sprite's transparent runs, so the whole width x height rectangle comes out tinted.

Selected by fdps_draw_scene_layer at 0002c5ee: when a scene layer's mode byte is 1 and a map tile's movement-grid cell is marked (byte 1 of the cell is not 0xff) and bit 0x80 of the tile's attribute flag is clear, that layer draws the tile through mode 0x0a rather than mode 9. Layer mode 1 is what every shipped DSC%02d.DAT in Field2.vfs gives its first layer, so this kernel is the ordinary way the battle map paints its movement/target range highlight: each marked tile is redrawn tinted toward DAT_00060154, at the blend level ramp[DAT_0006015c / 4] that pulses between 2 and 7 out of 16, and because the 0b11 op tints instead of skipping, the tint covers the whole 24x24 tile rather than only its opaque pixels.

Algorithm:
Entered by a plain CALL from fdps_blit_dispatch with that function's registers and frame still live: ESI = the RLE command byte stream, EDI = the first destination pixel of the first row in an 8bpp linear surface, EDX = pitch - width, EAX and ECX zeroed, and EBP still the dispatcher's frame pointer. EDX is spilled to DAT_00070030 at once because the body needs EDX as scratch; the end of every row adds it back to EDI from there.
[EBP+0x1c], the dispatcher's sixth argument, is a pointer to a four-dword blend descriptor: +0 blend_table, +4 alpha, +8 rgb444_lut, +0xc tint_color. blend_table is an [18][256] array of dwords holding every palette entry pre-scaled by a weight with one colour channel per byte -- the same table fdps_blit_tint_rect takes under that name, of the kind fdps_build_palette_tables builds at 000653f0. Rows 0..8 hold weights 0..8 at 0x400 bytes per row; rows 9..17 hold the complementary weights and begin 0x2400 further on. alpha is folded into 0..8 exactly as fdps_blit_tint_rect folds it: for alpha <= 8 the tint reads row alpha and the source pixels read row 9+alpha, and for alpha > 8 alpha is replaced by 16-alpha and the two rows swap, so either way the tint ends up weighted by the caller's alpha and the pixel by 16-alpha. The two row addresses are parked in [EBP+0xc] and [EBP+0x10], the masks 0x0f0f0f and 0xffff in [EBP+0x14] and [EBP+0x18], and blend_table[tint row][tint_color] is fetched once, before any drawing, into [EBP+0x1c]. Those six slots are the dispatcher's own incoming arguments, which the kernel destroys.
Every pixel is blended by the same sequence: read the scaled source colour blend_table[pixel row][pixel], add the scaled tint, shift right by 4 to divide out the /16 of the weights, mask with 0x0f0f0f to leave four bits per channel at bits 0..3, 8..11 and 16..19, fold those into a 12-bit index with (v & 0xffff) | (v >> 12), and read the palette byte at rgb444_lut[index]. That byte is what gets stored to EDI.
Each row loads BX with the row width from DAT_00070024 and decodes command bytes until BX is exactly zero. A command byte's low six bits give len = (byte & 0x3f) + 1, in 1..64, and its top two bits select the op:
  0b00 RLE fill -- read one stream byte, write its blended colour to len pixels with REP STOSB; BX -= len.
  0b01 stretched fill -- read one stream byte, write its blended colour to len pixels spaced two apart with the first landing at EDI+1, leaving the pixels in between untouched; BX -= 2*len.
  0b10 literal copy -- for each of len stream bytes write its blended colour; BX -= len.
  0b11 backdrop tint -- consume no stream byte; for len pixels read the pixel already at EDI, blend the tint into it and write it back; BX -= len. This is the op that fdps_blit_rle_passthrough, fdps_rle_blit_with_palette_remap and the kernel at 0x00057916 implement instead as a transparent skip (ADD EDI,ECX).
ECX carries every run length for REP and LOOP only because the dispatcher zeroed it, and the pixel byte indexes the tables cleanly only because EAX is re-zeroed before each load. When BX reaches zero the row ends: EDI += DAT_00070030, the remaining-row counter DAT_00070022 is decremented, and the outer loop reloads BX from DAT_00070024 for the next row. The routine returns when DAT_00070022 reaches zero.

Parameters:
  none on the stack -- the inputs arrive in registers and globals prepared by fdps_blit_dispatch:
  ESI -- base of the RLE command byte stream, pointing past the caller's header.
  EDI -- destination address of the first pixel of the first row, in an 8bpp linear surface.
  EDX -- pitch - width, saved to DAT_00070030 and added to EDI at the end of every row.
  EBP -- the dispatcher's frame pointer; [EBP+0x1c] is its sixth argument, the pointer to the blend descriptor described above, and [EBP+8..0x1c] are then reused as scratch.
  DAT_00070024 -- row width in pixels, reloaded once per row.
  DAT_00070022 -- number of rows still to draw, decremented once per row.

Returns:
  nothing. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are all left modified, DAT_00070030 is overwritten, and the caller's argument slots [EBP+8] through [EBP+0x1c] are destroyed; fdps_blit_dispatch survives that because it reads none of them after the call and unwinds through POPs.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; the only caller is fdps_blit_dispatch, and DAT_00070022/DAT_00070024/DAT_00070030 are that dispatcher's blit parameter block, not library state]

Rebuild note:
The 0b11 op here is not the transparent skip it is in the rest of the family: it reads each destination pixel back and blends the tint into it, so the backdrop inside the sprite's bounding box is tinted as well as the sprite. Writing the family's obvious 'advance past transparent runs' body leaves an untinted hole in the shape of the sprite's transparency. In the same vein the 0b01 stretched fill writes its first pixel at EDI+1 rather than EDI while consuming 2*len columns of row width, so a straightforward for (i = 0; i < len; i++) dst[i*2] = c is off by one pixel. The consequence is visible, not theoretical: this kernel is the battle map's movement-range highlight, so a transparent-skip body would leave the highlight tinting only the opaque pixels of each map tile and not the tile as a whole.

=== 00057883 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP filler inside the address range of FUN_00057793

=== 000578c7 [EOL]
3-byte NOP filler (90 90 90) in a gap inside FUN_00057793's address span; no refs, no code reaches it.

=== 00057916 [PLATE]
Blit mode 11: decodes an RLE 4-op sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface, alpha-blending every pixel it draws with one constant palette colour and leaving the transparent runs untouched.

Algorithm:
On entry EDX, the end-of-row advance, is spilled to DAT_00070030 because the body needs EDX as scratch. [EBP+0x1c] -- fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument, still live in its frame -- points at a four-dword tint descriptor {blend_table, alpha, rgb444_lut, tint_color}. Those fields are unpacked into the dispatcher's own argument slots, which this routine reuses as scratch: [EBP+0x08] = rgb444_lut, and [EBP+0x14] = 0x000f0f0f and [EBP+0x18] = 0x0000ffff are the two fold masks.
blend_table is the [18][256] dword table fdps_build_palette_tables writes at 000653f0: each entry is a palette colour packed one 4-bit channel per byte and pre-multiplied by that row's weight, rows 0..8 carrying weights 0..8 and rows 9..17 the complementary 16..8. alpha (0..16) is folded so both row indices stay in 0..8: for alpha <= 8 the constant colour reads row alpha ([EBP+0x0c]) and the sprite pixels read row 9+alpha ([EBP+0x10]); for alpha > 8 alpha is replaced by 16-alpha and the two rows swap. Either way the constant colour ends up weighted by alpha and the sprite pixel by 16-alpha. blend_table[tint_row][tint_color] is fetched once and parked in [EBP+0x1c].
Each row reloads the row width from DAT_00070024 into BX and then consumes command bytes from ESI until BX is exactly zero. The top two bits of the command byte select the op and the low six carry len-1, so len = (cmd & 0x3f) + 1, i.e. 1..64:
  00 fill      -- one pixel byte from the stream, blended once, REP STOSB over len destination bytes; width -= len.
  01 stretched -- one pixel byte, blended once, written into every second destination byte across a 2*len span (INC EDI then STOSB), so the even byte of each pair keeps what was there; width -= 2*len.
  10 literal   -- len pixel bytes from the stream, each blended and stored in turn; width -= len.
  11 skip      -- EDI += len with no write, a transparent run that leaves the backdrop as it was; width -= len. This op is what separates mode 11 from the otherwise identical mode 10 kernel fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop at 00057793, whose fourth op blends the destination byte instead of skipping it.
Blending one pixel index p is blend_table[pixel_row][p] plus the parked constant, shifted right by 4 (dividing out the /16 of the weights) and masked with 0x000f0f0f, which leaves 4 bits per channel at bits 0..3, 8..11 and 16..19; those are folded into a 12-bit index by (v & 0xffff) | (v >> 12), and the index selects the output byte from the 4096-entry inverse-palette table rgb444_lut. This is the same blend and fold that fdps_blit_tint_rect performs on an uncompressed rectangle.
At the end of a row EDI takes the advance saved in DAT_00070030 and the row counter at DAT_00070022 is decremented; the routine returns once that counter reaches zero.
Three NOPs sit at 00057a06 and three more at 00057a4a, right after the two-byte short JMPs at 00057a04 and 00057a48 (eb 5a 90 90 90 and eb 16 90 90 90), matching the NOP quartets that pad branch targets inside the body. They are unreachable filler, not a boundary problem.

Where it is used:
Exactly one call site in the whole image selects mode 11: 0002d198 in fdps_draw_map_unit, which draws a battle-map unit's 0x18 x 0x18 cell with alpha 8 and tint_color 0, taken when bit 0x80 of the unit's flag byte at record offset 5 is set. That bit is the acted-this-turn flag -- fdps_battle_mark_unit_done ORs it in and fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase tests it -- so on screen this kernel is what makes a unit that has already moved appear blended half-way into palette colour 0. fdps_draw_map_unit fills the descriptor's blend_table and rgb444_lut slots once at entry (0002cdbe, 0002cdc5) and writes the tint_color slot only on this path (0002d15a); its mode 9 calls leave that fourth slot alone because fdps_rle_blit_translucent reads only the first three fields.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. This is hand-written assembly; every input arrives in a register, in a global or in the caller's live frame, all set up by fdps_blit_dispatch immediately before the call:
    ESI          -- RLE command stream, advanced in place past the bytes it consumes
    EDI          -- destination pixel pointer, advanced in place
    EDX          -- end-of-row advance, computed by the caller as pitch - width
    [EBP+0x1c]   -- fdps_blit_dispatch's sixth argument: pointer to {uint *blend_table, int alpha, uchar *rgb444_lut, int tint_color}
    DAT_00070024 -- u16 row width in pixels, reloaded at the top of every row
    DAT_00070022 -- u16 rows remaining, decremented to zero by this routine

Returns:
  nothing. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are destroyed, and so are the caller's argument slots [EBP+0x08] through [EBP+0x1c].

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID candidate in either library set; sole caller is fdps_blit_dispatch; shares the blit state globals]

Rebuild note:
This kernel is not an ordinary C function: it runs on fdps_blit_dispatch's frame and uses that function's own argument slots [EBP+0x08] through [EBP+0x1c] as its scratch, and it destroys EBX, ESI and EDI, which Watcom's convention says a callee preserves. Rewriting it as a plain C routine taking (stream, dest, descriptor) and calling it from a rebuilt fdps_blit_dispatch that still reads its own arguments after the call gives the wrong result. alpha is also unchecked -- 16-alpha is formed by SUB ECX,0x10 / NEG ECX with no clamp, so any value above 16 indexes blend_table below its base. And the fourth descriptor field belongs to the tint kernels alone: fdps_draw_map_unit never writes it on its mode 9 calls, so declaring one descriptor struct and dutifully initialising all four fields at every call site is not what the original does.

=== 00057a06 [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP run: alignment filler in a gap inside FUN_00057916's address range

=== 00057a4a [EOL]
3-byte 0x90 NOP alignment filler inside the FUN_00057916 address range

=== 00057a74 [PLATE]
Blit mode 0x0c: draws one 4-op RLE sprite stream into an 8bpp destination surface as a translucent sprite, but only for the pixels whose palette index falls inside a caller-configured colour range; every pixel outside that range is written through opaque. Nothing in the shipped executable selects this mode.

Algorithm:
Entered by a plain CALL from fdps_blit_dispatch with that function's registers and stack frame still live and no prologue of its own: ESI = the RLE command stream, EDI = the first destination pixel, EDX = pitch - width (the end-of-row advance), EBP = the dispatcher's frame pointer.

Setup, once. EDX is parked in the dword global at 00070030. [EBP+0x1c], the dispatcher's arg6, points at a five-field blend descriptor the caller built on its own stack:
  +0x00  base of the brightness ramp table that fdps_build_palette_tables fills at 000653f0 -- 18 rows of 256 dwords, row j holding every palette colour packed with red in bits 16-19, green in 8-11 and blue in 0-3 and scaled by coefficient j (row 0 is zero, row 1 is the unscaled colour).
  +0x04  blend level, 0..16.
  +0x08  base of the 16x16x16 inverse-palette cube at 000643f0, 4096 bytes mapping a 4-bit-per-channel colour back to a palette index.
  +0x0c  low palette index of the range that gets blended; only the low 16 bits are read, and they are copied to the word at 00070050.
  +0x10  high palette index of that range, likewise 16 bits, copied to the word at 00070052.
The first three fields and the code that consumes them are fdps_rle_blit_translucent's, instruction for instruction: from the level it picks the two ramp rows that weight the two pixels -- for level <= 8 the source pixel is weighted by row level+9 and the destination by row level; above 8 the roles swap around row 16-level, so nine rows of coefficients cover all seventeen ratios. The paired coefficients sum to 16, which is what makes the later >> 4 a weighted average instead of a carry between channels, so level is the destination's share of the blend in sixteenths -- fdps_draw_composite_sprite builds the same descriptor at 000141f0 and sets this field to 16 minus the sprite part's opacity word at part+7. The two row addresses land in [EBP+0x0c] and [EBP+0x10], the channel mask 0x0f0f0f in [EBP+0x14], 0xffff in [EBP+0x18] and the cube base in [EBP+0x08] -- all of them fdps_blit_dispatch's own argument slots, used here as scratch.

Rows. Each row loads the column count from the word at 00070024 into BX and decodes command bytes from ESI until BX is exactly zero. The low six bits of a command byte give len = (cmd & 0x3f) + 1 (1..64) and the top two bits select the op:
  00 fill      -- one pixel byte follows; out of range it is REP STOSBed across len columns, in range each of the len destination pixels is blended with it in turn; BX -= len.
  01 stretched -- one pixel byte follows, written into every other column across a 2*len span starting at EDI+1 and leaving the columns in between as they were, blended the same way when in range; BX -= 2*len.
  10 literal   -- len pixel bytes follow, each range-tested and either stored or blended on its own; BX -= len.
  11 skip      -- no bytes follow; EDI += len leaves those columns untouched; BX -= len.
The range test is lo <= pixel <= hi against the two words at 00070050/00070052, done as signed 16-bit compares on the zero-extended pixel byte; the fill and stretched ops test their single pixel byte once and take a separate loop for each answer, the literal op tests every byte.
Blending one pixel: EAX = ramp_src[source pixel] + ramp_dst[*EDI], then >> 4 and & 0x0f0f0f, leaving one 4-bit channel in the low nibble of each of the three bytes; those nibbles are folded into a 12-bit index as green<<8 | red<<4 | blue and the byte read from the inverse-palette cube at that index is what gets stored.
At the end of a row EDI advances by the value parked at 00070030, the row counter at 00070022 is decremented in place, and the row loop restarts with a fresh column count; the routine returns when that counter reaches zero. The NOP runs and the three-byte gaps after the short jumps are branch-target padding, not code.

Parameters:
  none on the stack. This is hand-written assembly and every input arrives in a register, a global or the caller's frame, all of them set up by fdps_blit_dispatch immediately before the CALL:
    ESI          -- RLE command stream, advanced in place past the bytes it consumes
    EDI          -- destination pixel pointer, advanced in place
    EDX          -- end-of-row advance, computed by the caller as pitch - width
    [EBP+0x1c]   -- pointer to the blend descriptor described above (the dispatcher's arg6)
    DAT_00070024 -- u16 columns per row, reloaded at the top of every row
    DAT_00070022 -- u16 rows remaining, decremented to zero by this routine
  Unlike the mode 0 kernel at 00056a0d it does not need ECX zeroed on entry; it does XOR ECX,ECX itself at 00057ad6.

Returns:
  nothing. EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX, ESI and EDI are destroyed, as are the caller's argument slots [EBP+0x08] through [EBP+0x1c], and the globals at 00070022, 00070030, 00070050 and 00070052 are left holding this call's state.

Reachability: unreachable in the shipped executable. fdps_blit_dispatch is the only entry, it selects this kernel only when its mode argument is 0x0c, and no path in the program produces that value -- see the open_question field for the trace. The two range globals 00070050/00070052 are written and read by this function alone, so nothing else in the program observes its state either. The behaviour above therefore rests entirely on the instructions; no play-test can exercise it.

Pool: fdps  [no Function ID hit in either library set; it shares fdps_blit_dispatch's stack frame and blit state globals and is reached only from that dispatcher's mode == 0x0c arm]

Rebuild note:
The 12-bit inverse-palette index is folded green-major: after the & 0x0f0f0f the code ORs (packed >> 12) into (packed & 0xffff), putting green in bits 8-11, red in 4-7 and blue in 0-3, so the lookup is cube[g*256 + r*16 + b]. Writing the obvious cube[r*256 + g*16 + b] gives wrong colours, and it keeps giving them unless the cube generator is changed to match -- fdps_build_palette_tables fills 000643f0 in exactly that green-outer, red-middle, blue-inner order (loops at 0002b11a/0002b134/0002b144, arguments pushed at 0002b16a/0002b175). Second trap: the routine uses fdps_blit_dispatch's own argument slots [EBP+0x08..0x1c] as scratch, overwriting src, dst, width, height and pitch; a rewrite that keeps those as ordinary C locals and reads any of them after the blit gets the original values where the assembly has none. Third: no call site selects mode 0x0c, so this kernel's correctness cannot be established by playing the game whichever way a rebuild treats it -- keeping it earns no play-test coverage, and the only check available is reading it against the original.

=== 00057b1b [EOL]
3-byte NOP filler (90 90 90) inside the address span of FUN_00057a74

=== 00057b8a [EOL]
Three 0x90 NOPs: unreachable alignment filler inside FUN_00057a74, after a jmp and before live code at 00057b8d.

=== 00057bcd [EOL]

=== 00057c36 [EOL]

=== 00060004 [PLATE]
Battle rule flag: non-zero means cancelling the action menu ends the unit's turn; zero means the cancel is a take-back.

Read only, at two places in fdps_battle_unit_turn, each right after fdps_battle_action_menu has returned -1 for a player cancel. When the flag is zero and the unit had already walked a path, 000156b2 restores the pre-move tile into fields 0x00/0x01 of the unit record reached through data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr, sets 00069cd0 and calls fdps_map_cursor_move_to on the start tile, so the turn loop runs again from the beginning; when the unit had not moved, 000157ae just falls through and the loop repeats. When the flag is non-zero, both sites instead call fdps_battle_mark_unit_done, then fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event on the unit's current tile, and set the local loop-exit flag, so the cancel spends the turn where the unit stands.

No instruction in the image writes it and its initialised value is 0, so the shipped game always allows the take-back and the two commit-on-cancel paths never run.

Pool: fdps  [its only referencing function, fdps_battle_unit_turn, is game battle logic; no CRT or AIL code reaches it]

=== 00060008 [PLATE]
Player setting: nonzero when background music (CD audio) is enabled.

fdps_title_screen forces it to 1 at 0002a56b before starting the title track, so entering the
title screen always turns music back on. fdps_options_menu is the only place the player changes
it: at 0001849e it flips the low bit with XOR 1 and immediately re-enters
fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track so the change takes effect on the spot, and at 000183ef it
reads the flag to pick which of two menu strings to draw (text id 0xd when set, 0x31 when clear).
Every CD-audio entry point gates on it. fdps_cd_set_music_track and
fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track do not merely skip playing when it is 0: they substitute -1
for the track the caller asked for before storing it into the current-track slot DAT_00069d54,
so a music-off setting also erases the request, and they skip the play call afterwards.
fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll will not restart a finished track while it is 0. The flag is part of
the saved game: fdps_save_game_screen and fdps_battle_system_submenu copy it into the save
record next to DAT_00060158 and the sound-availability flag DAT_00069d70, and
fdps_load_game_screen and fdps_load_savegame copy it back out. Only 0 and 1 ever occur -- the
only writes in the program are a store of 1 and an XOR with 1.

Pool: fdps  [every referencing function is game logic; the CD routines that read it are the
game's own audio layer, not the AIL library]

Rebuild note:
It sits in initialised data with the value 1, not in _BSS: music is on before any code writes it.
Declaring it as a plain uninitialised global -- the obvious C for a boolean flag -- starts the
game silent and makes fdps_cd_set_music_track force the current-track slot to -1 on the first
call, so no music plays until the player visits the options menu or the title screen.

=== 0006000c [PLATE]
Which colour row of the NUMBER.CEL digit sheet fdps_draw_number draws its glyphs from.

Read only by fdps_draw_number, which computes glyph_index + 13 * this value and uses it to index the CEL offset table at +0x0f of the Number.cel sheet pointer in DAT_000643d8. The sheet holds 65 sprites: five rows of the same thirteen 6x8 glyphs, '0'-'9' then '+', '-' and '?', each row in a different colour. Callers set this global immediately before a draw and put it back to 0 afterwards, so 0 is the resting value and the default colour; only 0..3 are ever written, row 4 is never selected.

What each caller means by the value differs, because the global carries the colour and not the condition. fdps_draw_unit_status_panel writes 3 when a current value differs from its maximum, and 1 when the unit's status byte at +0x22, +0x23 or +0x24 is non-zero, 0 otherwise. fdps_shop_draw_member_entry writes 2 when the previewed stat is higher than the member's current one, 3 when it is lower, 0 when equal. fdps_draw_save_slot_panel writes 3 for the chapter number, 1 for the date and 2 for the time. fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel writes 3 when two values disagree. All of them write 0 before returning.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: the five referencing functions are all pool fdps UI painters, and it addresses a game asset, NUMBER.CEL]

Rebuild note:
fdps_draw_save_slot_panel draws the first of its six numbers, the leader's level, without setting this global at all -- it relies on the previous panel having left it at 0 on the way out. Turning the colour into a parameter of fdps_draw_number, or clearing the global at function entry, is the obvious rewrite and changes which colour that one figure comes out in.

=== 00060010 [PLATE]
Player option: non-zero plays combat as the full-screen battle animation, zero resolves it on the map. Initial value 1.

fdps_options_menu owns it: it is the third of the four settings that menu shows, drawn with label id 0x0f when set and 0x33 when clear, and flipped with XOR 1 when the player confirms cursor index 2 (index 0 flips the CD-music flag at 0x00060008 and replays the track, index 1 the SFX flag at 0x00069d70, index 3 the terrain-HUD flag at 0x00060158). It is one of the persisted settings: fdps_battle_system_submenu copies it into the save-state record at +0x0e (whole-file offset 0x30d1) and fdps_save_game_screen into the save slot at +0xa07; fdps_load_savegame and fdps_load_game_screen read it back from the same two places. The value is only ever 0 or 1. Two functions act on it. fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack: when it is 0 the exchange is played on the map -- cursor mode drops to 0 for one fdps_render_view_frame, fdps_battle_show_combat_gauges puts the HP bars up and fdps_unit_attack_target strikes, with the counterattack driven from that function; when it is non-zero the whole exchange is handed to the full-screen fight animation FUN_00018d60, which runs its own counterattack test. fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell: exactly 1 plays the spell through fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets, any other value through fdps_cast_spell_on_targets on the map.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- the options menu, the two AI action executors and the save/load pair]

Rebuild note:
It lives in initialised data with the value 1, so it must be defined as `uchar data_fdps_ui_battle_animation_enabled = 1;`. Declaring it without an initialiser makes a fresh game start with battle animations off and the OFF label showing. Its sense is also the reverse of FD2's data_fd2_ui_game_speed_flag, which occupies the same two save offsets: there non-zero meant fast and skipped the cinematic, here non-zero means play the full animation, so carrying FD2's comparisons across inverts the option.

=== 00060014 [PLATE]
Phase of the UI palette cycle: the offset, 0..15, at which fdps_cycle_ui_palette starts reading the three colour ramps each frame.

Initialised data, starts at 15. Only fdps_cycle_ui_palette (00015be0) touches it. When that routine finds a timer tick it has not serviced yet, it writes DAC entries 8..15 by reading ramp[phase + i] for i = 0..7 out of the red, green and blue ramps copied from 0x14740, 0x14758 and 0x14770, then does DEC on this variable and resets it to 15 when it reaches -1. One step per timer tick, so the colour wave marches across palette indices 8..15 in the direction of decreasing phase and repeats every 16 ticks. Values outside 0..15 never occur; -1 exists only for the instant between the DEC at 00015cd2 and the reset at 00015ce1.

Pool: fdps  [only reader/writer is the game UI routine fdps_cycle_ui_palette, and the ramps it indexes are game-authored data]

Rebuild note:
The phase runs up to 15 while the window read is 8 entries wide, so ramp[phase + i] reaches byte 22 of each ramp. The ramps are 24 bytes because their first 8 bytes are repeated at the end for exactly this reason; shortening them to the 16 distinct steps, or wrapping the index with % 16, changes the colours.

=== 00060018 [PLATE]
Auto-repeat hold counter: how many timer ticks the currently held key has been down, in the keyboard poll's own repeat filter.

Written only by fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat. When the scancode read through fdps_keyboard_scancode_ptr differs from the previous poll's code (DAT_00063fc4) the key is new and this is reset to 0. When the code is unchanged and the timer tick counter DAT_00069d64 has moved since the tick recorded in DAT_00063fc8, it is incremented -- so it advances at most once per timer tick however often the caller polls, and counts ticks rather than polls. It is then read back to decide the poll's result: the scancode is returned only when the counter has reached 5 and is a multiple of 3, otherwise the poll yields 0xff. The first repeat therefore lands on tick 6 and further repeats every 3 ticks after that. Range is 0 upward while one key stays down; it has no ceiling and no sentinel, and nothing outside this function reads it.

Pool: fdps  [reached only by fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat, application input policy with no CRT or AIL idiom]

=== 00060040 [PLATE]
Per-terrain percentage modifier applied to a unit's attack power, indexed by the tile attribute id 0..5.

Read-only; nothing writes it. fdps_map_load_tile_info publishes the attribute byte of the tile under a unit into DAT_00069d09, and the readers index this table with it. fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome and fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit apply the entry to the attacker's attack stat (unit record +0x48) as attack += entry * attack / 100, and only when fdps_unit_is_flying reports the attacker is on the ground; fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel prints the entry as a signed number in the terrain rows of the map cursor panel, directly above the defense figure. The values are { +5, 0, -5, -5, -5, 0 } percent: attribute 0 gives a +5% attack bonus, 1 and 5 are neutral, 2 through 4 cost 5%. Entries are signed 32-bit: -5 is stored as 0xfffffffb and the readers sign-extend with SAR EDX,0x1f before the signed divide by 100. The sibling defense table at 00060058 is indexed by the same byte and bounds this one at exactly six elements; nothing range-checks the index, so a tileset attribute byte above 5 would read into that sibling.

Pool: fdps  [all three readers are game combat and HUD code; no CRT or AIL code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
The entries are signed percentages stored as raw dwords, and the code sign-extends before a signed divide by 100. Declaring the table unsigned -- dword or uint, which the fb ff ff ff bytes invite -- turns every terrain penalty into an enormous attack bonus. The divide also truncates toward zero, so an attack stat below 20 gets no terrain adjustment at all; rounding it is not equivalent.

=== 00060058 [PLATE]
Per-terrain-class defence modifier, as a signed percentage applied to the defender's DP.

Read-only table of six int entries, indexed by the terrain combat class byte DAT_00069d09 that fdps_map_load_tile_info publishes for the tile it was just asked about. Values are {0, 0, +10, +10, -5, 0}: classes 2 and 3 give a defender +10% DP, class 4 costs it 5%, the rest are neutral.

fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome and fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit both apply it as DP_eff = DP + (table[class] * DP) / 100, using the tile under the DEFENDER and only when fdps_unit_is_flying says that unit is not flying. The sibling table at 00060040 is the attacker's AP side of the same pair, read from the tile under the attacker. fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel pushes the same entry to print the terrain's defence bonus in the cursor information panel. Nothing writes it.

Pool: fdps  [only game combat and HUD code reaches it; no library touches it]

Rebuild note:
Entry 4 is -5, stored as fb ff ff ff. Declaring the table unsigned (or as dword) turns that into 4294967291 and the terrain penalty becomes a colossal defence bonus; the multiply and divide in the original are signed (IMUL, then SAR/IDIV by 100). The division also truncates toward zero, so the modifier vanishes entirely for small DP -- rounding it is a behaviour change.

=== 00060070 [PLATE]
Non-zero while the village phase is running, so the shared window and drawing code takes its village variant and works over the static village screen instead of the live scrolling battle map.

fdps_run_village_phase sets it to 1 when it enters the village (chapter id at DAT_00069cf4 <= 0x19 and != 0x16) just before loading ShopWin.Cel from MISC.VFS, and clears it to 0 on that branch's one exit, after freeing the village buffers at DAT_00069d84 and DAT_00069d80 and just before it clears DAT_00060150 and data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr. The non-village branch jumps past both writes, so the flag is 0 everywhere outside the village. Only 0 and 1 are ever stored, and every read is a test against zero.

The readers are the shared UI routines, which the village submenus (shop, church, bar, item, secret) reach through fdps_run_village_phase and therefore run with the flag set. fdps_draw_text, fdps_message_window_wait_key, fdps_close_status_window, fdps_prompt_two_choice and fdps_spell_list_window_wait_input take the battle path that recomposites the scrolling map when it is 0 and the still-screen path when it is 1; fdps_draw_text also selects the message-window source address (0xaa44a when clear, 0xaa3d4 when set) from it. fdps_draw_unit_status_panel and fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input use it to switch the roster index onto a global channel: with the flag set the panel stores its caller's index into DAT_00063fb0 and the input loop reads that back in place of its own argument. fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window skips its screen-restore call when the flag is set, and fdps_load_game_screen only restores the save slot's DAT_00064110 field when it is clear.

Pool: fdps  [all 17 references are game code in pool fdps; no CRT or AIL code reaches it]

=== 00060074 [PLATE]
Per-chapter entry-handler table: slot N holds the address of the function that brings the game into chapter N+1.

Thirty read-only function pointers, one per chapter, in chapter order: slot 0 is fdps_chapter_01_init at 00020e90 and slot 29 is fdps_chapter_30_init at 00021610. Nothing writes the table; it is initialised data fixed up by the linker.

It is indexed by the 0-based chapter index in DAT_00069cf4, which runs 0..29 against the 1..30 the player is shown. Two sites dispatch through it. fdps_title_screen zeroes DAT_00069cf4 on the New Game path and immediately calls slot 0, which is how a new game starts chapter 1. fdps_run_village_phase calls table[DAT_00069cf4] on the way out of the village, guarded by the byte flag at 000643eb, which is how the game enters the next chapter after a village visit. Both call the slot for its side effects and ignore EAX.

The index that selects the slot is set from three places: each fdps_chapter_NN_end writes the following chapter's index (chapter 1's end writes 1, chapter 29's end writes 0x1d, and chapter 30's end writes nothing because the game is over), fdps_load_savegame takes it from byte +2 of the save slot, and fdps_icon_script_run takes it from an operand byte of an IconAni event script. None of the three range-checks the value against 30.

Every handler shares the same shape -- optionally add the character who joins this chapter to the roster, fdps_chapter_state_reset, run IconNN.dat out of IconAni.vfs, show the chapter title card, park the map cursor -- so the table is a jump table over 30 near-identical bodies rather than over 30 unrelated ones.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it, and its 30 entries are all settled fdps chapter handlers]

Rebuild note:
The table has exactly 30 entries and no terminator, and no caller bounds-checks DAT_00069cf4 before scaling it by 4 and calling. Do not add the range check: a save file or an IconAni script carrying a chapter index of 30 or more calls through the bytes of the string "IconAni.vfs" that immediately follows the table, and a rebuild that clamps or rejects the index behaves differently from the original on exactly the inputs where the difference is observable.

=== 00060120 [PLATE]
Pointer to the one resident FACE.CEL portrait record, or NULL when no portrait is loaded.

fdps_load_and_draw_portrait is the only writer that stores a live buffer: it frees whatever is here, clears the global, then (for portrait_index 0..159) mallocs the record's byte length taken from FACE.CEL's offset directory, freads the record in and blits it 125x100. The record deliberately outlives that call, so it is at most one portrait at a time. Three repaint paths -- fdps_prompt_two_choice, fdps_draw_text and fdps_message_window_wait_key -- test it against NULL and, when set, blit the same 125x100 image into their window buffer at offset 0x9ad0 with pitch 0x168, which is how the speaker portrait survives a panel redraw. It is freed and set back to NULL by fdps_load_and_draw_portrait on every call (including portrait_index -1, which only releases), by fdps_message_window_open when its window-height argument is negative, and by fdps_village_animate_window_zoom before it takes its own 0xfa00-byte screen snapshot; fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it at exit without clearing it. NULL is the only sentinel: the value is never inspected, only dereferenced.

Pool: fdps  [every referencing function is pool fdps; the buffer holds a game data file record and is consumed by fdps_blit_dispatch]

Rebuild note:
The portrait buffer is cached across calls on purpose. Writing fdps_load_and_draw_portrait so that it reads the record into a local buffer, or frees it after its own blit, draws correctly once and then loses the portrait on the next window repaint, because the repaint paths blit straight out of this global. Equally, the frees in fdps_message_window_open and fdps_village_animate_window_zoom are not incidental cleanup -- they are what makes the portrait disappear at those moments.

=== 00060124 [PLATE]
Pointer to the current chapter's loaded text block ("fdetxt%02d.txt"), the bank every chapter dialogue line is drawn from.

Written only by fdps_load_field_chapter_resources and fdps_field_load_chapter_resources: each frees the previous block if the pointer is non-zero, formats "fdetxt%02d.txt" with the chapter counter data at 00069cf4 PLUS ONE, and stores what fdps_vfs_load_entry returns for that member of the "Field.vfs" archive. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it at exit under the same non-zero guard. NULL means no chapter text is loaded; every writer and the shutdown path test for it before freeing.

Every other reference is a read that passes it as the text_base argument of fdps_draw_text, with the message id in the second argument: fdps_battle_show_win_fail_window (victory line 2, defeat line 3), fdps_play_ending_credit_roll, fdps_run_death_scripts, fdps_icon_script_run and fdps_icon_script_prompt_three_way_choice, the village screens fdps_village_item_menu, fdps_run_church_screen, fdps_run_bar_shop, fdps_run_weapon_shop and fdps_run_secret_menu, and the whole fdps_chapter_NN_event_* / fdps_chapter_NN_post_action family. The block itself is a table of signed 16-bit byte offsets followed by the token streams they point at; the message ids the callers pass are 0-based indices into that table and run roughly 0x04..0x23, each chapter's file supplying its own set.

Pool: fdps  [only pool_fdps code touches it; it holds a game data file loaded out of a game archive]

Rebuild note:
The file number is the chapter index plus one, while the Shop%02d.dat loaded two statements later in the same function uses the raw chapter index. Writing the chapter counter into both format calls loads the neighbouring chapter's dialogue.

=== 00060131 [PLATE]
One-shot flag: when set, fdps_run_village_phase skips the screen blank-out and the save-game prompt it would otherwise run for a chapter that has no village.

fdps_title_screen sets it to 1 at 0002a8c8, on the Load Game arm of the title menu, right after fdps_load_game_screen returns and just before it calls fdps_run_village_phase. fdps_run_village_phase reads it at 0003127c in its no-village branch (chapters 0x10, 0x11, 0x15, 0x16 and >= 0x1a): with the flag at 0 that branch clears VGA memory at 0xa0000 (64000 bytes), fades the palette to black through fdps_set_palette_range, and runs fdps_save_game_screen on a freshly zeroed 64000-byte page; with the flag non-zero the whole block is skipped, leaving the screen the load path put up. fdps_run_village_phase clears it back to 0 at 00031513 on every path out, so one write only ever affects one village phase. Values: 0 = do the blank-out and the save prompt, 1 = skip them.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_title_screen and fdps_run_village_phase reach it; it is game flow state, no library sees it]

Rebuild note:
fdps_title_screen sets this unconditionally, outside the `if (result == 1)` that guards the call to fdps_run_village_phase, so backing out of the load screen leaves it set and the next village phase that runs silently skips its save prompt. Writing the obvious thing -- moving the assignment inside that `if`, since that call is the only reader -- removes the leak and changes behaviour.

=== 00060138 [PLATE]
Base pointer of the CEL sprite-group cache: one heap block whose first 0x5a0 bytes are a slot table of 30 x 12 dword sprite offsets, followed by the sprite pixel data those offsets point into.

fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group is the only writer. On the first group (slot count at 00069cf0 is 0) it malloc()s 0x5a0 + group size, reads the group's pixels to p + 0x5a0 and fills slot 0; on every later group it realloc()s, appends the pixels at the byte cursor 0006411c and writes the twelve offsets of slot n at n * 0x30. The group key of slot n lives in the table at 00064060, so a repeat request returns the existing slot instead of appending. Each of the twelve dwords in a slot is a byte offset from this pointer, so a sprite address is *(int *)(p + slot * 0x30 + i * 4) + p, i running 0..11 over the twelve poses/frames of a group.

Readers index it by a unit's cache slot -- byte +2 of the 0x50-byte unit record -- times 0x30, then by pose: fdps_draw_map_unit, fdps_blit_unit_sprite, fdps_draw_unit_status_panel, fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input (poses 0, 3, 6, 9 via the +0, +0xc, +0x18, +0x24 displacements), fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up, fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel, fdps_spell_list_window_wait_input, fdps_shop_draw_member_entry, fdps_village_select_member, fdps_church_select_promote_candidate. fdps_village_signboard_menu and fdps_village_animate_walk_to_destination use the group given by 000601a4. fdps_draw_save_slot_panel takes the save-slot portrait from the fixed address p + *(int *)(p + 4), that is pose 1 of slot 0 of the ICON.CEL sheet it has just cached.

The cache is torn down and rebuilt whenever the resident sheet changes: fdps_build_map_unit_array, fdps_load_savegame, fdps_saveload_screen_build, fdps_draw_save_slot_panel, fdps_load_field_chapter_resources and fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members each free it when 00069cf0 is non-zero and then reset that count to 0; fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it when the pointer itself is non-NULL. Initial value is 0.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; the block is allocated, indexed and freed entirely by named game functions, no CRT or AIL module touches the address]

Rebuild note:
The teardown sites free this pointer and then zero the slot count at 00069cf0 without clearing the pointer, so it is left dangling on purpose; fdps_shutdown_free_resources guards its own free on the pointer being non-NULL, not on the count. Writing the obvious free(p); p = NULL; changes which guard fires at shutdown and silently repairs a latent double free, so keep the two guards exactly as they are.

=== 0006013c [PLATE]
Pointer to the resident copy of the current chapter's MAP%02d.DAT block from Field.vfs -- the map's scripted turn events, tile events and unit deployment table.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources writes it on every chapter load: it frees the previous block, formats "map%02d.dat" from the chapter index in DAT_00069cf4 and calls fdps_vfs_load_entry("Field.vfs", ...), then copies header byte +1 into DAT_00064118 and header byte +2 into DAT_0006410c. fdps_load_savegame writes it the other way: it frees the block, mallocs a fixed 0x8a3 bytes, aborts to the error path if that returns NULL, memmoves 0x8a3 bytes out of the save buffer, and copies the same two header bytes. fdps_battle_system_submenu memmoves 0x8a3 bytes the other way when the game is saved. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it if non-NULL. The initial value is 0 so the free-if-non-NULL guards are correct on the first chapter load.

The block is a fixed 0x83-byte header followed by records: +0 unused by any reader here (FD2's shap id), +1 party member count, +2 number of deployment records, +3..+0x32 sixteen 3-byte turn-event hooks (turn number, handler index, side) which fdps_battle_run_turn_events walks -- it matches byte +3 of a record against the turn counter DAT_00069ce8 and byte +5 against the acting side, then calls through the handler table at 000601c4 indexed by byte +4; +0x33..+0x52 sixteen 2-byte tile-step event hooks, read by fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event as +0x31 + DAT_00069d06 * 2 (a 1-based index) where a first byte of 0xff means the slot is empty and the second byte is the trigger kind; +0x53..+0x82 sixteen 3-byte tile pickup/event records, read by fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and read and written back by fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor as a byte at +0x53 and a short at +0x54; +0x83 onward N deployment records of 0x1a bytes each, consumed by fdps_deploy_wave (which loops over the count in header byte +2) and fdps_deploy_unit. Entry sizes in Field.vfs run from 209 bytes (MAP11.DAT, 3 records) to 0x8a3 = 2211 bytes (80 records), always 0x83 + N * 0x1a.

Pool: fdps  [only game functions reach it; it is loaded through the game's own VFS reader]

Rebuild note:
The save and load paths move a fixed 0x8a3 bytes, the size of the largest MAP%02d.DAT entry, while the chapter load path allocates only the entry's real size -- as little as 209 bytes. Keep both constants at 0x8a3: copying the entry's real length instead, or bounds-checking the copy, changes the savegame layout.

=== 00060140 [PLATE]
Pointer to the heap copy of the current map's "map%02d.cod" spawn-position table, NULL while no table is resident.

fdps_build_map_unit_array frees any previous table, then sprintfs "map%02d.cod" from its map_no and loads that entry of Field.vfs through fdps_vfs_load_entry into this pointer; fdps_deploy_wave loads the same file by passing this pointer's address to fdps_vfs_load_file_or_exit. Both free it and store NULL back before they return, so outside those two calls the value is NULL by design. The buffer is an 0xb-byte header followed by 6-byte records; record i is at pointer + 0xb + i * 6 and its first two fields are signed 16-bit tile coordinates (column, row), the remaining two bytes of the record being read by no caller. Records 0 .. data_fdps_map_scripted_deploy_count-1 (DAT_0006410c) are the anchor tiles of the map's scripted deployment entries, which fdps_deploy_unit reads for the unit it is placing; the party's start tiles follow them, so fdps_build_map_unit_array reads record DAT_0006410c + slot for player slot i. Do not confuse it with DAT_0006013c, which holds the resident map%02d.dat deployment table of 0x1a-byte unit records.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: game VFS loaders, the game's "map%02d.cod" string and the game's own unit-placement routines, with free() as a leaf service]

=== 00060144 [PLATE]
Pointer to the battle movement/marking grid: a 4-byte header (int16 tile width at +0, int16 tile height at +2) followed by width*height two-byte cells, cell (x, y) at +4 + 2 * (y * width + x).

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources is the only writer: on entry to a chapter it frees the previous block if non-NULL, takes the map's tile width and height from +7 and +9 of layer 0's mpl blob, mallocs 4 + 2 * width * height bytes, stores the two dimensions into the header and calls fdps_map_grid_reset to blank the cells. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it at exit. Byte 0 of a cell (base +4) is the flag byte: 0x40 marks the tile blocked -- fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles sets it for every living unit's tile, and fdps_deploy_unit and fdps_chapter_30_revive_wave_4_undead test it when hunting for a free tile; 0x80 marks movement-stops-here, set by fdps_move_grid_set_stop_flag and by fdps_move_grid_mark_zone_of_control for the four tiles around an enemy. Byte 1 of a cell (base +5) is the marker: fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range writes the remaining movement budget there and fdps_move_path_trace walks it downhill to build a path, fdps_collect_targets_in_range and fdps_collect_targets_in_line write 0 into the tiles in range, fdps_map_grid_collect_marked_tiles gathers the marked ones, fdps_draw_map_cursor and fdps_draw_scene_layers read it when compositing. The marker is read as a SIGNED byte and -1 (0xFF) is the not-marked / unreachable sentinel. fdps_map_grid_reset and fdps_move_grid_mark_zone_of_control return immediately when this pointer is NULL, which is its value outside a battle.

Pool: fdps  [all 59 references are in pool fdps game code; allocated, filled and freed entirely by the game]

Rebuild note:
The cell marker byte at +5 is compared against -1 as a signed char (fdps_collect_targets_in_range at 00011f2a onwards reads it via a char and tests != -1). Declaring that field unsigned char and keeping the literal -1 makes the comparison always true after integer promotion, and every tile then looks marked.

=== 00060148 [PLATE]
Pointer to the current chapter's per-cell event-code layer, the "M%02d.dtl" blob loaded from Field1.vfs.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources is the only writer: on every chapter load it frees the previous blob if non-null and stores the new fdps_vfs_load_entry result here, with %02d being the internal 0-based chapter index in DAT_00069cf4. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it and leaves it non-null. The blob is a 0x10-byte header followed by width*height one-byte cells starting at +0x10; the layer's own width is the signed word at +7, and it is NOT the terrain layer's width -- M00.DTL is 4112 bytes (0x10 + 64*64) while the same chapter's M000.MPL is 1451 (0xb + 720*2), so the two planes are different sizes and each read must use its own header. fdps_map_load_tile_info republishes the cell byte at (x,y) into DAT_00069d06, and that is the only path by which the layer is read. The byte is a code, not a tile: 0 means the cell carries nothing, and a non-zero value indexes the per-code already-taken flags at DAT_000640d8, the 2-byte trigger records at DAT_0006013c+0x31 (kind at +0x32) and the 3-byte reward records at DAT_0006013c+0x53. fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes is the only writer of the cell bytes: after a save is restored it walks the grid and, for a cell whose terrain attribute has bit 0x20 set and whose code is already flagged in DAT_000640d8, it bumps the terrain tile index by one and stores 0 here, which is how a consumed treasure or event stays consumed.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- four fdps functions, and the blob is a game resource out of the VFS]

Rebuild note:
The .dtl layer and the .mpl terrain layer both keep a width word at header+7 but their cell planes start at different offsets and their dimensions differ, so one shared header struct or one cached map width for both is wrong.

=== 0006014c [PLATE]
Non-zero while fdps_draw_map_units is in its shadow pass; zero for the sprite pass and at all other times.

fdps_draw_map_units is the only writer. It sets the flag to 1, walks unit indices 0 .. DAT_00060150-1 calling fdps_draw_map_unit on each, then clears the flag to 0 and walks the same range again, so every unit's shadow is on the surface before the first unit sprite goes down and no later unit can shadow an earlier one. fdps_draw_map_unit is the only reader and tests it once, after it has computed the unit's destination pointer: non-zero takes the shadow branch (vertical window DAT_00069ce0-0x1a .. +0xbe, sprite from the Shadow.cel sheet at DAT_000643dc, translucent mode 9 two scanlines below the cell), zero takes the sprite branch (window DAT_00069ce0-0x18 .. +0xc0, sprite from the map sprite cache at DAT_00060138, plus the ailment icon fdps_unit_select_status_icon picks). Only zero and one are ever stored. fdps_draw_map_unit's other caller, FUN_00015860, draws the single unit under the map cursor without touching the flag and depends on it being zero -- which it is, both from the initial value here and because fdps_draw_map_units always clears it on the way out.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: the two map-unit drawing routines, and nothing in the CRT or the sound library]

Rebuild note:
The clear to 0 at the end of the first pass in fdps_draw_map_units is load-bearing beyond that loop: it is what leaves the flag in the sprite state for FUN_00015860, which reads the flag but never sets it. Writing the obvious C -- hoisting the flag into a parameter of fdps_draw_map_unit, or dropping the trailing store because the second pass appears to be its only consumer -- makes the cursor unit draw as a shadow.

=== 00060150 [PLATE]
How many unit records are live in the array at data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr.

Wholesale writers set it when a map's unit array is (re)built: fdps_build_map_unit_array takes the map's slot count from 00064118, fdps_load_field_chapter_resources takes 00064114 and points the array at the roster buffer 00064108, fdps_load_savegame takes savegame byte +0x30C4, and fdps_run_village_phase clears it to 0 together with the array pointer. fdps_deploy_unit is the only incremental writer: with the count 0 it mallocs one 0x50-byte record, otherwise it reallocs the array to (count + 1) * 0x50, fills slot [count], and then increments -- so the unit just deployed is at the index the count held before the call, which is why fdps_chapter_23_event_give_martial_artist_ring and fdps_chapter_25_event_deploy_wave_1 read count - 1 to reach it. Everything else reads it. About forty functions -- the turn phases fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase / fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase / fdps_battle_player_phase_loop, the sweeps fdps_battle_tick_status_effects, fdps_draw_map_units, fdps_collect_targets_in_range, fdps_battle_count_remaining_units_on_side, the chapter end handlers, and so on -- use it as the exclusive upper bound of a signed unit-index sweep 0 .. count-1 and resolve each record through fdps_get_unit_record; fdps_battle_player_phase_loop instead wraps the active unit index with a signed modulo by it. Its value is a count of all units on the map, player, NPC and enemy alike, and it changes during a phase because chapter events deploy reinforcements mid-sweep. Zero carries a second meaning: 'no unit array is allocated'. fdps_deploy_unit branches on it to choose malloc over realloc, and fdps_build_map_unit_array, fdps_load_savegame and fdps_load_field_chapter_resources free the outgoing array only when it is non-zero. It travels through the savegame as a single byte at +0x30C4 alongside count * 0x50 bytes of records at +0x12A3; the load path mallocs a fixed 0x1E00 = 96 * 0x50 bytes, so 96 records is the save-format ceiling.

Pool: fdps  [all 61 references are game-logic functions; it counts the game's own 0x50-byte unit records]

Rebuild note:
The count is also the 'unit array is allocated' flag: fdps_deploy_unit mallocs a first record only when it is 0, and the frees in fdps_build_map_unit_array / fdps_load_savegame / fdps_load_field_chapter_resources are guarded by it and never by the pointer, so a rewrite that tests data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr instead -- the obvious C -- frees the roster buffer that the field path deliberately aliases and reallocs a stale pointer after fdps_run_village_phase. It also grows inside the phase loops when a chapter event deploys reinforcements, so the loop bound has to stay a re-read of the global and must not be hoisted into a local.

=== 00060154 [PLATE]
Palette index that scene-layer tiles marked by the movement grid are tinted toward. Initialised to 0xff and never written by any code.

Read in exactly one place: fdps_draw_scene_layer at 0002c374 copies it into the fourth dword of the blend descriptor it builds on its stack -- {shade-ramp table 000653f0, blend level, inverse colour cube 000643f0, this colour} -- and passes the descriptor to fdps_blit_dispatch as arg6. Only the mode 0x0a kernel fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop reads that fourth dword: it looks up blend_table[tint row][this value] once per blit and blends every pixel it writes, plus the destination pixels showing through the sprite's transparent runs, toward that constant colour. Mode 9 (fdps_rle_blit_translucent) reads only the first three dwords and ignores it. The one path that reaches mode 0x0a is the branch at 0002c5ee: a scene layer whose mode byte is 1, a tile whose attribute flag has bit 0x80 clear, and a movement-grid cell whose byte 1 is not 0xff (0xff being the unmarked value fdps_map_grid_reset writes). So this is the colour of the battle map's movement/target range highlight, applied at the pulsing blend level ramp[data at 0006015c / 4]. The value is a VGA palette index in 0..255; no code writes it, so the highlight colour is fixed at 0xff for the whole run.

Pool: fdps  [its only reference is game draw code, fdps_draw_scene_layer, and the kernel that consumes it is a game blit kernel; neither the CRT nor AIL touches it]

Rebuild note:
0xff here is a live palette index, not a "no tint" sentinel -- the neighbouring 0xff in the same function means "unmarked movement-grid cell", and treating this one the same way and skipping the tint would remove the range highlight.

=== 00060158 [PLATE]
User on/off setting for the battle-map terrain/unit info panel; ships enabled (image value 1).

Row 3 of the in-game options menu. fdps_options_menu reads it to choose the menu label id -- 0x18 when set, 0x3c when clear -- and flips it with XOR 1 when the player selects that row. The only gameplay reader is fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel, which draws nothing unless this flag AND the transition gate at 0x60159 are both non-zero; that panel shows the cursor tile's terrain cel with its AP and DEF modifiers, plus the sprite and current HP of any unit standing on the tile. It is part of the saved game: fdps_save_game_screen stores it at slot+0xa06 and fdps_load_game_screen restores it from there, and fdps_load_savegame restores it from the loaded buffer at +0x30d2. Transitions that must not draw the panel clear it and put it back: fdps_run_village_phase copies the current value to a local, writes 0 for the whole village phase and restores the saved value on the way out. Two paths instead force it back on without saving first -- fdps_title_screen writes 0 around the chapter-init handler call on the new-game path and then writes 1, and fdps_chapter_30_end writes 1 to this flag and to 0x60159 before the ending sequence. Values are 0 = panel off, 1 = panel on; nothing else is ever stored.

Pool: fdps  [only game code touches it -- the options menu, the save/load screens and the battle-map panel renderer; no CRT or Miles reference]

Rebuild note:
fdps_title_screen and fdps_chapter_30_end force this saved user setting back to 1 instead of restoring the value they clobbered. Keep the unconditional stores; turning them into a save/restore pair like the one in fdps_run_village_phase would leave the panel hidden where the original shows it.

=== 00060159 [PLATE]
Gameplay-active gate for the cursor/terrain info panel: nonzero while ordinary interactive play is on screen, zero while a scripted or transitional sequence owns the display.

Read by fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel, which draws nothing unless this flag and the user option DAT_00060158 are both nonzero. Cleared to 0 on entry to anything that must not show the panel -- fdps_battle_system_menu, fdps_battle_unit_turn, fdps_battle_advance_turn, fdps_title_demo, and the icon-script handlers fdps_icon_script_walk_units, fdps_icon_script_set_unit_facing, fdps_icon_script_blink_units_out, fdps_icon_script_animate_view_offset -- and stored back as 1 when interactive play resumes, in most places paired with the cursor-shape selector DAT_00069cd0 (0 with the flag cleared, 1 with it set). fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window latches the current value into DAT_00063fb8 and clears the flag while the status window is up; fdps_close_status_window copies DAT_00063fb8 back. fdps_icon_script_animate_view_offset saves the value in a local and restores it on exit, whereas the other three icon-script handlers write the literal 1 on their exit path instead of restoring. fdps_title_screen sets it, fdps_chapter_30_end sets it together with DAT_00060158. The only values ever stored are 0 and 1, and the image ships it as 1.

Pool: fdps  [all 14 referencing functions are pool_fdps game logic; no CRT or AIL code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
The image value is 1, not 0. Declaring it as a plain uninitialised flag ("static uchar data_fdps_ui_play_active_flag;") moves it into _BSS and starts it at 0, and the cursor/terrain info panel would then stay blank until the first code path that sets it runs. It must be defined in initialised data with an explicit = 1.

=== 0006015c [PLATE]
Phase of the pulsing blend applied to movement-grid-marked map tiles; cycles 0..0x37 and indexes the 14-entry blend-level ramp as phase / 4.

fdps_draw_scene_layer advances it at the top of every call, once per layer rather than once per frame, as (phase + 1) % 0x38. Later in the same function, when a cell's movement-grid byte is not 0xff (the unmarked value fdps_map_grid_reset writes), the tile is blitted through fdps_blit_dispatch at blend level ramp[phase / 4], the ramp being 02 03 04 05 06 07 07 07 06 05 04 03 02 02 copied from 0002b280 -- so marked tiles pulse between blend levels 2 and 7 out of 16 with each ramp step held for four advances. fdps_battle_unit_turn writes 0x14 before it starts marking the acting unit's movement range, and fdps_map_actor_use_item writes 0x14 before sweeping the cursor along a straight-line item's beam, so both restart the pulse at ramp index 5, the topmost level 7. Nothing else writes it and nothing reads it outside fdps_draw_scene_layer; the initial value is 0, giving ramp index 0 (level 2) for any drawing that happens before the first reset.

Pool: fdps  [all three referencing functions are game code and the value only feeds the game's scene renderer]

Rebuild note:
The advance lives in fdps_draw_scene_layer's prologue, so it ticks once per layer drawn, not once per frame. Hoisting it into the per-frame loop -- the natural home for an animation phase -- slows the pulse by the number of layers composited.

=== 00060160 [PLATE]
Which frame the two-frame scene tile animation is currently showing: 0 or 1.

Only fdps_draw_scene_layer touches it. Near the top of that function it compares the global tick counter at 00069d64 against the latch at 00060164 and, when more than 3 ticks have elapsed, flips this value with XOR 1 and re-latches the tick, so the animation advances on the tick clock rather than once per drawn layer. Later, for any tile whose attribute flag byte (tile_attr[tile * 4]) has low three bits equal to 1, this value is added to the tile index, so the tile alternates between its base graphic and the next one in the tileset. Values are 0 and 1 only: the image initialises it to zero and the sole write flips bit 0. Tiles flagged 2 use the separate four-frame animation derived directly from 00069d64 and never read this.

Pool: fdps  [its only two references are in the game's scene renderer fdps_draw_scene_layer; referencing_pools is fdps alone]

=== 00060164 [PLATE]
Tick at which the two-frame scene tile animation phase was last flipped.

Written and read only by fdps_draw_scene_layer, which owns the whole two-frame tile animation. On the first draw the value is still its image zero, and the function latches the current global tick counter DAT_00069d64 into it. On every later draw it subtracts the latch from the live tick and, when the gap is more than 3 ticks, inverts the phase byte DAT_00060160 with XOR 1 and re-latches the current tick. DAT_00060160 is then added to the tile index of every tile whose attribute flag byte has 1 in its low three bits, so those tiles alternate between two adjacent frames in the tileset roughly every 4 ticks.

The value is a timestamp on the tick counter's own scale, not a frame count of its own: it takes whatever DAT_00069d64 holds and nothing else. Zero is the not-yet-latched sentinel and is only ever seen before the first scene is drawn -- nothing resets it afterwards. The comparison is unsigned. Because fdps_draw_scene_layer runs once per layer rather than once per frame, whichever layer is drawn first past the threshold performs the flip and the remaining layers of that frame see the already-flipped phase, so all layers stay in step.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps code reaches it -- its sole referencing function is the game's scene renderer, and it gates a game-side animation phase byte in the same block of scene globals]

Rebuild note:
The phase is latched, not derived. Writing it as a function of the tick -- the shape the same function uses for its four-frame animation, ((DAT_00069d64 >> 2) & 3) -- looks equivalent and is not: this latch only advances while a scene is actually being drawn, so ticks that elapse while no scene is drawn are swallowed and the first draw after a pause flips the phase immediately, whereas a derived phase would have kept running.

=== 00060168 [PLATE]
Rotation position deciding which of a unit's active status-effect icons is drawn on the battle map.

fdps_draw_map_unit is the only code that touches it. Once per frame tick -- when the tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from the latch DAT_00069d18 -- that routine steps the icon sub-counter DAT_00069d1c modulo 0x19, and every time that sub-counter wraps to 0 it increments this counter, so it advances once every 25 ticks. It is then handed to fdps_unit_select_status_icon(unit_index, this) in the sprite pass; that routine reduces it modulo the number of non-zero status-effect timer bytes in the unit record (offsets 0x23, 0x22, 0x24, 0x25, 0x27) and returns the slot to blit out of the IconSts.cel sheet at DAT_000643d4, or -1 when the unit carries none. Only the remainder matters, so the counter simply counts up without bound and is never reset or wrapped; every unit on the map shares it, each rotating through its own set of effects. Its initial value is 0 (initialised data), and the divide in fdps_unit_select_status_icon is signed, so a negative value would yield no icon for most remainders -- in practice it only ever increments from 0.

Pool: fdps  [read and written only by fdps_draw_map_unit, and it feeds a game routine that indexes the 0x50-byte unit record]

=== 0006016c [PLATE]
Left pixel column of the terrain-info HUD panel: 0x19 (left of screen) or 0x124 (right of screen).

Only fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel touches it.
