=== 00061434 [PLATE]
The 387 emulator's scratch source operand: one 80-bit extended real, ten packed bytes, holding the operand of the instruction currently being emulated in the emulator's own working format.

Private to FUN_0004ec3c, the Watcom emu387 ESC-opcode interpreter, and never reached by address: the interpreter sets LEA EBP,[0x613c8] once per entry (0004eca2) and works its whole data run off that base, so this object is always addressed as EBP+0x6c. Every writer fills the same three fields -- significand low dword at +0, significand high dword at +4, sign and biased exponent word at +8. The memory-operand arms widen into it: FUN_00050b8a from a 32-bit float (0004efbb on), FUN_0005097e from an integer with the 16-bit form arriving sign-extended through CWDE at 0004f556 (0004f16a on), FUN_000509c4 from a 64-bit double in EAX:EDX (0004f2fa on), all with LEA EDX,[EBP + 0x6c] as the destination. It is then passed to the extended-real kernels FUN_00050352, FUN_00050360, FUN_00050794, FUN_000505bf and the comparison FUN_00050526 as the operand opposite the register slot at [EDI + EBP*0x1 + 0x1c]; the reversed instruction forms pass this object first instead, LEA EAX,[EBP + 0x6c] at 0004f039, 0004f077, 0004f207, 0004f3ab and 0005007c. Two arms fill it from inside the emulator rather than from memory: 0004f8f6 copies the constant L$1_emu387_ftst_zero in as FTST's comparand, and 0005002c copies the current register slot in before the shorter store formats run.

It is not part of the emulated 387 state, and that is what makes it a variable of its own rather than a field of the block below it. Three independent copies in this same function all stop exactly at this address and none crosses it: FLDENV and FSTENV move MOV ECX,0x7 then MOVSD.REP, 28 bytes (0004f0e7, 0004f145); FRSTOR and FSAVE move those 28 and then loop MOV ECX,0x8 times over MOVSD/MOVSD/MOVSW, 28 + 8*10 = 108 = 0x6c bytes (0004f4d2-0004f510, 0004f519-0004f53b); and the SIGFPE shim saves the emulator's state across the user handler with SUB ESP,0x6c and MOV ECX,0x1b / MOVSD.REP, again 27 dwords = 0x6c bytes, restoring the same width afterwards (0004ee5b-0004ee6e, 0004ee85-0004ee8f). The emulator's own notion of its state is therefore 000613c8..00061433 -- the 28-byte protected-mode environment image plus the eight 10-byte slots of L$N_emu387_register_stack -- and this scratch begins one byte past its end. Nothing preserves it, which is consistent: it is dead between instructions. The object after it, at 0006143e = EBP+0x76, is the precision-rounding continuation the arithmetic arms jump through.

Pool: crt  [FUN_0004ec3c, the emulated-coprocessor interpreter of the Watcom library, is the only function that reaches it; no game or AIL code does]

Rebuild note:
Declare it as ten packed bytes. Watcom's long double on x86 is the 8-byte double (FLOAT.H sets LDBL_MANT_DIG 53), so a floating declaration is two bytes short; and writing the +0/+4/+8 accesses as the natural struct of two dwords and a word pads to 12 under default alignment, which runs past 0006143d and clobbers the continuation pointer that every JMP dword ptr DS:[EBP + 0x76] jumps through. It also has to stay a separate object from the state block, laid down immediately after the register file and immediately before that continuation pointer: folding it into the state so the emulated FSAVE and the SIGFPE shim copy it too would write 118 bytes where the emulated instruction promises the user a 108-byte image.

=== 0006143e [PLATE]
Address of the routine that rounds each emulated x87 result to the precision the emulated control word selects; every arithmetic arm of the emulator tail-jumps here when it is done.

Written only by the FLDCW arm of the Watcom 80387 emulator FUN_0004ec3c. At 0004f10e the freshly loaded control word is masked with 0x300 -- the precision-control field, bits 8-9 -- and one of three code addresses is stored: 0x300 (64-bit extended) stores FUN_0004ec3c, the emulator's own dispatch entry, so nothing is rounded and the jump simply resumes the instruction-fetch loop; 0x200 (53-bit double) stores FUN_0004edac, which rounds the top register's significand to 53 bits (round-to-nearest-even carry into [EBX+4], then AND the low dword with 0xfffff800) and jumps to 0004ec3c; anything else (24-bit single) stores FUN_0004ed70, which rounds to 24 bits (AND the high dword with 0xffffff00, zero the low dword, carry into the exponent word at [EBX+8]) and likewise jumps to 0004ec3c. Read by 44 sites, all of them the same instruction JMP dword ptr DS:[EBP + 0x76] closing an arithmetic arm of FUN_0004ec3c -- 0004efd3, 0004f02a, 0004f182, 0004f7c8, 0004fe66, 000502b5 and the rest. EBP is the emulator's state-frame base, set by LEA EBP,[0x613c8] at 0004eca2 and 0004ed2d, so this is the frame's +0x76 slot, sitting immediately above the 10-byte scratch extended real at 00061434 and below the __hook387 flag at 00061444. Its initial image is four zero bytes; it becomes usable only after a control word has been loaded.

Pool: crt  [FUN_0004ec3c is the only function that reaches it and is the EMU387 80387 emulator, whose other file-statics this run already named L$N_emu387_control_word, L$N_emu387_register_stack, L$1_emu387_tag_field_masks]

Rebuild note:
All 44 reads are an indirect JMP, not a CALL, and at 64-bit precision the slot holds the dispatcher's own entry rather than a null "no rounding needed" marker. Ghidra prints the reads as (*DAT_0006143e)(), which invites writing a call followed by more code, or a null check around it; control never returns to the instruction after the jump, and a null check would break the extended-precision path.

=== 00061444 [PLATE]
Flag recording that __hook387 installed the 80x87 emulator itself, by taking over interrupt 7 and setting the EM bit in CR0, rather than through the Windows 386 enhanced-mode emulator interface.

__hook387 sets it to 1 at 00051b15, on its DOS/4G path only: after INT 2Fh AX=1600h finds no Windows and DPMI INT 31h AX=0A00h resolves "RATIONAL DOS/4G", it installs __int7 on vector 7 via _dos_setvect, sets byte +0x3e of the extender block passed in ES:EBP to 1 and ORs 0x04 (EM) into byte +0x40 of it, sets EM in the live CR0, and issues INT 21h AH=30h so the extender picks the change up. That path then returns 0; the Windows path returns 1 and sets the sibling flag has_wgod_emu (00061445) instead, so at most one of the two is ever set. __unhook387 reads it at 00051b54, but only once has_wgod_emu has tested clear: non-zero means undo exactly those edits -- restore byte +0x3e to 0, clear bit 2 of byte +0x40 and of CR0 with AND 0xfb, INT 21h AH=30h -- and zero means the emulator was never hooked this way and teardown does nothing. The only value ever stored is 1; neither routine clears it back to 0. Reached only through __sys_fini_387_emulator@00044629, which calls __unhook387 on two mutually exclusive branches selected by _Extender (0006044e).

Pool: crt  [file-static of the Watcom runtime object hook387.obj; only __hook387 and __unhook387 reference it]

=== 00061445 [PLATE]
Flag: nonzero once the 80x87 emulator has registered itself with the Windows 386 enhanced-mode VMM through the INT 2Fh AH=FAh emulator interface.

__hook387 (00051a56) writes 1 here at 00051a97, on the Windows path only: after INT 2Fh AX=1600h reports enhanced mode and the AH=FAh handshake returns AX=0x666 for AL=00h and AX=0 for AL=22h, it sets this byte and then issues AL=1Eh with ESI pointing at the emulator's registration block at 0x6a308, followed by AL=20h with CS, and returns AL=1. The DPMI / DOS-4G path taken when Windows is absent -- DPMI INT 31h AX=0A00h, _dos_setvect(7, __int7), CR0 EM bit set -- leaves this byte at 0 and sets the sibling flag at 00061444 instead, so at most one of the two is ever set. __unhook387 (00051b27) tests this byte first, at 00051b2b: nonzero means de-register with INT 2Fh AH=FAh AL=21h (CS in DX) then AL=1Fh, return AL=1 and never look at 00061444. That AL=1 is what tells __sys_fini_387_emulator (00044629) to skip the INT 7 vector restore at 000446a3. Values are only ever 0 or 1, and neither routine clears the byte back to 0.

Pool: crt  [reached only by __hook387 and __unhook387, both Function ID hits on EMU387.LIB hook387.obj; a module file-static with no PUBDEF of its own]

=== 00061448 [PLATE]
Initial x87 control word image (0x127F) that the Watcom CRT loads into the FPU at startup.

Supplied by CLIB3S's 8087cw.obj as a 2-byte _DATA object; no code in FDPS.LE writes it, so 0x127F is the only value it ever holds. __init_8087 (00044710) reads it with MOV AX and passes it to __init_80x87 (00051b7e) on the real-hardware path. __sys_init_387_emulator (000444a4) takes the emulator path: FINIT, then FLDCW word ptr [__8087cw], then four FLDZ to prime the register stack. Bit meaning of 0x127F: bits 0-5 = 0x3F, all six numeric exceptions masked; bit 6 set (legacy 8087 reserved bit); bits 8-9 = 10b, precision control 53-bit double, NOT the 64-bit extended precision the FPU defaults to after reset; bits 10-11 = 00b, round to nearest; bit 12 set, legacy infinity control.

Pool: crt  [PUBDEF __8087cw in CLIB3S 10.0a 8087cw.obj, image byte-identical; only CRT startup code reads it]

Rebuild note:
__8087cw comes from CLIB3S's own 8087cw.obj, pulled in by chk8087.obj's EXTDEF -- do not redeclare it in src/. Hand-writing it with the obvious x87 reset default 0x037F instead of 0x127F leaves the FPU in 64-bit extended precision and silently changes the rounding of every floating-point computation.

=== 0006144c [PLATE]
Function pointer to the routine that saves the 8087 register file into a caller-supplied buffer; the save half of the Watcom CLIB save8087 module's save/restore vector pair (__Rest8087 at 00061450 is the other half).

Lives in initialised _DATA and is linked in already pointing at the module's private one-byte RET stub at 00051b7d (_do_nothing in save8087.obj), so calling through it is harmless before anything installs a real handler. __init_8087 (00044710) rewrites it: when the real-coprocessor flag __real87 (00060395) is non-zero it stores 000446ff -- MOV EAX,[ESP+4]; FSAVE [EAX]; WAIT; RET -- and stores the matching FRSTOR stub 00044708 into __Rest8087, then calls __init_80x87 with __8087cw. With no coprocessor (emulator only) both slots keep the do-nothing RET. The only consumer is spawnve (000556a9), which pushes a stack buffer at EBP-0x36 and CALLs dword ptr [0006144c] at 0005578b to park the FPU state before it builds the child command line, and calls through __Rest8087 at 000559ed to put it back afterwards. The callee takes one cdecl argument, a pointer to the save area; there is no NULL check anywhere on the call path.

Pool: crt  [PUBDEF32 __Save8087 at offset 0 of the _DATA segment of CLIB3S.LIB save8087.obj; every reference is CRT code.]

Rebuild note:
This pointer is initialised data, not BSS, and its initial value is load-bearing: spawnve calls through it unconditionally with no NULL test. Writing the obvious `void (*__Save8087)(void *) = NULL;` makes any spawn on a machine without a real coprocessor jump to 0. The original initialiser is the address of a private one-byte RET stub in the same module, so a hand-written replacement must supply that stub and point at it rather than at NULL.

=== 00061450 [PLATE]
Function pointer through which the Watcom C runtime restores the 80x87 state that __Save8087 (0006144c) saved: the restore half of save8087.obj's save/restore vector pair.

Defined by CLIB3S 10.0a save8087.obj as the second of the two dwords in its 8-byte _DATA segment -- __Save8087 at offset 0, __Rest8087 at offset 4 -- and initialised by that object's own fixups to its file-static _do_nothing, the bare RET at 00051b7d. __init_8087 (00044710) is the only writer: when the x87-presence byte at 00060395 is non-zero it stores the FRSTOR stub at 00044708 here and the matching FSAVE stub at 000446ff into __Save8087 on the next instruction, then calls __init_80x87 (00051b7e). The two stubs are chk8087.obj's file-statics __rest_8087 (MOV EAX,[ESP+4]; FRSTOR [EAX]; RET) and __save_8087 (MOV EAX,[ESP+4]; FSAVE [EAX]; WAIT; RET). With no coprocessor both slots keep the do-nothing RET, so the save/restore pair costs nothing; nothing ever writes the slot back, and no caller null-checks it because it is never zero. The only reader is spawnve (000556a9), which calls __Save8087 at 0005578b to bank the FPU state before building the child process command line and calls through this slot at 000559ed to put it back afterwards. The argument both halves take is a pointer to the 108-byte 32-bit FNSAVE image; in spawnve's frame that is the local buffer at EBP-0x36, running to EBP+0x36.

Pool: crt  [PUBDEF __Rest8087 at _DATA+4 of CLIB3S 10.0a save8087.obj; the writer is chk8087.obj and the sole reader is spve.obj, both CLIB3S -- no game or AIL code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
__Rest8087 is initialised at link time to save8087.obj's do-nothing RET, not to null. Declaring it in src/ as a plain `void (*__Rest8087)(void *);` lands it in _BSS as null, and on a machine with no coprocessor -- where __init_8087 never overwrites it -- spawnve's unguarded CALL dword ptr [__Rest8087] transfers to address zero. It belongs to a CLIB3S library object and should not be redeclared at all.

=== 00061454 [PLATE]
Pointer to the CRT's environment vector: environ[0..n-1] are "NAME=value" strings and environ[n] is NULL.

Written only by __setenvp (00054f86), which the C startup runs before main. It first tests this variable against zero (00054f8d CMP dword ptr [environ],0x0 / JNZ) and does nothing if it is already set, so the table is built exactly once. Otherwise it loads the DOS environment block through the far address in _Envptr/_Envseg (00060451/00060455) -- FS gets the selector, the block is a run of NUL-terminated "NAME=value" strings ended by an empty string -- allocates one block holding the pointer table followed by copies of the strings, stores its base here, then fills one slot per string (offset advancing by 4 at 00055026) with the address of that string's copy, writes 0 into the slot after the last one at 0005502c, and zeroes the remaining reserved slots through the scratch pointer at 00061458. On allocation failure it leaves this NULL.

Read by getenv (000451a8), which returns 0 immediately if either this or the name is NULL and otherwise walks the slots until the NULL terminator comparing names; by __cenvarg (0005600f), which substitutes it when the caller's envp argument is 0; and by spawnl (00056502) and spawnvp (0004e1e9), which pass it as the envp of spawnve/spawnvpe so a child inherits the parent's environment. FDPS's own code never touches it.

Pool: crt  [environ is a PUBDEF of the linked Watcom 10.0a libraries and all five referencing functions are library functions -- the module that builds it, the one that searches it, and the three that hand it on to a child process]

Rebuild note:
The NULL value is load-bearing, not just an uninitialised pointer: __setenvp uses `environ == NULL` as its "not built yet" guard, so giving this variable any non-NULL initialiser -- for instance pointing it at a static empty vector so getenv is safe before startup -- makes __setenvp skip building the table and leaves the whole program with an empty environment.

=== 00061458 [PLATE]
Pointer to the per-entry allocation-flag byte array that runs alongside the C runtime's environ table; NULL until the table is built.

__setenvp (00054f86) is the only code in this image that touches it, and it runs once at startup, guarded by environ (00061454) still being NULL. __setenvp counts the n strings in the real-mode DOS environment block, copies them into one near-heap block, then makes a second _nmalloc of n*4 + 4 + n bytes: the first n*4 bytes are the environ pointer array, the next 4 are its NULL terminator, and the trailing n bytes are this mask. At 00055042 it stores environ + (n+1)*4 here, i.e. the first byte past the terminator, and immediately memsets those n bytes to zero, so every entry starts cleared. One byte per environ[i]: zero means environ[i] points into the single startup string block and must not be freed, nonzero means putenv/setenv replaced that entry with its own heap string which has to be freed before the slot is overwritten. Nothing reads it in this link -- putenv, setenv and clearenv are not linked in; the symbol is here only because wlink pulls in the whole of environ.obj for environ itself. It stays NULL on either allocation failure path, and stays NULL if __setenvp finds environ already set.

Pool: crt  [Watcom 10.0a CLIB3S.LIB, module environ, PUBDEF __env_mask at _DATA offset 4, four bytes after PUBDEF environ at offset 0 -- exactly the gap between 00061454 and this address]

=== 0006145c [PLATE]
The rule saying when daylight saving time begins, held in a struct tm whose fields the tzset code reuses as rule components.

__parse_tz (000521cd) fills it: after parsing the standard and daylight zone names it takes the first ',' clause of the TZ environment string and passes this address to L$N_tzset_parse_rule (000520c7); the second clause goes to __end_dst (00061480). __isindst (0005254b) reads the pair -- it calls FUN_0005250f (check_order in CLIB3S timeutil) with (__start_dst, __end_dst, tm_year) to learn which of the two falls earlier in the year, resolves each rule to a concrete date for that year, and sets tm_isdst on the struct tm handed to it. Field meanings inside the record are not the ordinary struct tm ones: tm_sec/tm_min/tm_hour (+0/+4/+8) are the wall-clock switch time, tm_mday (+0xc) is the week of the month 1..5 with 5 meaning 'the last one', tm_mon (+0x10) is the 0-based month, tm_wday (+0x18) is the weekday with 0 = Sunday, tm_yday (+0x1c) is the day of the year used by the J and n rule forms, and tm_isdst (+0x20) is the form flag -- 1 selects the tm_yday form, 0 the Mm.w.d form. tm_year (+0x14) is unused. The initialised image is the library's built-in US pre-2007 default M4.1.0 at 02:00 (first Sunday of April), matching timezone = 18000, __dst_adjust = 3600, daylight = 1 and tzname[0] = "EST" at 000614a4-000614b0.

Pool: crt  [only __parse_tz and __isindst touch it, both CLIB3S timeutil/tzset code, and __start_dst is a public symbol of the Watcom C library]

=== 000614a4 [PLATE]
Seconds that local standard time lags UTC -- the C library's `timezone`, positive west of Greenwich.

No instruction stores to it directly. __parse_tz (000521cd) is what sets it, indirectly: it hands this address and the tzname[0] buffer at 000614b0 to the zone-name-and-offset parser at 00051fb0, which writes the parsed standard offset here; the daylight clause of the TZ string is parsed into a stack temporary and only its difference from this value is kept, in __dst_adjust at 000614a8. If the TZ environment string is absent or unparsable the variable keeps its initialised value, 18000 = UTC-5, the library's built-in EST5EDT default that also seeds __dst_adjust = 3600, daylight = 1, tzname[0] = "EST" and the M4.1.0/M10.5.0 rules in __start_dst (0006145c) and __end_dst (00061480).

Readers: mktime (00051e12) adds it to the local seconds count to reach UTC and separately tests its sign (TEST/JLE at 00051f34) when deciding how to clamp a time that falls outside the representable range; _localtime (00045c29) subtracts it via __brktime, using this value for standard time and timezone - __dst_adjust when __isindst says the instant falls inside daylight saving time.

Pool: crt  [only _localtime, mktime and __parse_tz reach it, all CLIB3S time code, and `timezone` is a public symbol of the linked Watcom C library]

Rebuild note:
This lives in initialised data with the non-zero value 18000, and nothing in the program ever assigns it unless a parsable TZ variable is in the environment; declaring it uninitialised (or as `long timezone = 0;`) makes localtime and mktime run five hours away from the original on a machine with no TZ set.

=== 000614a8 [PLATE]
Daylight-saving adjustment in seconds: how much local time moves forward while DST is in effect.

Initialised to 3600 (one hour), the Watcom default that goes with timezone = 18000 and daylight = 1 at 000614a4 and 000614ac. __parse_tz writes it while parsing the TZ environment variable, as timezone minus the DST offset the TZ string gives; for "EST5EDT4" that is 5*3600 - 4*3600 = 3600. mktime reads it at 00051f07 and subtracts it from the assembled seconds only when the caller's struct tm has tm_isdst > 0 (the dword at +0x20). _localtime reads it at 00045c62 and passes timezone - __dst_adjust to __brktime as the effective offset when the timestamp falls inside the DST window; outside that window it passes timezone alone. A positive value means local clocks run ahead during DST; zero would mean the zone has no summer-time shift.

Pool: crt  [only __parse_tz, mktime and _localtime touch it, all CLIB3S tzset/time code; __dst_adjust is a PUBDEF of the linked Watcom libraries]

=== 000614ac [PLATE]
CRT timezone flag: non-zero when the active TZ setting names a daylight-saving-time zone.

Part of the Watcom timezone data block, which runs timezone (000614a4, seconds west of UTC), the DST adjustment (000614a8, seconds), this flag, the standard-time name buffer (000614b0, 31 bytes), the daylight-time name buffer (000614cf, 31 bytes) and the char *tzname[2] pointer pair (000614ee). The block's initial image is Watcom's default TZ "EST5EDT": timezone 18000, adjustment 3600, daylight 1, names "EST" and "EDT".

__parse_tz is the only writer. It clears this to 0 at 000521e3 before parsing the standard-time portion of the TZ string; if the string ends there it also empties the daylight-time name buffer and returns, leaving the flag 0. If a daylight-time name follows, it sets the flag to 1 at 0005221c and parses that name, then stores timezone minus the parsed DST offset into 000614a8. So the only values are 0 (no DST zone configured) and 1 (a DST zone is configured); it says nothing about whether a particular date is inside DST -- __isindst answers that, and it tests tzname[1][0] rather than reading this flag.

Nothing in FDPS.LE reads it: it exists because the C library publishes it for user code, and the game only reaches this block indirectly through localtime and mktime.

Pool: crt  [only __parse_tz touches it; it is the public 'daylight' variable of Watcom's <time.h>, and the whole surrounding block is library timezone state]

=== 000614b0 [PLATE]
Buffer holding the abbreviation of the local standard-time zone, the string tzname[0] points at. Watcom CLIB3S file-static 'stzone' of the tzset module.

The static initialiser is "EST" followed by NUL padding, the library default that goes with timezone (000614a4) = 18000 seconds and __dst_adjust (000614a8) = 3600. tzset (00051f6b) fetches the TZ environment string and hands it to __parse_tz (000521cd), which at 000521d7 pushes this buffer as the destination of the module's parse_offset helper at 00051fb0; that helper copies the leading alphabetic zone name out of TZ and returns the signed offset in seconds, which __parse_tz stores into timezone. The daylight-time counterpart is dtzone at 000614cf, filled by the second parse_offset call at 00052211-00052222; between the two calls __parse_tz sets daylight (000614ac) to 0 if TZ named no DST zone and to 1 if it did. Capacity is 30 characters plus the terminator.

No code in this image reads the bytes here directly. They are reached through tzname, the two-pointer array at 000614ee whose slots hold 000614b0 and 000614cf, so tzname[0] is always this buffer; __isindst (0005254b) reads the other slot at 00052556 and tests its first byte to decide whether a DST zone exists at all.

Pool: crt  [byte-identical to the _DATA image of the OMF module 'tzset' in WATCOM_10.0a CLIB3S.LIB, where it is the LOCSYM32 stzone at segment offset 0x54; only __parse_tz reaches it]

Rebuild note:
This buffer and dtzone are writable arrays, not string literals. Declaring tzname as char *tzname[2] = { "EST", "EDT" } compiles and looks right, but tzset would then have parse_offset write the parsed zone name into read-only literals. They must be two 31-byte char arrays with tzname initialised to point at them.

=== 000614cf [PLATE]
The daylight-saving zone name of the current TZ setting, the buffer that tzname[1] points at.

__parse_tz (000521cd) is the only writer. It scans the TZ environment string with the name+offset scanner at 00051fb0, first into the standard-zone buffer at 000614b0 with timezone (000614a4) and daylight (000614ac) = 0; if the string ends there it stores a NUL into byte 0 of this buffer (000521f9) and returns, leaving the DST name empty. Otherwise it calls the same scanner again with this buffer and a default offset of timezone - 3600, sets daylight = 1, and stores timezone minus the parsed daylight offset into __dst_adjust (000614a8). The reader is __isindst (0005254b), which does not touch the buffer directly: it loads tzname[1] from 000614f2 and tests its first byte, and an empty name makes it return 0 -- not in daylight time -- before it ever looks at __start_dst (0006145c) or __end_dst (00061480). _localtime (00045c29) and mktime (00051e12) reach that answer through __isindst. The buffer is 31 bytes, TZNAME_MAX + 1, and holds a NUL-terminated name; only byte 0 is cleared when the TZ string has no daylight part, so characters past the terminator can be stale. The initialised image is the library's built-in US default "EDT", matching "EST" at 000614b0, timezone = 18000 and __dst_adjust = 3600. The game never sets TZ, so that default is what the buffer holds for the whole run.

Pool: crt  [only __parse_tz and __isindst reach it, both CLIB3S tzset/timeutil code, and it is a file-static of the tzset module rather than a public library symbol]

=== 000614ee [PLATE]
The two time-zone name strings: tzname[0] is the standard-time abbreviation, tzname[1] the daylight-saving one.

Both slots are initialised at link time to point at the module's two 31-byte static buffers -- tzname[0] = L$N_tzset_stzone (000614b0, initially "EST") and tzname[1] = L$N_tzset_dst_zone_name (000614cf, initially "EDT"). Nothing in this program writes the array itself; __parse_tz (000521cd) rewrites the buffers in place from the TZ environment string, storing the standard name into 000614b0 and the DST name into 000614cf, and clears 000614cf to an empty string when TZ names no DST zone. __isindst (0005254b) reads tzname[1] and tests its first byte: an empty string there means "no daylight-saving rule", and the function returns 0 without consulting __start_dst / __end_dst. tzname[0] has no reader in this binary; only the initialiser touches it.

Pool: crt  [tzname is a public Watcom C library symbol declared in time.h; the only code that touches these bytes is CLIB3S tzset.obj's __parse_tz and __isindst.]

=== 000614f2 [EOL]
interior of the object at 000614ee

=== 000614f8 [PLATE]
The Miles AIL software mixer's variant selector: a 7-bit format mask that both mixer dispatchers rebuild from scratch on entry and then use, unscaled and unchecked, as the index into their own 128-slot dispatch table.

Written twice with two different encodings, and never read outside the mixer. AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample (00054564) builds the source-side mask for the inner mixing kernels at 00052a5c: bit0 = the DIG_DRIVER's output format at +0x18 is stereo (AIL format codes MONO_8=0, MONO_16=1, STEREO_8=2, STEREO_16=3), bit1 = the sample's own format at +0x34 is stereo, bit2 = that and flag 0x02 in the sample's flags at +0x38, bit3 = the sample is 16-bit, bit4 = unity volume (+0x40 == 0x7f) with centre pan (+0x44 == 0x40) and flag 0x01 set, which is the unscaled fast path, bit6 = anything else, which is the volume- and pan-scaled path, and bit5 = the 16.16 resample step differs from 1:1 by more than the tolerance in DAT_0006a008, so a pitch-shifting kernel is needed. Bits 0-4 and 6 are assembled in EAX and stored once at 000545cc; bit5 is ORed in afterwards at 0005463a. The same function then re-reads bits 1 and 3 at 0005460f and 0005461f, doubling the step words at 00061510 and 00061514 once for each, which converts a sample count into a byte count and is the direct confirmation that bit1 means stereo source and bit3 means 16-bit source. AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_format (00054765) instead builds the destination-side mask for the output converters at 0005285c, and the bit positions are not the same ones: bits 0-3 are the low nibble of the driver flags at +0x1c, bit3 is additionally forced on when driver flag 0x20 (split output buffer) is set, bit4 = stereo output, bit5 = 16-bit output, bit6 = the driver field at +0x64 is non-zero. Neither dispatcher null-checks the slot before the indirect call, so the mask only ever names a populated slot.

This dword is the first of the eight-dword mixer scratch block 000614f8-00061517 (source cursor, source end, destination cursor, destination end, fractional step, integer step, step+1) that AIL_internal_register_mix_globals (00054823) hands to the DPMI lock primitive at 0003cb01 as the literal linear range 0x614f8..0x61518, so that the mix kernels can touch it at interrupt time without faulting. It sits in initialised data with an image value of zero; nothing reads it before a dispatcher has written it.

Pool: ail  [only AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample, AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_format and AIL_internal_register_mix_globals reach it, all three ailv3.lib Function ID matches, and no game or CRT code touches the address]

Rebuild note:
The two dispatchers store mutually incompatible encodings in this one word -- stereo is bit1 for the mix-loop table but bit4 for the finalize table, 16-bit is bit3 versus bit5 -- so defining one set of flag macros for "the mixer flags" and using it on both sides indexes the wrong slot in one of the two 128-entry tables, and neither table null-checks before the indirect call. It must also stay the first object of the AIL mixer data module, because AIL_internal_register_mix_globals DPMI-locks the literal range 0x614f8..0x61518: the eight dwords have to be emitted contiguously and in this order or part of the interrupt-time scratch is left unlocked.

=== 000614fc [PLATE]
Source cursor for the low-level digital mixer: where inside the playing sample's PCM buffer the next mix pass starts reading.

AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample (00054564) sets it at 00054662 from the SAMPLE record it was handed -- start[current_buffer] + pos[current_buffer], where current_buffer is the 0/1 double-buffer index at sample+0x28, the buffer base pointers start[] are at sample+0x08 and the consumed-byte counts pos[] at sample+0x18. It is reloaded into ESI at 00054681 and passed that way to the mix loop selected out of the dispatch table at 00052a5c by data_ail_mix_flags (000614f8). That routine advances ESI; on return the caller writes ESI - start[current_buffer] back into pos[current_buffer] (000546b4) and compares ESI against the source end at 00061500 (000546b8) to decide whether this buffer is exhausted. The loop back-edge at 000546ed re-enters at 00054657, which recomputes this value from the SAMPLE record, so it carries no state between passes and is meaningless outside a mix call. Units are bytes whatever the sample width.

The mix routines take the cursor in ESI and do not read this location -- these two instructions are the only references to it in the program. It exists because it is one dword of the mixer's 32-byte parameter block 000614f8..00061518, which AIL_internal_register_mix_globals (00054823) DPMI-locks as a unit at 00054832 so the block stays resident for ISR-time mixing.

Pool: ail  [only AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample references it, and it sits inside the mixer module's locked data block alongside data_ail_mix_flags and the destination pointers]

=== 00061500 [PLATE]
Address one past the last byte of the digital sample data the mixer is currently consuming.

AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample writes it at the top of each mix pass, as the base of the active sample buffer plus that buffer's length ([ECX+EBX*4+0x8] + [ECX+EBX*4+0x10], EBX being the active buffer index held at [ECX+0x28]); the matching start cursor goes to data at 000614fc as base plus the saved play position ([ECX+EBX*4+0x18]). Every AIL_internal_mix_loop_* variant (0005389a through 0005452a) reads it as its source terminator: each begins CMP ESI,[this] / JNC ret, so the loop runs while the source cursor is strictly below it, and each iteration also checks the destination cursor EDI against the mix-buffer-end pointer at 00061508. On return AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample converts ESI back to a play position, then compares ESI against this pointer again to decide whether the buffer was drained: below means the mix buffer filled first and the sample buffer still has data, at or above means the sample buffer is exhausted and the driver moves on to the next one.

It is scratch shared by every voice: it is valid only for the duration of one dispatch call, and the loops take it from here rather than as a parameter because they are hand-written assembly entered by JMP through the mix dispatch table.

Pool: ail  [only the Miles AIL digital mixer reaches it; all 74 references sit in pool_ail functions]

Rebuild note:
The loops compare with JC/JNC, unsigned. Ghidra renders this as int, and a rewrite that copies that declaration gets a signed comparison against a flat-model address, which reverses the loop's exit test for any buffer allocated above 0x80000000. Declare it as a pointer (or at least unsigned).

=== 00061504 [PLATE]
Pointer to the start of the 32-bit mix accumulator (build) buffer the DIG mixing loops sum voices into.

AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample writes it at 00054644 from the driver record field at +0x50, just before it dispatches one sample into the mixer, and reads it straight back at 00054651 to prime EDI -- the running destination pointer that every AIL_internal_mix_loop_XX routine walks. The paired global at 00061508 receives this value plus the buffer length at +0x4c and is the limit each loop tests EDI against (CMP EDI,[0x61508]; JC back to the top). Each slot is a signed 32-bit accumulator: the loops do MOVSX EBP,AX then ADD dword ptr [EDI],EBP, stepping 4 bytes per mono output sample and 8 per stereo pair. The source side of the same pass is held by 000614fc (first sample byte, loaded into ESI) and 00061500 (one past the last). The value is scratch for a single mixing pass, always written immediately before it is read, and read nowhere else in the program.

Pool: ail  [its only two references are both inside AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample, and the buffer it points at is consumed solely by the AIL DIG mixing loops]

=== 00061508 [PLATE]
One past the last accumulator slot of the digital mixing buffer.

Written by AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample at 0005464c as the mix buffer base (stored alongside at 00061504) plus the buffer's byte length, taken from the +0x50 and +0x4c fields of the DIG driver state the dispatcher holds in EDI. It is rewritten at the head of every mix pass, before the dispatcher jumps into a mix-loop variant.

Read only as a loop limit. All 72 AIL_internal_mix_loop_XX variants and the dispatcher's own inner loop compare their destination cursor EDI against it with CMP/JC and stop when the cursor reaches it, the cursor advancing 4 bytes per mono sample or 8 per stereo frame. The slots it bounds are 32-bit signed accumulators that the loops sum into (ADD dword ptr [EDI],EBP), so the value is an address, never a count. It pairs with 00061500, the source end limit against which the same loops bound ESI.

Pool: ail  [only the Miles AIL digital mixer touches it -- the writer and all 73 readers are pool_ail mix functions.]

=== 0006150c [PLATE]
Fractional part of the digital mixer's source-advance step, held as a 0.32 fixed-point value: the low 16 bits of the 16.16 sample-rate ratio, pre-shifted left by 16.

Written only by AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample (MOV [0006150c],EAX at 00054607), which splits the 16.16 rate ratio it computed into an integer part -- scaled to bytes and stored as the two entries of the source-advance table at 00061510 (entry 0 = n, entry 1 = n+1) -- and this fraction. Every resampling loop in the mixer dispatch, AIL_internal_mix_loop_20 through AIL_internal_mix_loop_6f (00053c4e..0005453a), reads it once per output sample with ADD ECX,[0006150c], ECX being the running phase accumulator. The carry out of that 32-bit add is the "consume one extra source sample" bit: the plain-step loops fold it in directly with ADC ESI,[00061510], the stereo and 16-bit loops materialise it with XOR EBP,EBP / ADC EBP,EBP and then index ADD ESI,[EBP*4 + 0x61510]. The loops stop when the source pointer reaches data_ail_mix_source_end_ptr (00061500). A value of 0 means playback at exactly the whole-sample rate held in that table, i.e. no resampling drift.

Pool: ail  [every one of the 37 references is inside the Miles AIL digital mixer's sample loops and their dispatcher; no game or CRT code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
The fraction is stored pre-shifted (rate_frac << 16) so that plain unsigned 32-bit overflow of the phase accumulator IS the carry that advances the source one extra sample; rewriting it as a 16.16 step with an explicit `if (acc >= 0x10000)` test, or typing it signed, changes when that extra sample is taken. The integer part of the step is not in this variable either -- it lives in the two-entry table at 00061510, so the obvious `src += step >> 16` would always advance by zero.

=== 00061510 [PLATE]
Two-entry source-cursor advance table for the AIL software mixer's resampling kernels: how many source bytes to step for one output frame, entry [0] when the 16.16 fraction accumulator does not carry and entry [1] when it does.

AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample writes both entries at 0x0005462f-0x00054634, once per sample it serves, and only on the resampling path. It divides the sample's rate at [sample+0x3c] (clamped to at least 1) by the driver output rate at [drvr+0x14] to get a 16.16 step, stores the fractional half at 0x0006150c, puts the integer half in entry [0] and integer+1 in entry [1], then doubles both if bit 0x2 (stereo source) and again if bit 0x8 (16-bit source) is set in the mixer-variant word at 0x000614f8 -- so the entries are byte counts, not frame counts, and entry [1] is always entry [0] plus one whole source frame. It then sets bit 0x20 of that word, which selects a resampling kernel. When the step is within the tolerance held at 0x0006a008 of 1:1 the JBE at 0x000545d1 skips the whole block: neither entry nor the resample flag is written, the entries keep stale values, and the non-resampling kernel that runs instead never reads them.

The resampling kernels AIL_internal_mix_loop_20 through AIL_internal_mix_loop_6f read it. The stereo and 16-bit variants add the fraction at 0x0006150c into ECX, capture the carry with XOR EBP,EBP / ADC EBP,EBP and index the table: ADD ESI,[EBP*0x4 + 0x61510]. The mono 8-bit variants (loops 20, 21, 30, 31, 60, 61) fold the same choice into a single ADC ESI,[0x00061510], which is only equivalent because entry [1] is entry [0] plus one and their frame is one byte. Both entries are non-negative; the source cursor only moves forward, and the loops stop on the source end at 0x00061500 or the mix-buffer end at 0x00061508.

Pool: ail  [every reference is AIL mixer code, and the address lies inside 0x000614f8-0x00061518, the module-private data block AIL_internal_register_mix_globals DPMI-locks for interrupt-time use]

Rebuild note:
The two entries have to stay adjacent, in this order, as one 8-byte object. The resampling kernels reach the second one as [EBP*4 + &data_ail_mix_pitch_int_advance] with EBP the fraction-accumulator carry, so declaring them as two separate variables -- which FD2's alt-labels ail_mix_pitch_int and ail_mix_pitch_int_plus_one invite -- lets the toolchain pad or reorder them apart, and the mixer then steps the source pointer by whatever happens to follow the first dword. The result is corrupted audio, not a crash.

=== 00061514 [EOL]
interior of the object at 00061510

=== 00061518 [PLATE]
__EFG_printf -- the printf-side installable floating-point formatting hook of the Watcom C library: one function pointer through which formatted output reaches the %e/%f/%g conversion routine.

It is a two-slot pointer pair with __EFG_scanf at 0006151c, laid down by CLIB3S module noefgfmt, which initialises both slots to its own fatal-error stub FUN_00054b3b -- the routine that prints "Floating-point support not loaded" (00063698) through __fatal_runtime_error at 0004e219 and exits with status 1. When floating-point support is actually linked in, the startup initialiser FUN_0004cfc8 (CLIB3S setefg, __setEFGfmt), run from the C runtime's XI table, overwrites this slot with _EFG_Format at 00054c0f and the neighbouring slot with __cnvs2d at 00054d43. In this image that overwrite happens, so at run time the slot holds _EFG_Format and the no-support stub is never reached. The only reader is float_format at 0004ca19, prtf's trampoline for the 'e'/'E'/'f'/'F'/'g'/'G' conversions, which forwards its three arguments unchanged with CALL dword ptr [0x00061518] and returns the hook's result. Values are code addresses only; there is no sentinel and the slot is never null.

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S _DATA from noefgfmt, written by setefg and called by prtf; the one AIL reference at 00054828 pushes this address as the exclusive END bound of the DPMI lock range 000614f8..00061518 over AIL's own mixer state, so it does not touch these bytes at all]

Rebuild note:
The initial value is the no-support stub, not _EFG_Format and not zero. Defining this as a plain uninitialised pointer, or pre-setting it to _EFG_Format, throws away Watcom's link-float-support-only-if-referenced mechanism: the stub-initialised pair is what makes a build without floating-point conversion print a diagnostic instead of calling through a null pointer, and __setEFGfmt is what installs the real routine. Take both slots from the real CLIB3S rather than hand-writing them.

=== 0006151c [PLATE]
Function-pointer hook holding the scanf-side string-to-double converter.

The image initialises it to _no_support_loaded@00054b3b, the CLIB3S noefgfmt stub that prints "Floating-point support not loaded" and calls __fatal_runtime_error@0004e219. At startup __InitRtns walks the CRT initialiser list in .object2 and calls __setEFGfmt@0004cfc8, which overwrites this slot with __cnvs2d@00054d43 and the neighbouring __EFG_printf at 00061518 with _EFG_Format@00054c0f; that initialiser entry is present only because the program pulls in fltused, i.e. because it actually uses floating point. The only reader is scan_float@0004d960, which at 0004dc0b calls through the slot as void __cdecl (char *str, double *result) -- the collected numeric text and the destination double -- to service the %e/%f/%g conversions of __scnf, then tests the conversion flags at [ESI+0x10]. The slot is never null: it holds either the real converter or the fatal-error stub. Its printf-side twin is __EFG_printf at 00061518, written by the same routine.

Pool: crt  [PUBDEF of CLIB3S module noefgfmt, written by CLIB3S setefg and read by CLIB3S scnf; no game or AIL code touches it.]

Rebuild note:
The initial value is a live code pointer, not padding and not zero. Declaring this slot uninitialised, or initialising it straight to __cnvs2d, both diverge: the first turns a scanf("%f") in a program without float support into a call through a null pointer instead of the "Floating-point support not loaded" diagnostic, the second links the converter unconditionally and defeats Watcom's link-float-support-only-if-referenced mechanism. It also lives in writable initialised data despite the CONST/_DATA block name -- putting it in a read-only segment faults at startup when __setEFGfmt stores to it.

=== 00061520 [PLATE]
Watcom WVIDEO debugger-present flag: non-zero while the program runs under the Watcom debugger, zero otherwise.

Nothing inside FDPS.LE ever writes it. It sits in _DATA initialised to zero and is meant to be set from outside the image by the WVIDEO debugger when it loads the program. Its only reader is __EnterWVIDEO (FUN_00054f26), which tests it with CMP byte ptr [__WD_Present],0 at 00054f26: when it is non-zero the function marshals the caller's 16:32 far message pointer (selector from arg 2, offset from arg 1) and issues the debugger's INT 3 / inline 'WVIDEO' signature trap, returning 1; when it is zero it returns 0 and its caller __fatal_runtime_error (0004e219) falls back to the ordinary runtime-message path. Only two values exist for the code: 0 = no debugger attached, anything else = attached. In a normal run of the shipped executable it stays 0, so the WVIDEO branch is dead at run time.

Pool: crt  [PUBDEF __WD_Present at offset 0 of the 1-byte _DATA segment in CLIB3S enterdb.obj -- the same object whose _TEXT byte-matches __EnterWVIDEO]

=== 00061524 [PLATE]
Maximum number of significant digits the MATH387S ftos module will emit when formatting a floating-point value; a file-static of that module, initialised by the library to DBL_DIG + 2 = 17.

Written only by _SetMaxPrec (00055063), which stores its single int argument here and returns; that public entry point has no caller in this image. Nothing in this image reads it -- ftos.obj was pulled in for _FtoS (000551f3) and wlink links whole objects, and in Watcom 10.0a's ftos.obj the local MaxPrec is the target of exactly one fixup, the store in _SetMaxPrec. Values are a digit count: 17 is the library default, a smaller value would cap the digits _FtoS produces.

Pool: crt  [file-static _DATA item of MATH387S.LIB module ftos, whose _TEXT lands at 00055063-00055443; the game never touches it]

Rebuild note:
Four initialised bytes with no reader anywhere in the image look like slack between the CRT gate byte at 00061520 and the __dospawn EXEC parameter block at 00061528, but they are a live library static holding 17. This storage comes from MATH387S.LIB; do not re-declare it in src/, and do not treat its 11 00 00 00 as padding to be dropped or reused.

=== 00061528 [PLATE]
The Watcom C library's static DOS EXEC parameter block: the four far pointers (environment, command tail, FCB1, FCB2) plus the two child-state slots that INT 21h AH=4Bh takes in ES:EBX.

Written in full by __dospawn (000561db) on every spawn, then handed to DOS: 000561ed..00056223 store the caller's envp and cmd_tail as 32-bit offset plus 16-bit DS selector pairs and zero both FCB pointer pairs, 00056243 loads the block address into EBX, and 0005626b issues MOV AH,0x4b / INT 0x21 with AL = 4 (P_NOWAIT, mode == 1) or AL = 0. Nothing else in the image reads or writes it. Layout, packed with no padding: +0x00 dword env offset, +0x04 word env selector, +0x06 dword command-tail offset, +0x0a word command-tail selector, +0x0c dword / +0x10 word FCB1, +0x12 dword / +0x16 word FCB2, +0x18 and +0x1c dwords for the child's SS:ESP and CS:EIP that DOS returns under the AL=1 load-only subfunction. __dospawn never uses AL=1, so those last two dwords are only ever zeroed. The FCB pairs are always zero as well: this library path never passes FCBs. The block is 32 bytes; the three save slots that follow it at 00061548 (ESP), 0006154c (SS) and 0006154e (DS) are a separate scratch area __dospawn uses to restore the stack after the INT, and together with this block they make up the whole 0x28-byte _DATA segment of spawn386.obj.

Pool: crt  [only __dospawn reaches it, and the 10.0a CLIB3S.LIB spawn386.obj SEGDEF32 records give _TEXT 0xd3 and _DATA 0x28, matching this function and this run of data exactly]

Rebuild note:
The block is byte-packed. Declaring it as the obvious C struct of pointer/selector pairs lets the compiler align each 16-bit selector to a 4-byte boundary, growing it from 32 bytes to 40 and shifting every field DOS reads; the child would be handed a garbage environment segment and command tail. It needs explicit packing (#pragma pack(1)) or a raw byte array with hand-written offsets.

=== 00061548 [PLATE]
The Watcom C library's save slot for the caller's ESP across a DOS EXEC call.

Written and read only by __dospawn (000561db), which saves the whole stack context immediately before issuing INT 21h AH=4Bh: 0005622f stores SS to 0006154c, 00056236 stores ESP here, 0005623c stores DS to 0006154e. After the INT returns at 0005626f..0005627c the three are reloaded in the order SS, ESP, DS, because a real-mode EXEC may hand control back on a different stack. The value is always a pointer into the CRT's own stack (the region above 0006a3c0) and is meaningful only between the save and the restore, a few instructions apart; it is never read by anything else and never inspected as a number. The slot is the second half of spawn386.obj's 0x28-byte _DATA segment: the EXEC parameter block occupies 00061528-00061547 and this save area 00061548-0006154f.

Pool: crt  [only __dospawn reaches it, and it sits inside the _DATA segment of CLIB3S.LIB spawn386.obj, whose SEGDEF32 sizes match this function and this run of data exactly]

Rebuild note:
The save has to be a fixed static, not a local. Writing the obvious C - keeping the saved SS:ESP in a local or letting the compiler hold it in a register - loses it, because after INT 21h AH=4Bh the stack pointer is not guaranteed to be the one that was in force when the value was stored, so the only place it can be read back from is an absolute address that does not depend on SS:ESP. The restore order (SS, then ESP, then DS) matters for the same reason and must not be rearranged.

=== 0006154c [PLATE]
The stack selector (SS) that __dospawn parks in static memory across a DOS EXEC call.

Written at 0005622f, in the prologue __dospawn runs just before issuing INT 21h AH=4Bh: SS goes here, ESP into 00061548 and DS into 0006154e. Read back at 0005626f, the first instruction after the INT returns, where MOV SS,[0006154c] is followed immediately by MOV ESP,[00061548] and MOV DS,[0006154e] to put the stack back. DOS's EXEC function does not preserve SS:SP or DS, and the save cannot live on the stack precisely because the stack is what is being restored, so the three slots are statics in spawn386.obj's _DATA rather than locals. The value is whatever selector the program was running on; it is never inspected, only stored and reloaded. Nothing else in the image touches this address.

Pool: crt  [only __dospawn reaches it, and it sits inside the 0x28-byte _DATA of CLIB3S.LIB spawn386.obj, the object the pool triage matched __dospawn to]

Rebuild note:
The save area must stay in static storage and be restored SS first, then ESP. Keeping SS/ESP in C locals or letting the compiler cache them is not merely slower, it cannot work: after the EXEC the stack pointer they would be read through is the thing that was lost. Because they are statics, __dospawn is not re-entrant either -- a spawn issued from a signal handler while another is in flight overwrites the outer call's stack registers.

=== 0006154e [PLATE]
The data selector (DS) that __dospawn parks in static memory across a DOS EXEC call.

Written at 0005623c, the last of the three saves __dospawn (000561db) makes just before issuing INT 21h AH=4Bh: SS to 0006154c, ESP to 00061548, DS here. Read back at 0005627c, the third instruction after the INT returns, completing the restore order SS (0005626f), ESP (00056276), DS (here); the POP DS / POP ES pair that follows at 00056283 unwinds the copies pushed at 0005622e-0005622f. DOS's EXEC preserves neither SS:SP nor DS, and the save cannot live on the stack because the stack is exactly what is being recovered, so all three slots are file-statics in spawn386.obj's _DATA rather than locals. The value is whatever selector the program was running on; it is stored and reloaded and never inspected. Nothing else in the image touches this address. These two bytes are the tail of that object's 0x28-byte _DATA: the EXEC parameter block occupies 00061528-00061547 and this save area 00061548-0006154f.

Pool: crt  [only __dospawn reaches it, and it is the last word of the _DATA segment of CLIB3S.LIB spawn386.obj, the object pool triage matched __dospawn to]

Rebuild note:
The DS save must be a module-level static and must be reloaded after SS and ESP, not before. Writing the obvious C - a local, or trusting the compiler to preserve the register - fails, because a local is itself read through the SS:ESP the EXEC may have changed; and being statics, the three slots make __dospawn non-re-entrant, so a spawn issued while another is in flight overwrites the outer call's registers.

=== 00061571 [PLATE]
The double 1.5 that the map AI multiplies a damaging spell's per-target score by when the target is the protagonist.

Read-only, and read by exactly one instruction: FMUL double ptr [0x00061571] at 00013bf3, in the damaging-spell branch of fdps_score_targets_for_spell. That branch scores one candidate target at 0x18 (24) when the cast would kill it -- current HP at unit record +0x40 below the spell's damage figure -- and at 8 otherwise; when the target's character index at unit record +0x08 is 0, which is 蘭迪斯, the score is pushed through FILD, multiplied by this 1.5, truncated back to an int by __CHP / FISTP and then accumulated, so 8 becomes 12 and 24 becomes 36 and the AI leans on the protagonist. Nothing writes it. Both possible products are exactly representable, so the truncation never rounds anything away.

Pool: binary_artifact  [an unnamed 8-byte floating-point literal the compiler pooled into the CONST segment: it sits unaligned at 0x61571, flush against the terminator of the string literal "REST.WAV" at 0x61568, with three bytes of align-to-4 filler before the literal "rb" at 0x6157c. In the rebuilt source it is the constant 1.5 written inline in fdps_score_targets_for_spell, not a declared global.]

=== 0006157c [PLATE]
The pooled string literal rb, the fopen mode for opening a file read-only in binary mode.

Nothing writes it; it lives in the CONST literal pool in .object2 among the resource filename literals (s_REST.WAV_00061568 below it, the wb mode literal at 00061580, s_OpWin.wav_00061584 above it). === 00061580 [PLATE]
The fopen mode string "wb" used to create the save file FDE.SAV.

Read-only, and reached by exactly one call site: the save arm of fdps_battle_system_submenu pushes it at 000152a4 as the mode argument of fopen("FDE.SAV", "wb"). That branch has already built the 0x59cb-byte save image in a malloc'd buffer from the game globals, stored the fdps_compute_save_checksum result at +0x59c7 and scrambled the whole buffer with fdps_xor_crypt_buffer; it then fwrites all 0x59cb bytes through this stream and fcloses it. The matching read side uses the separate literal "rb" at 0006157c, in the load arm of the same function and in fdps_load_and_draw_portrait. The "b" is load-bearing: the image is encrypted binary, so a DOS text-mode stream would expand every 0x0a byte in it to 0x0d 0x0a.

This is one of a run of pooled literals in the CONST segment -- "REST.WAV" at 00061568, the double 1.5 at 00061571, "rb" at 0006157c, this "wb", "OpWin.wav" at 00061584 -- each laid down at a 4-byte boundary with the gap filled by whatever the assembler had to hand (0x04 here, 0x3b after "rb"). The filler is not part of the string.

Pool: binary_artifact  [an anonymous string literal the compiler pooled into CONST, not a global the source declared; in the rebuilt source it is the "wb" written inline in fdps_battle_system_submenu]

=== 000615a8 [PLATE]
The printf format "%d" and its NUL: the 3-byte read-only string literal a number is formatted through when the caller asks for no fixed field width.

Read only by fdps_draw_number@00017530, and only on its digit_count == 0 branch, which does sprintf(buf, "%d", value) so the figure comes out at its natural width with no zero padding and no overflow guard. Every other branch of that function formats through the separate, mutable "%.Nd" template it copies onto its stack from binary_artifact_local_array_init_number_format_14854. Nothing writes here and nothing indexes it: the address is loaded as an immediate at 000175d0 and pushed as the format argument at 000175d5, and that is the whole of its use. The callers that take the digit_count == 0 branch with a literal 0 are fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up@0001dd30 and fdps_level_up_apply_stat_gain@0001e370, both drawing the numbers on the level-up panel. The byte at 000615ab is not part of this object: it is alignment fill up to the next literal ("+" at 000615ac) and holds leftover rather than zero, the same as the fill byte after the "OpWin1.wav" literal at 0006159c.

Pool: fdps  [reached only by game code, and the text is the game source's own format string; the byte-identical copy at 000617bc serves the other module that needs one, which is wcc386 pooling string literals per module]

Rebuild note:
In a rebuild this is a literal inside the sprintf call, not a named global -- giving it a symbol invents one the original never had. The behavioural trap is folding fdps_draw_number's two format branches into one sprintf(buf, "%.*d", digit_count, value): a precision of 0 applied to the value 0 prints nothing at all, so the level-up panel would show a blank where the original shows "0". Keep the plain "%d" branch separate from the "%.Nd" template.

=== 000615ac [PLATE]
The C string literal "+": two bytes, the plus sign and its NUL, used as the sign prefix on a drawn number.

Read only by fdps_draw_number@00017530, and only on the path where the caller's show-sign flag (the byte parameter at EBP+0x24) is set and the value is not negative. There the function first strcpy()s the already-formatted digits into a scratch buffer at EBP-0x40, then copies these two bytes over the head of the output buffer with a single MOV AX,[000615ac] / MOV word ptr [EBP-0x2c],AX -- wcc386's inline expansion of strcpy(buf, "+") for a two-byte literal -- and then strcat()s the saved digits back on, so "123" becomes "+123". Negative values never take this branch: sprintf has already written the '-' and the JGE at 000175ec skips over it, so no string ever gets "+-". The '+' that lands in the buffer is later turned into a glyph by the character switch at 0001766e, which maps '0'..'9' to 0..9, '+' to 10, '-' to 11 and '?' to 12, and then indexes the number font as data_fdps_number_glyph_color_row * 13 + that column.

Pool: binary_artifact  [an image of a source-level string literal that wcc386 laid down in the .object2 literal run and loads inline; the source declares no global for it. Every literal in this run starts 4-byte aligned -- "Status.cel" at 00061590, "OpWin1.wav" at 0006159c, "%d" at 000615a8, this one, "FACE.CEL" at 000615b0 -- with the gap to the next boundary left as uninitialised fill, which is why the two bytes at 000615ae..000615af read as the junk "X," and got swept into Ghidra's string definition for the neighbour.]

=== 00061660 [PLATE]

=== 0006168c [PLATE]
The pooled string literal "rb", the fopen mode for reading a file in binary mode.

Nothing writes it; it sits in the CONST literal pool in .object2 between s_RankUp.dat_00061680 and the four temp-file name literals it is always paired with. Three functions take its address, twelve references in all, and each of them uses it for the same four fopen/fread/fclose pairs: FMer1.tmp -> 0x4800 bytes at DAT_000653f0 and FMer2.tmp -> 0x1000 bytes at DAT_000643f0 on the way in, then Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp back into the same two buffers on the way out. Those are the 18-row brightness ramp table and the 16x16x16 RGB-to-palette-index cube: the FMer pair is the fight-screen palette written from Fight.pal, the Mer pair the map palette written from Fde.pal, both dumped by fdps_load_global_resources at startup. fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange and fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets swap the tables into fight mode and back around one blow; fdps_play_ending_credit_roll does the same around the credit roll. None of the three checks the fopen result.

A byte-identical "rb" lives at 0006157c for the module holding fdps_battle_system_submenu and fdps_load_and_draw_portrait; wcc386 pools string literals per object, so the same two characters appear once per module that needs them.

Pool: binary_artifact  [a compiler-emitted literal image, not a variable anybody declared; naming.md forbids a data_fdps_ name for a string literal, and in the rebuilt source this is the mode string written inline in each fopen call]

Rebuild note:
The 'b' is load-bearing. These four reads are fixed-size fread calls over binary palette tables; opening them with "r" instead puts the stream in DOS text mode, where CRLF pairs collapse and 0x1a is taken as end of file, so the 0x4800-byte and 0x1000-byte reads come up short and leave the blend tables partly stale. Nothing checks the return value, so the failure shows up as wrong colours rather than as an error.

=== 00061704 [PLATE]
The read-only string literal "M": the MISC.VFS clip-name prefix for a spell cast by a non-enemy unit.

Nothing writes it. Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- the single reference is inside fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets, and it sits in the CONST literal pool among that same code's strings, "Miss.wav" below and the four %s..saf formats above]

=== 00061708 [PLATE]
The pooled read-only literal "E", the clip-name prefix of the enemy-side family of spell animation clips in MISC.VFS.

Nothing writes it. One site reads it: fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets@0001a4c0, which takes the casting unit's 0x50-byte record from fdps_get_unit_record and tests its side code at byte +0x06. The %02d is the spell id, so an enemy casting spell 13 plays EB13.saf, EL13.saf, EE13.saf and ES13.saf while the same spell cast by a player unit plays the MB13/ML13/ME13 clips.

MISC.VFS ships the E family for spell ids 00, 01, 02, 05-09, 13, 23, 32 and 37 only (with ES13 the sole enemy S clip), against an M family that covers the whole id range: the spells enemies actually cast are a subset of the spells the party can cast, and the container is stocked accordingly.

=== 000617b0 [PLATE]
Read-only string literal "Turn.saf": the BaseAni.vfs member name of the turn-banner sign animation sheet.

Nothing writes it as data. Rebuild note:
Write the name as the literal "Turn.saf". === 000617bc [PLATE]
The pooled read-only literal "%d", the sprintf format both battle-display routines print a number with.

Nothing writes it. Two sites read it, and both are the format argument of sprintf (0x00042d41). fdps_draw_turn_number@0001ea80 prints the battle turn counter DAT_00069ce8 into an 8-byte stack buffer and then walks the resulting digits, painting each one as a composite sprite from the "Turn.saf" bank at a 28-pixel pitch. fdps_show_number_indicator@0001f510 prints its value argument -- damage taken, HP healed, MP restored or a stat gain -- into a 5-byte stack buffer that was pre-seeded with the four-space string at 0001c2cd, then queues the digits right-aligned into the four cells of the floating-popup queue at DAT_00064120 / DAT_000641e8 / DAT_000642b0.

Both callers depend on the conversion being plain "%d" with no width or padding: each re-runs strlen over the formatted buffer to decide how many digits there are -- the turn banner to know how many sprites to paint, the popup to right-align into its four cells by emitting a digit only while strlen(buffer) > 3 - cell. A width or zero-fill in the format would change the digit count and so change what both of them draw.

The literal is 3 bytes at 000617bc. 000617bf is a single leftover fill byte that aligns the next literal, "PLYPHASE.SAF" at 000617c0, to 4 bytes; Ghidra's auto-analysis string s_PLYPHASE.SAF_000617bf begins on that fill byte rather than on the literal.

Pool: binary_artifact  [a string-literal image wcc386 emitted into the CONST literal pool, not a variable the game declared; only game code reaches it, but naming.md keeps literals out of the data_fdps_ family]

=== 000617e8 [PLATE]
The pooled read-only literal "%d", the sprintf format fdps_draw_text prints an embedded number with.

Nothing writes it. One site reads it, as the format argument of sprintf (0x00042d41): in fdps_draw_text@0001ff60, the handler for token -6, the text-stream control code that means "insert a number here". It formats the pending number DAT_00064038 into a 12-byte stack buffer at EBP-0x3c, takes strlen of the result, and then paints the buffer one character at a time with fdps_draw_glyph, passing (character - '0') as the glyph index and advancing the cursor by a fixed 0x10 per digit rather than by the glyph advance DAT_0006044b.

That digit loop depends on the conversion being plain "%d" with no width, flag or padding: strlen decides how many glyphs get drawn, and every character it walks is turned into a glyph index by subtracting '0', so a space from a width specifier or a zero-fill would both change the count and feed fdps_draw_glyph an index the digit sheet does not have.

This is a distinct copy of the same two characters as binary_artifact_string_literal_decimal_format_617bc, which serves fdps_draw_turn_number and fdps_show_number_indicator; Watcom pools literals per translation unit, so the text appears once per module that uses it. The literal is 3 bytes; 000617eb is a 0x00 fill byte aligning "Chapter.saf" at 000617ec to a 4-byte slot.

=== 00061a04 [PLATE]

=== 00061b1c [PLATE]
The double 1.15 a unit's attack power is multiplied by while its attack buff is running.

Read-only, and read by exactly one instruction: FMUL double ptr [0x00061b1c] at 00024e41, in fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats. That function seeds an attack total from the unit record's base attack word at +0x37 and adds the ap modifier of every equipped inventory item; once the sum is complete it tests the buff timer byte at unit record +0x22, and when that byte is non-zero the total is pushed through FILD, multiplied by this 1.15, chopped back to an integer by __CHP / FISTP and stored as the unit's attack word at +0x48. A byte-identical 1.15 at 00061b24 does the same job for defense under the timer at +0x23. The timer bytes +0x22 .. +0x27 are the unit's six status timers, counted down one per turn by FUN_0001fa30, which re-runs this function when one hits zero so the buff drops back out of the stat. Nothing writes this constant.

Pool: binary_artifact  [an unnamed floating-point literal the compiler pooled into CONST: it sits in the run of string literals between "Sure.wav" and "OpWin1.wav", on the align-to-4 filler after the former, and the compiler emitted a separate identical copy at 00061b24 for the defense branch instead of sharing one. In the rebuilt source it is the constant 1.15 written inline in fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats.]

Rebuild note:
The buffed attack is a double multiply truncated toward zero, not a percentage in integer arithmetic. Writing ap = ap * 115 / 100, or rounding the product instead of chopping it, gives a different number for some attack values -- 1.15 is not exactly representable, and on the x87 with the default extended-precision control word every multiple of 20 lands just under the integer, so base attack 20 buffs to 22 and 100 buffs to 114, one lower than integer scaling gives. Keep it as (int)(total * 1.15) so the compiler emits the same FILD / FMUL / __CHP / FISTP sequence.

=== 00061b24 [PLATE]
The double 1.15 that scales a unit's defence total while its defence buff is running.

Read-only, and read by exactly one instruction: FMUL double ptr [0x00061b24] at 00024e5b, in fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats. That function sums a unit's base defence (the signed word at unit record +0x39) with the dp bonuses of its equipped items, and then, only when the status timer byte at unit record +0x23 is non-zero, pushes the total through FILD, multiplies it by this 1.15, truncates it back to an int with __CHP / FISTP and stores it as the defence word at record +0x4a -- the field fdps_draw_unit_status_panel prints highlighted while +0x23 runs. The byte at +0x23 is the defence-buff timer, one of the six status timers at +0x22..+0x27 that FUN_0001fa30 counts down one per turn, calling this function again when one hits zero so the multiplier drops back out. Its twin at 00061b1c is a byte-identical 1.15 used two instructions earlier for the attack total, gated on the attack-buff timer at +0x22. Nothing writes either copy.

Pool: binary_artifact  [an unnamed 8-byte floating-point literal the compiler pooled into the CONST segment, not a declared global: it is 4-aligned rather than 8-aligned, packed between the string literals "Sure.wav" at 0x61b0d and "OpWin1.wav" at 0x61b2c, and a second byte-identical copy exists at 0x61b1c -- one shared const double would have served both multiplies. In the rebuilt source it is the constant 1.15 written inline in fdps_unit_recompute_combat_stats.]

Rebuild note:
The multiply must stay double arithmetic with a truncating conversion. The nearest double to 1.15 is slightly below 1.15, so the obvious integer rewrite total = total * 115 / 100 disagrees with the original wherever the exact product is a whole number: a defence total of 20 gives 20 * 1.15 = 22.999999999999998 which __CHP chops to 22, while the integer form gives 23. Ghidra prints the conversion as ROUND(); 0x0003d4ec is __CHP and it chops toward zero, so the C must be an assignment to an integer, never a rounding call.

=== 00061c2c [PLATE]
The pooled string literal "rt": the fopen mode for opening an existing file for reading in text mode, with CR/LF translation.

Nothing writes it -- it is read-only literal-pool data in .object2, sitting between the "Please use install function.\n" message and the filename literal "Disk.no" at 00061c30. === 00061c38 [PLATE]
The pooled read-only literal "%s", the fscanf conversion main uses to read the tokens of the installation record file.

Nothing writes it. Three sites read it, all in main and all in the startup installation check, and all three are the format argument of fscanf (0x00043243). main first calls access("DISK.NO", 0) and aborts with the "please use install function" message if the file is missing; it then opens "Disk.no" in text mode (fopen with the "rt" literal at 00061c2c) and pulls three whitespace-delimited tokens out of it. The first two go to a 20-byte stack buffer and are discarded; the third is stored in the global string buffer at 000643e8, which later code uses as the installed-data location. fclose follows, the CD-ROM state global at 00069d54 is set to -1, and fdps_cdrom_detect decides whether the game may start.

All three reads are plain "%s" with no field width, so each stops at the first whitespace and writes as many characters as the token has; the second read overwrites the first in the same stack buffer, which is what makes the first two tokens throwaway.

The literal is 3 bytes at 00061c38. 00061c3b is a single leftover fill byte (0x8b) aligning the next literal, "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!", to the 4-byte slot at 00061c3c.

Pool: binary_artifact  [a string-literal image wcc386 emitted into the CONST literal pool, not a variable the game declared; only game code reaches it, but naming.md keeps literals out of the data_fdps_ family]

=== 00061c3c [PLATE]
String literal: "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!\a\n" -- the first line of the fatal message printed when the game cannot see its CD-ROM.

Read-only; nothing writes it. The sole reader is main, which calls fdps_cdrom_detect at 000292d7, sign-extends its 16-bit result and compares it with 1. Exactly 1 means the disc was found and execution continues at 0002930c with fdps_audio_init(0x19); any other value falls through to printf of this string, then printf of the follow-up literal at 00061c63+1 ("Check your CDROM please!!!"), then exit(1). The text carries no format specifiers; the 0x07 byte before the newline is a BEL that beeps the PC speaker as the message is printed. This is the second of the two startup gates, the first being the access("DISK.NO") installation check that prints the literals at 00061be8 and 00061c0c.

Pool: binary_artifact  [an anonymous string literal the compiler placed in CONST, reached only as an immediate address in main, not a global the game declares]

Rebuild note:
Re-emit the text byte for byte, including the '\a' before '\n' and the grammatical slip "is not install". Silently correcting the typo, or dropping the BEL because it looks like stray control data, changes what the player sees and hears when the disc check fails.

=== 00061c64 [PLATE]
The pooled read-only literal "Check your CDROM please!!!\n", the second line of the message printed when the game cannot find its CD-ROM.

Nothing writes it; it sits in the CONST literal pool of .object2 between the fatal-error headline at 00061c3c and the farewell literal at 00061c80. One site reads it: main@00029220, on the branch taken when fdps_cdrom_detect@0003c636 returns anything other than 1 (000292d7 CALL / CWDE / CMP dword ptr [EBP-0x8],0x1 / JZ 0002930c). That branch calls printf twice -- first with the "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!\a\n" line at 00061c3c, then with this one -- and then exit(1), so the process does not come back from it. === 00061dc0 [PLATE]
String literal "FMer1.tmp": the name of the on-disc cache file holding the 0x4800-byte palette-blend table built from Fight.pal, and the file whose mere existence tells the next startup that the whole four-file blend cache is already on disc.

Read-only, one function, two call sites, both in fdps_load_global_resources and both at the very end of startup after every VFS resource has been loaded:

  00029f9c  access("FMer1.tmp", 0) -- mode 0 is the existence check. A zero result (cache present) jumps to 0002a0ba, the read path; any non-zero result (cache absent) falls through to the generate path.
  00029fc6  fopen("FMer1.tmp", "wb") on the generate path, the mode being the literal at 00061dcc. It fwrites 0x4800 bytes from the buffer at 000653f0 -- the blend table fdps_build_palette_tables has just produced from the Fight.pal image at 000643e4 -- and fcloses it.

The generate path then writes three more files with the same template: FMer2.tmp (00061dd0) takes the 0x1000-byte table at 000643f0 from the same Fight.pal pass, and after a second fdps_build_palette_tables call on the Fde.pal image at 000643bc, Mer1.tmp (00061ddc) takes 0x4800 bytes from 000653f0 and Mer2.tmp (00061de8) takes 0x1000 bytes from 000643f0. The read path at 0002a0ba reads only Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp back into those same two buffers, with the mode literal "rb" at 00061df4. So the two buffers end up holding the Fde.pal tables either way, and FMer1.tmp and FMer2.tmp are never read by any code in the image -- this literal's live role is as the sentinel of the presence check, and its content is the Fight.pal half of the cache kept for its own sake.

Nothing deletes these files; they persist in the working directory between runs, which is what makes the check meaningful. The name is written in mixed case and the DOS file system is case-insensitive, so the on-disc entry is FMER1.TMP.

=== 00061dcc [PLATE]
The fopen mode string "wb" used to create the four palette-blend cache files.

Read-only, and reached by exactly one function: fdps_load_global_resources, in the cache-generate arm at the end of startup. That arm is taken when access("FMer1.tmp",0) returns non-zero, i.e. the cache is absent. It calls fdps_build_palette_tables on Fight.pal and writes the two resulting tables out -- fopen("FMer1.tmp","wb") + fwrite of 0x4800 bytes from 000653f0 at 00029fba, then fopen("FMer2.tmp","wb") + fwrite of 0x1000 bytes from 000643f0 at 00029ff6 -- then calls fdps_build_palette_tables again on Fde.pal, overwriting the same two globals, and writes those out the same way as "Mer1.tmp" at 0002a040 and "Mer2.tmp" at 0002a07c. Each file is closed immediately after its fwrite. The matching read side uses the separate literal "rb" at 00061df4, in the cache-present arm of the same function, which freads Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp back into the same two globals.

The "b" is load-bearing: the payload is a raw blend table, so a DOS text-mode stream would expand every 0x0a byte in it to 0x0d 0x0a and the cache would read back short and misaligned.

This is one of a run of pooled literals in the CONST segment -- "celFMer1.tmp" at 00061dbd, this "wb", "FMer2.tmp" at 00061dd0, "elMer1.tmp" at 00061dda, "LevMer2.tmp" at 00061de5, "rb" at 00061df4 -- each laid down on a 4-byte boundary with the gap filled by leftover text ('el' before this literal, 'm' after it). The filler is not part of the string.

=== 00061ddc [PLATE]

=== 00061de8 [PLATE]
String literal "Mer2.tmp": the name of the disc cache file for the 16x16x16 RGB-to-palette-index lookup cube built from Fde.pal.

Used at two sites, both in the closing block of fdps_load_global_resources, and nowhere else. That block decides once per run whether the colour tables have to be recomputed: access("FMer1.tmp", 0) at 00029f9c is the whole cache test, and its result selects one of two branches.

  Cache miss (FMer1.tmp absent). fdps_build_palette_tables runs twice, first over the Fight.pal image at 0x000643e4, then over the Fde.pal image at 0x000643bc. === 00061e3c [PLATE]
