=== 00064030 [PLATE]
Text entry id spliced in where a message carries the -4 substitution control code.

Written by every routine that is about to show a message with a name in it, immediately before the fdps_draw_text call: an item name id as item_id + 0xc9 (fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor, fdps_run_death_scripts, fdps_village_item_sell_loop) or a character name id as unit-record byte +0x08 or +0x07 plus 1 (fdps_shop_buy_loop, fdps_village_item_sell_loop, fdps_village_item_transfer_loop, fdps_village_member_equip_loop, fdps_church_promote_loop). Read only by fdps_draw_text, which on the -4 token recurses as fdps_draw_text(data_fdps_all_game_text_ptr @ 000643c4, this value, cursor, pitch, 0xd0, 0, 0x6d) and continues from the cursor that call returns -- so the value is an entry index into the global text block, not the caller's, and the substituted text always comes out in the standard message colours. The companion slot at 00064034 serves the -5 token and 00064038 the -6 integer, so a message can name two things and a number. No sentinel: the slot is never cleared, it just holds whatever the last publisher put there.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: the message text drawer and the shop, village, church and battle routines that publish a name for it]

=== 00064034 [PLATE]
Text-entry id substituted into a message at control code -5: the second name slot.

Written by whichever routine is about to draw a message that contains a -5 token, always as an index into the global text block: fdps_shop_buy_loop (item id + 0xc9, the item-name range), fdps_village_item_transfer_loop (item id + 0xc9), fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor (item id + 0xc9), fdps_church_promote_loop (class code + 0xa1, the class-name range). Read only by fdps_draw_text, which on token -5 calls itself on the global text block at 000643c4 with this id, in the fixed message colours 0xd0 / 0 / 0x6d rather than the caller's, and continues from the cursor that call returns. Its partner at 00064030 is the -4 slot, and 00064038 is the numeric slot the -6 token formats; the three are consecutive and belong together. No writer ever clears it, so it holds the last name published until someone publishes another.

Pool: fdps  [only game code touches it: fdps_draw_text plus the shop, village, church and battle message routines]

Rebuild note:
The slot is a file-scope global, written well before the draw call and never cleared, and fdps_draw_text reaches it from inside its own recursion rather than from a parameter. fdps_village_item_sell_loop publishes only the -4 slot and draws its refusal message with whatever this one still holds. Turning the substitution ids into arguments of fdps_draw_text, or zeroing them after each message, changes what those messages render.

=== 00064038 [PLATE]
The numeric operand of the message system's text substitution -- the number that escape -6 prints into a message string.

Written by whichever routine is about to show a message containing a figure, then read out of band by fdps_draw_text: when its escape dispatch meets -6 it does sprintf(buf, decimal format at 000617e8, this value) and draws the resulting digits one at a time, 0x10 pixels apart. It is the third of the three substitution slots -- escapes -4 and -5 take text entry ids from data_fdps_dialog_last_action_text_id_param and data_fdps_dialog_subst_text_id_2, escape -6 takes this number.

Writers, and what the number means in each: fdps_shop_buy_loop stores the item's price (word +0x13 of the ITEM.DAT record), then subtracts three quarters of the trade-in item's price from it in place, so the slot ends up holding the balance owed -- positive means the player pays and it is compared against the party gold total at 000643a4, zero or less means the shop pays and the routine negates the slot before adding it to gold. fdps_village_item_sell_loop stores price*3/4, the sell offer, and adds it to gold once the message is dismissed. fdps_church_promote_loop stages the promotion gains one line at a time -- movement (byte +1 of the promotion record), then the stat bytes at +1, +3, +5, +7 and +9 -- showing message 0x217 for each and adding the same value into the unit's fields at +0x3b, +0x37, +0x39, +0x3e, +0x40/+0x42 and +0x44/+0x46. fdps_battle_tick_status_effects stores maxHP/10 as the poison damage figure and passes it on to fdps_show_number_indicator. fdps_level_up_apply_stat_gain stores the rolled stat gain, hands it to fdps_draw_number, then adds it to the stat. fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor and fdps_run_death_scripts store a gold amount and add it to party gold after the message.

Signed 32-bit; negative values are meaningful (the shop uses the sign to decide who pays). Several readers take only the low word or low byte, because the value is being added into a short or char field of a unit record -- those are narrowing conversions, not a narrower variable.

Pool: fdps  [only game-logic functions reach it, and its whole role is the game's message and shop UI]

Rebuild note:
This has to stay a file-scope global written before the message call, not an argument passed to it. fdps_draw_text takes no numeric parameter -- it picks the value up from here when it hits escape -6 -- so folding the value into a local or an extra argument at any of the eight writers leaves the message printing whatever the previous writer left behind.

=== 0006403c [PLATE]
Width in pixels of one font cell; 16 for the whole run of the program.

Written once, by fdps_load_global_resources at startup, as part of the block of font and decoration metrics it publishes together: this width, the cell height at 0006403d, the drop-shadow column and row displacements at 0006403e and 00064042, the bytes-per-glyph stride at 00064046 and the outline-style flag at 0006404a. Nothing else ever writes it, so it is 0 from the CRT's _BSS clear until main calls fdps_load_global_resources and 0x10 afterwards. Read as a loop bound in the two glyph routines, re-read on every iteration: fdps_blit_glyph_1bpp walks this many columns per row, taking one bit of the 1bpp bitmap per column and a fresh source byte whenever the column index is a multiple of 8, so a row consumes ceil(width/8) bytes; fdps_draw_glyph fills this many bytes per row when it paints the background cell before the glyph. With height 16 the two make a 16x16 cell, matching the 0x20-byte per-glyph stride at 00064046.

Note that only the blitters read it: fdps_draw_text advances its cursor by a hardcoded 0x10 per glyph, so the pitch of a text line does not follow this value.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- the startup resource loader that sets it and the two glyph routines that read it; no CRT or AIL reference]

=== 0006403d [PLATE]
Height in pixels of one glyph cell of the game's 1bpp font.

Written once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which stores 0x10 here and 0x10 into the width byte data_fdps_glyph_cell_width immediately before it, giving the 16x16 cell the Chinese font sheet uses; nothing else writes it. Read as a zero-extended byte on every loop iteration by fdps_draw_glyph, as the row count of the background-fill loop that paints the cell before the glyph is drawn, and by fdps_blit_glyph_1bpp, as the outer loop bound over the glyph's source rows. It pairs with data_fdps_glyph_cell_width, which bounds the column loop in both functions; together they define the cell, and the font sheet's per-glyph stride is a separate global (00064046). The value is a pixel count and never approaches 0x80; a value of 0 would make both loops draw nothing.

Pool: fdps  [only game rendering code reaches it -- the two glyph blitters and the resource loader; no Watcom runtime or Miles object has a glyph renderer]

=== 0006403e [PLATE]
Horizontal offset, in pixels, at which fdps_draw_glyph places a glyph's drop shadow.

Set once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which stores 1 here as part of the font metric block it initialises before opening MISC.VFS (0006403c/0006403d glyph cell width and height, 00064042 the shadow's row offset, 00064046 the bytes-per-glyph stride of the 1bpp font sheet, 0006404a the decoration style flag, 0006404b and 0006404f the glyph advances). Nothing else writes it, so its value is 1 for the whole run.

Read only by fdps_draw_glyph, and only on the drop shadow path: when the style flag at 0006404a is zero and the caller passed a non-zero outline_color, the glyph is blitted once in that colour at dst + this value + (00064042) * pitch, i.e. one pixel right and one pixel down from the glyph body. When 0006404a is non-zero the function draws a 4-connected one-pixel outline instead and never looks at this variable. The value is a signed pixel displacement added to the destination pointer; positive means right.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_draw_glyph and fdps_load_global_resources reach it, and it is a font rendering metric of the game's own text engine]

=== 00064042 [PLATE]
Vertical displacement, in destination rows, of the drop shadow drawn under each glyph of the game's 1bpp font.

Written once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which stores 1 here and 1 into the column companion at 0006403e in the same straight-line block; nothing else in the image writes it. Read only by fdps_draw_glyph, and only on the branch taken when the outline-style flag at 0006404a is zero and the caller passed a non-zero outline_color: the glyph is blitted once in that color at dst + [0006403e] + this value * pitch, so with the startup values the shadow lands one pixel down and one pixel right of the glyph body, which is drawn on top of it afterwards. The value is a signed row count multiplied by the destination pitch, so a negative would lift the shadow above the glyph and zero in both offsets would hide it exactly under the body. When the outline flag is non-zero the four-way one-pixel outline path runs instead and this global is never read.

Pool: fdps  [both references are game code -- the glyph renderer fdps_draw_glyph and the resource loader fdps_load_global_resources; neither the Watcom runtime nor Miles contains a glyph renderer]

=== 00064046 [PLATE]
Byte stride between consecutive glyph bitmaps in the 1bpp font sheet.

Written once, with the literal 0x20, by fdps_load_global_resources while it seeds the font metric block at 0006403c-00064052, just before it loads Fdetxt.fon into the font pointer at 000643cc; nothing else in the program writes it, so it is 32 for the life of the process. Read once, by fdps_draw_glyph, which computes glyph_bits = font_base + glyph_index * this before any blitting -- the only place a glyph index becomes a bitmap address. 32 is what one 16x16 1bpp cell costs, 16 rows of 2 bytes, and agrees with the cell width and height bytes 0x10/0x10 at 0006403c/0006403d that fdps_draw_glyph uses to fill the background cell. FD2 renders the same font and writes this number as a literal 0x20 inside its glyph blitter instead of keeping a global. It sits in _BSS, so it reads 0 until fdps_load_global_resources runs; main calls that before anything draws text.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_draw_glyph and fdps_load_global_resources reach it, and neither the Watcom runtime nor Miles contains a glyph renderer]

=== 0006404a [PLATE]
Selects which decoration fdps_draw_glyph draws under a glyph: non-zero means a 4-connected one-pixel outline, zero means a single drop shadow.

Written once, by fdps_load_global_resources at 00029698, which sets it to 0 as part of the run of font metrics it installs at startup (cell width 0006403c = 0x10, cell height 0006403d = 0x10, shadow column offset 0006403e = 1, shadow row offset 00064042 = 1, bytes per glyph 00064046 = 0x20, this flag, glyph advance 0006404b = 0x10, line height 0006404f = 0x12). Read once, by fdps_draw_glyph at 0001fdf4. When it is non-zero the glyph bitmap is blitted four times in outline_color at dst+pitch, dst-1, dst-pitch and dst+1; when it is zero a single shadow blit is done instead at dst + 00064042 * pitch + 0006403e, and only when outline_color is non-zero. Either way the glyph body is drawn last, on top. No code writes any value other than that startup 0, so every glyph in this build gets the drop shadow and the outline branch is never taken.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_draw_glyph and fdps_load_global_resources touch it, both pool fdps; it is a game font-rendering parameter with no library counterpart]

=== 0006404b [PLATE]
Horizontal advance, in pixels, that fdps_draw_text moves the drawing cursor after each glyph.

Written once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which stores 0x10 here inside the straight-line block that seeds the whole font metric run at 0006403c-0006404f (glyph cell width and height, drop-shadow column and row offsets, the 0x20 bytes-per-glyph stride of the 1bpp font sheet, the outline-vs-shadow style flag, and the line height at 0006404f). Nothing else in the image writes it, so it is 0x10 for the whole run.

Read only by fdps_draw_text, on the ordinary-glyph path: after calling fdps_draw_glyph for a token that is not a control code, the routine adds this value to the destination cursor so the next glyph lands one cell to the right. The value is a signed pixel count added to a byte address, so it assumes the destination is 8bpp, one byte per pixel. With the startup value it equals the glyph cell width at 0006403c, i.e. the font is drawn with no extra letter spacing. It is not used by the -6 number code, which advances by a literal 0x10 per digit of its own, nor by the line break code -2, which uses the line height at 0006404f multiplied by the destination pitch.

Pool: fdps  [both references are game code -- the game's own text renderer fdps_draw_text and the resource loader fdps_load_global_resources; neither the Watcom runtime nor Miles has a glyph renderer]

=== 0006404f [PLATE]
Vertical distance in destination rows from one line of drawn text to the next.

Written once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which stores 0x12 (18 rows) here at the end of the block that also publishes the glyph cell width and height at 0006403c/0006403d, the drop-shadow offsets at 0006403e/00064042, the outline-style flag at 0006404a and the horizontal glyph advance at 0006404b; nothing else in the image writes it. Read once by fdps_draw_text, at entry, into a local that the rest of the call uses -- so a text entry is laid out with whatever value was in place when drawing began. Its only use is the -2 line-break token, which increments the line counter and restarts the cursor at dest + pitch * this value * line_count, measuring from the current line origin rather than stepping the cursor, so the value is the full line pitch and not the gap between lines. 18 is the 16-row glyph cell plus two rows of leading; the horizontal companion, the per-glyph cursor advance at 0006404b, is 0x10.

Pool: fdps  [both references are game code -- the text renderer fdps_draw_text and the startup resource loader fdps_load_global_resources; neither the Watcom runtime nor Miles draws text]

=== 00064060 [PLATE]
Key table of the CEL sprite group cache: element i is the .CEL group index whose 12 sprites are cached in slot i.

Written only by fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group. On the first call after a cache reset (slot count DAT_00069cf0 == 0) it seeds element 0 with the requested group index; on any later call it scans elements 0..DAT_00069cf0-1 for the requested group and returns that slot number on a hit, and on a miss stores the group index into element DAT_00069cf0 before reallocating data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr, appending the group's pixels at the byte cursor DAT_0006411c and incrementing the slot count. Read nowhere else. Valid entries run 0..DAT_00069cf0-1; slots at or past the count hold stale keys, because the functions that drop the cache (fdps_build_map_unit_array, fdps_load_field_chapter_resources, fdps_load_savegame, fdps_saveload_screen_build, fdps_draw_save_slot_panel, fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members) free the buffer and zero the count without touching this table. Values are whatever group indices the caller asks for; there is no sentinel.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group reaches it, and it is one of the four private globals of the game's own sprite cache]

Rebuild note:
The append in fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group is unbounded -- it writes element[count] with nothing checking count against 30. Declare the array with exactly 30 elements and do not add the bounds check that looks missing: the original relies on no chapter ever asking for a 31st distinct group, and a check that clamps or refuses would change behaviour where the original silently ran past the table into the per-cell event flags at 000640d8.

=== 000640d8 [PLATE]
Per-chapter one-shot flags for the 32 map cell events, one byte each, indexed by the cell event code.

fdps_chapter_state_reset clears all 32 bytes when a chapter's map is loaded, so this is per-chapter state, not lifetime progress. It is part of the savegame: fdps_battle_system_submenu copies the 32 bytes to offset 0x30a3 of the save block and fdps_load_savegame copies them back. The index is the cell event code fdps_map_load_tile_info publishes at 00069d06, taken from the byte layer behind data_fdps_map_cell_event_code_layer_ptr; the same code indexes the 3-byte cell records at data_fdps_tile_event_data_table_ptr + 0x53 + code * 3. Code 0 means the cell carries no event, so the live slots are 1..31.

0 means the event has not fired, non-zero that it has. fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor tests the flag before offering the search prompt and sets it to 1 once the cell's item or money has been taken; fdps_map_actor_behavior_step does the same for an AI actor in mode 5, using the cell code held in the actor's record at +0x3d; the icon script opcode 0x13 in fdps_icon_script_run writes an arbitrary byte to an arbitrary slot. All of them then call fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes, which walks every cell of the map and, where the tile attribute class is 0x20 or 0x60 and this flag is set, increments the tile id and zeroes the cell's byte in the event-code layer -- that is what turns an opened chest over on screen. Chapter handlers use individual slots directly as one-shot latches by absolute address rather than through the index: 000640da is slot 2, latched by fdps_chapter_30_event_deploy_wave_2, and 000640ea is slot 18, latched by fdps_chapter_26_event_wave_2_defeated_line and fdps_chapter_27_event_deploy_wave_1.

Pool: fdps  [only game functions reach it, and it hangs off the map event layer and the chapter reset]

Rebuild note:
Slot 0 is the "no cell event" code and must never be treated as an ordinary flag. fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes zeroes a cell's byte in the event-code layer once it has applied it, so every later full-map pass reads code 0 for that cell and tests element 0; handing slot 0 to a real event, or letting the icon-script opcode 0x13 set it, makes previously consumed cells advance their tile again on each sweep.

=== 000640f8 [PLATE]
One flag per save slot: non-zero when that slot of FDE.SAV holds a saved game, zero when it is empty.

Written by fdps_saveload_screen_build, which reads the whole 0x59cb-byte FDE.SAV (or fills the buffer with 0xff when the file does not exist), XOR-decrypts it, and for each slot i in 0..2 examines the marker byte at record + 0xa00 of the record at buf + 0x312b + i * 0xa28: marker 0xff stores 0 here, any other value stores 1. Read by fdps_save_slot_select_loop, which on Space/Enter accepts the highlighted slot only when the save/load mode flag at 00064104 is zero (saving, any slot allowed) or this flag is non-zero for the highlighted slot (loading, empty slots refused). The index is the slot number the cursor keys move over, 0..2, matching the three panel rows drawn at y = 0x1a + i * 0x34 by fdps_draw_save_slot_panel.

Pool: fdps  [only the save/load menu functions fdps_saveload_screen_build and fdps_save_slot_select_loop reach it, both pool fdps; no library code touches it]

Rebuild note:
Emptiness is 0xff, not 0. The marker byte is tested against 0xff and every other value -- 0x00 included -- counts as an occupied slot; writing the obvious flag = (marker != 0) makes a slot whose marker byte is zero unselectable in the load menu.

=== 00064104 [PLATE]
Save/load screen mode flag: non-zero while the load screen is up, zero while the save screen is up.

Written only at the entry of the two screen drivers: fdps_save_game_screen sets it to 0 and fdps_load_game_screen sets it to 1, before either builds its page with fdps_saveload_screen_build. Read only by fdps_save_slot_select_loop, the modal three-slot cursor loop both screens share: on Space/Enter it confirms the slot when this flag is 0 (save mode, any of the three slots may be overwritten) or when the flag is non-zero and data_fdps_ui_save_slot_occupied_flags[slot] is non-zero (load mode, only a slot that holds a save may be picked). Values are exactly 0 and 1; nothing else is ever stored, and the flag is not consulted anywhere outside the save/load UI.

Pool: fdps  [only the three game save/load UI functions reference it; no library code touches it]

=== 00064108 [PLATE]
Base pointer of the persistent party roster: 32 consecutive 0x50-byte unit records holding every character the player currently has, with their class, stats, equipment and carried items.

fdps_load_global_resources allocates the block once at startup with malloc(0xa00) = 32 * 0x50, and that store at 000296c5 is the only write to this pointer in the image. Record i lives at ptr + i * 0x50 and fdps_get_roster_record returns exactly that; the number of records in use is the separate counter at 00064114, which fdps_roster_add_character uses as the append index. Byte +7 of a record is the character id that fdps_saveload_screen_build, fdps_load_field_chapter_resources and fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members feed to fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group; +0x40/+0x42 are current and maximum HP and +0x44/+0x46 current and maximum MP, which fdps_build_map_unit_array restores when the party takes the field. fdps_build_map_unit_array memmoves roster record i over battlefield slot i on entering a map, fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units copies the surviving battle state back afterwards, and fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats and fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members edit the records in place. In field and village mode there is no separate battlefield array at all: fdps_load_field_chapter_resources points data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr at this same block and sets data_fdps_map_unit_count from the roster count, so map code walks the roster records directly. The whole 0xa00-byte block is the party section of a save: fdps_save_game_screen memmoves it out to offset 0x8a3 of the save record, fdps_load_savegame and fdps_load_game_screen memmove it back, and fdps_battle_system_submenu takes the same snapshot for the in-battle save. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees the block at exit, and fdps_title_demo frees it when the attract demo ends and sets the count at 00064114 to 0, in both cases leaving this pointer holding the old address.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; the roster, the save layout and the 0x50-byte unit record are all game state, with malloc/free/memmove used as leaf services]

Rebuild note:
In field and village mode data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr aliases this block instead of owning a copy, so it must not be freed as if it were the map's own array -- fdps_load_field_chapter_resources frees the previous array only when it differs from this pointer, and fdps_run_village_phase clears data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr to 0 rather than freeing it; a rewrite that frees the map unit array unconditionally when swapping it double-frees the roster. The block is also allocated exactly once, so fdps_title_demo's free leaves this pointer dangling for the rest of the run; do not repair that by nulling it, reallocating, or guarding the second free, because it changes what shutdown and every later roster read touch.

=== 0006410c [PLATE]
Number of scripted char-spawn records in the map's map%02d.dat, cached from header byte +2.

Written by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources and fdps_load_savegame, both as
(uint)data_fdps_tile_event_data_table_ptr[2], right after that routine loads "map%02d.dat" from
Field.vfs; header byte +1 goes to DAT_00064118 in the same breath. The value counts the 0x1a-byte
deployment records that start at offset 0x83 of the same blob, one per unit the map script places
(fdps_deploy_wave walks records 0..count-1 there and calls fdps_deploy_unit on each whose byte
+0x15 matches the wave number; it re-reads the byte from the buffer rather than this copy, so the
two are always the same number). Range is 0..255, a plain count with no sentinel.

Read once, by fdps_build_map_unit_array, where it is the base index into the map%02d.cod placement
table at data_fdps_map_spawn_pos_table_ptr: the scripted units own placement records 0 to
count-1, so party slot i takes record (count + i), at offset 0xb + (count + i) * 6.

Pool: fdps  [only the three game routines above touch it; it is derived from a game resource file
and consumed by game map setup]

Rebuild note:
This count doubles as the offset of the party's block inside map%02d.cod. Indexing that placement
table by the party slot number alone -- the obvious loop -- drops every party member onto a
scripted unit's start tile.

=== 00064110 [PLATE]
Run-once flag for the bar's hidden lucky-draw bonus game: nonzero once the draw has been taken.

fdps_title_screen clears it to 0 on entering the title screen. fdps_run_bonus_lottery tests it first and returns immediately unless it is 0 (the draw also needs the system date to be 1998-01-28); after paying out the prize it sets it to 1, so the draw cannot happen twice. The flag is part of the saved game: fdps_save_game_screen stores it as a dword at +0x9ec of the slot record -- inside the 0xa00-byte live-state block it has just copied, not after it -- and fdps_load_game_screen reads it back from slot+0x9ec into this global, but only when data_fdps_village_mode_flag is 0. Only 0 and 1 are ever stored; the test is against 0, so any nonzero value means 'already drawn'.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- fdps_title_screen, fdps_run_bonus_lottery, fdps_save_game_screen, fdps_load_game_screen -- and it encodes a game rule, not library state]

Rebuild note:
The flag is a standalone global, not a field of the 0xa00-byte save block, and the load side restores it only when data_fdps_village_mode_flag is 0. Writing the obvious unconditional assignment on load, or treating slot+0x9ec as part of the memmoved block, changes when the bonus draw becomes available again.

=== 00064114 [PLATE]
Number of characters currently in the party roster.

The roster itself is the 0xa00-byte buffer malloc'd at 000296c5 and held in DAT_00064108, i.e. 32 records of 0x50 bytes; this counter says how many of those 32 slots are live, so it runs 0..32 and every roster index runs 0..count-1. fdps_roster_add_character is the only writer that grows it: it forms the new record at DAT_00064108 + count * 0x50, fills it, calls fdps_roster_recompute_combat_stats(count) and then INCs the counter, with no capacity check. fdps_title_screen and fdps_title_demo reset it to 0 when a new game or the demo starts; fdps_load_savegame and fdps_load_game_screen restore it from the saved image. It is read as a loop bound almost everywhere the party is walked -- fdps_roster_write_back_battle_units, fdps_build_map_unit_array, fdps_saveload_screen_build, fdps_church_promote_loop, fdps_roster_add_item_to_all, fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members, fdps_battle_find_unit_by_character_id -- and as the scroll clamp in fdps_shop_select_buy_target, fdps_shop_render_buy_target_frame and fdps_village_select_member, where cursor moves are gated on count-1 and count-3. fdps_load_field_chapter_resources copies it into data_fdps_map_unit_count when a chapter's map is built, which is how the roster count becomes the battle unit count. fdps_village_signboard_menu wraps the signboard marker with (data_fdps_village_marker_roster_idx + 1) % count, so a count of zero would divide by zero there; in practice the village is never entered with an empty roster. fdps_play_ending_credit_roll deliberately loops i from 0 to count inclusive and treats i == count as an extra, fixed class-12 entry rather than a roster member.

Pool: fdps  [all 20 referencing functions are pool fdps; nothing in the CRT or the sound library touches it]

Rebuild note:
The counter is an int in memory but crosses both save paths as a single unsigned byte -- MOV AL,[0x00064114] into offset 0x30cc of the save image (fdps_battle_system_submenu) and into offset 0xa01 of the slot summary record (fdps_save_game_screen), read back with AND EAX,0xff. Declaring that save-record field as an int shifts every field after it and breaks compatibility with original save files.

=== 00064118 [PLATE]
How many player-side unit slots the current map fields, taken from byte +1 of its map%02d.dat header.

Written by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources and fdps_load_savegame, each time the map%02d.dat blob is (re)loaded into data_fdps_tile_event_data_table_ptr: the byte at +1 lands here and the byte at +2, the map's scripted deployment count, lands in DAT_0006410c. Read only by fdps_build_map_unit_array, which seeds data_fdps_map_unit_count with it, mallocs data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr at this many 0x50-byte unit records, and fills slot i for i in 0..value-1: slots below the party roster count DAT_00064114 get the roster record copied in with side byte +6 = 2 (player side), slots at or above it get a zeroed record with the retired bit at +5 set. Zero means the map fields no player units at all and the array is not allocated. The value is a byte from the map file, so it runs 0..255 in practice, and it stays fixed for the map while data_fdps_map_unit_count grows past it as fdps_deploy_wave appends scripted units.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps functions reference it, and it is read out of a game resource file]

=== 0006411c [PLATE]
Byte count of the CEL sprite cache buffer at data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr that is currently in use, which is also the offset at which the next group's pixel data is appended.

Only fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group touches it. On the seeding call (data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_group_ids empty, entry count at 00069cf0 zero) it is set to 0x5a0 + the first group's pixel size: 0x5a0 is the fixed offset table reserved at the head of the buffer (30 groups x 12 sprites x 4 bytes) and the pixel data of every group follows it. On a cache miss the same function reads it as the realloc size base (realloc(cache_ptr, used + group_size)) and as the fread destination offset (cache_ptr + used), stores used + (entry_offset - first_entry_offset) into the twelve offset-table slots of the new group, then adds the group's size to it. Values are byte offsets relative to the buffer base, never pointers, because the buffer moves on every realloc. It is not reset when the cache is torn down (fdps_build_map_unit_array, fdps_saveload_screen_build, fdps_draw_save_slot_panel, fdps_load_savegame, fdps_load_field_chapter_resources, fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members and main free the buffer and zero the entry count only); correctness rests on the zero-count branch assigning it rather than accumulating into it.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group reaches it, and it indexes a game-private sprite cache]

Rebuild note:
This is a byte offset into a realloc'd buffer, not a pointer. Writing the offset table as cache_ptr + used pointers -- the obvious C -- leaves every previously cached group's entries dangling as soon as the next group reallocs the buffer to a new address.

=== 00064120 [PLATE]
Per-cell horizontal pixel offset inside its own popup, for the queue of floating indicators that hover over battle units.

One of three parallel 200-byte queues indexed by the shared cursor at 0x00064378: this one holds the cell's x offset within the popup, DAT_000641e8 the index of the unit the cell floats over, DAT_000642b0 the Number.cel glyph id (0xff meaning a blank cell that is skipped). Written by the four producers, each appending cells at the cursor and then advancing it: fdps_show_number_indicator writes i*6 + 2 for all four digit cells of a number, while fdps_show_miss_indicator, fdps_show_cure_indicator and fdps_show_sprite_indicator write i*6 + 1 with cell 1 kerned in by one pixel for their fixed words. Read only by fdps_play_indicator_queue, which for each queued cell blits the glyph at x = tile_x * 24 - DAT_00069ce4 + this byte + 24, then resets the cursor to 0 after its 22 bouncing frames, emptying all three queues at once. Values are small unsigned pixel counts, zero-extended at the point of use; index range is 0 to the current cursor value, and the layout gives room for 200 cells, which nothing checks against.

Pool: fdps  [only battle-display game functions reach it, all in pool fdps; it is written and read alongside the game's own unit records and camera scroll globals]

=== 000641e8 [PLATE]
Per-cell unit index for the floating battle indicator queue: for each queued glyph, which unit it floats over.

One of three parallel 200-byte queues filled in lockstep and indexed by the shared cursor data_fdps_battle_indicator_queue_count at 00064378: 00064120 holds each cell's pixel x offset inside its popup, this array holds the owning unit index, and 000642b0 holds the glyph id in Number.cel (0xff meaning a blank cell). Written by the four producers fdps_show_number_indicator (four cells per call, one per digit of a right-aligned number), fdps_show_miss_indicator, fdps_show_cure_indicator (four cells each for their fixed word) and fdps_show_sprite_indicator (one cell per non-zero sprite id, up to four); each stores its unit_index parameter as a byte into slot cursor + i and then advances the cursor. Read only by fdps_play_indicator_queue, which for each of the 22 playback frames walks slots 0..count-1 and passes this byte to fdps_get_unit_record to fetch the unit's tile x and y from record bytes 0 and 1, so the glyph tracks the unit as the camera scrolls; it then resets the cursor to 0, which is the only thing that empties the queue -- the bytes themselves are left stale and are never read past the cursor. Values are indices into the 0x50-byte unit record array based at data_fdps_map_unit_array_ptr, so they run over the units alive on the current map; there is no sentinel, a blank cell is marked in the glyph queue instead.

Pool: fdps  [only the five battle indicator functions touch it, and its values are indices into the game's own unit record array]

=== 000642b0 [PLATE]
Glyph ids of the floating indicator queue: one sprite id per queued cell, indexed by the shared queue cursor data_fdps_indicator_queue_cursor at 00064378.

Third of three parallel 200-byte queues -- 00064120 holds each cell's pixel x offset inside its popup, 000641e8 the index of the unit the popup floats over, this one the sprite id. Four producers append cells and bump the cursor: fdps_show_number_indicator writes four cells per call, glyph_base + digit - '0' for each digit of a right-aligned number and 0xff for the leading blanks; fdps_show_miss_indicator and fdps_show_cure_indicator copy a fixed four-id label from 0001c2d2 and 0001c2d6; fdps_show_sprite_indicator copies up to four caller-supplied ids, stopping at the first zero, and advances the cursor only by the number of cells it wrote. fdps_play_indicator_queue reads the cells 0..cursor-1 for 22 frames, skips any cell whose id is 0xff, and blits the rest out of the Number.cel sheet at DAT_000643d8 with fdps_cel_blit_sprite; it then resets the cursor to 0, which is the only thing that empties the queue -- the bytes themselves are never cleared. Values are sprite indices into that sheet: 0x00 upward for the digit run used by damage numbers, 0x0d for the MP/stat-gain digits, 0x27 for the healing digits, and 0xff reserved as the blank-cell marker. Nothing bounds-checks the cursor against 200.

Pool: fdps  [only the five game battle-display functions reach it, and it is written from the same code that walks the game's unit records]

Rebuild note:
0xff, not 0, is the blank-cell marker: glyph id 0 is a legitimate value that fdps_show_number_indicator queues for the digit '0' of a damage number, and the queue lives in _BSS so its untouched bytes are already 0. Writing the player's skip test as 'if (id == 0) continue' or treating a zeroed cell as empty drops the zero digits out of damage numbers.

=== 00064378 [PLATE]
Number of cells currently queued in the floating battle-indicator queue; also the index at which the next cell is appended.

The queue is three parallel byte arrays indexed by cell number: 0x00064120 holds each cell's x offset in pixels into the indicator glyph sheet, 0x000641e8 the unit index the cell floats above, and 0x000642b0 the glyph id (0xff meaning a blank cell). This counter says how many of those slots are live.

Four producers append to it. fdps_show_number_indicator, fdps_show_miss_indicator and fdps_show_cure_indicator each write four cells at [count + 0..3] and then add 4. fdps_show_sprite_indicator writes at [count + loop index] for each of its glyph slots but adds only the number of non-zero sprite ids it actually wrote, so it can advance by less than the number of slots it touched. fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets stores 0 on entry to start a fresh queue for the item it is about to resolve.

fdps_play_indicator_queue drains it: it returns immediately when the count is 0, otherwise it animates 22 frames of the queued cells bouncing up and back, walking cells 0 through count-1 on each frame, waits 500 ms and stores 0 back. Nothing bounds-checks the count against the 200-byte capacity of the three arrays, so at most 50 four-cell indicators may be queued between drains.

Pool: fdps  [only battle-display code in pool_fdps reaches it; no CRT or AIL reference exists]

Rebuild note:
fdps_show_sprite_indicator advances this counter by the number of non-zero sprite ids it wrote, not by the number of slots it indexed. Writing the obvious 'count += 4' that its three sibling producers use would shift every later cell and stop the next producer from overwriting the slots this one left unwritten, changing what the drain loop draws.

=== 0006437c [PLATE]
Destination tile column, in tiles, for the effect that relocates a unit.

Written by fdps_battle_item_menu and fdps_battle_spell_command, both times as the confirmed cursor's map pixel x at 00069cd4 divided by the 0x18-pixel tile size, right after fdps_map_cursor_select_loop mode 6 has asked the player for a tile the unit may stand on. 00064380 holds the matching row. Read only by fdps_cast_spell_on_targets, in the spell_id == 0x15 (傳送術) branch: it scales the pair back up by 0x18 for fdps_map_cursor_move_to, then writes the two tile coordinates into the first target's unit record bytes +0x00 and +0x01, moving that unit to this tile. The range is a map column index, 0 upward; the CRT zeroes it at startup and nothing uses a sentinel value.

The write in fdps_battle_item_menu, which fires for item use_effect 0x19 and 0x1c, has no reader: fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets has no branch for either code, so the tile those items ask for is discarded.

Pool: fdps  [only game battle code reaches it -- the item menu, the spell command loop and spell resolution]

=== 00064380 [PLATE]
The y tile coordinate of the destination tile the player picked for a teleport effect on the battle map; the matching x is the dword at 0006437c.

Written in exactly two places, both from the map cursor's pixel row DAT_00069ccc divided by the 0x18-pixel tile size, and both only after fdps_map_cursor_select_loop mode 6 -- the second pick that asks for a tile the target may stand on -- has been confirmed: fdps_battle_spell_command writes it for spell 0x15 (傳送術), fdps_battle_item_menu for an item whose use_effect is 0x19 or 0x1c. Read only by fdps_cast_spell_on_targets, in its spell 0x15 arm: fdps_map_cursor_move_to(x * 0x18, y * 0x18) walks the cursor to the tile, then the low bytes of the pair are stored into target 0's record bytes +0x00 and +0x01, which are that unit's tile x and y, and the spell animation is replayed there. Only the first target of the hit list is moved. The value is a tile row, 0-based, in the same units as unit record byte +0x01, not a pixel row. Nothing on the item path ever reads it: fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets has no branch for use_effect 0x19 or 0x1c, so the item menu's write is dead.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps functions reach it: fdps_battle_item_menu, fdps_battle_spell_command, fdps_cast_spell_on_targets]

Rebuild note:
The teleport destination reaches fdps_cast_spell_on_targets only through this global and 0006437c, never as a parameter. Passing the picked tile down as an argument -- the obvious rewrite -- changes behaviour on the AI cast path: fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell calls fdps_cast_spell_on_targets with the spell the AI scorer chose and never writes these two, so a spell 0x15 cast from there teleports its target to whatever tile the player last picked, or to tile (0,0) if no one has picked one yet, because the CRT zeroes _BSS. Keep the globals and keep the read unconditional.

=== 00064390 [PLATE]
Tick at which the spell-list window last drew a frame, and the phase source for that window's animations.

Written only by fdps_spell_list_window_wait_input, on the last line of each frame it draws, with the live tick counter DAT_00069d64. Read by the same function and by nothing else: the frame is skipped entirely unless DAT_00069d64 differs from this latch, so the window repaints at most once per tick. While the frame is being drawn the latch still holds the tick of the PREVIOUS frame, and both of the window's animation phases are derived from it in that state -- the scroll-arrow blink is (value / 8) & 1, alternating each arrow between two Command.cel sprites every 8 ticks, and the caster's walk-cycle frame is (value % 16) / 4 with 3 folded back to 1, giving the 0, 1, 2, 1 cycle. The arithmetic is signed throughout (SAR by 0x1f before the shift and before IDIV), so the value is a signed tick, not an unsigned one. Zero at startup because it lives in _BSS, which makes the first frame after the window opens always draw.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_spell_list_window_wait_input reaches it; it is this window's private frame-pacing state]

Rebuild note:
The two animation phases are computed from this latch while it still holds the previous frame's tick, and the latch is advanced to DAT_00069d64 only after the frame has been composed. Writing the obvious loop -- latch the new tick at the top of the frame and derive the phases from the live counter -- shifts both the arrow blink and the walk cycle by one tick.

=== 000643a0 [PLATE]
Base of the BaseWav.vfs sound-effect pack, held resident in memory for the whole run.

Written once, at startup, by fdps_load_global_resources: fdps_vfs_load_file("BaseWav.vfs", misc_vfs) allocates one block holding the entire nested VFS container and returns its base here; a null result makes that function call fdps_wait_any_key and exit(1), so past startup the value is always a valid pack base and never null. Read by fdps_play_sfx, which passes it as the image base to fdps_vfs_image_get_entry together with the effect's 8.3 name; that helper walks the 0x1a-byte directory entries at the offset named in the pack's 0x0b-byte header and returns a pointer to the member's WAV bytes inside this same block, which fdps_play_sfx hands straight to fdps_audio_start_wav. Nothing is copied out: the sample AIL plays lives inside this buffer, so the block must stay allocated and unmoved while any effect is sounding. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it unconditionally as the first member of the resource-pointer block 000643a0..000643e4.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps functions reach it; the pointer is produced by the game's own VFS loader and consumed by the game's own directory walker, AIL only ever sees the interior pointer]

=== 000643a4 [PLATE]
The party's total gold.

Every gold transaction in the game is an add or a subtract on this one dword. fdps_shop_buy_loop compares the price standing in data_fdps_dialog_last_action_value_param against it and subtracts on a purchase, adding the same amount back on an accepted sale; fdps_village_item_sell_loop adds the offer; fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor and fdps_run_death_scripts add the money found on the map or left by a dying unit; fdps_run_bonus_lottery adds a flat 0x4e20 (20000) on the winning result; fdps_chapter_16_event_wandering_smith_forge adds back 0x1388 (5000) when the forging fails; fdps_chapter_25_event_marian_buys_wind_god_bow requires at least 0x7530 (30000), the 風神弓's list price, and subtracts exactly that. fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members subtracts the whole revive bill unconditionally and only afterwards clamps the balance up to 0 if it went negative -- the one place the value is corrected instead of checked first. fdps_draw_party_gold and fdps_battle_show_win_fail_window read it and render it as an 8-digit decimal. fdps_save_game_screen stores it as a dword at +0xa02 of the save slot and fdps_battle_system_submenu at +0x30cd of the in-battle save buffer; fdps_load_game_screen and fdps_load_savegame read those two offsets back into it. Nothing initialises it for a new game: the starting balance is the zero the CRT leaves in _BSS.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it, and every reference is a gold transaction]

Rebuild note:
The value is signed and the code depends on it. fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members subtracts the full revive bill first and clamps a negative balance back to 0 only afterwards, and the shop's affordability tests are signed (JG at 00033df1, JGE at 0003a2b4). Declaring it unsigned -- the obvious choice for money -- makes the clamp unreachable and turns an over-budget revive into roughly four billion gold.

=== 000643a8 [PLATE]
Heap pointer to the resident in-memory image of the BaseAni.vfs archive, the container holding the game's shared SAF animation streams.

Written exactly once, by fdps_load_global_resources, which pulls BaseAni.vfs out of the already-open Misc.vfs with fdps_vfs_load_file and calls fdps_wait_any_key then exit(1) if the load returns NULL; the pointer therefore is non-NULL for the whole run and is never reassigned. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it, between the 0x64108 scratch buffer and the BaseWav.vfs image at 000643a0. Readers pass it as the archive base to fdps_vfs_image_get_entry, which searches the image by member name and returns a pointer into it plus the member size through its third argument: fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead fetches "Explo.Saf", fdps_play_attack_animation fetches "EasyAni.Saf", and fdps_baseani_get_entry_or_exit is the general accessor, storing its result in DAT_000643ec and bailing out when the member is missing. A returned entry points inside this buffer and is not separately allocated, so nothing frees it. NULL only ever means startup has not reached the load yet -- the CRT zeroes this address as part of _BSS.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: fdps_load_global_resources, fdps_shutdown_free_resources, fdps_baseani_get_entry_or_exit, fdps_play_attack_animation, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead]

Rebuild note:
BaseAni.vfs does not exist as a file on disk; it is a member inside MISC.VFS that the game loads whole into memory and then searches in place. Rebuilding this as fdps_vfs_open("BaseAni.vfs") -- the obvious reading of a .vfs filename -- fails at startup, and freeing the buffer after the first lookup breaks every later animation, because the entry pointers handed out by fdps_vfs_image_get_entry point into this allocation.

=== 000643ac [PLATE]
Base of the decoded Command.cel sprite sheet, the shared UI artwork held resident for the whole run.

Written once, at startup, by fdps_load_global_resources (0002982c): fdps_vfs_load_file("Command.cel", misc_vfs) allocates one block holding the whole cel and returns its base here; a null result makes that function call fdps_wait_any_key and exit(1), so past startup the value is always a valid sheet base and never null. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it (000294ae) as one member of the resource-pointer block 000643a0..000643e4, and nothing else writes it.

Two kinds of reader. The ring menus go through the cel's own offset table by hand: fdps_render_ring_menu_frame (00015a70, 00015af2) and fdps_blit_command_sprite (00015ba6) take the sprite stream as base + *(int *)(base + 0xf + index * 4) -- 0x0f is the fixed start of the CEL offset table, see resource_info/cel.md -- and hand that straight to fdps_blit_dispatch as a 0x19 x 0x16 (25x22) image in mode 0. Each ring slot is drawn as two sprites out of this sheet: the button plate, (slot == cursor_dir ? 0x1a : 0x1b) + cmd_disabled[slot], and the command icon over it, cmd_icons[slot] + cmd_disabled[slot] * 0x24, so the sheet is laid out as two banks and a greyed-out entry takes its artwork from the bank 0x24 sprites further in. The icon ids come from the per-menu initialiser images at 0x146e0, 0x14700, 0x24d50 and 0x311a4 and run over both banks, roughly 4..0x18 for the lit bank. The other readers call fdps_cel_blit_sprite with an explicit sprite id: fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up draws sprite 0x23 as the experience-award panel (0001de66) and fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members draws 0x2a, 0x2b, 0x3a and 0x29 as the church revive dialog's labels and buttons (0003a0d4, 0003a0fa, 0003a159, 0003a1b0).

Pool: fdps  [every reference is game code -- the ring-menu renderer, the level-up panel and the revive dialog -- and the value is produced by the game's own VFS loader]

=== 000643b0 [PLATE]
Pointer to the LEVUP.CEL sprite sheet, the artwork of the full-screen level-up window.

Written once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which calls fdps_vfs_load_file on the resource name LEVUP.CEL and aborts the program through the load-failure path when the result is NULL, so by the time the game runs this is always a valid block. fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up is the only reader in the game: when a unit's running experience total reaches 100 it paints sprite 0 of this sheet into a 164x66 window buffer, then draws the new level, the learned spell names and the five stat gains on top of it before compositing the window onto the scene at (98, 88). fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it along with the other global sheets. NULL means the sheet has not been loaded yet, which only holds between the CRT clearing _BSS and fdps_load_global_resources running.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; it holds a game resource loaded out of the VFS]

=== 000643b4 [PLATE]
Pointer to the 0x306-byte heap buffer holding the three decoded 43x6 8bpp images of the per-unit HP gauge bar.

fdps_load_global_resources writes it during startup: it loads EasyBar.cel out of Misc.vfs, mallocs 0x306 bytes, memsets them to 0, and decodes the CEL's three sub-images with fdps_blit_dispatch mode 0 into base + i * 0x102, each 0x2b (43) wide by 6 high at pitch 0x2b, then frees the CEL temporary. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees the buffer at exit. fdps_draw_unit_gauge is the only reader: base + gfx_index * 0x102 selects the filled colour (index 1 or 2, chosen by the unit record's side byte at +6), while the unfilled remainder of the bar is always taken from image 0 as base + 2 + fill_width, i.e. image 0 is the empty track and gfx_index never reaches it. Columns 0..1 and 0x29..0x2a of each image are the bar's end caps, the 0x29 (41) columns between them are the interior the fill divides. Palette index 0 in the art is the transparency key at draw time.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps functions reference it, and it holds a game resource decoded from the game's own EasyBar.cel]

Rebuild note:
The memset to 0 after the malloc is load-bearing, not defensive hygiene: the decode is an RLE blit that leaves skipped pixels untouched, and palette index 0 is what fdps_draw_unit_gauge treats as transparent, so any byte the decode does not write must already be zero. Allocating without clearing leaves heap garbage that draws as opaque colour inside the bar.

=== 000643b8 [PLATE]
Pointer to the CUSOR.CEL sprite sheet, the 24x24 overlay tiles the battle map draws its cursor and its range indicators from.

Written once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which loads "Cusor.cel" out of MISC.VFS with fdps_vfs_load_file; a NULL result makes that function call fdps_wait_any_key and exit(1), so once the game is running the value is always a valid sheet base and never NULL. The only reader is fdps_blit_cursor_tile: it resolves a sprite's pixel stream through the sheet's dword offset table at the hardcoded header offset 0x0f -- src = p + *(int *)(p + sprite_index * 4 + 0xf) -- and passes it to fdps_blit_dispatch as a 24x24 blit at pitch 0x168 in mode 0, the plain RLE kernel, so palette index 0 of the cursor art reads through as transparent. The sheet holds 20 sprites of 24x24; the caller at 0002c6a0 uses indices 0..0x11, the single-tile cursors plus the edge, corner and centre pieces it assembles the move- and attack-range diamonds out of, and nothing bounds-checks the index. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it unconditionally as one of the resource pointers in the 000643a0..000643e4 block. Zero from the CRT's _BSS clear until fdps_load_global_resources runs.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- the startup loader, the map cursor blitter and the shutdown free -- and it holds a game resource loaded out of the VFS]

=== 000643bc [PLATE]
Pointer to the game's main VGA palette: the 768 bytes of Fde.pal, 256 entries of three 6-bit DAC components in R,G,B order.

fdps_load_global_resources loads it at startup with fdps_vfs_load_file("Fde.pal", misc_vfs); a null result makes that function call fdps_wait_any_key and exit(1), so past startup it is always a valid 768-byte block. fdps_load_savegame frees the block and reloads the same member with fdps_vfs_load_entry("MISC.VFS", "Fde.pal") while restoring a save, and fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it at exit. Those are the only writes.

Every read hands it to fdps_set_palette_range(ptr, 0, 0xff, r_bias, g_bias, b_bias), which walks all 256 entries and writes component + bias, clamped to 0..63, out to DAC ports 0x3c8/0x3c9. Bias 0,0,0 means "restore the normal screen": fdps_title_screen, fdps_run_village_phase, fdps_show_chapter_title_card, fdps_play_movie, fdps_play_ending_credit_roll, fdps_church_promote_unit and both combat routines end that way, the two combat routines thereby replacing the Fight.pal palette at 000643e4 that they installed on entry. A negative bias darkens and a positive one brightens the same base, which is how every fade is done: fdps_icon_script_fade_to_black and fdps_icon_script_fade_in ramp the bias from 0 down to -0x3c, and back from -0x40 up to 0, one VBLANK at a time, fdps_transition_zoom uses -3 * (8 - step), fdps_play_movie and fdps_show_chapter_title_card blank with -0x40, fdps_map_actor_use_item and fdps_play_spell_11_cutscene flash white with a positive bias, and fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit flashes green with (-0x40, 0x40, -0x40) for poison and white with 0x3f for a critical. Opcode 0x15 of the icon script feeds fdps_icon_script_run's three script bytes straight in as the three biases. Because each step re-derives the DAC from this untouched base rather than from the current DAC, the ramps do not accumulate error and always land back on the exact original palette at bias 0. Nothing in the image writes through the pointer, so the bytes are never modified in place; the pointer itself is reassigned when a savegame is loaded, which frees the block (00023f26) and reloads the same Fde.pal (00023f48).

The other reader is fdps_build_palette_tables at 0002a032, which derives the 16-level shade ramps at 000653f0 and the 16x16x16 inverse-lookup cube at 000643f0 from this palette and writes them out as Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp. That path runs only when the cache is absent: fdps_load_global_resources tests access("FMer1.tmp", 0) first and freads the four .tmp files instead when they are there, and a shipped install has all four, so on a normal run this call never executes.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; the palette is a game resource loaded by the game's own VFS loader and consumed by the game's own DAC primitive, with malloc/free used as leaf services]

=== 000643c0 [PLATE]
Pointer to the decoded SELBAR.CEL sheet, the highlight bar drawn under whichever list entry the cursor is on.

fdps_load_global_resources writes it at startup with the return of fdps_vfs_load_file on "SelBar.cel" out of Misc.vfs; a NULL result there takes the missing-member reporter at 0x000567a0 and exits(1), so every later read may assume it is non-NULL. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it. The sheet holds 3 sprites bounded by 151x17 (resource_info/cel.md), and the sprite index picks the bar width for the list being drawn: sprite 0 is the full-width row bar used by fdps_draw_unit_inventory and fdps_draw_spell_list_page at x 0, y = row * 0x11 + 8; sprite 1 is the shop item cell bar used by fdps_shop_select_item; sprite 2 is the name-row bar used by fdps_shop_render_buy_target_frame, fdps_village_select_member and fdps_church_select_promote_candidate. All readers pass it as the sheet argument of fdps_cel_blit_sprite.

Pool: fdps  [only game UI code reaches it; it holds a game resource loaded from the game's own VFS]

=== 000643c4 [PLATE]
Pointer to the resident global game-text block, the contents of FDETXT00.TXT.

fdps_load_global_resources loads Fdetxt00.txt out of the VFS at startup and stores the buffer here; a NULL result makes it wait for a key and exit(1). fdps_shutdown_free_resources free()s it on the way out. Nothing else writes it, so the block stays resident for the whole run -- unlike the per-chapter text in data_fdps_current_chapter_text_ptr, which is reloaded at every chapter.

Every read hands it to fdps_draw_text as the text_base argument. That routine takes the entry's signed 16-bit word at text_base[text_id] and adds it to the base as a byte offset to find the token stream. Message ids seen in the callers group into ranges: 0x01+character_id for character names (fdps_draw_unit_status_panel, fdps_shop_draw_member_entry, fdps_village_select_member, fdps_church_select_promote_candidate, fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members), 0x97+ and 0xa1+ for the status-panel and class labels, 0xc9+item_id for item names (fdps_draw_unit_inventory, fdps_shop_draw_item_entry), 0x1be+spell_id for spell names (fdps_draw_spell_list_page, fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up), and 0x1e6-0x22a for the fixed prompts of the battle menus, village shops, church, bar, secret menu, lottery, save/load and the CD check. fdps_draw_text also recurses into this same block for its -4 and -5 substitution tokens, using the entry ids in data_fdps_dialog_last_action_text_id_param and data_fdps_dialog_subst_text_id_2.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; it is filled from the game's own VFS loader and consumed by the game's text renderer]

=== 000643c8 [PLATE]
Pointer to the 0xaf8-byte buffer holding the three 117x8 gauge-bar graphics decoded from Bar.cel.

fdps_load_global_resources allocates it once at startup with malloc(0xaf8) (00029de2), zeroes it with memset, then loops i = 0..2 decoding sub-image i of the temporary Bar.cel load, taken from Misc.vfs, into base + i * 0x3a8 through fdps_blit_dispatch as a 0x75 by 8 rectangle at pitch 0x75, and frees the raw cel afterwards. 0x75 * 8 = 0x3a8 and 3 * 0x3a8 = 0xaf8, so the block is exactly three 117x8 8bpp images packed end to end with no header, slack or row padding. Graphic 0 is the empty track, graphic 1 the HP fill and graphic 2 the MP fill: fdps_draw_unit_status_panel draws the HP bar with bar_index 1 at panel offset 0x9396 and the MP bar with bar_index 2 at 0xab56. The only reader is fdps_draw_gauge_bar (00017753, 000177ab), which blits the filled columns from this pointer + bar_index * 0x3a8 and the remaining columns from this pointer + fill_width -- graphic 0 advanced by the same number of columns -- both through fdps_blit_transparent_rect at source pitch 0x75; fdps_draw_gauge_bar_proportional reaches the art the same way, via that function. The pointer lives for the whole run and is never reallocated or cleared; fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it at 000294d8, between the Number.cel sheet at 000643d8 and the font at 000643cc. It is zero until the startup load, since it sits in _BSS.

Pool: fdps  [reached only by game code -- the startup resource loader, the shutdown free and the bar renderer -- and its contents are decoded from the game's own Bar.cel in Misc.vfs]

=== 000643cc [PLATE]
Pointer to the resident 1bpp font sheet, the file Fdetxt.fon loaded whole into the near heap.

fdps_load_global_resources writes it during startup from fdps_vfs_load_file("Fdetxt.fon"); a null result there is fatal, the routine tears the video mode down and exits with status 1. fdps_shutdown_free_resources releases it with free(). The single consumer is fdps_draw_text, which passes it as the font_base argument of fdps_draw_glyph for every glyph it draws -- message tokens and the decimal digits of the -6 number code alike. fdps_draw_glyph reaches glyph n at this base + n * data_fdps_font_glyph_stride_bytes; that stride and the cell metrics are not read from the file, fdps_load_global_resources hard-codes them (0x20 bytes per glyph, a 0x10 by 0x10 cell, 0x10 pixels of advance) just before loading it. The pointer is never cleared after the free and never reloaded, so it is valid from the end of global resource loading until process exit.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: the loader, the shutdown free and the text renderer]

=== 000643d0 [PLATE]
Pointer to the Message.cel sheet, the 302 x 73 panel that the game's message window is drawn from.

fdps_load_global_resources writes it once at startup with the return of fdps_vfs_load_file on "Message.cel" out of Misc.vfs; a NULL result there goes to the missing-member reporter at 0x000567a0 and exit(1), so past startup every read may assume a valid CEL image. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it. The block is kept as the loaded CEL file, never decoded into a standing bitmap, so each reader decodes sprite 0 out of it again: fdps_message_window_open renders it into its 0x561e-byte panel buffer at pitch 0x12e for the six-step slide-up open, fdps_message_window_close does the same for the slide-down close, fdps_message_window_open_from_tile blits it scaled at pitch 0x168 for the seven-step zoom out of a speaker's tile, and fdps_draw_text redraws it at (0x1d, 0x8c) on the battle map when a page-break token composes a fresh panel. Sprite index 0 is the only entry ever asked for.

Pool: fdps  [only pool_fdps code reaches it: the loader, the shutdown free and the four message-window and text routines]

=== 000643d4 [PLATE]
Base of the decoded IconSts.cel sheet, the status-effect icons drawn over units on the battle map.

Written once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources (00029902) from fdps_vfs_load_file("IconSts.cel", Misc.vfs); a null result there makes that function call fdps_wait_any_key and exit(1), so past startup the value is always a valid sheet base and never null. Zero before that, since _BSS is cleared at startup.

The only reader is fdps_draw_map_unit, in its sprite pass. After drawing the unit it calls fdps_unit_select_status_icon(unit_index, data_fdps_map_unit_status_icon_cycle), which returns 0..4 -- the slot of the status-effect timer that is showing this cycle, the five slots being unit-record offsets 0x23, 0x22, 0x24, 0x25 and 0x27 in that order -- or -1 when the unit carries no active effect, in which case nothing is drawn. A non-negative answer is used directly as the CEL frame index: the sprite address is sheet + *(int *)(sheet + frame * 4 + 0x0F), the standard CEL offset table (resource_info/cel.md), and the strip is blitted opaque at 0x18 by 0x0b, 13 scanlines below the top of the unit's cell (dst + 0x1248 at pitch 0x168). Only frames 0..4 are ever fetched, and the blit size is hard-coded rather than taken from the sheet header.

fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it unconditionally as one member of the resource-pointer block 000643a0..000643e4, without clearing it.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: the loader, the map-unit drawer and the shutdown free, all pool fdps]

=== 000643d8 [PLATE]
Pointer to the in-memory NUMBER.CEL sprite sheet, the 65 digit and sign glyphs the game draws numbers with.

fdps_load_global_resources writes it once during startup from fdps_vfs_load_file("Number.cel", ...) and aborts the program through the fatal-error path at 000299fd when the load returns NULL, so every reader may assume it is non-NULL. fdps_shutdown_free_resources free()s it at exit, alongside the neighbouring resource pointers at 000643d4 and 000643c8. The buffer is a raw CEL container: readers skip the 15-byte header and index the u32 offset table hardcoded at +0x0f, adding the base back to the entry to reach the sprite's RLE stream. fdps_draw_number uses glyph index 13 * data_fdps_number_glyph_color_row + g, where g is 0..9 for the digits, 10 for '+', 11 for '-' and 12 for '?', giving five colour rows of thirteen glyphs; fdps_play_indicator_queue hands the same pointer to fdps_cel_blit_sprite in mode 0 with a glyph id out of data_fdps_indicator_queue_glyph_ids to draw floating damage and healing figures. Sprites are 6x8; the sheet header's own width and height fields are never read.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- loaded by the game's VFS reader and consumed by the game's number and indicator drawing]

=== 000643dc [PLATE]
Pointer to the loaded SHADOW.CEL sprite sheet, the 14 24x24 cels used for unit ground shadows and the small blinking UI markers.

Written once during startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which calls fdps_vfs_load_file on "Shadow.cel" and stores the malloc'd buffer here; a null result there is fatal and takes the abort path. fdps_shutdown_free_resources passes it to free at shutdown and does not clear it, so it is a dangling pointer after that point and nothing reads it again. Readers treat the buffer as a raw CEL file and index it through the offset table at the hardcoded file offset 0x0f: fdps_draw_map_unit takes *(int *)(shadow_index * 4 + ptr + 0x0f) + ptr for the per-unit shadow cel and the fixed entry at +0x13 (cel 1) for the other case, while fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input and fdps_spell_list_window_wait_input pass the sheet to fdps_cel_blit_sprite with cel 3 into a 0x240-byte (24x24) scratch buffer, and fdps_prompt_two_choice draws cels 8 and 0xd plus the animated cursor cels 4 + phase and 9 + phase. Cel indices run 0..13.

Pool: fdps  [only game presentation and resource code reaches it; loaded from the game's own VFS and blitted by the game's own CEL blitter]

=== 000643e0 [PLATE]
Pointer to the loaded ADWIN.CEL sheet, the single 43x55 frame that is the background of the tile-info panel shown beside the tactical-map cursor.

Written once at startup by fdps_load_global_resources, which looks ADWin.cel up in Misc.vfs through fdps_vfs_load_file and, on a NULL result, reports through the routine at 000567a0 and exits(1) -- so once the game is running the value is always a valid block. fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel is the only reader: on every frame in which the panel is enabled (data_fdps_ui_terrain_hud_user_enabled and 00060159 both non-zero) it blits sprite 0 of this sheet into the caller's 0x168-pitch frame buffer at x = data_fdps_ui_terrain_hud_panel_offset, y = 0xa0, then draws the terrain icon, the two terrain numbers from the tables at 00060040 and 00060058, and -- when fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor finds a unit under the cursor -- that unit's 24x24 sprite and its current HP on top of it. The panel offset is flipped between 0x124 and 0x19 in the same function so the panel sits on whichever side of the screen the cursor is not. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees this block together with the other global sheets. NULL means the sheet is not loaded yet, which only holds between the CRT clearing _BSS and fdps_load_global_resources running.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it, and it holds a game resource loaded out of the VFS]

=== 000643e4 [PLATE]
Pointer to the combat-scene VGA palette: the 768 bytes of Fight.pal, 256 entries of three 6-bit DAC components in R,G,B order.

fdps_load_global_resources loads it at startup with fdps_vfs_load_file("Fight.pal", misc_vfs), immediately after the main palette at data_fdps_vga_main_palette_ptr; a null result makes that function call fdps_wait_any_key and exit(1), so past startup it is always a valid 768-byte block. That store at 0002978c is the only write in the image, and fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees the block at exit.

Every read hands it to fdps_set_palette_range(ptr, 0, 0xff, 0, 0, 0) -- always with zero bias, never as the base of a fade -- on entry to a full-screen scene whose art is indexed against this palette: fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange, fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets, fdps_church_promote_unit and fdps_play_ending_credit_roll. Each of those four makes the same paired switch: it also reads FMer1.tmp over the 0x4800-byte shade-ramp table at 000653f0 and FMer2.tmp over the 0x1000-byte 16x16x16 inverse-lookup cube at 000643f0 -- the two tables derived from this palette -- and on the way out uploads data_fdps_vga_main_palette_ptr (Fde.pal) again and reads Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp back over the same two tables. The BACK*, STAND*, ACT* and MAGIC* sprites those scenes load carry palette indices meant for this palette and come out miscoloured under any other. Nothing in the image writes through the pointer, so the 768 bytes stay as loaded for the whole run.

The one reader that is not the DAC path is fdps_load_global_resources itself: when access("FMer1.tmp", 0) fails, it calls fdps_build_palette_tables(ptr) to derive the shade ramps and the inverse-lookup cube from this palette and writes them out as FMer1.tmp and FMer2.tmp, then repeats with the main palette for Mer1.tmp and Mer2.tmp. A shipped install has all four files, so on a normal run that branch never executes.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; a game resource loaded by the game's own VFS loader and consumed by the game's own DAC primitive, with malloc and free used as leaf services]

Rebuild note:
The two fdps_build_palette_tables calls in the cache-absent branch share their output buffers at 000653f0 and 000643f0, and this palette has to be the first of the two. Building from the main palette first and this one second produces the same four .tmp files but leaves the shared tables holding the combat-palette version while the map view runs, and nothing reloads Mer1.tmp until the first combat scene ends.

=== 000643e8 [PLATE]
Holds the CD-ROM path prefix the game prepends to every file it reads off the disc.

Written once, by main() at startup: after access("DISK.NO", 0) confirms the game was installed, main opens "Disk.no", throws away the first two whitespace tokens into a stack buffer with fscanf("%s") and stores the third token here. The shipped file reads "CDROM at e:", so the stored value is the bare drive spec "e:" -- no trailing backslash, because every consumer's format string supplies the separator itself. Nothing else ever writes it. fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track formats "%s\\Pack.vfs" from it and probes that path with access() to decide whether the required disc is in the drive, then reads "Pass.Dat" out of that container for the disc number. fdps_play_movie formats "%s\\fd.exe", "%s\\%s.Vid" and "%s\\%s.Aud" from it to build the spawnlp() command line for the external FMV player. The array is three bytes, exactly a two-character drive spec plus its terminator; the byte that follows at 000643eb is the unrelated return-to-title request flag.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- main, fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track, fdps_play_movie -- and its content is a game installation setting]

Rebuild note:
The value is the THIRD whitespace token of Disk.no, not the line: the file reads "CDROM at e:" and main deliberately discards "CDROM" and "at" with two throwaway fscanf("%s") calls. It also carries no trailing separator. Reading the whole line, or storing the drive with a trailing backslash, yields "CDROM at e:\\Pack.vfs" or "e:\\\\Pack.vfs" and the disc check then never finds the disc -- the game sits in the "insert disc" prompt forever.

=== 000643eb [PLATE]
Program-wide quit request: non-zero once the player (or the ending sequence) has asked the game to stop, zero for the whole of a normal session.

main clears it at 00029347, just before its first fdps_title_screen call, and then runs the outer game loop as while (flag == 0) { fdps_battle_player_phase_loop(); dispatch on data_fdps_shared_scene_request; }. Setting it is the only way out of that loop: when the test at 0002935d sees a non-zero byte main falls through to fdps_shutdown_free_resources, fdps_audio_shutdown, fdps_cd_stop_audio, int386(0x10) back to text mode and the "Thank you for playing Flame Dragon Plus!!" printf. Nothing clears it again, so the value is terminal -- once 1, the program is on its way out.

Four places set it to 1, all of them a confirmed "yes" to quit. fdps_title_screen at 0002a8f7 takes the last title-menu item. fdps_battle_system_submenu at 00015014 and fdps_run_bar_shop at 00035ef0 both draw text 0x1f0, run fdps_prompt_two_choice, and set it only when the answer is 0, then draw the acknowledgement text 0x1f1. fdps_chapter_27_end at 0003b981 and fdps_chapter_30_end at 0003bad2 set it after the closing movie, which is how finishing the game ends the process rather than returning to the title.

The flag is also the unwind signal for the nested loops between those writers and main, and fdps_run_village_phase is the one that polls it: at 00031228 it returns 0 immediately if the flag is already set, at 00031491 it loops back to the village menu only while the flag is clear, and at 000314f0 it runs the next chapter's init handler from the table at 00060074 only when the flag is clear. So a quit chosen deep inside the village or a battle menu drops out through every level with the normal teardown intact instead of terminating on the spot.

Values are 0 and 1 only; every reader tests against zero, never against 1.

Pool: fdps  [only game code touches it, and it is the game's own outer-loop state]

Rebuild note:
fdps_chapter_27_end and fdps_chapter_30_end end the game by setting this byte and returning, not by calling exit(). Writing the obvious exit(0) at the end of the ending sequence skips fdps_shutdown_free_resources, fdps_audio_shutdown, fdps_cd_stop_audio and the int386(0x10) return to text mode, leaving the machine in VGA mode 0x13 with CD audio still playing.

=== 000643ec [PLATE]
Pointer to the entry most recently looked up in the resident BaseAni.vfs archive image.

Written and read only by fdps_baseani_get_entry_or_exit, which stores the return of fdps_vfs_image_get_entry(data_fdps_animation_baseani_archive_ptr, name, &size) here, tests it against zero, and returns it. Non-null means the address of that entry's data inside the archive image held by data_fdps_animation_baseani_archive_ptr -- nothing is allocated or copied, so the value stays valid until fdps_shutdown_free_resources releases the archive. Zero means the archive has no such entry, and the caller path then prints "File not found: %s" and calls exit(1), so the value is never observed as null after the function returns. It is always written before it is read, and no other function reaches it.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_baseani_get_entry_or_exit touches it, and it holds a pointer into a game resource archive]

=== 000643f0 [PLATE]
16x16x16 inverse-palette cube: for each 4-bit-per-channel RGB triple, the index of the nearest entry in the current 256-colour palette.

Built by fdps_build_palette_tables, which walks green 0..15 in the outer loop, red in the middle and blue in the inner one and stores fdps_palette_find_nearest_color(red*4, green*4, blue*4, palette) sequentially, so the lookup key is green << 8 | red << 4 | blue -- green-major, not the natural red-major order. fdps_load_global_resources builds it once per palette at startup and caches it: FMer2.tmp holds the cube for Fight.pal and Mer2.tmp the cube for Fde.pal, each written and read back with a single 0x1000-byte fwrite/fread. fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange, fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets, fdps_church_promote_unit and fdps_play_ending_credit_roll swap the two cached cubes in and out of this same buffer with fread as they enter and leave the battle palette.

It is read only through the blitters: fdps_blit_blend_transparent_rect (0x30360) takes it as its inverse_palette argument and, after adding two weighted packed colours from the 18 x 256 dword weighted packed-colour ramp table at DAT_000653f0 and shifting the sum right by 4, folds the three 4-bit channels into that 12-bit key and stores the resulting index into the destination. The same pair of tables is handed to the tint and fade blitters by fdps_draw_composite_sprite, fdps_draw_unit_gauge, fdps_draw_map_unit, fdps_draw_scene_layer, fdps_message_window_open/close, fdps_play_vfs_animation, fdps_show_game_over, fdps_shop_draw_member_entry, fdps_village_select_member, fdps_village_animate_walk_to_destination, fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window, fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up, fdps_play_spell_11_cutscene and fdps_run_bonus_lottery. Values are plain palette indices 0..255 with no sentinel.

Pool: fdps  [only game graphics code reaches it; nothing in the Watcom CRT or Miles AIL does paletted colour matching]

Rebuild note:
The cube is indexed green << 8 | red << 4 | blue, so declaring it as cube[16][16][16] and subscripting [r][g][b] silently swaps red and green in every blended pixel. Its 4096-byte extent is also a file format: Mer2.tmp and FMer2.tmp are dumps of this array, and a build that changes the element size or the axis order will read stale caches left by the original game as garbage rather than rebuilding them.

=== 000653f0 [PLATE]
The game's shade-ramp lookup table: 18 rows of 256 packed nibble-per-channel colour words, one row per shade level, indexed [shade_level][palette_index].

fdps_build_palette_tables fills all 18 rows from the active 256-entry VGA palette: it zeroes row 0, writes row 1 (which lands at 000657f0) as the packed word 0x000R0G0B built from each palette entry's top 4 bits per channel, then fills rows 2..17 with row 1 multiplied by that level's coefficient from binary_artifact_local_array_init_palette_shade_multipliers_2ae40. fdps_load_global_resources writes all 0x4800 bytes to the palette cache file and freads them back; fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange, fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets, fdps_play_ending_credit_roll and fdps_church_promote_unit do the same save/restore around the field-palette to fight-palette swap (Mer1.tmp holds the field copy, FMer1.tmp the fight copy). Every blend blit reads it: fdps_blit_tint_rect and the sibling blitters called from fdps_draw_unit_gauge, fdps_draw_composite_sprite, fdps_draw_map_unit, fdps_draw_scene_layer, fdps_message_window_open, fdps_message_window_close, fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up, fdps_play_vfs_animation, fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window and fdps_show_game_over are handed this address together with the 16x16x16 inverse colour cube at 000643f0 and a shade level in 0..17; they scale source and destination colours through the selected row, add them, and turn the sum back into a palette index through the cube.
