Several callers instead lay the three-dword block {this address, level, 000643f0} on the stack as one blend descriptor (0002a96c, 0002cdbe, 0002c366, 00031f6c, 0002863a, 00036559, 000141f0, 0001baf6, 000332df, 000339cc). Each entry holds its three 4-bit channels in the low nibble of bytes 2, 1 and 0, which is what lets one multiply scale all three at once.

The anchor at 000657f0 is row 1 of this table, not a variable of its own.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; built, persisted and consumed entirely by fdps_ functions]

Rebuild note:
All 18 rows are one contiguous object: fdps_load_global_resources and the battle palette swap fread/fwrite 0x4800 bytes from this address in one call, so declaring the row at 000657f0 as a second array (the shape the code suggests, because the compiler folded &table[1][0] into an absolute address) makes that transfer run off the end of the first array. Also keep the packing: each channel sits in the LOW nibble of its byte (red bits 16-19, green 8-11, blue 0-3), and the 4 bits of headroom above each channel are exactly what stops the multiply by the shade coefficient, whose maximum is 16, from carrying one channel's product into the next byte -- packing 8-bit components at bits 16/8/0 the obvious way makes red bleed into green and green into blue.

=== 000657f0 [EOL]
interior of the object at 000653f0

=== 00069bf0 [PLATE]
Per-layer horizontal scroll position for the field's scrolling scene layer table, one signed int per layer slot, in 1/8-pixel fixed point.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources fills it when a chapter's field is loaded: dsc%02d.dat in Field2.vfs holds the layer count in its first dword followed by one 0x20-byte record per layer, and dword 1 of each record becomes that slot's starting x. fdps_draw_scene_layers then advances it: once per tick, gated on the tick pair 00069d14/00069d64, it adds the per-layer step at 00069c50 to every active slot, and for each layer it draws it computes the blit x as (DAT_00069ce4 * 00069c80[slot] + this[slot]) >> 3 before calling fdps_draw_scene_layer -- so the stored value is eight times the pixel offset, and the shift is arithmetic because a layer that scrolls left runs negative. The slot index runs 0 .. DAT_00069cdc-1, where 00069cdc is the layer count read from dsc%02d.dat; the array is 6 slots wide, matching the 6-entry draw-order list fdps_build_scene_layer_draw_order fills. This is one column of an eight-column structure of arrays covering 00069bf0..00069cb0: x here, y at 00069c08, per-tick step y at 00069c38 and step x at 00069c50, parallax factors y at 00069c68 and x at 00069c80, and the three per-layer resource pointers at 00069c20 (.cel), 00069c98 (attr .dat) and 00069cb0 (.mpl).

Pool: fdps  [reached only by fdps_draw_scene_layers and fdps_field_load_chapter_resources; it holds field scene state parsed from a game resource file]

Rebuild note:
The stored value is a signed 1/8-pixel fixed-point quantity, not a pixel coordinate. Declaring the column unsigned, or dropping the >>3 and treating the file's dword as pixels, gives layers that scroll eight times too fast and left-scrolling layers that wrap to a huge positive x.

=== 00069c08 [PLATE]
Per-scene-layer vertical scroll offset, in eighths of a pixel, one entry per layer (capacity 6).

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources seeds entry i from offset +0x04 of layer i's 0x20-byte record in the chapter's dsc%02d.dat blob (Field2.vfs); the record count at the head of that blob becomes the live layer count at 00069cdc, which bounds every loop over this array. fdps_draw_scene_layers advances it once per frame tick, entry i += data_fdps_scene_layer_scroll_step_y[i] (the array at 00069c38, also from the same record, at +0x14), which is what makes a layer drift on its own. On the draw pass the same function turns it into a pixel origin: y = (view_origin_y * data_fdps_scene_layer_parallax_factor_y[i] + this[i]) >> 3, with view_origin_y at 00069ce0 and the parallax factor at 00069c68 -- a factor of 8 tracks the camera one-for-one, smaller values make the layer lag, which is the parallax. The result is passed as the layer blit's y origin alongside the x origin built the same way from data_fdps_scene_layer_scroll_offset_x (00069bf0). Values are signed and free-running: nothing wraps or clamps them, a negative step walks the accumulator below zero and it stays there.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_field_load_chapter_resources and fdps_draw_scene_layers reach it, both game code]

Rebuild note:
The conversion to pixels is >> 3 on a signed int, not / 8. Writing the obvious `/ 8` makes Watcom emit the round-toward-zero correction, which shifts a layer one pixel whenever the accumulator is negative -- and a negative scroll step in the dsc record puts it there.

=== 00069c20 [PLATE]
Per-layer terrain tile CEL sheets for the field's scrolling scene layer table: slot i holds the heap block of m<chapter><i>.cel, or a stale pointer when slot i is above the current layer count.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources is the only writer. For each slot i below the layer count at 00069cdc -- read from the first dword of dsc%02d.dat -- it builds "m%02d%d.cel" from the chapter number at 00069cf4 and i, and stores fdps_vfs_load_entry("Field1.vfs", name) here; the same loop iteration stores that layer's m<chapter><i>.mpl cell grid at 00069cb0 and its attr<chapter><i>.dat tile-attribute blob at 00069c98. The blob is a CEL sheet in the format resource_info/cel.md describes: width at +0x07 and height at +0x09 (0x18 by 0x18 for these), the sprite count as a signed 16-bit at +0x0b, and the pixel-run offset table at +0x0f. Sprite number n in the sheet is terrain tile id n, the value the .mpl cell grid stores two bytes per cell.

Three loops free it, each bounded by the layer count at 00069cdc and none of them clearing the slot: the loop at the top of fdps_field_load_chapter_resources, which frees the outgoing chapter's layers before the new count is read; fdps_load_field_chapter_resources, which frees them and then sets the count to 0; and fdps_shutdown_free_resources at exit.

Readers: fdps_draw_scene_layers passes slot i as the tile-sheet argument of fdps_draw_scene_layer alongside the .mpl at 00069cb0 and the attribute blob at 00069c98, once for every slot the draw order lists. Two more take slot 0 directly, with no count test, because layer 0 is the playable map: fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel blits sprite DAT_00069d04 -- the tile id under the cursor, latched by fdps_map_load_tile_info -- into the terrain HUD panel, and fdps_cel_expand_sheet_24x24 reads the sprite count at +0x0b and expands the whole sheet into a flat buffer of 0x240-byte 24x24 blocks for fdps_battle_map_overview.

This is one column of the structure of arrays at 00069bf0..00069cb0, six slots wide throughout: scroll x at 00069bf0 and y at 00069c08, per-tick step x at 00069c50 and y at 00069c38, parallax factors x at 00069c80 and y at 00069c68, blend mode bytes at 00069cf8 and depth bytes at 00069cfe.

Pool: fdps  [all six referencing functions are game code, and the contents come from the game's own Field1.vfs resources]

Rebuild note:
Slots are freed only over the live layer count and are never set to NULL, so a slot left behind by a chapter with more layers keeps a dangling pointer. A teardown written the obvious way -- free all six slots -- double-frees those stale slots.

=== 00069c38 [PLATE]
Per-layer vertical auto-scroll step for the field's scrolling scene layer table, one signed int per layer slot, in 1/8-pixel fixed point per tick.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources writes it when a chapter's field is loaded: dsc%02d.dat in Field2.vfs holds the layer count in its first dword followed by one 0x20-byte record per layer, and dword 6 of each record becomes that slot's y step. fdps_draw_scene_layers is the only reader: once per tick, gated on the tick pair 00069d14 / 00069d64, it adds this slot's step to the y scroll accumulator at 00069c08 for every slot 0 .. DAT_00069cdc-1, exactly as the x step at 00069c50 is added to the x accumulator at 00069bf0. Nothing else touches it, so a slot whose record carries 0 is a layer that does not drift on its own and moves only through the parallax term. The value is in the same 1/8-pixel units as the accumulator, which fdps_draw_scene_layers reduces with an arithmetic shift right by 3 before passing it as the blit y; a negative step scrolls the layer upward. The array is 6 slots wide, matching the 6-entry draw-order list fdps_build_scene_layer_draw_order fills, and is one column of an eight-column structure of arrays covering 00069bf0..00069cb0: x accumulator at 00069bf0, y accumulator at 00069c08, step y here, step x at 00069c50, parallax factors y at 00069c68 and x at 00069c80, and the three per-layer resource pointers at 00069c20 (.cel), 00069c98 (attr .dat) and 00069cb0 (.mpl).

Pool: fdps  [reached only by fdps_draw_scene_layers and fdps_field_load_chapter_resources; it holds field scene state parsed from a game resource file]

Rebuild note:
The step is 1/8 pixel per tick and is applied once per change of the tick counter, not once per frame. Treating the dsc dword as whole pixels, or adding it on every call to fdps_draw_scene_layers, scrolls the layers far faster than the original; declaring the column unsigned breaks upward-scrolling layers, whose step is negative.

=== 00069c50 [PLATE]
Per-tick horizontal scroll step for the field's scrolling scene layer table, one signed int per layer slot, in 1/8 pixel per tick.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources fills it when a chapter's field is loaded: dsc%02d.dat in Field2.vfs holds the layer count in its first dword followed by one 0x20-byte record per layer, and dword 4 of each record becomes that slot's x step. fdps_draw_scene_layers is the only reader: at the top of the frame it compares the tick at 00069d14 with the tick at 00069d64 and, when they differ, walks slot 0 .. 00069cdc-1 adding this column into the x accumulator at 00069bf0 and the y step at 00069c38 into the y accumulator at 00069c08, then latches the new tick. A slot's value is therefore applied once per tick, not once per drawn frame. The value is signed and comes straight out of the resource file: a positive step drifts the layer right, a negative step left, and zero pins the layer to the map. Units are eighths of a pixel, because the accumulator this feeds is combined with the parallax term and reduced with an arithmetic shift by 3 before it is used as a blit x.

This is one column of an eight-column structure of arrays covering 00069bf0..00069cb0: scroll x at 00069bf0 and y at 00069c08, per-tick step x here and step y at 00069c38, parallax factors y at 00069c68 and x at 00069c80, and the three per-layer resource pointers at 00069c20 (.cel), 00069c98 (attr .dat) and 00069cb0 (.mpl).

Pool: fdps  [reached only by fdps_draw_scene_layers and fdps_field_load_chapter_resources; it holds field scene state parsed from a game resource file]

Rebuild note:
The column is signed and is applied per tick, not per frame. Declaring it unsigned turns every left-drifting layer into a step of about four million eighth-pixels, and moving the add out of the 00069d14 / 00069d64 tick guard into the per-frame path makes every layer scroll at frame rate instead of tick rate.

=== 00069c68 [PLATE]
Per-layer vertical parallax factor for the field's scrolling scene layer table, one signed int per layer slot, in eighths: how far the layer follows the viewport's y origin.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources writes it when a chapter's field is loaded: dsc%02d.dat in Field2.vfs holds the layer count in its first dword followed by one 0x20-byte record per layer, and dword 3 of each record (byte offset 0xc) becomes that slot's y factor. fdps_draw_scene_layers is the only reader, in both of its passes: for each slot it draws it computes the layer's vertical scroll offset as (DAT_00069ce0 * this[slot] + 00069c08[slot]) >> 3 and passes it as the y argument of fdps_draw_scene_layer, where DAT_00069ce0 is the viewport origin's y in map pixels and 00069c08 is the slot's own accumulated auto-scroll position. Because the sum is reduced by an arithmetic shift of 3, the factor is in eighths of the viewport movement: 8 makes the layer track the camera one for one, 4 makes it move at half speed, 0 pins it to the map, and a negative value makes it drift against the camera. The multiply is signed and so is the shift, so the whole chain is meant to go negative. The slot index runs 0 .. DAT_00069cdc-1, where 00069cdc is the layer count read from dsc%02d.dat; the array is 6 slots wide, matching the 6-entry draw-order list fdps_build_scene_layer_draw_order fills. This is one column of an eight-column structure of arrays covering 00069bf0..00069cb0: x accumulator at 00069bf0, y accumulator at 00069c08, per-tick step y at 00069c38 and step x at 00069c50, parallax factor y here and x at 00069c80, and the three per-layer resource pointers at 00069c20 (.cel tileset), 00069c98 (attr .dat) and 00069cb0 (.mpl map).

Pool: fdps  [reached only by fdps_draw_scene_layers and fdps_field_load_chapter_resources; it holds field scene state parsed from a game resource file]

Rebuild note:
The factor is in eighths of the viewport origin and is combined with the accumulator before the shift, not after: the original computes (camera_y * factor + accumulator) >> 3 with a signed multiply and an arithmetic shift. Writing the obvious camera_y * factor + accumulator, or shifting the two terms separately, or declaring the column unsigned, makes every parallax layer scroll eight times too far and turns a negative factor -- a layer that drifts against the camera -- into an enormous positive one.

=== 00069c80 [PLATE]
Per-layer horizontal parallax factor for the field's scrolling scene layer table, one signed int per layer slot, in eighths of the camera's motion.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources fills it when a chapter's field is loaded: dsc%02d.dat in Field2.vfs holds the layer count in its first dword followed by one 0x20-byte record per layer, and dword 3 of each record becomes that slot's x factor. Nothing else writes it, and fdps_draw_scene_layers is its only reader: for each layer it draws it computes the source scroll origin as (DAT_00069ce4 * this[slot] + DAT_00069bf0[slot]) >> 3 and passes it to fdps_draw_scene_layer as scroll_x. DAT_00069ce4 is the shared view origin in x, DAT_00069bf0 is that layer's own scroll accumulator, and the arithmetic shift by 3 puts both terms in the same 1/8-pixel scale -- so a factor of 8 makes the layer track the camera one for one, a smaller factor makes it lag behind, and 0 pins it to the map. The slot index runs 0 .. DAT_00069cdc-1, where 00069cdc is the layer count read from dsc%02d.dat; the array is 6 slots wide, matching the 6-entry draw-order list fdps_build_scene_layer_draw_order fills. This is one column of an eight-column structure of arrays covering 00069bf0..00069cb0: scroll accumulator x here at 00069bf0 and y at 00069c08, per-tick step y at 00069c38 and step x at 00069c50, parallax factor y at 00069c68 and x here, and the three per-layer resource pointers at 00069c20 (.cel tileset), 00069c98 (attr .dat) and 00069cb0 (.mpl tile map).

Pool: fdps  [reached only by fdps_draw_scene_layers and fdps_field_load_chapter_resources; it holds field scene state parsed from a game resource file]

Rebuild note:
The column is signed and its product with the view origin is reduced by an arithmetic shift. Declaring it unsigned makes the whole expression unsigned under C's usual arithmetic conversions, so the >> 3 becomes a logical shift and every layer whose combined scroll origin is negative -- which fdps_draw_scene_layer explicitly expects and floors by hand -- jumps to a huge positive offset instead.

=== 00069c98 [PLATE]
Per-layer pointers to the loaded "attr<chapter><layer>.dat" tile-attribute blob of each scene layer -- one column of the 6-slot scene layer table.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources writes it: for each layer i below the layer count at 00069cdc it loads "attr%02d%d.dat" from Field2.vfs with fdps_vfs_load_entry and stores the block in slot i; the same routine frees the previous chapter's slots first, using the count still left over from that chapter. fdps_load_field_chapter_resources frees every slot and then zeroes the layer count; fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees them at exit. Neither clears the slots, so after a free the stale pointers stay in the array and only the layer count keeps them from being used again.

The blob is a raw resource image: 0x11 bytes of header, then one 4-byte attribute record per tile id. fdps_map_load_tile_info reads slot 0 as [ptr] + 0x11 + tile_id*4 and publishes the record's bytes 0, 1, 2 and 3 into 00069d08, 00069d0a, 00069d09 and 00069d0b; byte 2 is the terrain type, which fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range uses as the index into the acting class's 8-entry movement-cost table (0xff there meaning impassable). fdps_draw_scene_layers passes slot i to the layer blitter FUN_0002c330 as its seventh argument, alongside the layer's mpl image at 00069cb0 and cel at 00069c20.

Index range is 0..layer count-1, the count coming from the first dword of "dsc<chapter>.dat"; the array itself has room for exactly 6.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: the field loaders, the shutdown path, the scene compositor and the battle map readers]

Rebuild note:
The free loop at the top of fdps_field_load_chapter_resources runs over the OUTGOING chapter's layer count, before the count is replaced from the new "dsc<chapter>.dat". Freeing all six slots instead, or moving the free loop after the descriptor load, double-frees or leaks whenever two chapters differ in layer count.

=== 00069cb0 [PLATE]
Per-layer pointers to the loaded "m<chapter><layer>.mpl" cell grid of each scene layer -- the tile-id column of the 6-slot scene layer table. Slot 0 is the playable map, and the rest of the game reads it straight through this address.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources is the only writer. For each slot i below the layer count at 00069cdc -- the first dword of dsc%02d.dat -- it builds "m%02d%d.mpl" from the chapter number at 00069cf4 and i and stores fdps_vfs_load_entry("Field1.vfs", name) at 00022ad6; the same loop iteration stores that layer's tile sheet m<chapter><i>.cel at 00069c20 and its attribute blob attr<chapter><i>.dat at 00069c98. Three loops free it, each bounded by the layer count and none of them clearing the slot: the loop at the top of fdps_field_load_chapter_resources (00022812), fdps_load_field_chapter_resources (00031622), and fdps_shutdown_free_resources (0002960f) at exit.

The blob is a raw .MPL image: the four bytes "MPL\0" at +0, the width as a signed 16-bit at +7, the height at +9, then width*height 16-bit tile ids from +0xb in row-major order, so cell (x,y) sits at +0xb + (y*width + x)*2. The shipped sizes agree -- M110.MPL is 401 bytes = 11 + 15*13*2, M000.MPL is 1451 = 11 + 30*24*2 (resource_info/vfs.md). A cell's tile id is both the sprite number in that layer's CEL sheet at 00069c20 and the index into the 4-byte attribute records of the blob at 00069c98.

fdps_draw_scene_layers passes slot i as the image argument of fdps_draw_scene_layer, once for every slot the draw order lists. Every other reader takes slot 0 with no count test, because layer 0 defines the map: fdps_field_load_chapter_resources reads its width and height to malloc the working grid at 00060144 as width*height*2+4; fdps_battle_map_overview, fdps_render_map_overview_scaled and fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes take both dimensions; fdps_animate_move_step_right takes the width and fdps_walk_step_down the height, each times the 0x18-pixel tile size, as the scroll extent; fdps_map_load_tile_info and fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range read cells out of the grid at +0xb; fdps_icon_script_run opcode 0x14 writes one. fdps_map_actor_use_item is the exception and reads the wrong offsets -- see the rebuild note on that function.

Index range is 0 .. layer count-1; the array itself has room for exactly 6.

Pool: fdps  [all thirteen referencing functions are game code, and the contents come from the game's own Field1.vfs resources]

Rebuild note:
Nine of the thirteen referencing functions see only slot 0, as a plain pointer that is dereferenced -- MOV EAX,[0x00069cb0] then MOVSX word ptr [EAX + 0x7]. Declaring this global the obvious way, as a single byte * map pointer, makes the two loops that walk it as (&it)[i] run off into the neighbouring column at 00069cc8. It is a 6-element array, and every scalar-looking use is element 0.

=== 00069cc8 [PLATE]
Free-running walk-animation counter shared by every unit sprite drawn on the tactical map, cycling 0..15.

fdps_draw_map_unit owns it: when the frame tick at 00069d64 differs from the value latched in 00069d18, that function re-latches the tick and steps this counter as (n + 1) % 0x10, alongside the status-icon counter at 00069d1c. The latch is what keeps the step to once per tick even though fdps_draw_map_units calls the draw routine twice per unit (shadow pass and sprite pass).

Both fdps_draw_map_unit and fdps_blit_unit_sprite read it the same way: the walk frame is counter / 4 with the value 3 folded back to 1, so the three sprites of a facing play 0, 1, 2, 1 and one full ping-pong takes 16 ticks. fdps_draw_map_unit additionally uses counter % 2 as a one-pixel horizontal displacement for a unit carrying the paralysis counter at record +0x26, which pins it to frame 0 and makes it shiver in place instead of walking.

The counter is global, not per unit: every unit on the map animates in lockstep, and nothing resets it at chapter or battle start -- it simply continues from wherever the previous map left it. The CRT zeroes it at startup, so the first map begins at frame 0.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_draw_map_unit and fdps_blit_unit_sprite reach it, both game-logic map rendering]

Rebuild note:
The walk phase is a single global, not a field of the 0x50-byte unit record. Giving each unit its own phase -- the obvious layout, and the one FD2's record used -- makes units animate out of step with each other, which the original never does.

=== 00069ccc [PLATE]
Map cursor position on the Y (row) axis, in map pixels: tile row * 0x18, except mid-walk where it is stepped 4 pixels at a time.

Paired with data_fdps_map_cursor_world_x at 00069cd4; the view-window origin it is drawn against is 00069ce0 (Y) / 00069ce4 (X). fdps_chapter_state_reset clears it to 0 when a chapter starts, fdps_load_savegame restores it as saved-record byte 0x30c9 * 0x18, and fdps_icon_script_run / fdps_icon_script_scroll_view_to_tile park it one tile inside the scrolled view. The player moves it in fdps_map_cursor_select_loop and fdps_battle_player_phase_loop: scancode 0x48 (Up) subtracts one tile if the cursor is not already on row 0, 0x50 (Down) adds one tile while it stays below map_height * 0x18. fdps_map_cursor_move_to walks it toward a requested target and scrolls 00069ce0 to keep it inside the window. Readers divide by 0x18 to get the 0-based tile row: fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor, fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor, fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel, fdps_map_load_tile_info callers and the battle menu/spell/item command functions all do so, and fdps_draw_map_cursor and fdps_render_ring_menu_frame use the raw pixel value minus 00069ce0 to place the cursor and ring-menu sprites. fdps_collect_targets_in_line does not read it as a cursor at all: it saves it, drives it along a straight line of tiles so that fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor sees each tile in turn, and restores it before returning. The value can be negative for the duration of that scan, which is exactly what its bound test looks for.

Pool: fdps  [all 25 referencing functions are pool fdps; nothing in crt or ail touches it]

Rebuild note:
fdps_collect_targets_in_line passes its scan position to fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor through this global and 00069cd4, not as arguments. Rewriting the scan with local x/y and calling the finder with them, or dropping the save/restore, silently changes which units the line hits and leaves the player's cursor moved. It must also stay a signed int: as an unsigned type the scan's (-1 < value) bound test is always true and the compiler emits DIV instead of IDIV.

=== 00069cd0 [PLATE]
Which cursor footprint fdps_draw_map_cursor paints on the battle map this frame.

Written all over the game logic, always with a literal or with an ability's area-of-effect code plus 2. 0 means paint nothing, and is stored before any sequence that must not have a cursor over it: the walk in fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_opponent and fdps_map_actor_move_toward_nearest_reachable_opponent, the rest sequence in fdps_unit_rest, the level-up banner in fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up, the status sweep in fdps_battle_tick_status_effects, the icon-script sequences (fdps_icon_script_run, fdps_icon_script_walk_units, fdps_icon_script_set_unit_facing, fdps_icon_script_blink_units_out) and every chapter reinforcement event that pans the camera. 1 is the ordinary single-tile cursor and is what those sequences store on the way out; fdps_chapter_state_reset also leaves it at 1. 2..6 come from fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell and fdps_battle_spell_command (spell record byte +4, plus 2), fdps_battle_item_menu and fdps_map_actor_use_item (item record byte +0x12, plus 2), and fdps_map_actor_use_item stores a bare 6 at 00027356 before it scrolls the cursor across the map.

Read in three places. fdps_draw_map_cursor dispatches: 1 is the bare cursor tile (sprite 0), 2 the bare tile with sprite 1, 3/4/5 the radius-1/2/3 diamonds, and 6 draws nothing at all -- it instead divides the cursor position by the 0x18-pixel tile size and clears byte 1 of that cell in the battle grid at DAT_00060144, marking every tile the cursor travels over. fdps_map_cursor_move_to re-renders a frame at each step of a cursor move only while this is non-zero. fdps_map_cursor_select_loop derives the targeting radius from it: the value itself when it is 1, otherwise the value minus 1, handed to fdps_collect_targets_in_area -- so the same variable that picks the drawn footprint also picks which tiles the selection actually hits.

Pool: fdps  [only game-logic functions reach it; no library code touches this address]

Rebuild note:
The exit paths store the literal 1, they do not restore what the variable held on entry, and fdps_map_cursor_select_loop reads the targeting radius back out of it as mode-1. Writing the obvious save/restore around the hidden-cursor sequences, or giving the drawing its own variable, changes which tiles an ability can select.

=== 00069cd4 [PLATE]
Battle/map cursor position, X axis, in map pixel coordinates (24 pixels per tile) rather than tile columns.

Written as tile_x * 0x18: fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes it together with data at 0x69ccc/0x69ce0/0x69ce4 when a chapter starts, fdps_load_savegame restores it from byte 5 of the save record times 0x18, and fdps_icon_script_run / fdps_icon_script_scroll_view_to_tile park it one tile in from the view origin. fdps_map_cursor_select_loop and fdps_battle_player_phase_loop move it with the arrow keys, scancode 0x4b subtracting 0x18 and 0x4d adding 0x18, clamped so it never leaves the range [0x18, map_width_px - 0x18]. fdps_map_cursor_move_to slides it toward a requested pixel position and then scrolls the view origin at 0x69ce4 so that the cursor stays between 0x18 and 0xd8 pixels inside the 0x138-pixel-wide (13 tile) visible window; fdps_animate_move_step_left / fdps_animate_move_step_right nudge it 4 pixels at a time while a unit walks, so between those steps the value is NOT tile aligned.

Almost every reader divides it back to a tile column with a signed IDIV by 0x18 and passes that to a helper: fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor, fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor, fdps_battle_unit_turn, fdps_battle_action_menu, fdps_battle_item_menu, fdps_battle_spell_command, fdps_map_actor_use_item, fdps_battle_map_overview. Readers that draw subtract the view origin at 0x69ce4 first to get a screen pixel X: fdps_draw_map_cursor (which also offsets by +/-0x18 and +/-0x30 to place the pieces of the multi-tile cursor shape selected by 0x69cd0), fdps_render_ring_menu_frame and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel. fdps_collect_targets_in_line saves the value, walks it along a line by +/-0x18 per step while it stays within [0, map_width_px), and restores it before returning.

Pool: fdps  [all 138 xrefs are in pool_fdps game logic; nothing in the CRT or the sound library touches it]

Rebuild note:
fdps_collect_targets_in_line drives fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor, which takes no arguments, by writing this global and restoring it afterwards; rewriting the scan with a local x and a find_unit(x, y) call breaks it. The value is also deliberately allowed to go negative there and the guard is a signed test, so it must stay a signed int.

=== 00069cd8 [PLATE]
Base address of the heap array of 0x50-byte unit records for the map currently in play; the number of live records is held separately in DAT_00060150.

NULL while no map is loaded -- _BSS leaves it zero at startup and fdps_run_village_phase stores 0 back into it after dropping the array. Four routines publish a block into it. fdps_build_map_unit_array frees the previous array when DAT_00060150 is non-zero, sets the count to the map's player-slot count DAT_00064118 and mallocs DAT_00064118 * 0x50 for it. fdps_deploy_unit appends: with the count still 0 it mallocs one 0x50-byte record, otherwise it reallocs to (DAT_00060150 + 1) * 0x50. fdps_load_savegame frees the old block and mallocs a fixed 0x1e00 bytes -- room for 96 records regardless of the count -- then memmoves DAT_00060150 * 0x50 bytes into it from offset 0x12a3 of the save buffer; the matching save side is the memmove out in fdps_battle_system_submenu. fdps_load_field_chapter_resources adopts the field/village roster block DAT_00064108 together with its count DAT_00064114, freeing the outgoing block only when it is not that same block. fdps_relocate_unit_array moves the array to a fresh, randomly displaced allocation and is called at the top of every unit iteration in fdps_battle_unit_turn, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase and FUN_00012960, so the address changes constantly. fdps_shutdown_free_resources frees it when non-NULL.

Readers resolve record i as base + i * 0x50, i running 0 .. DAT_00060150 - 1. fdps_get_unit_record is the accessor that does exactly that, but most call sites inline the IMUL: fdps_battle_unit_turn, fdps_map_actor_behavior_step, fdps_battle_player_phase_loop, fdps_map_cursor_select_loop, fdps_draw_map_unit, fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel, fdps_battle_map_overview, fdps_unit_select_status_icon, the four move-step animators, and the scanning loops fdps_battle_find_unit_at_cursor, fdps_battle_find_unit_by_character_id, fdps_collect_targets_in_area, fdps_move_grid_block_occupied_tiles and fdps_move_grid_mark_opposing_zones_of_control. Record fields the code reaches through this pointer: +0 and +1 the unit's tile column and row, +2 its CEL sprite-cache slot, +5 the status flags -- bit 0 out of play, bit 7 has already acted this phase, set by fdps_battle_mark_unit_done and cleared for every unit by fdps_units_clear_status_bit7 -- +6 the side with 2 meaning the player, +7 and +8 the character id, +0x20 the class id that fdps_map_cursor_select_loop passes to fdps_get_class_record as class + 1.

Pool: fdps  [every one of the 51 references is game code; the 0x50-byte record stride and the count at DAT_00060150 are the game's own map state]

Rebuild note:
This pointer does not always own its block, and the block moves. fdps_load_field_chapter_resources assigns it DAT_00064108 and guards the preceding free with 'pointer != DAT_00064108'; write the obvious 'free(units); units = field_units;' and the guarded case double-frees a block the other global still points at. Separately, fdps_relocate_unit_array reallocates the array on every unit iteration, so no record pointer survives a call to it -- hoisting 'unit = &units[i]' out of a loop that calls it, which is what a C rewrite naturally does, leaves a pointer into memory that has been memset to zero and freed.

=== 00069cdc [PLATE]
Number of scene layers the current field chapter has, i.e. how many entries of the parallel scene-layer arrays at 00069bf0/00069c08/00069c20/00069c38/00069c50/00069c68/00069c80/00069c98/00069cb0 are live.

Set from data by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources: it loads "dsc%02d.dat" for the chapter in DAT_00069cf4 out of Field2.vfs and stores the blob's first dword here (0002297b), then walks 0..count-1 scattering that file's 0x20-byte records into the parallel per-layer globals and loading "m%02d%d.mpl", "m%02d%d.cel" and "attr%02d%d.dat" for each layer. Reset to 0 by main at startup (0002933d) and by fdps_load_field_chapter_resources at 00031662 once it has freed the layer buffers of the outgoing chapter. Read purely as a loop bound: fdps_field_load_chapter_resources (000227f6) and fdps_shutdown_free_resources (000295f3) free the i-th pointer of each layer array for i < count; fdps_draw_scene_layers walks it three times per frame (0002bf83, 0002bff7, 0002c113), once per drawing pass; fdps_build_scene_layer_draw_order fills draw_order[0..count-1] with 0,1,2,... (0002c236) and then bubble-sorts it, using count-1 as the outer bound (0002c265) and count-i-1 as the inner (0002c284). Zero is the legitimate no-layers state and every loop degenerates cleanly to no iterations; the value is otherwise a small positive count -- the arrays it indexes hold 6 elements.

Pool: fdps  [only game functions reach it, and it is filled from a game resource file]

=== 00069ce0 [PLATE]
Vertical origin of the scrolling tile-map view, in map pixels; the x counterpart is at 00069ce4.

fdps_chapter_state_reset zeroes it when a chapter starts; fdps_load_savegame restores it as saved_tile_row * 0x18 and fdps_battle_system_submenu writes it back out as origin / 0x18. The cursor loops fdps_map_cursor_select_loop and fdps_battle_player_phase_loop scroll it a tile (0x18) at a time to keep the cursor row 00069ccc inside the window, fdps_map_cursor_move_to clamps it to 0 .. map_rows * 0x18 - 0xc0 (0xc0 = 192 px = 8 tiles, the window height) and keeps the cursor between +0x18 and +0x90 of it, and fdps_walk_step_down / fdps_animate_move_step_up nudge it by 4 pixels per animation pass, six passes per tile. The icon-script opcodes set it directly: fdps_icon_script_run opcode 0x0d writes tile_row * 0x18, fdps_icon_script_scroll_view_to_tile steps it one pixel per frame toward a target and then stores the exact target, and fdps_icon_script_animate_view_offset saves it, drives an offset animation and restores it. fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets and fdps_cast_spell_on_targets shake the view by adding rand()%4 - 2 for a few frames and restore the saved value afterwards, so the value is briefly negative when the view sits at the top of the map.

Every drawing pass reads it. fdps_blit_cursor_tile and fdps_draw_map_unit convert a map position to a scene-buffer offset as (map_y - origin + 0x18) * 0x168 + (map_x - 00069ce4) and cull to origin - 0x18 < y < origin + 0xc0; fdps_blit_unit_sprite, fdps_play_attack_animation, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units, fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up and fdps_battle_compute_unit_gauge_position place sprites at unit_record[1] * 0x18 - origin plus a fixed bias; fdps_draw_scene_layers multiplies it by data_fdps_scene_layer_parallax_factor_y[layer] for the parallax backdrops; fdps_show_number_indicator, fdps_show_miss_indicator, fdps_show_cure_indicator and fdps_show_sprite_indicator cull by tile row against origin / 0x18 - 1 .. origin / 0x18 + 8; fdps_render_ring_menu_frame and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel use 00069ccc - origin as the cursor's on-screen y.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; it is read and written solely by the tile-map view, cursor and drawing functions]

Rebuild note:
Declare it a signed int. It goes negative during the item/spell screen shake, the /0x18 conversions are signed truncating divisions, and fdps_map_cursor_move_to's "if (origin < 0) origin = 0" clamp becomes dead code under an unsigned type, which would let the view scroll off the top of the map.

=== 00069ce4 [PLATE]
X of the battle map view window's top-left corner, in world pixels.

The camera origin for everything drawn on the tactical map. Screen X for a map object is object_x - this, and the visible window is 0x138 (312) pixels = 13 tile columns wide, so the visible tile columns run this / 0x18 - 1 through this / 0x18 + 0xd. fdps_blit_cursor_tile and fdps_draw_map_unit reject anything outside this .. this + 0x138 before drawing; fdps_blit_unit_sprite, fdps_play_attack_animation, fdps_play_death_animation_and_mark_dead, fdps_play_vfs_animation_over_units, fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up and fdps_battle_compute_unit_gauge_position all place sprites as tile_column * 0x18 - this plus a per-caller offset; fdps_show_number_indicator, fdps_show_miss_indicator, fdps_show_cure_indicator and fdps_show_sprite_indicator use the divided-by-0x18 form for their visibility test; fdps_draw_scene_layers multiplies it by data_fdps_scene_layer_parallax_factor_x to derive each background layer's own scroll. 00069ce0 is the matching Y.

fdps_chapter_state_reset sets it to 0 at the start of a chapter. It follows the cursor during play: fdps_map_cursor_move_to, fdps_map_cursor_select_loop and fdps_battle_player_phase_loop keep the cursor global 00069cd4 inside a margin of it (a whole tile at a time in the loops, clamped to 0 at the low end and to map_width * 0x18 - 0x138 at the high end), and fdps_animate_move_step_left / fdps_animate_move_step_right scroll it 4 pixels at a time while a unit walks, so mid-walk it is not tile-aligned. fdps_icon_script_run opcode 0x0d sets it outright from a tile column in the icon script, fdps_icon_script_scroll_view_to_tile pans it to a target tile in equal steps and then writes the exact target, and fdps_icon_script_animate_view_offset, fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets and fdps_cast_spell_on_targets shake the view by writing saved_origin + offset each frame and restoring the saved value at the end. fdps_battle_system_submenu stores it into the savegame as a single tile-column byte at buffer offset 0x30c6 and fdps_load_savegame restores it as that byte * 0x18. Values are pixel offsets into the map, normally >= 0 and a multiple of 4.

Pool: fdps  [only game-logic functions reference it; it is the tactical map camera]

Rebuild note:
The view-shake and view-pan loops write origin = saved_origin + step_offset, not origin += step_offset. Writing the natural += accumulates the ramp (ICON06.DAT's -6,-12,-18,-24 becomes -6,-18,-36,-60) and leaves the camera displaced when the loop ends.

=== 00069ce8 [PLATE]
The battle turn number of the battle in progress, 1-based.

fdps_chapter_state_reset sets it to 1 when a chapter's battle state is initialised; fdps_load_savegame restores it from byte 0x30c3 of the save image (zero-extended, 0002410c) and fdps_battle_system_submenu stores it back there as a single byte (000151c8), so the persisted range is 0..255 even though the variable is a 32-bit signed int. fdps_battle_advance_turn raises it by one per turn cycle at 0001e5fd -- after the enemy phase, after fdps_battle_run_turn_events has already run for the turn just played, and only when the battle-end code at 0x00069da0 is still 0, so an aborted battle does not advance it.

Readers fall into three groups. Display: fdps_draw_turn_number formats it with sprintf("%d") and fdps_battle_show_win_fail_window draws it in 3 digits on the result window. Scripted schedules: fdps_battle_run_turn_events compares it against the turn byte of each entry of the map's turn-event table at 0x0006013c + 3 to decide which handler fires this turn. Chapter scripts: the per-chapter event and post-action handlers branch on it, either against a literal turn (chapter 8 at turns 1, 3, 4, 10, 12; chapter 22 at 1, 3, 5, 8, 9; chapter 24 at 5, 8, 7, 10, 13, 15), as a deadline (chapter 16's wandering smith and chapter 20's sword upgrade need turn <= 0x14, chapters 15 and 24 need turn <= 0x19, chapter 19 needs turn <= 0x14), or as the key that picks a reinforcement wave -- fdps_deploy_wave is called with turn - 1 (chapter 3), turn - 4 (chapter 10), turn - 7 (chapter 17), turn itself (chapter 18), turn + 4 (chapter 23) and turn / 2 (chapter 28).

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: the battle loop, the chapter event scripts and the save/load pair, no library reference at all]

Rebuild note:
The counter is 1-based and is read for a turn before it is advanced for that turn. It lives in _BSS, so the CRT zeroes it, but the first player phase runs with the value 1 that fdps_chapter_state_reset wrote, and fdps_battle_advance_turn increments it only after fdps_battle_run_turn_events has fired the turn's scripted events. Starting it at 0, or incrementing at the top of the turn instead of after the events, shifts every scheduled reinforcement wave and every deadline by one turn.

=== 00069cec [PLATE]
Experience owed to the unit currently acting, accumulated over one action and spent by the level-up routine.

Cleared at the top of each action by fdps_battle_action_menu, fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack, fdps_map_actor_cast_chosen_spell, fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange, fdps_map_actor_use_item, fdps_apply_item_effect_to_targets and fdps_battle_player_phase_loop. While the action resolves, fdps_unit_apply_damage and fdps_unit_apply_heal add a share of the damage or healing they just applied, and fdps_unit_apply_status_effect adds the target's level (record +0x21) times 10; fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit and fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome instead assign, from the target's level times the enemy record's reward field, scaled by the attacker/defender ratio. Before the award the caller scales the total: fdps_map_actor_move_and_attack and fdps_battle_action_menu take (total * 15) / 10 with signed truncating division, and fdps_battle_spell_command divides by a per-spell divisor.

fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up is the sole consumer. It returns immediately when the value is 0, clamps anything above 99 down to 99, adds the result to the unit's leftover-experience byte at record +0x3c, shows it in the level-up window through fdps_draw_number, and zeroes the global on its way out. fdps_icon_script_run pokes it to 99 directly for the debug command that levels a unit ten times over. Range after the clamp is 0..99; 0 is the sentinel meaning "nothing to award".

Pool: fdps  [only game-logic functions reference it; it is written and read entirely inside the battle and unit modules]

Rebuild note:
fdps_unit_award_exp_and_level_up leaves this global untouched on all three of its early exits (value is 0, unit retired, unrecognised id) -- only the path that runs to the end clears it. Clearing it on entry or in a single exit epilogue, which is the natural way to write the function, changes behaviour: the callers rely on the leftover surviving those exits and clear it themselves at the start of the next action.

=== 00069cf0 [PLATE]
Number of CEL sprite groups currently held in the cache, i.e. how many slots of data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr and data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_group_ids are live.

fdps_cache_cel_sprite_group is the only function that raises it and the only one that reads it for anything but a zero test. When it is 0 that function takes the seeding path: it writes the requested group index into slot 0 of data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_group_ids, mallocs the cache buffer, fills the twelve dword sprite offsets of slot 0 and increments this to 1. When it is non-zero the same function scans slots 0..count-1 for the requested group and returns the slot on a hit; on a miss it stores the key at slot count, reallocs, appends the pixels at the byte cursor data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_buffer_used, writes the twelve offsets of the new slot at element count * 0xc (slot * 0x30 bytes), then increments this and returns count - 1. So the value is both 'how many groups are cached' and 'the slot the next group will take', and the function's return value is always this value minus one.

Everywhere else it is read only as the cache-populated flag: fdps_build_map_unit_array (00022bf1), fdps_load_savegame (00024070), fdps_saveload_screen_build (000249ab), fdps_draw_save_slot_panel (00024a8f), fdps_load_field_chapter_resources (0003166c) and fdps_roster_revive_fallen_members (00039f35) each free data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr when this is non-zero and then store 0 here, dropping the whole cache before loading the sheet they need. main stores 0 at startup (00029333), before anything has been allocated.

Values: 0 means nothing is cached and the next request will malloc a fresh buffer; otherwise slots 0..count-1 are valid and slots at or past it hold stale keys and offsets, because the teardown sites reset only this variable. Nothing bounds it against the 30 slots that fit in the 0x5a0-byte offset table reserved at the head of the cache buffer.

Pool: fdps  [only game functions reach it; it counts entries in a cache that game code allocates, indexes and frees, with no CRT or AIL reference]

Rebuild note:
This count, not the pointer, is the cache-empty predicate. The six teardown sites free data_fdps_cel_sprite_cache_ptr and zero this variable while deliberately leaving the pointer dangling, so rewriting the test as the obvious cache_ptr != NULL reads freed memory as a populated cache; keep every guard on the count exactly as written, and reset only this variable at teardown.

=== 00069cf4 [PLATE]
The 0-based id of the chapter the game is currently playing or about to play, 0..0x1d for the player's chapters 1..30.

fdps_title_screen sets it to 0 when a new game starts and fdps_title_demo sets it to 0x19 for the attract-mode battle. fdps_load_savegame (00023f58) and fdps_load_game_screen (000245ae) restore it from a save slot record, and fdps_save_game_screen writes its low byte back into the slot. Each fdps_chapter_NN_end handler stores the next chapter's index as its last act -- fdps_chapter_01_end stores 1, ... fdps_chapter_29_end stores 0x1d -- so the village phase that main runs next belongs to the following chapter; chapter 30's handler deliberately leaves it alone and goes to the ending instead. fdps_icon_script_run can also store it (00021c26) from a script opcode operand, which is how a scripted scene jumps chapters.

Readers use it two ways. As a table index: main, fdps_run_village_phase, fdps_battle_enemy_turn_phase, fdps_battle_npc_turn_phase, fdps_battle_unit_turn and fdps_battle_tick_status_effects scale it by 4 and call through data_fdps_chapter_init_handler_table (0x60074), data_fdps_chapter_post_action_handler_table (0x6028c) and data_fdps_chapter_end_handler_table (0x60304); fdps_check_secret_code_key scales it by 8 to pick the chapter's secret-code key sequence. As the %02d of a per-chapter asset name: fdps_field_load_chapter_resources and fdps_load_field_chapter_resources format it into fdetxt%02d.txt (with +1), map%02d.dat, M%02d.dtl, dsc%02d.dat, m%02d%d.mpl, m%02d%d.cel, attr%02d%d.dat and Shop%02d.dat (raw), and fdps_deploy_wave formats it into map%02d.cod. It is also compared against literal chapter ids to gate content -- fdps_shop_select_buy_target, fdps_village_select_member and fdps_roster_add_item_to_all test >= 0x17, fdps_run_village_phase tests 0xf/0x11/0x15/0x16/0x19 to choose which village layout runs, and fdps_play_ending_credit_roll tests 0x1d and 0x1a. fdps_battle_show_win_fail_window prints it as chapter+1, the number the player sees.

Pool: fdps  [all 133 references come from pool_fdps game-logic functions; no CRT or AIL code touches it]

Rebuild note:
The global is 0-based but the asset names built from it are not consistently 0-based: fdetxt%02d.txt takes the value plus one while map%02d.dat, M%02d.dtl, dsc%02d.dat, m%02d%d.mpl, m%02d%d.cel, attr%02d%d.dat, Shop%02d.dat and map%02d.cod take it raw. Normalising the off-by-one -- storing a 1-based chapter number, or adding 1 at every sprintf -- loads the wrong chapter's files.

=== 00069cf8 [PLATE]
Per-layer tile-attribute mode for the six scene layers: 0 draws the layer's tiles straight, non-zero drives them through the layer's tile attribute table.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources writes all six entries when a field map is loaded, taking byte +0x1c of each 0x20-byte layer record in dsc%02d.dat (Field2.vfs); entry i belongs to layer i, and only the entries below the layer count at 00069cdc are meaningful. fdps_draw_scene_layers reads entry i once per layer in each of its two passes and passes it as the last argument of fdps_draw_scene_layer, which branches three ways: 0 skips the tile attribute table (data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_attr_ptr) entirely, so the layer gets no animated tiles, no 0x80 palette-remap tiles and no marked-tile highlight, and every tile goes through fdps_blit_dispatch mode 0 (fdps_rle_blit_passthrough); 1 enables the attribute path and blends marked tiles with mode 0xa (fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop); any other non-zero value enables the attribute path and blends marked tiles with mode 9 (fdps_rle_blit_translucent).

Pool: fdps  [reached only by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources and fdps_draw_scene_layers, both game logic]

Rebuild note:
The value is not a boolean even though the code tests it against 0 and then against 1: 0, 1 and "any other non-zero" are three distinct rendering paths in fdps_draw_scene_layer. Declaring it as a flag, or collapsing the 1-versus-other test into an if/else on truth, loses the mode 9 marked-tile blend.

=== 00069cfe [PLATE]
Draw depth of each of the six scene layer slots -- the key the layer draw order is sorted by, and the test that decides whether a layer is painted behind or in front of the map's units.

fdps_field_load_chapter_resources is the only writer. After loading dsc%02d.dat for the chapter at data_fdps_chapter_current_chapter_id it takes the layer count from the file's first dword into data_fdps_scene_layer_count, then for each slot i copies dword 7 of that slot's 8-dword record into this byte, truncating it, alongside the layer's scroll steps, parallax factors and its blit mode byte at 00069cf8.

fdps_build_scene_layer_draw_order reads it to sort: it fills the caller's array with 0,1,2,... and bubble-sorts those slot indices into ascending order of this byte, compared unsigned, so equal depths keep slot-index order. fdps_draw_scene_layers then walks the sorted order twice. The first pass blits every slot whose depth is strictly below 10 through fdps_draw_scene_layer; then fdps_draw_map_cursor and fdps_draw_map_units draw the cursor and the units; then the second pass blits every slot whose depth is strictly above 10, so those land on top of the units. Depth 10 is therefore the units' own plane, and a layer carrying exactly 10 is blitted by neither pass.

Values are whatever the chapter's dsc file supplies, read as an unsigned byte, and only their order and their relation to 10 matter. The index runs 0 .. data_fdps_scene_layer_count-1; the array has room for exactly 6.

Pool: fdps  [all three referencing functions are game code, and the values come from the game's own dsc%02d.dat layer descriptor]

Rebuild note:
The two passes test depth < 10 and depth > 10, and nothing draws depth == 10; writing the natural complementary split (< 10 and >= 10, or <= 10 and > 10) makes any layer with depth exactly 10 appear where the original leaves it invisible. Both the passes and the sort compare the byte unsigned, so declaring the array as char inverts the order of any depth of 0x80 or more.

=== 00069d04 [PLATE]
Terrain tile id of the map cell most recently queried by fdps_map_load_tile_info.

fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) is the only writer: it reads the 16-bit cell value at data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_map_ptrs[0] + 0xb + (y * width + x) * 2, where width is the map header word at +7, and stores it here as the first member of the tile-info output block that occupies 00069d04..00069d0c. The same value is used inside that function as the row index into the terrain attribute table at data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_attr_ptr[0] + 0x11, four bytes per row, whose bytes land in 00069d08..00069d0b. Readers call fdps_map_load_tile_info first and then pick this value up: fdps_battle_map_overview turns it into a tile bitmap address, tile sheet + 6 + id * 0x240 (24 x 24 = 0x240 bytes per tile), when it builds the pointer grid for the zoomed-out battlefield view; fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel passes it together with data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_sheet_ptrs[0] to the tile blit at 0002dba0 to draw the terrain under the cursor into the information panel. The value is an index into the tile sheet of layer 0 and runs over that sheet's tile count; it is read sign-extended everywhere, and there is no sentinel - fdps_map_load_tile_info does no bounds checking, so an out-of-range x or y simply stores whatever 16-bit word the address arithmetic lands on.

Pool: fdps  [all three referencing functions are game code and it is derived from the game's own map layer pointers]

=== 00069d06 [PLATE]
Event / searchable-cell code of the map cell most recently examined, published by fdps_map_load_tile_info.

fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) is the only writer: it indexes the map's third layer behind data_fdps_map_cell_event_code_layer_ptr (own width word at +7, 1-byte cells from +0x10) at y * width + x and stores that byte here, zero-extended, alongside the rest of the tile-info block it publishes -- tile id at 00069d04, the four terrain attribute bytes at 00069d08..00069d0b and the second-layer byte at 00069d0c. Every reader therefore calls that function first and then reads this slot for the cell it just named.

How the value is read depends on the 0x60 field of the terrain attribute byte at 00069d08. When that field is 0 the cell may carry a scripted chapter event: fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event treats 0 here as "no event" and otherwise fetches the cell's 2-byte record from data_fdps_tile_event_data_table_ptr at base + code * 2 + 0x31 -- byte 0 is the index into data_fdps_chapter_event_handler_table with 0xff meaning no handler, byte 1 is the occasion the record fires on. When the 0x60 field holds 0x20 or 0x40 the cell is searchable and the value is the searchable-cell code instead: fdps_map_find_chest_cell scans the grid for the cell whose code equals its cell_code argument, fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor and fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes use it to index the 32-entry data_fdps_map_cell_event_triggered_flags, and fdps_map_actor_behavior_step supplies byte 0x3d of the acting unit's 0x50-byte record as the code to hunt for. Nothing bounds-checks the value in either role.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it: fdps_map_load_tile_info writes it, and the five readers are all battle/map game functions]

Rebuild note:
The two roles index their tables differently. As a searchable-cell code it is a plain 0-based index into data_fdps_map_cell_event_triggered_flags; as an event code it is 1-based, because fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event forms base + code * 2 + 0x31 while the tile-event table itself begins at image offset 0x33. Writing the obvious table[code] against a pointer to 0x33 reads one record too far and misfires every tile event.

=== 00069d08 [PLATE]
Attribute flags of the map cell most recently published by fdps_map_load_tile_info.

fdps_map_load_tile_info is the only writer: it copies byte [0] of the cell's 4-byte entry in the tile-attribute table behind data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_attr_ptr (base + 0x11 + tile_id * 4) here, alongside the same entry's other three bytes at 00069d09, 00069d0a and 00069d0b and the cell's event code at 00069d06. Readers must call that helper for the cell they care about first; the value is otherwise stale.

Only the 0x60 field is read anywhere. It is a two-bit special-cell class, and each reader tests a different subset of it: fdps_map_set_pending_tile_event acts only when the field is 0 (an ordinary cell, the only kind that can carry a scripted tile event), fdps_map_find_chest_cell hunts class 0x20, fdps_battle_search_cell_at_cursor searches classes 0x20 and 0x40 with prompt message 0x20a and 0x20b respectively, and fdps_map_apply_triggered_cell_changes turns over classes 0x20 and 0x60. The remaining bits (0x9f) are never examined by any of the five references.

Pool: fdps  [written and read only by battle/map game code, and sourced from the game's own tile-attribute table]

Rebuild note:
The 0x60 field is a four-valued class, not a flag. Each site tests its own subset -- 0 alone, 0x20 alone, 0x20 or 0x40, 0x20 or 0x60 -- so collapsing them into one predicate such as (attr & 0x20) or (attr & 0x60) != 0 changes behaviour: class 0x40 is searchable but is never turned over, and class 0x60 is turned over but cannot be searched.

=== 00069d09 [PLATE]
Terrain type of the map cell most recently loaded by fdps_map_load_tile_info: byte 2 of that cell's 4-byte terrain-attribute entry.

fdps_map_load_tile_info is the only writer. It resolves the cell's tile id from the terrain layer, indexes the attribute table at data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_attr_ptr (4-byte entries starting at +0x11) and publishes byte 2 here, at the same time as the entry's other three bytes go to 00069d08, 00069d0a and 00069d0b. Every reader calls fdps_map_load_tile_info first and then uses this value, zero-extended, as an index. fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range and fdps_map_cursor_select_loop index the moving unit's per-class movement-cost byte table with it and treat a cost below 0x14 as enterable (0xff marks terrain the class cannot cross). fdps_combat_compute_hit_outcome, fdps_unit_resolve_attack_hit and fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel index data_fdps_battle_tile_attr_ap_modifier_table and data_fdps_battle_tile_attr_def_modifier_table, both int[6], to scale AP and DP by percent. fdps_deploy_unit and fdps_chapter_30_revive_wave_4_undead accept a cell only while the value is below 5.

The value is the strategy guide's terrain column M1..M8 minus one, and the modifier tables confirm the mapping: 0 = open ground (AP +5%, DP +0%), 1 = steps or brush (0%, 0%), 2 = grass (AP -5%, DP +10%), 3 (-5%, +10%), 4 (-5%, -5%), 5 = flight-only ground (0%, 0%), 6 = impassable. The AP and DP tables stop at index 5, so a value of 6 or above has no entry; the code bounds-checks nothing.

Pool: fdps  [written by fdps_map_load_tile_info and read by map, pathfinding, combat and HUD code only; referencing_pools is fdps alone]

=== 00069d0a [PLATE]
Byte +1 of the attribute entry of the map cell most recently passed to fdps_map_load_tile_info; it is zero in every shipped attribute table and nothing reads it.

Written only by fdps_map_load_tile_info (0002ba76), which for the cell (x, y) it is given looks the tile id up in the terrain layer, then copies the four bytes of that tile's attribute entry -- entry at data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_attr_ptr[0] + 0x11 + tile_id * 4 -- into four separate globals: +0 to data_fdps_map_current_tile_attr_flags, +2 to data_fdps_map_tile_terrain_type, +1 to here, +3 to 00069d0b. Read by nothing: this is the only reference to the address in the program. The attribute tables are the ATTRxxx.DAT members of Field2.vfs loaded per chapter layer by fdps_field_load_chapter_resources, and across all 69 of them all 26,344 entries have byte +1 equal to zero, so the value here is always 0 -- the field is reserved padding in the record, and the copy into this global is a dead store the game never consults.

Pool: fdps  [the only reference is game code, fdps_map_load_tile_info, and the data comes from a chapter resource file]

Rebuild note:
The four attribute bytes are NOT stored to the four globals in order. The original writes +2 to 00069d09, +0 to 00069d08, +1 to 00069d0a and +3 to 00069d0b; writing the obvious in-order loop or four in-order assignments puts the always-zero byte into data_fdps_map_tile_terrain_type and the terrain class into this reserved global, which silently zeroes every terrain AP/DP modifier and every terrain movement cost in the game.

=== 00069d0b [PLATE]
Combat-screen backdrop id of the map cell most recently published by fdps_map_load_tile_info.

fdps_map_load_tile_info is the only writer: it resolves the cell's tile id from the terrain layer, indexes the tile-attribute table behind data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_attr_ptr (4-byte entries starting at +0x11) and copies byte [3] here, at the same time as the entry's other three bytes go to 00069d08, 00069d09 and 00069d0a. The value is therefore only meaningful for the cell of the last call.

Both readers use it the same way. fdps_combat_play_attack_exchange calls fdps_map_load_tile_info for the defender's tile (record bytes +0x00/+0x01), then, when the attack is a travelling one, again for the attacker's tile; fdps_combat_play_spell_on_targets calls it for the caster's tile. Each time the byte is decremented in place if it is non-zero, formatted through "Back%02d.saf" and loaded from BackGrnd.vfs as the full-screen fight backdrop.

The tile carries the id 1-based and the file name is 0-based, which is what the decrement converts. Zero is left alone rather than wrapped, so a cell holding 0 and a cell holding 1 both open Back00.saf. The decrement writes back to this global, so after either reader runs the slot no longer holds the table's raw value; nothing reads it again before the next fdps_map_load_tile_info call refreshes it.

Pool: fdps  [written by a map routine and read by two combat-playback routines, all game code; referencing_pools is fdps alone]

Rebuild note:
The non-zero guard is load-bearing. Writing sprintf(name, "Back%02d.saf", backdrop - 1) unconditionally turns a cell whose backdrop byte is 0 into Back255.saf (or Back-1.saf if the value is widened signed) and fails the VFS lookup, where the original quietly loads Back00.saf.

=== 00069d0c [PLATE]
Movement-grid marker of the map cell most recently queried by fdps_map_load_tile_info: how much movement budget is left on that cell, or 0xff when the cell is not in the current unit's reach.

fdps_map_load_tile_info(x, y) is the only writer. It takes the cell's two-byte entry in the grid behind data_fdps_battle_move_grid_ptr -- header of two int16 dimensions, cells from +4, cell (x, y) at +4 + 2 * (y * width + x) -- and copies byte 1 of it here, where width is the terrain layer's own width word at data_fdps_scene_layer_tile_map_ptrs[0] + 7. It publishes this alongside the rest of the tile-info block: tile id at 00069d04, cell event code at 00069d06 and the four terrain-attribute bytes at 00069d08..00069d0b. The value is whatever fdps_move_grid_flood_fill_range last painted into that cell -- the movement points still unspent on arrival -- and 0xff means the flood never reached it, either because fdps_map_grid_reset blanked the grid or because the tile is out of range or blocked.

Both readers call fdps_map_load_tile_info immediately before reading, and both use the value only as a reachability test against 0xff. fdps_battle_move_unit_toward uses it when the direct route to the requested destination is blocked: it replays the relaxed path step by step, probes each tile, and keeps the last tile whose value is not 0xff as the new destination, so the unit walks as far along the blocked route as its range allows. fdps_map_cursor_select_loop uses it when the player confirms with the cursor: for every selection mode except 5 and 6 the tile is rejected outright when the value is 0xff, and only then does mode 4 confirm directly or the other modes go on to fdps_collect_targets_in_area. Mode 6 does not consult this byte at all; it tests the per-class movement cost through data_fdps_map_tile_terrain_type instead.

Pool: fdps  [all three references are battle/map game functions, and the byte is copied out of the game's own movement grid]

Rebuild note:
The sentinel test is unsigned. Ghidra prints both reads as DAT_00069d0c != -1, but the emitted code zero-extends the byte and compares it with 0xff, so the variable is an unsigned char. Transcribing the decompiler's -1 literally against an unsigned char makes the comparison always true after integer promotion, and every tile then looks reachable -- fdps_map_cursor_select_loop would confirm targets outside the unit's range and fdps_battle_move_unit_toward would retarget to the far end of a blocked route.

=== 00069d10 [PLATE]
Value of the interrupt-driven timer tick counter (00069d64) at the moment the last main-view frame was presented; fdps_render_view_frame spins on it to hold the game to one frame per tick.

Written and read only by fdps_render_view_frame, at the very end of that function and nowhere else. After the composed 0x138 x 0xC0 image has been blitted to the mode 13h screen, the routine loops on `MOV EAX,[0x00069d10]` / `CMP EAX,[0x00069d64]` / `JZ` back to the load (0002bf35-0002bf40), so it stays inside the loop for as long as this latch still equals the current tick, and leaves it on the first tick the interrupt handler advances; it then stores that new tick here (0002bf47) and frees the scene buffer. The value has no meaning of its own -- only whether it equals the current tick -- so every tick number is valid and there is no sentinel. All sixteen callers of fdps_render_view_frame (battle menus, the map cursor loop, savegame load) get their frame rate from this one latch. Sibling latches use the same tick counter with a non-blocking test instead of a spin: data_fdps_ui_palette_last_cycle_tick (00063fbc), data_fdps_unit_status_window_last_tick (00063fc0), and 00069d14 in fdps_draw_scene_layers, which skips the scene-layer animation step for a tick it has already served.

Pool: fdps  [its only referencing function, fdps_render_view_frame, is game presentation code; no CRT or AIL code reaches this address]

Rebuild note:
This latch is one half of a spin loop whose other half is changed by an interrupt handler, and the loop re-reads BOTH globals on every iteration. Declaring either as a plain uint -- the obvious C -- lets the compiler keep them in registers and the loop never terminates; the tick counter 00069d64 and this latch must both be volatile for the frame pacing to work at all.

=== 00069d14 [PLATE]
Value of the global tick counter at 00069d64 the last time fdps_draw_scene_layers advanced the parallax scroll accumulators.

Written only by fdps_draw_scene_layers (0002bf60), which reads it on entry and compares it with the tick counter that fdps_timer_tick_handler (00030790) increments. When the two are equal the function skips straight to building the draw order, so the scroll state does not move; when they differ it walks i over 0 .. data_fdps_scene_layer_count-1 adding data_fdps_scene_layer_scroll_x_step[i] into data_fdps_scene_layer_scroll_x_accumulator[i] and data_fdps_scene_layer_scroll_step_y[i] into data_fdps_scene_layer_scroll_offset_y[i], then stores the current tick here. The effect is that the auto-scroll of the background layers advances by exactly one step per tick value observed, however many times per tick the scene is drawn; a tick that elapses while no draw happens is simply not made up. Values are tick counts, not indices, and the whole 32-bit range is meaningful; zero is not a sentinel, it is just the _BSS starting value, and the first draw after startup takes the advance branch unless the counter happens to still be zero.

The neighbouring latches follow the same idiom against the same counter for different work: 00069d10 in fdps_render_view_frame, which spins until the tick changes, and 00069d18 in fdps_draw_map_unit.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_draw_scene_layers reaches it, and the data it gates is the scene layer scroll state]

=== 00069d18 [PLATE]
Latched copy of the global timer tick, used to run the battle map's shared unit-animation clock exactly once per tick.

fdps_draw_map_unit is the only function that touches it. On entry it compares the free-running tick counter at 00069d64 (incremented by fdps_timer_tick_handler from the AIL timer callback) against this latch; when they differ it stores the tick here and steps the two counters the map animation owns -- data_fdps_map_unit_walk_anim_counter modulo 0x10 and the status-icon counter at 00069d1c modulo 0x19, the latter bumping the icon cycle at 00060168 each time it wraps to 0. The latch is what keeps the clock to one step per tick even though fdps_draw_map_units calls the routine twice for every unit on the map (shadow pass and sprite pass). The value is meaningless in itself: only equality with the current tick is ever tested. Zeroed by the CRT at startup along with the tick counter, so the first call finds them equal and steps nothing; it is never reset afterwards, so re-entering the map simply latches the tick that is current then.

Pool: fdps  [the only referencing function is fdps_draw_map_unit, game code, and the tick source it mirrors is game-owned BSS]

=== 00069d1c [PLATE]
Frame-tick counter that paces the map units' status-icon rotation: counts 0..0x18 and rolls over every 25 ticks.

Owned entirely by fdps_draw_map_unit. Inside the block that runs only when the frame tick DAT_00069d64 differs from the value latched in DAT_00069d18 -- the latch is what keeps the step to once per tick even though fdps_draw_map_units calls the routine twice per unit -- 0002cdfe..0002ce11 does counter = (counter + 1) % 0x19, and 0002ce17 tests the result: on the wrap to 0 it increments data_fdps_map_unit_status_icon_cycle (00060168), which fdps_draw_map_unit later hands to fdps_unit_select_status_icon to choose which ailment icon a unit shows. So one full pass of this counter is one step of the ailment-icon rotation, 25 frame ticks apart. Its value therefore only ever runs 0 through 0x18; nothing else reads it and nothing resets it. Its sibling in the same block, data_fdps_map_unit_walk_anim_counter (00069cc8), is stepped the same way modulo 0x10 and drives the walk frames.

Pool: fdps  [reached only by fdps_draw_map_unit, a game-logic function; no CRT or AIL code touches it]

=== 00069d20 [PLATE]
Value of the global frame tick counter (00069d64) as of the last tick on which fdps_cycle_scene_palette actually advanced the scene's colour cycle.

Written and read only by fdps_cycle_scene_palette (0002eab0), which the game's frame and input loops -- fdps_render_view_frame, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop, fdps_prompt_two_choice, FUN_00021f60 -- call once per iteration. That function first copies its per-scene R/G/B ramps to the stack and calls fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll, and only then compares this latch against 00069d64 (0002ec84): equal means the current tick has already been serviced and it returns without touching the DAC, so the scene palette animation advances at most once per timer tick however fast the caller's loop spins. When they differ it reads the scene id at 00069cf4, steps the shared phase at 00069d24 and reprograms the top of the DAC, and on the way out (0002f226) stores the current tick here. Every exit from the body passes through that store, including the scene ids that match no case and change no colours, so an unrecognised scene still consumes its tick.

The value has no meaning of its own -- only whether it equals the current tick -- so every tick number is valid and there is no sentinel. _BSS zeroes it at startup, which matches a tick counter that also starts at zero: the first call before the first timer tick sees equality and services nothing.

Pool: fdps  [the sole referencing function is fdps_cycle_scene_palette, game rendering code; no CRT or AIL code reaches this address]

Rebuild note:
The CD-music poll must stay ahead of this test. Hoisting the guard to the top of the function -- the obvious way to write "nothing to do yet" -- stops fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll from running on the calls that fall inside an already-serviced tick, and that poll is what restarts a finished CD track, so background music stops looping.

=== 00069d24 [PLATE]
Position in the current scene's VGA palette colour-cycling animation, at quarter-step resolution.

Written and read only by fdps_cycle_scene_palette, which runs once per frame tick. That function switches on the scene id at 00069cf4 (cases 0, 2, 8, 0x14, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x1a, 0x1c, 0x1d) and, in the branch it lands in, does phase = (phase + 1) % (count * 4), then passes phase / 4 as the offset into the three per-channel colour ramps it hands to fdps_set_palette_range_on_retrace(first_dac_index, red + phase/4, green + phase/4, blue + phase/4, count). The times-four period is the animation's speed control: the colours advance one DAC entry every four frame ticks. count is the number of DAC entries the scene cycles -- 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 or 15 -- so the value here runs 0 through count*4-1, i.e. 0..0x13 up to 0..0x3b, and is always non-negative in practice because the CRT zeroes _BSS and nothing ever stores a negative value. Scene ids outside the switch leave it untouched.

One single phase is shared by all ten scene branches; it is not reset when the scene changes, and the modulus it is folded by changes with the scene.

Pool: fdps  [the only referencing function is fdps_cycle_scene_palette, a game-logic function; no CRT or AIL code reaches this address]

Rebuild note:
This is one global shared by every scene case, not a per-scene counter. Giving each case its own static -- the obvious tidy-up when the branches are written out as separate blocks -- changes the animation: a scene entered after another scene currently resumes at whatever phase the previous one left behind, folded by the new scene's own count*4.

=== 00069d30 [PLATE]
The game's pool of eight AIL digital sample handles, one per simultaneously playable voice.

fdps_audio_init is the only writer: when AIL_install_DIG_INI succeeds it sets the digital-driver-present flag at 00069d71 and fills slots 0..7 with AIL_allocate_sample_handle(DAT_00069d68), storing each return unchecked. When the driver is absent the loop never runs and all eight slots keep the zero the CRT left in _BSS. Nothing else ever writes the table, and no slot is released or re-allocated while the game runs.

fdps_audio_start_sample, fdps_audio_start_wav and fdps_sfx_play each claim a voice the same way: scan i = 0..7 calling AIL_sample_status on slot i and take the first whose status is not 4 (AIL's SMP_PLAYING), returning -1 when all eight are busy; the handle they claimed is then passed to AIL_init_sample, AIL_set_sample_address and the rest, and the slot index 0..7 becomes the caller's voice id. fdps_audio_stop_sample takes such an index and calls AIL_stop_sample on that one slot, or, when handed -1, walks all eight and stops every voice. fdps_audio_sample_is_playing reads slot [sample_index] and reports whether AIL_sample_status returns 4. The valid index range everywhere is 0..7, with -1 meaning 'no voice' as a return value and 'all voices' as fdps_audio_stop_sample's argument.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it; the game allocates and owns the handles and merely passes them into AIL public entry points]

Rebuild note:
fdps_audio_init stores AIL_allocate_sample_handle's return without checking it, so a driver that runs out of voices leaves a null handle in the middle of the table and the voice scan still passes it to AIL_sample_status. Writing the obvious guard -- breaking out of the allocation loop, or skipping null slots in the scan -- changes which voices exist and which slot a sound lands on.

=== 00069d50 [PLATE]
Handle of the AIL timer that drives the game's audio service tick.

Written once by fdps_audio_timer_install with the return value of
AIL_register_timer(fdps_timer_tick_handler); the same function then reads it three times --
once to test it against -1, then to pass it to AIL_set_timer_frequency(handle, rate) and
AIL_start_timer(handle). No other function in the program touches it: the timer is never
reprogrammed, stopped or released after startup, so the handle is write-once and its only
readers are the three calls that arm the timer. Values are an AIL timer slot index, 0..15
(AIL keeps sixteen timer slots -- data_ail_timer_state_table and its parallel tables), with
-1 as the failure sentinel meaning AIL had no free slot. On -1 the function prints
" Timer fail !!!
" and carries on, so the sentinel can reach AIL_set_timer_frequency and
AIL_start_timer unchanged.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_audio_timer_install, a game function, references it; AIL keeps its own
timer bookkeeping in its own globals and never reads this one]

Rebuild note:
The -1 failure branch only prints; it does not return, and the invalid handle is passed on to
AIL_set_timer_frequency and AIL_start_timer. Writing the obvious `if (handle == -1) { printf(...);
return; }` changes behaviour. Keep the fall-through, and keep the variable signed so the
comparison against -1 reads the same.

=== 00069d54 [PLATE]
Which background music the game currently wants the CD-ROM drive playing, as a 0-based music index, or -1 when no music is selected.

main writes -1 at startup, before the game loops that poll it begin. fdps_cd_set_music_track is the normal writer: it copies its music_index argument here, first forcing it to -1 when the music-enabled flag data_fdps_audio_bgm_enabled_flag is zero, then either calls fdps_cd_stop_audio (value -1) or fdps_cd_play_track with this value + 1. fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track performs the same publish-then-play sequence twice, once per disc it checks. fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll is the reader that makes the selection persist: every 75 ticks, if this value is not -1, music is enabled, and fdps_cd_audio_is_idle reports playback has stopped, it re-issues fdps_cd_play_track with this value + 1, so the chosen track repeats indefinitely.

Values: -1 is the sentinel for "nothing selected", and it is the only value that means silence -- it is what both the music-off setting and an explicit stop request collapse to. Any other value is a 0-based music index whose CD track number is one higher; the callers seen so far pass 1 (title screen), 2 (village) and the byte operand of an IconAni script opcode, with the operand 0xff mapped to -1.

Pool: fdps  [only game code reaches it -- main and the three fdps CD helpers; no CRT or AIL module touches it]

Rebuild note:
This lives in _BSS, so the CRT zeroes it, and 0 is a valid music index (CD track 1), not the idle state. The idle state is -1 and only main's explicit store establishes it, so that store is load-bearing and must not be dropped as a redundant initialisation of a zeroed global.

=== 00069d5c [PLATE]
Playback rate the game hands to AIL for every PCM voice it starts through fdps_audio_start_sample.

Written only by fdps_audio_set_sample_playback_rate (00030810), which stores its single argument here unmodified and returns; read only by fdps_audio_start_sample (00030630), which pushes it at 000306f4 as the rate argument of AIL_set_sample_playback_rate on the voice it claimed out of data_fdps_audio_sample_handle_table, between AIL_set_sample_loop_count and AIL_start_sample. The units and range are AIL's (samples per second); no call site in the image supplies a concrete value. Neither of the two functions has a caller in the image and nothing else writes this slot, so as linked it holds the _BSS zero the CRT leaves and AIL is asked for rate 0 -- meaning the sample's own recorded rate. The sibling voice starters fdps_sfx_play and FUN_00030a00 do not consult it.

Pool: fdps  [both referencing functions are pool_fdps game audio code; AIL only ever sees the value as a call argument]

Rebuild note:
Declare it uninitialised. It is read before anything writes it, and giving it a plausible default such as 11025 would change the rate argument AIL receives.
