=== 00069e64 [PLATE]
Hours field of the Miles AIL debug-log timestamp clock: whole hours elapsed since AIL_startup.

AIL_startup zeroes it at 0003d836 together with the minutes (00069e74), seconds (00069e70) and hundredths (00069e78) fields, and AIL_internal_init_globals_once DPMI-locks its four bytes so the timer ISR may touch them. AIL_internal_log_timer_tick, installed by AIL_startup as a periodic callback, carries hundredths -> seconds -> minutes -> hours and increments this field whenever the minutes field passes 59; the tick first tests whether the clock already reads 99:59:59.99 and returns without incrementing if it does, so the clock saturates instead of wrapping and this field never exceeds 99. AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix reads it and passes it as the first of the four timestamp values to the fprintf that heads every log line, ahead of minutes, seconds and hundredths, writing to the log stream held in 00069e7c. Range 0..99.

Pool: ail  [only AIL_startup and the two AIL log-clock routines reach it; no game or CRT code refers to it]

=== 00069e68 [PLATE]
Handle of the Miles AIL 100Hz timer that drives the library's debug-log clock.

Written once, in AIL_startup@0003d718, with the result of AIL_internal_register_timer_inner(AIL_internal_log_timer_tick); read back on the next line to hand to AIL_internal_set_timer_frequency_inner (100 Hz) and AIL_internal_start_timer_inner, and never touched again -- there is no release path, the timer runs until AIL_shutdown tears the registry down. The value is a slot byte offset into the AIL timer registry (status array data_ail_timer_state_table at 0x000604a0, callbacks at data_ail_timer_callback_table at 0x00060460), so 0 is the first legal slot and -1 is the 'registry full' sentinel that the set-frequency and start entries silently ignore; AIL_startup itself checks nothing. Both stores lie past the early-out at 0003d749, so the timer is only registered on the AIL_DEBUG path -- with the environment variable unset the log file never opens, this global keeps its _BSS zero and no log timer exists. AIL_internal_init_globals_once@0003d566 DPMI-locks these 4 bytes along with the seven other statics of this module, because the block is reachable at IRQ0 time.

Pool: ail  [only AIL_startup and AIL_internal_init_globals_once, both ailv3.lib Function ID hits in ail_code.obj, reference it; no game or CRT code reaches it]

=== 00069e6c [PLATE]
Nesting depth of the AIL public API calls currently on the stack, kept for the debug log.

Every public AIL_ entry point increments it on entry and decrements it on the way out; the decrements are concentrated in shared epilogues reached by fall-through or tail-JMP (0003d942, 0003dca7, 0003e18a, 0003eb44, and AIL_internal_log_decrement_nesting), so error returns decrement it too. 0 means no AIL API call is in progress, 1 means the outermost call, above 1 means an AIL call made from inside another AIL call. Two readers, both in the debug-log harness: the gate every wrapper runs after incrementing, 'if (DAT_00069e80 != 0 && (nesting == 1 || DAT_00069e84 != 0))', which by default logs only the outermost call and logs nested calls as well once DAT_00069e84 is set; and AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix, which prints the full timestamp line when nesting == 1 and otherwise emits nesting-1 copies of the '.' indent string at 00062279, one per enclosing call. AIL_startup is the only writer that assigns an absolute value: it stores 1 at 0003d886 so the startup banner prints in outermost form, calls AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix, then stores the 0 it is holding in ESI back at 0003d891. Otherwise the variable relies on the CRT zeroing _BSS for its initial 0.

Pool: ail  [all 106 referencing functions are AIL_ entry points in pool_ail; no game or CRT code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
Every exit path of every AIL API wrapper has to decrement this, error returns included -- in the original those paths tail-JMP into a shared DEC epilogue, so it is easy to write a C wrapper with an early 'return' that skips the decrement. One missed decrement leaves the depth permanently above 1 and silently turns the debug log off for the rest of the run, because the gate then only fires when DAT_00069e84 is set.

=== 00069e70 [PLATE]
Seconds field of the AIL debug-log timestamp clock, 0..59.

AIL_startup zeroes it together with the other three fields (hours at 00069e64, minutes at 00069e74, hundredths at 00069e78) at 0003d844, and AIL_internal_init_globals_once registers it with the DPMI page-lock helper at 0003cb93 (address, 4 bytes) so the timer ISR can touch it. AIL_internal_log_timer_tick is the only writer afterwards: it increments the hundredths counter each tick, and when that reaches 100 it zeroes it and increments this one; when this one reaches 60 (0x3c) it is zeroed and the minutes counter is incremented. The tick handler returns without counting at all once the whole clock reads 99:59:59.99, so the timestamp saturates instead of wrapping. AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix reads it at 0003d691 as the third of the four values it formats into the hh:mm:ss.cc prefix in front of every log line.

Pool: ail  [only AIL_startup, AIL_internal_init_globals_once, AIL_internal_log_timer_tick and AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix reach it; no game or CRT code refers to it]

=== 00069e74 [PLATE]
Minutes field, 0..59, of the elapsed-time clock the AIL log stamps its lines with.

Zeroed by AIL_startup (0003d718) at 0003d83e together with its three siblings -- hours at 00069e64, seconds at 00069e70, hundredths at 00069e78 -- immediately before AIL_startup installs AIL_internal_log_timer_tick (0003d60a) as a periodic callback and stores the handle at 00069e68.

AIL_internal_log_timer_tick is the only writer afterwards. It advances the four counters as one 100 Hz clock: hundredths increment every tick and reset at 100, which increments seconds; seconds reset at 60, which increments this cell; this cell resets at 60, which increments hours. The clock saturates rather than wraps -- the first thing the tick does is compare all four against 99, 59, 59, 99, and return without advancing anything once 99:59:59.99 is reached.

AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix (0003d676) is the only reader. It loads all four and, when the log verbosity flag at 00069e6c is 1, prints them through the format literal at 0006225c, "[%.02u:%.02u:%.02u.%.02u] ", this cell filling the second field. When that flag is not 1 the timestamp is replaced by fourteen spaces from binary_artifact_string_literal_ail_log_timestamp_pad_space_62277, the width the rendered stamp occupies.

The cell is one of the eight 4-byte statics AIL_internal_init_globals_once (0003d566) DPMI page-locks, because the tick that writes it runs at interrupt time.

Pool: ail  [referencing_pools is ail alone; all four referencing functions are AIL library bodies]

=== 00069e78 [PLATE]
Hundredths-of-a-second field of the AIL log timestamp clock; runs 0..99.

AIL_startup zeroes it together with the seconds, minutes and hours fields at 00069e70, 00069e74 and 00069e64, then registers AIL_internal_log_timer_tick as a timer callback and sets that timer to 100 Hz, so one tick is one unit of this field. Each tick increments it; on reaching 100 the tick clears it and carries into the seconds field, which carries at 60 into minutes, which carries at 60 into hours. The clock saturates rather than wrapping: while hours reads 99 and minutes and seconds both read 59 and this field reads 99, the tick returns having incremented nothing. AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix reads hours, minutes, seconds and this field and formats them as the prefix on every log line. AIL_internal_init_globals_once passes this address with a length of 4 to the DPMI page-lock helper at 0003cb93 so the tick callback can touch it from interrupt context.

Pool: ail  [only the Miles sound library's own log and startup code reaches it]

=== 00069e7c [PLATE]
Stream the AIL debug log is written to; NULL while the log is not open.

AIL_startup opens the log file with fopen at 0003d76f and stores the FILE * here; if the open fails the pointer stays NULL and the rest of the log setup is skipped. On success AIL_startup reads the stream's _handle field (EAX + 0x10), calls setbuf at 00045bc5 with a NULL buffer so log lines reach disk unbuffered, and writes the banner lines. Every AIL public entry point then reads this pointer and passes it as the stream argument of fprintf at 00045183 to record its own name and arguments -- AIL_call_driver, AIL_API_read_INI, AIL_install_DIG_driver_file, AIL_start_sample and the rest -- and prints the call's result the same way on the way out. AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix writes the line prefix through it: the clock fields data_ail_log_timestamp_hours, data_ail_log_clock_minutes, data_ail_log_clock_seconds and data_ail_log_timer_centiseconds, then one pad string per level of data_ail_log_call_nesting_depth. AIL_shutdown closes it with fclose at 0003d93a. AIL_internal_init_globals_once registers the four bytes at 0003d5a6 with the page-lock helper at 0003cb93, so the pointer stays resident for interrupt-time code. Whether a log line is emitted is decided before the pointer is loaded: some sites test the flag at 00069e80 (CMP dword ptr [0x00069e80],0x0 at 0003e10c), and many others were compiled down to an always-taken skip (XOR EAX,EAX / TEST EAX,EAX / JZ, as at 0003e516). Nothing tests this pointer for NULL at the fprintf sites.

Pool: ail  [only pool_ail code reaches it; it is the Miles library's own log stream]

Rebuild note:
The fprintf call sites never null-check this pointer -- the guard is the separate enable flag at 00069e80 and the constant-false tests the compiler folded in. It lives in _BSS, so it is NULL until AIL_startup opens the log; rewriting a logging block without its guard, or making the guard a runtime-true condition, calls fprintf on a NULL stream instead of quietly logging nothing.

=== 00069e80 [PLATE]
Non-zero once the Miles AIL debug log is open and armed; zero when the library is not tracing.

AIL_startup is the only writer. It clears this flag and the nested-trace flag at 00069e84 on entry (0003d725), reads getenv("AIL_DEBUG") for the log file name and returns immediately if it is unset, sets 00069e84 when getenv("AIL_SYS_DEBUG") is also set, opens the file with fopen(name,"w+t") into the log stream at 00069e7c and returns if that fails, writes the banner, zeroes the four timestamp-clock fields at 00069e64/00069e70/00069e74/00069e78, registers AIL_internal_log_timer_tick as a 100Hz timer whose handle goes to 00069e68, and only then stores 1 here (0003d880). So the flag is armed last: it means the log file is open AND the log clock is running, not merely that AIL_DEBUG was set. With AIL_DEBUG unset it keeps the zero the CRT gave _BSS for the whole run and every wrapper's logging branch is dead.

Every public AIL_ entry point reads it, and only reads it, as the first term of the trace gate it runs after bumping the call-nesting depth at 00069e6c: 'if (DAT_00069e80 != 0 && (DAT_00069e6c == 1 || DAT_00069e84 != 0))', then a final check that AIL_internal_get_isr_lock_count_3eeda returns 0. When the gate passes, the wrapper fprintf's its own name and arguments to the stream at 00069e7c, prefixed by the hh:mm:ss.cc timestamp that AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix emits. A zero here disables the entire trace regardless of nesting depth or of AIL_SYS_DEBUG.

Nothing clears it. AIL_shutdown reads it twice -- once for its own entry line and once for the exit gate at 0003d90f that fcloses the log stream -- but leaves it set, so after shutdown the flag still says 'armed' while 00069e7c points at a closed FILE.

Pool: ail  [all 108 referencing functions are AIL_ entry points and AIL internals in pool_ail; no game or CRT code reaches it]

=== 00069e84 [PLATE]
Non-zero when the AIL debug log should record nested API calls as well as outermost ones; set from the AIL_SYS_DEBUG environment variable.

AIL_startup is the only writer. It clears this flag together with the log-enable flag at 00069e80 (0003d723-0003d72b), calls getenv("AIL_DEBUG") to get the log file name, and -- only if that name exists -- calls getenv("AIL_SYS_DEBUG") at 0003d74e and stores 1 here when the call returns a non-NULL pointer (0003d75f). The value of AIL_SYS_DEBUG is never looked at, only its presence. AIL_internal_init_globals_once registers the variable with the DPMI page-lock helper at 0003cb93 (address, 4 bytes) alongside 00069e7c and 00069e80, so the flag stays resident for code reached from an interrupt handler. Nothing writes it again, and it relies on the CRT zeroing _BSS for its value if AIL_startup never runs.

Every one of the 106 public AIL_ entry points reads it, always as the second disjunct of the same gate: 'if (DAT_00069e80 != 0 && (data_ail_log_call_nesting_depth == 1 || DAT_00069e84 != 0))'. With the flag 0 the log therefore carries only calls the application itself made -- nesting depth 1 -- and with the flag non-zero it carries AIL-internal calls made from inside another AIL call as well, which AIL_internal_log_print_timestamp_prefix then indents with one '.' per enclosing call. Pool: ail  [all 106 referencing functions are AIL_ entry points in pool_ail, plus AIL_startup and AIL_internal_init_globals_once; no game or CRT code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
The flag records only whether AIL_SYS_DEBUG exists in the environment, never what it is set to, so AIL_SYS_DEBUG=0 turns nested logging ON. Writing the obvious 'atoi(getenv("AIL_SYS_DEBUG"))' or a comparison against "1" changes which calls appear in the log.

=== 00069ea8 [PLATE]
The delay() calibration constant: how many DOS Get System Time calls (INT 21h AH=2Ch) this machine completes in one second.

Written once at startup by __delay_init (00043c82) and by nothing else. __delay_init is not called from main or from game code -- it is reached through the CRT rt_init record at 000638f0, which __InitRtns walks during Watcom startup. It polls INT 21h AH=2Ch until the seconds field in DH changes, counts how many further such calls complete during the following second, and stores that count here. Read only by __delay (00043cb0), which converts its millisecond argument into a spin count as (milliseconds * this + 500) / 1000 using an unsigned divide, clamps a zero result up to 1, and then issues that many INT 21h AH=2Ch calls. The value is therefore a machine-speed-dependent unsigned count, zero until the init table has run, and it is the single scale factor behind every delay() the game uses to pace palette fades, banner slides and combat animation.

Pool: crt  [only __delay_init and __delay, the two published symbols of CLIB3S delay.obj, reach it; the game never touches it]

=== 00069eac [PLATE]
Watcom CRT near/far heap flag: nonzero means the far heap is known to be coalesced, so a heap walk can be skipped; any operation that puts memory back into the heap clears it.

Defined by CLIB3S module heapmod together with its sibling __nheap_clean at 00069ead (that module's entire _BSS is these two bytes). In FDPS only __HeapManager_expand writes it, and only ever with zero: once at 0004d0e7, when an in-place expand swallows a whole adjacent free block and the mini-heap free count at [heap+0x1c] is decremented, and once at 0004d12c, when the expand splits the adjacent free block and leaves a smaller remainder. Nothing in FDPS reads it -- the modules that consume the flag (the far-heap _heapchk / _heapmin variants) were not linked in, so in this binary it is written and never tested. The near-heap counterpart __nheap_clean is cleared the same way by _nmalloc and _nfree, and is set to 1 by _nheapchk in the library.

Pool: crt  [only __HeapManager_expand, a CLIB3S nexpand function, touches it; the symbol is an EXTDEF of nexpand.obj resolved by heapmod.obj, so it is the library's own variable and keeps the library's name]

=== 00069ead [PLATE]
Watcom CRT near-heap flag: nonzero means the near heap has been walked and found consistent since the last change to it, so a re-walk can be skipped; anything that allocates or releases memory clears it.

Defined by CLIB3S module heapmod together with its sibling __fheap_clean at 00069eac -- that module's whole _BSS is these two bytes, __fheap_clean at offset 0 and this one at offset 1. In FDPS only two functions touch it and both only ever store zero: _nmalloc (0003d383) at 0003d465, on the path where it has carved a block out of a mini-heap and is about to return it, and _nfree (0003d486) at 0003d4da, after the freed block has been merged back into the free list and __LargestSizeB4MiniHeapRover at 00060390 has been updated. Nothing in FDPS reads it: the library modules that consume the flag -- _nheapchk, which sets it to 1 once a full walk of the near heap has succeeded, and _nheapmin, which tests it to decide whether the heap must be walked before shrinking -- were not linked into this binary, so here the flag is written and never tested. The CRT zeroes it at startup along with the rest of _BSS, which is the correct initial state: an unwalked heap is not known to be clean.

Pool: crt  [only _nmalloc and _nfree, two CLIB3S near-heap modules, reach it; the symbol is a PUBDEF32 of heapmod.obj, so it is the library's own variable and keeps the library's name]

=== 00069eb0 [PLATE]
Table of the up to 16 sound drivers currently installed; each slot is the AIL_DRIVER handle returned by AIL_internal_install_driver_inner, or NULL for a free slot.

AIL_internal_init_runtime_defaults clears all 16 slots at 00045adf when the library starts up. AIL_internal_install_driver_inner scans slots 0..15 upward from 000457a2, takes the FIRST slot whose dword is zero, stores the new driver pointer there, and then stamps that slot index back into the driver: 000457b6 MOV EAX,[EBP+0xc] / MOV word ptr [EAX+0x32],CX, where CX is the loop index. So a driver knows which row it occupies. AIL_internal_uninstall_driver_inner scans the same 16 slots at 00045963 comparing the stored pointer against the driver being removed and zeroes the matching slot; slots are never compacted, so the table stays sparse. AIL_internal_shutdown_inner walks slots 15 down to 0 at 00045b01 and calls AIL_uninstall_driver on every non-NULL entry, tearing drivers down in reverse installation order. AIL_internal_init_state_arrays DPMI-locks the whole 0x40-byte table at 00045221 and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_state_arrays_3fa8c unlocks it at 00045b44, because the interrupt-time mixer and timer code walks it.

Pool: ail  [only AIL library functions read or write it; the game reaches drivers through its own handles, never through this table]

Rebuild note:
The table is index-stable and sparse, not a stack. Installing writes into the first zero slot and the chosen index is stored inside the driver, and uninstalling zeroes that slot in place. Writing the obvious drivers[count++] = drvr with a compacting removal would renumber live drivers and hand the driver a slot number that no longer matches the table.

=== 00069ef0 [PLATE]
The Miles sound library's last-error message: a 256-byte NUL-terminated text buffer holding the description of the most recent AIL failure.

AIL_internal_init_runtime_defaults empties it at startup by storing a zero byte to element 0. === 0006a038 [PLATE]
The 24-byte Miles IO_PARMS block describing the hardware configuration of the sound driver currently being installed: IO port, IRQ, 8-bit DMA and 16-bit DMA in the first four 16-bit fields, four 32-bit driver-specific extras after them.

AIL_internal_dig_driver_setup_full and AIL_internal_mdi_driver_setup_full share it, one at a time. Each fills all 24 bytes with 0xff (memset with -1) so that every field reads as 'unspecified', then copies in the configuration it is about to try and calls AIL_internal_dig_apply_io_parms / AIL_internal_mdi_apply_io_parms, which substitute the driver's own defaults for any field left negative and hand the merged block to the driver as call 0x304. The candidates are tried in order: the IO_PARMS the caller of the DIG/MDI driver install entry point supplied, then the block AIL_get_IO_environment parses out of the BLASTER-style environment variable, then each 0x18-byte entry of the configuration table inside the loaded driver image in turn (that scan runs only when data_ail_preference_table[0x10] is 1). When one of them succeeds the setup routine copies the winning parameters back over this block from its frame, so after a successful install it holds the configuration the driver is actually running on; after a failed one it holds the last candidate tried. A field of -1 means the value was never specified and the driver's default was used in its place.

Nothing in this image reads it back -- it is written for inspection only. AIL_internal_init_state_arrays DPMI-locks the whole 0x18 bytes at startup, next to the driver-handle table at 00069eb0, the error text at 00069ef0 and the preference table at 00069ff0, and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_state_arrays_3fa8c unlocks them at shutdown.

Pool: ail  [every reference is in pool_ail library code; nothing in the game or the CRT touches it]

Rebuild note:
The 'unspecified' value in this record is -1 and the fields are signed. Zeroing it -- by leaving it to the _BSS clear, or by writing IO_PARMS io = {0} -- or declaring the fields unsigned makes every field look specified, so the driver's defaults are never substituted and the driver is told to use IO port 0 on IRQ 0.

=== 0006a050 [PLATE]
Saved EFLAGS image of the interrupted context while AIL_internal_driver_timer_isr runs with interrupts disabled.

It is live only inside that one critical section; between ticks the contents are stale. The ISR reaches this store only after clearing the reentry guard test on data_ail_driver_timer_isr_reentry_guard at 00061010, so no nesting can overwrite a live value. === 0006a054 [PLATE]
Miles AIL's static IO_PARMS block -- the 24-byte hardware-configuration record that AIL_get_IO_environment hands back to its caller.

Written in one place only, by AIL_internal_get_IO_environment_inner at 000459e9: after the driver has been asked to parse the environment variable named at descriptor+0x12 (getenv, strncpy into descriptor+0x3a, then AIL_call_driver command 0x303), a REP MOVSD of six dwords copies the driver's own IO environment from descriptor+0x16 into these 24 bytes, and 000459eb loads the same address into EAX as the return value. Every reader therefore reaches it through that returned pointer rather than by name; AIL_internal_mdi_driver_setup_full at 000497f0 is the consumer, calling AIL_get_IO_environment and passing the result to AIL_internal_mdi_apply_io_parms. The record is Miles IO_PARMS: IO port, IRQ, 8-bit DMA and 16-bit DMA as words, then four dwords of driver-specific parameters, with -1 meaning 'field not present' (the .INI parser pre-fills its own copy of the same block with 0xFF). On every failure path -- no such environment variable, variable unset, or the driver rejecting it -- the function returns NULL and leaves these bytes exactly as the previous call left them. Distinct from the shared driver-setup IO_PARMS scratch at 0006a038, which the DIG and MDI install paths fill from caller-supplied parameters.

Pool: ail  [the sole referencing function is AIL_internal_get_IO_environment_inner, and the block is the return buffer of the public Miles entry AIL_get_IO_environment]

Rebuild note:
It has to stay one file-scope static whose address is returned; the failure paths do not touch it, so a rewrite that clears the block before calling the driver, or that returns a local or a caller-filled buffer, changes what a later caller sees. It also starts all-zero because the CRT zeroes _BSS, not filled with the 0xFF 'field not present' markers AIL uses for IO_PARMS elsewhere, so pre-initialising it to 0xFF to match that convention would feed the driver a configuration the original never produces.

=== 0006a090 [PLATE]
The C library's single static result buffer for asctime(): the 26-character "Www Mmm dd hh:mm:ss yyyy\n\0" date text.

Written only by _asctime (00045ccc), which fills it character by character and NUL-terminates it at offset 25; the only code that names the address is the public wrapper asctime (00045dbc), which passes it as _asctime's buffer argument and returns it. ctime (00045df8) reaches it indirectly, being asctime(localtime(timer)), so both entry points hand back this same storage and each call overwrites the previous result. The layout is fixed: weekday abbreviation at 0-2, month abbreviation at 4-6, day of month at 8-9 (leading zero blanked to ' '), hour, minute and second at 11-12, 14-15 and 17-18 with ':' at 13 and 16, the four year digits at 20-23, '\n' at 24 and NUL at 25; offsets 3, 7, 10 and 19 are spaces. Nothing bounds-checks it, and the year field is fixed at four digits because _asctime splits tm_year by 100 into century and year-in-century. It sits in _BSS immediately above the static struct tm at 0006a06c that localtime (00045c7f) returns, the other static of the same time cluster.

Pool: crt  [reached only by asctime, a Watcom CLIB3S asctime.obj entry point; a file-static of that module with no public symbol, hence the L$N_ form]

=== 0006a0ac [PLATE]
The 12-byte register block the digital mixer's interrupt handler hands to the sound driver when it has finished filling a half of the driver's double buffer: six 16-bit slots, of which only the two at offsets 4 and 6 are ever written.

AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr is the only code that fills it, and it issues exactly one call with it. Each time the driver reports that the hardware has moved on to the other half of its buffer (the ISR reads that half index through drvr+0x34 into 0006a0c4 and compares it with the last one seen at drvr+0x38), the ISR mixes the half that just fell idle; then, and only if bit 4 of the driver's flag byte at drvr+0x1c is set, it writes 0 into the slot at offset 4 and the index of the half it just filled -- 0006a0c4 XOR 1, the same value it passes to AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_format and leaves in the word at 0006a0b2 -- into the slot at offset 6, and calls AIL_call_driver(drvr->drvr, 0x405, this block, NULL) at 00046320. Drivers that do not set that flag bit are never told; they pick the buffer up on their own. The other four slots -- offsets 0, 2, 8 and 10 -- are written by nothing in the image: they hold the zero the CRT's _BSS clear left there, and that zero is what the driver sees in those registers on every call.

AIL_internal_init_clock_globals DPMI-locks all 0xc bytes of it at startup (PUSH 0xc / PUSH 0x6a0ac at 00045e60, through the lock helper at 0003cb93), in the same run as the mixer's other statics at 0006a0b8 through 0006a0cc, which are locked 4 bytes apiece; AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_dig_mix_416f0 unlocks the same list at shutdown. The lock is what lets the handler touch the block at interrupt time.

Pool: ail  [all three references are in pool_ail library code; nothing in the game or the CRT reaches it]

Rebuild note:
This block is a file-static that is only ever half written, and it has to stay one. The ISR sets the two 16-bit slots at offsets 4 and 6 and relies on the _BSS clear for the other four; it is also DPMI-locked because the only code that touches it runs inside an interrupt handler. Writing the obvious thing -- declaring the record as a local inside AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr and setting just those two fields, which is what the single call site invites -- both passes the driver whatever the stack happened to hold in the other four registers and puts the block on a page that can be swapped out under the handler.

=== 0006a0b8 [PLATE]
Cursor the digital-audio mix ISR walks the current DIG_DRIVER's sample array with: while the ISR is running it points at the 0x894-byte sample slot being examined this iteration.

AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr is the only code that reads or writes it. Once that ISR has decided the driver's buffer really needs refilling, it loads the driver's sample-array pointer from dig_driver+0x5c into this variable and the slot count from dig_driver+0x60 into the companion counter at 0006a0bc (00046276-00046282), then walks the array: a slot whose status word at +4 holds 4 -- Miles' SMP_PLAYING -- is handed to AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample and counted in 0006a0cc (00046290-0004629d), and every slot, played or not, advances this cursor by 0x894 and decrements the count (000462ab-000462be), the loop ending when the count reaches zero. The number of slots that were playing is then written back into the driver at +0x64, its n_active_samples field. The cursor is reloaded from memory at the top of each iteration rather than kept in a register, but nothing outside this ISR changes it -- the only other references to the address are the DPMI lock and unlock calls.

Between interrupts the value is stale: it is left pointing one slot past the end of the array the last pass walked, and no one reads it there. The pass that uses it always writes it before reading it, so the _BSS zero it starts life with is never observed.

It is a static rather than a local because the mixer's working set has to stay resident while interrupts are being serviced: AIL_internal_init_clock_globals DPMI-locks exactly these four bytes (PUSH 0x4 / PUSH 0x6a0b8 at 00045eab, into the lock helper at 0003cb93) as part of the run of mix-ISR statics from 0006a0ac to 0006a0cc, and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_dig_mix_416f0 unlocks the same four bytes at 000477db.

Pool: ail  [all six references are pool_ail library code -- the mix ISR plus the lock/unlock pair; no game or CRT code reaches it]

=== 0006a0bc [PLATE]
Countdown of DIG driver sample slots still to visit in the current mixing pass.

AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr writes it once per timer tick: at 0004626e it takes the driver record pointer from 0006a0c0 (the DIG_DRIVER handed to the ISR), reads the slot count from driver+0x60 and stores it here, storing the matching array base from driver+0x5c into the cursor at 0006a0b8. The loop at 0004628b then runs while this is non-zero, stepping the cursor 0x894 bytes per iteration and decrementing this by one at 000462b8. Only slots whose status word at +0x4 equals 4 are passed to AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample; the tally of those goes into 0006a0cc and is written back to driver+0x64 at 000462d3. Zero therefore means the pass is complete, and it is zero whenever the ISR is not running. The loads at 000461d3, 00046254, 00046331 and 0004638a are dead -- ESI is restored by the POP sequence before each RET -- and are the compiler's residue from caching this global in a register. AIL_internal_init_clock_globals DPMI page-locks these 4 bytes at startup and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_dig_mix_416f0 releases them at shutdown.

Pool: ail  [only AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr, AIL_internal_init_clock_globals and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_dig_mix_416f0 reference it; no game or CRT code reaches it]

=== 0006a0c0 [PLATE]
Pointer to the digital sound driver that AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr is currently servicing.

Written once per interrupt at the top of AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr (000461f5), from the driver argument the ISR was entered with, immediately after the reentry guard at 00061098 is set to 1. Every subsequent step of the ISR reloads it rather than keeping it in a register, and reads the driver record through it: +0x54 is the 'mixing suspended' flag that aborts the pass when non-zero; +0x34 points at the driver's own halfword giving the buffer half the hardware is playing, which is read into 0006a0c4 and compared against the last-served half at +0x38; +0x5c and +0x60 are the head and the count of the active sample list, copied to 0006a0b8 and 0006a0bc for the mixing loop; +0x64 receives the count of samples that actually contributed, staged in 0006a0cc; bit 0x10 of the byte at +0x1c selects drivers that must be told to flip buffers, which is done with AIL_call_driver(*driver, 0x405, &data at 0006a0ac, NULL); +0x58 is a silent-pass counter incremented while +0x64 stays zero and reset when it does not. Field +0 is the driver handle AIL_call_driver takes. The pointer is never cleared, so between interrupts it still names the driver from the last pass.

DPMI-locked as a four-byte object by AIL_internal_init_clock_globals (00045e51) and unlocked by AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_dig_mix_416f0 (00047781), like each of its neighbours 0006a0b8, 0006a0bc, 0006a0c4 and 0006a0c8.

Pool: ail  [only AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr and the two DPMI lock/unlock routines reference it; no game or CRT code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
This must stay a file-static, not become a local in the ISR. Nothing outside one interrupt reads it, so the obvious rewrite folds it into a local variable -- but then the DPMI lock and unlock lists in AIL_internal_init_clock_globals and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_dig_mix_416f0 would be locking a variable that no longer exists, and a hardware interrupt would be dereferencing an unlocked stack slot that a memory manager is free to page out.

=== 0006a0c4 [PLATE]
The DMA buffer half the .DIG driver reports it is currently playing -- 0 or 1, or -1 when the driver reports no half in play.

Written once per pass by AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr at 0004622d, which takes the pointer in DIG_DRIVER+0x34, sign-extends the 16-bit driver status word it addresses (MOVSX EDI,word ptr [EDI]) and stores it here. The ISR then decides whether there is work: -1, or a value equal to the previous pass's copy in DIG_DRIVER+0x38, means no half has flipped and the pass falls through without mixing. When it has changed, the free half is this value exclusive-ORed with 1, and that is how both reads use it -- at 000462d6 as the buffer_index argument of AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_format(drvr, buffer_index), which builds the mix into that half, and at 000462fe into the halfword at +6 of the VDI register block at 0006a0ac immediately before driver call 0x405, which hands the filled half to the .DIG driver. AIL_internal_init_clock_globals (00045e9e) and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_dig_mix_416f0 (000477ce) take its address to DPMI-lock and unlock these four bytes, because the ISR touches it at interrupt time.

Pool: ail  [the only code that reaches it is AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr and the DIG mixer's DPMI lock/unlock pair; it is one of the individually locked four-byte scalars of that ISR's private state block 0006a0b8-0006a0cc]

Rebuild note:
Every read happens in the same ISR pass as the write, so it looks like a scratch temporary that ought to be a local. It cannot be: its address is handed to the DPMI lock and unlock helpers with a length of 4, so it has to stay a file-static of the DIG mixer module.

=== 0006a0c8 [PLATE]
Saved EFLAGS image of the interrupted context while AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr runs with interrupts disabled.

Written once per mixer interrupt at 00046201 by AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr, from the return value of the save-flags-and-CLI thunk at 0003dcb0, right after the ISR has taken ownership by setting data_ail_audio_mix_isr_reentry_guard at 00061098 to 1 and has stashed its driver-state pointer in the global at 0006a0c0. The copy that CALL 0x0003dcb0 leaves in EAX is also kept in EDI for the shortest exit path at 00046211; the global exists because EDI is reused as a sequence index at 0004622d, so the longer paths have nowhere else to find the value. === 0006a0cc [PLATE]
Number of sample slots the digital mix ISR found playing on the current pass, published to the driver's n_active_samples field.

AIL_internal_audio_mix_isr owns it end to end. Once that ISR has decided the driver's buffer really needs refilling, it zeroes this counter at 00046269 and then walks the current DIG_DRIVER's sample array using the cursor at 0006a0b8 and the remaining-slot count at 0006a0bc, both loaded from dig_driver+0x5c and +0x60 at 00046276-00046282. A slot whose status word at +4 holds 4 -- Miles' SMP_PLAYING -- increments this counter at 00046297 and is handed to AIL_internal_mix_dispatch_sample; every slot, played or not, advances the cursor by 0x894 and decrements the count, the loop ending when the count reaches zero (00046290-000462be). The total is then read at 000462cd and stored into the driver record at +0x64, its n_active_samples field.

The driver's copy, not this variable, is what the rest of the pass consults: at 0004632e the ISR reloads dig_driver+0x64 and, if it is zero, falls through to bump the idle-pass counter at dig_driver+0x58, while a non-zero value resets that counter to 0 at 0004633b. Values run from 0 to the driver's slot count; there is no sentinel. Between interrupts the variable holds the previous pass's total and no one reads it there -- each pass writes 0 before it reads, so the zero the CRT leaves in _BSS is never observed.

It is a static rather than a local because the mixer's working set has to stay resident while interrupts are being serviced: AIL_internal_init_clock_globals DPMI-locks exactly these four bytes (PUSH 0x4 / PUSH 0x6a0cc at 00045e7e, into the lock helper at 0003cb93) in the same run that locks 0006a0c8, 0006a0bc, 0006a0c4, 0006a0b8 and the 12-byte block at 0006a0ac, and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_dig_mix_416f0 releases the same four bytes at 000477b0.

Pool: ail  [all five references are Miles AIL library code -- the mix ISR plus its DPMI lock and unlock pair; no game or CRT code reaches it]

Rebuild note:
The counter is DPMI-locked by literal address with a hard-coded length of 4, so it has to stay a file-scope global inside the locked data block. The obvious C -- a local counter declared in the mixing loop, which is all its lifetime needs, since it is zeroed at the top of every pass -- moves the storage onto the stack, outside the locked region, where it can take a not-present page at interrupt time.

=== 0006a0d0 [PLATE]
Scratch cursor into an XMIDI event stream, handed to the variable-length-quantity reader so it can be advanced across the VLQ it consumes.

Written only in FUN_00048f90, the XMIDI event interpreter: at 000492e0 it is set to the current sequence's event pointer (the dword at +0x14 of the sequence state that DAT_0006a0d8 points at) plus one, i.e. to the byte just after the event's status byte. Its address is then passed to AIL_internal_xmidi_read_vlq (000481d0), which reads the variable-length quantity there and leaves this pointing at the first byte past it. FUN_00048f90 reads it back at 000492f2 and subtracts the untouched event pointer, so the VLQ's value plus that difference is the whole event's size in bytes -- status byte, length field and payload -- which is how the interpreter steps over a variable-length event. It has no meaning between calls; nothing else reads it. AIL_internal_init_mdi_state_arrays DPMI-locks it (4 bytes at 0006a0d0) with the rest of the MDI state, and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_mdi_state_arrays_45030 unlocks it, because the interpreter runs at interrupt time.

Pool: ail  [only the Miles sound library reaches it, and it is in the MDI state block that AIL's own init/shutdown pair DPMI-locks]

Rebuild note:
This reads like a local variable and must not become one: the lock and unlock helpers take its address and a length of 4, so it has to stay a module-scope static with a stable address, or the MDI state stops being page-locked for the timer ISR.

=== 0006a0d4 [PLATE]

=== 0006a0d8 [PLATE]
Cursor into the MDI driver's sequence array: the XMIDI sequence the MDI service routine is currently interpreting.

FUN_00048f90, the MDI timer service routine, is entered with the MDI_DRIVER in EBP; it sets this pointer from the driver's sequence-array base at [EBP+0x18] and the loop count at 0006a0e0 from the driver's sequence count, then walks the array, adding the 0x6d4-byte record stride at 00049647 and decrementing 0006a0e0 after each sequence. === 0006a0dc [PLATE]
Slot index into the note-off queue of the XMIDI sequence currently being serviced.

Written and read only by the timer-serviced sequencer tick FUN_00048f90, as the loop cursor over the 32-slot queue that lives inside the sequence state pointed to by 0006a0d8 -- the parallel arrays at seq+0x514 (channel), seq+0x594 (note) and seq+0x614 (ticks left), with the live count at seq+0x510. The note-aging loop at 00049032 sets it to 0 and walks it up to 0x20, decrementing each slot's tick counter, re-sending the channel status with OR AL,0x80 to release a note whose time has run out, and marking that slot free by storing -1 into its seq+0x514 entry. The note-on path at 0004942a resets it to 0 and scans the same table for the first seq+0x514 entry equal to -1; on exit the value is the slot number to fill, and the value 0x20 means the scan ran off the end with no free slot, which is the branch at 00049464 that copies AIL's diagnostic 'Internal note queue overflow' into data_ail_error_text. Range is 0..0x20 inclusive; -1 is the free-slot sentinel stored in the table, never a value this index takes. === 0006a0e0 [PLATE]
Number of XMIDI sequences the MDI service routine still has to visit on the current timer tick.

FUN_00048f90, the MDI timer service routine, is entered with the MDI_DRIVER in EBP. Having claimed data_ail_mdi_serve_reentry_guard, it sets this counter from the driver's sequence count at mdi_driver+0x1c (00048fbf) and the cursor data_ail_mdi_serve_sequence from the sequence-array base at mdi_driver+0x18 (00048fcd). It reads the counter immediately (00048fc7) and jumps to 00049661, past the whole pass, when it is zero, so a driver with no sequences does nothing. Otherwise the two statics advance together at the foot of the loop (0004963a-00049653): the counter is decremented, the cursor gains the 0x6d4-byte sequence-record stride, and the body repeats from 00048fda while the counter is still non-zero. === 0006a0e4 [PLATE]
Beat-clock increment for one MDI service tick at a quarter-note denominator, in units of 1/16 microsecond: 16000000 / data_ail_preference_table[10] (the MDI service rate in Hz).

Written and read only by FUN_00048f90, the MDI sequence service routine, in its handler for the MIDI Set Time Signature meta event (FF 58 04 nn dd cc bb). The handler stores the numerator nn as beats per measure in sequence+0x60, computes this quotient, then scales it by the denominator exponent dd: dd-2 is placed in DAT_0006a0e8 and this value is shifted left by dd-2 when that is non-negative and arithmetically right by 2-dd when it is negative, giving the per-service-tick increment stored in sequence+0x64. On every service call FUN_00048f90 adds sequence+0x64 to the beat accumulator sequence+0x68 and compares it against sequence+0x6c, the tempo in microseconds per quarter note scaled by 16 from the Set Tempo meta event; crossing that threshold advances the beat counter sequence+0x58 and, once it reaches sequence+0x60, the measure counter sequence+0x5c. The factor of 16 shared by this value and the tempo threshold is the fixed-point scale that gives the accumulator sixteenth-of-a-microsecond resolution.

The value is not the shifted result: the store here happens before the shift and the shifted copy goes only to the sequence record, so this global always holds the unscaled quarter-note figure from the most recent time-signature event.

AIL_internal_init_mdi_state_arrays DPMI-locks these 4 bytes at startup and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_mdi_state_arrays_45030 unlocks them at shutdown, alongside the routine's other statics, because the service routine runs from the timer interrupt.

Pool: ail  [reached only by AIL code -- the MDI service routine and the two DPMI lock/unlock helpers for the MDI state arrays; no game or CRT function touches it]

Rebuild note:
The denominator scaling must stay a two-branch if/else. dd-2 is negative for a half- or whole-note denominator, and writing the single expression value << (dd - 2) is undefined behaviour for a negative shift count; the original explicitly negates the count and uses an arithmetic right shift on that path.

=== 0006a0e8 [PLATE]
Working temporary of the meta-event handler inside the MDI timer service routine: the tempo it has just decoded, or the time-signature shift it is about to apply.

Only FUN_00048f90, the MDI service routine, touches it, and only from the two meta-event arms its type dispatch at 0004913d reaches. The Set Tempo arm (0x51, at 000491f1) assembles the three data bytes big-endian into microseconds per quarter note, parks the value here at 00049218 and stores it times 16 into the sequence's beat threshold at SEQUENCE+0x6c. The Time Signature arm (0x58, at 00049234) puts data[0], the beats per bar, into SEQUENCE+0x60 and puts data[1] - 2 here at 00049255: the denominator exponent counted from the quarter note, 0 for x/4, +1 for x/8, -1 for x/2 and so on. That number is the shift applied to 0006a0e4, which holds 16000000 / data_ail_preference_table[10] -- the microsecond-times-16 span of one service tick at the MDI service rate -- negative shifts going right through SAR at 0004928b and non-negative left through SHL at 00049295, with the result written to SEQUENCE+0x64. SEQUENCE+0x64 is then the amount the beat accumulator SEQUENCE+0x68 gains per service tick; the tail of the routine at 00049532 adds it, and each time the accumulator reaches SEQUENCE+0x6c it takes a beat off, bumps the beat-within-bar counter SEQUENCE+0x58, and rolls that into the bar counter SEQUENCE+0x5c when it reaches SEQUENCE+0x60.

The two roles never overlap: the arms are alternatives and the tempo written at 00049218 is dead, overwritten by the next Time Signature event before anything reads it. Nothing outside a call to FUN_00048f90 can rely on the contents. AIL_internal_init_mdi_state_arrays (00047e30) DPMI-locks these 4 bytes and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_mdi_state_arrays_45030 (0004b080) unlocks them.

Pool: ail  [reached only by the three Miles MDI functions; no game or CRT code touches it]

Rebuild note:
The MDI interpreter's scratch variables are file-scope statics precisely so AIL_internal_init_mdi_state_arrays can page-lock them for interrupt-time use, and it locks this address by name as its own 4 bytes. Writing the obvious C -- a local int inside the meta-event switch -- puts it on unlocked stack pages that the timer ISR then touches.

=== 0006a0ec [PLATE]
Status byte of the XMIDI event the sequencer is currently decoding, reduced to its event-type nibble once the channel has been split off.

Written and read only by FUN_00048f90, the timer-serviced XMIDI sequencer tick. At 000490d2 it takes the byte standing at the event cursor of the sequence being served (seq+0x14, reached through data_ail_mdi_serve_sequence), zero-extended to a dword. A value below 0x80 is not a status byte at all: it is the XMIDI inter-event delay, and it ends the event burst for this tick -- the byte is then consumed at the bottom of the loop into the sequence's delta-time countdown at seq+0x2c. So 0x00-0x7f is the loop's terminator, never an event. 0xf0 and 0xf7 take the sysex path at 000492d2, which reads the payload length as a VLQ and copies it into the driver's output buffer; 0xff takes the meta path, whose meta number is put in 0006a0f8 (0x2f end of track, 0x51 tempo, 0x58 time signature). Everything else is a channel event: at 0004936c the low nibble is split off into data_ail_mdi_event_channel and this variable is overwritten with status & 0xf0, so from that point on it holds only the event type, and it is tested against 0x90 to spot the note-on that has to be parked in the sequence's 32-slot note-off queue. Statuses 0xf8-0xfe reach that same path and simply reduce to 0xf0, which is not 0x90, so they fall through to the operand-length table that steps the cursor.

The value means nothing between ticks: it is rewritten from the stream on every pass round the event loop and never read before being written. AIL_internal_init_mdi_state_arrays DPMI-locks these 4 bytes at 00047edc and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_mdi_state_arrays_45030 releases them at 0004b12c, because the routine that uses it runs at timer-interrupt time.

Pool: ail  [only the AIL MDI layer reaches it: the serve routine plus the two DPMI lock/unlock helpers; no game or CRT code references it]

Rebuild note:
Keep data_ail_mdi_event_status a file-scope static, not a local. Its whole live range sits inside one loop of the serve routine, so the obvious C is a local uint, but the library DPMI-locks this exact address with an explicit length of 4 so the interrupt-time sequencer never touches unlocked memory; folding it into the stack frame silently drops it out of the lock list.

=== 0006a0f0 [PLATE]
Set when the sequence being serviced has decoded its End Of Track meta event during this tick.

Owned by the MDI sequencer tick FUN_00048f90 and read nowhere else. Cleared to 0 at the top of each sequence's block, immediately before the delta accumulator at seq+0x54 is advanced by seq+0x44. Set to 1 by the meta-event decoder when the number after an 0xFF status byte is 0x2f, i.e. FF 2F End Of Track; the same branch then either consumes one repeat from seq+0x28 and rewinds the read pointer seq+0x14 to seq+0x10 plus 8, or calls AIL_stop_sequence, puts the sequence in state 2 and invokes the user end-of-sequence callback at seq+0x24.

Once set it short-circuits the remainder of that sequence's tick: the event-fetch loop breaks instead of reading the next status byte, the delta-time byte is not consumed into seq+0x2c, and the beat/measure accounting at seq+0x58..seq+0x6c plus the volume and tempo ramps at seq+0x34 and seq+0x44 are all skipped. It is not cleared again until the next call reaches this sequence, so a sequence that loops back does not start playing its new pass until the following tick. The note-duration aging loop at seq+0x510 is deliberately outside the guard and keeps running.

Values: 0 means keep interpreting, 1 means end of track seen. Sequences whose state at seq+4 is not 4 never touch it.

Pool: ail  [only FUN_00048f90, AIL_internal_init_mdi_state_arrays and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_mdi_state_arrays_45030 reach it, all Miles internals]

Rebuild note:
This is a static, not a per-tick local, and the difference is visible. Writing the natural 'break out of the sequence' or clearing the flag when the loop-back rewind rearms seq+0x14 would let the rewound track's first events play in the same tick and would drop the queued note-offs that the seq+0x510 aging loop still emits on the remaining 100-tick iterations after end of track.

=== 0006a0f4 [PLATE]
Number of XMIDI stream bytes the sequence's event pointer must advance to clear the payload of the meta or SysEx event being interpreted.

Written and read only inside FUN_00048f90, the MDI service routine that interprets XMIDI events for the sequence data_ail_mdi_serve_sequence points at. Both writes take the value from AIL_internal_xmidi_read_vlq (000481d0). In the meta-event path (0004912b) the reader is handed the sequence's own +0x14 event pointer and has already stepped it past the length VLQ, so the value stored at 00049130 is the payload length alone. In the SysEx-shaped path (000492e0 onward) the reader works on the scratch cursor data_ail_xmidi_vlq_scan_ptr and the sequence pointer is left where it was, so the value stored at 00049302 is the payload length plus the width of the length VLQ itself, recovered by subtracting the pre-call stream position.

Every read is the same step, once per meta-event case (000491a7, 000491e3, 00049226, 000492c4, 00049356): load the sequence state and add this to the event pointer at +0x14, which leaves that pointer on the next event's delta time. === 0006a0f8 [PLATE]
Meta-event number of the XMIDI meta event the sequencer is currently decoding.

Written and read only by FUN_00048f90, the timer-serviced XMIDI sequencer tick. Once data_ail_mdi_event_status is seen to be 0xff, this takes the byte after the 0xff marker at the sequence's event cursor (seq+0x14, reached through data_ail_mdi_serve_sequence), zero-extended to a dword; the cursor then steps past both bytes and the payload length is read as a VLQ into 0006a0f4. Three numbers are decoded, everything else being skipped by its length alone: 0x2f end of track, which sets the event-loop terminator 0006a0f0 and then either rewinds the cursor to seq+0x10+8 for another repeat or, when the loop count at seq+0x28 runs out, calls AIL_stop_sequence, puts the sequence in state 2 and invokes the user end-of-sequence callback at seq+0x24; 0x51 set tempo, whose three payload bytes are assembled big-endian and stored times 16 in seq+0x6c; and 0x58 time signature, whose first payload byte becomes the beat count at seq+0x60 while the second, minus 2, shifts 16000000/data_ail_preference_table[10] into the tick period at seq+0x64, left for a positive exponent and right for a negative one, after which the beat and bar counters at seq+0x58 and seq+0x5c are restarted.

The value means nothing between events: it is rewritten from the stream every time a 0xff is met and is never read before being written. AIL_internal_init_mdi_state_arrays DPMI-locks these 4 bytes at 00047eeb and AIL_internal_dpmi_unlock_mdi_state_arrays_45030 releases them at 0004b13b, because the routine that uses it runs at timer-interrupt time.

Rebuild note:

=== 0006a0fc [PLATE]
A 512-byte working copy of the XMIDI sequence's TIMB chunk, filtered down to the timbres the MDI driver does not already hold, and the block that is then handed to the driver to load.

AIL_internal_init_sequence_inner (0004a0f0) is the only function that touches it. Having located the TIMB, RBRN and EVNT chunks of the sequence image and stored their addresses at seq+8, seq+0xc and seq+0x10, it memmoves 0x200 bytes from the TIMB chunk into this buffer at 0004a2d8 -- a fixed length, not the chunk's own length -- and from then on works only on the copy. The layout is IFF as Miles writes it: 'TIMB' at +0, a big-endian chunk length at +4, a little-endian entry count at +8, and count two-byte entries from +0xa, each a (patch, bank) pair with the patch in the low byte. The scan at 0004a2fb..0004a391 walks the entries and asks the driver's timbre-query vector at mdi_driver+0x1a4 whether each one is already loaded; a hit is deleted in place -- the tail shifts down two bytes (0004a352-0004a366), the entry count at +8 is decremented, and the length bytes at +4/+5 are decremented by two with a borrow -- and the same index is retried, so what is left in the buffer is exactly the timbres still to load.

If the count reaches zero there is nothing to do and the routine returns 1. Otherwise it refuses to run with the timer ISR locked: a non-zero AIL_internal_get_isr_lock_count puts 'No timbres loaded' in data_ail_error_text and returns -1. On the normal path all 0x200 bytes are memmoved to *(mdi_driver+8) + 0x100 at 0004a42f, the driver's timbre-request area, and AIL_call_driver is invoked with function 0x503. A zero status word back from the driver means a timbre was rejected, and sprintf builds 'Driver could not install timbre bank %u, patch %u' into data_ail_error_text.

Nothing reads the buffer between calls; every sequence initialisation rewrites it from scratch, so its resting value (zero, since it is _BSS) is never significant. Its single-entry counterpart is data_ail_single_timbre_timb_chunk, which stages one timbre for AIL_install_timbre through the same driver-side area.

Pool: ail  [only AIL_internal_init_sequence_inner reaches it, and its content is a Miles XMIDI IFF chunk]

Rebuild note:
The copy in and the copy out are both a flat 0x200 bytes regardless of the chunk's declared length, so the buffer deliberately over-reads the XMIDI image and always writes a full 512 bytes into the driver's request area; the obvious memcpy(buf, timb, 8 + chunk_len) changes what the driver is handed. The in-place length fixup is also not what it looks like: it decrements the byte pair at +4/+5, which is the TOP half of the big-endian 32-bit IFF length, so writing a correct decrement of the length field produces different bytes here.

=== 0006a2fc [PLATE]
Head of the CRT's free list of stdio stream link nodes -- the streams that have been closed but whose link node and FILE object are held for reuse (__ClosedStreams).

Points at a two-field link node -- next at +0, FILE * at +4 -- or is NULL when nothing is being held. Same node type as the open-stream list head __OpenStreams at 0006a300. _BSS, so it starts NULL, and __InitFiles stores NULL into it again at 000548ff after it has built the initial __OpenStreams chain from the static __iob entries. __freefp is the only writer that adds to it: it walks __OpenStreams for the node whose +4 matches the FILE * being closed, unlinks it there and pushes it here, so pushes are LIFO and the chain runs most-recently-closed first. __allocfp consumes it: it pops the head, takes that node's FILE from +4, keeps only bits 0x4003 of the old flag word at [fp+0xc], memsets the 0x1a-byte FILE to zero, restores those bits and pushes the node back onto __OpenStreams -- only when this list is empty does it fall through to scanning the static __iob at 00061150 or allocating a new FILE. __doopen (FUN_00042675, the file-static close_file of the fopen module, used by freopen) searches this list when the FILE * it was handed is not on __OpenStreams and moves the matching node back to __OpenStreams, which is how freopen revives an already-closed stream; if it is on neither list the caller fails with EBADF. __purgefp walks the chain calling free on each node and leaves the head NULL; it frees the 8-byte node only, never node->stream, because a dynamically allocated FILE is released at close time by __shutdown_stream and the FILEs still reachable from here are the static __iob entries.

Pool: crt  [a data EXTDEF of CLIB3S.LIB's allocfp module, paired with __OpenStreams; every one of the ten references is CRT stdio code]

=== 0006a300 [PLATE]
Head of the CRT's singly linked list of open stdio streams (__OpenStreams).

Points at a two-field link node -- next at +0, FILE * at +4 -- or is NULL when no stream is open. _BSS, so it starts NULL; __InitFiles builds the initial chain at startup by pushing one node per static __iob entry, stepping __iob at 00061150 by sizeof(FILE)==0x1a. __allocfp pushes a node for each newly allocated FILE and __freefp unlinks the node whose stream field matches and moves it to the free-link list at 0006a2fc. Readers walk it from the head following +0 until NULL: fclose and __doopen (FUN_00042675) look up a stream by comparing the incoming FILE * against +4, __flushall flushes every stream whose flag word at [stream+0xc] matches its mask argument, and L$N_ioexit_docloseall closes them all at exit. Pushes are LIFO, so the chain runs newest stream first and the static __iob entries end up last.

Pool: crt  [named by the CLIB3S.LIB ioexit.obj EXTDEF list; every reference is CRT stdio, no game or AIL code touches it]

=== 0006a304 [EOL]
interior of the object at 0006a304

=== 0006a304 [PLATE]
Number of bytes of conventional (real-mode) DOS memory the C runtime keeps free when it has to fall back on DOS allocation for the near heap -- the CLIB3S variable behind WLINK's MINREAL option.

It lives in _BSS, so it starts at 0, and nothing in FDPS ever assigns it: a program that wanted conventional memory left over (for a spawned real-mode child, say) would supply its own 'unsigned __near __minreal = N;' and the linker would take that definition in place of minreal.obj's. The only reader is RationalAlloc (FUN_0004412f), and only after its preferred DPMI INT 31h AX=0501 allocation has failed. 0004417c tests the top twelve bits through the high word at 0006a306 and 00044187 clamps the variable itself -- not a copy -- to 0xfffff, so that the paragraph count cannot overflow BX. 0004419b then takes __minreal >> 4 | 1 paragraphs from DOS with INT 21h AH=48h, allocates the caller's block with a second AH=48h, and gives the first block straight back with AH=49h. That first block is a spacer: it pins the low end of free conventional memory while the real block is taken above it, leaving __minreal bytes free below the heap block. The OR BL,0x1 forces at least one paragraph, which is why the reserve/free pair still happens when the value is 0, as it always is here.

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB minreal.obj defines it as the 4-byte _BSS public __minreal; grownear.obj reaches it as an EXTDEF, and no game or AIL code touches it]

=== 0006a308 [PLATE]
The 128-byte floating-point state area that __hook387 registers with Windows 386 enhanced mode, so the VMM has somewhere to keep this program's emulated 80x87 state (hook387.obj's own FPArea).

Nothing in FDPS reads or writes these bytes. The single reference in the image is 00051a9f MOV ESI,0x6a308 inside __hook387 (00051a56), which passes the address out and never looks at it again. __hook387 gets that far only on its Windows path: INT 2Fh AX=1600h must report enhanced mode (AL neither 00h nor 80h), and the 80x87-emulator interface INT 2Fh AH=FAh must answer AX=0666h to AL=00h and AX=0000h to AL=22h. It then sets L$N_hook387_win386_emulator_registered (00061445) to 1, issues AH=FAh AL=1Eh with ESI pointing here and BX=CX=DX=0, and follows it with AH=FAh AL=20h passing the same address split as BX = low half, CX = high half, with DX = CS -- so the block is handed over twice, once as a linear address and once alongside the emulator's code selector. __hook387 then returns 1. On the other path -- no Windows, DPMI INT 31h AX=0A00h resolving "RATIONAL DOS/4G", INT 7 hooked to __int7 and CR0.EM set, which sets L$N_hook387_hooked (00061444) instead -- the address is never handed out and the buffer stays untouched. __unhook387 (00051b27) de-registers with AH=FAh AL=21h (DX = CS) then AL=1Fh, and does not pass the address again.

The internal layout belongs to the emulator interface, not to the C library: hook387.obj reserves the block as its entire _BSS segment, 0x80 bytes with FPArea at offset 0, and declares no structure over it. It sits in _BSS, so the CRT startup zeroes it before __hook387 runs; anything ever written into it is written from outside this program.

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(hook387), the module that also defines __hook387 and __unhook387, names _BSS offset 0 "FPArea" in its LPUBDEF and sizes that segment 0x80; the only reference in the image is that module's own __hook387]

Rebuild note:
Nothing in the program ever touches these 128 bytes -- __hook387 only hands the address out over INT 2Fh AH=FAh -- so a faithful rewrite is tempted to delete the buffer as dead, shrink it to whatever it looks like it needs, or make it a local of __hook387. All three are wrong: the other side of the emulator interface owns the block after registration, long after __hook387 has returned, so it has to stay a file-static of exactly 128 bytes at a fixed address, and the declaration has to survive a compiler that can see no use for it (hook387.obj reserves it as its entire _BSS segment, length 0x80).

=== 0006a388 [PLATE]
Static struct tm that Watcom's gmtime() fills in and returns a pointer to.

Written only by _gmtime (000523af), which gmtime (000523d2) calls as _gmtime(timer, this buffer) and whose return value it passes straight back; _gmtime does the breakdown through __brktime (0005226f), handing it the 25567-day offset from 1900-01-01 to the epoch. gmtime returns this address, so every caller shares one buffer and each call overwrites the previous result -- it is UTC only, with no timezone or DST adjustment applied, which is what separates it from the localtime buffer at 0006a06c. Layout is Watcom 10.0a's struct tm: nine ints in order tm_sec, tm_min, tm_hour, tm_mday, tm_mon, tm_year (years since 1900), tm_wday (0=Sunday), tm_yday (0..365), tm_isdst (always 0 here). Lives in _BSS, so it is all zeroes until the first gmtime call.

Pool: crt  [the only reference is the CRT's own gmtime; it is the file-static result buffer of module gmtime]

=== 0006a3ac [PLATE]
The C runtime's _doserrno: the raw DOS error code returned by the last INT 21h call the runtime made that failed.

Written only by __set_doserrno (0004be05), which fetches this address from __get_doserrno_ptr (0005488d) and stores its int argument through it. Its callers are __set_errno_dos (0004bd4a), spawnve, spawnvpe and __cenvarg: each passes the value DOS returned in AX with carry set, and __set_errno_dos then maps that code to a POSIX error number and puts the mapped value in the neighbouring errno cell at 0006a3b0 through __set_errno. The values are DOS error numbers as INT 21h reports them (2 file not found, 3 path not found, 5 access denied, 8 not enough memory, and so on); 0 means no failure has been recorded yet. In this image the cell is write-only -- __get_doserrno_ptr has exactly one caller, __set_doserrno, so no code ever reads the value back. It lives in _BSS, so the CRT zeroes it at startup and it stays 0 until the first failed DOS call.

Pool: crt  [the _BSS cell of CLIB3S.LIB's errno module, paired with errno at 0006a3b0 and reached only through the library's own accessor; no game code touches it]

=== 0006a3b0 [PLATE]
The C runtime's errno cell: the error code the most recent failing library call recorded, zero when nothing has failed.

Written only through __get_errno_ptr@00054887, which returns its address; nothing stores to it directly, which is why the cell carries a single reference. __set_errno@0004bdf9 is the general setter and is fed by __set_EDOM@0004bdda, __set_ERANGE@0004bde9 and __set_EINVAL@0004bde5, by __set_errno_dos@0004bd4a after it maps a raw DOS error through the table at 00061139, and by the file primitives directly (close and read store 4, read and write store 6, write stores 0xC, the fopen mode parser stores 9). sbrk@0004e6ab and __brk@0004e76d store 5 through the accessor when an allocation fails. spawnve@000556a9 and spawnvpe@00054dc7 read the cell back and compare it against 1. The values are Watcom's own numbering from its errno.h, not the POSIX one: 0 EZERO, 1 ENOENT, 2 E2BIG, 3 ENOEXEC, 4 EBADF, 5 ENOMEM, 6 EACCES, 9 EINVAL, 0xC ENOSPC, 0xD EDOM, 0xE ERANGE. The CRT zeroes it with the rest of _BSS at startup and nothing else resets it, so a value here only means "the last failure was this", never "a call just failed".

Pool: crt  [reached only by CLIB3S.LIB's own accessor; Watcom 10.0a's H/errno.h declares this cell as `extern volatile int errno;` and macro-expands every source-level use of errno to (*__get_errno_ptr()), which is exactly the shape in the image. No game or AIL code touches it.]

=== 0006a3b4 [PLATE]
Watcom CRT ___Argc: the argument count the C startup hands to main.

Written exactly once, at the tail of __Init_Argv (0004e0f1, MOV dword ptr [0006a3b4],EBP). EBP was set at 0004e061 by LEA EBP,[EAX+1], where EAX is the word count returned by the counting pass of _SplitParms (0004e053) over the command line at _LpCmdLine (00060424) -- the +1 is the argv[0] slot. Read exactly once, by __CMain (0004df88), which pushes it behind ___Argv (0006a3b8) and calls main at 0004df8f, so this is literally main's argc. Range is 1 upward; it is never 0, because argv[0] is always counted.

___Argc is a mirror of _argc (000603b4), not the same variable. __Init_Argv keeps the two in step only on the success path: at 0004e0d4 it stores EBP into _argc, then at 0004e0f1 the same EBP here. When malloc fails at 0004e079 the branch at 0004e085 goes to 0004e0e2, which zeroes _argv and _argc from EAX = 0, and then falls straight into 0004e0ec -- so ___Argv gets the NULL out of _argv, but ___Argc still gets the counted EBP. FDPS accepts no command-line options, so in practice the value is 1.

Pool: crt  [PUBDEF32 ___Argc at offset 0 of the 8-byte _BSS segment of Watcom 10.0a CLIB3S ___argc.obj, with ___Argv at +4 landing on 0006a3b8; the only referencing functions are the CRT's __Init_Argv and __CMain]

Rebuild note:
___Argc/___Argv and _argc/_argv are two separate pairs. Writing __CMain as main(_argc, _argv) -- the obvious thing, since they hold the same values on every normal run -- drops the allocation-failure asymmetry, where _argc is 0 but ___Argc still holds the parsed count and ___Argv is NULL, i.e. main is entered with argc > 0 and argv == NULL. Keep both pairs and keep the store order at 0004e0d4/0004e0f1.

=== 0006a3b8 [PLATE]
Watcom CRT ___Argv: the argument vector the C startup hands to main. ___Argv[0] is the program name, ___Argv[1..___Argc-1] the parsed command-line words, ___Argv[___Argc] is NULL.

Written exactly once, at the tail of __Init_Argv (0004e0f7), from the value loaded out of _argv (000603b8) one instruction earlier at 0004e0ec. __Init_Argv is the XI auto-init routine that __CMain runs through __CommonInit (0004df7c) before main: it scans _LpCmdLine (00060424) to count the words, allocates one block holding a copy of the command-line text followed by (count+1) pointer slots, stores _LpPgmName (00060428) into slot 0, fills the rest, NULL-terminates, and publishes the block base in _argv. Read exactly once, by __CMain (0004df81), which pushes it as main's second argument at 0004df87 and calls main at 0004df8f.

___Argv is a mirror of _argv (000603b8), not the same variable, and the two are kept in step only on the success path. When the allocation at 0004e079 fails, the branch at 0004e085 reaches 0004e0e2, which stores EAX = 0 into _argv and _argc, and then falls straight into the common tail at 0004e0ec -- so ___Argv picks up the NULL out of _argv, while ___Argc (0006a3b4) still receives the counted EBP. FDPS accepts no command-line options, so in practice this points at a two-slot vector: the program name and the NULL.

This is the last dword of _BSS (00063930-0006a3bb), so the CRT's startup clear leaves it NULL until __Init_Argv writes it.

Pool: crt  [PUBDEF32 ___Argv at offset 4 of the 8-byte _BSS segment of Watcom 10.0a CLIB3S ___argc.obj, with ___Argc at offset 0 landing on 0006a3b4; the only referencing functions are the CRT's __Init_Argv and __CMain]

Rebuild note:
___Argv/___Argc and _argv/_argc are two separate pairs. Writing __CMain as main(_argc, _argv) -- the obvious thing, since they hold the same values on every normal run -- drops the allocation-failure asymmetry, where _argc/_argv are zeroed but ___Argc still holds the parsed word count and ___Argv is NULL, i.e. main is entered with argc > 0 and argv == NULL. Keep both pairs, keep the store order at 0004e0f1/0004e0f7, and keep ___Argv sourced from _argv rather than from the register that held the block base.

=== 0006a3c0 [PLATE]
The Watcom startup's copy of the two PSP-derived strings: the command tail first, NUL-terminated, then the program name immediately after it, also NUL-terminated.

L$1_cstrt386_start_body writes it once, before main runs. It computes this address as the end of _BSS (0006a3bc) rounded up to a 16-byte boundary at 0004344f, skips the leading spaces of the DOS command tail at PSP:80h, copies the rest here with REP MOVSB at 00043478 and appends two NUL bytes at 0004347c-0004347d; the environment scan that follows copies the program name over the second of those NULs (000434b2). The same aligned address is recomputed at 00043500 and stored in _LpCmdLine (00060424), _LpPgmName (00060428) receives the address of the program-name copy, and _STACKLOW (00060430) the first free byte past it, which is where the near heap begins. Nothing writes the buffer after startup. The readers are __CMain (0004df4c), which splits _LpCmdLine into argc/argv before calling main, and anything that reads _LpPgmName. The extent is whatever the two strings need: at most a 127-byte command tail plus its NUL and a DOS path of at most 128 bytes including its NUL. The CRT's BSS clear runs afterwards and stops one paragraph short of this address, at 0006a3bc, so it never touches the copy just made.

Pool: crt  [written and read only by the CLIB3S cstrt386 startup object, and its pointers _LpCmdLine, _LpPgmName and _STACKLOW are the Watcom low-globals block]

Rebuild note:
This buffer has no storage of its own in the image: its address is (_end + 15) & ~15, computed at run time, it lies above the 00063930-0006a3bc span the CRT zeroes, and _STACKLOW, the base the near heap grows up from, is derived from where the copied strings end. Declaring it in C as char cmdline_buffer[256] would place it inside _BSS instead, move _end, and shift both this address and the near-heap base.
