=== 00070000 [PLATE]
Selector half of the INT 09h keyboard vector that was in place before the game installed its own handler.

fdps_install_keyboard_isr writes it: INT 21h with AX=3509h returns the current INT 09h handler in ES:EBX, and the routine stores EBX at 00070002 (the offset half) and ES here, then points the vector at fdps_keyboard_isr with AX=2509h. fdps_uninstall_keyboard_isr is the only reader: it loads this word into DS and the offset into EDX and calls INT 21h AX=2509h to put the original handler back. The value is a protected-mode selector, meaningful only to the DPMI host; zero is the image's initial value and means no handler has been saved yet. There is a single slot, so a second install without an intervening uninstall would overwrite the saved vector and lose the original handler.

Pool: fdps  [both referencing functions are pool_fdps game code; neither the CRT nor the sound library touches this object]

=== 00070002 [PLATE]
Offset half of the INT 09h (keyboard IRQ) handler that was installed before this program hooked it.

Written once by fdps_install_keyboard_isr, which calls INT 21h/AX=3509 to fetch the current INT 09h vector into ES:EBX, stores EBX here and the ES selector into the word at 00070000, then points INT 09h at fdps_keyboard_isr (00056837) with DS=CS. Read once by fdps_uninstall_keyboard_isr, which loads this offset into EDX, the companion selector into DS, and calls INT 21h/AX=2509 to restore the original handler before clearing the shutdown flag at 00070006. The value is a raw protected-mode code offset supplied by the DOS extender, meaningful only as the EDX half of the DS:EDX pair handed back to Set Interrupt Vector; the game never calls through it, so the installed ISR does not chain to the old handler. Zero here means no vector has been captured yet.

Pool: fdps  [both referencing functions are the game's own keyboard-hook pair; no CRT or AIL code reaches this address.]

=== 00070006 [PLATE]
The raw keyboard scancode latch: the last byte the game's INT 09h handler read from port 0x60, or 0xff when no key is pending.

fdps_keyboard_isr writes it on every keyboard interrupt, unfiltered -- make codes and break codes (bit 7 set, i.e. >= 0x80) alike -- before it de-duplicates the code against 00070021 and appends make codes only to the ten-entry ring buffer at 0007000f. fdps_uninstall_keyboard_isr stores 0xff once it has put the original INT 09h vector back; 0xff is also the value in the image, and it is not a scancode but the no-key-pending state. No caller names the address: fdps_keyboard_scancode_ptr returns a pointer to this byte and consumers work through it. fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat reads it, compares it with data_fdps_input_key_repeat_prev_scancode and turns a held key into repeats no faster than one per timer tick; fdps_map_cursor_select_loop and the other input loops store 0xff back through the pointer to throw away a key left over from before the loop; fdps_animate_move_step_down tests it for scancodes 2 and 3, the two keys that fast-forward unit movement. Only the most recent interrupt survives here, so a key pressed and released between two polls is seen only as its break code -- code that wants every keystroke reads the ring buffer instead.

Pool: fdps  [all three referencing functions are pool_fdps game code and belong to the game's own keyboard ISR; neither the CRT nor the sound library reaches into the 00070000 object]

Rebuild note:
Declare it unsigned. Watcom's default char is signed, so writing 'char' here makes the 0xff sentinel and every break code negative: the ISR's unsigned 'below 0x80' make-code test would then admit releases into the ring buffer, and fdps_read_scancode_auto_repeat's zero-extending widen to uint would become a sign extension and never match the stored previous code.

=== 0007000f [PLATE]
Ten-slot ring buffer of raw AT keyboard make codes, filled by the game's own INT 9 handler.

fdps_keyboard_isr writes it: after reading port 0x60 it drops the code when it repeats the previous one (DAT_00070021) or when bit 7 is set (a break/key-release code, CMP BL,0x80 / JNC), and otherwise stores the make code at the tail index DAT_0007001d, then increments that index and wraps it to 0 at 10. fdps_read_keyboard_queue drains it: it returns 0xff when the head index DAT_00070019 equals the tail, otherwise takes the slot at the head, advances the head and wraps it at 10. fdps_flush_keyboard_queue and fdps_wait_any_key discard the contents by assigning tail := head. Every stored value is therefore a make code in 0x01..0x7f; 0xff is not a stored value but the reader's empty-queue sentinel, and it is also what the ten slots are initialised to in the image. Because empty is head == tail, the ring holds at most nine pending keys: an eleventh keypress with nothing read makes the tail lap the head, and the queue then reads as empty rather than full.

Pool: fdps  [both referencing functions are pool fdps; this is the game's own INT 9 ring, not the BIOS buffer and not a library object]

Rebuild note:
The ISR has no full check. Adding one, or sizing the ring so the tail cannot lap the head, changes behaviour: in the original an overrun silently discards every pending key instead of dropping only the newest.

=== 00070019 [PLATE]
Read cursor of the keyboard scancode ring at data_fdps_input_scancode_queue; the index of the next make code the game will consume, 0..9.

fdps_read_keyboard_queue is the only function that advances it: when it differs from the write cursor at 0007001d the reader takes data_fdps_input_scancode_queue[head], then increments the head and wraps it to 0 when it reaches 10. fdps_wait_any_key busy-waits while head equals the write cursor and then assigns the write cursor := head, and fdps_flush_keyboard_queue does that assignment on its own; both discard the queue contents by moving the writer's cursor back rather than by moving this one forward, so this value only ever walks forward one slot per key actually consumed. head == write cursor means the queue is empty, which is also the state the object image starts in, both cursors being zero. fdps_keyboard_isr never touches this variable -- it owns the write cursor only -- so the ring has exactly one producer and one consumer and neither index is shared.

Pool: fdps  [all three referencing functions are pool fdps; this is the game's own INT 9 ring buffer, with no library reaching it]

=== 0007001d [PLATE]
Producer cursor of the 10-entry keyboard scancode ring at data_fdps_input_scancode_queue: the index of the slot the next scancode will be stored in, 0..9.

fdps_keyboard_isr is the only code that advances it: on a make code (BL < 0x80) it stores the scancode at data_fdps_input_scancode_queue[this index], increments, and wraps to 0 when the value reaches 10. fdps_read_keyboard_queue consumes from the separate read cursor at 00070019 and treats read == write as 'queue empty', returning 0xff in AL. fdps_wait_any_key spins while read == write and then empties the queue; fdps_flush_keyboard_queue empties it unconditionally. Both empty it by assigning the read cursor into THIS variable, i.e. the write cursor is rolled back onto the read cursor rather than the read cursor being advanced. There is no separate count, so a ring that has taken 10 unread scancodes reads as empty again.

Pool: fdps  [only game code touches it -- the four referencing functions are the game's own INT 9 handler and its queue accessors; it lives in the 00070000 low-level input object]

Rebuild note:
The flush path assigns write = read, not read = write. Writing the natural 'read_index = write_index' looks equivalent but is not: this variable is also written by the INT 9 handler, so rolling it back is what the original does to scancodes that arrive during the flush, and the queue's fill state after a flush differs if the assignment is inverted. Keep the direction, and keep the wrap test as an exact '== 10' with no bounds check.

=== 00070021 [PLATE]
The keyboard ISR's private copy of the previous scancode, used to swallow repeats of a code already seen.

fdps_keyboard_isr is the only function that touches it. After reading port 0x60 and latching the code in data_fdps_input_last_scancode, it compares the new code with this byte; on a match it does nothing further but the PIC EOI, so the code is neither recorded nor queued. On a mismatch it stores the new code here and, if the code is a make code (below 0x80), appends it to data_fdps_input_scancode_queue. That is what stops the 8042's typematic repeat of a held key from filling the ten-slot ring: the first make code goes in, every repeat of it is dropped, and the next distinct code -- normally the matching break code -- reopens the filter. The byte is initialised to 0xff in the object3 image, which is not a scancode and so guarantees the first code of the run is never filtered.

It holds the same value as data_fdps_input_last_scancode only until a consumer touches that one. data_fdps_input_last_scancode is public through fdps_keyboard_scancode_ptr and the input loops store 0xff into it to consume a key, and fdps_uninstall_keyboard_isr does the same on shutdown; this byte is never written from outside the ISR, so the filter still knows which key is being held after the latch has been cleared.

Pool: fdps  [its one referencing function, fdps_keyboard_isr, is pool fdps game code; neither the CRT nor the sound library reaches into the 00070000 input object]

Rebuild note:
Keep it as a second variable. The obvious rewrite compares the incoming code against data_fdps_input_last_scancode, which the ISR has just assigned, and drops this byte as redundant; that breaks held keys, because once an input loop clears the latch to 0xff the next typematic repeat no longer matches and is queued as a fresh keypress.

=== 00070022 [PLATE]
Number of source rows the RLE sprite blitter still has to draw; in the scaling variants, the source height the vertical Bresenham accumulator is measured against.

fdps_blit_dispatch writes it once per blit from the height argument (MOV BX,word ptr [EBP+0x14] at 000568ff) immediately after storing the width at 00070024, then enters the selected variant. Every non-scaling variant -- fdps_rle_blit_passthrough, fdps_rle_blit_remap_sprite_and_backdrop, fdps_rle_blit_with_palette_remap, fdps_rle_blit_recolor, fdps_rle_blit_rotated, fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_horizontal, fdps_rle_blit_translucent, fdps_rle_blit_tint, fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop and fdps_rle_blit_translucent_color_range -- finishes a row by advancing EDI to the next destination line and then DEC word ptr [0x00070022] / JNZ, returning only when the counter reaches zero. The test is at the bottom of the loop, so the value on entry is exactly the number of rows drawn and an entry value of 0 means 65536 rows, not none. fdps_rle_blit_scaled and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled never decrement it: they hold it as the source height, compare the accumulator at 00070026 (stepped by 0007002a) against it with unsigned CMP/JA, and subtract it to wrap the accumulator when a source row is consumed, counting destination rows in 0007002c instead. fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_vertical reads it, decrements the register copy and multiplies by the destination pitch at 0007002e to find the bottom row it starts from. The word is scratch shared by the whole family, valid only for the blit in progress.

Pool: fdps  [only the game's own blitter family reaches it; no CRT or AIL code refers to this address]

Rebuild note:
The row loop is a do-while: entry height 0 draws 65536 rows, not zero. Rewriting it as for (row = 0; row < height; row++), or adding a zero-height guard, changes behaviour for that input, so keep the post-decrement form and leave the guard out.

=== 00070024 [PLATE]
Source width in pixels of the sprite currently being blitted -- the pixel count each RLE kernel loads into BX at the top of every row.

fdps_blit_dispatch is the only writer: it publishes its 'width' argument here, its 'height' argument into the row counter at 00070022 and its 'pitch' argument into 0007002e, then jumps to one of thirteen blit kernels selected by the mode byte 0-12. All the readers are those kernels, which take no arguments and pick their geometry up from this block. The straight-copy family -- fdps_rle_blit_passthrough, _remap_sprite_and_backdrop, _with_palette_remap, _recolor, _translucent, _translucent_color_range, _tint, _tint_sprite_and_backdrop and _skip_row -- reloads this word into BX at the start of each row, decodes command bytes until BX reaches exactly zero, then decrements 00070022 and starts the next row. fdps_rle_blit_scaled and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled use it as the denominator of a Bresenham-style accumulator: the accumulator gains the step at 00070028 per source pixel and loses this width per destination pixel emitted. fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_horizontal adds it to the destination pointer to start at the right-hand end of the row and walks backwards; fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_vertical adds it to the pitch and negates the sum to walk rows upwards. The value is an unsigned pixel count, truncated to 16 bits from the dispatcher's int argument; it stays valid only for the duration of one dispatch call, and the kernels never write it.

Pool: fdps  [the sole writer and all fifteen reading functions are pool_fdps game code; this is the game's own blit parameter block, not a library object -- neither the CRT nor the sound library reaches it]

=== 00070026 [PLATE]
Vertical Bresenham error accumulator for the scaled RLE sprite blitters.

fdps_rle_blit_scaled (00056c5e) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) seed it at the top of a blit with the destination height held in 0007002a. After each destination row has been emitted they run the row-advance loop: while this value is <= the source height in 00070022 they call fdps_rle_skip_row (00056dc9), which consumes one whole source row of 00070024 pixels from the RLE stream, and add the destination height; once the value exceeds the source height they subtract the source height and store the remainder back here. It therefore holds how far the source cursor has run ahead of the destination cursor, always in the range 1..(source height + destination height), and it is what makes source rows repeat when the sprite is stretched and drop when it is squashed. Unsigned throughout -- the loop test at 00056d8c and 000574c4 is CMP/JA. It is scratch shared by the whole blitter block at 00070022-00070031 (00070022 source height, 00070024 source width, 00070028 destination width, 0007002a destination height, 0007002c destination rows remaining, 0007002e destination pitch, 00070030 per-row destination advance), which fdps_blit_dispatch (000568db) fills in from its arguments before choosing a blitter. fdps_rle_blit_rotated (00056e2a) loads it at 000570a9 into DX and overwrites DX on the very next instruction, so that routine does not actually use the value.

Pool: fdps  [reached only by the three game RLE blitters; no CRT or AIL code refers to it]

Rebuild note:
The accumulator starts each blit at the destination height, not at zero, and the row-advance loop tests <= the source height before the first skip. Writing the usual "acc = 0; acc += dst_h; if (acc >= src_h)" Bresenham instead shifts the source-to-destination row mapping by one row and loses the last destination row at integer scale factors.

=== 00070028 [PLATE]
Width in pixels of the destination rectangle the scaling RLE blitters draw; also the numerator of their horizontal Bresenham step.

Written once per blit, only by the two scaling variants. fdps_rle_blit_scaled takes it from its first extra argument (word at [EBP+0x1c]) and puts the destination height in 0007002a from [EBP+0x1e]. fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled takes it from field +0 of the parameter block whose address arrives in [EBP+0x1c], with the destination height at +4 and the rotation step pair at +8 and +0xc. Neither of the plain blit variants touches it, and neither does fdps_blit_dispatch, which sets only the source width at 00070024 and data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows at 00070022.

Each destination row begins by loading it twice: into BX as the number of pixels still to emit on the row, and into BP as the starting value of the horizontal accumulator. Decoding then runs the classic ratio loop -- while the accumulator is below the source width at 00070024 the blitter consumes another source pixel and adds this value to the accumulator; when the accumulator reaches the source width it subtracts the source width, writes one destination pixel and decrements BX. The row ends when BX reaches zero, so exactly this many pixels are written per row. The end-of-row advance is precomputed once at entry as 00070030 = 0007002e (destination pitch) - this width, added to EDI after each row. Note the accumulator starts at this value rather than at zero, so the very first source pixel is already credited; the vertical axis is the same arrangement one axis over, 0007002a stepping the accumulator at 00070026 against data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows. The word is scratch, valid only for the blit in progress.

Pool: fdps  [both referencing functions are the game's own blitter family; no CRT or AIL code reaches this address]

Rebuild note:
The destination-pixel loop is a do-while on BX, so a destination width of 0 emits 65536 pixels rather than none; and the pitch-minus-width advance at 00070030 is computed in 16 bits and zero-extended, so a destination wider than the pitch wraps to a huge forward advance instead of stepping backwards. Writing for (x = 0; x < dest_width; x++) or a signed int advance changes behaviour in both cases.

=== 0007002a [PLATE]
Height in rows of the destination rectangle the two resampling RLE blit modes are drawing into.

Written once per blit, immediately after the destination width at 00070028. fdps_rle_blit_scaled (blit mode 4) reads it as the high half of fdps_blit_dispatch's packed sixth argument, word ptr [EBP+0x1e]; fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (blit mode 6) reads it from the second field of the four-int geometry record that same argument points at, word ptr [record+4]. No other blit variant touches it, and neither routine ever writes it again.

It is read for two purposes. Both routines seed the destination-row counter at 0007002c and the vertical resampling accumulator at 00070026 with it before the row loop starts. Then, at the end of every destination row, the vertical Bresenham adds it to that accumulator once for each whole encoded source row fdps_rle_skip_row steps over, looping while the accumulator has not passed the source height at 00070022 and subtracting the source height once on exit. So the source row advance per destination row is dest_height / src_height: a source row is re-decoded from its start when scaling up and rows are skipped when scaling down.

A value of 0 is not a no-op. The vertical Bresenham adds this word to an accumulator until the accumulator exceeds the source height, so zero makes that loop at 00056d8c (and 000574c4) run forever; the destination-row counter it seeds is also tested only after being decremented, which would ask for 65536 rows. Callers are expected to pass a positive height.

Pool: fdps  [both referencing functions are pool fdps members of the game's own RLE blitter family; no CRT or AIL code reaches this address]

Rebuild note:
The two callers disagree about how the geometry reaches them. Mode 4 unpacks width and height from one 32-bit argument as two adjacent words, so the height is at argument+2; mode 6 takes a pointer to a record whose fields are 4 bytes apart and reads the height at record+4, with only the low word of each field used. Declaring the mode-6 record as an array or struct of shorts picks up the wrong field.

=== 0007002c [PLATE]
Number of destination rows the scaled RLE blitters have still to write.

Written twice, each time as the seed of an output-row loop: fdps_rle_blit_scaled at 00056c7d and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled at 00057221 both copy data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_dest_height (0007002a) into it before the first row. Read only by the tail of those same loops (00056dbb, 00057543), which decrement it once per finished destination row -- after EDI has been advanced to the next destination line -- and repeat while it is non-zero, so the routine returns exactly when it reaches 0.

It is the output-side counterpart of data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows (00070022), and the two must not be confused: that word carries the source height in these two variants, which they compare the vertical Bresenham accumulator at 00070026 against and subtract from it when a source row is consumed, but never decrement. This word is what actually counts the blit down to its end. It is part of the graphics scratch block at 00070022-00070033 that fdps_blit_dispatch and the scaling variants fill in before drawing; no function outside those two blitters touches it.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_rle_blit_scaled and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled reference it, both pool_fdps, and it belongs to the game's own blitter scratch block]

Rebuild note:
The loop is DEC/JNZ, i.e. do-while, not a counted for loop: a destination height of 0 writes 65536 rows rather than none. A faithful rewrite must keep the post-test form.

=== 0007002e [PLATE]
Destination row stride in bytes for the RLE sprite blitter: how far apart two vertically adjacent pixels sit in the destination buffer.

fdps_blit_dispatch (000568db) is the only writer. It stores the low 16 bits of its pitch argument here (MOV word ptr [0x0007002e],DX at 000568ea) next to the source width at 00070024 and the row count at 00070022, then keeps the full 32-bit pitch minus width in EDX as the row advance the straight-copy kernels consume, and jumps to the kernel the mode byte selects. The readers are the kernels that have to derive their own row step. fdps_rle_blit_scaled (00056c5e) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) form the destination row advance 00070030 = this value minus the destination width in 00070028. fdps_rle_blit_rotated (00056e2a) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled zero-extend it into EBP and publish it, negated according to which quadrant the rotation falls in, as the vertical step in 00070038 and 00070040. fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_horizontal (00057551) uses it directly as the per-row EDI advance (ADD EDI,EDX at 000575dd). fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_vertical (000575ed) multiplies it by remaining_rows-1 to land the destination pointer on the last row, then falls through to fdps_rle_blit_passthrough with -(this + source width) as an upward row step.

The value is unsigned and is in practice the width of the destination surface -- 320 for the VGA page, the sprite cache width for off-screen composition. It is not state that survives a blit: every blit rewrites it before dispatching, so nothing reads a stale value.

Pool: fdps  [written and read only by the game's own blit family; no CRT or AIL code refers to it]

=== 00070030 [PLATE]
Byte displacement that moves the destination pointer from the end of one output row to the start of the next; the memory copy of the advance the register-based blitters keep in EDX.

fdps_blit_dispatch (000568db) computes it once per blit as the destination pitch argument minus the destination width argument (MOV EDX,dword ptr [EBP+0x18]; SUB EDX,dword ptr [EBP+0x10] at 000568e7-000568f1) and hands it to the selected variant in EDX. The variants that need EDX as scratch for their blend arithmetic spill it here on entry -- fdps_rle_blit_translucent (0005761b), fdps_rle_blit_tint_sprite_and_backdrop (00057793), fdps_rle_blit_tint (00057916) and fdps_rle_blit_translucent_color_range (00057a74) all begin with MOV dword ptr [0x00070030],EDX -- and each finishes a row with ADD EDI,dword ptr [0x00070030] followed by DEC word ptr [0x00070022], returning when the row counter reaches zero. fdps_rle_blit_scaled (00056c5e) does not use the dispatcher's value: its rows are the stretched destination width, so at 00056c8b-00056c99 it recomputes the advance as the destination pitch at 0007002e minus the scaled destination width at 00070028 and stores that instead, consuming it at 00056db5. fdps_rle_blit_passthrough (00056a0d) and the variants that jump into it keep the advance in EDX for the whole blit and never read or write this dword; fdps_rle_blit_mirrored_vertical (000575ed) negates EDX before entering that loop, which is why the quantity is signed. This is scratch belonging to the blitter block at 00070022-00070031 (00070022 rows remaining, 00070024 source width, 00070026 vertical scaling accumulator, 00070028 destination width, 0007002a destination height, 0007002c destination rows remaining, 0007002e destination pitch, 00070030 this advance) and is meaningful only for the blit in progress.

Pool: fdps  [only the game's own RLE blitter family reaches it; no CRT or AIL code refers to this address]

Rebuild note:
fdps_rle_blit_scaled builds this dword out of 16-bit arithmetic zero-extended to 32 bits (XOR EBP,EBP at 00056c74, then MOV BP / SUB BP before MOV dword ptr [0x00070030],EBP), while the four spilling variants store a full 32-bit signed EDX. Writing the obvious signed advance = dst_pitch - dst_width for the scaled path makes a destination narrower than the pitch difference come out negative, where the original wraps in 16 bits and zero-extends to a large positive advance, sending the destination pointer the other way.

=== 00070034 [PLATE]
Destination x step, in bytes, taken for each source pixel advanced along a source row by the rotating RLE blitters.

Holds +1 or -1. fdps_rle_blit_rotated (00056e2a) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) both open by reading the caller's two rotation components (a 12.12 fixed-point pair, 0x1000 = 1.0) and branching on their signs into one of four quadrant cases; each case writes this variable together with data at 00070038, 0007003c and 00070040, the other three components of the destination step matrix. This one is the horizontal step for source-x advance and takes the sign of the first component; 00070038 is the vertical step (+/- the destination pitch read from 0007002e) for the same advance, while 0007003c and 00070040 are the horizontal and vertical steps applied once per source row by the outer loop at 000570a9-0005710d.

The pixel loop keeps a 12.12 accumulator in DX, adds the absolute first component (0007004c) to it per source pixel, and adds this value to the destination pointer EDI each time the accumulator crosses 0x1000 -- so the destination walks one pixel left or right for every whole unit of horizontal travel the rotation calls for. The image holds 1 here, but that initial value is dead: all four quadrant branches write it before any read.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_rle_blit_rotated and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled reference it; it is game sprite-rendering scratch state]

=== 00070038 [PLATE]
Signed destination-pointer delta of one screen row, applied by the rotating RLE blitters when walking one pixel along a source row crosses into the next destination row.

Written once per blit, by fdps_rle_blit_rotated (00056e2a) at 00056e71 / 00056e9d / 00056ecf / 00056efc and by fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) at 00057172 / 0005719e / 000571d0 / 000571fd. Both routines take the two 4.12 fixed-point rotation terms -- the cosine-like term and the sine-like term, from words [arg+0x1c] and [arg+0x1e] for the unscaled variant and from record+8 and record+0xc of the geometry record for the scaled one -- load the destination pitch at 0007002e zero-extended into EBP, and pick one of four sign cases. This word always receives minus the sign of the sine term times the pitch: +pitch when that term is <= 0, -pitch when it is > 0. The three siblings are set in the same breath: 00070034 gets sign(cos)*1, 0007003c gets sign(sin)*1, 00070040 gets sign(cos)*pitch.

Read only inside the pixel loop, and only after a carry. The blitter tracks two 4.12 accumulators as it walks a source row: one steps by the cosine magnitude at 0007004c and, on passing 0x1000, moves EDI horizontally by 00070034; the other steps by the sine magnitude at 0007004e and, on passing 0x1000, moves EDI vertically by this value (00056f74-00056f7b, 00056fd4-00056fe3, 0005703e-00057045, 00057092-00057097 in the unscaled routine, which keeps that accumulator in BP; 000572de, 00057383, 0005741e, 000574aa in the scaled routine, which spills it to 00070046). Together 00070034 and this word are the destination basis vector for the source X axis; 0007003c and 00070040 are the basis vector for the source Y axis, applied once per source row by the row-advance tail at 000570a9-000570ff. Both blitters store this value before drawing anything and never touch it again during the blit, so it is single-use scratch, not state that survives a call.

Pool: fdps  [both referencing functions are pool fdps members of the game's own RLE blitter family; no CRT or AIL code reaches this address]

Rebuild note:
The vertical step for the source-X walk is minus the sine term's sign, while the horizontal step for the source-Y walk at 0007003c is plus it. Deriving all four deltas from one sign pair without negating this one mirrors the sprite vertically.

=== 0007003c [PLATE]
Horizontal component, +1 or -1 byte, of the destination-pointer step the rotating blitters take when they advance from one source row to the next.

One of four dword step slots at 00070034/00070038/0007003c/00070040 that fdps_rle_blit_rotated and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled fill in before their decode loop and then only read; nothing else in the image touches them. Both kernels are jumped into on fdps_blit_dispatch's frame and take the rotation from its sixth argument as two 16-bit fixed-point components with 0x1000 meaning one whole pixel -- fdps_rle_blit_rotated reads them straight out of the argument dword (DX = word [EBP+0x1c], AX = word [EBP+0x1e], 00056e3c), fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled treats the argument as a pointer to a 16-byte block and takes them from offsets 8 and 0xc (0005712b). Each kernel then branches on the two signs (00056e4d/00056e57, 0005714e/00057158), stores the magnitudes into 0007004c and 0007004e, and writes the signs into the four slots: 00070034 = sign(DX), 00070038 = -sign(AX) * pitch, this slot = sign(AX), 00070040 = sign(DX) * pitch, pitch being the destination pitch fdps_blit_dispatch published at 0007002e. Sign here is +1 for a strictly positive component and -1 for zero or negative. 00070034 and 00070038 drive the within-row walk; this slot and 00070040 drive the row advance at 000570b0-000570ff resp. 000574ed-0005753c, which runs once per source row after EDI has been popped back to the row start: the accumulator at 00070048 gains 0007004e, and every time it reaches 0x1000 it loses 0x1000 and this step is added to EDI. Net effect of the four slots is that one source pixel across moves the destination point by (DX, -AX) and one source row down moves it by (AX, DX), both in 1/4096 pixel -- a rotation. When the AX component is zero the accumulator never reaches 0x1000, so the -1 stored in that case is never applied.

Pool: fdps  [the only two functions that reach it are game blit kernels in pool_fdps; this is the game's own blit parameter block, and neither the CRT nor the sound library touches the object]

Rebuild note:
The two step pairs are driven by crossed accumulators. Within a row the destination x step (00070034) is carried by the DX component and the y step (00070038) by the AX component; in the row advance this x step is carried by the AX component and the y step (00070040) by the DX component, and the y step's sign is the opposite of its within-row partner's. Writing the obvious thing -- one accumulator per axis, or the same component driving x in both loops -- turns the rotation into a shear. The carry test is also a single if, not a while: an accumulator that gains more than 0x1000 in one step loses only one 0x1000 and takes only one step, so a while loop diverges wherever a rotation component exceeds one pixel.

=== 00070040 [PLATE]
Destination y step, in bytes, taken for each source row advanced by the rotating RLE blitters.

Holds plus or minus the destination row pitch read from data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_dst_pitch (0007002e). fdps_rle_blit_rotated (00056e2a) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) both open by reading the caller's two rotation components (a 12.12 fixed-point pair, 0x1000 = 1.0) and branching on their signs into one of four quadrant cases; each case writes this variable together with the data at 00070034, 00070038 and 0007003c, the other three terms of the destination step matrix. This one takes the sign of the first component, so it and 00070034 are the matrix's diagonal (cosine) terms, while 00070038 and 0007003c carry the second component's sign with opposite polarity, as the sine terms of a rotation do.

It is read in exactly one place, the outer per-source-row block at 000570a9-0005710d (000574e6-0005754a in the scaled variant). That block restores the row-start destination pointer, adds the absolute second component (0007004e) into the accumulator at 00070048 and steps the pointer horizontally by 0007003c on carry, then adds the absolute first component (0007004c) into the accumulator at 0007004a and adds this value to the pointer on carry -- so the destination walks one scanline up or down for every whole unit of vertical travel the rotation calls for as it moves down the source image. The row counter at data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows (00070022) ends the loop.

The image holds zero here, but that initial value is dead: all four quadrant branches write this variable before the first read.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_rle_blit_rotated and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled reference it; it is game sprite-rendering scratch state]

=== 00070044 [PLATE]
Fractional part of the rotated blitter's destination cursor in the horizontal direction, in units of 1/4096 of a pixel.

fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) is the only function that touches it, and it is one half of the pair that walks the destination cursor along a rotated source row; the other half is 00070046, the vertical fraction. At the top of every destination row (00057239) both are reset to 0. Each time the row loop emits a pixel it adds the horizontal component of the rotation step -- the word at 0007004c -- to this value; if the sum reaches 0x1000 one whole destination column has been crossed, so it subtracts 0x1000 and advances the destination pointer EDI by the signed one-byte column step at 00070034. The remainder is stored back here, so the value is always in 0..0xfff. The same idiom appears once in each of the four RLE opcode arms (000572b7, 00057354, 000573f7, 00057485) because the decode loop is unrolled per opcode, not because there are four different meanings.

The geometry comes from the four-word record fdps_blit_dispatch hands over in [EBP+0x1c]: destination width at +0, destination height at +4, and the two rotation step components at +8 and +0xc. The entry code at 0005714e-0005720d takes the absolute values of the two steps into 0007004c and 0007004e and pushes their signs into the four direction dwords 00070034 (plus or minus 1), 00070038 and 00070040 (plus or minus the destination pitch) and 0007003c (plus or minus 1), which is why this accumulator is unsigned. Between rows the routine runs the same overflow dance on a second pair, 00070048 and 0007004a, with the two step words crossed over -- that is the axis perpendicular to the row, and it is what rotates the whole sprite rather than shearing it. Those two are zeroed once at function entry (00057133, 0005713c), not per row.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled reads or writes it, and it sits in the graphics scratch block that starts at data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows]

Rebuild note:
This pair is reset at the top of every destination row while the row-to-row pair at 00070048/0007004a is reset only once per blit. Hoisting all four initialisations to one place -- the obvious thing to do once they become local variables of one C function -- restarts the sprite's rows on carried-over sub-pixel phases and shifts pixels along every row but the first.

=== 00070046 [PLATE]
Fractional part of the rotated blitter's destination cursor in the vertical direction, in units of 1/4096 of a destination scanline.

fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) is the only function that touches it. It is the second half of the pair that walks the destination cursor along one rotated source row; the first half is 00070044, the horizontal fraction. Both are reset to 0 at the top of every destination row (00057239, 00057242), inside the row loop that 0005754a closes back to 0005722f. Each time the row loop emits a source pixel it adds the vertical rotation magnitude, the word at 0007004e, to this value; when the sum reaches 0x1000 one whole destination scanline has been crossed, so it subtracts 0x1000 and advances the destination pointer EDI by the signed pitch step at 00070038. The remainder is stored back here, so the value is always in 0..0xfff. The same idiom appears once in each of the four RLE opcode arms -- solid run (000572be), dithered run (0005735b), literal run (000573fe) and transparent skip (0005748c) -- because the decode loop is unrolled per opcode, not because there are four different meanings.

In the three arms that draw, the carry branch writes the pixel a second time at the current EDI before stepping vertically (000572dc, 00057381, 0005741c; in the dithered arm the extra write is under the same OR AH,AH / JZ guard as the first one). That fills the hole a diagonal step would otherwise leave. The transparent arm has no such write because it draws nothing.

The geometry comes from the four-word record fdps_blit_dispatch hands over in [EBP+0x1c]: destination width at +0, destination height at +4, and the two rotation components at +8 and +0xc. The entry code at 0005714e-00057214 branches on the two signs, stores the magnitudes into 0007004c and 0007004e, and writes the signs into the four step dwords -- 00070034 and 0007003c hold plus or minus 1 (one destination column), 00070038 and 00070040 hold plus or minus the destination pitch at 0007002e (one destination row). Between rows the routine runs the same overflow dance on a second pair, 00070048 and 0007004a, with the two magnitude words crossed over; that is the axis perpendicular to the row, and it is what rotates the sprite rather than shearing it. Those two are zeroed once at function entry (00057133, 0005713c), not per row.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled reads or writes it, and it sits in the graphics blit scratch block that runs from data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows at 00070022 up to 0007004f]

Rebuild note:
When this accumulator carries, the three drawing arms store the pixel a second time at the pre-step position before moving the destination pointer down a scanline; the horizontal partner at 00070044 has no such second store. Writing the obvious loop -- advance the cursor by both accumulators, then write one pixel -- leaves holes wherever the rotation steps vertically. This pair is also re-zeroed at the top of every destination row while the row-to-row pair at 00070048/0007004a is zeroed only once per blit, so hoisting all four initialisations together carries sub-pixel phase from one row into the next.

=== 00070048 [PLATE]
Horizontal fraction of the rotated blitter's destination cursor as it steps from one source row to the next, in units of 1/4096 of a pixel.

Only fdps_rle_blit_rotated (00056e2a) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) touch it, and both use it the same way. It is one half of a pair with 0007004a, the vertical fraction; both are zeroed once at function entry (00056e2a/00056e33 and 00057133/0005713c), not per row. The row loop saves the row-start destination pointer with PUSH EDI at its head and restores it with POP EDI at its foot (00056f26 / 000570a8); immediately after the restore the routine adds the row-step's horizontal component -- the word at 0007004e -- to this value, and if the sum reaches 0x1000 one whole destination column has been crossed, so it subtracts 0x1000 and advances EDI by the signed one-column step at 0007003c. The remainder is stored back here, so the value is always in 0..0xfff. The vertical half runs immediately after on 0007004a with the step word 0007004c and the plus-or-minus-pitch step at 00070040, and then DEC word ptr [0x00070022] decides whether another source row follows.

Note the crossover: this row-step pair uses the two magnitude words 0007004c and 0007004e swapped relative to the per-pixel pair inside the row loop, which adds 0007004c to the horizontal accumulator and 0007004e to the vertical one. Walking along a row and walking down the rows move the destination cursor in perpendicular directions, and that swap is exactly what turns the blit into a rotation instead of a shear. The two magnitudes themselves are the absolute values of the two geometry words the caller passes in [EBP+0x1c] / [EBP+0x1e]; the four-way sign branch at the head of each kernel (00056e4d-00056f13) strips their signs into the four direction dwords 00070034, 00070038, 0007003c and 00070040, which is why this accumulator is unsigned.

In fdps_rle_blit_rotated the per-pixel accumulators are not globals at all: they are DX and BP, cleared at the row-loop head at 00056f20/00056f23. The scaled twin keeps them in 00070044/00070046 instead and clears them per row there.

Pool: fdps  [only the two fdps rotated-blit kernels read or write it; it sits in the blitter scratch block that runs from data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_remaining_rows at 00070022 upward]

Rebuild note:
The row-step accumulators take the step components crossed over relative to the per-pixel accumulators: this horizontal one is advanced by 0007004e and the vertical one by 0007004c, the opposite of the pixel loop. Writing the obvious row_frac_x += step_x pairing shears the sprite instead of rotating it. This pair is also zeroed once per blit while the pixel pair is zeroed at every row.

=== 0007004a [PLATE]
Fractional part of the rotated blitter's vertical destination position as it advances from one source row to the next, in units of 1/4096 of a pixel.

fdps_rle_blit_rotated (00056e2a) and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (00057114) are the only functions that touch it. Both zero it once, at function entry (00056e33, 0005713c), together with its horizontal partner at 00070048. It is then read and rewritten exactly once per source row, in the row-advance tail that runs after the pixel loop has popped EDI back to the row start: 000570db-000570ff in the unscaled routine, 00057518-0005753c in the scaled one. Each pass adds the first rotation component's magnitude, the word at 0007004c, to this value; if the sum reaches 0x1000 one whole destination row has been crossed, so it subtracts 0x1000 and advances the destination pointer EDI by data_fdps_graphics_rle_rotate_dst_y_step_per_src_y (00070040), which is plus or minus the destination pitch. The remainder is stored back here, so the value is always in 0..0xfff. The partner at 00070048 does the same dance with the second component (0007004e) and the plus-or-minus-one-byte horizontal step at 0007003c; the two together move the destination point by the rotation's source-Y basis vector once per source row, while the pair at 00070044/00070046 moves it by the source-X basis vector once per emitted pixel.

The test is a single if, not a loop: an increment larger than 0x1000 would still lose only one 0x1000 and take only one row step.

Pool: fdps  [only the two game blit kernels reference it; no CRT or AIL code reaches the address]

Rebuild note:
This pair is zeroed once per blit, while the per-pixel pair at 00070044/00070046 is zeroed at the top of every destination row. Initialising all four accumulators together once the four become locals of one C function -- the obvious thing to do -- makes each row start on the previous row's leftover sub-pixel phase and shifts pixels on every row but the first.

=== 0007004c [PLATE]
Magnitude of the cosine term of the sprite rotation, in units of 1/4096 of a pixel: how far the destination cursor advances along its primary axis for each source pixel stepped.

Written once per blit, by fdps_rle_blit_rotated at 00056f0c and by fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled at 0005720d, always as the absolute value of the caller's first 4.12 fixed-point rotation component (word [EBP+0x1c] for the unscaled kernel, record+8 of the geometry record for the scaled one). Both kernels branch on the signs of the component pair first, negate whichever is <= 0, and fold the sign into the four signed destination steps at 00070034/00070038/0007003c/00070040, so this word is never negative and is below 0x1000 for a true rotation. Its partner data at 0007004e is the sine magnitude; the two drive the two diagonals of the same 2x2 step matrix.

It is read in two places. The pixel loop adds it once per source pixel emitted to the horizontal destination fraction -- register DX in fdps_rle_blit_rotated (00056f45, 00056fa5, 0005700f, 00057063), data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_rot_pixel_step_x_accumulator at 00070044 in fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled (0005729a, 00057337, 000573da, 00057468) -- and when the sum reaches 0x1000 one whole destination column has been crossed, so 0x1000 is subtracted and EDI advances by data_fdps_graphics_rle_rotate_dst_x_step_per_src_x (00070034). The per-source-row block adds it once per finished row to the vertical row fraction at 0007004a (000570e2, 0005751f); when that reaches 0x1000 EDI advances by data_fdps_graphics_rle_rotate_dst_y_step_per_src_y (00070040). Both carries subtract 0x1000 exactly once, so one source step never advances the destination by more than one pixel.

Pool: fdps  [the only two functions that reference it are fdps_rle_blit_rotated and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled, both pool_fdps sprite kernels]

Rebuild note:
This word holds the absolute value of the rotation component, not the caller's signed value -- the sign lives in the four dword step slots. Adding a signed component to the accumulator, or carrying with "while (acc >= 0x1000)" or "acc / 0x1000" in place of the original's single "if (acc >= 0x1000) acc -= 0x1000;", changes the picture whenever the component is negative or is 1.0 or larger.

=== 0007004e [PLATE]
Magnitude of the sine term of the blit rotation, 4.12 fixed point with 0x1000 meaning 1.0.

Written once per blit, at 00056f13 by fdps_rle_blit_rotated and at 00057214 by fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled, from the second of the two rotation components the caller supplies -- word [frame+0x1e] of fdps_blit_dispatch's frame for the unscaled kernel, word +0xc of the geometry record for the scaled one. Both kernels first branch on the signs of the two components into one of four quadrant cases, store the sign information in the four destination-step dwords at 00070034, 00070038, 0007003c and 00070040, and NEG the component here if it was not positive, so this word is always the absolute value and the inner loop never has to look at a sign. Its partner, the cosine magnitude, is the word at 0007004c.

Read in two places. Stepping one pixel along a source row adds it to the vertical sub-pixel accumulator -- BP in fdps_rle_blit_rotated, data at 00070046 in fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled -- and when that accumulator reaches 0x1000 one whole destination row has been crossed, so 0x1000 is subtracted and the destination pointer advances by 00070038. Stepping to the next source row adds it to the accumulator at 00070048, whose carry moves the destination pointer horizontally by 0007003c (000570b7, 000574f4). That pairing -- source x contributing to destination y and source y contributing to destination x -- is the off-diagonal term of the rotation matrix; 0007004c carries the diagonal term. A value of 0 means no rotation about this axis, 0x1000 means a quarter turn.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_rle_blit_rotated and fdps_rle_blit_rotated_scaled reach it; no CRT or AIL code touches this block]

Rebuild note:
The rotation terms are stored here with their signs stripped and the signs carried separately in the four step dwords, and every carry test on the accumulators is an unsigned compare against 0x1000. Rewriting this in C with the signed rotation terms fed straight into the accumulators, or declaring this word signed, changes which source pixels land on which destination pixels in three of the four quadrants.

=== 00070050 [PLATE]
Lowest palette index that fdps_rle_blit_translucent_color_range blends instead of copying.

Written once, at the top of fdps_rle_blit_translucent_color_range, from field +0x0c of the blit parameter block the caller passes on the stack; data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_translucent_color_max at 00070052 takes field +0x10 at the same time. All three RLE run decoders in that function then test each decoded source pixel against the pair: an index below this value or above the maximum is written to the destination unchanged, an index inside the inclusive window [min..max] is looked up in the shade ramp and combined with the pixel already on screen. The compare is signed and the pixel is zero-extended from a byte, so the effective range of an index is 0..255. Nothing outside this function touches the variable.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_rle_blit_translucent_color_range reads or writes it]

Rebuild note:
The source pixel is zero-extended (XOR EAX,EAX; LODSB) before the signed compare against this bound. Declaring the pixel as plain char - signed by default under Watcom - makes every palette index 128..255 compare below the minimum and silently lose its translucency; the index must be held as unsigned char or widened to int before the range test.

=== 00070052 [PLATE]
Highest palette index that fdps_rle_blit_translucent_color_range blends instead of copying.

Written once, at the top of fdps_rle_blit_translucent_color_range, from field +0x10 of the blit parameter block the caller passes on the stack; data_fdps_graphics_rle_blit_translucent_color_min at 00070050 takes field +0x0c in the same pair of instructions. All three RLE run decoders in that function then test each decoded source pixel against the pair: an index below the minimum or above this value is written to the destination unchanged, an index inside the inclusive window [min..max] is looked up in the shade ramp and combined with the pixel already on screen. Both ends of the window are inclusive - the two blend paths branch on JLE and the copy path on JG. The pixel is zero-extended from a byte before the signed compare, so an index runs 0..255. Nothing outside this function touches the variable.

Pool: fdps  [only fdps_rle_blit_translucent_color_range reads or writes it]
